# MONTH OF JANUARY

[Woodcut headpiece]

*Having 31 days.*

*On the first day: The Circumcision in the Flesh of our Lord, God, and Savior Jesus Christ;*  
*And the commemoration of our father among the saints, Basil the Great, Archbishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia.*  
*If the temple be of Saint Basil, we celebrate a Vigil.*  
*At Small Vespers, on "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 4, Tone 3: Idiomela:*

Having welcomed Christ into thy soul through thy pure life, the fountain of life, O sacredly blessed Basil, thou didst pour forth rivers of pious teachings upon the inhabited world; watered by them, the faithful people of the Church, offering the fruit of lips confessing Him, bring thanksgiving unto Him Who glorifies thy memory unto ages of ages. *(Twice)*

The chrism of grace poured out upon thee anointed thee to minister sacredly the Gospel of the heavenly Kingdom, O Basil revealed by God; having become the sweet savor of Christ, with the fragrance of His knowledge thou didst fill the inhabited world. Therefore, favorably receiving the voices of thy servants, entreat great mercy for us who honor thee.

*By Byzantios:*
Clothed in hierarchical vestments, O Basil, champion of the Trinity, thou didst stand before the judgment seat, enduring danger for the faith; and having displayed steadfast suffering, thou didst put to shame the fury of the prefects raging with the power of impiety. And when he threatened thee with unmerciful dismemberment, having courageously resolved upon this, O father, and become a martyr by volition, thou didst receive the crown of victory from Christ, Who has great mercy.

[Fol. 1v]
*Month of January*

...the crown of victory from Christ, Who has great mercy.

*Glory, Tone 5:*
Having learned the nature of things that exist, and having perceived the instability of them all, thou didst find One immutable, the super-essential Creator of all; and cleaving all the more unto Him, thou didst cast away desire for things that are not. Pray that we also may obtain divine desire, O Basil revealed by God.

*Both now, of the Feast:*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2.*  
*Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме єѵфра́ѳовъ):*

A light-bearing temple of the thrice-radiant ray art thou; thou dost illumine the souls of those who are nourished by thy words, O Basil.

*Verse: My mouth shall speak wisdom, and the meditation of my heart understanding.*  
A heavenly trumpet is the sound of thy voice, and a fire whereby all heretical teachings are consumed, O Basil.

*Verse: The mouth of the righteous shall meditate wisdom, and his tongue shall speak judgment.*  
Glorifying the one Thrice-radiant Light divided in Persons, but One in essence, thou didst cast down Arius and Sabellius, O Basil.

*Glory, and both now:*  
The bodily circumcision of the God-Man Word, and the memory of Basil the Great, we piously venerate.

*After the Our Father, the Troparion of the Saint; Glory, and both now, of the Circumcision. Litany, and Dismissal.*  
*At Great Vespers, Matins, and the Liturgy, the entire order is celebrated as printed in order.*[^11]

*At Great Vespers, after "Blessed is the man," the first antiphon.*  
*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 10: of the Feast, 4, Tone 8. Idiomela:*

He Who descended, the Savior, unto the human race, accepted wrapping in swaddling clothes; He did not disdain bodily circumcision: eight-day-old according to His Mother, unoriginate according to His Father. Unto Him let us, the faithful, cry aloud: Thou art our God, have mercy on us! *(Twice)*

The all-good God was not ashamed to be circumcised with bodily circumcision; but He gave Himself as an example and pattern unto all for salvation: for the Creator of the Law fulfills the requirements of the Law, and the prophecies of the prophets concerning Him. O Thou Who holdest all things in Thy palm, and wast wrapped in swaddling clothes: Lord, glory to Thee!

*Other Stichera of the Saint, on 4, Tone 4.*  
*Tone 4, Podoben: "Called from on high" (Зва́нный свы́ше):*

O thou named after kingship, who by love of wisdom and artistic skill didst shepherd the royal priesthood, Christ's holy nation, O father [Fol. 2r]
...the royal priesthood, Christ's holy nation, O father, thou didst shepherd with love of wisdom and skill; then with the crown of the Kingdom did the King of kings and Lord of all adorn thee, the co-eternal and co-unoriginate Son united to Him Who begot Him; pray Him to save and enlighten our souls.

Adorned with hierarchical vestments, rejoicing thou didst proclaim the Gospel of the Kingdom, O Basil, as a fountain of orthodox teachings for the Church; enlightened by which, we now theologize and glorify one Godhead in the Father Almighty, and in the Only-Begotten Word of God, and in the Divine Spirit, indivisibly in three Persons: pray Him to save and enlighten our souls.

Dwelling together with the heavenly choirs and taking up thy abode with them, O father Basil, whose manner of life thou didst also emulate through the splendor of the purity of thy life, while yet living in the flesh with those upon earth as though bodiless: entreat Christ our God on behalf of those who delight in thy divinely-inspired teaching, that we may be delivered from tribulations and the darkness of ignorance, and that He may save and enlighten our souls.

*Glory, Tone 6. By Anatolius:*
Having become a lover of wisdom, O venerable one, and preferring that companionship which is toward God, having chosen the contemplation of death as thy consort, thou didst lead a comely life. For having surrounded thyself with the strongholds of temperance against carnal passions, and having kept the nobility of thy soul unenslaved through the rule of divine study, by the wealth of virtue thou didst subject all carnal mindedness to the spirit. Therefore, having hated the flesh and the world and the ruler of this world, as thou standest before Christ, entreat great mercy for our souls.

*Both now, Tone 6, the first Sticheron:*  
*He Who descended, the Savior:*  
*Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day.*  
*Reading from Genesis (Chapter 17):*[^12]

The Lord appeared to Abraham, and said unto him: I am thy God; be well-pleasing before Me, and be blameless. And I will establish My covenant between Me and thee, and will multiply thee exceedingly. And Abraham fell upon his face; and God spoke unto him, saying: As for Me, behold, My covenant is with thee, and thou shalt be a father of a multitude of nations. Neither shall thy name any more be called Abram, but thy name shall be Abraham; for a father of a multitude of nations have I made thee. And I will increase thee exceedingly, and make nations of thee, and kings shall come forth from thee. And I will establish [Fol. 2v]
...My covenant between Me and thee, and between thy seed after thee in their generations, for an everlasting covenant, and I will be their God. And Abraham fell upon his face, and bowed down to the Lord. And God said unto Abraham: Thou also shalt keep My covenant, thou and thy seed after thee in their generations. And this is the covenant which thou shalt keep between Me and you, and between thy seed after thee in their generations: ye shall circumcise your foreskin, and it shall be for a sign of the covenant between Me and you, and between thy seed after thee in their generations. And every male child among you shall be circumcised when eight days old, throughout your generations. And the uncircumcised male who shall not circumcise his foreskin on the eighth day, that soul shall be destroyed from its generation, because he has broken My covenant.[^13]

*Reading from Proverbs (Chapter 8):*[^14]
The Lord created Me the beginning of His ways for His works. Before the ages He established Me, in the beginning, before He made the earth, and before He made the deeps; before the water springs came forth; before the mountains were settled, and before all the hills He begets Me. The Lord made the lands and the uninhabited wastes, and the inhabited summits under heaven. When He prepared the heaven, I was present with Him; and when He set apart His throne upon the winds. When He made firm the upper clouds, and when He made sure the fountains of the deep. When He appointed the sea its limit, that the waters should not pass His commandment; and when He made strong the foundations of the earth: I was by Him, harmonizing all things. I was She in Whom He took delight; and daily I rejoiced before His face at all times.

*Reading from Proverbs (Chapter 10):*[^15]
The mouth of the righteous drips wisdom, but the tongue of the unrighteous shall perish. The lips of righteous men drip grace, but the mouth of the ungodly is perverse. False balances are an abomination before the Lord, but a just weight is acceptable unto Him. Wheresoever insolence enters, there also is dishonor; but the mouth of the humble meditates wisdom. The integrity of the upright shall guide them, but the overthrow of the rebellious shall despoil them. Possessions profit not in the day of wrath, but righteousness delivers from death. When a righteous man dies, he leaves regret; but the destruction of the ungodly is sudden and despised. The righteousness of the blameless makes straight paths, but in ungodliness (see fol. 3r)[^16] [Fol. 4r][^17]
*Day 1*

...was circumcised as an eight-day-old man. Glory to Thy all-good counsel; glory to Thy dispensation; glory to Thy condescension, O Thou Who alone art the Lover of mankind! And Dismissal.

*At Compline, the Kontakion of the Saint; Glory, and both now, of the Feast.*  
*And we chant Midnight Office according to custom, with the kathisma. After the first Trisagion, the Troparion of the Feast. After the second Trisagion, the Kontakion of the Feast. The prayers, "Remember, O Lord, in the hope of resurrection," we do not say, but only: "Lord, have mercy" (12 times). And Dismissal.*

*At Matins, on "God is the Lord," Troparion of the Feast (twice); Glory, of the Saint; Both now, of the Feast.*  
*After the first Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 5.*  
*Tone 5, Podoben: "Co-unoriginate with the Father" (Собезнача́льное сло́во):*

As the royal adornment of the Church let us all praise Basil, the inexhaustible treasury of teachings; for by them he taught us to revere the Holy Trinity, united indeed in essence, but divided in Hypostases.

*Glory, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thy tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й, сп҃се):*
O all-wise Basil, as thou standest before the Trinity, pray that on the day of judgment grace, mercy, and the cleansing of transgressions may be obtained by us who sing unto thee and honor thy memory, that with mouth and heart we may glorify the one Lover of mankind.

*Both now:*
The Creator and Master of all the world, Who is above with the Father and the Spirit, is circumcised on earth as an eight-day-old infant. Truly divine and marvelous are Thy works: for Thou, O Master, wast circumcised for our sake, as Thou art the fulfillment of the Law.

*And we read in the Commentary Gospel, the instruction of Basil the Great unto monks.*

*After the second Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8.*  
*Tone 8, Podoben: "Of wisdom" (Прему́дрости):*

Having divinely drawn the secret wealth of ineffable wisdom, thou didst pour forth for all the waters of Orthodoxy, divinely gladdening the hearts of the faithful, and most worthily drowning the unbelieving. Thence, through the twofold labors of piety, thou wast shown to be an invincible champion of the Trinity, O hierarch Basil: pray Christ God to grant remission of transgressions unto those who celebrate thy holy memory with love.

*Glory, Tone 3, Podoben: "Of the divine faith" (Боже́ственныя вѣ́ры):*
Thou didst water the whole inhabited world as with streams by thy teachings, the dogmas of piety gathered together; for truly the fountain of life rested in thee, O Basil: pray Him, as thou hast acquired boldness, O divinely-inspired one [Fol. 4v]
*Month of January*

...as thou hast acquired boldness, O divinely-inspired one, to grant us great mercy.

*Both now, Tone 4:*
He Who is invisible by nature is now visible in the flesh; the uncreated Word is now fashioned, being born of a pure Virgin; therefore according to the Law, for the sake of us men, He is circumcised as an eight-day-old infant: unto Him therefore let us bow down as unto our Savior.

*After the Polyeleos, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8.*  
*Tone 8, Podoben: "Of wisdom" (Прему́дрости):*

By the power of divine words thou didst cast down dark heresies; thou didst drown all the arrogance of Eunomius, for thou didst proclaim the Spirit to be God unto men; and by the lifting up of thy hands thou didst put the enemies to death; thou didst drive away all the service of Sabellius, and thou didst abolish all the vain musings of Nestorius, O holy hierarch Basil: pray Christ God to grant remission of transgressions unto those who celebrate thy holy memory with love.

*Glory:*
The grace of thy divine words and the mystical height of thy dogmas became for us a ladder of divine ascent; for having acquired the trumpet of the Holy Spirit, O father, thereby thou didst proclaim the divine teachings. Therefore also thou hast taken up thine abode in a place of green pastures, having received the rewards of thy struggles, O venerable hierarch Basil: pray Christ God to grant remission of transgressions unto those who celebrate thy holy memory with love.

*Both now:*
The Master and Creator of men, having received flesh from thy most pure womb, showed thee to be the protectress of mankind, O all-immaculate one. Therefore we all flee unto thee, asking cleansing of transgressions, O Sovereign Lady, and to be delivered from eternal torment and from every malice of the cruel ruler of this world. Therefore we cry unto thee: pray thy Son and God to grant remission of transgressions unto those who bow down in faith to thy all-holy Nativity.

*And we read the funeral oration of Gregory the Theologian concerning Basil the Great, in four parts.*[^18]

*Gradual, the first antiphon of Tone 4.*  
*Prokeimenon, Tone 4:*  
*My mouth shall speak wisdom, and the meditation of my heart understanding.*[^19]  
*Verse: Hear this, all ye nations; give ear, all ye that inhabit the world.*[^20]  
*Let every breath.*  
*Gospel according to John, pericope 36.*[^21]  
*After Psalm 50, Idiomelon Sticheron, Tone 6:*  
*Grace was poured out*[^22] [Fol. 5r]
*Day 1*

...upon thy lips, venerable father, and thou becamest a shepherd of Christ's Church, teaching the rational sheep to believe in the consubstantial Trinity in one Godhead.

*Canon of the Feast.*  
*The composition of Stephen.*  
*The Heirmos twice, and the troparia to 4, Tone 2.*  
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*  
Come, O ye peoples, let us sing a song unto Christ God, Who divided the sea and guided the people whom He brought forth from the bondage of Egypt, for He hath been glorified.

*Troparion:*  
Bearing the image of the future age, the octave of days is illumined and sanctified by Thy voluntary poverty, O Christ; for on this day Thou wast circumcised in the flesh according to the Law.

*Troparion:*  
Christ accepts circumcision on the eighth day from His Nativity, and today He folds up the shadow, causing the light of the new grace to shine forth.

*Another Canon of the Saint, to 8. The composition of John of Damascus.*  
*Tone and Heirmos the same.*  
*Troparion:*  
Thy voice was fitting, O Basil, for those who desire to begin thy praises; but receiving our supplication, O father, grant us grace unstintingly.

*Troparion:*  
Thou didst walk the rough path of the virtues and didst reach the smooth and unopposed heavenly ascent, and thou wast shown to all as an example, O Basil.

*Troparion:*  
The passionate surging that torments the flesh thou didst discipline by the desire of love of wisdom; therefore thou dwellest in the incorruptible kingdoms, O father Basil.

*Troparion:*  
The passions of the soul, fittingly, O Basil, together with those of the body, thou didst cut down with the spiritual sword; and thou didst offer thyself as a sacrifice unto the Master.

*Troparion:*  
Having become an initiate of ineffable mysteries, O Basil, thou didst mystically instruct the royal priesthood of Christ, O holy father: plainly thou didst make the Trinitarian light shine upon us.

*Theotokion:*  
Who can worthily recount thy conception which is beyond word? For thou, O all-pure one, didst give birth in the flesh unto God, Who hath appeared unto us as Savior and Lord.

*Katavasia, the first choir sings the Heirmos:*  
He uncovered the bottom of the deep, and on dry land leads His own; therein covering the adversaries, the Lord strong in battle, for He hath been glorified.  
*The other choir, Heirmos:*  
Israel passes through the surging storm of the sea, which straightway appeared as dry land; but the dark deep, a watery grave, completely covered the captains of Egypt [Fol. 5v]
*Month of January*

...completely covered the captains of Egypt by the mighty power of the Master's right hand.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*  
Establish us in Thee, O Lord, Who by the Tree didst put sin to death, and plant Thy fear in the hearts of us who sing unto Thee.

*Troparion:*  
The superessential Word, having become incarnate, was circumcised for the cessation of the Law; and He granted unto us the firstfruits of divine grace and incorruptible life.

*Troparion:*  
Christ having become incarnate was shown as the fulfiller of the Law, not as being contrary to God, and He deigned voluntarily to be circumcised on the eighth day.

*Of the Venerable [Saint].*  
*Troparion:*  
Thy memory, O father, concurred and shone forth together with the Nativity of Christ, Whose ineffable mystery thou didst plainly make known by thy teachings.

*Troparion:*  
Being established in the fear of the Lord—for this is the beginning of wisdom[^23]—thou wast winged with a higher love of wisdom, O Basil.

*Troparion:*  
Being filled with every instruction, not only of that which is lowly and trampled upon, but much more of the higher, thou wast shown as a light unto the world, O Basil.

*Troparion:*  
O all-wise Basil, thou didst enter through action, and action thou didst show to be the stepping-stone to the most divine contemplation; and clearly wast thou instructed in the true knowledge of reality.

*Theotokion:*  
Seedlessly in thy womb didst thou conceive God, and ineffably thou givest birth unto Him incarnate, upon Whom the venerable hosts of heaven dare not gaze, O Ever-Virgin.

*Katavasia, the first choir:*  
The Lord Who gives strength unto our kings, and exalts the horn of His anointed,[^24] is born of a Virgin and comes unto baptism: unto Him, O ye faithful, let us cry aloud: There is none holy like our God!  
*The other choir:*  
As many of us as have been loosed from the ancient snares, of the food of lions whose jaws are shattered, let us rejoice and open wide our mouth, weaving a hymn from words of sweet melody, wherein He delights in granting gifts unto us.

*Kontakion of the Feast, Tone 3, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дѣ́ва дне́сь):*  
The Lord of all endures circumcision, and as good circumcises the transgressions of men; He gives salvation today unto the world; and in the highest rejoices also the Hierarch of the Creator, the radiant, divine initiate of Christ, Basil.

*Then the Sessional Hymn of the Saint, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of wisdom" (Прему́дрости):*

[Fol. 6r]
*Day 1*

Having learned the words of wisdom, and laid aside the writing of the Law, thou didst proclaim unto all the words of grace; and the tablets of souls thou didst smooth with thy words, wherein thou didst inscribe divine teachings. Therefore, having passed through the gloom of the body's veil, thou didst shine forth in the Spirit, O holy hierarch Basil: pray Christ God to grant remission of transgressions unto those who honor thy holy memory with love. *(Twice)*

*Glory, and both now, of the Feast, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared today" (Ꙗ҆ви́лся є҆сѝ дне́сь):*  
As Thou art an abyss of love for mankind, Thou didst clothe Thyself, O Master, in the form of a servant, and wast circumcised in the flesh, granting Thy great mercy unto all men.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*  
I have heard, O Lord, the report of Thy dispensation, and I glorified Thee, O Thou Who alone art the Lover of mankind.

*Troparion:*  
Circumcision ceased from the time when Christ was voluntarily circumcised, saving the multitude of the Gentiles by grace.

*Troparion:*  
It prefigures the unceasing life of the future eighth age, wherein the Master was circumcised in the flesh.

*Of the Venerable [Saint]:*  
*Troparion:*  
The Church, the bride of Christ, is adorned even as by the Nativity, so also by thy memory, O all-blessed one.

*Troparion:*  
Thou wast shown to be invincible, fighting for God, O Basil, submitting in all things to His command.

*Troparion:*  
Thou wast given by God unto the Church as a defense and a firm wall, O all-blessed Basil.

*Troparion:*  
Thou wast shown to be a sharp axe against the adversaries of God, and a fire consuming delusion, O father Basil.

*Theotokion:*  
We pray thee, O pure one, who didst seedlessly conceive God, ever to intercede for thy servants.

*Katavasia:*  
I have heard, O Lord, Thy voice which Thou didst utter, the voice of one crying in the wilderness,[^25] when Thou didst thunder over many waters, testifying to Thy Son; being filled with the Spirit that descended, he cried aloud: Thou art Christ, the wisdom and power of God!  
*The other choir:*  
Cleansed by the fire of mystical contemplation, the prophet sings the renewal of mankind; he lifts up his voice, clapping in the Spirit, revealing the incarnation of the ineffable Word, by Whom the dominions of the mighty have been shattered.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*  
O Lord, Giver of light and Maker of the ages, guide us in the light of Thy commandments; for other than Thee we know no other God [Fol. 6v]
*Month of January*

...for other than Thee we know no other God.

*Troparion:*  
Having come forth ineffably from the Virgin Mother, O Lord, Thou didst not disdain to be clothed in human form; as an infant according to the Law, Thou didst fulfill the Law.

*Troparion:*  
She that bore Thee became like unto night, loving the shadow of the Law, out of whom Christ appeared, shining forth as the Light of the world.

*Of the Venerable [Saint].*  
*Troparion:*  
The Church truly celebrates a twofold feast today: the Circumcision, as of the Master Who appeared on earth as an infant, and the memory of a wise and thrice-blessed servant.

*Troparion:*  
The unapproachable Light having rested in thee, O venerable one, Christ showed thee to be a most radiant lamp unto the world; therefore we sing thy memory, O Basil.

*Troparion:*  
Expounding from divine treasures the genesis written down veiledly on Sinai by Moses,[^26] thou didst inscribe it unto all, O most blessed Basil.

*Troparion:*  
Neither Moses the lawgiver, nor Joseph who was before the Law, was such a distributor of grain as thou; for of the divine Flesh, thou thyself wast shown to be the divider, O Basil.[^27]

*Theotokion:*  
Unto thee who didst bear Christ, the Maker of all, we cry: Rejoice, O pure one; rejoice, thou that didst cause the Light to shine upon us; rejoice, thou that didst contain the uncontainable God!

*Katavasia:*  
Jesus, the Prince of Life, comes to loose the condemnation of Adam the first-formed; and needing no cleansing as God, He cleanses the fallen in the Jordan, wherein having slain the enmity, He grants the peace that surpasses all understanding.[^28]  
*The other choir:*  
Washed by the Spirit's cleansing from the poison of the dark and polluted enemy, we have anchored at a new, unerring path that leads to inaccessible joy, accessible only unto those with whom God is reconciled.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*  
A vast abyss of sins encompasses me, and imitating the prophet I cry unto Thee: Bring me up from corruption, O Lord![^29]

*Troparion:*  
The Law received an end from the time when Christ became an infant; being the fulfiller of the Law, He received circumcision and loosed the curse of the Law.

*Troparion:*  
The Sabbath-keeping and circumcision of the Hebrew arrogance ceased at the nod of Christ Who appeared, and the spring of grace shone forth.

*Of the Venerable [Saint].*  
*Troparion:*  
Thou didst abundantly nourish the souls of the poor that were wasting away with hunger, and didst fill the hearts of the ravenous with every [Fol. 7r]
*Day 1*

...with every divine gladness, O Basil.

*Troparion:*  
Thou didst richly nourish the hungry with heavenly food; for thy word is the bread of angels, O Basil, whereby thou wast an outstanding distributor of wheat.[^30]

*Troparion:*  
Like a bee, O Basil, thou didst laboriously gather the flower of every virtue, and becoming skilled in them, thou art blessed.

*Troparion:*  
Thou wast eager to separate thyself from the world and to live with God; therefore having left the unstable and corruptible things, O all-blessed Basil, as wise thou didst acquire the abiding ones.

*Theotokion:*  
Save thy servants from dangers, O Birthgiver of God, for next to God we all flee unto thee as an unbreakable wall and protection.

*Katavasia:*  
The voice of the Word, the lamp of the Light, the morning star of the Sun, the Forerunner, cries aloud in the wilderness unto all peoples: Repent, and be cleansed beforehand! For behold, Christ stands by, Who delivers the world from corruption.[^31]  
*The other choir:*  
With an all-blessed voice the Father manifested the Beloved, Whom He brought forth from the womb:[^32] "This One," He says, "is My radiant, consubstantial Son, Who has sprung forth from the human race: My living Word, and a man through providence."

*Kontakion, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared today" (Ꙗ҆ви́лся є҆сѝ дне́сь):*  
Thou wast shown as an unshakable foundation of the Church, distributing an inviolable dominion unto all men, sealing it with thy decrees, O heaven-revealed, venerable Basil.

*Ikos:*  
A cup of chastity, the mouth of wisdom, and the pedestal of teachings, Basil the Great, mentally shines upon all. Come therefore, and let us stand in the house of God, fervently gazing upon him, adorned by his wonders, enlightened as by a ray of his life, refreshed by the pure Spirit, imitating his faith, warmth, and humility, whereby he was shown to be a house of God's nature; crying unto him, let us sing: O heaven-revealed, venerable Basil!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*  
At the golden image served in the plain of Dura, Thy three youths disregarded the ungodly decree; but cast into the midst of the fire, being bedewed they sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^33]

*Troparion:*  
Radiant and most radiant is the Nativity of Christ, which today subscribed the mystery of the future renewal; for according to the order of the Law the Savior is circumcised, not as God, but as man, and the fulfillment of the Law [Fol. 7v]
*Month of January*

...and the fulfillment of the Law.

*Troparion:*  
Fulfilling the Law, the Creator of the Law is voluntarily circumcised today in the flesh, working the circumcision of the winter of sins, and granting us to cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Of the Venerable [Saint].*  
*Troparion:*  
The Son is the image of the Father, and the Spirit of the Son; and thou, O Basil, art an undefiled mirror of the Spirit, and a dwelling of the whole Trinity. Blessed is thy memory, and those who glorify it are glorified!

*Troparion:*  
Having plunged thy mind into the unsearchable depths of God, and having gathered the pearl of great price of understanding, thou didst fill the world with wisdom, and didst teach men to cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*  
United in breath of mind, a holy pair, like one soul undivided in two bodies, Basil in Gregory and Gregory in Basil, united by divine desire: now pray Christ for your flock![^34]

*Troparion:*  
A father of orphans, and protector of widows, and wealth of the poor, consolation of the sick, and pilot of those in wealth, a staff of old age, and an instructor of youth, and a rule of virtue for monastics wast thou shown to be, O Basil.

*Troparion:*  
Having cleansed thy mind from all mire of defilement, O Basil, with thy desired spirit thou didst examine spiritual things; therefore singing unto the Trinity, with boldness thou didst cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*  
Moses foresaw thee as the burning bush on Mount Sinai, O pure one, who didst unburnt receive the unendurable radiance of the ineffable essence, which united itself to the grossness of the flesh, one of the holy Hypostases within it.[^35]

*Katavasia:*  
The young men of piety who partook of the fiery furnace, a whistling wind of dew preserved unharmed, and the descent of God's angel; therefore being bedewed in the flame, they gratefully sang: Blessed art Thou, the exceedingly praised Lord and God of our fathers![^36]  
*The other choir:*  
He Who quenched the high furnace flame that held the pious youths, burned the heads of the dragons with the stream, and washes away all the intolerable gloom of sin with the dew of the Spirit.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*  
God the Word, Who by ineffable wisdom established all things, and brought them from non-existence into being: bless as the Lord, ye works, and exalt Him [Fol. 8r]
*Day 1*

...and exalt Him unto all ages.

*Troparion:*  
On the eighth day the Master is circumcised as an infant, and He receives the name Jesus, for He is the Savior and Lord of the world.

*Troparion:*  
The eighth day, the holy and most glorious memory, was fittingly joined to Christ's Nativity; honoring it with faith, we sing unto the Lord and highly exalt Him unto the ages.

*Of the Venerable [Saint].*  
*Troparion:*  
Unto Him Who by ineffable providence granted Basil unto the world as a light of piety and a trumpet of theology: bless the Lord, ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*  
Unto Him Who by rich operation dwelt in wise Basil, and through him was piously theologized: bless the Lord, ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*  
Having delighted in thy divine words, O Basil, celebrating unceasingly in thy memory we cry aloud: Bless the Lord, ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*  
Rays of words didst thou emit unto the world, O Basil, guiding men by the light to honor the one Trinitarian essence: Bless the Lord, ye works of the Lord!

*Theotokion:*  
Unto God the Word, Who came forth from the Father before the ages, timeless, and in the latter times shone forth from the Virgin: bless the Lord, ye works of the Lord!

*Katavasia:*  
A most glorious mystery did the Babylonian furnace display, pouring forth dew, for the Jordan was about to receive the immaterial Fire in its streams, and to embrace the Creator baptized in the flesh, Whom the peoples bless and highly exalt unto all ages.  
*The other choir:*  
Creation is known to be free, and those who were formerly darkened are now sons of light; the ruler of darkness alone groans. Now let the former wretched heritage of the Gentiles fervently bless the Cause.

*At Ode 9 we do not sing "More honorable," but we sing the Refrains of the Circumcision:*  
*Magnify, O my soul, the Lord Who was circumcised in the flesh according to the Law.*  
*Ode 9. Heirmos:*  
He Who before the sun was shone forth as God the Illuminator, Who came unto us bodily from a virginal womb, having ineffably become incarnate: O blessed all-pure one, thee, O Birthgiver of God, do we magnify.  
*Then the second choir sings the same Refrain and Heirmos.*  
*The remaining three we sing as refrains to the troparia:*  
*Magnify, O my soul, Him Who on the eighth day receives circumcision. (Twice)*  
*Today the Master is circumcised in the flesh as an infant, fulfilling the Law. (Once)*  
*Today the Master was circumcised in the flesh* [Fol. 8v]
*Month of January*

...according to the Law, and was named Jesus. *(Once)*

*Troparion:*  
Transcending the boundaries of all human nature, Christ is born supernaturally of the Virgin; and as the writing of the Law commands, He is circumcised in the flesh, and is shown as the fulfiller of the Law.

*Troparion:*  
Come, let us celebrate in holiness the glorious names of the Master Christ; for today He was divinely named Jesus; and with these we magnify also the memory of the Saint.

*Then the Refrains of the Saint to his troparia:*  
*Magnify, O my soul, Basil the Great among hierarchs. (Twice)*  
*Magnify, O my soul, the most radiant lamp of the universe. (Twice)*  
*Magnify, O my soul, Basil the Great from Caesarea. (Twice)*  
*This instead of "Glory":*  
*Magnify, O my soul, him that adorned the Church of Christ.*  
*Instead of "Both now":*  
*Magnify, O my soul, the Virgin, the most pure Birthgiver of God, more honorable than the heavenly hosts.*

*Troparion:*  
As a faithful sheep of Christ, O Basil, thou didst follow the life-bearing footsteps of the Chief Shepherd; for thou didst surrender thy soul unto the tormentor, O father, valiantly enduring danger for the Church, O all-blessed one.

*Troparion:*  
Seeing the all-holy gathering of Christ's Church adorned by thy hierarchical ministry, O wise one, the all-destroying tormentor fell as though struck by thunder; for he could not endure the radiance of the Spirit that was in thee, O Basil.

*Troparion:*  
Thou wast counted worthy of the seat of the Apostles, the choir of Christ's passion-bearers, the tabernacles of the patriarchs, the delight of the righteous, and the joy of the prophets, O Basil; for thou wast a servant of the Birthgiver of God and an initiate of the Trinity.

*Theotokion:*  
The only Lord, Who covers His upper chambers with waters, Who bounds the sea and dries up the deeps,[^37] having received flesh from thee, O pure one, hastens from Bethlehem to the Jordan to be baptized in the flesh.

*Then both choirs coming together sing the first Refrain of the Feast and the Heirmos:*  
*First Refrain:* Magnify, O my soul, the Lord Who was circumcised in the flesh according to the Law.  
*Heirmos:*  
Every tongue is at a loss to praise thee worthily, and even an intellect beyond the world is dazed to sing unto thee, O Birthgiver of God; nevertheless, as thou art good, accept our faith, for thou knowest our divine longing: for thou art the protectress of Christians; thee do we magnify.  
*Then Refrain:*  
*Refrain:* Magnify, O my soul, the Virgin, the most pure Birthgiver of God, more honorable than the heavenly hosts.  
*And the Heirmos:*  
O marvels of thy birthgiving that are beyond understanding! O all-pure Bride, blessed Mother [Fol. 9r]
*Day 1*

...blessed Mother, through whom having obtained all-perfect salvation, worthily we praise as Benefactor, offering a song of thanksgiving as our gift.

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "In the Spirit in the sanctuary" (Дꙋ́хомъ во ст҃и́лищи):*  
By the desire of love of wisdom, O father, thou didst circumcise the veil of thy soul, and thou wast shown to the world as a sun through wonders; and thou didst illumine the minds of the faithful, O divinely-wise one, initiate of the Trinity, O wise Basil, and minister of the Birthgiver of God. *(Twice)*

*Glory, and both now, of the Feast:*  
He that fulfilled the Law is circumcised in the flesh as an eight-day-old infant, the Creator of the ages; and as man He is wrapped in swaddling clothes, and is nourished with milk, He Who as God upholds all things by immeasurable power and lifts them up by His nod.

*At the Praises, Stichera to 6, Tone 5.*  
*Tone 5, Podoben: "Rejoice" (Ра́дꙋйся):*  
*Sticheron:*  
He endures circumcision in the flesh, Who was ineffably begotten as the Word of the Father without cutting or corruption, and as God from God, abiding in immutable Godhead; therefore having become under the Law, though above the Law, He delivers all from the curse of the Law, and grants blessing from on high. Therefore, praising His all-good condescension, we sing and gratefully glorify, entreating Him to grant great mercy unto our souls. *(Twice)*

*Sticheron:*  
Having become a son of God by grace through the regeneration of divine baptism, thou didst confess, O venerable one, the Son of God and Word, pre-eternal, to be God by nature and in truth, consubstantial and co-unoriginate with the Father; and by the brightness of thy words thou didst stop the unrestrained mouths of the heretics. Therefore thou hast also taken up thine abode in the heavenly kingdoms, reigning with Christ Who alone reigns by nature, Who richly dispenses great mercy unto the world.

*Sticheron:*  
Within the heavenly temple, as a sacred hierarch thou didst find room, clad with action and contemplation, the principles of wisdom, as with a holy vestment; and now serving as priest at the altar on high, O venerable one, and standing before God, and performing the immaterial service: graciously remember, O all-blessed Basil, those who celebrate thy sacred and all-honorable memory, praying Christ Who grants great mercy unto the world.

*Sticheron:*  
Wholly consecrated to God, and from childhood dedicated in every way [Fol. 9v]
*Month of January*

...being illumined with the rays of transcendent wisdom, thou didst elucidate the understanding of reality, clearly expounding and wisely proclaiming, establishing good order among things, a work of most divine knowledge. Therefore we proclaim thee as a divinely-speaking and divine teacher, and a radiant lamp of the Church, praying Christ Who grants great mercy unto the world.

*Sticheron:*  
Being established in the fear of God, thou didst understand the beginning of wisdom, O Basil;[^38] through wisdom and uprightness of life thou didst surpass fear, O father; and having mingled thyself with God through love, thou becamest most intimate unto Him. Therefore, having been instructed in divine statutes and judgments, thou didst teach the ways of men, and didst adorn the minds of the faithful, illuminating the assembly by spiritual ordinances. Pray Christ, therefore, to grant great mercy unto our souls.

*Glory, Tone 6:*  
Grace was poured out upon thy lips, venerable father, and thou becamest a shepherd of Christ's Church, teaching the rational sheep to believe in the consubstantial Trinity in one Godhead.

*Both now, Tone 8:*  
The Savior, condescending unto the human race, accepted wrapping in swaddling clothes; He did not abhor bodily circumcision, eight days old according to His Mother, unoriginate according to His Father. Unto Him, O ye faithful, let us cry aloud: Thou art our God, have mercy on us!

*Great Doxology.*  
*After the Trisagion, the Troparion of Basil; Glory, and both now, of the Feast. Litanies, and Dismissal.*  
*And the brethren are anointed with oil from the lamp of the Saint, if the superior wills, and we sing an idiomelon sticheron.*  
*At the First Hour, the Troparion of the Feast; Glory, of Basil; Both now, Theotokion of the Hours. After the Trisagion, the Kontakion of the Feast. And the rest, and the complete Dismissal.*  
*At the Hours, we say the Kontakia of the Feast and of the Saint, alternating them.*  
*At the Liturgy:*  
*The Beatitudes from the Canon of the Feast, Ode 3; and of the Saint, Ode 6.*  
*After the Little Entrance, the Troparion of the Feast and of the Saint; Glory, the Kontakion of the Saint; Both now, of the Feast.*  
*Prokeimenon, Tone 6: Save, O Lord, Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance.[^39] Verse: Unto Thee, O Lord, will I cry.[^40]*  
*And of the Saint, Tone 1: My mouth shall speak wisdom.[^41]*  
*Epistle to the Colossians, pericope 254 [Col. 2:8–12].[^42] And of the Saint, to the Hebrews, pericope 318 [Heb. 7:26–8:2].[^43]*  
*Alleluia, Tone 8: Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel.[^44] Verse: The mouth of the righteous shall meditate wisdom.[^45]*  
*Gospel according to Luke, pericope 6 [Luke 2:20–21, 40–52].[^46] And of the Saint, pericope* [Fol. 10r]
*Day 1*

...pericope 104 [John 10:9–16].[^47] And the rest. The Divine Liturgy of Basil the Great is celebrated. And instead of "It is truly meet," we sing: All of creation rejoices in thee.[^48]  
*Kinonikon:* Praise the Lord from the heavens.[^49] *Another:* In everlasting remembrance shall the righteous be.[^50]

*If the Circumcision of the Lord and of Saint Basil the Great occur on Sunday:*[^51]  
*Mark:*  
*We celebrate a vigil. At Small Vespers, the resurrection stichera as usual. At the Aposticha, one resurrection sticheron of the Tone. Then the aposticha stichera of Basil from Great Vespers, Tone 1, idiomela, with their refrains. Glory, Tone 6: Grace was poured out: Both now: The all-good God was not ashamed: After Our Father, the resurrection troparion; Glory, of the Saint; Both now, of the Feast. And dismissal.*  
*At Great Vespers: At "Lord, I have cried," we sing 3 resurrection stichera, and 3 of the Feast, and 4 of the Saint. Glory, of the Saint: Lover of wisdom; Both now, Dogmatikon Theotokion of the Tone (Tone 1). Entrance. Prokeimenon. And the 3 readings. At the Litiya, the sticheron of the temple; and of Saint Basil. Glory, of the Saint; Both now, of the Feast. At the Aposticha, stichera of the Octoechos; Glory, of the Saint; Both now, of the Feast. At the blessing of loaves, the troparion of the Saint twice, and Rejoice, O Virgin Birthgiver of God once; and reading from the Apostolic Epistles.*  
*At Matins: At "God is the Lord," the resurrection troparion twice; Glory, of the Saint; Both now, of the Feast. After the kathismata, the resurrection sessional hymns with their theotokia; and reading in the Commentary Gospel, Sunday before Theophany. After the Polyeleos, the troparia: The assembly of angels; and the Hypakoe of the Tone, and all the sessional hymns of the Saint, one after the other. Glory, the sessional hymn after the Polyeleos; Both now, of the Feast. And reading in the Theologian, the Funeral Oration on Basil the Great.[^52] The Anavathmoi and the Prokeimenon of the Tone. Let every breath. Resurrection Gospel. Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ; and Psalm 50. Resurrection sticheron. Canon: the resurrection canon with its heirmos to 4; and of the Feast to 4; and of the Saint to 6. Katavasia: The Lord mighty in battles uncovered the bottom of the deep; and He marches over the surging deep:[^53] each choir sings its own heirmos. After Ode 3, the kontakion of the Feast, and the sessional hymn of the Saint twice; Glory, and both now, of the Feast. After Ode 6, the kontakion of the Saint, and the ikos; and we read the Prologue. At Ode 9 we sing "More honorable." But the refrains of the Feast and of the Saint we do not sing. Resurrection exapostilarion; Glory, of the Saint; Both now, of the Feast. At the Praises, 4 resurrection stichera, and 4 of the Saint from the prosomoia, with his special refrains. Glory, the evangelical sticheron; Both now: Most blessed art thou: Great Doxology. Resurrection troparion. Litanies, and dismissal* [Fol. 10v]
*Month of January*

*...and dismissal. And the Catechesis of Theodore the Studite.[^54] Oil is also given as usual from the lamp of the Saint. And procession into the narthex, and the First Hour. And the final dismissal. At the Hours, the resurrection troparion; Glory, of the Feast; and both now, Theotokion of the Hours. After the Trisagion, the kontakion of the Feast. At the Third Hour, the resurrection troparion; Glory, of the Saint; and both now, Theotokion of the Hours. After the Trisagion, we say the kontakia of the Saint and of the Feast, alternating them.*  
*At the Liturgy:*  
*The Beatitudes of the Tone to 4; and of the Feast, Ode 3, to 4; and of the Saint, Ode 6, to 4. After the Entrance, the troparion of the resurrection, and of the Feast, and of the Saint; Glory, the kontakion of the Saint; Both now, of the Feast.*

*Epistle of the Sunday before the Enlightenment: To Timothy, pericope 298 [2 Tim. 4:5–8].[^58] Another Epistle, to the Colossians, pericope 254 [Col. 2:8–12].[^59]*

*Sunday before Theophany: Prokeimenon, Tone 6: Save, O Lord, Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance.[^69] Verse: Unto Thee, O Lord, will I cry, O my God.[^70] Epistle to Timothy, pericope 298 [2 Tim. 4:5–8].[^71] Alleluia, Tone 8: God be merciful unto us.[^72] Gospel according to Mark, pericope 1 [Mark 1:1–8].[^73] Kinonikon: Praise the Lord from the heavens.[^74]*

*The Second Day of the Month of January:*
*Forefeast of the Enlightenment [Theophany]. And the commemoration of our father among the saints, Sylvester, Pope of Rome.*  
*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera, Tone 4.*  
*Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*  
*Sticheron:*  
Let us devoutly proclaim in advance songs of the forefeast of the honorable baptism of our God; for behold, He desires as man [Fol. 11r]
*Day 2*

...as man in the flesh to come unto His Forerunner, and to ask for the saving baptism, for the edification of all who with faith are holily enlightened and made partakers of the Spirit.

*Sticheron:*  
Christ is shown, God is manifest, as David most clearly forescribed; and He comes unto His servant asking for baptism.[^75] O river Jordan, be filled with gladness! Let the earth and the sea, the mountains and hills, and the hearts of men now leap for joy, receiving the noetic Light!

*Sticheron:*  
The river of peace, and the torrent of delight as it is written,[^76] O Almighty One: how shall the river streams receive Thee, O Lord, as Thou goest up naked, Who clothest heaven with clouds, and didst strip bare all the malice of the enemy, and clothest the earthborn with incorruption?

*Other Stichera of the Saint, Tone 8.*  
*Tone 8, Podoben: "O marvelous wonder" (Ѡ҆ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесє̀):*  
*Sticheron:*  
O father, hierarch Sylvester, sacredly enlightened with the light of the priesthood, thou didst enlighten the faithful with radiant teachings to honor the Trinity consubstantial in essence, and thou didst drive away the darkness of heresies. Therefore today we joyfully celebrate thy radiant memory in clarity.

*Sticheron:*  
O God-bearing father Sylvester, thou wast shown to be a pillar of fire, holily leading the sacred assembly; and an overshadowing cloud, delivering the faithful from Egyptian delusion, and leading them unto the divine land always by thine unerring teachings. Therefore we honor thy glorious and all-sacred memory.

*Sticheron:*  
O God-speaking father Sylvester, by the streams of thy prayers thou didst firmly shut up the manifold dragon;[^77] moved by holiness, thou didst bring the multitude of the pagans unto Him, and didst humble the insolence of the Jews, working great wonders openly before them. Therefore we honor and bless thee.

*Glory, and both now, Tone 6:*  
Christ, the Truth, comes to the Jordan to be baptized by John, and He says unto him: "I have need to be baptized of thee, and comest thou to Me?" "I, who am grass, dare not touch the Fire; do Thou sanctify me, O Master, by Thy divine manifestation!"

*At the Aposticha, idiomela stichera, Tone 4.*  
*By John the Monk [of Damascus]:*  
*Sticheron:*  
Radiant indeed was the bygone feast, but more radiant still is the one that is coming, O Savior! For that one had an angel as herald, and this one found the Forerunner as preparer; that one, by shed blood [Fol. 11v]
*Month of January*

...by shed blood, Bethlehem wept as childless; but this one reveals the font with blessed waters to be rich in children. Then a star announced unto the Magi; but now the Father hath revealed Thee unto the world. O Thou Who wast incarnate and comest again visibly: Lord, glory to Thee!

*Tone 2. Verse:*  
*Therefore will I remember Thee from the land of Jordan and of the Hermonites.[^78]*  
*By Andrew of Jerusalem [of Crete]:*  
*Sticheron:*  
Again my Jesus is cleansed in the Jordan, or rather He cleanses our sins; for He comes truly unto baptism, desiring to wash away Adam's handwriting.[^79] And He says unto John: "Come, serve with Me, O baptizer, at the beginning of this strange mystery; come, stretch forth thy hand quickly, and touch the head of Him that crushed the serpent's head, and opened paradise, which transgression shut through the serpent's deceit, by the eating of the tree of old!"

*Tone 3. Verse:*  
*The waters saw Thee, O God, the waters saw Thee, and were afraid.[^80]*  
*Sticheron:*  
Radiant indeed was the bygone feast, and more glorious still is the present day! In that one the Magi worshiped the Savior; in this one a glorious servant baptizes the Master. There the shepherds piping beheld and marveled; here the Father's voice proclaimed the Only-Begotten Son.

*Glory, and both now, in the same Tone [Tone 3]:*  
*Sticheron:*  
Come, all ye faithful, having left the Judean country, let us pass over into the wilderness of the Jordan, and let us see today Him Who appeared in the flesh for our sake, asking for baptism in the streams of the Jordan! The Baptizer shrank back and cried aloud with fear: "I dare not lay a hand of clay upon the Fire! The Jordan and the sea fled, O Savior, and turned back;[^81] and how shall I lay my hand upon Thy head, before Whom the Seraphim tremble? The Jordan fled when Elisha received Elijah's mantle:[^82] how shall it not sink into the chasm and deeps, seeing Thee naked in the streams? And how shall I not be wholly consumed by the fire that flames forth from Thee?" "Why delayest thou, O Baptizer, to baptize my Lord?" the Jordan cries unto John: "Why dost thou prevent the cleansing of many? He hath sanctified all creation; suffer Him to sanctify me also and the nature of waters, for unto this He hath appeared!"

*Troparion of Sylvester, Tone 4:*  
A rule of faith, and an image of meekness, a teacher of temperance did the reality of things show thee forth unto thy flock; therefore by humility thou didst acquire lofty things, by poverty riches [Fol. 12r]
*Day 2*

...O father Sylvester: pray Christ God that our souls may be saved.

*Glory, and both now, of the Forefeast, in the same Tone [Tone 4]:*  
*Troparion:*  
Make ready, O Zebulun, and adorn thyself, O Naphtali![^83] O river Jordan, stand still and receive with leaping the Master Who comes to be baptized! Rejoice, Adam with the foremother; hide not yourselves as in paradise of old; for seeing you naked He hath appeared, that He may clothe you in the first robe: Christ hath appeared, desiring to renew all creation!

*At Compline we sing the Triodion [canon of three odes]: the heirmoi twice, the troparia to 6, and at the end both choirs sing the heirmos together. But if the Triodion has two heirmoi, we sing the heirmos of the first author twice, and the troparia of both authors to 6; and at the end both choirs sing the heirmos of the second canon together. In this manner we sing the canon and heirmoi also at the other Complines.*  
*Triodion, whose acrostic is... For the second:*  
*Tone 2. Ode 1. Heirmos:*  
Unto Him Who by His divine command dried up the impassable surging sea, and guided the Israelite people to pass through on foot, let us sing unto the Lord, for He is gloriously glorified.[^84]  
*Refrain:* Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.  
*Troparion:*  
The timeless condescension of the Creator, having first shone forth from the Virgin, hath illumined the world; and now Christ Himself, performing another mystery, comes to the Jordan unto a strange regeneration for the earthborn.  
*Refrain:* Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.  
*Troparion:*  
Serving a fearful work, the Forerunner now goes before to the Jordan, the voice of the Word, enriching impoverished Adam with Godhead; for Christ comes, rich in the Spirit, with the gift of baptism.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*  
The fire was struck with fear before the pious youths, who were conformed in soul to their undefiled bodies; and the fire fed on boundless matter drew back, unwearied; but as the flame died down, an eternal song was sung: All ye works, bless the Lord, and highly exalt Him unto all ages.[^85]  
*Troparion:*  
"Then shall I know you as My chosen vessels, if the seal of My gift is imaged in you, flashing forth the thrice-radiant light unto baptism," Christ the Word said unto those who abide in the sloth of despondency: "for herein do I grant the way of salvation, and bestow the life of freedom upon all."  
*Troparion:*  
The contrary order of natural things is accomplished in thee [Fol. 12v]
*Month of January*

...is accomplished in thee now: for I, who am less, have need of the blessing of thee that art better. Therefore I fear to touch Thy head, the Forerunner cried unto the Redeemer: for it is not fitting that fire should draw near unto grass; do Thou rather sanctify me, Thy servant.

*Another Diodion [canon of two odes].*  
*Whose acrostic is... For the third:*  
*In the same Tone [Tone 2]. Heirmos:*  
Unto the tyrant's decree...  
*Troparion:*  
Having shaken off the soul-sleep of despondency, with vigilance of heart let us cry aloud unto Him that comes to the streams to cleanse souls: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!  
*Troparion:*  
May the action of the soul be made fit in us in highest contemplation, that having appeared doubly radiant, we all may appear before the Master Who cleanses all with divine streams!  
*Troparion:*  
Having adorned the talent with active word in twofold labor, with faith as servants let us bring it unto the Master Who gave it, as He comes to be baptized for the renewal of souls.[^86]  
*Instead of "Glory", we say:*  
*We bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord.*  
*And to the last troparion we say: Both now.*  
*Then coming together we sing:*  
*We praise, we bless, we worship the Lord, singing and highly exalting Him unto all ages.*  
*And we sing the Heirmos:*  
Not submitting unto the tyrant's decree, the three venerable youths, cast into the furnace, confessed God, singing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*  
Thou hast magnified Christ, Who brought forth Thee, O Birthgiver of God, from whom our Creator clothed Himself in a body of like passions with us, which looses our offenses; blessing her, all generations, we magnify Thee.  
*Troparion:*  
Having shaken off all passionate defilement, worthily receive mentally the image of divine baptism; for the Creator comes to grant a strange cleansing, being baptized in the streams, and to show a new change unto all.  
*Troparion:*  
Gazing upon Christ Who humbles Himself willingly, even unto the form of a servant, let us now humble ourselves under His mighty hand, being lifted up in spirit; that we may honor Him Who is baptized with pure deeds.[^87]  
*Another. Heirmos:*  
Him Whom nothing can contain...  
*Troparion:*  
Having laid aside all sinful gloom, pure, let us appear before the Master Who cleanses all with divine streams [Fol. 13r]
*Day 2*

Unto Christ Who comes to be baptized in the river Jordan, come, let us draw near, having cleansed ourselves with streams of tears!

*Instead of "It is truly meet," we sing the Heirmos:*  
*Heirmos:*  
Thee that containedst in the womb the uncontainable God, and broughtest forth joy unto the world, we praise, O Virgin Birthgiver of God.  
*And a bow [prostration].*  
*After the Trisagion, the Kontakion of the Forefeast.*  
*Thus we say at Compline until the Feast.*  
*At Matins: At "God is the Lord," the Troparion of the Forefeast twice; Glory, of the Saint; Both now, of the Forefeast.*  
*After the first stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 1.*  
*Tone 1, Podoben: "Thy tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й сп҃се):*  
*Sessional Hymn:*  
Clothed in my poverty, O my Jesus, Thou comest forward, mingling Thyself with servants, and asking for baptism from a servant, O Lover of mankind! Therefore, seeing Thee, John cried aloud: "How shall I baptize Thee, Who hast no defilement at all, O all-good God?"  
*Glory, and both now, in the same Podoben:*  
*Sessional Hymn:*  
Christ comes forward in His goodness unto the river streams of Jordan, and in them He desires to work our renewal by grace. Receive Him joyfully, O divine Forerunner, and wash Him in the waters Who willed it so, the only Lover of mankind!  
*After the second stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4.*  
*Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*  
*Sessional Hymn:*

*Sticheron of the Prophet:*

*Other Stichera of the Martyr, in the same Tone [Tone 8].*  
*Tone 8, Podoben: "O marvelous wonder" (Ѡ҆ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*  
Seeing the abiding mist of deceit, thou didst flee far away, O passion-bearer Gordius, awaiting God; and tested by many pains, and vexed by hunger, as a champion knowing his own strength, thou didst rush unsummoned against the adversaries.[^153]  

Relying upon these things, thou camest unto the multitude of the adversaries, O all-glorious Gordius, counting the assembly of the lawless as nothing; and standing in the midst as a self-praising herald, with a loud voice thou didst proclaim Christ the Creator and Lord, co-unoriginate with the Father, and equal in honor and co-everlasting with the honorable Spirit.[^154]  

For having thy head severed with the sword, thou didst manifestly pass from life unto life, from death unto immortality, and from corruption unto incorruption, not waiting for nature's mortality, but led willingly to die. O thy struggles, O passion-bearer Gordius, by which, O martyr, thou didst magnify Christ, the only compassionate One!  

*Glory, and both now, Tone 6.*  
*By John the Monk [John Damascene]:*  
O marvelous wonder! He that baptizes with the Holy Spirit and with fire comes unto the Jordan to be baptized by John: God not naked, nor mere man, but in two natures, the one and same Only-begotten Son. Seeking baptism as man from a mortal, yet as God taking away the sin of the world, and granting great mercy unto all.[^155]  

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 6.*  
*Tone 6, Podoben: "Having been three days" (Трїдне́венъ):*  
Behold, the illumination of the faithful, behold, our cleansing is about to be in the river streams, that He may wash away the defilement of human malice, and renew us who are crushed.  

*Verse: Therefore will I remember Thee from the land of Jordan and Hermon.[^156]*  
When Thy Forerunner saw Thee coming, O Lord, and asking to be baptized by him, he cried with fear: "O my God, my Creator, how shall I baptize [Fol. 19r]
*Day 3*

...the Undefiled One?"[^157]  

*Verse: The waters saw Thee, O God, the waters saw Thee and were afraid.[^158]*  
Let us, the faithful, gather spiritually at the streams of the Jordan, that we may plainly see a great wonder: for the Creator of all hath appeared visible, and is come to be baptized!  

*Glory, and both now, Tone 5:*  
Unto the river Jordan Christ our God comes to baptism, willing to cleanse us from our iniquities by His manifestation, as He alone is good and the Lover of mankind.  

*Troparion of the Martyr, Tone 4:*  
Thy martyr, O Lord, Gordius, in his suffering received an incorruptible crown from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength, he cast down the torturers, and crushed the powerless insolence of the demons. By his supplications, save our souls![^159]  

*Troparion of the Forefeast, in the same Tone [Tone 4]:*  
Make ready, O Zebulun, and adorn thyself, O Naphtali! O river Jordan, halt; receive, leaping for joy, the Master Who comes to be baptized! Be glad, Adam with our first mother; hide not yourselves as in paradise of old: for seeing you naked, He hath appeared, that He may clothe you in the first garment; Christ hath appeared, willing to renew the whole creation.[^160]

*Troparion:*  
A snare was Herod's device, who sought to attain security by unlawfully slaughtering children; for Christ our Redeemer bestows life upon all, being baptized without slaughter.[^162]  

*Troparion:*  
Cruel was Herod's counsel, who first slew the age of infants, filling Bethlehem with blood; but now Christ comes to make children of the Church by baptism.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*  
When the tyrant's voice prevailed, the furnace was heated sevenfold of old; wherein the youths were not burned, having trampled upon the king's decree, but cried aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages![^165]  

*Troparion:*  
Drawing springs of tears from our eyes, ye faithful, let us cleanse every defilement of the soul, and in light we shall see Light, as Christ comes to be baptized; unto Whom the Father bears witness from heaven, and the coming of the Holy Spirit shines forth in the form of a dove.[^166]  

*Troparion:*  
Christ comes taking away every tear from every face, painlessly calming the painful diseases of souls with water, and renewing fallen men unto regeneration, who exalt Him supreme unto the ages.[^167]  

*Troparion:*  
Souls are sacredly ministered to by the God-given bath of baptism, and by the fire of the Spirit which cleanses passions and consumes all the matter of defiled malice; granting grace to cry aloud in compunction: We exalt Thee supreme, O Christ, unto the ages!  

*Another [Triodion]. Heirmos:*  
Unto the pillar of malice...  

*Troparion:*  
Having shaken off the sleep of malice from the eyelids of our souls, ye faithful, let us remove deceit from our hearts, and with warm tears wash our understanding, that we may be shown forth as beholders of Him Who hath appeared, glorifying Christ unto the ages.  

*Troparion:*  
Let us not bring in a defiled word of evil thoughts; but having meditated upon the divine Word, let us bring hymns of praise unto the Word Who for our sake appeared in the flesh, and enlightens those sitting in darkness; Whom all creation blesses, glorifying Him unto the ages.  

*Troparion:*  
The depth of wisdom of the hidden mystery is now revealed unto men; the abyss of God's judgments is now opened unto the faithful, as God hath appeared with flesh upon earth for the renewal of the human race; Whom all creation blesses, glorifying Him unto the ages.[^168]

*We praise, bless, and worship the Lord, singing and exalting Him supreme unto all ages.*  
*Heirmos:*  
All of us having mocked the pillar of the malice of cruel Herod, come unto the Jordan, let us go, ye faithful, that we may behold Christ the Redeemer, baptized in the flesh in the streams by the Forerunner; Whom all creation blesses, glorifying Him unto the ages.[^170]  

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*  
With pure souls and undefiled lips, come, let us magnify the undefiled and most pure Mother of Emmanuel; offering through her prayer unto Him Who was born of her: Spare our souls, O Christ God, and save us![^171]  

*Troparion:*  
Let no one be uncomprehending and ungrateful toward Christ; despising His longsuffering forbearance and goodness, let him not disdain it; but with fear and joy let us serve Him, singing: Spare our souls, O Christ God, and save us![^172]  

*Troparion:*  
The Forerunner says unto the disobedient people: "Who has warned you to flee from the wrath to come, O generation of vipers? Produce therefore fruits worthy of repentance,[^173] crying aloud: Spare our souls, O Christ God, and save us!"  

*Troparion:*  
O the audacity of blind folly! For while the foreigners worshipped Christ as Redeemer, honoring Him with gifts, His own people madly sought to slay Him Who was born; spare our souls, O Christ God, and save us![^174]  

*Another [Triodion]. Heirmos:*  
*More honorable than the Cherubim:*  
Correcting now the all-destroying fall of Adam, the new Adam has appeared, granting the freedom of renewed being most gloriously by baptism.[^175]  

*Troparion:*  
Fulfilling the Law and the Prophets, and accomplishing all righteousness, the Savior of all now bows beneath the hand of a servant, snatching man away from the bondage of the enemy.  

*Troparion:*  
Unto the nations the great light of God, unto the darkened a divine dawn has shone forth; unto those sitting of old in the shadow of death, Christ the Sun of glory has shone forth.[^176]  

*Troparion:*  
The angelic hosts surrounded the Redeemer being baptized in the Jordan, and with trembling sang of the great mystery, His unutterable condescension.

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*  
The cleft [rock] cut through the uncut [sea], and the sun saw the earth which it had not seen; the water drowned the fierce enemy, and Israel traversed the impassable path; and the song was sung: Let us sing unto the Lord, for gloriously has He been glorified![^185]

Rejoicing with the celestial choir, and feasting and making glad together with them, and worthily filled with divine illumination, O God-inspired one: by thy prayer preserve those celebrating thy venerable memory with faith, singing unto the Lord.  
*Troparion:*  
Radiant with the angel-like beauty and goodness of thy soul, and also in bodily manner, thou didst receive brightly the supreme dawn of divine radiance, O God-proclaimer; and rejoicing thou didst cry aloud: Let us sing unto the Lord, for gloriously has He been glorified!  
*Troparion:*  
Living thy life blamelessly and being adorned with the form of good adornment, and cleansing thyself with good manners, O all-blessed one, thou wast called the prophet of true piety: Let us sing unto the Lord, for gloriously has He been glorified!  
*Theotokion:*  
Pure Mother of God the Almighty, Lady who didst spring from the royal tribe, and having born in the flesh beyond nature the One God Who reigns over all: save me from perils, who sing unto thy Son: For gloriously has He been glorified!

*Theotokion:*

Therefore having boldly rebuked the deceit, thou wast beheaded with the sword, O glorious one, and didst depart unto endless life, O all-praised one: Entreat Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who honor thy holy memory with love![^207]

*Kontakion of the Forefeast:*  
Being today in the streams of the Jordan, the Lord cries aloud unto John: "Fear not to baptize Me, for I am come to save Adam the first-formed!"[^247]  
*Ikos:*  
I do not compel thee, O Baptist, to go beyond the boundaries; I say not unto thee: "Tell Me what thou sayest unto the lawless, and teachest sinners"; only baptize Me in silence, and awaiting what comes from baptism: for on this account thou shalt receive a dignity which was not unto the angels, for I will make thee greater than all the prophets: for none of them saw Me openly, but in figures, shadows, and enigmas; but thou hast seen Me standing before thee: for I am come to save Adam the first-formed![^248]  
*Ode 7. Heirmos:*  
The God-wise youths worshipped not the creature rather than the Creator; but manfully trampling upon the threat of fire, they rejoiced, singing: Blessed art Thou, O all-hymned Lord and God of our fathers![^249]  
*Troparion:*  
Crushed by transgressions, and lying in the darkness of transgression, O Lord, having mercy, Thou hast had compassion on me in Thy goodness; and Thou comest, O Master, to be baptized in Jordan's waters.[^250]  
*Troparion:*  
"What is this strange vision?" the angelic choirs cried aloud: "He Who made lakes and rivers by His command, comes to be clothed with Jordan's streams; for by this He renews Adam!"  
*Troparion:*  
Unutterable is the height, and measureless the depth of Thy dispensation, O Master, surpassing all comprehension of the mind: how Thou cleansest those on earth with water and the Holy Spirit![^251]  
*Another [Canon of the Prophet]. Heirmos:*  
The Hebrew youths in the furnace boldly trampled upon the flame, and turned the fire into dew, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages![^252]  
*Troparion:*  
Thou didst foretell the all-honorable coming of Thee Who rulest over all, O glorious prophet Malachi, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages![^253]  
*Troparion:*  
Receive the glorious Prophet Malachi who prays unto Thee, O Bountiful One, for those who piously sing and cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages!  
*Theotokion:*  
Unto all me, the whole of me, without confusion according to hypostasis, Thou didst unite Thyself, O Word of God, having clothed Thyself in me from the pure Virgin, O Bountiful One: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages![^254]  
*Another [Canon of the Martyr]. Heirmos:*  
Thou Who didst bedew the youths in the furnace, and didst preserve the Virgin who gave Thee birth after childbirth: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^255]  

[Fol. 24v]
*Month of January*

...having attained the glory of martyrdom, thou keepest festival with the angels, O crown-bearer, crying aloud unto Christ: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers![^256]  
*Troparion:*  
Having pious boldness, thou didst rebuke the impious, singing with a loud voice: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers![^257]  
*Troparion:*  
Pray now that they may be delivered from transgressions, who honor thy venerable memory with faith, and sing with a loud voice: Blessed is the God of our fathers!  
*Theotokion:*  
Thou washest away the home-grown thorns of sin by the raining down of thy healings, O blessed and all-pure Birthgiver of God, who without seed gavest birth to God.[^258]  
*Ode 8. Heirmos:*  
The birthgiving of the Birthgiver of God saved the pious youths in the furnace: then prefigured, but now in actuality, it rouses the whole universe to sing unto Thee: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages![^259]  
*Troparion:*  
The voice of the Parent from on high bears witness unto the Son consubstantial, Who enters into the waters, and sends forth Thy blessing through them, O blessed Christ; and the Holy Spirit proclaims Thee unto all as God incarnate.[^260]  
*Troparion:*  
Keep festival, O creation, having recognized the holy divine manifestation! Sing, ye angels; be glad, O sea; leap for joy, ye lakes and fountains; and rivers, mystically clap your hands with songs, as Christ stands before you with blessings, enlightening you![^261]  
*Troparion:*  
We sing in praise unto the Lord Who has appeared upon the waters, and by them has renewed our brokenness, and crushed the heads of the invisible enemies; and we cry aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages![^262]  
*Troparion:*  
O wonder of wonders! How can He Who is the God of all creation be created, and be renewed from the Birthgiver of God, and renew by water, and rebuild us with water and the marvelous renewal of the Spirit, as the only Benefactor?[^263]  
*Another [Canon of the Prophet]. Heirmos:*  
Having become victors over the tormentor and the flame by Thy grace, strictly cleaving unto Thy commandments, the youths cried aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^264]  
*Troparion:*  
Having become estranged from every material manifestation, O sacredly revealed one, thou hast appeared as an undefiled mirror of divine radiance, singing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him supreme unto the ages.[^265]  
*Troparion:*  
Thou wast a beholder of unutterable glory, and of heavenly mysteries [O blessed initiate] [Fol. 25r]
*Day 3*

...having become a preacher, singing unceasingly: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him supreme unto the ages.[^266]  
*Theotokion:*  
Having known thee as the Mother of Life and Parent of God, with orthodox faith we all call thee blessed, O Virgin Mother, blessing together thy most pure birthgiving, and honorably exalting it unto all ages.[^267]  
*Another [Canon of the Martyr]. Heirmos:*  
The God-proclaiming youths in the furnace, trampling upon the flame with the fire, sang: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^268]  
*Troparion:*  
The grace that accompanied thee, having invisibly enlightened thee, O martyr, filled thee with valor, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^269]  
*Troparion:*  
Hastening with a swift course, O sufferer, thou didst attain unto the desired goal of the Kingdom, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!  
*Troparion:*  
Unto never-ending ages abides the glory and immortal praise of Thy martyrs: Let all us works bless Thee as the Lord.[^270]  
*Theotokion:*  
Having conceived the bodiless Word incarnate, O pure one, thou didst reverse Eve's ancient curse, having given birth unto a blessing for the world.[^271]  
*Ode 9. Heirmos:*  
Let every earthborn mortal leap for joy, enlightened in spirit; and let the nature of the bodiless minds keep festival, honoring the sacred festival of the Mother of God, and let it cry aloud: Rejoice, O all-blessed Birthgiver of God, pure Ever-virgin![^272]  
*Troparion:*  
Behold the Lamb Who takes away the transgressions of mankind! He is come and stands before the servant, asking for baptism; He stands in the form of a servant, seeking to free those enslaved by the deceiver, who had lost their first beauty.[^273]  
*Troparion:*  
God has manifestly appeared, incarnate out of goodness; He Who truly clothes Himself with clouds comes to be clothed with Jordan's waters: let us all now with joy celebrate beforehand His honorable manifestation.  
*Troparion:*  
Leap for joy, and prepare beforehand to yield water flowing into life eternal, O Jordan! Ye rivers, dance, seeing now the stream of delight entering into Jordan's streams, and drying up the outpouring of malice![^274]  
*Troparion:*  
The saving day has dawned upon us who always slept in the night of grievous evils: for Christ the Lord is come, being the noetic Sun of righteousness, willing to bow His head unto the servant, and to be baptized in the flesh.[^275]  
*Theotokion:*  
The Cherubim and all heavenly nature are filled with awe, O all-immaculate one, at the comprehension-surpassing dignity of thy precious [Fol. 25v]
*Month of January*

...birthgiving, having made Himself like unto us in unutterable tenderheartedness, and having been baptized in the flesh, Whose divine manifestation we now all celebrate, rejoicing.[^276]  
*Another [Canon of the Prophet]. Heirmos:*  
Every ear was struck with fear at the ineffable condescension of God: how the Most High willingly descended even unto flesh from the virginal womb, having become man; therefore, O most pure Birthgiver of God, we the faithful magnify thee.[^277]  
*Troparion:*  
The divinely radiant and honorable feast of the prophet has arrived, illuminating with prophetic splendors those who come in faith and sing, and pouring forth healings unto the souls of all, and enlightening them as God-wise.[^278]  
*Troparion:*  
Preserve Thy Church with Thy sovereign, life-originating right hand, O Much-merciful One, through the supplications of Thy pleased-one, who foretold unto us Thy divine incarnation, whereby salvation has shone forth and redemption unto souls.  
*Theotokion:*  
Ripe do I reap life, unharmed by the tree of knowledge; for thou, O all-immaculate one, didst bud forth Christ the Tree of Life, Who showed the entrances of life unto all; therefore as the all-pure Birthgiver of God, we the faithful proclaim thee.[^279]  
*Another [Canon of the Martyr]. Heirmos:*  
The birthgiving of the Ever-virgin, prefigured on the mountain unto the lawgiver in fire and the bush, for the salvation of us the faithful, with unceasing hymns do we magnify.[^280]  
*Troparion:*  
Pray unto God to be merciful unto those who honor thee with faith, and who celebrate thy light-bearing and honorable feast, O Gordius, adornment of martyrs!  
*Troparion:*  
Now being filled with incorruptible food, and the vision of God, O Gordius, and with the never-setting light, in the eternal dwellings thou receivest the reward of thy struggles.[^281]  
*Troparion:*  
Having despised transient, corruptible, and trampled glory, O God-wise martyr, thou now truly enjoyest ever-existing glory and joy, standing before the eternal throne.  
*Theotokion:*  
Having been saved, O Virgin, from the first curse by thy divine birthgiving, singing worthily with unceasing voices we cry aloud: Rejoice, O Birthgiver of God, our hope![^282]  
*Exapostilarion, Tone 3, Podoben: "In the Spirit in the sanctuary" (Дꙋ́хомъ во свѧти́лищи):*  
Giving heed, having left the most glorious wonder, let us run unto the Jordan with fervent soul, and there we shall behold a fearful mystery: for my Christ has stood naked in a manner befitting God, clothing me in the garment of the Heavenly Kingdom.[^283]  
*Glory, both now, the same.*

*Sticheron 1:*  
Having heaven as His throne, the Master came upon earth, incarnate of the Virgin; and having stood at the Jordan, He asks for the cleansing of all from John. All ye families of the earth, let us sing unto Him: Blessed art Thou Who hast appeared, O our God, glory to Thee![^285]  
*Sticheron 2:*  
Christ is come unto the streams of the Jordan, asking for baptism, He Who cleanses sins. Let all the earth leap for joy, let the heavens be glad: Rejoice, O church of the gentiles, having been betrothed unto the King, cry aloud in faith: Blessed art Thou Who hast appeared, O our God, glory to Thee!  
*Sticheron 3:*  
Let the mountains drop down the sweetness of gladness; mystically clap your hands now, ye nations; let the wilderness blossom; O Jordan, receive Him; come, O Baptist; serve the mystery of the Redeemer, rejoicing! Ye people, let us sing: Blessed art Thou Who hast appeared, O our God, glory to Thee![^286]  
*Sticheron 4:*  
The Light from Light, Who shone forth before the ages, has appeared unto those sitting in night, and has cleansed the darkness of sin, and enlightened: dance, O Adam, and be glad, O Eve: Christ the redemption is come! O forefather, cry aloud: Blessed art Thou Who hast appeared, O our God, glory to Thee![^287]  
*Glory, Tone and Podoben the same:*  
A Star from Jacob has shone forth unto the world; and having taken upon Himself the burning sin of men, He buries it in the waters of the Jordan, shining with the radiance of Godhead, and granting the enlightenment of the knowledge of God unto the nations: Blessed art Thou Who hast appeared, O our God, glory to Thee![^288]  
*Both now, Podoben the same:*  
Having become the fulfiller of the Law according to the flesh, Christ is come unto the Jordan to accomplish the beginning of salvation, as He is tenderhearted; and He bows His head unto the Baptist, who cries aloud in faith. Ye people, let us cry: Blessed art Thou Who hast appeared, O our God, glory to Thee!

*Other Stichera of the Venerable Father, Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*[^302]  
*Sticheron 1:*  
When thou didst wound thy soul with divine desire, O all-blessed one, rejoicing thou didst take up thy cross and follow Christ; and having put to death the carnal mind through abstinence, thou didst receive the living operation of the Spirit, to loose the winter of infirmities by the warmth of thine acceptable prayers: therefore with one accord we call thee blessed.[^303]  
*Sticheron 2:*  
When by fervent prayers and most steadfast fasting thou didst cleanse the contemplative faculty of the soul, O father, thou becamest a temple of the Thrice-radiant Godhead; and having received the holy divine anointing of priesthood, thou didst enter into the inner sanctuary, sacrificing Him Who was slain for thy sake in unutterable condescension.[^304]  
*Sticheron 3:*  
Meek and guileless didst thou appear in integrity of character, O father Theoctistus; thou didst inherit truly the land of the meek, and being divinized through communion thou enjoyest the food, and joy, and true gladness; where remember unceasingly those who honor thee sincerely, and who celebrate thy divine falling asleep.[^305]  
*Glory, both now, Tone 3:*  
Fair indeed was the feast that has passed, but more glorious is the present day: in that one the Magi worshipped the Savior, but in this one the glorious servant baptizes the Master; there the shepherds playing on their pipes saw and were amazed, but here the Father's voice proclaimed the Only-begotten Son.[^306]

*Sticheron 1:*

*Verse: Therefore will I remember Thee from the land of Jordan, and of Hermonim.*  
*Sticheron 2:*

*Verse: The waters saw Thee, O God, the waters saw Thee and were afraid.*
