Christ the Truth comes unto the Jordan to be baptized by John, and he says unto Him: "I have need to be baptized by Thee, and comest Thou to me? I who am grass dare not touch the Fire: sanctify me, O Master, by Thy divine manifestation!"[^311]  
*Troparion of the Apostles, Tone 3:*  
O holy apostles, entreat the merciful God to grant remission of transgressions unto our souls.[^312]

Be glad, O Adam, with the first mother; hide not yourselves as in paradise of old: for seeing you naked, He has appeared, that He may clothe you in the first garment. Christ has appeared, willing to renew all creation![^313]

*Whose acrostic is: I sing the long song of Great Thursday. Tone 6. Heirmoi in pairs. Troparia on 6. Then the Heirmos by both choirs together.*[^314]  
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*  
The divided Red Sea is cleft, and the wave-nurturing deep is dried up; the same becoming at once passable unto the unarmed, and a grave unto the fully armed. And a God-fitting song was sung: Gloriously has Christ our God been glorified![^315]  
*Troparion:*  
The all-originating Cause and Giver of life, the immeasurable Wisdom of God, built a temple for Herself from the pure, unwedded Mother; and now She comes unto the streams of the Jordan, enriching the earthborn with Godhead unto renewal.[^316]  
*Troparion:*  
Initiating into mysteries, the Wisdom of God summons all those from the nations unto the light, who formerly lay in the unilluminated darkness of ignorance, leading them up into the knowledge of the truth, unto light through baptism, for those who cleanse their hearts and recognize in spirit.[^317]  
*Troparion:*  
Let us now listen unto the prophetic voices accomplished in the Spirit: for He Who baptizes in the Spirit and with fire, Christ, goes unto the Jordan. Come unto Him and be enlightened, and your faces shall not be put to shame.[^318]  
*Ode 3. Heirmos:*  
Being Lord of all and Creator God, the Passionless One having impoverished Himself [Fol. 28r]
*Day 4*

...united what He had made unto Himself; and by the streams wherein Thou wast pleased to come, being Thyself, Thou didst proclaim unto the people: "Draw the water of life, and be established in faith!"[^319]  
*Troparion:*  
Thou comest, O Savior, to bestow the grace of baptism that looses both souls and bodies together; therefore Thou now grantest unto us also grace upon grace, crying: "Draw the water of life, and be established in faith!"[^320]  
*Troparion:*  
The foolish man, not knowing God, is corrupted; for by unseemly undertakings he is deprived of every good thing, and falls away from all salvation: whose portion let all of us who know Christ escape![^321]  
*Ode 4. Heirmos:*  
Foreseeing the ineffable depth of Thy mystery, O Christ, the Prophet proclaimed: "Thou hast established the mighty grace of baptism unto all who receive it with faith, for the redemption of our sins."[^322]  
*Troparion:*  
Unto baptism that gushes forth remission of the earthquake unto mortals, Thou callest all who are burdened with transgressions, who have lived grievously in uncleanness, promising to grant them rest of soul, as Thou art compassionate.[^323]  
*Troparion:*  
Thou unitest Thyself unto my flesh, that Thou mayest bestow Thy Godhead upon me; for being the unchangeable image of Thy Father, Thou art contained beneath the hands of Thy creation, O Savior, having appeared as man without sin, by like cleansing like, O Word.[^324]  
*Troparion:*  
Drink, and anointing, and the Spirit of Thy seal of knowledge, O Savior, and the mystical gifts, and the worthy works of divine gifts: for the Father sent Thee, the Only-begotten, as a cleansing unto the world.[^325]  
*Ode 5. Heirmos:*  
Held fast now by the bond of fear, the Forerunner refuses to baptize, seeing Christ in reverent awe standing naked upon the water, Who covers the highest places with water.[^326]  
*Troparion:*  
Holding the uncontainable and highest water in the air, bridling the deeps and checking the seas, the Wisdom of God comes unto the Jordan, receiving baptism from the hand of the servant.[^327]  
*Troparion:*  
Having conformed Himself to human nature, Christ now comes to cleanse it by baptism; He Who encompasses the heaven with clouds and clothes Himself with light is seen naked in the streams of the Jordan; and He Who upholds all things is held by a hand.[^328]  
*Ode 6. Heirmos:*  
The lowest deep of sins has compassed me about, and no longer enduring the tempest, as Jonah unto the Master I cry [Fol. 28v]
*Month of January*

...unto Thee: Lead me up from corruption![^329]  
*Troparion:*  
Knowing Thee as Lord, the heavens declare Thy glory unto the earth at Thy birthgiving, O Savior; and now the Father proclaims Thee as the beloved Son being baptized.[^330]  
*Troparion:*  
Let everyone bearing defilement wash it away with drops of tears, and with trembling draw near unto Christ, hoping that by fire and the Divine Spirit He will cleanse our nature.[^331]  
*Ode 7. Heirmos:*  
The youths in Babylon feared not the flame of the furnace; but cast into the midst of the flame, being bedewed they sang: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers![^332]  
*Troparion:*  
Nodding the head unto enmity, let no one deceitfully move to render evil unto his neighbor, having wrongly felt evil for evil; but in love let us honor the Lord Who has appeared.[^333]  
*Troparion:*  
Ye who are Christ's friends, suffer a little together with Him Who armed Himself and comes to receive baptism, and has appeared in our image for cleansing, and for the redemption of transgressions.[^334]  
*Troparion:*  
"If anyone descends with Me and is buried with Me by baptism, with Me he shall enjoy glory and resurrection," Christ now proclaims: Whom let us faithfully bless![^335]  
*Ode 8. Heirmos:*  
Jeoparding their lives for the ancestral laws, the blessed youths in Babylon spat upon the senseless decree of the tyrant; and joined together in the fire wherewith they were not consumed, they sang a worthy hymn unto the Sovereign Ruler: Sing unto the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages![^336]  
*Troparion:*  
Ye guests fed wisely at Bethlehem with divine food, having glorified Him Who was incarnate with the angels, shepherds, and Magi: now let us mystically go unto the Jordan, seeing the great mystery which Christ Himself accomplishes: Whom we exalt supreme unto all ages.[^337]  
*Troparion:*  
Observing the chief commandments of the Law and the prophets, being established by love, let us become imitators of Christ, Who took flesh out of exceeding love, and reconciled us unto the Father by baptism, and taught us to sing: Sing unto the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages![^338]  
*Troparion:*  
He was about to receive Him Who comes to cleanse the sins of the world with water; but held fast by fear he forbade Him, saying: "I have need to be baptized by Thee," the friend answering the Bridegroom, the voice unto the Word, and the lamp unto the Sun: "Thee do we exalt supreme unto all ages."[^339]  
*Ode 9. Heirmos:*  
Of the Master's hospitality [Fol. 29r]
*Day 4*

...and of the immortal table having enjoyed beforehand in the poor cave, now let us run unto the Jordan, beholding a strange mystery, mediatrix of heavenly radiance.[^340]  
*Troparion:*  
Depart from Bethlehem, ye nurslings of wonders, unto the region of Jordan, and there behold the works mystically accomplished: by baptism Christ Who is come to renew Adam; for He was incarnate.[^341]  
*Troparion:*  
The Creator, begotten of the Father before the ages, was born at the last, unchangeably incarnate of the pure Virgin, the Maiden of God; being two-fold, God and man, to renew Adam by baptism.[^342]  
*Troparion:*  
As man in essence, not in phantasm, Thou camest as one in the midst of all, asking for baptism, the only guiltless One in nature: for Thou camest to bury the offences of men, being baptized in the waters.[^343]

...of salvation with the fire of the Spirit in the streams of the Jordan, as God, unto the human race.[^352]  
*Three Canons: Of the Forefeast with the Heirmos on 6; of the Apostles on 4; and of the Venerable Father on 4. Canon of the Forefeast, whose acrostic is: According to the Alphabet. Tone 6.*[^353]  
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*  
Having traversed the deep on foot as on dry land with their footsteps, seeing Pharaoh the pursuer drowned, Israel cried aloud: Let us sing a song of victory unto God![^354]  
*Troparion:*  
Let creation rejoice, let the families of the nations sing: Jesus the King of all the earth comes beforehand, to work our cleansing by Jordan's streams.[^355]  
*Troparion:*  
Having clothed Thyself in the flesh as in a bridal purple robe from virginal blood, O Lord, Thou comest naked unto the river streams, clothing my nakedness.[^356]  
*Troparion:*

*Ikos:*  
I do not demand that thou exceed thy bounds, O Baptist; I say not unto thee: "Tell Me what thou sayest unto the lawless and teachest sinners"; only baptize Me in silence, and wait for what comes from baptism: for on this account thou shalt receive a dignity which was not granted even unto the angels; for I will make thee greater than all the prophets. For none of them saw Me openly, but only in figures, and shadows, and riddles; but thou hast seen Me standing before thee: for I am come to save Adam, the first-formed.[^385]

Thy flock leaps with joy today, celebrating the light-bearing memory of thy falling asleep, which do thou bless from heaven; and after thy passing, cease not, O thrice-blessed one, to stand before God together with the angels, O all-blessed one.[^476]  
*Theotokion:*  
O pure one, who didst give birth unto Life for mortals unto redemption: quicken my soul which is dead through transgressions, as thou art compassionate, as the only protectress of them that flee beneath thy shelter, O all-immaculate one.[^477]  
*Exapostilarion of the Apostles, Tone 2, Podoben: "Give Ear, Ye Women" (Же́ны оу҆слы́шите):*  
O all-praised apostles of Christ the All-Compassionate, both disciples and beholders of God, keep not silence praying for us who celebrate your memory with love: that we may find remission of transgressions and divine grace in the Day of Judgment.[^478]  
*Glory... Both now... of the Forefeast, Tone 3, Podoben: "Thou Hast Visited Us" (Посѣти́лъ ны̀):*  
Make ready, O Zebulun; adorn thyself, O Naphtali: receive, O Jordan, the Creator of all and God, Who comes unto thee in the flesh, desiring to wash away our sins.[^479]  
*At the Praises, Stichera on 4, Tone 6, Podoben: "The Angelic Powers" (А҆́ггелскїѧ):*  
He Whom the voice of one crying prefigured, Christ, is come unto the streams of Jordan, and said unto the Forerunner: "Come, wash Me with the waters, baptize Me now Who have descended; for I am come to wash Adam from the first fall." Blessed art Thou Who hast appeared, our God: glory to Thee![^480]  
*Sticheron:*  
"In nowise have I searched out the heights of heaven, nor the number of the stars, nor have I measured the earth; and how, O Master," said the Forerunner, "shall I touch Thy head with my hand? How shall I baptize Him Who holds creation in His palm? Therefore I cry unto Thee: Blessed art Thou Who hast appeared, our God: glory to Thee!"[^481]  
*Sticheron:*  
"Being enthroned together with the Father and the Spirit, Thou art borne up by angelic hosts; yet in a small cave, as a stranger, Thou wast born in Bethlehem for Thy tender compassion. Therefore even now lend Thy right hand unto Me, that I may wash away the world's transgressions in Me."[^482]  
*Sticheron:*  
Thou didst drown sin of old in the days of Noah, having opened by Thy word the cataracts of heaven; and how shall Jordan endure, beholding Thee? For already it will turn back its stream. All creation hath recognized Thee, and I cry unto Thee: Blessed art Thou Who hast appeared, our God: glory to Thee![^483]  

[Fol. 35v]
*Month of January*

*Glory... Tone 6, Podoben: "The Angelic Powers" (А҆́ггелскїѧ):*  
"That the Father's good pleasure may be fulfilled, I am come upon earth, having clothed Myself in poverty: heaven is My throne, and earth My footstool; yet I bow My neck unto thee, for unto this am I come: baptize Me, Who cleansest the transgressions of men in Me."[^484]  
*Both now... the same Tone and Podoben:*  
"Thou Who formerly didst guide as light by a pillar and a cloud, and didst sprinkle dew in the wilderness; Thou Who rulest over all things, ineffable by nature: how hast Thou clothed Thyself in the form of a servant? As hay, I shall not touch Thee Who art fire. Do Thou Thyself baptize me, for I need to receive cleansing from Thee."[^485]  
*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*  
The Father's radiance of glory hath appeared upon the streams of Jordan, cleansing the defilement of our souls by baptism.[^486]  
*Verse: Therefore I will remember Thee from the land of Jordan and of the Hermonites [LXX Ps. 41:7].*  
*Sticheron:*  
Receive in a manner befitting a servant, O Prophet John, the Redeemer of the world, and baptize the Creator, unto the regeneration of mortals.[^487]  
*Verse: The waters saw Thee, O God, the waters saw Thee and were afraid [LXX Ps. 76:17].*  
*Sticheron:*  
The Illumination is come, Redemption hath appeared: come ye unto the Jordan, let us assemble to be cleansed, and to sing the forefeast hymns.[^488]  
*Glory... Both now... the same Tone and Podoben:*  
Today Christ grants saving release unto men, cleansing the defilement of souls by the fire of baptism.[^489]  
*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes from the Canon of the Forefeast, Ode 3, and of the Apostles, Ode 6.*  
*Prokeimenon, Tone 8: Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world [LXX Ps. 18:5].*  
*Verse: The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of His hands [LXX Ps. 18:2].*  
*The Epistle to the Romans, Pericope 96 (Rom. 8:8–14)[^490].*  
*Alleluia, Tone 4: The heavens shall confess Thy wonders, O Lord [LXX Ps. 88:6].*  
*The Gospel from Luke, Pericope 50 (Lk. 10:1–15)[^491].*

[Fol. 36r]
*Month of January, on the 5th Day.*[^493]  
*Forefeast of the Illumination; and of the Holy Martyrs Theopemptus and Theonas; and of the Venerable Mother Synkletike.*  
*At "Lord, I have cried", Stichera of the Martyrs, 3, Tone 4, Podoben: "As One Valiant among Martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*  
*Sticheron:*  
Let us hymn wise Theonas and Theopemptus: for obeying the dogmas of Christ, brightly abolishing every ungodly service, they served holily, honorably, and with good hope, courageously confessing the one God and Lord before the face of torturers, and receiving crowns from on high.[^494]  
*Sticheron:*  
Having forsaken downward-dragging corruption, the enjoyment of foods, and the blossoming glory of praises as temporary, ye cleaved unto Christ, inflamed by His fair beauty; and ye offered yourselves as sweet-smelling briars, and were crowned in a manner befitting God with the crown of the incorruptible Kingdom.[^495]  
*Sticheron:*  
Having hated the world, O transcendent martyrs, ye were gathered into the church of the firstborn, and with the angels ye sing an incorruptible song, standing together before God: having cast off the foul deceit of idols, ye martyrologically put to shame the folly of the torturers.[^496]  
*Other Stichera of the Venerable Mother, Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the Heavenly Ranks" (Нбⷭ҇ныхъ чинѡ́въ):*  
*Sticheron:*  
Having truly desired the glory of the Fathers, thou didst love incorruptible glory: therefore, having departed from pleasant things, thou didst give over thy body unto all afflictions; and now thou receivest the recompense of afflictions, reigning with Christ.[^497]  
*Sticheron:*  
He Who permitted Job to him that asked, desiring to test thee also as gold, left thy body unto the oppression of the evil one: therefore, having put the tempter to shame by patience in sicknesses, thou wast crowned with the crown of victory.[^498]  
*Sticheron:*  
Having desired the fair beauty of the Bridegroom Christ, and wishing to betroth thyself unto Him by all forms of good deeds, thou didst adorn thyself with the painful labors of abstinence: therefore now thou reignest with Him in His bridal chamber.[^499]  
*Glory... Both now... Tone 2:*  
Make ready, O river Jordan, for behold, Christ God comes to be baptized [Fol. 36v]
*Month of January*

...to be baptized by John, that Thou mightest crush the heads of invisible serpents by Thy Godhead in its waters. Rejoice, O wilderness of Jordan! Ye mountains, leap with gladness! For the Eternal Life comes to recall Adam. O voice of one crying, cry aloud, O John the Forerunner: "Prepare the ways of the Lord, and make His paths straight!"[^500]  
*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having Risen on the Third Day" (Трїдне́венъ):*  
*Sticheron:*  
Earth and earthly beings, leap and rejoice! The Stream of sweetness is baptized in the river, drying up the outpouring of wickedness, and pouring forth divine remission.[^501]  
*Verse: Therefore I will remember Thee from the land of Jordan and of the Hermonites [LXX Ps. 41:7].*  
*Sticheron:*  
Jesus, the Giver and Son of Light, having no need to be baptized, ascends in the flesh upon the streams of Jordan, desiring to enlighten them that are in darkness: with faith let us earnestly meet Him![^502]  
*Verse: The waters saw Thee, O God, the waters saw Thee and were afraid [LXX Ps. 76:17].*  
*Sticheron:*  
Having taken the form of a servant, Thou comest forward to be baptized by a servant in the streams of Jordan, O Christ, delivering us from the bondage of the ancient sin, and sanctifying and enlightening us.[^503]  
*Glory... Both now... Tone 6:*  
Let the wilderness of Jordan rejoice, and let it blossom as a lily: for the voice of one crying hath been heard in it: "Prepare the way of the Lord!" For He Who established the mountains by scale, and the valleys by measure, Who fills all things as God, is baptized by a servant. He begins to become poor, He Who grants rich gifts. Eve heard: "In sorrow shalt thou bring forth children"; but now the Virgin hears: "Rejoice, thou full of grace, the Lord is with thee, Who hath great mercy!"[^504]  
*Troparion, Tone 4:*  
The river Jordan was turned back of old by the mantle of Elisha, when Elijah had been taken up, and the waters were divided hither and thither; and the wet path became dry for him, truly as a type of baptism, whereby we traverse the flowing path of life: Christ hath appeared in the Jordan to sanctify the waters.[^505]  
*At Compline, the Canon, the acrostic whereof is: "Today also I sing of the Great Saturday." Heirmos twice, and Troparia on 6; and again the same Heirmos by both choirs together. Tone 6.*[^506]  
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*  
Him Who of old covered the pursuer and tyrant with the surge of the sea, the streams of Jordan hide and conceal, now washing Me [Fol. 37r]
*Day 5*

...cleansing with human cleansing: for gloriously hath He been glorified.[^507]  
*Troparion:*  
O Lord my God, we sing a light-named hymn and a forefeast song unto Thee, Who by Thy divine appearance dost mystically renew us, and leadest us up unto divine brightness.[^508]  
*Troparion:*  
Beholding Thee, the Pre-eternal One on high and newly revealed below, O Savior, transcendent and earthly beings were dismayed, and they sang of Thy condescension which surpasses speech.  
*Troparion:*  
That Thou mightest fill all things with Thy glory, Thou didst empty Thyself even unto the form of a servant; and now Thou bowest Thy head in a manner befitting a servant beneath the hand of a servant, compassionately cleansing my creation.  
*Ode 3. Heirmos:*  
Beholding Thee, Who foundedst the whole earth upon the waters without restraint, concealed in the flesh in the waters, creation was gripped by great amazement, crying aloud: There is none holy besides Thee, O Lord![^509]  
*Troparion:*  
Thou didst show forth types of Thy Theophany of old through the prophets, but now Thou hast revealed hidden things by deeds, showing the mysteries unto men today, granting new regeneration.[^510]  
*Troparion:*  
The Jordan stretched forth its waters as shoulders, with trembling to receive the Creator baptized bodily in the flesh, and sanctifying all things, of them that cry: There is none holy besides Thee, O Lord!  
*Troparion:*  
As oil and provision for the journey unto salvation, Christ grants baptism unto them that perceive His divine illumination, who sing with joy: There is none holy besides Thee, O Lord, Lover of mankind!  
*Ode 4. Heirmos:*  
Foreseeing Thy coming unto baptism, Habakkuk was dismayed and cried aloud: Thou didst mount Thy horses upon the sea, O Savior, troubling many waters.[^511]  
*Troparion:*  
When Thou wast revealed in the body, the earth was sanctified, the waters were blessed, heaven was enlightened; and the race of men was delivered from the bitter tyranny of the enemy.[^512]  
*Troparion:*  
With a divine voice the Forerunner now comes from the wilderness unto the Jordan, saying: "Repent ye, for the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand!" summoning all unto the glory of God.  
*Troparion:*  
He Who turned the sea of old into dry land, and poured forth fountains from the flinty rock, now accomplishes the cleansing of transgressions in the streams of Jordan by the fire of the Spirit.  
*Ode 5. Heirmos:*  
Isaiah, beholding the unwaning light of Thy Theophany which mercifully came to pass unto us, O Christ, rising early out of the night cried aloud: Come, ye that are enlightened, wash yourselves[^513] [Fol. 37v]
*Month of January*

...manifestly with divine water and the Spirit, and cleanse both soul and body.[^514]  
*Troparion:*  
Thou dost make new the earth-born, having become the new Adam, O Creator, performing a strange regeneration with fire and the Spirit and water, and a marvelous renewal without crushing or melting furnaces, making all new through God-working baptism.  
*Troparion:*  
With the Spirit Thou dost make new souls, and with water Thou dost sanctify the composite body, building up man as a living being: for Thou providest suitable remedies for the twofold nature by Thy wise providence, as the Physician of bodies and souls.  
*Troparion:*  
Having surpassed the highest birth from the Father before all ages, Thou art come unto him that is born of the barren one, asking for baptism as man; but from water Thou hast mystically through the Spirit made the Church fruitful with many children, O Savior, which formerly was childless.  
*Ode 6. Heirmos:*  
The divine Baptist was gripped, but not held fast, by fear: for though hay shrinks from drawing near unto fire, yet having heard: "Suffer it to be so now", he ran, fulfilling the command as a servant; and at the divine voice testifying from on high, he heard of the Pre-eternal Son.[^515]  
*Troparion:*  
Thou wast enrolled, but not enslaved, obeying the Caesar's decree: for though giving us solace from bondage, Thou willingly obeyest and payest the didrachma; yet us who were sold of old by the law of sin hast Thou now freed, and accounted worthy of adoption.[^516]  
*Troparion:*  
Thou reignest, but not in a worldly manner, being King by nature: for though born according to the flesh of the seed of David, Thou didst accept the throne of this kingdom, O Savior; yet Thou hast the proper dominion of the Kingdom together with the Father always before all ages, and unto the ages with the Spirit.  
*Troparion:*  
The ruler of the world and of them that are in the waters was indeed proclaimed of old; but he is choked by Thy cleansing, and cast down as the lakeside legion of old; and the creation of Thy hands, O Savior, which was enslaved by him, hast Thou accounted worthy of deliverance by Thy mighty hand.  
*Ode 7. Heirmos:*  
An ineffable wonder! He Who delivered the venerable youths from the flame in the furnace bows His head, and asks for baptism from a servant, cleansing them that cry aloud: O God our Redeemer, blessed art Thou![^517]  
*Troparion:*  
The stream of Jordan was divided of old by the mantle, prefiguring[^518] [Fol. 38r]
*Day 5*

...prefiguring Thy baptism, whereby the tunic of passions is rent asunder, and the garment of incorruption is woven for them that cry aloud unto God: Blessed art Thou![^519]  
*Troparion:*  
The rich stream, having received within itself the Creator being baptized, was shown forth as a fountain of living water, unto the salvation of us who sing: O God our Redeemer, blessed art Thou![^520]  
*Troparion:*  
Significantly typifying the divine death, by threefold immersion in the water in baptism we rise together with Christ, partaking of His third-day resurrection, and crying aloud unto Christ: Blessed art Thou unto the ages![^521]  
*Troparion:*  
The one grace of the Father, the Son, and the Spirit accomplishes this, by a gift unto them that faithfully desire divine baptism, who have received the power of adoption to cry aloud: O God, blessed art Thou![^522]  
*Ode 8. Heirmos:*  
Be dismayed with fear, O heaven, and let the foundations of the earth be shaken! For behold, He Who of old consumed with water the sacrifice of the righteous one most gloriously, is now clothed with water. Bless Him, ye youths; hymn Him, ye priests; exalt Him supreme, all ye people, unto all ages![^523]  
*Troparion:*  
Christ comes to grant redemption by baptism unto all the faithful: for through this He cleanses Adam, raises up him that was fallen, puts to shame the tyrant that cast him down, opens the heavens, brings down the Divine Spirit, and grants communion of incorruption.[^524]  
*Troparion:*  
The deceit of the enemy hath ceased: for the voice of one crying in the wilderness cries: "Prepare the way of the Lord!" and commands: "Make all His paths straight!" For the valley is humbled, the nature of mortals is exalted, and the mountain and hill of the enemies are brought low.  
*Troparion:*  
O most marvelous gifts! O divine grace and ineffable love! For behold, with water He cleanses me, with fire He enlightens me, and with the Divine Spirit the Creator and Master perfects me, the Sinless One Who is now clothed in my nature in the Jordan.  
*Ode 9. Heirmos:*  
Weep not, ye men guilty of evil deeds, choked by the snares of despair; but in peace of soul let us draw near unto Him Who cleanses all things, as the only Pure One, Who grants forgiveness through baptism.[^525]  
*Troparion:*  
After Thy marvelous birth from the Virgin preternaturally of old, Thou didst amaze all, O Word of God; and now we magnify Thee, as Thou accomplishest a great mystery most gloriously[^526] [Fol. 38v]
*Month of January*

...most gloriously through honorable communion, making the font fruitful with many children by the Divine Spirit.  
*Troparion:*  
The earth was sanctified by Thy holy nativity, O Word, while the heavens declared Thy glory by a star; and now the nature of waters is blessed as Thou art baptized in the flesh; and the race of mortals ascends again unto its former nobility.  
*Troparion:*  
Let all the earth rejoice, let heaven be glad, let the world leap for joy, let rivers clap their hands, let fountains and lakes, deeps and seas rejoice together: for Christ comes to cleanse and save Adam by divine baptism.  
*And again the Heirmos, and a prostration.*[^527]  
*At Matins, at "God is the Lord", the Troparion of the Forefeast, thrice.*  
*After the first Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "The Angelic Choir" (Ли́къ а҆́ггелскїй):*  
Rejoice, O river Jordan, for within thee the Creator of all comes willingly to receive baptism from a servant, as He is tender-hearted. Be glad, dance for joy, O Adam, and Eve our foremother: the Redemption of all is come, our Supremely Good God![^528]  
*Glory... Both now... the same Tone and Podoben:*  
Being the Master and Stream of sweetness, He comes forward to be baptized in the streams of the river, desiring to give me to drink of the waters of cleansing. Beholding Whom, John cried aloud: "How shall I stretch forth my hand upon Thy head, before Whom all things tremble?"[^529]  
*After the second Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 3, Podoben: "Beholding the Beauty of Thy Virginity" (Красотѣ̀ дѣ́вства):*  
Clothing the nakedness of Adam in the garment of glory, O Tender-hearted One, Thou desirest to be stripped naked in the flesh in the river Jordan. O most marvelous wonder! How shall the water receive Thee, O Master and Lord, Who coverest Thine upper chambers with waters, as it is written? All of us hymn Thy Theophany, O Jesus our Benefactor![^530]  
*Glory... Both now... Podoben: "Of the Divine Faith" (Бж҃твенныѧ вѣ́ры):*  
The Radiant Sun comes to enlighten in the Jordan, having shone forth from the Virgin as from a cloud, Christ our God: driving away the gloom of sin, and enlightening the ends of the world. Let us piously pray to receive His illumination, asking to receive great mercy.[^531]  
*Three Canons: of the Forefeast with the Heirmos on 6; of the Martyrs on 4; and of the Venerable Mother on 4.*[^532]  
*Canon of the Forefeast, Tone 4.*  
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*  
Delivered from bitter bondage, Israel traversed the impassable deep as dry land, beholding the enemy drowned, and sang a song unto God our Benefactor[^533] [Fol. 39r]
*Day 5*

...Who works wonders with a high arm: for gloriously hath He been glorified.[^534]  
*Troparion:*  
Christ comes unto baptism, Christ comes unto the Jordan, Christ now buries our sins in the water as He is good: with gladness let us sing unto Him: for gloriously hath He been glorified.  
*Troparion:*  
Let the clouds drop down eternal gladness with rejoicing: Christ Jesus comes forward to drown the streams of sin in the waters of Jordan, granting enlightenment unto all.  
*Troparion:*  
Behold the Light appears, behold Cleansing is revealed, behold the Savior is at hand to cause divine rays to shine upon them that are in darkness: let us receive Him joyfully with pure thoughts.  
*Another Canon, of the Martyrs, Tone 7.*  
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*  
Let us sing a song of victory unto the Lord, Who submerged all Pharaoh's power in the sea: for gloriously hath He been glorified.[^535]  
*Troparion:*  
Come, ye faithful, let us celebrate in harmony the all-glorious memory of the sufferers, glorifying Christ in spiritual songs.  
*Troparion:*  
The passion-bearers of Christ and firm champions of the faith, having strongly arrayed themselves against impiety, conquered the enemies.  
*Troparion:*  
The ungodly persecutor and stranger to Christ's faith, having wickedly raged against the passion-bearers, is brought to naught by faith.  
*Theotokion:*  
Save this flock which thou hast acquired, O Mother of God, from every distress, praying unto the Savior and our God.[^536]  
*Another Canon, of the Venerable Mother, Tone 2.*  
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*  
Come, ye people, let us sing a song unto Christ God, Who divided the sea and guided the people whom He led out of Egyptian bondage: for gloriously hath He been glorified.[^537]  
*Troparion:*  
I come to crown thy memory with songs, relying upon thee, foolish and wholly unclean as I am: but grant me a word of wisdom and understanding through thine intercessions.  
*Troparion:*  
Having raised thy whole mind unto divine height, and having known the abyss of good things and the goodness of delight, thou didst endure all things that befell thee.  
*Troparion:*  
Having given wings to thy mind unto God Most High, Thou didst lighten by abstinence and painful labors thy body which dragged thee down to things below, desiring great glory.  
*Theotokion:*  
Remaining what He was, and incarnate of thy womb: He granted unto us what we were at first, having delivered us from deceit[^538] [Fol. 39v]
*Month of January*

...having delivered us from transgressions, O Mother of God.[^539]  
*Ode 3. Heirmos:*  
Let not the mortal boast in his wisdom or wealth, but with faith of the Lord crying orthodoxly unto Christ God, and singing ever: Establish me, O Master, upon the rock of Thy commandments![^540]  
*Troparion:*  
He Who sits before all ages with the Father and the Spirit, now in these last times incarnate of the Virgin as He knows, Christ comes unto baptism, granting immortality unto all through the divine bath.  
*Troparion:*  
Desiring to bury our sins with water in the streams of Jordan, out of the tender compassion of His mercy, Christ God comes forward; and He builds up us who were corrupted, through baptism.  
*Troparion:*  
To cover the shameful nakedness of Adam our forefather, Thou willingly art stripped naked; and with the streams of Jordan Thou coverest Thyself, Who coverest Thine upper chambers with waters, O Christ, only Abundantly Merciful One.  
*Another Canon [of the Martyrs]. Ode 3. Heirmos:*  
My heart is established in the Lord, my horn is exalted in my God, my mouth is enlarged against mine enemies, I have rejoiced in Thy salvation [LXX 1 Kings / 1 Sam. 2:1].[^541]  
*Troparion:*  
Let us praise the champions of piety and faith, the divine sufferers, Theopemptus and most glorious Theonas.  
*Troparion:*  
Ye were shown forth as a rule, a model, and a pattern, O great-martyrs of Christ, becoming guides of the saints unto suffering.  
*Troparion:*  
Emulating their virtuous life, the martyrs, standing together at the tribunal, cried aloud: "We are all Christians!"  
*Theotokion:*  
Thou wast born ineffably of the Virgin, Thou appearedst as Thou didst well-please, O Lover of mankind; and Thou hast renewed the world, O Lord.[^542]  
*Another Canon [of the Venerable Mother]. Ode 3. Heirmos:*  
Establish us in Thee, O Lord, Who by the Tree didst put sin to death, and plant Thy fear in the hearts of us who sing of Thee.[^543]  
*Troparion:*  
Thou didst not spare thy flesh through many wounds, nor when utterly and unrestrainedly tormented unto the painful labors of abstinence, wherein the tempter was enfeebled.  
*Troparion:*  
Thou didst choose the narrow path of life, which mediates incorruptible and divine life, having spat upon the broad way, than which nothing is truly more bitter unto him that hath understanding.  
*Troparion:*  
While the flower of youth burned, thou didst pinch it from without by hardship and the painful labors of abstinence; and the burning of thine eyes thou didst quench with streams of tears.  
*Theotokion:*  
The Word Who became incarnate of thee, O all-pure one, desiring to [cleanse] the defilement of the flesh[^544] [Fol. 40r]
*Day 5*

...desiring to wash it away in a manner of cleansing, the flowing of water is set in motion.[^545]  
*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the Highest" (В вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*  
O Christ, Who tenderly washest away the multitude of transgressions out of Thy boundless mercy, Thou comest as man to be baptized in the waters of Jordan, clothing me with a garment, who was grievously stripped of ancient glory.[^546]  
*Then the Sessional Hymn of the Martyr, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thy Tomb, [O Savior]" (Гро́бъ тво́й):*  
Theopemptus was revealed from among those bodies here below; with his steadfast right hand and fellow-sufferer, not enduring the opposition of the tormentors, he is threatened. Rejoicing thereat, he cries aloud: "I honor the One Who buried the transgressions of mortals in the streams of Jordan!"[^547]  
*Another Sessional Hymn of the Venerable Mother, Tone 5, Podoben: "Co-unoriginate [Word]" (Собезнача́льное):*  
Thou didst surpass the painful labor of the fasting endurance of the ascetics; thou enjoyest greater mansions in the heavens, and hast been filled with superior radiance. For thou didst manly tread the rugged path, having conquered present things, and wast likened unto the angels, and now partakest of their glory.[^548]  
*Glory... Both now... of the Forefeast, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thy Tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й сп҃се):*  
The great Rain advances unto the river streams, having willed to be baptized in the flesh. Unto Whom the divine Forerunner, terrified, said: "How shall I baptize Thee, Who hast no defilement at all? How shall I stretch forth my right hand upon the head, at which all things tremble?"[^549]  
*Ode 4. Heirmos:*  
Habakkuk heard of old Thy marvelous report, O Christ, and with fear cried aloud: "God shall come from Teman [the south], and the Holy One from the mountain of dense shade [LXX Hab. 3:3], to save His anointed ones: glory to Thy power, O Lord!"[^550]  
*Troparion:*  
Draw ye water of life! Behold, now the River of the world is truly come, to dry up the turbid waters of unbelief, and to pour forth enlightenment unto them that sing unto Him: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^551]  
*Troparion:*  
Rejoice, O wilderness that thirsted before, and all human nature! For now the Stream of sweetness is revealed, quenching the burning heat of sin with the waters of Jordan. Unto Whom we faithfully sing: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^552]  
*Troparion:*  
Let us in our mind take up the voice of one crying in the wilderness prophetically: "Prepare ye the straight ways of Christ!" [LXX Isa. 40:3], saying unto Him Who comes: that by baptism He may cleanse us who are grown old, having dissolved the first condemnation.[^553]  

[Fol. 40v]
*Month of January*

*Another Canon [of the Martyrs]. Ode 4. Heirmos:*  
I heard Thy report and was afraid; I understood Thy works and was dismayed, O Lord [LXX Hab. 3:2].[^554]  
*Troparion:*  
Christ's great-martyrs filled the universe with divine words as a river, and brought deceit to naught.[^555]  
*Troparion:*  
Truly the passion-bearers found imperishable wealth: wealth, glory, and the brightness of earthly things they spat upon.[^556]  
*Troparion:*  
Arming themselves with Christ's weapon, the holy passion-bearers cast down all the tormentors' cruelty in this.[^557]  
*Theotokion:*  
Pure Mother, blessed holy Virgin, save from every distress them that sing of thee.[^558]  
*Another Canon [of the Venerable Mother]. Ode 4. Heirmos:*  
Thou camest from the Virgin, not an intercessor, nor an angel, but Thyself, O Lord, incarnate, and hast saved all of me, a man. Therefore I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^559]  
*Troparion:*  
Excelling in the beauties of the body, thou wast betrothed unto many who obtained not their desire; therefore, having worn thyself out, thou didst partake of divine beauty.[^560]  
*Troparion:*  
Thou didst endure bodily affliction as Job, thou didst utter no word to hasten thy death; but having transcended years and nature, thou didst receive the divine dwelling.[^561]  
*Troparion:*  
Thou didst withdraw from kinsfolk, parents, and possessions, seeking Christ alone, the imperishable and unfailing Wealth; with Whom thou wast revealed as a partaker of the glory on high.[^562]  
*Theotokion:*  
Thy childbearing delivered Adam from corruption, without man-made corruption, for the conception was above man: therefore deliver me, O Maiden, from corruption and evils.[^563]  
*Ode 5. Heirmos:*  
Make Thine unwaning light to shine, O Christ, in the hearts of them that faithfully sing of Thee, granting us peace which passes understanding. Therefore, hastening from the night of ignorance unto the day by Thy light, we glorify Thee, O Lover of mankind.[^564]  
*Troparion:*  
Being the King of peace, O Christ, Thou hast destroyed the middle wall of enmity, having appeared in the likeness of flesh unto them that are on earth: therefore, seeing Thy coming, John marveled with fear, when commanded to lay his hand upon Thee.[^565]  
*Troparion:*  
Christ our Savior now comes by the waters to crush the heads of the dragons, and cries aloud unto the trembling baptizer: "Stretch forth thy hand[^566] [Fol. 41r]
*Day 5*

...and touch My head; and shake off dread, accomplishing what is commanded.[^567]  
*Troparion:*  
The Prophet showed forth of old the grace of baptism by the Divine Spirit, having smitten the streams of Jordan with his mantle, which were divided, making a way for us unto divine rebirth, in which Christ appeared.[^568]  
*Another Canon [of the Martyrs]. Ode 5. Heirmos:*  
Rising early at dawn, O Word, unto Thy glory and praise, unceasingly we hymn the image of Thy Cross, which Thou hast given unto us as a weapon unto help.[^569]  
*Troparion:*  
Wise sufferers, armed with faith, having valiantly conquered the tortures of lawless enemies, received crowns together.[^570]  
*Troparion:*  
Neither flattery, nor deceit, nor earthly glory was able to cut short the course of your faith, O sufferers: therefore ye also rejoice.[^571]  
*Troparion:*  
Standing before the throne of the Lord's glory, unceasingly pray with the angels to grant cleansing of transgressions unto them that sing of you in faith.[^572]  
*Theotokion:*  
O pure Virgin full of grace, who in time didst bear the Word beyond words, pray Him to save our souls.[^573]  
*Another Canon [of the Venerable Mother]. Ode 5. Heirmos:*  
O Lord, Giver of light and Creator of the ages, guide us in the light of Thy commandments: for beside Thee we know no other God.[^574]  
*Troparion:*  
Wise one, thou wast a temple of the Word Who dwells in pure spirits; for by many labors of abstinence thou didst cleanse the beauty of thy soul, O most glorious one.[^575]  
*Troparion:*  
Thou didst mortify the flesh, dyed by natural grace through many labors, making radiant the image of the soul that shines brightly with the light of virtues.[^576]  
*Troparion:*  
Having inflamed the matter of the body with desire of thy soul for Christ, now with the immaterial angels thou truly rejoicest immaterially, beholding God.[^577]  
*Theotokion:*  
Crush the heads of the dragons that now nest in the streams, O all-undefiled Head of the pious: Who wast truly born without seed from thy womb.[^578]  
*Ode 6. Heirmos:*  
Wholly held fast by measureless passions, and fallen down into the whale of evils, yet bring me up out of corruption, O God, as of old Thou didst Jonah, and through faith grant me dispassion, that in the voice of praise and the spirit of salvation I may sacrifice unto Thee.[^579]  
*Troparion:*  
Showing the compassion of mercies, Christ, looking upon the servants with unchangeable[^580] [Fol. 41v]
*Month of January*

*Troparion:*

*Troparion:*  
The fleeing sea is divided [LXX Ps. 113:3], showing unto the new people the divine passage, which He Who came in the flesh wrought in the river, Who of old most gloriously poured forth water from the rock: let us glorify Him as God, Who built up our brokenness.[^583]  
*Another Canon [of the Martyrs]. Ode 6. Heirmos:*  
Jonah cried aloud from the belly of hades: Bring up my life out of corruption! [Jonah 2:3, 7]; and we cry aloud unto Thee: O Almighty Savior, have mercy upon us![^584]

Suffering at the tribunal, the martyrs brought idols' deceit to naught, and by their suffering destroyed all impiety from the earth.[^585]

*Theotokion:*

*Another Canon [of the Venerable Mother]. Ode 6. Heirmos:*  
Wandering in the abyss of sin, I invoke the fathomless abyss of Thy tender mercy: bring me up from corruption, O God![^589]  
*Troparion:*  
Enlightened by spiritual radiance, thou didst cast away all carnal delight as belonging to night; for thou wast wounded by desire for good things.[^590]  
*Troparion:*  
Thy luminous memory is radiant today, from afar enlightening the darkening of souls, O adornment of struggling monastics.[^591]  
*Troparion:*  
Thou didst preserve the purity of virginity, honoring the incorruptible bridal chamber; for thou wast kindled with desire for Christ, Thy marvelous Bridegroom.[^592]  
*Theotokion:*  
That we might be filled with glory, the Lord of glory came unto inglorious mankind: being washed as man, Thy Son glorified men.[^593]  
*Kontakion of the Forefeast, Tone 4:*  
In the streams[^594] [Fol. 42r]
*Day 5*

...today being in the streams of Jordan, the Lord cries aloud unto John: "Fear not to baptize Me, for I am come to save Adam, the first-formed!"[^595]  
*Ikos:*  
I do not compel thee, O baptizer, to transcend thy bounds; I do not say unto thee: Tell Me what thou sayest unto the lawless and teachest unto sinners; only baptize Me in silence, and wait for what comes from baptism; for on this account thou shalt receive a dignity that was not given unto the angels; for I shall make thee greater than all the prophets: of them indeed not one saw Me openly, but only in types, shadows, and enigmas; but thou hast seen Me standing before thee: for I am come to save Adam, the first-formed.[^596]  
*Ode 7. Heirmos:*  
The holy youths, who of old openly showed themselves for piety's sake, traversed the intolerable furnaced flame as a bridal chamber, and singing in harmony, they chanted a song: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^597]  
*Troparion:*  
Christ appeared as salvation, granting enlightenment: let heaven rejoice, and let the clouds truly drop down righteousness [LXX Isa. 45:8], unto them that cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^598]  
*Troparion:*  
The fleece which Gideon foresaw, full of a bowl of dripping water [LXX Judg. 6:38], openly declared Thy baptism, O Christ, which Thou didst undertake to be baptized, unto them that sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^599]  
*Troparion:*  
Elisha, healing the barren, salty waters [LXX 4 Kings / 2 Kings 2:19–22], prefigured the rich childbearing of the honorable font that was mystically to be, unto them that sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^600]  
*Another Canon [of the Martyrs]. Ode 7. Heirmos:*  
Thou didst bedew the burning furnace, O Savior, and didst save the youths who sang and said: Blessed art Thou unto the ages, O Lord God of our fathers![^601]  
*Troparion:*  
Ye received the end of martyrdom together, slain by the sword with women and children, crying aloud unto Christ: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers![^602]  
*Troparion:*  
The saints rejoiced, seeing themselves finished by swords, and with faith cried aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers![^603]  
*Troparion:*  
The cruelty of the ungodly was consumed from the earth, and they fell down upon the earth and were broken; and by confession through tortures the martyrs received crowns.[^604]  
*Theotokion:*  
Save thy flock, O all-holy pure one, from every distress: as the only mediatress of our race, O blessed Birthgiver of God, all-hymned one.[^605]  
*Another Canon [of the Venerable Mother]. Ode 7. Heirmos:*  
The God-opposing command of the lawless tyrant lifted up[^606] [Fol. 42v]
*Month of January*

...a high flame; but Christ spread out spiritual dew upon the pious youths: He Who is blessed and supremely glorified.[^607]  
*Troparion:*  
Devising evil things, the adversary attempted to weaken the strength of thy soul through diseases; and having assaulted Job's endurance, he was wisely repulsed by sufferings, wounded by thine endurance, O wise one.[^608]  
*Troparion:*  
Now thy soul hath turned away from the surges of life unto the tranquil haven, being rich in virtues among divine dwellings, O wise one, where through thy patient-suffering many a resting-place was prepared beforehand.[^609]  
*Troparion:*  
Thou didst wisely give instruction in community life, saying never to change one's place; for endurance mediates great recompenses; and truly thou wast not negligent to profit monastics by words and deeds.[^610]  
*Theotokion:*  
The nature of water washes me from sin, by the wisdom of thy preternatural childbearing; for the cleansing of God, the Creator of light, cleanses him that is defiled by many sins, O Bride of God, O Virgin.[^611]  
*Ode 8. Heirmos:*  
The dew-bearing furnace showed of old an image of a supernatural wonder: for the fire burned not the young children, revealing Christ's seedless divine birth from the Virgin. Therefore chanting let us sing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages![^612]  
*Troparion:*  
Let us theologically chant good praise in all things: He is come, He hath appeared! He descends unto the waters and is stripped naked, Who clothes the heaven with clouds; and He is baptized, cleansing us who sing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages![^613]  
*Troparion:*  
Come, let us go in spirit unto the Jordan, and let us behold a great vision in it: for the Light and Enlightenment comes, and bows Himself beneath the hand of the servant, who cries aloud with trembling: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages![^614]  
*Troparion:*  
The Coal which Isaiah foresaw [Isa. 6:6], kindled in the waters of Jordan, consumed all the matter of sins, and gave building up unto them that are broken: therefore chanting let us sing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages![^615]  
*Another Canon [of the Martyrs]. Ode 8. Heirmos:*  
The only unoriginate King of glory, Whom the heavenly powers bless, and the ranks[^616] [Fol. 43r]

...of angels tremble: hymn Him, ye priests; exalt Him supreme, all ye people, unto all ages![^617]

Confessing the one tender-hearted King of glory, the wise sufferers received the honors of victory, crying aloud with good courage: Ye people, exalt Him supreme unto all ages![^618]  
*Troparion:*  
Firmly standing against the tormentors, suffering valiantly, Christ's sufferers conquered the deceit of idols, crying aloud with good courage: Ye people, exalt Him supreme unto all ages![^619]  
*Troparion:*  
Like valiant adamantine warriors, having conquered the threats and tortures of the tormentors, they joyfully cried aloud: Hymn Him, ye priests; exalt the Lord supreme, all ye people, unto all ages![^620]  
*Theotokion:*  
The one tender-hearted, pre-eternal Word, Who was born of the Virgin in these last times and saved the human race: hymn Him, ye priests; exalt Him supreme, all ye people, unto all ages![^621]  
*Another Canon [of the Venerable Mother]. Ode 8. Heirmos:*  
Unto God, Who descended into the fiery furnace unto the Hebrew children, and changed the flame into dew: hymn Him as Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him supreme unto all ages![^622]  
*Troparion:*  
Dwelling on earth, thou didst truly desire to reach the land of the blessed, where the angelic ranks, the venerable, the ascetics, and virgins dwelling eternally hymn Christ unto all ages.[^623]  
*Troparion:*  
Being superior to many by nature's beauty, thou tookest care for the soul, wisely preserving the form of soul-beauty; therefore, having extinguished bodily beauty, thou wast kindled with the abstinence of thy soul.[^624]  
*Troparion:*  
Having acquired a watchful mind toward God with spiritual vigilance, Thou didst put completely to sleep the wiles of the crafty deviser of evils, O glorious one; and now having fallen asleep, Thou livest unto the ages.[^625]  
*Theotokion:*  
Desiring to renew them that are on earth, Thy Son hastens unto the Jordan as man, O pure one, out of extreme love; for there He crushed him who crushed all, and renews the world through thine intercessions.[^626]  
*Ode 9. Heirmos:*  
An ineffable mystery is the Virgin! For the holy maiden was revealed as heaven, the Cherubic throne, and the light-bearing bridal chamber of Christ God the Almighty: her do we piously magnify as the Birthgiver of God.[^627]  
*Troparion:*  
A strange and most glorious mystery do I behold: Jesus comes willingly unto the river Jordan, crying aloud unto John: "Lend Me thy right hand, accomplishing awesome things[^628] [Fol. 43v]

Let the wilderness of Jordan blossom [LXX Isa. 35:1–2]! Unto you that lie in darkness a great light hath appeared [LXX Isa. 9:2]: seeing it, leap for joy! Christ comes from Galilee, willing to be baptized in the flesh by a servant.[^630]  
*Troparion:*  
Rejoice now, O Jordan, and dance for joy, O John; leap, all the universe, for behold, Christ is appeared: He is stripped naked and baptized, clothing mankind in the garment of incorruption.[^631]  
*Another Canon [of the Martyrs]. Ode 9. Heirmos:*  
The Mother above nature, and Virgin according to nature, the only blessed one among women: in songs do we the faithful magnify as the Birthgiver of God.[^632]  
*Troparion:*  
Having trampled underfoot all idolatry through faith, Christ's passion-bearers piously finished their divine course, and confirmed it by faith.[^633]  
*Troparion:*  
Having despised all earthly things through faith, Christ's passion-bearers zealously suffered together, and received healings from God.[^634]

The passion-bearers, having manly armed themselves with faith, cast down the enemy regiments by the Lord's Cross, and received crowns.[^635]  
*Theotokion:*  
Thou who didst conceive the incomprehensible Word in thy womb, and didst bear Him unto us without seed: fervently pray that our souls may be saved.[^636]  
*Another Canon [of the Venerable Mother]. Ode 9. Heirmos:*  
The Son of the unoriginate Father, God and Lord, incarnate of the Virgin appeared unto us, to enlighten the darkened and to gather the dispersed: therefore do we magnify the all-hymned Birthgiver of God.[^637]  
*Troparion:*  
Brightened by the virtues of virginity, O glorious one, thou didst adorn thyself with the crown of an ascetic life; therefore with a double crown thy marvelous Bridegroom crowned thee, with Whose love thou wast wounded.[^638]  
*Troparion:*  
The hope of future things which Thou hadst in thy heart did not put thee to shame, O all-honorable Syncletica; for now Thou hast received the recompense of thy sufferings from the Savior, for which Thou didst traverse every form of abstinence.[^639]  
*Troparion:*  
Thou didst clothe thyself with Christ unto strength and confirmation, O venerable one, and didst bring down to the earth the arrogance of him that spoke unrighteousness against the height; therefore Jesus the Giver of victory adorned thee with the crown of victory.[^640]  
*Theotokion:*  
In thee the fall of the forefather received strength, having almost no strength remaining; for by the baptism of Thy Son all malice is now submerged; therefore do we proclaim thee the cause of cleansing.[^641]  
*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "By the Spirit in the Sanctuary" (Дх҃омъ во ст҃и́лищи):*  
When[^642] [Fol. 44r]
*Day 5*

...when Jordan beheld Thee stripped naked, with trembling it said unto him that was born of the barren: "Leave off, O John, from baptizing the Lord, Who cleanses all creation with fire and the Spirit; for unto this is He come, to enrich earthly things and the nature of water."[^643]  
*Glory... Both now...:*  
He Who shone forth from the Virgin in Bethlehem in the flesh now hastens unto the Jordan, to wash away the defilement of earthborn mortals, bringing them that are in darkness unto light by divine baptism.[^644]  
*At the Praises, Stichera on 4, Tone 6, Podoben: "Go Before, Ye Angelic Hosts" (А҆́ггелскїѧ предыди́те си́лы):*  
Why dost thou hesitate, O baptizer, concerning the dispensation which I accomplish for the salvation of all? Leave former things now, and consider what is profitable. Believe in God Who descended, and drawing near, minister unto Me; for as God I am come in tender mercy, to cleanse Adam from his fall.[^645]  
*Troparion:*  
Taking our sins upon Thy shoulders, Thou art come, O Jesus, unto the streams of Jordan; and I am struck with dread at Thy fearsome coming. How then dost Thou command me to baptize Thee? Thou art come Thyself to cleanse me, and how dost Thou ask baptism of me, O Cleansing of all?[^646]  
*Troparion:*  
Being the Word incomprehensible in My nature, yet clothed in the form of a servant [Phil. 2:7], I am come unto the Jordan; refuse Me not in any way! Come, fear not, draw near unto Me, and having laid thy right hand upon My head, cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O our God Who hast appeared, glory to Thee![^647]  
*Troparion:*  
Beyond understanding is Thine immeasurable poverty, O Word of God, for the sake of me who was fallen! For I have known Thee, that out of tender mercy Thou hast clothed Thyself in Adam and renewest them that are descended from Adam; and obeying Thy command, faithfully I cry unto Thee: Blessed art Thou, O our God Who hast appeared, glory to Thee![^648]  
*Glory... Tone 6, the same Podoben:*  
Serving the Master with trembling, John rejoices in soul, and cries aloud with gladness: "Rejoice with me, all generations of our forefather! For our Expectation is come; Christ is come unto the Jordan, to cleanse all from Adam's sin, as He is tender-hearted."[^649]  
*Both now... Tone 6, the same Podoben:*  
Let us sing, ye people, unto Him Who was born of the Virgin and baptized in the river Jordan, and let us cry aloud unto Him: O King of all creation, grant us uncondemned, with a pure conscience faithfully to attain Thy holy third-day resurrection from the dead![^650]

*Verse: Therefore will I remember Thee from the land of Jordan and Hermon [LXX Ps. 41:7].*

*Glory... Both now... Tone 6, Anatolian:*

*After "It is Good", the Trisagion Prayers. After the "Our Father": Troparion. Then the Litany, and the Dismissal.*[^655]  
*The Typikon for the Eve of the Holy Theophany should be known:*  
*Take note: If Theophany falls on Sunday or on Monday, we chant the Hours on Friday, and eat twice in the day: monastics eat cheese and oil [butter], and laymen meat. But if Theophany falls on Tuesday, we chant the Hours on Monday. If Theophany falls on Wednesday, we chant the Hours on Tuesday. If Theophany falls on Thursday, we chant the Hours on Wednesday. If Theophany falls on Friday, we chant the Hours on Thursday. On all these days, from Monday onwards, on the eves before Theophany we keep the fast: we by no means taste cheese or oil [butter], but only cabbage soup with vegetable juices, and kutia.*[^656]  
*(Woodcut: Winged cherub tailpiece ornament)* [Fol. 45r]
*The Order of the Hours Sung on the Eve of the Enlightenment [Theophany].*[^657]  

*At the beginning of the second hour [c. 8:00 AM], the bell is struck; and having gathered in the temple, the priest vests in the phelonion, and the deacon in the sticharion.*[^658]  
*The paraecclesiarch sets an analogion adorned opposite the Royal Doors, and lights a candle upon the candlestick. And the priest goes forth with the Gospel into the temple, or into the refectory, through the Royal Doors, the deacon preceding him with the censer. And he places the Holy Gospel upon the analogion. And standing before the analogion, he makes the beginning according to the custom; and after the beginning, the reader:*[^659]  
> **Reader:** *Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee. O Heavenly King... and the rest.*
*After the exclamatory blessing, the priest censes the Holy Gospel upon the analogion round about, and the other icons, and the whole temple, and the superior, and the brethren. And the reader reads:*  

*Psalm 5:*  
Give ear to my words, O Lord, understand my cry. Attend to the voice of my supplication, my King and my God; for unto Thee will I pray. O Lord, in the morning Thou shalt hear my voice; in the morning I will stand before Thee and Thou shalt look upon me; for Thou art not a God that desirest iniquity. The worker of evil shall not dwell with Thee, neither shall the transgressors abide before Thine eyes. Thou hast hated all them that work iniquity; Thou shalt destroy all them that speak falsehood. The man of blood and deceit the Lord abhors; but as for me, in the multitude of Thy mercy I will enter into Thy house; I will worship toward Thy holy temple in Thy fear. Lead me, O Lord, in Thy righteousness; because of mine enemies direct my way before Thee. For there is no truth in their mouth; their heart is vain. Their throat is an open sepulchre; with their tongues they have dealt deceitfully. Judge them, O God; let them fall from their counsels; according to the multitude of their ungodliness cast them out, for they have provoked Thee, O Lord. And let all them that hope in Thee be glad; they shall rejoice unto ages, and Thou shalt dwell in them. And all they that love Thy name shall boast in Thee; for Thou shalt bless the righteous man. O Lord, as with a shield of good pleasure Thou hast crowned us.[^660]  

*Psalm 22:*  
The Lord is my shepherd, and nothing shall be wanting to me; in a place of green pasture, there hath He made me to dwell. He hath nurtured me beside the water of rest; my soul [Fol. 45v]
*The First Hour*  

...He hath converted. He hath guided me along the paths of righteousness for His name's sake. For though I walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for Thou art with me; Thy rod and Thy staff, they have comforted me. Thou hast prepared a table before me against them that afflict me. Thou hast anointed my head with oil, and Thy cup that inebriates me, how excellent it is! And Thy mercy shall follow me all the days of my life, and that I may dwell in the house of the Lord unto length of days.[^661]  

*Psalm 26:*  
The Lord is my enlightenment and my Savior: whom shall I fear? The Lord is the defender of my life: of whom shall I be afraid? When the wicked drew near against me to eat up my flesh, they that afflict me and mine enemies, they became weak and fell. Though an host should encamp against me, my heart shall not fear; though war should rise up against me, in this have I hoped. One thing have I asked of the Lord, this will I seek after: that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life, to behold the delight of the Lord, and to visit His holy temple. For He hid me in His tabernacle; in the day of my troubles He sheltered me in the secret place of His tabernacle. He set me up upon a rock; and now, behold, He hath lifted up mine head above mine enemies. I went round about, and offered in His tabernacle a sacrifice of praise and shouting; I will sing and chant unto the Lord. Hear, O Lord, my voice wherewith I have cried; have mercy on me, and give ear unto me. Unto Thee my heart hath said: I will seek the Lord. My face hath sought Thee; Thy face, O Lord, will I seek. Turn not away Thy face from me, and turn not aside in wrath from Thy servant. Be Thou my helper; cast me not off, and forsake me not, O God my Savior. For my father and my mother have forsaken me, but the Lord hath taken me up. Set a law for me, O Lord, in Thy way, and guide me in the right path, because of mine enemies. Deliver me not over unto the souls of them that afflict me; for unjust witnesses have risen up against me, and falsehood hath lied unto itself. I believe that I shall see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living. Wait on the Lord; be of good courage, and let Thine heart be strengthened, and wait on the Lord.[^662]  

*Glory... Both now... Alleluia (thrice). Lord, have mercy (thrice).*  
*Glory... Troparion, Tone 4:*  
The river Jordan once turned back before the mantle of Elisha, when Elijah was taken up; and the waters were divided[^663] [Fol. 46r]
*Before the Theophany*  

...the waters were divided hither and thither, and the watery path became dry land unto him, as a true figure of baptism, whereby we pass through the flowing course of life: Christ hath appeared in the Jordan to sanctify the waters.[^664]  

*Both now... Theotokion:*  
What shall we call thee, O full of grace? Heaven? For thou hast shone forth the Sun of Righteousness. Paradise? For thou hast budded forth the Flower of incorruption. Virgin? For thou hast remained undefiled. Pure Mother? For thou hast held in thy holy embrace a Son, Who is the God of all. Him do thou beseech, that He save our souls.[^665]  

*Then we chant these Troparia twice, Tone 8, the work of Sophronius, Patriarch of Jerusalem:*  
Today the nature of the waters is sanctified, and the Jordan is divided, and turns back the streams of its waters, beholding the Master being baptized.[^666]  

*And the second choir chants the same Troparion, without a refrain.*

*The Reading is from the Epistle of the Holy Apostle Paul to the Romans (Pericope 91 [Rom. 6:3-11]):*  
Brethren, as many of us as were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into His death. Therefore we were buried with Him by baptism into death; that like as Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should begin to walk in newness of life. For if we have been planted together in the likeness of His death, we shall be also in the likeness of His resurrection: knowing this, that our old man was crucified with Him, that the body of sin might be destroyed, that henceforth we should not serve sin. For he that is dead is justified from sin. Now if we be dead with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with Him: knowing that Christ, being raised from the dead, dies no more; death hath no more dominion over Him. For in that He died, He died unto sin once; but in that He lives, He lives unto God. Likewise reckon ye also yourselves to be dead indeed unto sin, but alive unto God through Jesus Christ our Lord.[^711]

*The Reading is from the Holy Gospel according to Mark (Pericope 2 [Mark 1:9-15]):*

And immediately the Spirit drove Him into the wilderness. And He was there in the wilderness forty days, tempted of Satan; and was with the wild beasts; and the angels ministered unto Him. Now after that John was put in prison, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the Gospel of the kingdom of God, and saying: "The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand; repent ye, and believe in the [Fol. 53r]
*Before the Theophany*

...Gospel."[^712]

Let Thy tender mercies speedily anticipate us, O Lord, for we are brought very low. Help us, O God our Savior, for the glory of Thy name; O Lord, deliver us, and purge away our sins, for Thy name's sake [LXX Ps. 78:8-9].[^713]

O God and Lord of hosts, and Maker of all creation, Who through the compassion of Thine incomparable mercy hast sent down Thine Only-begotten Son, our Lord Jesus Christ, for the salvation of our race, and by His precious Cross hast torn asunder the handwriting of our sins, and thereby triumphed over the principalities and powers of darkness: do Thou Thyself, O Master, Lover of mankind, accept also from us sinners these prayers of thanksgiving and supplication; and deliver us from every destructive and dark transgression, and from all enemies, visible and invisible, that seek to do us harm. Nail our flesh to Thy fear, and incline not our hearts unto words or thoughts of wickedness; but wound our souls with Thy love, that looking ever unto Thee, and guided by the light that comes from Thee, beholding Thee, the unapproachable and everlasting Light, we may unceasingly send up confession and thanksgiving unto Thee, the unoriginate Father, with Thine Only-begotten Son, and Thine all-holy, good, and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. *Psalm 113:*  
When Israel went forth out of Egypt, the house of Jacob from a barbarous people, Judea became His sanctuary, Israel His dominion.[^718] The sea saw it and fled; Jordan was driven back. The mountains skipped like rams, and the hills like lambs of the flock. What ailed thee, O sea, that thou fleddest? And thou, O Jordan, that thou wast driven back? Ye mountains, that ye skipped like rams, and ye hills like lambs of the flock? At the face of the Lord the earth was moved, at the face of the God of Jacob; Who turned the rock into pools of waters, and the flint into fountains of waters. Not unto us, O Lord, not unto us, but unto Thy name give glory, for Thy mercy and for Thy truth's sake; lest at any time the nations say: "Where is their God?" But our God is in heaven and on earth; all things whatsoever He hath pleased, He hath done. The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the works of men's hands. They have a mouth, and speak not; eyes have they, and see not. They have ears, and hear not; noses have they, and smell not. Hands have they, and handle not; feet have they, and walk not; neither shall they make a sound with their throat. Let them that make them become like unto them, and all they that put their trust in them. The house of Israel hath hoped in the Lord: He is their helper and defender. The house of Aaron hath hoped in the Lord: He is their helper and defender. They that fear the Lord have hoped in the Lord: He is their helper and defender. The Lord hath been mindful of us, and hath blessed us; He hath blessed the house of Israel, He hath blessed the house of Aaron. He hath blessed them that fear the Lord, the small with the great. May the Lord add unto you, unto you and unto your children. Blessed are ye of the Lord, Who made heaven and earth. The heaven of heavens belongs to the Lord, but the earth hath He given to the sons of men. The dead shall not praise Thee, O Lord, nor any that go down into hell. But we that live will bless the Lord, from henceforth and unto the age.[^719]

They shall feed in all the ways, and their pasture shall be in all the paths. *Before the Theophany*

*The Reading is from the Epistle of the Holy Apostle Paul to Titus (Pericope 302 [Titus 2:11-14; 3:4-7]):*  
My child Titus, the grace of God that brings salvation hath appeared to all men, teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly in this present world: looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Savior Jesus Christ; Who gave Himself for us, that He might redeem us from all iniquity, and purify unto Himself a peculiar people, zealous of good works. But when the kindness and love of God our Savior appeared: not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to His mercy He saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Spirit, which He shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior; that being justified by His grace, we should be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life.[^730]

*The Reading is from the Holy Gospel according to Matthew (Pericope 6 [Matt. 3:13-17]):*

And Jesus, when He was baptized, went up straightway out of the water; and, lo, the heavens were opened unto Him, and He saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove, and lighting upon Him. And lo, a voice from heaven, saying: "This is My beloved Son, in Whom I am well pleased."[^731]

O Master, Lord Jesus Christ our God, Who hast long endured over our sins, and hast brought us even unto the present hour, wherein, hanging upon the life-creating tree, Thou didst make way for the entrance of the penitent thief into Paradise, and by death didst destroy death: cleanse us, Thy sinful and unworthy servants; for we have sinned and committed iniquity, and are not worthy to lift up our eyes and look upon the height of heaven, because we have forsaken the way of Thy righteousness, and walked according to the desires of our hearts. But we beseech Thine immeasurable goodness: spare us, O Lord, according to the multitude of Thy mercy, and save us for Thy holy name's sake, for our days have vanished in vanity. Pluck us out of the hand of the adversary, and forgive us our sins; and mortify our carnal mind, that, having put off the old man, we may put on the new, and live unto Thee, our Master and Benefactor. And so following Thy commandments, may we attain unto everlasting rest, where is the dwelling place of all them that rejoice. For Thou art in truth the true gladness and joy of them that love Thee, O Christ our God, and unto Thee do we send up glory, with Thine unoriginate Father, and Thine all-holy, good, and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.[^733]

...performs deeds of mercy, and judgment for all that are wronged. He made known His ways unto Moses, His will unto the sons of Israel. He has not dealt with us according to our iniquities, nor rewarded us according to our sins. For according to the height of heaven from the earth, the Lord has made His mercy to prevail over them that fear Him. As far as the east is from the west, so far has He removed our iniquities from us. As a father has compassion upon his sons, so has the Lord compassion upon them that fear Him; for He knows our fashioning, He remembers that we are dust. As for man, his days are as the grass; as a flower of the field, so shall he blossom forth. For a wind passes over it, and it shall not be, and its place shall know it no more. But the mercy of the Lord is from eternity and unto eternity upon them that fear Him, and His righteousness is upon sons of sons, unto them that keep His covenant, and remember His commandments to do them. The Lord has prepared His throne in heaven, and His kingdom rules over all. Bless the Lord, all ye His angels, mighty in strength, that perform His word, to give ear unto the voice of His words. Bless the Lord, all ye His hosts, His ministers that do His will. Bless the Lord, all ye works of His, in every place of His dominion. Bless the Lord, O my soul.[^735]

*The Confession of the Orthodox Faith of the First Council.[^739] (If there is a Liturgy, we do not say this here, but after "Both now" we say "Forgive, remit," and the rest.)*  
I believe in one God, the Father Almighty, Maker of heaven and earth, and of all things visible and invisible. And in one Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God, the Only-begotten, begotten of the Father before all ages. Light of Light, true God of true God, begotten, not made, of one essence with the Father, by Whom all things were made. Who for us men and for our salvation came down from the heavens, and was incarnate of the Holy Spirit and the Virgin Mary, and became man; and was crucified for us under Pontius Pilate, and suffered, and was buried; and rose again on the third day according to the Scriptures; and ascended into heaven, and sits at the right hand of the Father; and shall come again with glory to judge the living and the dead; Whose kingdom shall have no end.

*Of the Second Council:[^740]*  
And in the Holy Spirit, the Lord, the Giver of life, Who proceeds from the Father and the Son;[^741] Who with the Father and the Son together is worshipped and glorified; Who spoke through the prophets. And in one holy, catholic, and apostolic Church. I confess one baptism for the remission of sins. I look for the resurrection of the dead, and the life of the world to come. Amen.

*Psalm 33:*  
I will bless the Lord at all times, His praise shall continually be in my mouth. In the Lord shall my soul be praised; let the meek hear and be glad. Come, ye children, give ear unto me: I will teach you the fear of the Lord. Who is the man that desires life, loving to see good days? Many are the afflictions of the righteous, and from them all the Lord will deliver them. The Lord keeps all their bones; not one of them shall be broken. The death of sinners is evil, and they that hate the righteous shall offend. The Lord will redeem the souls of His servants, and none of them that hope in Him shall offend.[^745]
