*Vespers with the Liturgy of Basil the Great takes place at its proper time.*  
*Be it known:*  
*Note: If the Eve of Theophany falls on a Saturday or a Sunday: There is no fasting, and the troparia of the Royal Hours with the readings are not chanted on Saturday and Sunday; but we chant the Royal Hours beforehand on Friday according to custom, as indicated in order. We also say Psalm 33, "I will bless the Lord," and the Dismissal. And on that day we eat cheese and eggs.[^746] If the Eve falls on Saturday: Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Communion Hymn of the day; the Epistle and Gospel first of the Saturday before Theophany, and then of the day in order. After "Especially," we chant "It is truly meet." If, however, the Eve of Theophany falls on Sunday: Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, Gospel, and Communion Hymn first of the Sunday before Theophany, and then of the day in order. After "Especially," we chant "It is truly meet." After the dismissal of the Liturgy, we eat morsels [of bread] and drink one cup of wine. But we eat a complete meal after the dismissal of Vespers, with oil; but cheese, eggs, and fish we in no wise presume to touch.[^747]*  
*It is fitting to know:*  
*Note: If the Day of Illumination falls on a Sunday, we chant nothing resurrectional, but the entire order of the feast, at Vespers, and at Matins, and at the Liturgy In the same month, on the 6th day: The Holy Theophany of our Lord, God, and Savior Jesus Christ.*[^748]
*At the 5th hour of the day, the semantron sounds for the great bell, and thereafter all the heavy bells. And having gathered into the temple, we begin Vespers, and we chant the customary Psalm [103]. Then the Great Ektenia. And after the ektenia, if it be Saturday, we chant the Kathisma: "Blessed is the man," the entire kathisma. If on Sunday, we chant the first antiphon. But if on other days, the Kathisma is not chanted, but immediately we chant "Lord, I have cried," in Tone 2. The priest performs the Proskomedia. The deacon censes the church according to custom. And we chant the Stichera of the Feast on 8, Tone 2: Idiomela by John the Monk:*[^749]

Beholding the Enlightener of us all, Who enlightens every man, coming to be baptized, the Forerunner rejoices in soul and trembles in hand; he points Him out and says unto the people: "This is He that redeems Israel, Who frees us from corruption. O sinless Christ our God, glory to Thee!" *(Twice)*

As our Redeemer was being baptized by a servant, and witnessed unto by the descent of the Spirit, the angelic hosts looking on were struck with awe; and a voice was borne from heaven from the Father: "This One Whom the Forerunner baptizes with his hand, is My beloved Son, in Whom I am well pleased: O Christ our God, glory to Thee!"

The streams of Jordan received Thee, the Fountain, and the Comforter descended in the form of a dove; He Who bowed down the heavens bows His head; the clay cries out and shouts unto the Potter: "Why dost Thou command me things that are above me? I have need of Thy baptism: O sinless Christ our God, glory to Thee!" *(Twice)*

Desiring to save straying man, Thou didst not disdain to clothe Thyself in the form of a servant; for it was fitting for Thee, the Master and God, to take upon Thyself our nature for our sake; for when Thou wast baptized in the flesh, O Redeemer, Thou didst make us worthy of remission. Therefore we cry aloud unto Thee: O Christ our God, glory to Thee! Thou didst bow Thy head unto the Forerunner, Thou didst crush the heads of the dragons; having come into the streams, Thou didst enlighten all things, that we may glorify Thee, O Savior, the Enlightener of our souls.[^750]

*Entrance with the Gospel.*  
*Prokeimenon of the day.*  
*Reading from Genesis (Chapter 1:1–13):*[^751]  
In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth. And the earth was invisible and unformed, and darkness was over the abyss, and the Spirit of God was borne over the water. And God said: "Let there be light," and there was light. And God saw the light, that it was good; and God separated between the light and the darkness. And God called the light Day, and the darkness He called Night. And there was evening, and there was morning, one day.  
And God said: "Let there be a firmament in the midst of the water, and let it divide between water and water"; and it was so. And God made the firmament; and God divided between the water which was under the firmament, and the water which was above the firmament. And God called the firmament Heaven; and God saw that it was good. And there was evening, and there was morning, the second day.  
And God said: "Let the water under the heaven be gathered into one gathering, and let the dry land appear"; and it was so. And the water under the heaven was gathered into its gatherings, and the dry land appeared. And God called the dry land Earth, and the gatherings of the waters He called Seas; and God saw that it was good. And God said: "Let the earth bring forth green grass, yielding seed according to its kind and according to its likeness, and the fruit tree yielding fruit whose seed is in itself, according to its kind upon the earth"; and it was so. And the earth brought forth green grass, yielding seed according to its kind and according to its likeness, and the fruit tree yielding fruit whose seed is in itself according to its kind upon the earth; and God saw that it was good. And there was evening, and there was morning, the third day.

*Reading from Exodus (Chapter 14:15–18, 21–23, 27–29):*[^752]  
The Lord said unto Moses: "Why criest thou unto Me? Speak unto the children of Israel, and let them journey forward. And do thou lift up thy rod, and stretch forth thine hand over the sea, and divide it; and let the children of Israel go into the midst of the sea upon dry ground. And lo, I will harden the heart of Pharaoh, and of his servants, and of all the Egyptians, and they shall go in after them; and I will be glorified in Pharaoh, and in all his host, and in his chariots, and in his horses. And all the Egyptians shall know that I am the Lord, when I am glorified in Pharaoh, and in his chariots, and in his horses." And Moses stretched forth his hand over the sea, and the Lord drove back the sea with a strong south wind all that night, and made the sea dry land, and the water was divided. And the children of Israel went into the midst of the sea upon dry ground, and the water was a wall unto them on the right hand and on the left. And the Egyptians pursued, and went in after them to the midst of the sea, even all Pharaoh's horses, his chariots, and his horsemen. And Moses stretched forth his hand over the sea, and the water returned to its place toward morning; and the Egyptians fled under the water; and the Lord shook off the Egyptians in the midst of the sea. And the water returned and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, and the captains, and all the host of Pharaoh that went after them into the sea; there remained not so much as one of them. But the children of Israel walked upon dry land in the midst of the sea.[^753]

*Reading from Exodus (Chapter 15:22–27; 16:1):*[^754]  
Moses took the children of Israel from the Red Sea, and brought them into the wilderness of Shur; and they went three days in the wilderness, and found no water to drink. And they came to Marah, and could not drink the water of Marah, for it was bitter; therefore the name of that place was called Bitterness. And the people murmured against Moses, saying: "What shall we drink?" And Moses cried unto the Lord, and the Lord showed him a tree; and he cast it into the water, and the water was made sweet. There God made for him ordinances and judgments, and there He proved him, and said: "If thou wilt diligently give ear unto the voice of the Lord thy God, and wilt do that which is pleasing before Him, and wilt give ear to His commandments, and keep all His ordinances, I will not bring upon thee any disease which I brought upon the Egyptians; for I am the Lord that heals thee." And they came to Elim, and there were twelve springs of waters, and seventy trunk-stems of palm trees; and they encamped there beside the waters. And they set out from Elim, and the whole congregation of the children of Israel came into the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai.

*Troparion, Tone 5:*  
Thou hast appeared in the world, O Thou that didst make the world, that Thou mightest enlighten them that sit in darkness: O Lover of mankind, glory to Thee![^755]

*Verse 1:*  
God be compassionate unto us and bless us; cause Thy face to shine upon us, and be merciful unto us; that we may know Thy way upon earth, Thy salvation among all the nations that Thou mightest enlighten them that sit in darkness: O Lover of mankind, glory to Thee![^756]

*Verse 2:*  
Let the peoples praise Thee, O God; let all the peoples praise Thee. Let the nations be glad and rejoice, for Thou shalt judge the peoples with equity, and guide the nations upon earth.  
*Refrain:* That Thou mightest enlighten them that sit in darkness: O Lover of mankind, glory to Thee!

*Verse 3:*  
Let the peoples praise Thee, O God; let all the peoples praise Thee. The earth has yielded her fruit; let God, our God, bless us; let God bless us, and let all the ends of the earth fear Him.  
*Refrain:* That Thou mightest enlighten them that sit in darkness: O Lover of mankind, glory to Thee!

*Glory... Both now...*  
*Troparion:* Thou hast appeared in the world, O Thou that didst make the world, that Thou mightest enlighten them that sit in darkness: O Lover of mankind, glory to Thee!

*Reading from Joshua the Son of Nun (Chapter 3:7–8, 14–17):*[^757]  
The Lord said unto Joshua: "On this day I begin to magnify thee before all the sons of Israel, that they may know that as I was with Moses, so will I be with thee. And now command the priests that bear the ark of the covenant, saying: When ye are come to a part of the water of the Jordan, ye shall stand in the Jordan." And so the priests that took up the ark of the covenant of the Lord went into the Jordan; and the feet of the priests bearing the ark were dipped in a part of the water of the Jordan. (Now the Jordan was overflowing all its banks, as in the days of wheat harvest.) And the waters that came down from above stood in one heap, standing very far off from the city of Adam, even unto the parts of Kiriath-jearim; and those that went down toward the Sea of Arabah, even the Salt Sea, wholly failed; and the people stood opposite Jericho. And the priests that bare the ark of the covenant of the Lord stood ready on dry ground in the midst of the Jordan. And all the children of Israel crossed over on dry ground, until all the people had finished passing over.

*Reading from the Fourth Book of Kings (Chapter 2:6–14):*[^758]  
Elijah said unto Elisha: "Tarry here, I pray thee, for the Lord has sent me to Jordan." And Elisha said: "As the Lord lives, and as thy soul lives, I will not leave thee." And they two went on, and fifty men of the sons of the prophets went and stood opposite afar off and they two stood by Jordan.[^759] And Elijah took his mantle, and wrapped it together, and smote the waters, and the water was divided hither and thither, and they two went over on dry ground. And it came to pass, when they were gone over, that Elijah said unto Elisha: "Ask what I shall do for thee, before I be taken away from thee." And Elisha said: "I pray thee, let a double portion of thy spirit be upon me." And Elijah said: "Thou hast asked a hard thing; nevertheless, if thou see me when I am taken from thee, it shall be so unto thee; but if not, it shall not be so." And it came to pass, as they still went on and talked, that behold, there appeared a chariot of fire, and horses of fire, and parted them both asunder; and Elijah was taken up by a whirlwind as into heaven. And Elisha saw it, and he cried: "My father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof!" And he saw him no more; and Elisha took hold of his own clothes, and rent them in two pieces. And Elisha took up the mantle of Elijah that fell from him, and went back, and stood by the bank of Jordan. And Elisha took the mantle of Elijah that fell from him, and smote the waters, and they did not divide. And Elisha said: "Where now is the God of Elijah, Appho?"[^760] And Elisha smote the waters a second time, and the waters divided, and he went over on dry ground.

*Reading from the Fourth Book of Kings (Chapter 5:9–14):*[^761]  
Naaman, captain of the host of the king of Syria, came with his chariots and with his horses, and stood at the door of the house of Elisha. And Elisha sent a messenger unto him, saying: "Go and wash in Jordan seven times, and thy flesh shall return unto thee, and thou shalt be clean." And Naaman was wrathful, and went away, and said: "Behold, I said: He will surely come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of the Lord his God, and strike his hand over the place of the leprosy, and take it away from my flesh. Are not Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than the Jordan, and all the waters of Israel? May I not wash in them, and be clean?" So he turned and went away in a rage. And his servants came near, and spake unto him, and said: "My lord, if the prophet had bid thee do some great thing, wouldest thou not have done it, as he said unto thee: Wash, and be clean?" And Naaman went down, and dipped himself seven times in Jordan, according to the saying of the man of God; and his flesh turned again unto him like the flesh of a little child, and he was cleansed.

*Troparion, Tone 6:*

*Refrain:* For where should Thy light have shone forth, save upon them that sit in darkness: glory to Thee!

*Refrain:* For where should Thy light have shone forth, save upon them that sit in darkness: glory to Thee!

*Reading from the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 1:16–20):*[^764]  
Thus says the Lord: "Wash yourselves, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from your souls before Mine eyes; cease to do evil; learn to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow. Come now, and let us reason together, says the Lord: though your sins be as scarlet, I will make them white as snow; and though they be as crimson, I will make them white as wool. And if ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land; but if ye will not, neither listen unto Me, the sword shall devour you; for the mouth of the Lord has spoken these things."

*Reading from Genesis (Chapter 32:1–5):*[^765]  
Jacob looked up, and saw the host of God encamped; and the angels of God met him. And Jacob said when he saw them: "This is the camp of God"; and he called the name of that place Camps [Mahanaim]. And Jacob sent messengers before him to Esau his brother unto the land of Seir, the country of Edom. And he commanded them, saying: "Thus shall ye speak unto my lord Esau: Thus says thy servant Jacob: I have sojourned with Laban, and stayed until now; and I have oxen, and donkeys, and sheep, and men-servants, and maid-servants; and I have sent to tell my lord" unto my lord Esau, that thy servant may find grace before thee." And the messengers returned to Jacob, saying: "We came to thy brother Esau, and lo, he himself comes to meet thee, and four hundred men with him." And Jacob was greatly afraid, and was perplexed; and he divided the people that were with him, and the oxen and the sheep, into two camps. And Jacob said: "If Esau come to one camp and smite it, then the other camp shall be saved." And Jacob said: "O God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac, the Lord Who saidst unto me: 'Return unto the land of thy birth, and I will deal well with thee.' Let me be content with all the righteousness and all the truth which Thou hast shown unto Thy servant; for with this my staff I passed over the Jordan."[^766]

*Reading from Exodus (Chapter 2:5–10):*[^767]
The daughter of Pharaoh came down to wash herself at the river; and her maidens walked along by the river. And when she saw the ark in the flags, she sent her maid and took it. And when she had opened it, she saw the child weeping in the ark. And the daughter of Pharaoh had compassion on it, and said: "This is one of the Hebrews' children." And his sister said to Pharaoh's daughter: "Wilt thou that I go and call to thee a nurse of the Hebrew women, that she may nurse the child for thee?" And Pharaoh's daughter said to her: "Go." And the maiden went and called the child's mother. And Pharaoh's daughter said unto her: "Take this child away and nurse it for me, and I will give thee thy wages." And the woman took the child and nursed it. And when the child was grown, she brought him unto Pharaoh's daughter, and he became her son. And she called his name Moses, and said: "Because I drew him out of the water."

*Reading from Judges (Chapter 6:36–40):*[^768]
Gideon said unto God: "If Thou wilt save Israel by mine hand, as Thou hast said: behold, I will put a fleece of wool on the threshing-floor; and if the dew be on the fleece only, and [it be dry upon] all the earth [beside], then I shall know that Thou wilt save Israel by mine hand, as Thou hast said." And it was so. And Gideon rose up early on the morrow, [and pressed] the fleece, and wrung the dew out of the fleece, a bowl full of water. [And] Gideon said unto God: "Let not Thine anger be kindled against [me], and I will speak but this once: let me prove, I pray Thee, but this once with the fleece; let it now be dry only upon the fleece, and upon all the ground [let there be dew." And] God did so that night: for it was dry [upon the fleece only,] and there was dew on all the ground.

*Reading from the Third Book of Kingdoms (Chapter 18:30–39):*[^769]
Elijah said unto the people: "Come near unto me." And all the people came near unto him. And Elijah took twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Israel, unto whom the word of the Lord came, saying: "Israel shall be thy name." And with the stones he built an altar in the Name of the Lord, and he repaired the altar of the Lord that was broken down. And he made a trench about the altar, as great as would contain two measures of seed. And he put the wood in order on the altar which he had made, and cut the burnt sacrifice in pieces, and laid them on the wood, and compassed the altar. And Elijah said: "Fill four water-pots with water, and pour it on the burnt sacrifice, and on the wood." And he said: "Do it the second time." And they did it the second time. And he said: "Do it the third time." And they did it the third time. And the water ran round about the altar; and the trench was filled with water. And Elijah cried aloud unto heaven, and said: "Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and of Israel, hear me this day by fire! And let all this people know that Thou art the one Lord God of Israel, and that I am Thy servant, and that I have done all these things for Thy sake; and turn Thou the heart of this people back again." Then the fire of the Lord fell from heaven, and consumed the burnt sacrifice, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust, and licked up the water that was in the trench. And when all the people saw it, they fell on their faces, and said: "Truly the Lord is God; He is God!"

*Reading from the Fourth Book of Kingdoms (Chapter 2:19–22):*[^770]
The men of the city of Jericho said unto Elisha: "Behold, the situation of this city is pleasant, as thou, lord, seest; but the water is bad, and the ground barren." And Elisha said: "Bring me a new cruse, and put salt therein." And they brought it to him. And he went forth unto the spring of the waters, and cast the salt in there, and said: "Thus says the Lord: 'I have healed these waters; there shall not be from thence any more death or barren land.'" So the waters were healed unto this day, according to the saying which Elisha spoke.

*Reading of the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 49:8–15):*[^771]
Thus says the Lord: "In an acceptable time have I heard Thee, and in a day of salvation have I helped Thee; and I formed Thee, and gave Thee for a covenant of the nations, to establish the earth, and to inherit the desolate heritages; saying to them that are in bonds: 'Go forth!' and to them that are in darkness: 'Show yourselves!' They shall feed in the ways, and their pastures shall be in all high places. They shall not hunger, neither thirst; neither shall the heat nor sun smite them; for He that hath mercy on them shall comfort them, and by the springs of water shall He guide them. And I will make all My mountains a way, and every path a pasture for them. Behold, these shall come from afar; and lo, these from the north and from the sea; and these from the land of the Persians. Sing, O heavens, and be joyful, O earth; let the mountains break forth into joy, and the hills into righteousness; for the Lord hath comforted His people, and will have mercy upon His afflicted. But Zion said: "The Lord hath forsaken me, and my God hath forgotten me." Can a woman forget her sucking child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? Yea, they may forget, yet will I not forget thee, says the Lord."

The waters saw Thee and were afraid. The Forerunner trembled, and cried aloud, saying: "How shall the lamp enlighten the Light? How shall the servant lay his hand upon the Master? Sanctify me and the waters, O Savior, Who takest away the sin of the world!"

*Reading of the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 35:1–10):*[^777]
Thus says the Lord: "Let the thirsty wilderness be glad; let the desert rejoice, and blossom as the lily. Yea, it shall blossom abundantly, and rejoice with joy and singing; the glory of Lebanon shall be given unto it, the honor of Carmel; and My people shall see the glory of the Lord, and the excellency of God. Be strong, ye relaxed hands, and be comforted, ye feeble knees! Say to them that are faint-hearted: 'Be strong, fear not; behold, our God will render judgment; He will come and save us.' Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall hear. Then shall the lame leap as an hart, and the tongue of the stammerers shall be clear; for in the wilderness shall water break out, and a torrent in a thirsty land. And the parched ground shall become a pool, and in the thirsty land springs of water. There shall be the joy of birds, a dwelling-place of reed-grass, and reeds, and pools. And there shall be a clean way, and it shall be called a holy way; and the unclean shall not pass over it, neither shall there be an unclean way there; but the dispersed shall walk upon it, and they shall not go astray. No lion shall be there, nor shall any ravenous beast go up thereon, nor be found there; but the redeemed shall walk there, and the gathered of the Lord shall return, and come to Zion with songs and gladness, and everlasting joy upon their head; praise and joy and gladness shall overtake them; sorrow, sighing, and pain have fled away."

*Reading of the Prophecy of Isaiah (Chapter 55:1–13):*[^778]
Thus says the Lord: "All ye that thirst, go to the water; and as many as have no money, go ye and buy; and eat and drink wine and fat, without money and without price. Why do ye spend your money for that which is not bread, and your labor for that which satisfies not? Give ear diligently unto Me, and eat ye that which is good, and your soul shall delight itself in good things. Incline your ears, and follow My paths; hear Me, and your soul shall live in good things; and I will make an everlasting covenant with you, even the sure mercies of David. Behold, I have given him for a witness to the nations, a leader and commander to the nations. Behold, nations that knew thee not shall call upon thee, and peoples that knew thee not shall run unto thee, because of the Lord thy God, and for the Holy One of Israel; for I have glorified thee. Seek ye God, and when ye find Him, call upon Him. And when He shall draw near unto you, let the wicked forsake his ways, and the unrighteous man his counsels, and return unto the Lord your God, and ye shall find mercy, for He will abundantly pardon your sins. For My counsels are not as your counsels, neither are your ways My ways, says the Lord. For as the heaven is distant from the earth, so is My way distant from your ways, and your thoughts from My mind. For as the rain or the snow comes down from heaven, and returns not thither, but waters the earth, and makes it bring forth and bud, and gives seed to the sower, and bread for food: so shall My word be that goes forth out of My mouth; it shall not return unto Me void, until it shall accomplish all things that I willed, and I will prosper My ways and My commandments. For ye shall go out with joy, and be taught with gladness; for the mountains and hills shall skip, awaiting you with joy, and all the trees of the field shall clap their branches. And instead of the bramble shall come up the cypress, and instead of the nettle shall come up the myrtle; and the Lord shall be for a name, and for an everlasting sign, and shall not fail."

*Epistle to the Corinthians, Section 143 (1 Cor. 10:1–4):*[^780]
Brethren, I would not have you ignorant, that all our fathers were under the cloud, and all passed through the sea; and were all baptized unto Moses in the cloud and in the sea; and did all eat the same spiritual food; and did all drink the same spiritual drink; for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.

*Alleluia, Tone 4:*
The voice of the Lord is upon the waters; the God of glory hath thundered, the Lord is upon many waters.

*Gospel according to Mark, Section 2 (Mark 1:9–11):*[^781]
At that time, Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized by John in the Jordan. And straightway coming up out of the water, He saw the heavens opened, and the Spirit like a dove descending upon Him. And there came a voice from heaven, saying: "Thou art My beloved Son, in Whom I am well pleased."

*And the deacon says the litany:*
> **Deacon:** "In peace let us pray to the Lord."
*Choir:* Lord, have mercy.
> **Deacon:** "For the peace from above, and for the salvation of our souls, let us pray to the Lord."
For the peace of the whole world, the good estate of the holy churches of God, and the union of all, let us pray to the Lord.
For this holy temple, and for those who enter into it with faith, reverence, and the fear of God, let us pray to the Lord.
For our Most Reverend Archbishop [Name], and for our God-loving Bishop [Name],[^782] for the venerable priesthood, the diaconate in Christ, and for all the clergy and the people, let us pray to the Lord.
For our Great King [Name],[^783] let us pray to the Lord.
That He will subdue and humble under his feet every enemy and adversary, let us pray to the Lord.
For this holy monastery, and for every monastery, city, and countryside, and for the faithful dwelling in them, let us pray to the Lord.
For seasonable weather, for the abundance of the fruits of the earth, and for peaceful times, let us pray to the Lord.
For those who travel by sea or by land, for the sick, the suffering, for captives, and for their salvation, let us pray to the Lord.
That these waters may be sanctified by the power, operation, and descent of the Holy Spirit, let us pray to the Lord.
That there may be sent down upon these waters the cleansing operation of the supersubstantial Trinity, let us pray to the Lord.
That they may be for the cleansing of the souls and bodies of all who in faith draw from them, receive them, and partake of them, let us pray to the Lord.
That there may be granted unto them the grace of redemption, the blessing of the Jordan, by the power, operation, and descent of the Holy Spirit, let us pray to the Lord.
That Satan may quickly be crushed under our feet, and every wicked counsel directed against us be brought to naught, let us pray to the Lord.
That we may be enlightened with the illumination of understanding and piety, through the descent of the Holy Spirit, let us pray to the Lord.

That it may be a gift of sanctification, a cleansing of sins, unto the healing of soul and body, and for every surpassing benefit, let us pray to the Lord.
That it may be shown forth for the sanctification and salvation of our souls, let us pray to the Lord.
That it may be for the driving away and cleansing of every adverse power and assault of visible and invisible enemies, let us pray to the Lord.
That it may be shown forth as a medicine and cleansing of every infirmity of our souls and bodies, let us pray to the Lord.
That the power of the soul-destroying adversary may be drowned in this water, let us pray to the Lord.
That we who receive the sanctification of this water may be enlightened by the grace of Christ, let us pray to the Lord.
That it may be unto all who anoint themselves therewith in faith, or partake thereof, for the cleansing of defilement of flesh and spirit, let us pray to the Lord.
That the grace of purification of the supersubstantial Trinity may descend upon it, let us pray to the Lord.
For those who draw and drink of it unto the sanctification of souls and bodies, let us pray to the Lord.
That it may be a fountain of incorruption, and the sanctification of homes, let us pray to the Lord.
That it may be blessed even as the streams of Jordan, let us pray to the Lord.
That we may be accounted worthy to be filled with sanctification through the partaking of these waters, by the invisible manifestation of the Holy Spirit, let us pray to the Lord.
That we may be accounted worthy of the Heavenly Kingdom through the partaking of these waters, let us pray to the Lord.
That the Lord God will hear the voice of our supplication, and have mercy upon us, let us pray to the Lord.
That we may be delivered from all affliction, wrath, danger, and necessity, let us pray to the Lord.
Help us, save us, have mercy on us, and keep us, O God, by Thy grace.
Calling to remembrance our most holy, pure, most blessed and glorious Lady, the Birthgiver of God and ever-virgin Mary, with all the saints, let us commit ourselves and one another, and our whole life unto Christ our God.

*Exclamation:*
> **Priest:** "For Thou art a merciful God, and Lover of mankind, and unto Thee do we send up glory: to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages."
*Choir:* Amen.

*While these petitions are said by the deacon, the priest says secretly this prayer in himself. But if there be no deacon, he says it after the conclusion of the diaconal petitions:*
O Lord Jesus Christ, only-begotten Son, Who art in the bosom of the Father, True God, Fountain of life and immortality, Light of Light, Who didst come into the world to enlighten it: illumine our mind by Thy Holy Spirit, and receive us who offer Thee majesty and thanksgiving for Thy marvelous mighty deeds from the beginning of the world, and for Thy saving dispensation in the latter days; wherein, having clothed Thyself in our weak and low estate, and having condescended to the measure of a servant, O King of all, Thou didst moreover endure to be baptized by the hand of a servant in the Jordan, that having sanctified the nature of water, O Sinless One, Thou mightest make a way for our regeneration through water and the Spirit, and restore us unto our original freedom. Celebrating the commemoration of which divine mystery, we pray Thee, O Master, Lover of mankind: sprinkle also upon us, Thine unworthy servants, according to Thy divine promise, clean water, the gift of Thy compassions, so that over this water the supplication of us sinners may be acceptable through Thy goodness, and that Thy blessing may be granted through it unto us and unto all Thy faithful people, to the glory of Thy holy and adorable Name. For unto Thee is due all glory, honor, and worship, with Thine unoriginate Father, and Thy most holy and good and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages.

*And after the prayer he does not say an exclamation aloud, but softly says: "Amen." And when "Calling to remembrance our most holy, pure, most blessed..." is said, the priest again begins aloud this prayer: "Great art Thou, O Lord, and marvelous..." which is found below.*
*Note: But it should be known that the present prayer, that is: "O Supersubstantial Trinity," is read indeed in some places, but in the Great Church [of Constantinople] and on the Holy Mountain [of Athos] it is not said.[^784] But do thou, for the sake of the remembrance of the great divine mysteries therein, not omit it; but upon the completion of the litany and the above-written prayer, immediately say aloud, before "Great art Thou, O Lord," this prayer, the work of Sophronius, Patriarch of Jerusalem:*[^785]

*Prayer of Sophronius, Patriarch of Jerusalem:*
O Supersubstantial, All-good, and All-divine Trinity: Almighty, All-overseeing, invisible, incomprehensible, Creator of intellectual substances and rational natures, transcendent Goodness, Light unapproachable that enlightenest every man that comes into the world: shine forth also in me, Thine unworthy servant; enlighten the eyes of my understanding, that I may dare to hymn Thine immeasurable compassion and power; and let my prayer be acceptable for the people that stand here, and let not my sins and transgressions hinder Thy Holy Spirit from coming hither; but grant me without condemnation to cry unto Thee, and to say now, O All-good Trinity:[^786]
We glorify Thee, O Master, Lover of mankind, Almighty, pre-eternal King!
We glorify Thee, Creator and Fashioner of all!
We glorify Thee, without father from a mother, and without mother from a Father!
For in the preceding feast we beheld Thee as an infant, but in the present we see Thee as full-grown, manifest as our God, perfect from the Perfect.
For today the time of festival hath come upon us all, and the angels celebrate together with men, and the choir of the saints gathers with us.
For today the grace of the Most Holy Spirit, in the likeness of a dove, came down upon the waters.
Today the Sun that never sets hath arisen, and the world is illumined by the light of the Lord.
Today the moon with its bright rays enlightens all the earth.
Today the light-bearing stars adorn the universe with the brightness of their shining.
Today the clouds drop down from heaven the rain of righteousness upon mankind.
Today the Uncreated One of His own will has hands laid upon Him by His own creation.
Today the gathering of waters upon its shoulders lifts up the grace of sanctity.
Today the Invisible One becomes visible, that He may make us see Him.
Today the Prophet and Forerunner draws near unto the Creator with love, and stands with trembling, seeing God's condescension unto us.
Today the Unoriginate bows His neck unto His servant, that He may destroy the dragon dwelling in the waters.
Today the prophet's hand touches the crown of Him Who consumes with fire, that He may clothe us with the garment of incorruption.
Today the waters of Jordan are ordered into healing for men by the manifestation of our God.
Today through mystical streams all creation is watered.
Today the sins of men are washed away by the waters of Jordan.
Today paradise is opened unto men, and the Sun of Righteousness shines forth upon us.
Today the bitter water that was in the time of Moses for the people is turned into sweetness by the coming of the Lord.
Today we are delivered from the ancient lamentation, and like a new Israel have been saved.
Today we are set free from darkness, and are illumined with the light of the knowledge of God.
Today we put off the old bonds of sin, and are clothed in new robes.
Today the salt waters of the sea are changed into sweetness by Thy manifestation, O Master.
Today the gloom of the world is abolished by the manifestation of Christ our God.
Today all nature from above is brightly enlightened.
Today deceit is brought to naught, and the good coming prepares the way of salvation for us all.
Today the holy and Orthodox faith of the Church has shone forth, the spiritual festival of those who keep feast. Today the things above celebrate together with the things below, and the things below hold converse with the things above. Today the sacred and loud-voiced festival of the Orthodox rejoices. Today the Master hastens unto baptism, that He may lift up mankind to the heights. Today the Unbending One bows down unto His servant, that He may set us free from bondage. Today we have purchased the Heavenly Kingdom, for of the Kingdom of the Lord there is no end. Today the earth and the sea of this world have divided the joy, and the world is filled with gladness. The waters saw Thee, O God, the waters saw Thee, and were afraid; Jordan was driven back, having seen the fire of the Godhead bodily descending and entering into it. Jordan was driven back, seeing the Holy Spirit in the form of a dove descending and hovering round about it. Jordan was driven back, seeing the Invisible One made visible, the Creator incarnate, the Master in the form of a servant. Jordan was driven back, and the mountains skipped, seeing God in the flesh; and the clouds gave a voice, marveling at Him Who was come, Light of Light, True God of True God, seeing today in Jordan the Master's festival: and Him Who drowned in Jordan death itself, the fruit of transgression, and the sting of error, and the bonds of Hades, and granted unto the world the baptism of salvation. Therefore I also, Thy sinful and unworthy servant, declaring the greatness of Thy wonders, seized with fear, in compunction cry unto Thee:

*And straightway the priest begins aloud this prayer:*
"Great art Thou, O Lord, and marvelous are Thy works, and no word suffices to hymn Thy wonders!" *(Thrice. And he signs the water thrice with three burning candles).*[^787]
For of Thine own will Thou hast brought all things out of non-existence into being; and by Thy power Thou upholdest creation, and by Thy providence Thou orderest the world. Thou from four elements didst compound creation, and with four seasons hast crowned the circle of the year. Before Thee tremble all the spiritual powers; Thee the sun hymns; Thee the moon glorifies; Thee the stars attend; Thee the light obeys; before Thee the deeps shudder; Thee the springs serve. Thou didst stretch out the heaven like a curtain;[^788] Thou didst establish the earth upon the waters; Thou didst wall round the sea with sand; Thou didst pour out the air for breathing. The archangelic powers minister unto Thee;

the angelic choirs bow down before Thee; the many-eyed Cherubim and the six-winged Seraphim, standing round about and flying, cover themselves with fear of Thine unapproachable glory. For Thou, being God ineffable, unoriginate, and uncircumscribed,[^789] didst come down upon earth, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men; for Thou, O Master, through the tender mercy of Thy lovingkindness, couldst not endure to behold mankind tormented by the devil, but Thou didst come and save us. We confess Thy grace, we proclaim Thy mercy, we conceal not Thy benefactions. Thou hast set free the generations of our nature; Thou didst sanctify a virginal womb by Thy nativity; all creation hymns Thee Who hast appeared. For Thou, our God, hast appeared upon earth, and hast dwelt among men; Thou didst sanctify the streams of Jordan, having sent down from heaven Thy Holy Spirit, and didst crush the heads of the dragons nesting there.[^790]
Do Thou Thyself, therefore, O Lover of mankind, O King, come now also through the visitation of Thy Holy Spirit, and sanctify this water.
*The priest, saying this thrice, blesses the water with his hand, dipping his fingers crosswise at each verse; then he says this prayer:*
And grant unto it the grace of redemption, the blessing of Jordan; make it a fountain of incorruption, a gift of sanctification, a loosing of sins, a healing of infirmities, a total destruction of demons, unapproachable to hostile powers, filled with angelic strength; that all who draw thereof and partake thereof may have it for the purification of souls and bodies, for the healing of passions, for the sanctification of homes, and profitable unto every good purpose. For Thou art our God, Who by water and the Spirit didst renew our nature grown old through sin. Thou art our God, Who didst drown sin with water in the days of Noah. Thou art our God, Who by the sea didst deliver through Moses the Hebrew race from the bondage of Pharaoh. For Thou art our God, Who didst cleave the rock in the wilderness, and waters gushed forth, and streams overflowed, and didst satisfy Thy thirsting people.[^791] Thou art our God, Who by water and fire didst turn Israel through Elijah from the error of Baal.[^792]
Do Thou Thyself now also, O Master, sanctify this water by Thy Holy Spirit.
*And the priest makes the sign of the cross, having breathed upon the water crosswise thrice; after this he says:*
And grant unto all who touch it, and partake of it, and anoint themselves with it, sanctification, health, purification, and blessing.

And save, O Lord, the most holy Universal Hierarch, [Name], Pope of Rome, and Thy servant, our right-believing King, [Name] *(Thrice).*[^793]
And preserve them under Thy shelter in peace; and subdue under their feet every enemy and adversary; and grant unto them all petitions unto salvation, and life eternal. Remember, O Lord, the Archbishop [Name], or our Bishop [Name], all the presbyterate, the diaconate in Christ, and every priestly order; and the people standing here, and our brethren who have departed for blessed reasons; and have mercy on them and on us, according to Thy great mercy; that both by all the elements, and by angels, and by men, visible and invisible, Thy most holy name may be glorified, of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.
> **Priest:** "Peace be unto all."
> **Deacon:** "Bow your heads unto the Lord."
*The priest, having bowed down, prays secretly:*
Incline Thine ear, O Lord, and give ear unto us, Thou Who didst deign to be baptized in Jordan, and didst sanctify the waters; bless all of us who, by the bowing of our neck, signify our condition of servitude; and make us worthy to be filled with Thy sanctification through partaking of this water; and let it be for us, O Lord, unto the health of soul and body.
*Exclamation:*
For Thou art our sanctification, and unto Thee do we send up glory, and thanksgiving, and worship, together with Thine unoriginate Father, and Thy most holy and good and life-creating Spirit, now and ever, and unto ages of ages. Amen.
*And straightway, blessing the water crosswise with the precious cross, he immerses it upright, plunging it into the water and lifting it up, holding it with both hands, singing this troparion in Tone 1:*
When Thou, O Lord, wast baptized in Jordan, the worship of the Trinity was made manifest; for the voice of the Parent bore witness unto Thee, calling Thee the beloved Son, and the Spirit in the form of a dove confirmed the certainty of the word. O Christ God Who hast appeared and enlightened the world, glory to Thee!
*And in like manner he signs the water with the cross a second time, and in like manner a third time, the superior himself singing the same troparion, and the other priests singing with him. Then the choirs also sing the same troparion. And the superior, having taken the holy water in a vessel, and having turned his face toward the west, holding the precious cross in his left hand, and in his right hand with basil sprinkles crosswise in all directions.[^794] And the other priests approach* unto the superior, two by two, and kiss the precious cross, and he signs them with basil on the face with the holy water crosswise; in the same order also all the brethren. Then the troparion is sung by all many times, until all the brethren are sanctified by the sprinkling of water and by partaking.
*And straightway we enter into the church, and sing the sticheron:*
*Glory, and now, Tone 6:*
Let us believers hymn the greatness of God's benefaction concerning us! For having become man on account of our transgression, He is purified in Jordan for our purification: the only pure and incorrupt One, sanctifying me and the waters, and crushing the heads of the dragons in the water. Let us draw water, therefore, with gladness, O brethren! For the grace of the Spirit is invisibly bestowed by Christ God, the Savior of our souls, upon those who draw with faith.
*Then:*
Blessed be the name of the Lord, from this time forth and forevermore.
*(Thrice, and Psalm 33:)* I will bless the Lord at all times:
*And antidoron is given by the priest, and the dismissal.*
*After the dismissal, whether there is a Liturgy or not, a candle-stand is set in the midst of the church, and the clerics, both choirs standing together, sing the troparion of the feast:*
*Glory, and now, Kontakion.*
*And we enter into the refectory, and eat with oil; and we also drink wine.*
*Cheese, however, and what is similar to it, and fish we in no wise dare to eat; for it is forbidden by the divine canons.*
*Thus is the service done when it is a fast day on the eve of the Enlightenment.*
*Instruction concerning the Holy Water.* *(Note)*
*Be it known unto all concerning the holy water:* That some who keep themselves from tasting holy water on account of food do not do well; for on account of God's grace it was given for the sanctification of the world and of all creation. Therefore in all places, even unclean ones, and everywhere it is sprinkled, which are even under our feet. And where is their reason not to drink of it? But let them know that it is not on account of tasting food that there is defilement in us, but from our unclean deeds; and having been cleansed from these, we drink this holy water without hesitation.
Concerning this water that spiritual swallow, the golden-worded ecumenical teacher, John, Patriarch of Constantinople, made known in his homily On Christians Gathering in the Holy Church of God[^795] church, and concerning the Baptism, the incipit of which is:
*All of you are in good cheer today, but I alone am in affliction through sickness.*[^796]
He testifies, saying: "Therefore, then, is not the day on which He was born called the Theophany [Manifestation], but the day on which He was baptized? For this is the day on which He was baptized and sanctified the nature of waters. For this reason also, at midnight on this feast, all draw water, carry it to their homes, and preserve it, keeping it through the whole year, since it is the day of sanctified waters. And an evident sign occurs, in that the nature of those waters is not corrupted by length of time; but for a whole year, and two, and three, and often for many years, the water drawn today remains whole and fresh, and after so long a time compares with waters taken freshly from springs."
*(Note)* *It is fitting also to know this:*
*That if the eve of the Holy Theophany falls on a Saturday or a Sunday, there is no fast.*[^797]
*And the Liturgy of Chrysostom is celebrated in its own time according to custom, as always.*
*And after the dismissal of the Liturgy we do not go to the refectory; but as we sit in the church porch, the refectorian gives a piece of bread to each, or a small wheaten loaf, and a few figs and dates, and one cup of wine, so that it may not be called a fast; and we await the evening gathering. After this, having departed to our cells, we keep silence until the evening time.*
*And the Liturgy of Basil the Great is celebrated on the feast day itself; and instead of "It is truly meet," we sing the heirmos of Ode 9 of the feast.*[^798]
*And at the evening hour of the day, the great bell is sounded, and then all the heavy bells; and when we are gathered in the temple and the priest has given the blessing, we sing Vespers according to custom: the Psalm, "Bless the Lord, O my soul." If it be Saturday evening, we sing "Blessed is the man," the entire kathisma. But if it be Sunday evening, we sing the first antiphon. At "Lord, I have cried," we sing the stichera of the feast, on 8, Tone 2: "Our Enlightener"; Glory, and now, same Tone: "Thou didst bow Thy head unto the Forerunner"; then, the Entrance with the Gospel* "O Gladsome Light." The Prokimenon of the day, and the readings according to their order, with the troparia and their verses. But the Trisagion we do not sing, since the Divine Liturgy is not celebrated. And after the reading of the paremias, the Little Litany; and after the exclamation, the Prokimenon, Epistle, and Gospel, as prescribed above. The Litany, "Let us all say," and "Vouchsafe, O Lord," and we complete the evening prayer; the priest says the exclamation. And we go forth unto the baptistery [font], where a table is prepared, and the superior or priest officiates according to the order, as was indicated before, while they sing the troparia: "The voice of the Lord is upon the waters"; and the rest of the rite of the blessing of water takes place without change. And after the sprinkling of the holy water, we enter into the church and sing the sticheron: *Glory, and now, Tone 6:* "Let us believers hymn"; and the dismissal. Then the troparion of the feast; *Glory, and now, Kontakion:* "Thou hast appeared today"; and having drunk the holy water, we enter into the refectory, and eat fully, with oil, and we drink wine.
*(Note)* *It is fitting to know:*
*That on whatever day the feast of the Holy Theophany falls, we sing Great Compline thus:*
*At the tenth hour of the night the bells are rung, and then a chime on all the bells. And the priest, having vested together with the deacon, makes the beginning, as on all the feasts of the Lord. The deacon says:* **"Bless, Master."** *The priest:* **"Blessed is our God."** *And while the priest censes, we say Great Compline from the beginning: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee," "O Heavenly King," the Trisagion, and the rest. "God is with us" we sing with melody; and instead of the usual troparia, "Enlighten my eyes," we say the troparion of the feast; and instead of "Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us," we say the kontakion of the feast. After the Doxology, the Litya takes place according to custom.*
*And at the Litya we sing the automela stichera, Tone 4:*
*By Monk Cosmas:*
He Who clothes Himself with light as with a garment, having deigned for our sake to become like unto us, is clothed today in the streams of Jordan; not Himself having need of them for purification, but ordering our regeneration through Himself. O the wonder! Without fire He refines, and He builds up without destroying, and saves those who are enlightened in Him, Christ God and the Savior of our souls.
*[By the same, same Tone:]*
Seeing Him Who is the divine Spirit and fire that purifies the sin of the world coming unto him, the Baptist was seized with dread and, trembling, cried aloud, saying: "I dare not touch Thy most-pure head; do Thou Thyself sanctify me, O Master, by Thy divine manifestation, O only Lover of mankind!"
Come, let us imitate the wise virgins; come, let us meet the Master Who has appeared; for He has come as a Bridegroom unto John. Jordan, having seen Thee, was afraid and halted; John cried aloud: "I dare not hold the head of the Immortal One!" The Spirit was descending in the form of a dove to sanctify the waters; and a voice came from heaven: "This is My Son, Who has come into the world to save the human race; O Lord, glory to Thee!"
Christ is baptized, and comes up from the water, for He raises the world up with Himself; and He beholds the heavens opening, which Adam closed against himself and those with him. And the Spirit bears witness to the Godhead, for He runs beforehand unto His Like; and a voice from heaven, for from thence is He testified of, the Savior of our souls.
The hand of the Baptist trembled when it touched Thy most pure head; the river Jordan turned back, not daring to minister unto Thee. For if it was held in awe before Joshua, the son of Nun, how should it not have feared its own Creator? But Thou didst fulfill all the dispensation, O Savior, that Thou mightest save the world by Thy manifestation, O only Lover of mankind.
*Glory, Tone 8:*
*By Monk John:*
O Lord, desiring to fulfill what Thou didst ordain from the ages, Thou didst receive from all creation ministers of Thy mystery: from the angels, Gabriel; from men, the Virgin; from the heavens, the star; and from the waters, Jordan; in which Thou didst do away with the iniquity of the world. O our Savior, glory to Thee!
*Now, same Tone:*
*By Anatolios:*
Today creation is enlightened; today all things rejoice, heavenly things together with earthly; angels and men mingle together. For where the King comes, there also comes His host. Let us hasten therefore unto Jordan, and let us all see John, how he baptizes the uncreated and sinless head! Therefore, chanting the apostolic voice, let us cry out in unison: "The grace of God that brings salvation unto all men hath appeared,[^799] illuminating and granting great mercy unto the faithful!"
*At the Aposticha, automela stichera, Tone 2:*
*By Anatolios:*
Having seen Thee coming unto him at the river Jordan, John said: "O Christ God, why hast Thou come unto Thy servant, having no defilement, O Lord? And in whose name shall I baptize Thee? In the name of the Father? But Thou bearest Him in Thyself! In the name of the Son? But Thou art Thyself the incarnate One! In the name of the Holy Spirit? And this Thou knowest how to give unto the faithful with Thy breath! O God Who hast appeared, have mercy on us!"
*Verse:* The sea saw and fled, Jordan turned back.[^800]
The waters saw Thee, O God, the waters saw Thee and were afraid;[^801] for the Cherubim cannot gaze against Thy glory, nor can the Seraphim look upon it; but standing by with fear, the ones bear Thee up, and the others glorify Thy power. With them, O Compassionate One, we proclaim Thy praise, saying: "O God Who hast appeared, have mercy on us!"
*Verse:* What ailed thee, O sea, that thou fleddest? And thou, O Jordan, that thou wast driven back?[^802]
Today the Creator of heaven and earth comes in the flesh unto Jordan, asking for baptism, the Sinless One, that He may cleanse the world from the deceit of the enemy; and the Master of all is baptized by a servant, and grants purification through water unto the human race. Unto Him let us cry aloud: "O our God Who hast appeared, glory to Thee!"
*Glory, and now, Tone 8:*
*By Theophanes:*
Seeing the Sun Who shone forth from the Virgin, the radiant luminary born of a barren mother, asking for baptism in Jordan, cried unto Him in awe and joy: "Do Thou Thyself sanctify me, O Master, by Thy divine manifestation!"
*Then:* Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart:
*Trisagion. After Our Father:*
*Troparion of the feast, Tone 1:*
When Thou, O Lord, wast baptized in Jordan, the worship of the Trinity was made manifest; for the voice of the Parent bore witness unto Thee, calling Thee the beloved Son, and the Spirit in the form of a dove confirmed the certainty of the word. O Christ God Who hast appeared and enlightened the world, glory to Thee! *(Thrice).*
*And the blessing of the loaves according to custom. Then:* Blessed be the name of the Lord: *(Thrice. And the Psalm:)* I will bless the Lord at all times: *unto:* shall not lack any good thing.[^803] *And the reading of the feast.*
*And after the reading and after the Six Psalms, at "God is the Lord," the troparion of the feast, thrice; and the usual stichologies.*
*After the first stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 3, Podoben: "Awed by the beauty of thy virginity" (Красотѣ̀ дѣ́вства):*
When Thou didst appear in Jordan, O Savior, and wast baptized by the Forerunner, O Christ, Thou wast testified of as the beloved Son; therefore also Thou wast revealed as co-unoriginate with the Father; and the Holy Spirit descended upon Thee, through Whom also being enlightened we cry aloud: "Glory to God Who is in Trinity!"
*Glory, and now, Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*
Thou hast sanctified the streams of Jordan, Thou didst crush the dominion of sin, O Christ our God; Thou didst bow Thyself unto the hand of the Forerunner, and didst save the human race from deception. Therefore we entreat Thee: save our souls!
*After the second stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 5, Podoben: "Co-unoriginate Word" (Собезнача́лное сло́во):*
He Who is most gloriously clothed with light[^804] is encompassed by the streams of Jordan; wherein Thou, O Word of God, hast renewed the nature of Adam, crushed by evil disobedience. Therefore we praise Thee, and we all glorify Thy holy manifestation!
*Glory, and now, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph marveled" (Оу҆диви́ся i҆ѡ́сифъ):*
"O river Jordan, why art thou amazed, beholding the Invisible One naked?" "I saw and trembled," he said; "and how was I not to be afraid and turn back? His angels trembled as they looked upon Him; heaven was dismayed, and earth trembled, and the sea was troubled, and all things visible and invisible. Christ appeared at the Jordan to sanctify the waters!"
*And the reading of the feast. After the Polyeleos, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph marveled" (Оу҆диви́ся i҆ѡ́сифъ):*
Come, let us believers see where Christ was baptized! Let us follow therefore unto the river Jordan, unto the voice of him who cries in the wilderness; and we shall see there the Maker of Adam, having hands laid upon Him by a servant's hand on account of His ineffable compassion; and let us cry out unto Him with a loud voice: "Thou hast come and appeared in Jordan to sanctify the waters!"
*Glory, and now, the same. And the reading. Gradual Hymns, the first antiphon of Tone 4.*
*Prokimenon, Tone 4:* The sea saw and fled, Jordan turned back. *Verse:* What ailed thee, O sea, that thou fleddest? And thou, O Jordan, that thou wast driven back? *Let every breath:*
*Gospel of Mark, pericope 2.*[^805]
*After Psalm 50, Glory, Tone 2:*
Let all things rejoice today, Christ having appeared in Jordan! *Now, the same.*
*Then the idiomelon sticheron, Tone 6:*
God the Word appeared in the flesh unto the human race; He stood to be baptized in Jordan, and the Forerunner said unto Him: "How shall I stretch forth my hand, and touch the head of Him Who holds all things? Though Thou art an infant from Mary, yet I know Thee as God before the ages! Thou walkest upon the earth, praised by the Seraphim, and I, a servant, have not learned to baptize the Master. Incomprehensible Lord, glory to Thee!"
*Two canons: the heirmoi of both canons twice, and the troparia on 12. At the conclusion, the first choir sings the heirmos of the first canon, and the second choir the heirmos of the second canon.*
*The first canon, the composition of kyr Cosmas the Monk.*[^806]
*Its acrostic: Baptism is the purification of the sins of earthborn men.*[^807] *Tone 2.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
The Lord mighty in battles has uncovered the bottom of the deep, and leads His own through the dry land, having covered the adversaries therein; for He is glorified![^808]
*Troparion:*
The Lord, King of the ages, renews corrupted Adam by the streams of Jordan, and crushes the heads of the dragons nesting there; for He is glorified!
*Troparion:*
Having clothed Himself in material flesh with the immaterial fire of the Godhead, the Lord, incarnate of the Virgin, is wrapped about with the water of Jordan; for He is glorified!
*Troparion:*
Washing away the filth of men, the Lord, having become like them as He willed, yet remaining what He was, was purified in Jordan, enlightening those in darkness; for He is glorified!
*Another canon, the composition of John of Damascus.*[^809] *Tone 2.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Israel traverses the billowing storm of the sea, having manifestly seen the dry land; while the dark deep covered the Egyptian captains together in a watery grave, by the mighty strength of the Master's right hand.[^810]
*Troparion:*
When the light-bearing dawn appeared unto men, Thou, O King of the sun, didst now bow Thy neck from the wilderness unto the waters of Jordan, to snatch away the gloomy choir of the forefather, and to cleanse creation of every defilement.
*Troparion:*
O unoriginate Word, buried together with the streams for him whom Thou didst restore anew, corrupted by deceit, Thou didst ineffably receive from the Father this mighty voice: "This is My beloved Child, equal to Me by nature!"
*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
The Lord Who gives strength unto our kings, and exalts the horn of His anointed ones,[^811] is born of the Virgin, and comes unto baptism; unto Him let us believers cry aloud: "There is none holy like our God!"[^812]
*Troparion:*
Rejoice today, O Church of Christ, she that was formerly barren and grievously childless; for by water and the Spirit sons have been born unto thee, crying out in faith: "There is none holy like our God!"
*Troparion:*
With a loud voice the Forerunner cries in the wilderness: "Prepare ye the ways of Christ, and make straight the paths for our God,[^813] crying out in faith: 'There is none holy like our God!'"[^814]
*Another, Heirmos [Iambic]:*
As many of us as have been loosed from the ancient snares of the lions whose jaws were broken in pieces,[^815] let us rejoice and open wide our mouth, weaving a word of melodious song, whereby He delights in the gifts bestowed upon us.
*Troparion:*
He who previously planted mortification in creation, transformed into the nature of a maleficent beast, is darkened by the bodily coming; having rushed at daybreak against the Master, to crush his own hostile head.
*Troparion:*
The nature fashioned by God, buried in the bounds of the tyrant's belly, He draws unto Himself; the regeneration of earthborn men is born anew, the Master mightily accomplishing the work; for He has come, desiring to cleanse it.
*Hypakoe, Tone 5:*
When by Thy manifestation Thou didst enlighten all things, then the salty sea of unbelief fled, and Jordan flowing downward turned back, lifting us up unto heaven; but by the height of Thy divine commandments, O Christ God, preserve us through the prayers of the Birthgiver of God, and have mercy on us.
*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I heard, O Lord, Thy voice which Thou didst speak, the voice of him who cries in the wilderness, when Thou didst thunder over many waters,[^816] bearing witness unto Thy Son; being filled with the Spirit Who descended, he cried: "Thou art Christ, the Wisdom and Power of God!"[^817]
*Troparion:*
"Who has seen the sun, which is exceedingly bright by nature, being cleansed?" cries the preacher. "Shall I then wash with waters Thee, the radiance of glory, the express image of the ever-existing Father?[^818] And shall I, being grass, touch the fire of Thy Godhead? For Thou art Christ, the Wisdom and Power of God!"
*Troparion:*
"Moses showed the divine reverence which he had when he fell down before Thee; for when he understood that Thou didst speak from the bush, he straightway turned away his face;[^819] but how shall I behold Thee openly? Or how shall I lay my hand upon Thee? For Thou art Christ, the Wisdom and Power of God!"
*Troparion:*
"Performing that which belongs to the soul wisely, and honored with speech, I yet stand in awe of inanimate things. For if I baptize Thee, the mountain smoking with fire will accuse me;[^820] the sea that fled in twain, and this Jordan that turned back! For Thou art Christ, the Wisdom and Power of God!"[^821]

*Another, Heirmos [Iambic]:*
Cleansed by the fire of mystical contemplation, the prophet, singing the renewal of mortal men, lifts up his voice, inspired by the Spirit, revealing the incarnation of the ineffable Word, by Whom the dominion of the mighty was shattered.[^822]

*Troparion:*
Sent forth from the Father, O all-radiant Word, to drive away the dark and evil assault of the night, and to uproot the sins of men, Thou comest, O Good One, to draw forth radiant sons by Thy baptism from the streams of the Jordan.

*Troparion:*
Having clearly foreseen the renown Word Himself, the herald cries aloud unto creation: "This is He Who was before me,[^823] yet second in the flesh, radiant in the likeness of our form by divine power, to take away our hostile sin!"[^824]

*Troparion:*
Carrying within Himself life-giving pasture, God the Word catches the dragons, rushing upon their nests with many snares; and having overthrown him who wounded the universal race of man, having destroyed him, He delivers creation.[^825]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Jesus, the Prince of Life,[^826] comes to loose the condemnation of Adam the first-formed; and needing no purification as God, He cleanses the fallen in the Jordan, wherein, having slain the enmity, He grants the peace that surpasses all understanding.[^827]

*Troparion:*
When countless multitudes came together to be baptized by John, he himself stood in their midst, and proclaimed unto those who were present: "Who has warned you, O disobedient ones, to flee from the wrath to come?[^828] Bring forth fruits worthy for Christ; for being now present, He grants peace!"

*Troparion:*
The Husbandman and Creator, standing in the midst as one of all, searches the hearts; and taking the purifying winnowing-fan in His hand,[^829] He all-wisely separates the universal threshing floor, burning the unfruitfulness, while unto the fruitful He grants eternal life.

*Another, Heirmos [Iambic]:*
Washed by the cleansing of the Spirit from the venom of the dark and defiled enemy, we have attained unto a new, unerring path, leading unto inaccessible joy, accessible only unto those with whom God has been reconciled.

*Troparion:*
Having seen him whom He fashioned with His fingers bound in the darkness of transgressions with inescapable chains,[^830] the Creator raises him up and sets him upon both His shoulders;[^831] now in the abundant waters washing away the shame of old and the evil nature of Adam.

*Troparion:*
With piety let us eagerly run unto the pure fountains of saving streams, beholding the Word from the incorrupt Virgin, bringing drawing-vessels for our divine thirst, sweetly healing the sickness of the world.[^832]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
The voice of the Word, the lamp of the Light,[^833] the morning star, the Forerunner of the Sun, cries aloud in the wilderness unto all the peoples: "Repent and be cleansed beforehand; for behold, Christ is present, delivering the world from corruption!"[^834]

*Troparion:*
Born incorruptibly from God and the Father, Christ is incarnate without defilement from the Virgin; the strap of Whose sandal—the conjunction of the Word with us—the Forerunner teaches that it is hard to loose,[^835] delivering the earthborn from deceit.

*Troparion:*
With final fire Christ baptizes the adversaries who acknowledge Him not as God;[^836] but by the Spirit He renews through the water of grace those who recognize His Godhead, delivering them from transgressions.

*Another, Heirmos [Iambic]:*
With an all-blessed voice the Father revealed the Beloved Whom He brought forth from the womb:[^837] "Yea," He says, "this My Son, being of one essence and radiant with light, has sprung forth from the human race, My living Word, and a mortal man by divine providence!"[^838]

*Troparion:*
From the deep-dwelling beast, the prophet who spent three nights strangely tossed within its entrails came forth anew, foreshadowing unto all in the latter days the salvation of regeneration from the man-slaying serpent.[^839]

*Troparion:*
The initiate beholds the Spirit sent forth from the Father from the opened expanse of the all-radiant heavens, and resting upon the all-pure Word, having descended in an ineffable manner as a dove,[^840] and reveals Him unto the peoples who have come unto the Master.

*Kontakion, Tone 4:*
Today Thou hast appeared unto the universe, and Thy light, O Lord, has been signed upon us,[^841] who with understanding chant unto Thee: Thou hast come and hast appeared, the Inaccessible Light![^842]

*Ikos:*
Unto Galilee of the Gentiles, unto the country of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, as the prophet said, a great light, Christ, has shone upon those who were darkened.[^843] A radiant dawn has appeared, shining forth from Bethlehem, or rather the Lord from Mary, the Sun of Righteousness,[^844] sending forth rays unto the whole universe. Therefore, all ye who are naked from Adam, come, let us clothe ourselves in Him, that we may be warmed; for He covers the naked and enlightens the darkened: Thou hast come and hast appeared, the Inaccessible Light!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
When the pious youths were cast into the fiery furnace, the moist, whistling breath of the wind and the descent of the angel of God preserved them unharmed;[^845] therefore, bedewed in the midst of the flame, they gratefully sang: "O most praised Lord and God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!"[^846]

*Troparion:*
Just as in heaven, the angelic Powers stood in the Jordan with trembling and wonder, beholding so great a condescension of God: how He Who holds the structure of the waters above the heavens stood in the waters clothed in the flesh,[^847] the God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Of old the cloud and the sea prefigured the marvel of divine baptism, wherein the ancient people of the Law were baptized as they departed;[^848] the sea was an image of the water, and the cloud of the Spirit; initiated by which, we cry aloud: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto ages!"

*Troparion:*
All we faithful, in Whom we have received perfection, theologizing ceaselessly with the angels, let us glorify the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit; for behold, the Trinity is consubstantial in hypostases, yet one God, unto Whom we sing: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto ages!"

*Another, Heirmos [Iambic]:*
He Who quenched the soaring flame of the furnace that enclosed the pious youths has burned up the heads of the dragons in the stream,[^849] and washes away all the uncontrollable gloom of sin with the dew of the Spirit.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst depict Thyself by transforming into dew the dread Assyrian flame;[^850] therefore, the water, now clothing Thyself as a flame, O Christ, burns up the harmful, hidden malice, calling [us] back from the slippery path.

*Troparion:*
When the Jordan was divided of old, the people of Israel passed through on dry ground,[^851] portraying Thee, the Most Mighty, Who unhesitatingly upholdest creation, now in the waters, [guiding them] unto an incorruptible and profitable path.

*Troparion:*
The all-destroying deluge of old washed away [the ungodly], mercifully purposing to bring them to corruption, working strange and purging wonders; but now, O Christ, having drowned sin out of loving-kindness, Thou hast wrought human salvation![^852]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
The Babylonian furnace showed forth a marvelous mystery, pouring forth dew, because the Jordan was to receive in its streams the immaterial Fire, and to encompass the Creator baptized in the flesh; Whom the peoples bless and supreme-exalt unto all ages![^853]

*Troparion:*
"Put away all fear," the Deliverer said unto the Forerunner, "and obey Me as the Good One; draw near unto Me, for this I became by nature; yield unto My command and baptize Me Who have descended; Whom the peoples bless and supreme-exalt unto all ages!"[^854]

*Troparion:*
When the Baptist heard the words of the Master, with trembling he stretched forth his palm; yet having touched with his hand the head of his Creator, he cried unto Him Who was baptized: "Sanctify me, for Thou art my God; Whom the peoples bless and supreme-exalt unto all ages!"

*Troparion:*
The manifestation of the Trinity took place in the Jordan; for the supreme-divine Nature Itself—the Father proclaimed: "This He Who is baptized is My beloved Son!"[^855] and the Spirit came upon His Equal; Whom the peoples bless and supreme-exalt unto all ages!

*Another, Heirmos [Iambic]:*
Creation is known to be set free, and they who were formerly darkened are now sons of light; the champion of darkness alone groans; now let the formerly wretched inheritance of the Gentiles eagerly bless the Author of its salvation.[^856]

*Troparion:*
Bedewed in the fire and illumined by three all-radiant hypostases, the three God-beholding youths clearly showed forth the supreme Nature, Which by human admixture, through dew, mercifully consumes in fire every destructive deceit.[^857]

*Troparion:*
Let every earthly nature be clothed in white, now lifted up from its fall unto heaven; for washed in the flowing streams by the Word by Whom all things are preserved,[^858] and brightly cleansed, it has fled from the former defilement of transgressions.

*At Ode 9 the brethren light the candles again. We do not sing "More honorable," but we sing the refrains of the feast:*
*Refrain:*
*Magnify, O my soul, the most honorable Virgin, the all-pure Birthgiver of God, higher than the hosts on high!*

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Every tongue is at a loss to praise thee according to thy worth, and even an intellect beyond this world is dazed in singing thy praise, O Birthgiver of God; nevertheless, since thou art good, accept our faith, for thou knowest our divine longing; for thou art the protectress of Christians, and thee do we magnify![^859]

*Then the second choir sings the same refrain and heirmos. And the remaining six refrains are sung once before each troparion:*
*Refrain:*
*Magnify, O my soul, Him Who asks baptism of the Forerunner!*

*Refrain:*
*Magnify, O my soul, Him Who comes to be baptized in the Jordan!*

*Troparion:*
Come in the Spirit, ye who are enlightened, and let us now draw near, singing unto God with faith: "This poor Adam cried out in his fall, and the Lord heard him;[^860] and coming in the streams of the Jordan, He renewed the corrupt one!"

*Refrain:*
*Magnify, O my soul, Him Who was testified unto by the Father's voice!*

*Refrain:*
*Magnify, O my soul, One of the Trinity Who bowed His neck and received baptism!*

*Troparion:*
"Wash yourselves, make yourselves clean," says Isaiah; "put away your evil deeds from before the Lord;[^861] ye that thirst, go unto the living water;[^862] for Christ sprinkles renewing water upon those who run unto Him in faith, and baptizes with the Spirit unto life that grows not old!"

*Refrain:*
*O Prophet, come unto Me, stretch forth thy hand and baptize Me quickly!*

*Refrain:*
*O Prophet, suffer it now and baptize Me Who desire it, for I have come to fulfill all righteousness!*[^863]

*Troparion:*
We the faithful are preserved by grace and by the seal; for as of old the Hebrews escaped destruction because the doorposts were smeared with blood,[^864] so also this divine font of regeneration shall be for us an exodus,[^865] whence also we shall behold the unwaning light of the Trinity!

*Then the first choir sings the refrain of the second canon:*
*Refrain:*
*Today the Master bows His neck beneath the hand of the Forerunner!*

*Another, Heirmos [Iambic]:*
O marvels of thy childbearing surpassing understanding, O all-pure Bride, blessed Mother! Through whom having obtained all-perfect salvation, we worthily praise Him as our Benefactor, bringing as a gift a song of thanksgiving.[^866]

*And the second choir likewise sings the refrain and the heirmos; and the other five refrains, one of them twice:*
*Refrain:*
*Today John baptizes the Master in the streams of the Jordan!*

*Refrain:*
*Today the Master buries human sin in the waters!*

*Troparion:*
We have known that which was shown unto Moses in the bush,[^867] now accomplished here by strange ordinances; for as the Virgin was preserved unharmed though bearing fire, having given birth unto the light-bearing Benefactor, so is He now revealed in the streams of the Jordan!

*Refrain:*
*Today the Master is testified unto from on high as the beloved Son!*

*Refrain:*
*Today the Master comes to sanctify the nature of the waters!*

*Refrain:*
*Today the Master receives baptism by the hand of the Forerunner!*

*Troparion:*
O King without beginning, by the communion of the Spirit Thou hast anointed and made perfect the human essence, having washed it from darkness with clean streams; and Thou hast put to shame the exalted might of the foe, now transforming us unto unending life.

*Then both choirs, having come together, sing the first refrain of the feast and the heirmos: "Every tongue is at a loss..." Then the refrain of the second canon and the heirmos: "O marvels of thy childbearing..." And a prostration.*

*Exapostilarion, Tone 3, Podoben: "Thou hast visited us" (Посѣти́лъ ны̀):*
The grace and truth of the Savior have appeared in the streams of the Jordan,[^868] and He has enlightened those that were sleeping in darkness and the shadow of death;[^869] for He has come and appeared, the Inaccessible Light! *(Thrice)*

*At the Praises, Stichera on 4, Tone 1, by Patriarch Germanus:*
*Sticheron 1:*
Light from Light, Christ our God has shone upon the world, God Who has appeared; unto Him, O ye peoples, let us bow down!

*Sticheron 2:*
How shall we servants worthily honor Thee, the Master, O Christ? For in the waters Thou hast renewed us all!

*Sticheron 3:*
When Thou wast baptized in the Jordan, O our Savior, Thou didst sanctify the waters, having the hand of the servant laid upon Thee,[^870] and healing the passions of the world. Great is the mystery of Thy dispensation! O Lord Who lovest mankind, glory to Thee!

*Sticheron 4:*
The True Light has appeared and grants enlightenment unto all![^871] Christ, Who is higher than all purity, is baptized with us; He puts sanctification into the water, and it becomes a cleansing for souls; that which appears is earthly, but that which is understood is higher than the heavens; through the washing comes salvation, and through the water the Spirit; through immersion our ascent unto God is accomplished. Marvelous are Thy works, O Lord, glory to Thee![^872]

*Glory..., Tone 6, by Anatolius:*
Thou hast clothed Thyself with the waters of the Jordan, O Savior, Who clothest Thyself with light as with a garment;[^873] and Thou didst bow Thy head unto the Forerunner, Thou Who didst measure heaven with a span,[^874] that Thou mightest turn the world away from deceit, and save it as the Lover of mankind!

*Both now..., Tone 2, by the same:*
Today Christ has come to be baptized in the Jordan; today John touches the head of the Master; the powers of the heavens were astonished, beholding the marvelous mystery; the sea saw and fled, Jordan seeing it turned back![^875] But we who are enlightened cry aloud: "Glory to God Who has appeared, and was seen on earth, and has enlightened the world!"

*The Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, the troparion of the feast. Litanies and dismissal. And holy sanctified water is given, while we sing the sticheron of the feast.*
*Then the First Hour. At the First Hour, the troparion of the feast; after the Trisagion, the kontakion of the feast, and the rest; and the complete dismissal. On this day the Liturgy is celebrated early, on account of the blessed At the Liturgy, Antiphon 1, Psalm 113, Tone 1:*[^876]
*Verse 1:* When Israel went out of Egypt, the house of Jacob from a barbarous people.[^877]
*Through the prayers of the Birthgiver of God, O Savior, save us!*
*And the other choir:*
*Verse 2:* Judea became His sanctuary, and Israel His dominion.[^878]
*Through the prayers of the Birthgiver of God, O Savior, save us!*
*Verse 3:* The sea saw it, and fled; Jordan was driven back.[^879]
*Through the prayers of the Birthgiver of God, O Savior, save us!*
*Verse 4:* What ailed thee, O sea, that thou didst flee? and thou, Jordan, that thou wast driven back?[^880]
*Through the prayers of the Birthgiver of God, O Savior, save us!*
*Glory..., Both now...:*
*Through the prayers of the Birthgiver of God, O Savior, save us!*

*Antiphon 2, Psalm 114, Tone 2:*[^881]
