*Verse 1:* I am well pleased that the Lord will hear the voice of my supplication.[^882]
*Save us, O Son of God, Who wast baptized in the Jordan, who sing unto Thee: Alleluia!*
*Verse 2:* For He has inclined His ear unto me, and in my days I will call upon Him.[^883]
*Save us, O Son of God, Who wast baptized in the Jordan, who sing unto Thee: Alleluia!*
*Verse 3:* The sorrows of death compassed me, the perils of hades found me; I found affliction and sorrow, and I called upon the name of the Lord.[^884]
*Save us, O Son of God, Who wast baptized in the Jordan, who sing unto Thee: Alleluia!*
*Verse 4:* Merciful is the Lord, and righteous; yea, our God is merciful.[^885]
*Save us, O Son of God, Who wast baptized in the Jordan, who sing unto Thee: Alleluia!*
*Glory..., Both now...:*
*Only-begotten Son...*

*Antiphon 3, Psalm 117, Tone 1:*[^886]
*Verse 1:* O give thanks unto the Lord, for He is good; for His mercy endures unto ages.[^887]
*Troparion, Tone 1:*
When Thou wast baptized in the Jordan, O Lord, the worship of the Trinity was made manifest; for the voice of the Parent bore witness unto Thee, calling Thee His beloved Son, and the Spirit in the form of a dove confirmed the certainty of the word. O Christ God Who hast appeared and hast enlightened the world, glory to Thee![^888]
*Verse 2:* Let the house of Israel now say, that He is good, that His mercy endures unto ages.[^889]
*When Thou wast baptized in the Jordan, O Lord...*
*Verse 3:* Let the house of Aaron now say, that He is good, that His mercy endures unto ages.[^890]
*When Thou wast baptized in the Jordan, O Lord...*
*Verse 4:* Let all that fear the Lord now say, that He is good, that His mercy endures unto ages.[^891]
*When Thou wast baptized in the Jordan, O Lord...*

*Entrance Hymn:*
Blessed is He that comes in the name of the Lord; we have blessed you out of the house of the Lord; God is the Lord, and has appeared unto us![^892]
*When Thou wast baptized in the Jordan, O Lord...*
*Glory..., Both now...:*
*Kontakion, Tone 4:*
Today Thou hast appeared unto the universe, and Thy light, O Lord, has been signed upon us, who with understanding chant unto Thee: Thou hast come and hast appeared, the Inaccessible Light!

*Instead of the Trisagion, we sing:*
"As many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. Alleluia!"[^893]

*Prokeimenon, Tone 4:*
Blessed is He that comes in the name of the Lord; God is the Lord, and has appeared unto us![^894]
*Verse:* O give thanks unto the Lord, for He is good; for His mercy endures unto ages.[^895]
*The Epistle to Titus, pericope 302 (Titus 2:11–14; 3:4–7).*
*Alleluia, Tone 1:*
*Verse:* Bring unto the Lord, O ye sons of God, bring unto the Lord the young rams.[^896]
*Verse:* The voice of the Lord is upon the waters.[^897]
*The Gospel according to Matthew, pericope 6 (Matthew 3:13–17).*
*Communion Verse:*
The grace of God that brings salvation has appeared unto all men.[^898]

*At the refectory there is great consolation for the brethren. We eat fish, cheese, and eggs, and we drink wine; and laymen eat meat, even if it be on Wednesday or Friday. And the homily of Chrysostom is read, of which the incipit is: "All of you in good cheer..."*[^899]

*In the same month, on the 7th day: The Synaxis of the Holy Glorious Prophet, Forerunner, and Baptist John. In the evening there is no kathisma reading, on account of the vigil that was kept, unless it be Saturday.*

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the feast, 3, Tone 2:*
*Sticheron 1:*
Beholding our Enlightenment, Who enlightens every man,[^900] coming to be baptized, the Forerunner rejoices in soul and trembles with his hand; he points Him out and says unto the peoples: "Behold Him Who delivers Israel, Who frees us from corruption![^901] O sinless Christ our God, glory to Thee!"

*Sticheron 2:*
When our Deliverer was baptized by a servant, and witnessed unto by the descent of the Spirit, the angelic hosts shuddered as they beheld; and a voice was borne from heaven from the Father: "This Whom the Forerunner's hand baptizes is My beloved Son, in Whom I am well pleased!"[^902] O Christ our God, glory to Thee!

*Sticheron 3:*
The streams of Jordan received Thee, the Fountain; and the Comforter descended in the form of a dove; He Who bowed the heavens bows His head; the clay cries and shouts unto the Potter:[^903] "Why dost Thou command me things beyond my power? I have need to be baptized of Thee!"[^904] O sinless Christ our God, glory to Thee!

*And of the Forerunner, 3, Tone 1, Podoben: "O all-praised martyrs" (Всехва́льнїи мꙋ́ченицы):*
*Sticheron 1:*
Seeing Thee coming unto him, O Christ, and asking for baptism, the Forerunner cried out in trembling: "Why dost Thou command me to accomplish that which is beyond my strength, O Almighty Lord? How shall I touch Thee with my hand, Who holdest all things in Thy hand? Do Thou rather baptize me, Thy servant!"[^905]

*Sticheron 2:*
"I have appeared fully as a man unto Mine own, and I have become accessible unto thee, though inaccessible by nature; being rich, I willingly became poor,[^906] that I might enrich him who became impoverished with forgiveness and deliverance. Draw near and baptize Me, Who am not subject unto corruption, and Who take away the world from corruption!"

*Sticheron 3:*
"I am constrained on every side, and I know not how to flee," the Forerunner said unto the Creator; "Thou art the torrent of delight, O Compassionate One;[^907] how then shall the river streams receive Thee, the Most High, Who pourest forth salvation unto those who honor Thy holy appearance, O Word?"

*Glory..., Tone 6:*
O lamp in the flesh, Forerunner of the Savior, offspring of the barren woman, friend of Him Who was born of the Virgin,[^908] Whom thou didst worship with leaping in the womb,[^909] and Whom thou didst baptize in the waters of the Jordan: pray unto Him, we entreat thee, O prophet, that we may escape the surging waves of tribulations to come!

*Both now..., of the feast, in the same Tone:*
God the Word appeared in the flesh unto the human race; He stood to be baptized in the Jordan, and the Forerunner said unto Him: "How shall I stretch forth my hand and touch the head of Him Who holds all things? Even though Thou art an infant from Mary, yet I know Thee to be the pre-eternal God! Thou walkest upon the earth, Who art hymned by the seraphim,[^910] and I, being a servant, have not learned to baptize the Master. O Incomprehensible Lord, glory to Thee!"

*Entrance. Great Prokeimenon, Tone 7:*[^911]
Our God is in heaven and on earth; all things whatsoever He pleased, He has done![^912]
*Verse 1:* When Israel went out of Egypt, the house of Jacob from a barbarous people; Judea became His sanctuary, and Israel His dominion.[^913]
*Verse 2:* The sea saw it, and fled; Jordan was driven back.[^914]
*Verse 3:* What ailed thee, O sea, that thou didst flee? and thou, Jordan, that thou wast driven back?[^915]
*And again:* Our God is in heaven and on earth; all things whatsoever He pleased, He has done!

*Then the litany.*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*
*Sticheron 1:*
When John the Forerunner saw Thee coming unto him, O Master, he was astonished, and as a noble servant he cried aloud in fear: "What condescension is this, O Savior? What poverty is this wherein Thou hast clothed Thyself? In the riches of Thy goodness, being compassionate, Thou hast lifted up man who had humbled himself, by clothing Thyself in him!"

*Verse:* The sea saw it, and fled; Jordan was driven back.[^916]

*Sticheron 2:*
"Come unto Me Who accomplish the saving mystery," Thou didst answer the Forerunner; "serve Me with fear, and be not afraid; for to renew Adam who was shattered by sin, I am baptized as a man, being undefiled by nature, in the waters of the Jordan wherein thou seest Me come!"

*Verse:* What ailed thee, O sea, that thou didst flee? and thou, Jordan, that thou wast driven back?[^917]

*Sticheron 3:*
"Who among the earthborn has ever seen the sun being cleansed?" John said in reply, "or Him Who clothes heaven with clouds stripped bare,[^918] and the Fashioner of fountains and rivers stepping into the waters? I marvel at Thine ineffable dispensation, O Master: burn not Thy servant with Thy dread command!"

*Glory..., Tone 4, by Byzantios:*
As a lover of the Spirit and a divinely-speaking swallow of grace, thou didst clearly proclaim unto the human race the dispensation of the King of Kings, Who shone forth brightly from the pure Virgin for our renewal, O Forerunner, utterly taking away the habits of those that mourn, directing the acceptable hearts of those baptized in repentance unto life ever-existing, O blessed and divinely-called one!

*Both now..., in the same Tone:*
Come, let us imitate the wise virgins;[^919] come, let us go forth to meet the Master Who has appeared; for He comes as a Bridegroom unto John; the Jordan, seeing Thee, was afraid and stayed its flow; John cried aloud: "I dare not touch the head of the Sinless One!" The Spirit descended in the form of a dove to sanctify the waters, and a voice came from heaven: "This is My beloved Son,[^920] Who has come into the world to save the human race!" O Lord, glory to Thee!

*Troparion, Tone 2:*
The memory of the righteous is celebrated with hymns of praise,[^921] but for thee the testimony of the Lord suffices, O Forerunner; for thou hast proved to be truly more honorable than the prophets, since thou wast accounted worthy to baptize in the streams Him Whom thou didst preach. Therefore having suffered for the truth rejoicing, thou didst proclaim the good tidings even unto those in hades of God Who appeared in the flesh, Who takes away the sin of the world,[^922] and grants unto us great mercy.

*Glory..., Both now..., of the feast:*
*Troparion, Tone 1:*
When Thou wast baptized in the Jordan, O Lord, the worship of the Trinity was made manifest; for the voice of the Parent bore witness unto Thee, calling Thee His beloved Son, and the Spirit in the form of a dove confirmed the certainty of the word. O Christ God Who hast appeared and hast enlightened the world, glory to Thee![^923]

*At Compline, after the Trisagion, the kontakion of the Forerunner:*
*"Fearing Thy coming in the flesh..."*[^924]

*At the Midnight Office, we say the usual kathisma.*
*After the first Trisagion, instead of "Behold, the Bridegroom," we say the troparion of the feast. After the second Trisagion, the kontakion of the Forerunner: "Fearing Thy coming in the flesh..."*

*At Matins, at "God is the Lord," the troparion of the feast, twice. Glory..., of the Forerunner; Both now..., of the feast. After the first stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 1, Podoben: "While the stone was sealed" (Ка́мени запеча́танꙋ):*
When Jesus was born of the Virgin Mary, and was baptized in the Jordan by John, the Spirit descended upon Him, visible in the form of a dove.[^925] Therefore the prophet spoke with the angels, crying aloud: "Glory to Thy coming, O Christ! Glory to Thy kingdom! Glory to Thy dispensation, O Thou Who alone lovest mankind!"

*Glory..., Both now..., the same.*

*After the second stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared today" (Ꙗ҆ви́лсѧ є҆сѝ дне́сь):*
Seeing Thee in the streams of the Jordan desiring to be baptized, O Christ, the great Forerunner cried aloud with gladness: "Thou hast come and hast appeared, the Inaccessible Light!"[^926]

*Glory..., Both now..., the same.*

*The first canon of the feast with the heirmos on 6, the troparia on 4; and the second with the heirmos on 4. The heirmoi of both canons of the feast twice; and of the Forerunner on 4.*

*Canon of the Feast, Tone 2.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
The Lord, mighty in battles,[^927] uncovered the bottom of the deep, and leads His own through dry ground; having covered the adversaries therein, for He has been glorified![^928]

*Troparion:*
He renews corrupt Adam by the streams of the Jordan, and crushes the heads of the nesting dragons,[^929] the Lord, the King of ages, for He has been glorified!

*Troparion:*
Having clothed Himself in material flesh with the immaterial fire of the Godhead, the Lord incarnate of the Virgin is encompassed by the water of the Jordan, for He has been glorified!

*Troparion:*
Washing away the filth of men, cleansed by these things in the Jordan, having willed to make Himself like unto them while remaining that which He was, the Lord enlightens those who are in darkness, for He has been glorified!

*Another Canon of the Feast [Iambic], in the same Tone.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Israel passes through the surging storm of the sea, which was clearly revealed as dry land; but the black deep, a grave strewn with water, completely covered the Egyptian captains by the mighty power of the right hand of the Master.[^930]

*Troparion:*
When the light-bearing dawn appeared unto men, coming now from the wilderness unto the waters of the Jordan, O King, Thou didst bow Thy neck unto the sun, to snatch the forefather from the dark assembly, and to cleanse creation from every defilement.

*Troparion:*
O Word without beginning, having buried with Thyself in the streams him who was corrupted by deception, Thou bringest him forth new, receiving from the Father this ineffable, mighty voice: "This is My beloved Child, equal unto Me in nature!"[^931]

*Canon of the Forerunner.*
*A composition of Theophanes,*
*whose acrostic is:*
*"O Baptist of Christ, receive my praises."[^932] Tone 2.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Unto Him Who by His divine command dried up the impassable surging sea, and guided the people of Israel to walk on foot through it, let us sing unto the Lord, for He has been gloriously glorified![^933]

*Troparion:*
As I am submerged by the storm of passions, O Forerunner, hasten to save me by thy prayers; for thou thyself wast an honorable and most pure receptacle of dispassion, dedicated unto the Lord from on high from infancy.

*Troparion:*
Standing before God rejoicing, the angel announced good tidings unto honorable Zacharias, the holy officiating father, concerning thee, an equal of the angels, O all-blessed one, who becamest the Forerunner and friend of the Lord.[^934]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast filled with the All-Holy Spirit while yet carried inside the womb of thy mother; and with fair leaping thou didst rejoicingly proclaim the Virgin Fruit, and didst bow down before Him, O all-honorable prophet![^935]

*Troparion:*
Let us praise the divine and divinely-wise Forerunner of the Lord, who first cut open an untrodden, strange path of life for all men, and baptized Christ in the streams of the Jordan, and who is divinely-wise.[^936]

*Theotokion:*
O sanctified temple of virginity, who didst bear God the Word in thy womb: save by thy prayers those who flee unto thee and call upon thee, O pure one, dispelling the onset of tribulations, O all-immaculate one!

*Katavasia:*
*"The Lord, mighty in battles, uncovered the bottom of the deep..."*
*Another:*
*"Israel passes through the surging storm of the sea..."*

*By choirs:*
*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
The Lord, Who gives strength unto our kings and exalts the horn of His anointed ones,[^937] is born of the Virgin, and comes unto baptism; unto Him let us the faithful cry aloud: "There is none holy as our God!"[^938]

*Troparion:*
Rejoice today, O Church of Christ, who formerly wast barren and grievously childless;[^939] for by water and the Spirit sons have been born unto thee, crying aloud in faith: "There is none holy as our God!"

*Troparion:*
With a loud voice the Forerunner cries aloud in the wilderness: "Prepare ye the ways for Christ, and make straight the paths for our God,"[^940] crying aloud in faith: "There is none holy as our God!"

*Another [Iambic]. Heirmos:*
As many of us as have been released from the ancient snares of the lions whose teeth have been shattered,[^941] let us rejoice and open wide our mouth, weaving a hymn from words of sweet melody, delighting in the gifts He has bestowed upon us.

*Troparion:*
He who formerly planted mortification in creation, having armed himself in the nature of the malevolent beast, is darkened by the coming in the flesh; when the dawn appeared, having assaulted the Master, he had his hostile head crushed.

*Troparion:*
The Master draws unto Himself the nature formed by God, which had been buried within the confines of the tyrant's belly; the renewal of the earthborn is born again, powerfully accomplishing His work; for He comes desiring to cleanse it.

*Another [of the Forerunner]. Heirmos:*
Having established me upon the rock of faith,[^942] Thou hast opened wide my mouth against mine enemies; for my spirit rejoiced when singing: "There is none holy as our God, and there is none righteous beside Thee, O Lord!"[^943]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst loose the reproach of barrenness,[^944] having recognized the divine childbirth of the Virgin; thou didst leap for joy in thy mother's womb, O all-praised fellow-dweller with the angels, most blessed Forerunner of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Having prepared the paths of the Lord, thou didst walk before His face, O prophet, as a lamp as a lamp unto all, revealing the radiance of the Father's glory[^945] which appeared in the flesh for our sake, thou hast proved to be more excellent than all.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst shine forth like the dawn, proclaiming the Sun of Righteousness[^946] unto those in darkness; for thou wast the preacher and forerunner of the salvation of all, and didst say unto all: "Draw near unto Christ in faith, and ye shall be saved!"

*Theotokion:*
Having received ineffable joy, thou didst conceive without seed thy Master, O Mother of God, Who has called the whole universe; unto Whom also we cry aloud: "For there is none holy beside Thee, O Lord!"[^947]

*Katavasia:*
*"The Lord, Who gives strength unto our kings..."*
*Another:*
*"As many of us as have been released from the ancient snares..."*

*Kontakion, Tone 4:*
Today Thou hast appeared unto the universe, and Thy light, O Lord, has been signed upon us, who with understanding chant unto Thee: Thou hast come and hast appeared, the Inaccessible Light![^948]

*Ikos:*
Unto Galilee of the Gentiles, unto the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, as the prophet said, a great light, Christ, has shone forth.[^949] Unto those that were darkened, a radiant dawn has appeared shining from Bethlehem, and even more, the Lord from Mary, the Sun of Righteousness, shines His rays upon the whole universe.[^950] Therefore, all ye naked descendants of Adam, come, let us clothe ourselves in Him, that we may be warmed; for He covers the naked and enlightens the darkened. Thou hast come and hast appeared, the Inaccessible Light!

*Then the Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of the Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
The Jordan ministers with its streams, and John stretches forth a corruptible hand, when Thou Who art invisible didst appear in the flesh for baptism. But the one indeed was turned back with fear, while the other immediately held Thee, the incorruptible One, with trembling; truly the Lamb of God,[^951] the ever-living Fountain; and Thou hast cleansed fountains and seas and mankind. For the Trinity shone from on high: the Parent names Thee Son, and the Holy Spirit descends!

*Glory..., Both now..., the same.*

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I heard, O Lord, Thy voice which Thou didst speak, the voice of one crying in the wilderness,[^952] when Thou didst thunder over many waters,[^953] bearing witness unto Thy Son; and being wholly filled with the Spirit Who had descended, he cried aloud: "Thou art Christ, the Wisdom and the Power of God!"[^954]

*Troparion:*
"Who has ever seen the sun being cleansed," the preacher cries aloud, "which is all-radiant by nature? Shall I then wash Thee with waters, the Radiance of the glory, the Image of the ever-existing Father?

And shall I, who am hay, touch the fire of Thy Godhead?[^955] For Thou art Christ, the Wisdom and the Power of God!"[^956]

*Troparion:*
Moses showed the divine reverence he had when he encountered Thee; for when he perceived Thee calling out from the bush, he immediately turned away his face;[^957] how then shall I gaze clearly upon Thee, or how shall I lay my hand upon Thee? For Thou art Christ, the Wisdom and the Power of God!

*Troparion:*
Performing that which pertains to the soul wisely, and honored with reason, I am ashamed before inanimate things; for if I baptize Thee, the mountain smoking with fire accuses me,[^958] as well as the sea that fled in two,[^959] and this Jordan that turned back![^960] For Thou art Christ, the Wisdom and the Power of God!

*Another [Iambic]. Heirmos:*
Cleansed by the fire of a mystic vision, the prophet, hymning the regeneration of men, lifts up his voice, sounding by the Spirit, revealing the incarnation of the ineffable Word, by Whom the dominions of the mighty were shattered.[^961]

*Troparion:*
Sent from the Father, O all-radiant Word, Thou comest to drive away the evil-darkened assault of night, and to uproot the sins of men; and by Thy baptism, O Good One, to draw forth radiant sons from the streams of the Jordan!

*Troparion:*
Foreseeing the very Word Himself That was foretold, the preacher cries aloud unto creation: "This is He Who was before me, though second according to the flesh;[^962] He came forth conformed unto us by divine power, to take away our hostile sin!"

*Troparion:*
Carrying within Himself life-giving pasture, God the Word catches the nests of dragons, assaulting them with manifold snares and casting them down; and tripping up him who wounded the universal race, having consumed him, He delivers creation!

*Another [of the Forerunner]. Heirmos:*
I sing unto Thee, for I heard Thy report, O Lord, and was afraid;[^963] for Thou comest unto me, seeking me who was lost; therefore I glorify Thy great condescension toward me, O Most Merciful One!

*Troparion:*
Thou wast sent by the Master to wash the defiled with water, preparing them to receive Christ Who takes away sin,[^964] and driving away deception by the dawn of divine knowledge, O all-honorable one!

*Troparion:*
Entreat Him to heal me of the serpent's bites, O blessed one, who didst baptize Christ in the waters of the Jordan, wherein the Savior crushed the malice of the nesting dragons!

*Troparion:*
Adorned with the wisdom of God, thou camest as a preacher of Christ; for thou wast the voice of one crying, saying: "Repent ye!"

as the prophet proclaimed,[^965] showing thee unto us as being greater than all men.[^966]

*Troparion:*
Living a strange life untrodden by men, thou didst stand before the waters of the Jordan, O most excellent one, having heard the Father's voice and having beheld the descent of the Spirit.[^967]

*Theotokion:*
The Lord Who created all things is Himself formed according to our nature, having dwelt in thy most holy womb, O all-pure one; He clothed Himself in the form of man, and saved His own image!

*Katavasia:*
*"I heard, O Lord, Thy voice which Thou didst speak..."*
*Another:*
*"Cleansed by the fire of a mystic vision..."*

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Jesus, the Author of life, comes to loose the condemnation of Adam the first-formed; and having no need of cleansings as God, He cleanses the fallen one in the Jordan, wherein, having slain the enmity, He grants the peace that surpasses all understanding.[^968]

*Troparion:*
When people without number had gathered to be baptized by John, he himself stood in their midst and proclaimed unto those standing by: "Who warned you, O disobedient ones, to flee from the wrath to come?[^969] Bring forth fruits worthy for Christ; for He Who now stands before you grants peace!"

*Troparion:*
The Sower and Creator stands in the midst, as the One Who alone searches the hearts of all;[^970] and taking the cleansing winnowing-fan in His hand, He all-wisely purges the threshing floor of the whole world, burning the barrenness, and granting eternal life unto the fruitful![^971]

*Another [Iambic]. Heirmos:*
Washed from the dark and defiled poison of the enemy by the cleansing of the Spirit, we have arrived at a new and unerring path, leading unto inaccessible joy, accessible only unto those with whom God has been reconciled.[^972]

*Troparion:*
Having seen him whom He fashioned with His fingers bound fast in the darkness of transgressions by inescapable bonds, the Creator lifts him up high and sets him upon both His shoulders;[^973] for now in the abundant waters He washes away the shame of the ancient, evil disposition of Adam.

*Troparion:*
With piety let us eagerly run unto the most pure fountains of the saving stream, contemplating the Word from incorruptible waters, bringing drawing-vessels of divine thirst, sweetly healing the infirmity of the world.[^974]

*Another [of the Forerunner]. Heirmos:*
Enlightenment of those lying in darkness, Salvation of the despairing, O Christ my Savior:[^975] unto Thee I rise early, O King of peace, enlighten me with Thy radiance; for beside Thee I know no other God![^976]

irradiated with the supernatural splendors of virtues, as though from heavenly mystagogy thou didst stand before the waters of the Jordan, O Forerunner, baptizing and cleansing with water those who draw near unto thee in soul with faith.

*Troparion:*
Desiring to baptize the pure and incorruptible Light, thou didst show thyself to be a most pure vessel, O John; for thou wast chosen before all by Him as greater than all,[^977] and more honorable than the prophets, since thou wast accounted worthy to see Him Who was prophesied![^978]

*Troparion:*
Having been sent before the face of the Lord,[^979] he showed His paths unto all men; trembling, the Forerunner touches His crown and baptizes Him, saying: "Beside Thee I know no other God!"[^980]

*Troparion:*
Who has ever seen, or who has ever heard, of the Defilement-free One bowing His crown unto creation, He Who holds all things in His hand? Therefore the Baptist cried aloud in trembling: "Beside Thee I know no other God!"

*Theotokion:*
The Son of God is clearly shown to be thy Son, O Virgin, accomplishing works as God by a single will; therefore we all truly name thee Mother of God and Sovereign Lady, for we know no other Mother of God!

*Katavasia:*
*"Jesus, the Author of life..."*
*Another:*
*"Washed from the dark and defiled poison..."*

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
The voice of the Word, the lamp of the Light, the daystar of the Sun,[^981] the Forerunner, cries aloud in the wilderness unto all peoples: "Repent ye and cleanse yourselves beforehand; for behold, Christ is present, delivering the world from corruption!"[^982]

*Troparion:*
Born incorruptibly from God and the Father, Christ is incarnate of the Virgin without defilement; the Forerunner teaches that it is not easy to unloose the latchet of the Word's union from us,[^983] delivering the earthborn from deception.

*Troparion:*
Christ baptizes with final fire those that oppose Him, and who think Him not to be God;[^984] but by the Spirit He renews through the water of grace those who acknowledge His Godhead, delivering them from transgressions.

*Another [Iambic]. Heirmos:*
With the all-blessed voice of the Father He made manifest the Desired One, Whom He poured forth from the womb:[^985] "Yea," He says, "this My consubstantial Son, being light-radiant, has sprung forth from the human race: My living Word, and a man by dispensation!"

*Troparion:*
From the deep-sea monster, having strangely wandered three nights in its belly, the prophet came forth immediately,[^986] prefiguring unto all in the last times the salvation of regeneration from the man-slaying serpent.

*Troparion:*
The disciple sees the firmament of heaven of the all-radiant Scriptures opened from the Father; and the Spirit, remaining upon the all-pure Word, having descended like a dove in an ineffable manner,[^987] is revealed unto the people who came unto the Master.

*Another [of the Forerunner]. Heirmos:*
Wallowing in the abyss of sin, I call upon the unfathomable abyss of Thy tender mercy; lead me up from corruption, O God![^988]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst go before as the voice of the Word, and thou didst shine forth as a light-bearing star, O Forerunner, proclaiming the Sun of Righteousness.[^989]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst not know earthly cares, and thou wast enriched with heavenly hopes; upon earth thou didst accomplish thy life like an angel, O all-blessed one.

*Troparion:*
We know thee as the seal of the prophets, as the mediator between the Old and the New,[^990] and as the Baptist and Forerunner, proclaiming beforehand Christ the Savior.

*Theotokion:*
Truly ineffable is thy conception, unspeakable and incomprehensible is thy childbirth, known and believed by all the faithful, O only Bride of God!

*Katavasia:*
*"The voice of the Word, the lamp of the Light..."*
*Another:*
*"With the all-blessed voice of the Father..."*

*Kontakion, Tone 6:*
Fearing Thy coming in the flesh, the Jordan turned back with dread; and John, fulfilling the prophetic ministry, withdrew with trembling; the angelic ranks were astonished, beholding Thee baptized in the flesh in the streams; and all those who were in darkness were irradiated, hymning Thee Who hast appeared and hast enlightened all things![^991]

*Ikos:*
Unto Adam who was blinded in Eden, the Sun appeared from Bethlehem and opened the pupils of his eyes,[^992] washing them with the waters of the Jordan; unto him who was blackened and darkened, the unquenchable light shone forth. No longer is there night for him, but always day; for his sake the morning towards morning was born; for having hidden himself at evening, as it is written,[^993] he found the dawn shining upon him; he who had fallen at evening was changed from gloom, and reached the morning of Him Who appeared and enlightened all things!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
A spirit of dew blowing and the descent of the angel of God preserved unharmed the pious youths who were cast into the fiery furnace;[^994] therefore bedewed in the flame, they sang thankfully: "O Lord and God of our fathers, supremely praised, blessed art Thou!"[^995]

stood in the waters clothed in flesh,[^996] the God of our fathers![^997]

*Troparion:*
Of old the cloud and the sea prefigured the wonder of divine baptism,[^998] wherein the ancient people of the Law were baptized when going forth; the sea was a type of the water, and the cloud of the Spirit; initiated by which we cry aloud: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto ages!"

*Troparion:*
All ye faithful, wherein we have received perfection, theologizing unceasingly with the angels, let us glorify the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit; for behold, the Trinity is consubstantial in Hypostases, yet one God, unto Whom we sing: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord, unto ages!"

*Another [Iambic]. Heirmos:*
He Who consumed the heads of the dragons in the stream,[^999] Who quenched the high fiery flame of the furnace carrying the pious youths, and put to rest the uncontrollable murk of sin, washes it all away by the dew of the Spirit.[^1000]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst render quenched the Assyrian flame prefiguring Thee, changing it into dew;[^1001] therefore the water now, like a flame, O Christ, burns the harmful, covert malice which clothed it, calling men back from the stumbling path.

*Troparion:*
When the Jordan was divided of old, the people of Israel passed through on dry ground;[^1002] now those being nourished in the waters praise Thee, the Most Powerful, Who without delay upholdest creation, unto an incorruptible and profitable path.

*Troparion:*
We know that formerly the all-destructive deluge mercifully brought all unto destruction; O Thou Who doest most great and marvelous things![^1003] But now, O Christ, through Thy tender mercy, Thou hast drowned sin for the salvation of mankind!

*Another [of the Forerunner]. Heirmos:*
The bush unburnt by fire upon the mountain,[^1004] and the Chaldean furnace bearing dew,[^1005] clearly prefigured thee, O Bride of God; for thou didst receive in a material womb the divine immaterial Fire without being consumed. Therefore unto Him Who was born of thee we sing: "Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!"

*Troparion:*
Having celebrated baptism and accomplished the mysteries clearly given unto thee by God, O Forerunner, like a gentle lamb offered in sacrifice thou wast brought as a victim;[^1006] therefore with thee we sing in harmony: "Blessed is the God of our fathers!"

*Troparion:*
Thou wast a new Elijah with boldness, O Forerunner, and didst rebuke the king who acted lawlessly; and an immaterial life thou didst show unto us, even as he did, O thrice-blessed one;[^1007] therefore with thee we sing, O prophet: "Blessed is the God of our fathers!"[^1008]

*Troparion:*
Having inherited the divine honor of being greater than the prophets, and the forerunner of the apostles of Christ, thou wast revealed as the fulfillment of the Law and clearly the beginning of the new grace;[^1009] therefore with thee we sing, O thrice-blessed one: "Blessed is the God of our fathers!"

*Theotokion:*
With hymns let us all the pious worthily sing of the all-honorable and God-welcoming Mother of God, as having given birth unto God the Only-begotten Who appeared unto us men; unto Whom we the faithful sing in harmony: "Blessed is the God of our fathers!"

*Katavasia:*
*"A spirit of dew blowing and the descent of the angel of God..."*
*Another:*
*"He Who consumed the heads of the dragons in the stream..."*

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
The Babylonian furnace showed forth a most glorious mystery when it poured forth dew; for the Jordan was to receive in its streams the immaterial Fire, and to encompass the Creator baptized in the flesh; Whom the peoples bless, and supremely exalt unto all ages![^1010]

*Troparion:*
"Lay aside all fear," the Deliverer said unto the Forerunner, "and obey Me as the Good One; draw near unto Me, for by nature this is what I have become; submit unto My command and baptize Me Who have descended; Whom the peoples bless, and supremely exalt unto all ages!"

*Troparion:*
When the Baptist heard the words of the Master, with trembling he stretched forth his palm; yet having touched with his hand the crown of his Creator, he cried aloud unto Him Who was baptized: "Sanctify me, for Thou art my God; Whom the peoples bless, and supremely exalt unto all ages!"

*Troparion:*
The manifestation of the Trinity took place at the Jordan; for the supreme divine Nature, the Father, proclaimed: "This is My beloved Son Who is baptized!" and the Spirit came unto Him Who is like Him; Whom the peoples bless, and supremely exalt unto all ages![^1011]

*Another [Iambic]. Heirmos:*
Creation is acknowledged as truly set free, and those formerly darkened are now sons of light; the ruler of darkness alone groans; now let the universal heritage of the nations, formerly wretched, fervently bless the Cause![^1012]

*Troparion:*
The three God-seers bedewed in the fire, most excellently with three all-radiant steps, clearly prefigured the transcendent Nature united with the human, mercifully sailing through the fire with dew,[^1013] every mournful delusion.[^1014]

*Troparion:*
Let all earthly nature be clothed in white, now raised up to heaven from its fall; for by the Word by Whom all things are preserved,[^1015] having been washed in the flowing streams, it has escaped its former transgressions, washed all-radiantly.

*Another Canon [of the Forerunner]. Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Of old, the furnace of fire in Babylon, by God's command, burned up the Chaldeans, but bedewed the faithful, who sang: "Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!"[^1016]

*Troparion:*
Thee who didst appear upon earth as equal to the angels through an altered manner of life, and higher than all men, O all-blessed John, we honor with joy, crying aloud: "Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!"

*Troparion:*
Thou didst teach, O prophet, one Essence of the Godhead in three equally powerful Hypostases; for by the voice of the Parent and by the descent of the Spirit thou didst recognize Him Who was baptized, the co-eternal Word of God.[^1017]

*Troparion:*
As a spiritual morning announcing the Sun Who shone forth from the Virgin, thou didst run forth from a barren womb, O all-honorable John, and didst proclaim the Lamb Who in His love for mankind takes away the sin of the world.[^1018]

*Troparion:*
Looking down upon us from on high, O blessed one, preserve us by thy prayers who follow thy divine preaching, O all-blessed one, and who abide, O Forerunner, in the teachings of thy divine and saving doctrines.

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst ineffably conceive the co-eternal Radiance of the glory of the Father, and the Word without beginning Who is understood as being in the beginning;[^1019] and now of thee, O all-pure one, He has unchangeably become the Firstborn of creation.[^1020]

*Katavasia:*
*"The Babylonian furnace showed forth a most glorious mystery..."*

*Another [Katavasia]:*
*"Creation is acknowledged as truly set free..."*

*At Ode 9, we do not sing "More honorable," but we sing the refrains of the feast, and of the Forerunner, and the heirmoi.*

*Refrain:*
*Magnify, O my soul, her who is more honorable than the heavenly hosts, the all-pure Virgin Mother of God.*

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Every tongue is at a loss to praise thee worthily, and even a mind from beyond this world is bewildered when singing thy praise, O Mother of God; yet, being good, accept our faith, for thou knowest our divine love; for thou art the protectress of Christians, and thee do we magnify![^1021]

*Then the second choir sings the same refrain and heirmos.*

*Refrain:*
*Magnify, O my soul, Him Who asked for baptism from the Forerunner.*

*Another Refrain:*
*Magnify, O my soul, Him Who came to the Jordan to be baptized.*

*Troparion:*
Come in spirit unto those who are being enlightened, O David;[^1022] sing unto God now, drawing near in faith, saying: "Be enlightened; this poor man, Adam, cried out in his fall, for the Lord heard him, having come into the streams of the Jordan, and He renewed him who was corrupted." *(Twice)*

*Refrain:*
*Magnify, O my soul, Him Who was borne witness to by the Father's voice.*

*Troparion:*
"Wash you, make you clean," says Isaiah;[^1023] "put away your wickedness before the Lord; ye that thirst, go unto the living water;[^1024] for Christ sprinkles with water, renewing those who draw near unto Him in faith, and He baptizes with the Spirit unto ageless life."

*Refrain:*
*Magnify, O my soul, the One of the Trinity Who bowed His neck and received baptism.*

*Troparion:*
We the faithful are preserved by grace and by the seal; for as of old the Hebrews escaped the destroyer by the blood-sprinkled threshold,[^1025] so also unto us this divine bath of regeneration[^1026] shall be an exodus, and thence we shall behold the unwaning Light of the Trinity.

*Then the first choir sings the refrain of the second canon:*
*Today the Master bows His neck beneath the hand of the Forerunner.*

*And the Heirmos:*
Beyond all comprehension are the wonders of thy childbearing, O all-pure Bride, O blessed Mother; through whom having obtained all-perfect salvation, we worthily praise as our Benefactor, bringing as a gift a song of thanksgiving.[^1027]

*Then the second choir sings the same refrain and heirmos.*

*Refrain:*
*Today John baptizes the Master in the streams of the Jordan.*

*Troparion:*
We have come to know the things revealed unto Moses by the bush;[^1028] come, accomplished through strange ordinances! For as the Virgin was preserved, though bearing fire, having brought forth the light-bearing Benefactor, so is He now revealed in the streams of the Jordan.

*Refrain:*
*Today the Master buries the sin of mankind in the waters.*

*Troparion:*
Anointing and perfecting human nature, O King without beginning, by communion with the Spirit, having washed it from darkness with pure streams, Thou hast put to shame the haughty power [of the adversary],[^1029] now to bestow it again in unceasing life.

*Another [Canon of the Forerunner]. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
God the Luminary Who shone forth before the sun, Who came unto us in the flesh, ineffably incarnate from the virginal womb: O blessed and all-pure one, thee, O Mother of God, do we magnify![^1030]

*Refrain to the troparia of the Forerunner.*

*Refrain:*
*Magnify, O my soul, him who is great among the prophets, the Forerunner.*

*Troparion:*
From the wilderness the voice of the Forerunner shows forth the Word Who came unto us in the flesh; and He Who is present prepares to baptize most joyfully, cleansing souls from sin because of faith.

*Troparion:*
Grace and the Law clearly set thee forth as an honorable mediator,[^1031] sealing the one and beginning the other, preferred by the word above all the prophets, having lived above visible things, O all-honorable one.

*Troparion:*
Having displayed a manner of life like unto the bodiless powers, he rejoices with the angelic choirs, and standing before the Throne he piously is glad, entreating forgiveness and salvation for those who praise him.

*Theotokion:*
*First Refrain:*
*Magnify, O my soul, her who is more honorable than the heavenly hosts, the all-pure Virgin Mother of God.*

*Theotokion:*
Through compassion the Deliverer of all becomes man and receives a birth in the flesh, in His love for mankind being above men as the Lover of mankind, from thy virginal womb, O all-blessed Mother of God.

*And at the descent both choirs sing together the refrain of the feast.*
*Then the Katavasia:*
*"Every tongue is at a loss..."*
*Then the refrain to the Mother of God, and the Heirmos:*
*"Beyond all comprehension..."*
*And a metania.*

*Exapostilarion of the Forerunner, Tone 3, Podoben: "In the Spirit in the sanctuary" (Дꙋ́хомъ во ст҃или́щи):*
Thou didst wonderfully make ready the paths of the Lord,[^1032] for thou wast the voice of His coming, and His most true preacher, higher than the prophets, O blessed John; thou didst behold the Light, having accomplished His ineffable dispensation.

*Glory..., Both now..., of the feast:*
The Savior has appeared, grace and truth,[^1033] in the streams of the Jordan, and has enlightened those asleep in darkness and the shadow;[^1034] for the Inaccessible Light has come and appeared.[^1035]

*At the Praises, Stichera, Tone 1, on 4.*
*Idiomela.*
Light from Light has shone forth upon the world,[^1036] Christ our Savior, God Who has appeared; unto Him, O ye peoples, let us bow down!

*Sticheron:*
How shall we servants worthily honor Thee, O Christ our Master? For in the waters Thou hast renewed us all.

*Sticheron:*
Having been baptized in the Jordan, O our Savior, Thou didst sanctify the waters, when the hand of the servant was laid upon Thee, and Thou didst heal the passions of the world. Great is the mystery of Thy manifestation; O Lord, Lover of mankind, glory to Thee!

*Sticheron:*
The true Light has appeared and grants enlightenment unto all;[^1037] Christ is baptized with us, Who is higher than all purity; He imparts sanctification unto the water, and this becomes purification unto souls: a thing appearing on earth, yet understood as higher than the heavens; by the bath, salvation, and by the water, the Spirit; through immersion our ascent unto God is accomplished.[^1038] Marvelous are Thy works, O Lord, glory to Thee!

*Glory..., Tone 6. Idiomelon:*
An angel didst thou come forth from a barren womb, O Baptist; from thine infancy thou didst dwell in the wilderness, and wast revealed as the seal of all the prophets; for Whom they in diverse manners beheld and darkly proclaimed,[^1039] Him wast thou accounted worthy to baptize in the Jordan. And thou didst hear the Father's voice from heaven bearing witness unto His eternal Sonship;[^1040] and thou didst behold the Spirit in the form of a dove, drawing down that voice upon Him Who was baptized. But O thou who art higher than all the prophets, cease not to pray for us who faithfully celebrate thy memory!

*Both now..., Tone 2, by Anatolius:*
Today Christ has come to the Jordan to be baptized; today John touches the crown of the Master's head. The heavenly powers were astonished, beholding the most glorious mystery. The sea saw it and fled; Jordan having beheld it was driven back.[^1041] And we who have been enlightened cry aloud: "Glory to God Who has appeared, and was seen on earth, and has enlightened the world!"

*Great Doxology.*
*After the Trisagion, the troparion of the Forerunner; Glory..., Both now..., of the feast; litanies, and the dismissal. And the First Hour.*
*At the First Hour, the troparion of the feast; Glory..., of the Forerunner; Both now..., the Theotokion of the Hours. After the Trisagion, the kontakion of the feast, and the rest. And the complete dismissal.*
*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the feast, Ode 3, on 4; and of the saint, Ode 6, on 4. After the Little Entrance, the troparion of the feast and of the Forerunner. Glory..., kontakion of the Forerunner; Both now..., of the feast.*
*Entrance Hymn: "Save us, O Son of God, Who wast baptized in the Jordan, who sing unto Thee: Alleluia!"*[^1042]
*Thus we sing also until the Apodosis.*
*Prokeimenon, Tone 7:*
*The righteous man shall be glad in the Lord, and shall hope in Him.*[^1043]
*Verse: Hear, O God, my voice, when I pray unto Thee.*[^1044]
*Epistle to the Acts, Pericope 45 [Acts 19:1–8].*[^1045]
*Alleluia, Tone 5:*
*Light has dawned for the righteous, and gladness for the upright in heart.*[^1046]
*Verse: Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous.*[^1047]
*Gospel according to John, Pericope 3 [John 1:29–34].*[^1048]
*Communion Hymn: "The grace of God that brings salvation hath appeared unto all men."*[^1049]
*Another [Communion Hymn]: "In everlasting remembrance shall the righteous be."*[^1050]

*If the Synaxis of the Forerunner John falls on a Sunday, we sing as follows:*
*On Saturday evening at Small Vespers, the Sunday stichera and those of the Mother of God, as usual. At Great Vespers, after the Kathisma, at "Lord, I have cried," the Sunday stichera of the Tone, 3; and of the feast, 4, Tone 2: "Our Enlightener..."; and of the Forerunner, 3, Tone 1, Podoben: "All-praised martyrs" (Всехва́льнїи мꙋ́ченицы): Glory..., of the Forerunner; Both now..., the first Theotokion of the Tone. Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day. At the Litiya, the stichera of the feast, sung on the feast itself. Glory..., of the feast, Tone 8: "Willing to fulfill, O Lord..."; Both now..., the same Tone: "Today creation is enlightened..." At the Aposticha, the Sunday stichera according to the alphabet; Glory..., of the Forerunner, Tone 4; Both now..., of the feast.*
*At the Blessing of Loaves, the troparion: "O Virgin Mother of God, rejoice," once; and of the feast, once; and of the Forerunner, once; and we read in the Epistles of the Apostles.*
*Where there is no All-Night Vigil, at Compline after "It is truly meet" and after the Trisagion we say the kontakion of the Forerunner; Glory..., Both now..., of the feast.*
*(Mark!)[^1051]*
*At Matins: at "God is the Lord," the Sunday troparion, twice; Glory..., of the Forerunner; Both now..., of the feast.*
*After the usual stichologies, the Sunday Sessional Hymns with their Theotokia; and a reading from the Commentary on the Gospel according to Matthew, Sunday after Theophany. After the Polyeleos (the Amomos), their troparia, and the Hypakoe of the Tone; and we read in the Commentary on the Gospel, the Sunday of the series. But if the Sunday of the series is in the Octoechos, then we do not read the Gospel of the Sunday of the series. The Anavathmoi of the Tone, and the Prokeimenon. "Let every breath praise the Lord"; the Sunday Matins Gospel. "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ," and the rest of the Sunday order. The Sunday canon with the heirmos on 4; and both canons of the feast on 6; and of the Forerunner, on 4. Katavasia of the feast, both choirs together.*
*After Ode 3, the kontakion and ikos of the feast, and the Sessional Hymn of the Forerunner, twice; Glory..., Both now..., of the feast. And a reading on the Translation of the Hand of the Forerunner.[^1052]*
*After Ode 6, the kontakion and ikos of the Forerunner. At Ode 9, we sing "More honorable." The Sunday Exapostilarion; Glory..., of the Forerunner; Both now..., of the feast.*
*At the Praises, the Sunday stichera, 4; and of the feast, 4, with the festal verses written at evening at the Aposticha. Then we say the verse in Tone 8: "The righteous man shall be glad..."; and we sing the idiomelon sticheron of the Forerunner written at Glory at the Praises: "An angel didst thou come forth from a barren womb..." Glory..., the Gospel Sticheron; Both now...: "All-blessed art thou, O Virgin Mother of God..." Great Doxology, and troparion* the Sunday troparion only, and the litanies, and the dismissal.
*At the First Hour, the Sunday troparion; Glory..., of the feast; Both now..., the Theotokion of the Hours. After the Trisagion, the kontakion of the feast.*
*At the Third Hour, the Sunday troparion; Glory..., of the Forerunner; Both now..., the Theotokion of the Hours. After the Trisagion, the kontakion of the Forerunner. Likewise we speak at the remaining Hours, alternating the troparion and kontakion of the feast and of the Forerunner.*
*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Octoechos on 4; and of the feast, Ode 3, on 4, of both canons; and of the Forerunner, Ode 6, on 4.*
*After the Entrance, the Sunday troparion, and of the feast, and of the Forerunner. Then Glory..., kontakion of the Forerunner; Both now..., of the feast. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel of the Sunday after Theophany, and of the Forerunner.*
*Communion Hymn of the feast, and of the Forerunner: "In everlasting remembrance..."*
*If it is not the Apodosis, then we read the Epistle and Gospel of the Sunday of the series under one pericope.[^1053]*
*But if it is the Apodosis, we do not read the Epistle and Gospel of the Sunday of the series, and the Prokeimenon of the Tone is omitted.*

*It should be known how to proceed if the Afterfeast of the Baptism of Christ falls on a Sunday, and the saint is sung on 4 or on 6:[^1054]*
*On Saturday evening at Small Vespers, the Sunday stichera and those of the Mother of God, as usual. The Sunday troparion; Glory..., Both now..., its Theotokion.*
*At Great Vespers, after the Stichology, at "Lord, I have cried," the Sunday stichera, 4; and of the feast, 3, of that day; and of the saint, 3.*
*(Mark! If the saint is sung on 6, or has a Polyeleos, then we sing the Sunday stichera, 3; and of the feast, 3; and of the saint, 4; Glory..., of the saint. If not, Glory..., of the feast; Both now..., the first Theotokion of the Tone.)*
*At the Litiya, the stichera of the feast, that day's ordinary Aposticha stichera; Glory..., Both now..., of the feast.*
*(Mark! If the saint has a Doxastikon, Glory..., of the saint; Both now..., of the feast.)*
*At the Aposticha, the Sunday stichera; Glory..., of the saint, if there be one, and Both now..., of the feast; but if not, Glory..., Both now..., of the feast.*
*At the Blessing of Loaves, the troparion: "O Virgin Mother of God, rejoice," twice; and of the feast, once; and "Blessed be the name of the Lord," and the rest; and a reading in the Epistles of the Apostles.*
*At Matins, at "God is the Lord," the Sunday troparion, twice; Glory..., of the saint, if there be one; but if not, Glory..., Both now..., of the feast.*
*After the Kathismata, the Sunday Sessional Hymns and their Theotokia; and a reading in the Commentary on the Gospel, Sunday after Theophany; and the Amomos, and the troparia* "The assembly of the angels was amazed..."[^1055] The Hypakoe of the Tone, and a reading in the Commentary on the Gospel, the Sunday of the series.
*(Mark! If the saint has a Polyeleos: after the Polyeleos, the troparia: "The assembly of the angels was amazed..."; and after the litany, all the Sessional Hymns of the saint, and a reading.)*
*The Anavathmoi and the Prokeimenon of the Tone; "Let every breath praise the Lord"; the Sunday Matins Gospel; the Sunday sticheron; and the rest of the Sunday order. The Sunday canon with the heirmos on 4; and of the Mother of God on 2; and of the feast on 4; and of the saint on 4. Katavasia of the feast. If there be a Polyeleos or Doxology, we sing the Sunday canon with the heirmos on 4; and of the feast on 4; and of the saint on 6. After Ode 3, the kontakion and ikos of the feast, and of the saint if he has one, and the Sessional Hymn of the saint; Glory..., Both now..., of the feast; and a reading. After Ode 6, the Sunday kontakion and ikos, and the Prologue. At Ode 9, we sing "More honorable." The Sunday Exapostilarion; Glory..., of the saint, if he has one; if not, Glory..., Both now..., of the feast.*
*At the Praises, the Sunday stichera, 4; and of the saint, if he has them, 3 Prosomoia, and the Idiomelon at Glory, sung with his verses. If the saint has no Praises stichera, we sing the Sunday stichera, 4; and of the feast, 4, that day's morning Aposticha stichera with the festal verses; Glory..., the Gospel Sticheron; Both now...: "All-blessed art thou, O Virgin Mother of God..."; Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, the Sunday troparion only; litanies, and the dismissal, and the Catechesis, and the usual procession into the narthex; and the First Hour.*
*(Mark! At the First Hour, the Sunday troparion; Glory..., of the feast; Both now..., the Theotokion of the Hours. After the "Our Father," the kontakion of the feast. Likewise also at the remaining Hours, we say the kontakion of the feast and of the Sunday alternating; if there be a Polyeleos, also of the saint.)*
*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Tone on 6; and of the feast, the appointed Ode on 4. But if the saint has an Ode: the Sunday Beatitudes on 4; and of the feast, the appointed Ode on 4; and the saint's Ode 6 on 4. After the Entrance, the Sunday troparion, and of the feast; then of the temple, and of the saint if he has one. Glory..., the kontakion of the saint; Both now..., of the feast. But if the saint has no troparion and kontakion: Glory..., of the Sunday; Both now..., of the feast. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, and Gospel of the Sunday after Theophany; then of the saint, if he has them; if not, of the series; and the Prokeimenon of the Tone is omitted. Communion Hymn: "Praise the Lord from the heavens!"; another of the saint, if he has one; if not, of the feast.*
*(Mark! Saturday after Theophany: Prokeimenon, Alleluia, and Communion Hymn of the feast.)*

*Epistle to the Ephesians, Pericope 233 [Eph. 6:10–17].[^1056] Gospel according to Matthew, Pericope 7 [Matt. 4:1–11].[^1057]*
*Sunday after Theophany. Prokeimenon, Tone 1:*
*Let Thy mercy, O Lord, be upon us, according as we have hoped in Thee.*[^1058]
*Verse: Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous; praise is meet for the upright.*[^1059]
*Epistle to the Ephesians, Pericope 224 from the midpoint [Eph. 4:7–13].[^1060]*
*Alleluia, Tone 5:*
*I will sing of Thy mercies, O Lord, unto all ages; with my mouth will I make known Thy truth unto generation and generation.*[^1061]
*Verse: For Thou hast said: Mercy shall be built up unto all ages, Thy truth shall be prepared in the heavens.*
*Gospel according to Matthew, Pericope 8 [Matt. 4:12–17].[^1062]*
*Communion Hymn of the feast: "The grace of God that brings salvation hath appeared unto all men."*
*Another [Communion Hymn]: "Praise the Lord from the heavens, praise Him in the highest!"*

*Month of the Same, the 8th Day: Our Venerable Father George the Chozebite; and the Venerable Dominica; and Emilian the Confessor:*

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Venerable One, Tone 1.*[^1063]
*Tone 1, Podoben: "As one valiant among martyrs" (Кѡ до́блѧ):*[^1064]
The steadfast thoughts of thy soul were not shaken by the assaults [of the demons], O blessed one; for setting forth thy firm fasting like a rampart, thou didst keep thyself unwounded by the fierce combatant and utterly unharmed, and didst appear before the Master of all, crowned as a victor.

*Sticheron:*
Clad in darkness, worn by tears, and exhausted by all-night vigils, thou wast the greatest model for monks, and a common rule, and a crown of praise; for thou didst accomplish every kind of virtue, and wast revealed as an heir of the kingdom on high, through thy wise self-control.

*Sticheron:*
Neither the length of the journey nor the ruggedness of the places was able, O venerable one, to weaken the fervor of thy pilgrimage unto God; and having arrived there, thou didst rejoice in the places where the feet of our God walked;[^1065] thou wast not negligent in any way, until through self-control and labors and unto the heavenly Zion.

*Other Stichera of the Venerable Woman [Dominica], Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*[^1066][^1067]
Showing forth the desire of thy heart with tears, O glorious one, with contrition thou didst wet the earth, and with thy hair didst wipe Christ's footstool;[^1068] contemplating Him and seeing Him ever present Whom thou didst love, whose footsteps thou didst follow; and with most divine visions thou didst enlighten thy soul.

*Sticheron:*
From the west thou didst shine forth unto the east, O all-blessed one, like a bright star shining with the rays of thy virtuous deeds, O venerable one; and thou didst enlighten the minds of the faithful with the radiance of thy miracles; therefore we call thee blessed and honor thy memory, magnifying Christ Who has honorably glorified thee.[^1069]

*Sticheron:*
Wounded by the desire of the love of Christ, O all-praised Dominica, thou didst follow Him, having rejected corruptible glory and carnal pleasures and every other enjoyment of life; therefore Jesus, Lover of mankind and Savior of our souls, has made thee to dwell in His all-radiant bridal chamber.[^1070]

*Glory..., Both now..., Tone 4:*
He Who covers the heaven with clouds[^1071] is clothed today with the streams of the Jordan, and is cleansed with my cleansing, He Who takes away the sin of the world; and by the consubstantial Spirit from on high He is borne witness to, being the Only-begotten Son of the Father on high; unto Whom let us cry aloud: "O Christ our God Who hast appeared and saved us, glory to Thee!"

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 6.*
*Tone 6, Podoben: "The Angelic Powers" (А҆́гглскїя предъиди́те си́лы):*
Bright and enlightening mankind, self-radiant Light, Thou, O Jesus my Son, being baptized in the streams of the Jordan, hast shone forth completely, O Light consubstantial with Thy Father, through Whom all creation, having been enlightened, cries aloud unto Thee, O Christ: "Blessed art Thou Who hast appeared, O our God, glory to Thee!"

*Verse: The sea saw it and fled; Jordan was driven back.*[^1072]
*Sticheron:*
That we may be sufficiently filled with divine glory, come, let us mentally purify our senses; and beholding Christ baptized in the flesh and crushing the head of the deceiver,[^1073] singing praises with joy let us cry aloud unto Him: "Blessed art Thou Who hast appeared, O our God, glory to Thee!"

*Verse: What ailed thee, O sea, that thou fleddest? and thou, Jordan, that thou wast driven* back?[^1074]

*Sticheron:*
With living water Thou dost give us to drink in the river Jordan in Thy tender compassion, O my Jesus, Lover of mankind, who were parched with thirst; that having drunk from Thy source, immortal and light-bearing, O Christ, we may sing: "Blessed art Thou Who hast appeared, O our God, glory to Thee!"

*Glory..., Both now..., Tone 2:*
Seeing Thee coming unto him at the river Jordan, John said: "O Christ God, why hast Thou come unto Thy servant, O Lord Who hast no defilement? In whose name shall I baptize Thee? The Father's? But Thou bearest Him within Thyself. The Son's? But Thou Thyself art the Incarnate One. The Holy Spirit's? And This One Thou knowest how to give unto the faithful with Thy breath:[^1075] O God Who hast appeared, have mercy on us!"

*Troparion of the feast, Tone 1:*
When Thou wast baptized in the Jordan, O Lord, the worship of the Trinity was made manifest; for the voice of the Parent bore witness unto Thee, calling Thee His beloved Son, and the Spirit in the form of a dove confirmed the certainty of the word. O Christ God Who hast appeared and hast enlightened the world, glory to Thee![^1076]

*At Matins, at "God is the Lord," the troparion of the feast, three times.*
*After the first stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph marveled" (Оу҆диви́ся І҆ѡ́сифъ):*
Joshua the son of Nun leading the people across the river Jordan, and the Ark of God,[^1077] prefigured the future beneficence; for the mystical passage prefigures for us by both, through the Spirit, an image of the depiction and a true pattern of rebirth.[^1078] Christ has appeared at the Jordan to sanctify the waters!

*Glory..., Both now..., the same.*

*After the second stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "The shepherds' pipes" (Свирѣ́лей па́стырскихъ):*
Christ, Who enlightens the world, was revealed; from the height the Father bore witness, saying: "This is My beloved Son, in Whom I am well pleased; give ear unto Him!"[^1079] This is He Who enlightens the universe through His tender compassion, Who was baptized and saved as God the human race.

*Glory..., Both now..., the same.*

*Canon of the feast with the heirmos on 6, Tone 2.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
The Lord, mighty in battles,[^1080] uncovered the bottom of the deep, and leads His own through dry ground, having covered the adversaries therein, for He has been glorified![^1081]

*Troparion:*
He renews corrupt Adam by the streams of the Jordan, and crushes the heads of the nesting dragons,[^1082] the Lord, the King of ages, for He has been glorified!

*Troparion:*
Clothed in material flesh with the immaterial fire of the Godhead, the Lord incarnate of the Virgin is encompassed by the Jordan water, for He has been glorified![^1083]

*Troparion:*
Washing away the defilement of men, the Lord, Who enlightens those who are in darkness, by this is cleansed in the Jordan, having willed to assimilate Himself unto them, while remaining what He was, for He has been glorified![^1084]

*And two verses on 8:*
*Canon of the Venerable One, Tone 4.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
*I will open my mouth, and it shall be filled with the Spirit, and I will utter a word unto the Queen Mother; and I will appear radiantly keeping festival, and rejoicing I will sing her wonders.*[^1085]

*Troparion:*
Entreat Jesus, the Beginning of wisdom, O George, that grace to open my mouth may be given unto me, so that I, foolish though I be, may fittingly sing of thy memory, rejoicing with divine songs.[^1086]

*Troparion:*
Glorious one, thou didst live upon earth as though bodiless, and from here hast joined the bodiless ranks, singing with thrice-holy songs to the Bodiless One, and receiving His radiance.[^1087]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst disdain the world through thy transcendent thoughts; having fasted in the world where Christ was reared, Thou didst depart unto the incorruptible world, wise one, joined unto the ranks of the firstborn.[^1088]

*Theotokion:*
Having opened my mouth, pure one, I make utterance before singing of thee who didst bear Hypostatic Wisdom; but since I am unclean and unable to sing fittingly of thee, the all-pure one, I ask for help.[^1089]

*Another Canon to the Venerable Dominica,*
*Whose Acrostic is:*
*The fair maiden Dominica I now honor. Joseph.*[^1090]
*Tone 2. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
*Of old the overpowered might laid low Pharaoh's whole army in the deep; and the Word made flesh has abolished all-wicked sin, the most glorious Lord, for He has been gloriously glorified!*[^1091]

*Troparion:*
Having winged thy soul with divine desire, glorious one, thou didst fly over the snares of the flesh. Therefore I pray thee: by thy prayers, all-wise Dominica, deliver me who have been caught in the nets of the serpent![^1092]

*Troparion:*
Rejoicing, thou didst follow Christ, walking in the footsteps of His sacred ordinances, all-venerable one, and thou wast numbered among the ranks of virgins as a virgin and undefiled. Therefore we honor thee, having assembled in faith, O wonderfully worthy one.[^1093]

*Troparion:*
Having slumbered not at all with the drowsiness of malice, glorious one, thou hast conquered thou hast conquered by light-bearing deeds, and hast departed unto the unwaning light, illumined with brightness from thence, and enlightening those who sing unto thee.

*Theotokion:*
Both before childbirth incorrupt, pure one, and after childbirth thou didst remain Mother of God supernaturally. Therefore Dominica, having desired thee by the divine Spirit, was brought after thee incorrupt as a bride unto thy Son, O pure one.[^1094]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
*The Lord Who gives strength unto our kings, and exalts the horn of His anointed ones, is born of the Virgin, and comes unto baptism. Let us, the faithful, cry aloud unto Him: "There is none holy like our God!"*[^1095]

*Troparion:*
She that was barren of old and grievously childless, rejoice today, O Church of Christ! For by water and the Spirit sons were born unto thee, crying out in faith: "There is none holy like our God!"[^1096]

*Troparion:*
With a great voice the Forerunner cries aloud in the wilderness: "Prepare the ways of Christ, and make straight the paths of our God, crying out in faith: 'There is none holy like our God!'"[^1097]

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
*O Mother of God, living and bountiful fountain, spiritually establish thy singers who have gathered together in a choir, and in thy divine glory vouchsafe unto them crowns of glory.*[^1098]

*Troparion:*
Washing thyself with thy tears, thou didst cleanse thy flesh from worldly mire; and as with these river streams, thou didst drown the legions of demons through ascetic struggles.[^1099]

*Troparion:*
In holiness, blamelessness, and righteousness thou didst pass through life, wise one; furthermore, by ascetic labors thou didst inherit the life free of sorrow, O divinely blessed George.[^1100]

*Troparion:*
Consumed with divine desire, all-blessed one, thou didst depart unto the places of Zion, and there didst abide even unto death, all-wise one, wearing out thy flesh with labors.[^1101]

*Theotokion:*
Guide thy singer who has gone astray, O Maiden, unto the path of repentance, O Bride of God, who didst bear the Word Who cleanses the sins of the world.[^1102]

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
*The wilderness has blossomed like a lily, O Lord, the barren Church of the Gentiles, by Thy coming, wherein my heart has been established.*[^1103]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst save the sailors storm-tossed upon the sea, having cast into the sea oil with a blessing, and changing into a calm the tempest, O Dominica![^1104]

*Troparion:*
Shining with immaterial rays, a light-bearing angel announced to the hierarch that thou hadst arrived at the imperial city by divine bidding.[^1105]

*Troparion:*
Winged with the wings of abstinence, thou didst reach the glorious havens of dispassion; and thou wast a haven unto those engulfed in the depths of malice.[^1106]

*Theotokion:*
Strengthen my weakness, O Virgin, who didst bear the Power of the Most High, Which gives existence unto all, and Which has magnified Dominica's memory.[^1107]

*Kontakion of the Venerable One, Tone 4.*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared today" (Ꙗ҆ви́лсѧ є҆сѝ):*
Thou hast appeared as a most radiant beacon, O George, illuminating with divine rays those who faithfully cry unto thee: entreat Christ our Master on our behalf, Who was revealed in the streams and has enlightened the earthborn![^1108]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 5.*
*Tone 5, Podoben: "The Word co-unoriginate" (Собезнача́льное сло́во):*
Let us now sing and magnify the great one in fasting, the glorious citizen of heaven, and the intercessor of the faithful; for he strove truly to please with blameless labors and his glorious life Him Who was well pleased to be taken upon the Cross.[^1109]

*Glory..., of the Venerable One, Tone 4.*
*Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*
Thou didst crucify the flesh with its passions, and hadst all love toward Christ, O Dominica, thy bridegroom incorruptible; therefore thou didst receive a crown, and wast numbered among the angelic ranks, venerable one, diligently entreating Him on behalf of those who honor thee.[^1110]

*Both now..., of the feast, in the same Tone.*
Thou didst sanctify the Jordan streams, Thou didst crush the power of sin, O Christ our God; Thou didst bow Thine head beneath the hand of the Forerunner, and didst save the human race from deception. Therefore we entreat Thee: save our souls![^1111]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
*I heard, O Lord, Thy voice which Thou didst speak, the voice of one crying in the wilderness, when Thou didst thunder over many waters, bearing witness to Thy Son; being completely filled with the descending Spirit, he cried aloud: "Thou art Christ, the Wisdom and Power of God!"*[^1112]

*Troparion:*
"Who has seen the sun, which is naturally most bright, being cleansed?" the preacher cries aloud; "that I with waters may wash Thee, the Radiance of glory, the Image of the Ever-existing Father; and that I, being grass, may touch the fire of Thy Godhead? For Thou art Christ, the Wisdom and Power of God!"[^1113]

*Troparion:*
Moses, drawing near unto Thee, showed forth the godly reverence that he possessed; for when he perceived that Thou wast calling him from the bush, he immediately turned away his face; how then shall I gaze clearly upon Thee? Or how shall I lay my hand upon Thee? For Thou art Christ, the Wisdom and Power of God![^1114]

*Troparion:*
Performing a spiritual service, wise one, and honored with speech, have respect before inanimate things: for if I baptize Thee, the smoking mountain with fire, the sea that fled divided into two, and this Jordan driven back will accuse me; for Thou art Christ, the Wisdom and Power of God![^1115]

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
*He Who sits in glory upon the throne of the Godhead, upon a light cloud, Jesus the Transcendent God, is come with incorruptible hand, and has saved those who cry: "Glory to Thy power, O Christ!"*[^1116]

*Troparion:*
Generously nourishing thyself with fasts as with delicacies, O blessed one, thou didst present thy soul, now rejoicing, unto the Creator of all Who called thee, delighting in transcendent divine sweetness.[^1117]

*Troparion:*
Thou hast appeared as a certain heaven adorned with deeds as with stars, bearing the Lord as the sun, illuminating thy soul as the moon, and showing thee to be a partaker of His glory.[^1118]

*Troparion:*
Having descended from heaven for our sake, the Master found Zion to be truly a divine dwelling-place, whither thou, drawn by desire, didst ascend as by a ladder to the Zion on high, after having lived in this low one below.[^1119]

*Theotokion:*
He Who uncircumscribedly sits in the bosom of the Ever-existing One Who begot Him, is now seen circumscribedly sitting in thine embrace, showing thee who bore Him to be Ever-Virgin and truly incorrupt after childbirth.[^1120]

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
*Thou didst come from the Virgin, not an intercessor nor an angel, but Thyself, O Lord, incarnate, and hast saved me, the whole man. Therefore I cry unto Thee: "Glory to Thy power, O Lord!"*[^1121]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst flash forth the illumination of healings, driving away the gloom of passions and the legions of demons; and thou didst enlighten all who devoutly have recourse unto thee, O Dominica.[^1122]

*Troparion:*
The heavenly King glorifies thee, glorious one, before him who reigned upon earth, who was amazed at thy blameless life and thy miracles.[^1123]

*Troparion:*
The Lord, being the hearer of Thy prayers, manifestly designates Thy place wherein thou didst erect a dwelling of instruction, having driven away the spirits of malice, O Dominica.[^1124]

*Theotokion:*
Adam was stripped Adam was stripped of the garments of deadness through thy divine childbearing, and was clothed in the garment which the Word made flesh wove as one in thy womb.[^1125]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
*Jesus, the Prince of Life, comes to loose the condemnation of Adam the first-formed; and having no need of cleansing as God, He cleanses the fallen one in the Jordan, wherein, having slain the enmity, He grants the peace that passes all understanding.*[^1126]

*Troparion:*
When countless multitudes assembled to be baptized by John, he himself stood in their midst and cried aloud unto those who stood by: "Who has warned you, disobedient ones, to flee from the wrath to come? Bring forth fruits worthy of Christ; for He Who stands present now grants peace!"[^1127]

*Troparion:*
The Husbandman and Creator, standing in the midst, as the Only One searches out the hearts of all; and taking into His hand the cleansing fan, He all-wisely separates the threshing floor of the whole world, burning the barren, and granting eternal life unto the fruitful.[^1128]

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
*All things were amazed at thy divine glory; for thou, O unwedded Virgin, didst hold in thy womb the God over all, and didst bear the timeless Son, granting peace unto all who sing of thee.*[^1129]

*Troparion:*
The angels and the whole company of the venerable marveled, truly beholding the unceasing continuity of thy labors and thy harsh manner of life; for suffering like an inanimate stone, thou didst accomplish the fulfillment of virtues.[^1130]

*Troparion:*
Having stretched out thy soul, O great one, thou dost fill all with effusions of light and free them from the darkness of passions, even now sending forth saving movement like the purest sun.[^1131]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst withdraw from thy community, wise George, having loved above all the things fitting to this life Christ Who became a stranger unto men; therefore thou wast worthy of Him, being accounted worthy of grace from on high.[^1132]

*Theotokion:*
Pure one, thou hast adorned the plenitude of men; for thou wast shown to be more spacious than the breadth of the heavens, having borne God the Word, O Maiden, Who stretched out the heavens like a skin and refashioned earthly beings.[^1133]

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
*O Lord, Giver of light and Creator of the ages, guide us in the light of Thy commandments; for we know no other God besides Thee.*[^1134]

*Troparion:*
Having cultivated Having cultivated the soil and sown the furrow of the soul plenteously with the plow of prayers, pure one, thou didst reap fruit preserved in divine storehouses.[^1135]

*Troparion:*
The radiance of the all-creating Spirit, enlightening thy pure mind, shows things far off as near at hand, and foretells the fulfillment of future things.[^1136]

*Troparion:*
The power of the Spirit makes thee a guide through the hieratic action with the graceful anointing of ministry, commanding thee, divinely wise Dominica, to shepherd consecrated souls.[^1137]

*Theotokion:*
O Birthgiver of God, thou didst bear the Holy Lord of all; Dominica, having desired Him from her soul, triumphed over corrupting passions, singing of thee, O Virgin.[^1138]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
*The voice of the Word, the lamp of the Light, the dayspring of the Sun, the Forerunner, cries aloud in the wilderness unto all people: "Repent and be purified beforehand! For behold, Christ stands present, Who delivers the world from corruption!"*[^1139]

*Troparion:*
Christ is born incorruptibly of God the Father, and is incarnate of the Virgin without defilement; whose sandal-strap—the union of the Word with our nature—the Forerunner teaches is hard to unloose, delivering the earthborn from deception.[^1140]

*Troparion:*
With final fire Christ baptizes the adversaries, even those who do not acknowledge Him as God; but with the Spirit and the water of grace He renews those who perceive His Godhead, delivering them from transgressions.[^1141]

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
*Prefiguring the three-day burial, the Prophet Jonah cried aloud, praying in the belly of the whale: "Deliver me from corruption, O Jesus, King of powers!"*[^1142]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst cry aloud unto God with unceasing tears; and He saved Thee from life as from a ferocious sea-monster, unto the unfailing and ever-flowing fountains of deification.[^1143]

*Troparion:*
The choir of virtues set thee as a four-cornered wall, blessed one, fearing not the archers' arrows of noetic enemies; for as a mighty one thou dost overcome the tempter.[^1144]

*Troparion:*
Like an honorable sheep thou didst hasten to Chozeba; and leaning upon deeds as upon a staff, thou didst guide to Eden the sheep entrusted unto him.[^1145]

*Theotokion:*
The Lord dwelt as man in thy womb, pure one, vouchsafing me, a man, of incorruptible dwellings, overlooking my lawless deeds and transgressions.[^1146]

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
*In the deep Another Canon. Heirmos:*
*Wallowing in the abyss of sin, I call upon the unfathomable abyss of Thy loving-kindness: lead me up from corruption, O God!*[^1147]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst build the sacred prophecy of the divine Prophet Zechariah, divinely wise one; with him thou dost dance in the holy temple, O divinely wise Dominica.[^1148]

*Troparion:*
Thou hast appeared as an abundant stream of healings, washing away the flame of passions and pouring forth saving sanctification, O all-lauded virgin named after the Lord.[^1149]

*Troparion:*
As good, as fair, as honorable, as shining with the rays of virginity, the Bridegroom, the Lord, shall preserve thee for Himself, glorious one.[^1150]

*Theotokion:*
For my sake He became an infant like unto me, the All-perfect One, renewing me who had grown old through passions, for thy sake, O all-pure Bride of God.[^1151]

*Kontakion of the Feast, Tone 4:*
Thou hast appeared today unto the universe, and Thy light, O Lord, has been signed upon us, who with understanding sing unto Thee: "Thou hast come and revealed Thyself, O Light unapproachable!"[^1152]

*Ikos:*
Upon Galilee of the Gentiles, upon the land of Zebulun and the region of Naphtali, as the prophet said, Christ has shone forth a great light; unto those in darkness a bright ray has appeared, shining forth from Bethlehem; yet more, from Mary the Lord, the Sun of Righteousness, sends forth His beams upon the whole universe. Therefore, all ye who are naked from Adam, come, let us clothe ourselves in Him, that we may be warmed; for He covers the naked and enlightens those in darkness. Thou hast come and revealed Thyself, O Light unapproachable![^1153]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
*When the pious youths were cast into the fiery furnace, the whistling wind of dew and the descent of the angel of God preserved them unharmed; therefore, bedewed in the flame, they thankfully sang: "O most praised Lord and God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!"*[^1154]

*Troparion:*
Even as in heaven, the angelic hosts stood in the Jordan with trembling and wonder, beholding such a divine condescension: how He Who holds the structure of the waters above, stood in the waters bearing flesh, the God of our fathers![^1155]

*Troparion:*
Of old the cloud and the sea prefigured the marvel of divine baptism, wherein the people of old were baptized when the legal people went forth; the sea was an image of water, and the cloud of the Spirit; initiated by which, we cry: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto ages!"[^1156]

*Troparion:*
Let all of us Let all of us, the faithful, in Whom we have received perfection, speaking of God unceasingly with the angels, glorify the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit; for behold, the Trinity is consubstantial in Persons, yet One God, unto Whom we sing: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto ages!"[^1157]

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
*The divinely wise youths served not the creature rather than the Creator, but valiantly trampling underfoot the threat of fire, they rejoiced, singing: "O most praised Lord and God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!"*[^1158]

*Troparion:*
