Worn out by the labors of fasting, thou didst not surrender thyself unto satanic thoughts; for having set a steadfast mind toward the Lord Who is able to save, thou didst repel every assault.[^1159]

*Troparion:*
By prostrations, vigils, and fastings thou didst mortify all thy members that were upon the earth; and now thou dost live an incorruptible and painless life, blessed one, praying on behalf of us who sing of thee with love.[^1160]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst intensely desire to see the tomb of the Ever-existing One and to venerate it, wise one; and having arrived there, thou didst choose in venerable manner to die together through abstinence, O venerable one, with Him Who died out of loving-kindness.[^1161]

*Theotokion:*
They who know the Creator served not the creature, but knowing thee who bore Him, O Maiden, and recognizing God the true Word Who shone forth from thee, they cry: "O Lord and God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!"[^1162]

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
*The God-opposing command of the lawless tyrant raised a high flame, but Christ spread spiritual dew over the pious youths, He Who is blessed and supremely glorified.*[^1163]

*Troparion:*
Thy mind, being ever deified by gazes directed toward God, became god-beholding; whence thou didst turn away from carnal affection, singing, O divinely wise one: "Blessed and supremely glorified art Thou!"[^1164]

*Troparion:*
The All-Holy God Who rests in Thee reveals divine mysteries unto Thee; for thou didst behold a holy angel come and sanctify the honorable nature of the waters by the Spirit.[^1165]

*Troparion:*
Having become a temple of the Holy Spirit, while dwelling in the holy temple thou didst hear a voice instructing thee in divine mysteries and the departure from the body of him who reigned, O honorable one.[^1166]

*Theotokion:*
The Lord is my strength having pre-elected thee as the all-praised Mother and unwedded Bride; pure one, cease not ever to entreat Him on behalf of thy servants.[^1167]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
*The Babylonian furnace showed forth a most marvelous mystery when it poured forth dew, because the Jordan was to receive in its streams the immaterial Fire, and to encompass the Creator baptized in the flesh, Whom the peoples bless and supremely exalt unto all ages!*[^1168]

*Troparion:*
"Put away all fear," the Deliverer said unto the Forerunner; "and submit unto Me as good; approach Me, for such I have become in nature; obey My commandment and baptize Me Who have descended, Whom the peoples bless and supremely exalt unto all ages!"[^1169]

*Troparion:*
When the Baptist heard the Master's words, with trembling he stretched forth his palm; nevertheless, touching the head of his Creator with his hand, he cried aloud unto Him Who was baptized: "Sanctify me, for Thou art my God, Whom the peoples bless and supremely exalt unto all ages!"[^1170]

*Troparion:*
The manifestation of the Trinity took place in the Jordan: the transcendent divine nature Itself, the Father, proclaimed: "This One baptized is My beloved Son!" and the Spirit came unto His like, Whom the peoples bless and supremely exalt unto all ages![^1171]

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
*The childbearing of the Mother of God saved the pious youths in the furnace: then prefigured, but now realized, it moves the whole universe to sing unto Thee: "Praise the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!"*[^1172]

*Troparion:*
Thou gavest not slumber to thine eyelids nor sleep to thine eyes, O father, until thou didst make thyself an acceptable place and a dwelling for the Almighty, Whom all works praise and supremely exalt unto ages![^1173]

*Troparion:*
All-blessed one, thou didst find paradise as the recompense of thy measureless labors, which the Lord prepared for those who desire Him from the soul, the common kingdom, as they cry unceasingly: "Praise and supremely exalt Him unto ages!"[^1174]

*Troparion:*
The Monastery of Chozeba found thee a rule and most certain pattern, having traversed every form of virtuous deeds, O boast of the venerable, wise George; therefore, having lived divinely, they leap with joy together with thee unto all ages.[^1175]

*Theotokion:*
He Who is simple in divine nature was revealed from thee, O Birthgiver of God O Birthgiver of God, truly composite; for through ineffable loving-kindness in His Godhead, He received flesh from thy blood. Therefore, knowing thee to be the Mother of God, we hymn thee unto all ages.[^1176]

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
*Praise as the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt unto all ages, God Who descended into the fiery furnace unto the Hebrew youths, and changed the flame into dew.*[^1177]

*Troparion:*
Adorned with virtues and embellished with rays of miracles, O Dominica, thou didst ascend unto the fair bridal chamber of Christ the King, singing and supremely exalting Him unto ages.[^1178]

*Troparion:*
Having followed Christ the pure Shepherd, O holy lamb, thou didst settle with joy in the heavenly fold wherein is the gathering of the marked sheep, venerable one.[^1179]

*Troparion:*
Knowing through the all-effecting bidding of God the putting off of thy body, with the purest soul thou didst offer joyful praise unto the Cause of all, into Whose hands, pure one, thou didst commit thy spirit.[^1180]

*Theotokion:*
The Transcendent God is hieratically offered for our sake from thy blood, wishing out of compassion and mercy, O Virgin, to renew our corrupted nature, He Who is supremely glorified unto all ages.[^1181]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
*Every tongue is at a loss to praise thee as is meet, and even a transcendent mind is awed to sing of thee, O Mother of God; nevertheless, being good, accept our faith, for thou knowest our divine love; for thou art the protectress of Christians: we magnify thee.*[^1182]

*Troparion:*
Come in the Spirit, O David, unto those who are enlightened: "Now draw near," sing unto God in faith, saying: "Be enlightened!" This poor Adam in his fall cried aloud, and the Lord heard him, and having come into the streams of the Jordan, He renewed the corrupt one.[^1183]

*Troparion:*
"Wash yourselves and make you clean," says Isaiah; "put away your iniquities before the Lord; ye that thirst, go to the living water!" For renewing those who approach Him with faith, Christ sprinkles them with water, and baptizes them with the Spirit unto unaging life.[^1184]

*Troparion:*
We the faithful are preserved by grace and by the seal; for as the Hebrews escaped the destroyer of old through the threshold sprinkled with blood, so also this divine laver of regeneration shall be our exodus, whence we shall behold the unwaning light of the Trinity.[^1185]

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
*Let every earthborn mortal Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Let every earthborn mortal leap for joy, enlightened by the Spirit; and let the nature of the bodiless minds celebrate, honoring the sacred festival of the Mother of God, and cry aloud: Rejoice, all-blessed Mother of God, pure Ever-Virgin!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst spit upon all the sweetness of this life for the sake of the sweetness on high, for thou didst zealously choose a severe dwelling rather than a pleasurable life, and didst strive to quench the furnace of the passions with thy many tears, O George,[^1186] the venerable adornment of monastics.

*Troparion:*
Now as truly thou standest before God, O all-wise one, unto Whom thou didst first strive through self-mastery to unite thyself, and manifestly delightest in His appearances. Therefore grant unto all who honor thee enlightenment and communion in divine things.

*Troparion:*
Thou hast soared up unto the unwaning Light, O glorious one, having been delivered from the darkness of this life; and thou standest before the Almighty and the Tri-radiant Light with the ranks on high, and delightest in the radiance emitted from thence, O blessed one, and illuminest us who hymn thee.

*Theotokion:*
God, desiring to deify me wholly, is united wholly unto thee, and a mystery incomprehensible unto all is newly wrought: thou givest birth, an incorrupt Virgin, and God is seen in the flesh; Whom honoring, we now bless thee, O Mary, even as thou thyself didst foretell.

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
God the Word, Who by ineffable wisdom came to renew Adam, who through eating had fallen grievously into corruption, and was ineffably incarnate for our sake of the Holy Virgin, we the faithful magnify with one accord in hymns.

*Troparion:*
Most sacred choirs, beginning at thy honorable falling-asleep, appeared unto those who beheld thy godly soul, guiding thee with sacred hymnody into the place of the marvelous tabernacle, where the voice of those who feast resounds glorious things.

*Troparion:*
Having appeared as a most well-grown branch of the divine vine, thou hast brought forth for us divine clusters of compunction, pouring forth the wine of healings, O Domnica,[^1187] gladdening the souls and hearts of those who honor thee in faith.

*Troparion:*
From bodily passions, and defilements of soul, and every assault of the enemy, deliver us by thy prayers, who with love flee unto thy protection, O Domnica, and celebrate thy divine and honorable feast.

*Troparion:*
As a sunbeam illuminating the world, as a most fair bride of Christ, and as an honorable turtle-dove, as an olive tree, as a cedar, as an exquisite dove, we all praise thee, O Domnica, named after the Lord.[^1188]

*Theotokion:*
Spare me, O Lord, spare me when Thou shalt judge me, and condemn me not into the fire, nor rebuke me in Thy wrath: the Virgin who bore Thee, O Christ, and the multitudes of the angels and the ranks of the venerable plead with Thee.

*Exapostilarion of the Feast, Podoben: "Our Savior, the Grace and Truth, Hath Visited Us" (Посѣти́лъ ны̀):*
The Savior, grace and truth, hath appeared in the streams of the Jordan, and hath enlightened those sleeping in darkness and shadow; for the unapproachable Light is come and hath appeared.

*Glory... Both now... the same.*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
A great and dread mystery is accomplished, * for the Master of all * is baptized by the hand of a servant * unto the cleansing of all mankind.

*Verse:* The sea saw it and fled, * Jordan was driven back.[^1189]

The Father cried from on high: * "This is My beloved Son, * Who is now being baptized in the flesh * in the waters of the Jordan."

*Verse:* What ailed thee, O sea, that thou fleddest? and thou, Jordan, that thou wast driven back?[^1190]

The angelic ranks, * beholding the Master * Who took upon Himself the likeness of a servant * and was baptized in the waters, * marveled as they sang.

*Glory... Both now... Tone 2, Automelon (Самогла́сенъ):*
The waters saw Thee, O God, the waters saw Thee and were afraid;[^1191] for the Cherubim cannot gaze upon Thy glory, nor the Seraphim look upon it; but standing by with fear, the former indeed bear Thee, and the latter glorify Thy power. With them, O Compassionate One, we proclaim Thy praise, saying: O God Who hast appeared, have mercy on us!

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Feast, Ode 1 from both canons, on 6.*

*In the same month, on the 9th day. The Holy Martyr Polyeuctus.*

*Stichera of the Feast, Tone 8, Podoben: "O Lord, though Thou didst stand before the tribunal" (Гдⷭ҇и, а҆́ще и҆ на сꙋди́щи):*
O Lord, though Thou didst stand before John * at the Jordan as man, * yet Thou didst not depart from the throne, * sitting with the Father; * and having been baptized for our sake, * Thou didst deliver the world * from the bondage of the stranger, * as Thou art compassionate and the Lover of mankind.

O Lord, though Thou wast surrounded by the waters of the Jordan * as man, * yet witness was borne of Thee * from on high by the descent of the Spirit, * and the Father's voice testified of Thee as the Son. * But do Thou appear, and grant incorruption * unto our souls.

O Lord, Thou Who before the ages wast begotten of the Father * without change, * hast come in the latter years * and taken the form of a servant, * and as Creator hast renewed Thine own image. * For having been baptized, Thou hast granted incorruption * unto our souls.

*Other Stichera of the Saint, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joy of the Heavenly Hosts" (Не́бныхъ чинѡ́въ):*
As from a pit of passions, O Christ,[^1192] * and from the mire of clay, * the deceptions of idolatry, * they brought thee out, O martyr; * for He hath set thy feet upon the rock, * and mysteriously into the knowledge of Himself; * Whom do thou entreat that our souls may be saved.

Neither the longing of thy spouse, * nor the love of thy children, * nor thy dignity, * nor the wealth of possessions and goods * shook the steadfastness of thy soul * from the true faith that is in Christ, * O all-blessed Polyeuctus.[^1193]

Even before the grace * of thy martyr's suffering, O martyr, * thou wast truly adorned with the works of righteousness. * Therefore after these things thou wast counted worthy to be a faithful witness of Christ, * being baptized in thy blood * piously into His death.

*Glory... Tone 4, Byzantios (Вѷзантїево):*
The angelic hosts rejoice today at the memory of the Martyr Polyeuctus, and the human race feasts in faith, and joyfully cries out: Rejoice, all-praised one, who didst conquer the snare of the many-woven Beliar, and wast crowned by Christ with the crown of victory! Rejoice, soldier of our great King and Savior, who didst destroy the pagan shrines who didst destroy the pagan shrines, rejoicing the ornament of martyrs! Pray that they who in faith celebrate thy ever-honorable memory may be delivered from every threatening.

*Both now... Tone 5:*
Today the Creator of heaven and earth comes in the flesh unto the Jordan, asking for baptism, He Who is sinless, that He may cleanse the world from the deception of the enemy. And the Master of all is baptized by a servant, and grants cleansing unto the human race by water. Unto Him let us cry aloud: O our God Who hast appeared, glory to Thee!

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 6, Podoben: "On the third day" (Трїдне́венъ):*
Thou didst stand upon the waters, * incomprehensible unto all, * and didst bow Thy head unto the Forerunner. * Thou hast stilled the world, * and delivered it from bondage * by Thy baptism, O Sinless One.

*Verse:* The sea saw it and fled, * Jordan was driven back.[^1194]

The Father from on high bore witness of old unto His beloved Son, * and the Spirit testified, O Christ: * whereby the mystery of the Trinity was made known * when Thou wast baptized in the Jordan.

*Verse:* What ailed thee, O sea, that thou fleddest? and thou, Jordan, that thou wast driven back?[^1195]

Thou hast sanctified * all the waters of the Jordan, O Savior, * and the watery nature, as Thou art God; * therefore the human race * glorifies Thine appearance and praises it.

*Glory... Both now... Tone 4, by Cosmas the Monk:*
He Who covers Himself with light as with a garment vouchsafed for our sake to become as we are. Today He clothes Himself in the streams of the Jordan, not needing them for His own cleansing, but by Himself fashioning rebirth for us. O wonder! Without fire He refines, and without shattering He builds up, and saves those who are enlightened in Him, Christ God and the Savior of our souls.

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
Thy martyr Polyeuctus, O Lord, * through his suffering received an incorruptible crown from Thee, our God. * For having Thy strength, he laid low the tormentors * and shattered the frail boldness of the demons. * By his supplications, save our souls.

*Glory... Both now... Troparion of the Feast, Tone 1:*
When Thou wast baptized in the Jordan, O Lord, the worship of the Trinity was made manifest; for the voice of the Parent bore witness unto Thee, calling Thee His beloved Son, and the Spirit in the form of a dove confirmed the certainty of the word. O Christ God Who hast appeared and enlightened the world, glory to Thee!

*At Matins At Matins, after the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up" (Вознесы́йсѧ):*
Entreated by Thy compassions, O God, Thou hast sought out the one who had wandered and was lost, because of the mercy of Thy loving-kindness, O Lover of mankind. Therefore Thou didst come unto the Jordan, revealing the mystery of the Holy Trinity; and singing hymns we faithfully cry: Thou hast come and appeared, O unapproachable Light!

*Glory... Both now... the same.*

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "From the sheepfolds of the shepherds" (Ѡ҆вче́лей па́стырскихъ):*
The Master of all appeared unto us mystically in the streams of the Jordan, to cleanse every sin, as He is merciful and all-good. Let all creation leap for joy, for Christ the Lord is baptized, Who as God was well-pleased to save the human race.

*Glory... Both now... the same.*

*Canon of the Feast with the Heirmos on 8, and of the Saint on 4.*

*Canon of the Feast, Tone 2.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Israel traversed the sea's surge tossed with billows, which straightway appeared as dry land; and the black deep, a watery tomb, covered together the Egyptian captains, by the mighty strength of the right hand of the Sovereign.

*Troparion of the Feast:*
When the light-bearing dawn appeared unto men, coming now from the wilderness unto the waters of the Jordan, Thou, O King, the Sun, didst bow Thy neck, to snatch away the gloomy head of the prince of darkness, and to cleanse creation from all defilement.

*Troparion of the Feast:*
O Word without beginning, being buried together with the streams for Thy sake, Thou leadest the new man who had rotted away through deceit; and ineffably receiving from the Father the mighty voice: "This is My beloved Son, and equal unto Me is the youth by nature."

*Canon of the Saint, whose Acrostic is:*
By thy prayer grant me grace, O martyr.
*By Theophanes. Tone 8.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
He Who was cut cleaved the uncut, and the sun saw the earth which it had not seen; the water drowned the cruel enemy, and Israel passed through the impassable. And a song was sung: Let us sing unto the Lord, for He is gloriously glorified!

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Filled with the much-desired food, and filled with the blessed beam, O glorious one, and accounted worthy of the angelic choir, save those who praise thy festival, O Polyeuctus, singing unto the Lord: for He is gloriously glorified!

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Thy light-bearing and auspicious memory, full of the most divine Light, hath shone forth, brightly illuminating those who in faith sing unto thee, O noble warrior of Christ, all-blessed Polyeuctus, unto those who sing unto the Lord: for He is gloriously glorified!

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Quickened by the strength of the Spirit, and clothed with divine power, O blessed one, thou wentest forth steadfastly unto the contest against the proud one; and having mightily overthrown him, thou didst earnestly cry aloud: Let us sing unto the Lord, for He is gloriously glorified!

*Theotokion:*
O Mother of God, thou all-immaculate and all-pure Mother, remaining a Virgin, thou didst give birth unto the Incarnate One, Who was formerly bodiless, Who for our sake became poor by the wealth of His tender mercy, and saved those who cry unto Him: for He is gloriously glorified!

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
As many of us as have been released from the ancient snares, and from the food of lions whose limbs are crushed, let us rejoice and open wide our mouth, weaving words of song from words, whereby He delights in the gifts given unto us.

*Troparion of the Feast:*
He who previously planted death in creation, having transformed himself into the nature of the malevolent beast, is darkened by the bodily coming; having presumed early to assault the Master, he crushed his own hostile head.

*Troparion of the Feast:*
The Master draws unto Himself the God-fashioned nature that was buried within the confines of the tyrant's belly; the renewal of earthborn mortals is born again, as the Sovereign accomplishes a mighty deed; for He came desiring to cleanse it.

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
Thou art the confirmation of those who flee unto Thee, O Lord; Thou art the light of the darkened, and my spirit praises Thee.

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Thou didst change thy mindset unto piety, having been accounted worthy from on high of the divine sight of Christ,[^1196] O Polyeuctus.

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Desiring victory, thou didst spit upon all earthly things, O glorious one, and wast accounted worthy of the heavenly inheritance.

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Desiring the glory that is beyond the mind, thou didst strive patiently, and didst cast down the headless vanity of the idols.

*Theotokion:*
Direct my steps, O gracious one, that with a praiseworthy life I may go unto thy Son.

*Kontakion, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared today" (Ꙗ҆ви́лсѧ є҆сѝ дне́сь):*
When the Lord bowed His head in the Jordan, the heads of the serpents were crushed; and the severed head of Polyeuctus put the deceiver to shame.

*Ikos:*
In the Jordan the Creator of the ages, having bowed His head unto the Father, receives baptism having invisibly crushed the heads of the dragons, He gave power unto men over the proud one, who of old tripped up Adam in Paradise through the eating of the tree and brought upon him hopeless death. Therefore the sufferer Polyeuctus now, having not yielded unto the flatteries of his wife,[^1197] suffered steadfastly, stretching forth his head: by the severing of which he put the deceiver to shame.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 5, Podoben: "Co-beginning with the Father" (Собезнача́льное):*
As a good soldier of Christ the God of all, strengthened by His grace, thou didst turn thyself entirely unto His love, together with the faithful soldier Nearchus[^1198] who was with thee, O wise one. Therefore, having lawfully suffered, thou wast worthily crowned by the Lord, O martyr Polyeuctus.

*Glory... Both now... of the Feast:*
He Who is gloriously clothed with light as with a garment hath surrounded Himself with the streams of the Jordan; wherein Thou, O Word of God, hast renewed the nature of Adam that was broken by evil disobedience. Therefore we praise Thee, and all of us glorify Thy holy appearance.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Purified by the fire of mystical contemplation, singing of the renewal of men, the prophet proclaims a voice inspired by the Spirit, revealing the incarnation of the ineffable Word, by Whom the dominions of the mighty were shattered.

*Troparion of the Feast:*
Sent from the Father, O all-bright Word, to drive away the gloomy rush of night, Thou comest to uproot the sins of men, and by Thy baptism, O Gracious One, to draw bright sons from the streams of the Jordan.

*Troparion of the Feast:*
Having clearly foreseen the very Word That was named, the herald cries aloud unto creation: "This One, Who is after me in the flesh, but second before me, hath shone forth patterned with divine power, to take away our hostile sin."

*Troparion of the Feast:*
Bearing a life-creating pasture within Himself, God the Word lays low the many snares that had crept into the dens of dragons, and entraps him who had wounded the universal race; having destroyed him, He delivers creation.

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
Thou art my strength, O Lord, Thou art also my power; Thou art my God, Thou art my rejoicing, Who, without leaving the bosom of the Father, didst visit our poverty. Therefore with the Prophet Habakkuk I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion of the Saint:*
By a pious confession thou didst bring thyself, most exquisitely, unto the Master, accepting with love slaughter for His sake, O glorious one; and having become free from every blemish having become free from every blemish, therefore thou criest unto the Savior: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion of the Saint:*
The sweetness of piety became sweet unto thee, and thou wast winged with divine love; wounded with pure and bright desire, and inflamed with love for communion on high, thou singest unto the Master: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Bound unto Nearchus by an accounted like-mindedness, and instructed by his words in the pious Trinity-honoring faith, O godly-wise Martyr Polyeuctus, thou wast truly accounted worthy of the brightness of the martyrs that is greatly desired and beloved.

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Enrolled in the martyr army, thou didst receive an immovable kingdom; newly slain, thou didst enter into it while thy blood was yet dripping; and thou hast been taken up, O all-wise one, into unchangeable joy and unwaning light, and hast obtained great glory.

*Theotokion:*
The Heavenly One became like unto those on earth, and made them heavenly; and having suffered in a passible nature, He granted communion in divine impassibility: knowing Him Who was born of thee, the unwedded Maiden and Mother of God, we glorify Him.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Having washed away the venom of the dark and defiled enemy by the cleansing of the Spirit, we have arrived at a new, untrodden path, leading unto unapproachable joy, accessible only unto those with whom God is reconciled.

*Troparion of the Feast:*
The Creator, seeing him whom He had formed of dust held fast in the dark of transgressions by inescapable fetters, lifted him up and set him upon both His shoulders; now in the abundant waters He washes away the ancient shame of Adam's evil disposition.

*Troparion of the Feast:*
With piety let us eagerly run unto the most pure streams of the saving flow, beholding the Word born of the Incorrupt One, drawing forth to satisfy our divine thirst, sweetly healing the sickness of the world.

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
Why hast Thou cast me off from Thy presence, O Light never setting? and why hath foreign darkness covered me, the wretched one? But convert me, and direct my ways unto the light of Thy commandments, I pray Thee.

*Troparion of the Saint:*
That thou mightest obtain everlasting delight, O most blessed one, thou didst despise the fair things of this life, kinship of nature, sweetness, glory, and life itself; and thou hast not missed thy hope thou hast not missed thy hope.

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Having been mysteriously instructed in the divine mysteries of the Divine Image, with a steadfast mind thou didst set thyself apart unto the perfect contests; and having appeared as a trophy-bearer, thou wast accounted worthy of incorruptible crowns, O Polyeuctus.

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Having an inclination of mind that naturally hates evil, thou didst piously reject deified honor, and didst cast down vain gods, being kindled with zeal for piety, and filled with divinely-inspired fervor, O most glorious one.

*Theotokion:*
Following the utterance of thy lips, O all-pure one, we call thee blessed; for the Lord, having truly done great things unto thee, hath magnified thee, and by being born of thy womb, hath shown thee to be the true Mother of God.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
With an all-blessed voice the Father bore witness unto the Desired One, Whom He brought forth from His belly: "Yea," He says, "this consubstantial Son, being radiant, hath sprung forth from the human race; My living Word, and a man through providence."

*Troparion of the Feast:*
From the deep-sea beast, strangely tossing in the belly three nights, the prophet came forth straightway, showing beforehand unto all in the latter years the salvation of rebirth from the man-killing dragon.

*Troparion of the Feast:*
When the heaven of all-bright scriptures opened, the disciple sees the Spirit sent from the Father, abiding upon the most pure Word, having descended as a dove in an ineffable manner, and appearing unto the people who came unto the Master.

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
The abyss of sins and the storm of transgressions confound me, and drag me into the deep of oppressive despair; but stretch forth Thy mighty hand unto me as unto Peter, O Helmsman, and save me!

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Thou wast accounted worthy of the angelic rank, O venerable martyr, having manifestly shown angelic zeal; with them, therefore, O blessed one, earnestly pray that they who hymn thee may be delivered from tribulations.

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Thou didst fall asleep with love, O sufferer, with the sleep that is owed, when thy head was severed by the sword, O much-suffering one. And now in the heavens thou hast inherited an incorruptible portion, dwelling together with the martyrs.

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Thou wast conformed unto, and a partaker of, the sufferings of the Savior, Who for our sake endured the suffering of the Cross; and now, O blessed one, as He promised, thou reignest with Him unto unending ages.

*Theotokion:*
Having tender mercy, as thou didst give birth unto the Word Who loves mankind save us from cruel and oppressive misfortune; for we the faithful, O all-pure Lady, have acquired thee alone as an invincible intercessor.

*Kontakion of the Feast, Tone 4:*
Today Thou hast appeared unto the universe, and Thy light, O Lord, hath been signed upon us, who with understanding sing unto Thee: Thou hast come and appeared, O unapproachable Light!

*Ikos of the Feast:*
Unto Galilee of the Gentiles, unto the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, as the prophet said, Christ, a great Light, hath shone forth.[^1199] Unto those who sat in darkness a bright ray hath appeared, shining forth from Bethlehem, or rather from Mary; the Lord, the Sun of Righteousness, shines His beams upon the whole universe. Therefore, all ye who are naked from Adam, come, let us clothe ourselves in Him, that we may be warmed; for He covers the naked, and enlightens those in darkness. Thou hast come and appeared, O unapproachable Light!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The lofty furnace-flame burned the heads of the dragons in the stream, bearing the pious youths and quelling the unbearable gloom from sin, which He wholly washes away with the dew of the Spirit.

*Troparion of the Feast:*
Depicting Thee, the Assyrian flame, transformed into dew, is laid low as a cinder; therefore the water now, clothing the harmful malice like a flame, O Christ, weeps for the hidden one, calling back from the slippery path.

*Troparion of the Feast:*
When the Jordan was divided of old, the people of Israel passed through on dry ground; which now depicts Thee, the Most Mighty, Who upholdest creation without delay, in the waters, leading unto an incorruptible and profitable path.

*Troparion of the Feast:*
We know that the all-destructive flood was formerly sent mercifully to remove the corruption of all, O Thou Who hast wrought great and marvelous things! And now, O Christ, Thou hast drowned sin because of Thy tender-heartedness and the salvation of mankind.

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
The fire in Babylon of old was put to shame by God's condescension; therefore the youths in the furnace, dancing with joyful foot as in a meadow of flowers, sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion of the Saint:*
O Master, Thou didst show Thy power unto Thy servant; therefore he came uncalled, most eagerly, unto the contests, and having become a victor, sang: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Thy glorious and all-renowned feast hath shone forth, O martyr; for it brings the great light of thy manifestation, and illuminates those who cry in faith: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Thou hast found unstolen wealth, an abiding and unfailing dignity, and hast received glory that abides unto the ages, singing, O marvelous one: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
Having conceived, O Virgin, the Son Who is ever understood as co-abiding with the Unoriginate Father, thou didst give birth unto Him incarnate, to save those who cry in faith: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Creation is recognized as free, and the sons of light who were formerly darkened; the ruler of darkness alone groans. Now let the former wretched whole heritage of the nations earnestly bless the Author.[^1200]

*Troparion of the Feast:*
The three God-seers, bedewed in the fire and illuminated with three all-radiant beams, manifestly showed the Transcendent Nature united with human nature, mercifully burning away every destructive deceit with dew.

*Troparion of the Feast:*
Let every earthly nature be made white, being led up now from the fall unto heaven; for washed by flowing streams, it hath escaped from former sins through the Word by Whom all things are preserved, being most radiantly cleansed.

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
Sevenfold the Chaldean tormentor furiously kindled the furnace for the pious; but seeing them saved by a higher power, he cried unto the Creator and Redeemer: Ye youths, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Thy memory, rich in supplication, is celebrated today with sacred rites, O martyr and passion-bearer of Christ, Polyeuctus; for thou wast an acceptable and well-pleasing sacrifice unto Christ, Who was slain and sacrificed for thy sake; Whom the youths bless, the priests hymn, and the people supremely exalt unto all ages.

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Having shown on earth a martyr's resistance unto blood, O passion-bearer Polyeuctus, thou hast dwelt in the all-radiant bridal chamber in the heavens, baptized in the bath of thine own blood and singing unto the Master: Ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Raise up my soul, which is slain by falls, through thy martyr's boldness, by a divine command from on high reckoning it, O glorious one, fittingly turning her who cries unto the Master toward virtue: Ye priests, hymn; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, thou through whom we have found eternal joy! Rejoice, thou who didst loose Eve's grief, turning Adam's lamentation into brightness! Rejoice, thou who didst give birth unto God incarnate, O Virgin Mother of God, mediatress of the faithful who supremely exalt thee unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Beyond the mind are the marvels of thy childbearing, O all-pure Bride, blessed Mother! By whom having obtained all-perfect salvation, we worthily praise thee as Benefactress, bringing as a gift a song of thanksgiving.

*Troparion of the Feast:*
We have learned what was shown unto Moses by the bush; come, let us behold the things accomplished by strange ordinances; for as the Virgin was preserved carrying fire, having given birth unto the light-bearing Benefactor, so is He manifest in the streams of the Jordan.

*Troparion of the Feast:*
Anointing and perfecting human nature, O King without beginning, by communion with the Spirit, having washed it with pure streams and from darkness, Thou hast put the exalted arrogance to shame, to restore it now unto an unceasing life.

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*
Every hearing was awestruck at the ineffable condescension of God: how the Most High willingly came down even unto the flesh, being made man from a virgin's womb. Therefore we the faithful magnify the all-pure Mother of God.

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Come therefore, ye who love the martyrs, let us hymn the God-crowned martyr, whom the Most High glorified together with His light-bearing manifestation, and honored with an honorable day, and crowned, and adorned with divine virtues.

*Troparion of the Saint:*
By the streams of thy martyr's blood poured forth, thou didst drown the most hostile one who wrought wickedness; and watering the Church of Christ, thou didst make her radiant, O godly-blessed one, who in faith ever blesses thee.

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Be a helper unto me, O martyr, delivering me from various tribulations and distresses, loosing the bonds of heresy, and setting me free from the cruel prison by thy prayers, who hymn thee with pure mind, O most glorious one.

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst give birth, O all-pure one, unto Christ, the Head and the Fullness of the Law and the Prophets,[^1201] Who according to the tender mercy of His boundless abyss was well pleased to become incarnate for our sake of thee, and hath saved through faith who ever magnify thee in faith.

*Exapostilarion of the Saint, Podoben: "In the Spirit in the Sanctuary" (Дꙋ́хомъ во ст҃или́щи):*
Having acquired from a much-desiring soul the heavenly wealth that is greatly desired, O blessed Polyeuctus, and glory and brightness, being with God, thou didst receive a divine crown from the hand of the Most High, with the martyr ranks as a true martyr.

*Glory... Both now... of the Feast:*
Thou didst come in the form of a servant, O Word, and as man, Thou Who art ageless, askest for baptism. Earth and heaven were dismayed, and the angelic ranks, and the watery nature. And the Forerunner was afraid, and performed his ministry with fear and joy.

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 6, Podoben: "Ye Angelic Hosts, Go Before" (А҆́гглскїѧ предыди́те си́лы):*
Declare and say, O great prophet, who is he that cries in the wilderness? Why criest thou: "Draw cleansing water with gladness"?[^1202] Lo, John baptizes in the wilderness and cries aloud: "Christ comes! Blessed art Thou Who hast appeared, our God, glory to Thee!"

*Verse:* The sea saw it and fled, * Jordan was driven back.[^1203]

O beyond mind and ineffable loving-kindness! How doth the Creator of creation bow His most pure and divine head, by baptism introducing into it an image of humility for those who are enlightened? Wherein we sing: Blessed art Thou Who hast appeared, our God, glory to Thee!

*Verse:* What ailed thee, O sea, that thou fleddest? and thou, Jordan, that thou wast driven back?[^1204]

A living delight hath poured forth unto us from the torrent of the Jordan, the grace of baptism; whereby enlightened through baptism, we say: Glory to Him Who hath appeared in the world and granted life unto us! Wherein we sing: Blessed art Thou Who hast appeared, our God, glory to Thee!

*Glory... Both now... Tone and Podoben the same.*
Having turned away from harmful earthly things, come, let us spiritually cleanse our senses, and beholding Christ baptized in the flesh by John the Forerunner, let us all faithfully cry aloud, chanting with him: Blessed art Thou Who hast appeared, our God, glory to Thee!

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Feast, Ode 4, on 6.*

*In the same month, on the 10th day. Our Father among the Saints Gregory, Bishop of Nyssa; and the Venerable Dometian, Bishop of Melitene; and our Venerable Father Marcian, Presbyter and Oikonomos of the Great Church.*

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of Saint Gregory, Tone 2, Podoben: "O Venerable Father" (Преподо́бне ѻ҆́тче):*
O venerable father, most sacred Gregory,[^1205] reed filled with the breath of the Comforter, and most lucid tongue of piety, all-radiant lamp of divine brilliance, preacher of truth, foundation of theology, fountain of sublime dogmas, torrent of honey-flowing teachings, God-promised pipe delighting the thoughts of the faithful with God-inscribed songs: pray unto Christ, entreat Christ, O all-wise one, Who in the streams of the Jordan renewed the world, that He may save our race.

O venerable father, all-honorable Gregory, axe cutting down the onrushes of heretics, two-edged sword, weapon of the Comforter cutting off adulterous seeds, fire burning up the brushwood of heresies, and spade truly of husbandry, whereby the heavy and the light of doctrines is rightly discerned, and balance directing all certainties unto the path of salvation: pray unto Christ, entreat Christ ever, Who in the streams of the Jordan rebuilt the world, that He may save our race.

O venerable father, all-blessed Gregory, lips pouring forth blessed voices, drawing from the unfailing divine fountains of salvation, and explaining the words of prayer unto all,[^1206] a rule directing unto virtue; who, enlightened by divine contemplations, art illuminated with the beam of the Uncreated Trinity, whereof thou wast an unconquerable champion: entreat Christ, pray unto Christ, O all-wise one, Who in the streams of the Jordan rebuilt the world, that He may save our race.

*Other Stichera of Dometian, Tone 4, Podoben: "As One Valiant among Martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*
He who previously threatened * to consume the whole earth, * and boasted that he would dry up the sea, * is shown to be mocked by the faithful, * like a bird today and a most laughable gnat, unto whom the judge of woes is as a scarecrow, and he falls before the pleasing servants of Christ.[^1207]

*Sticheron of the Saint:*
Dometian[^1208] summons us today, ye faithful, * unto a table well-pleasing unto God; * let us come together unto him * with a cheerful disposition, * and feast together with him * for his righteous deeds, * entreating the Savior of our souls * to grant peace unto the world.

*Sticheron of the Saint:*
Thou hast increased the talent of Christ, * given unto thee, all-honorable one, * with double grace * as a sincere servant.[^1209] * Therefore thou hearest: "Well done, good servant, so be it unto thee, * as unto a true servant of the Good One; * and now enter into the joy of thy Lord," * having received the reward of thy labors.

*Glory... Tone 4:*
Having adorned the word of wisdom with blameless virtue, thou wast exceedingly adorned in both, O Gregory of Nyssa. By thy God-proclaiming voice thou didst intelligently adorn and gladden the people, wisely expounding the unified divinity of the Trinity. Therefore having overcome foreign-born heresies by orthodox teachings, thou didst raise up the rule of faith in the ends of the earth. Standing before Christ with the bodiless ministers, ask peace and great mercy for our souls.

*Both now... the same Tone:*
The hand of the Baptist trembled when it touched Thy most pure head; the river Jordan turned back, not daring to minister unto Thee. For if it was ashamed before Joshua the son of Nun,[^1210] how was it not to be afraid of its Creator? But Thou hast fulfilled the entire dispensation, O our Savior, that Thou mightest save the world by Thine appearance, O only Lover of mankind.

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
Let all creation * sing a new and fitting song * unto Christ Who was born of the Virgin * and baptized * in the Jordan today.

*Verse:* The sea saw it and fled, * Jordan was driven back.[^1211]

Let the prophetic trumpet, * the Forerunner, cry aloud: * "Bring forth unto the Lord * Who is baptized in the streams * the fruits of most excellent deeds!"[^1212]

*Verse:* What ailed thee, O sea, that thou fleddest? and thou, Jordan, that thou wast driven back?[^1213]

The divine Spirit, akin from on high, * in the form of a dove, * seen ineffably, * hath now run unto Christ like a branch.

*Glory... Tone 4:*
Having ordered a godly life, thou didst make action luminous through contemplation, O godly-blessed Gregory for having loved wisdom with divine desire, thou wast enriched with grace from the mouth of the Spirit. And dripping the sweetness of thy words like a honeycomb, thou ever gladdenest the Church of God with divine understandings. Therefore dwelling in the heavens with the saints, pray unceasingly for us who celebrate thy memory.

*Both now... the same Tone:*
Seeing Thee coming unto him, Who in the Spirit and fire cleansest the sin of the world, the Baptist cried out in trembling and fear, saying: I dare not hold Thy most pure head; do Thou sanctify me, O Master, by Thy divine appearance, O only Lover of mankind!

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
O God of our fathers, Who dealest ever with us according to Thy meekness, take not Thy mercy away from us, but by their prayers direct our life in peace.[^1214]

*Glory... Both now... Troparion of the Feast, Tone 1:*
When Thou wast baptized in the Jordan, O Lord, the worship of the Trinity was made manifest; for the voice of the Parent bore witness unto Thee, calling Thee His beloved Son, and the Spirit in the form of a dove confirmed the certainty of the word. O Christ God Who hast appeared and enlightened the world, glory to Thee!

*The Office of the Venerable Marcian is chanted at Compline.*
*Canon, Tone 4. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Let us all sing a song of victory unto God, Who hath wrought marvelous wonders with an high arm, and saved Israel: for He is glorified!

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Cleaving unto Christ, Who buried sin in the streams, with unslackening impulses thou didst dry up the torrents of the passions, O godly-wise Marcian.[^1215]

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Christ, being baptized, cleanses our weakness that had rotted through passions; Whom thou didst please, O Marcian, by diligent self-mastery, O father.

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst remain a Virgin after childbearing, for thou didst give birth unto God, Whom the great Forerunner baptized in the streams of the Jordan with great trembling, O all-pure Mother of God.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Let my heart be established in Thy will, O Christ God, Who didst establish the second heaven above the waters, and didst found the earth upon the waters, O All-Powerful One!

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Having descended, O Lord, Thou hast sanctified the streams of the Jordan today; and as a gift and an honorable and fair offering, Thou hast accepted glorious Marcian, to glorify Thee.

*Troparion of the Saint:*
The Lord Who covers heaven with clouds clothed thee with a sacred vestment as thou didst celebrate the sacred rites, reverenced by angels, as one who lived in the flesh as an angel on earth.[^1216]

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Thou didst build a sacred church for the godly-wise Anastasia,[^1217] adorning it with sacred and honorable offerings; therefore, O Marcian, thou hast made thy dwelling with her.

*Theotokion:*
He Who was born of thee, O Ever-Virgin, as He is tender-hearted, drowns the sin of the forefather in the river Jordan; Whom the Forerunner, having been commanded to baptize, was in dread.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Foreseeing through the Spirit the incarnation of the Word, O Prophet Habakkuk, thou didst preach, crying aloud: "When the years draw near, Thou shalt be known; when the time is come, Thou shalt show Thyself. Glory to Thy power, O Lord!"[^1218]

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Leap for joy, ye mountains; skip, ye hills;[^1219] Jesus, the Only Pure One, is baptized, making radiant the memory of the venerable one; whereby all the deceit of the demons is darkened, and the universe is enlightened.

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Having slain carnal pleasures through self-mastery, by thy divine utterance thou didst raise the dead, kissing him unto burial, O father,[^1220] and commanding him straightway to die again, until the common resurrection of all shall come.

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Thy life, adorned with the beauty of divine virtues, enlightens the faithful; and the shrine of thy relics flashes forth rays of marvels unto those who draw near in faith, O father, and who praise thee in faith.

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst give birth unto the Wellspring of salvation, Christ, Who sanctifies the fountains by His baptism; Whom Jordan seeing turned back with fear, and John baptizing was dismayed, O pure, all-hymned Virgin!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Grant us Thy peace, O Son of God, for other than Thee we know no God; Thy Name we name, for Thou art the God of the living and of the dead.[^1221]

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Thou hast crushed the heads of the dragons by Thy baptism, O Lord God Almighty, Who gavest authority and power unto divine Marcian over demonic deceits.

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Thou hast dispersed and given thine estate unto the poor, O godly-wise and all-blessed one; therefore thy remembrance abides unto the ages, and thy righteousness.[^1222]

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Thou didst pacify the turmoils of the passions, O venerable one, through thy mind; and thou didst build a church for the divine martyr, named after him,[^1223] unto the praise of the Lord Who is the Peace of all.

*Theotokion:*
A Virgin after childbearing hast thou appeared, truly pure, for thou didst give birth unto God, Whom John washes in the waters of the Jordan, unto the renewal of the world.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Imitating the Prophet Jonah, I cry aloud: Deliver my life from corruption, O Good One, and save me, O Savior of the world, who cry: Glory to Thee!

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Bestowing the torrent of delight upon us,[^1224] Christ is baptized in the streams of the Jordan, Who today hath enlightened the falling-asleep of the venerable one.

*Troparion of the Saint:*
The shrine of thy relics hath appeared as a spiritual vessel of myrrh, O sacred Marcian, pouring forth the myrrh of marvels unto those who flee unto thee.

*Troparion of the Saint:*
By thy prayer-inspired prayers thou didst drive away the rushing of boiling fire; thou didst preserve the church uninjured which thou didst build, O godly-blessed one.[^1225]

*Theotokion:*
O Virgin, thou dost suckle the Nourisher of all, Whom the Forerunner seeing leaped for joy, crying aloud: "The Redemption and Salvation of all hath appeared!"

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
Having searched the sacred Scriptures from childhood, O God-bearer Marcian, thou didst shine forth divinely, preaching the Son and Word of piety as consubstantial with the Father, and the Divine Spirit as sharing His throne. Therefore thou didst refute the impiety of Arius and Macedonius,[^1226] and didst make clear the faith to be glorified in orthodox manner. Pray unto Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who honor thy memory with love.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
By an image in the furnace, O Savior, the fire neither touched nor distressed Thy youths; then the three, as with one mouth, sang and blessed, saying: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Troparion of the Saint:*
The Wellspring of life is come, washing away our transgressions with waters, the Only-Begotten, Unoriginate Word of God; Whom glorious Marcian having well-pleased, passed over unto Him.

*Troparion of the Saint:*
By God-strengthened vigils, truly, thou didst lull to sleep the stubborn passions of the soul; and having fallen asleep in extreme old age, O blessed one, thou didst depart unto the Light as a son of day and a minister of Christ.[^1227]

*Troparion of the Saint:*
The flaming sword that guards the Tree of Life grants its back unto thee, O wise one;[^1228] therefore thou delightest in the joy of Paradise, chanting unto the Author of our salvation, O sacred Marcian.

*Theotokion:*
Without burning thy womb, Christ is born in a godly manner of thee, O pure one; Whom John seeing cried aloud: "Jesus is baptized, the salvation and redemption of the faithful!"

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Him Whom the angels and all the hosts dread as Creator and Lord, hymn, ye priests; glorify, ye youths; bless, ye people, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Thou hast regenerated mankind through Thy baptism, O most merciful God, Who today receivest Thy divine servant Marcian from earth unto ineffable glory.

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Seeing thee in church clothed with a sacred vestment as thou didst celebrate the sacred rites, O father, the people marveled, and with one accord sang of Christ the King of all, O all-blessed one.

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Thou didst acquire self-mastery and unceasing prayer, elevating humility, and true love, and dispassion, O father; therefore Christ granted thee the grace of marvels unto the ages.

*Theotokion:*
Thou containest beyond understanding Him Who cannot be contained, O Virgin; Whom when the Forerunner was about to baptize, he cried in dread and trembling: "Being Fire, O Christ, burn me not, who hymn Thee with love!"

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
The life-receiving, ever-flowing fountain, the light-bearing lamp of grace, the living temple, the all-pure tabernacle, more spacious than heaven and earth, the Mother of God, we the faithful magnify!

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Celebrate today, ye men; leap for joy, ye rivers and mountains; Jesus is baptized, the Savior hath appeared, and by His appearance glorifies the holy translation of Marcian.

*Troparion of the Saint:*
Thou hast reached the utmost of desires, having been loosed from bodily bonds, O God-bearing venerable one, beholding the brightness of the hierarchs, prophets, and apostles; together with them remember us who honor thee.

*Theotokion:*
Thou bearest God in thine arms, Who with God-working power nourishes all things; Whom seeing asking for baptism, the Forerunner is lost in amazement with dread, O Parent of God, and fulfills with fear what was commanded.

*Stichera, Tone 1, Podoben: "O All-Lauded Martyrs" (Прехва́льніи мꙋ́ченицы):*
O most sacred father, by the splendors of thy life the universe hath been enlightened, and demonic deceit hath been darkened; diseases are driven away merely by the touch of thy shrine; for divine grace, illuminating thy relics, looses the darkness of passions.

*Sticheron of the Saint:*
O father worthy of marvel, thou madest thyself a temple of the ever-existing Godhead; and thou didst erect sacred temples unto the praise of the Divine Trinity. By a word thou didst raise the dead, and didst acquire a merciful disposition, distributing wealth unto those who ask with eagerness.

*Sticheron of the Saint:*
Manifestly, O father, thou didst cover the nakedness of him that begged, entering naked thyself into the holy temple; and Christ clothed thee with a divine garment as thou didst celebrate the divine mysteries; at whose beauty they that saw marveled, and recognized thee as a servant of God.[^1229]

*Glory... Both now... the same Tone:*
Fearing Thy coming, O Christ, yet Thy servant opposes not Thy command: lo, with fear I stretch forth my hand. For I behold the Holy Spirit descending from on high, O Master, equal in honor with Thee and sharing the throne of the Unoriginate Father, bearing witness unto Thee baptized in the flesh.

*At Matins, after the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 3, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дѣ́ва дне́сь):*
Today the Master comes unto the Jordan to be baptized in the waters by the divine Forerunner. And from on high the Father bore witness: "This is My beloved Son, in Whom I am well pleased;"[^1230] and the Spirit appeared over Him in the strange form of a dove.

*Glory... Both now... the same.*

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph Marveled" (Оу҆диви́сѧ І҆ѡ́сифъ):*
The time of redemption: Christ hath appeared unto us in the river Jordan! Come, ye faithful, let us draw water for the remission of our sins; for Christ is come in the flesh, seeking the sheep carried off by wild beasts,[^1231] and having found it, as He is tender-hearted, He hath brought it into Paradise again. Christ hath appeared at the Jordan and enlightened the world!

*Glory... Both now... the same.*

*Canon of the Feast on 6, and of the Saints, two canons.*
*Canon of the Feast, Tone 2. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
He uncovered the bottom of the deep, and leads His own on dry land, having covered the adversaries therein, the Lord mighty in battles: for He is glorified![^1232]

*Troparion of the Feast:*
He renews Adam who had rotted away with the streams of the Jordan, and crushes the heads of the dragons that nested therein, the Lord the King of the ages: for He is glorified!

*Troparion of the Feast:*
Clothed in material flesh through the immaterial fire of the Godhead, the Lord, incarnate of the Virgin, is compassed by Jordan's water: for He is glorified!

*Troparion of the Feast:*
Washing away the filth of men, He is cleansed with them in the Jordan; having willed to be made like unto them while remaining that which He was, the Lord Who enlightens those in darkness: for He is glorified!

*Another Canon of Saint Gregory,[^1233] Tone 5. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
The horse and rider in the Red Sea, He that shatters battles with an exalted arm, Christ cast out; but Israel He saved, as they sang a song of victory.[^1234]

*Troparion:*
Being an abyss of wisdom, and a treasury of understanding, and the wellspring of essential goodness, grant unto me, O Christ, to hymn in songs Gregory, the luminary of Thy glorious Church.

*Troparion:*
Receive, O father Gregory, bright adornment of teachers, the humble singing offered out of love unto thy memory, wherein do thou make Christ merciful unto us.

*Troparion:*
The unapproachable Radiance found thy sacred soul cleansed from the mire of the passions; therefore, having made His abode in thee, O father, He showed thee forth as a light, instructing the ends of the earth.

*Troparion:*
By thy rich and wise word, O sacred initiate of mysteries, thou didst teach the honorable Church to theologize the Tri-hypostatic Monad, and the Trinity enthroned together and equal in honor, O Gregory.[^1235]

*Theotokion:*
Let faith alone be accounted, and not demonstration, for thy sacred wonders surpassing understanding, O Virgin Mother of God; for thou didst give birth unto the incomprehensible God the Word, Who clothed Himself in humanity.

*Another Canon of Saint Dometian,[^1236] Tone 1. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Thy victorious right hand is glorified in power in a manner befitting God; for it, O Immortal One, being all-powerful, shattered the adversaries, fashioning anew for the Israelites a path through the deep.[^1237]

*Troparion:*
Subdue the risings of the flesh and the assaults of passions, O God-receiver, and quell the warfare rising up in my soul, and keep me in a peaceful state, O father.

*Troparion:*
Having attained unto the wisdom on high through desire and steadfast love, thou didst subdue the flesh, and didst shake off earthly things, O venerable one, and wast truly in communion with God.

*Troparion:*
Wonderful Dometian, being lifted up little by little from the earth, came, walking from strength unto more perfect strength, and set ascents in his heart,[^1238] unto the heart he placed them.

*Theotokion:*
Steeped in the births of the flesh, the union which the Lord received He fashioned into humanity from thy virginal blood, invincible against the battle lines of adversaries.

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 3. Heirmos:*
The Lord Who gives strength unto our kings, and exalts the horn of His anointed ones, is born of the Virgin, and comes unto baptism; unto Him let us, the faithful, cry aloud: There is none holy as our God![^1239]

*Troparion of the Feast:*
Rejoice today, O Church of Christ, she that formerly was barren and grievously childless; for by water and the Spirit sons are born unto thee, crying out in faith: There is none holy as our God![^1240]

*Troparion of the Feast:*
With a great voice the Forerunner cries out in the wilderness: Prepare the ways for Christ, and make straight the paths for our God, crying out in faith: There is none holy as our God![^1241]

*Canon of Saint Gregory. Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Thou Who didst establish the earth upon nothing by Thy command, and didst suspend what gravitates uncontrollably, establish Thy Church upon the immovable rock of Thy commandments, O Christ, Who alone art good and the Lover of mankind.[^1242]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst completely subject unto the mind the flesh's errant wantonness; therefore, having traversed the path of the commandments without stumbling, thou didst fittingly become an abode of the Trinity, O Gregory.

*Troparion:*
Fittingly thou didst arm the irascible power of the soul against the serpent, O all-blessed one; and having wholly extended thy longing unto God, thou didst take wing unto the unsearchable and immutable beauty, O venerable one.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst join contemplation unto action, O father; therefore Christ, bringing it to thee, entrusted the governance of the Church, which thou didst steer blamelessly as an exquisite initiate of mysteries, O all-blessed Gregory.

*Troparion:*
Traversing the boundary of the virtues, O Gregory, and setting ascents in thy heart, thou wast taken up from the earth by unceasing course unto heavenly citizenship, even before thy departure from the flesh.

*Theotokion:*
Thou, O Mother of God, didst ineffably give birth unto Him Who shone forth from the incorrupt Father, without maternal pangs; therefore we orthodoxly proclaim thee to be the Birthgiver of God, who didst bear the incarnate Word.

*Canon of Saint Dometian. Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Thou Who alone knowest the weakness of human nature, and mercifully and mercifully formed in it, gird me with power from on high to cry aloud unto Thee, O Holy One: The animate temple of Thine ineffable glory, O Lover of mankind.[^1243]

*Troparion:*
The ancient enemy, unable in his might to shake the strength of thy soul, contrived at the time of thy departure to cast thee down through the phantasms of vile birds.

*Troparion:*
In his vaunting, the wretched serpent is justly brought to nothing by invocation; and he was turned into the likeness of dog-flies in utmost weakness, and lies beneath the fair feet of the faithful, being trampled down.

*Theotokion:*
The pre-eternal Son born of thee without seed, O Virgin Mother, renewed the world; the Lord, having put to death the hidden serpent with waters at His baptism, delivered men from corruption.

*Kontakion of the Feast, Tone 4:*
Today Thou hast appeared unto the universe, and Thy light, O Lord, is signed upon us, who with understanding hymn Thee: Thou hast come and hast appeared, the Light unapproachable![^1244]

*Ikos:*
Unto Galilee of the Gentiles, unto the country of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, as the Prophet said, a great light hath shone forth, even Christ.[^1245] Unto those darkened, a radiant dawn hath appeared, flashing forth from Bethlehem, or rather the Lord from Mary; the Sun of Righteousness shines forth rays upon the whole universe.[^1246] Therefore, ye who are naked from Adam, come, let us all clothe ourselves in Him, that we may be warmed; for He covers the naked, and enlightens the darkened. Thou hast come and hast appeared, the Light unapproachable!

*Kontakion of Saint Gregory, Tone 2, Podoben: "In Prayers" (Въ моли́твахъ):*
The divine hierarch of the Church and honorable mystic speaker of wisdom, the vigilant mind of Nyssa, Gregory, dances in chorus with the angels and delights in the divine light, praying unceasingly for us all.

*Sessional Hymn of Saint Gregory, Tone 3, Podoben: "Of the Divine Faith" (Бж҃е́ственныѧ вѣ́ры):*
Thou didst inherit the divine illumination, having lived an immaterial life; thou didst blossom forth with priesthood answering to thy name;[^1247] for having clarified with teachings surpassing nature, thou didst establish the world in orthodoxy, O venerable father: entreat Christ God to grant us great mercy.

*Glory... Another Sessional Hymn of Saint Dometian, Tone 1, Podoben: "When the Stone Had Been Sealed" (Ка́мени запеча́танꙋ):*
Adorned, O father, with the God-given anointing of the priesthood, thou didst make it radiant with divine virtues radiant with divine virtues of excellence and divine obedience unto Christ; and having finished thy course, thou criest aloud in the heavens with the angels: Glory to Thy compassion, O Savior; glory to Thy kingdom; glory to Thy dispensation, O Thou Who alone art the Lover of mankind!

*Both now... of the Feast, the same Tone and Podoben:*
Unto Him Who was born of the Virgin Mary, and baptized in the Jordan by John: the Spirit descended upon Him, seen in the form of a dove. Therefore the Prophet with the angels cried aloud, saying: Glory to Thy coming, O Christ; glory to Thy kingdom; glory to Thy dispensation, O Thou Who alone art the Lover of mankind!

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I heard, O Lord, Thy voice which Thou didst speak, the voice of one crying in the wilderness,[^1248] when Thou didst thunder over many waters, bearing witness unto Thy Son; being wholly filled with the Spirit Who had descended, he cried aloud: Thou art Christ, the Wisdom and Power of God![^1249]

*Troparion of the Feast:*
"Who hath ever seen the sun cleansed, which is most radiant by nature?" cries the Herald: "That I may wash with waters Thee, the Radiance of the Father's glory, the Image of the Ever-Existing One?[^1250] And being grass, shall I touch the fire of Thy Godhead? For Thou art Christ, the Wisdom and Power of God!"

*Troparion of the Feast:*
Moses, having shown the divine reverence which he possessed, drew near unto Thee; for when he perceived Thee speaking out of the bush, he immediately turned away his face;[^1251] but how shall I behold Thee clearly, or how shall I lay my hand upon Thee? For Thou art Christ, the Wisdom and Power of God!

*Troparion of the Feast:*
Performing the spiritual wisely and honored with speech, I am ashamed before inanimate things; for if I baptize Thee, a mountain smoking with fire shall accuse me, and the sea that fled in twain, and this Jordan that turned back:[^1252] for Thou art Christ, the Wisdom and Power of God!

*Canon of Saint Gregory. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Perceiving Thine emptyings befitting God, Habakkuk cried out unto Thee with trembling, O Christ, looking ahead: Thou hast come for the salvation of Thy people, to save Thine anointed ones![^1253]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast seen as an all-radiant pillar by thy life and word, O Gregory, kindled with warm zeal for orthodoxy against the approach of the new Judas.[^1254]

*Troparion:*
Having received spiritual grace, thou didst rend the garment of the Old Law's letter, and didst reveal unto us the hidden beauty of understanding.[^1255]

*Troparion:*
Christ the Good, showing forth all the forms of the virtues in mysteries entrusted them unto thee, O Gregory, as a servant of the Word, to declare them expansively unto the ends of the earth.

*Theotokion:*
Without confusion didst thou conceive incorruptibly in thy womb, and didst give birth before travail, and after childbirth didst remain a virgin, having borne God in the flesh.

*Canon of Saint Dometian. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Habakkuk, having perceived with farsighted eyes the mountain overshadowed by God's grace, proclaimed that the Holy One of Israel should come forth from thee, for our salvation and renewal.[^1256]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst show the Law to be a shadow of grace unto the Hebrews who honor God's law, O wise one, and the mystery of the true Theophany to be the Gospel, crying out unto Christ: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^1257]

*Troparion:*
Having flashed forth as a star of many lights from the East, thou dost enlighten the Church, proclaiming Christ the Sun of Righteousness with wise demonstrations in all piety, crying out unto Him: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Having broken away from all malice and with diligence from temporal love, O father, thou didst enlighten with light the ends of thy fatherland, O wise one; and thou didst rain down riches upon them with an abundant quantity of wealth.[^1258]

*Theotokion:*
The Word, being invisible God, having received visible human nature from a woman, accomplishes and cleanses in the river; He Who is a stranger to sin cleanses the transgressions of the fallen.

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Jesus, the Prince of Life, comes to loose the condemnation of Adam the first-formed; and needing no cleansing, as He is God, He cleanses the fallen one in the Jordan: wherein having slain the enmity, He grants peace which surpasses all understanding.[^1259]

*Troparion of the Feast:*
When countless multitudes assembled to be baptized by John, he himself stood in their midst and proclaimed to those standing by: "Who hath warned you, ye disobedient, to flee from the wrath to come?[^1260] Bring forth fruits worthy of Christ; for He that stands here now grants peace!"

*Troparion of the Feast:*
The Husbandman and Creator, standing in their midst, tests the hearts of all as He alone can do; and taking the purifying winnowing-fan in His hand, He all-wisely separates the threshing floor of the whole world: burning the unfruitful, He grants eternal life unto the fruitful.[^1261]

*Canon of Saint Gregory. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Thou Who clothest Thyself with light as with a garment, I awake early unto Thee, and unto Thee and unto Thee I cry: Enlighten my darkened soul, O Christ, as Thou alone art compassionate.[^1262]

*Troparion:*
As fire, thou didst burn up the thorn-bearing woven webs of heretical words, but the minds of the faithful thou didst enlighten, O blessed one, mystagogue Gregory.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst expose the iniquity of Eunomius, and his inescapable words; and the snares of his nets thou didst tear apart like spider webs.[^1263]

*Troparion:*
Most exceedingly didst thou refute the most godless Macedonius, who shamelessly reviled the Holy Spirit, proving him to be devoid of participation in Him, O Gregory.[^1264]

*Theotokion:*
Having seedlessly given birth unto Christ, our Righteousness and Redemption, O Mother of God, thou didst make free from the curse the nature of our forefather.[^1265]

*Canon of Saint Dometian. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Thou Who hast enlightened the ends of the world with the radiance of Thy coming, O Christ, and illuminated them with Thy Cross, enlighten the hearts of those who orthodoxly hymn Thee with the light of the knowledge of God.

*Troparion:*
The Master of creation looked upon the earth, and the causes of earthquakes shook and trembled grievously, O God-wise one; yet the earthquake turned thee not away from prayer nor shook the courage of thy soul, O father.[^1266]

*Troparion:*
Thou couldst not bear to hear the blasphemers speaking against the heights, O glorious one, nor the senseless speaking unrighteousness; but thou didst turn them back with thy pastoral staff, and didst heal the sick.

*Troparion:*
Unto those who preached one composite nature in Christ, O speaker of divine things, thou didst by no means yield; but thou didst catch them in the net of thy teachings, and didst lead them unto the light.[^1267]

*Theotokion:*
Elisha sweetened the bitterness of the waters with salt; and Thy Son and God, O Mother of God, baptizing in water, took away the bitterness and pain of sin.[^1268]

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 6. Heirmos:*
The voice of the Word, the lamp of the Light, the dayspring of the Sun, the Forerunner in the wilderness cries aloud unto all people: Repent and be purified beforehand! For lo, Christ stands present, delivering the world from corruption.[^1269]

*Troparion of the Feast:*
Born incorruptibly from God and the Father, Christ is incarnate without defilement from the Virgin; the strap of the union of the Word with us, the Forerunner teaches, is hard to loose, delivering the earthborn from deception.[^1270]

*Troparion of the Feast:*
With the final fire Christ baptizes the adversaries, but not those who confess Him to be God; but by the Spirit He renews with the water of grace those who understand His Godhead, delivering them from transgressions.[^1271]

*Canon of Saint Gregory. Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Raging with a soul-corrupting tempest, O Master Christ: calm the sea of passions, and bring me up from corruption, as Thou art compassionate.[^1272]

*Troparion:*
Having acquired humble mindedness, yet appearing unto all as a meek champion, O Gregory, against those who strove to diminish Christ's glory.

*Troparion:*
The alienation of the Trinity by Arius, and the audacious division by his word, O Gregory, thou didst utterly cast down their reasonings.[^1273]

*Troparion:*
Deeming the indivisible union of the Trinity to be a confusion, the god-fighting Sabellius was exposed through thee, O all-blessed Gregory.[^1274]

*Theotokion:*
A Virgin gave birth, and having given birth remained pure: carrying in her arms Him Who upholds all things, as truly having carried Him, O Virgin Mother.

*Canon of Saint Dometian. Ode 6. Heirmos:*
The uttermost deep hath compassed us, and there is none to deliver; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter; save Thy people, O our God: for Thou art the strength of the weak and their restoration.[^1275]

*Troparion:*
The people in distress were delivered as from a deadly snare, O venerable one, and a multitude of passions was driven far away by thy prayers; for the Persians themselves had thee as a protector.[^1276]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst destroy the onslaught of disease by prayer, O all-wise one, having swiftly fled unto the Virgin and Mother of the Redeemer; for being a shepherd, thou couldst not bear to see thy suffering flock neglected.

*Theotokion:*
The angelic ranks were struck with dread, beholding the Invisible One born in the flesh from the Virgin, and celebrated immaterially, coming to be baptized in the river.

*Kontakion, Tone 1, Podoben: "The Angelic Choir" (Ли́къ а҆́гг҃льскїй):*
Watching over the flock with spiritual fire, thou wast shown forth unto the world as a vigilant shepherd; and by the staff of thy wisdom and thy warm intercession, thou didst drive away all the evil-believing as wolves, keeping the flock unharmed, O all-wise Gregory.[^1277]

*Ikos:*
I am fallen into slothfulness, wretched as I am, and have fallen asleep unto death; but as a most vigilant shepherd, raise me up, O father, and put to sleep my passions that sorely torment me; that having arisen, I may purely hymn thy light-bearing translation, which the Glory of the universe worthily glorified, as a most faithful servant, as an all-wise teacher, as a friend and initiate, and as a steward of His traditions; whereof thou didst well preserve the anointing undefiled, O all-wise Gregory.[^1278]

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 7. Heirmos:*
When the pious youths were cast into the fiery furnace, the dewy breeze of the Spirit and the descent of the angel of God preserved them unharmed; therefore, bedewed in the flame, they sang thankfully: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers, praised above all![^1279]

*Troparion of the Feast:*
As in heaven, with trembling and wonder the angelic powers stood present at the Jordan, looking upon such a condescension of God: how He Who holds the structure of the waters above stood clothed in flesh in the waters, the God of our fathers![^1280]

*Troparion of the Feast:*
The cloud and the sea of old prefigured the marvel of divine baptism, wherein the ancient people of the Law were baptized as they went forth; the sea was an image of the water, and the cloud of the Spirit; by which we are perfected, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto ages![^1281]

*Troparion of the Feast:*
All ye faithful, wherein we have received perfection, theologizing unceasingly with the angels, let us glorify the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit; for lo, the Trinity is in consubstantial hypostases, yet one God, unto Whom we sing: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto ages![^1282]

*Canon of Saint Gregory. Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The Lord God of the fathers, praised above all, quenched the flame and bedewed the youths as they sang in unison: Blessed art Thou, O God![^1283]

*Troparion:*
Having united thyself through desire unto the radiance of the thrice-radiant Godhead, O Gregory, shining as a mirror unto all, thou dost flash forth with rays of light.

*Troparion:*
As a fatherly treasure thou didst leave thy words, providing purification for the soul's dispositions and fullness of understanding unto those who sing in faith: Blessed art Thou, O God!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst proclaim the Father as the primal Mind and Cause, the Begetter of the Word, and together the Producer of the Spirit, hymning the Trinity: Blessed art Thou, O God![^1284]

*Theotokion:*
O all-immaculate one, thou didst give birth unto the incarnate God, one hypostasis in two natures: unto Whom we all sing: Blessed art Thou, O God![^1285]

*Canon of Saint Dometian. Ode 7. Heirmos:*
Let us, the faithful, contemplate thee as a spiritual furnace, O Mother of God; for as He that is praised above all saved the three youths, so the praised and supremely glorified God of the fathers renewed the whole world within thy womb.[^1286]

...the God of the fathers, praised and supremely glorified.

*Troparion:*
The unfailing promise was manifestly accomplished for the faithful; for divine Dometian was vouchsafed grace to loose infirmities and drive out demons, proclaiming the praised and supremely glorified God.[^1287]

*Troparion:*
Having lived with us upon earth and dwelt in the flesh, He granted the grace of wonderworking unto those who followed Him and loved Him: the praised and supremely glorified God of the fathers.

*Troparion:*
Divine Dometian cast down impious heresies, the teachings of Severus; and he marked out the immutable and orthodox faith in a manner befitting God, proclaiming the praised and supremely glorified God.[^1288]

*Theotokion:*
Not departing from the Father's nature, the divine Word became incarnate of the Virgin; for He kept her unharmed, remaining undefiled in childbirth; and Christ receives the testimony from the Father, He that is supremely glorified unto ages.[^1289]

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 8. Heirmos:*
A most glorious mystery did the furnace of Babylon reveal, pouring forth dew, showing that the Jordan was about to receive the immaterial Fire in its streams, and to embrace the Creator baptized in the flesh: Whom people bless and exalt supremely unto all ages![^1290]

*Troparion of the Feast:*
"Lay aside all fear," the Redeemer said unto the Forerunner: "Obey Me as the Good One; draw near unto Me, for this I have become by nature! Submit unto My command and baptize Me Who have descended: Whom people bless and exalt supremely unto all ages!"[^1291]

*Troparion of the Feast:*
When the Baptist heard the Master's words, he stretched forth his hand with trembling; yet touching the crown of his Creator's head with his hand more boldly, he cried aloud: "Sanctify me, for Thou art my God: Whom people bless and exalt supremely unto all ages!"

*Troparion of the Feast:*
The manifestation of the Trinity took place at the Jordan; for the most divine Nature Itself, even the Father, cried aloud: "This is My beloved Son Who is baptized!" And the Spirit came unto His equal: Whom people bless and exalt supremely unto all ages![^1292]

*Canon of Saint Gregory. Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Unto Thee, the Creator of all, the youths in the furnace, weaving a universal choir, sang: All ye works of the Lord, hymn the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages![^1293]

*Troparion:*
Having received the whole radiance of the Comforter which came upon thee, O blessed one, thou didst cry, O venerable one: All ye works of the Lord, hymn the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
According to Christ's divine word, rivers of understanding flow forth unto us from thy belly; for grace hath shown thee forth in truth as an unceasing fountain unto the world, O father, unto the ages.[^1294]

*Troparion:*
O marvelous pair of brothers, kinsmen by the flesh and companion travelers in divine understanding! Let us worthily honor Basil together with Gregory unto the ages.[^1295]

*Troparion:*
The intelligible Light, having made His abode in thee, O father, set thee as an unquenchable luminary for the world, singing of the one thrice-radiant and divine Light: Whom we exalt supremely unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
Having given birth beyond understanding unto the Lord by a God-man word, and remaining a virgin: all ye works, let us worthily bless and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

*Canon of Saint Dometian. Ode 8. Heirmos:*
The youths of Israel in the furnace, shining brighter than gold with the beauty of piety in the furnace, said: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord; hymn the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages![^1296]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst transcend all the law of human nature and didst cleave unto God, the ultimate Desire, O speaker of divine things, singing unto Him: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
