Having heard the divine commandments, thou didst abundantly disperse thy wealth unto the needy, with the resolve of willing obedience, O God-receiver, worthy of wonder: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages![^1297]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast an inexhaustible fountain of healings, O Dometian, a wellspring of drink, a torrent of delight, and a river of peace unto those who cry aloud: Hymn the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages![^1298]

*Theotokion:*
The youths prefigured thee figuratively in the furnace, O Virgin, and Moses foreshadowed thee in the bush; and David, beholding thee who gavest birth without a man unto an Infant, the Lord of glory: Whom we exalt supremely unto all ages![^1299]

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Every tongue is at a loss to praise thee worthily, and even an otherworldly mind is dazed to hymn thee, O Mother of God; yet being good, accept our faith, for thou knowest our divine love: for thou art the protectress of Christians, and thee do we magnify![^1300]

*Troparion of the Feast:*
Come in the Spirit, O David, unto those who are enlightened: Now draw near Draw near unto God with faith, singing: Be enlightened! This poor man cried out, Adam in his fall; for the Lord heard him, coming in the streams of the Jordan, and renewed him who had been corrupted.

*Troparion of the Feast:*
Wash, be clean, Isaiah says, put away your wickedness before the Lord;[^1301] ye that thirst, go to the living water; for Christ sprinkles with water, renewing those who draw near unto Him in faith, and baptizes with the Spirit unto ageless life.

*Troparion of the Feast:*
We the faithful are preserved by grace and by the seal; for as the Hebrews of old escaped the destroyer when the threshold was stained with blood, so also for us this divine exodus, the laver of regeneration, shall be: and thence shall we behold the unwaning light of the Trinity.

*Another Canon of Saint Gregory. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Rejoice, O Isaiah! The Virgin had in her womb and brought forth a Son, Emmanuel, God and man; the Dayspring is His name;[^1302] Whom magnifying, we call the Virgin blessed.

*Troparion:*
Our mind, being unable worthily to praise the achievements and the splendors of thy words, O Gregory, confesses its defeat in a well-praising manner, yet proclaims thy praise beyond its power.

*Troparion:*
Most excellent initiate of heavenly mysteries, standing now before the Trinity with the choir of Apostles, and Prophets, Martyrs, Venerable ones, and Patriarchs: remember us who hymn thy memory, O Gregory!

*Troparion:*
Look down from on high, O protector, hierarch of the Church of Christ, granting victories unto our faithful King;[^1303] and shatter the yoke of servitude, saving thy singers by thy prayers, O Gregory.

*Theotokion:*
As having given birth unto the Creator of creation, O all-pure one, thou dost bear in all things the beginning of Him that is begotten, possessing uncreated and supernatural majesty; therefore, bowing down before thy childbearing, we glorify thee.

*Another Canon of Saint Dometian. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
The fiery bush revealed unburnt showed forth the image of thy pure childbearing;[^1304] and we now pray thee to quench the furnace of temptations raging against us, that we may unceasingly magnify thee, O Mother of God.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst restrain, O father, the desires of earthly loves, laying hold of what is most perfect; and the mansions of the patriarchs and the choirs of the righteous and the venerable received thee; with whom thou dost entreat the Almighty for our sake.

*Troparion:*
Thy homeland possessed as an honorable treasure thy much-suffering body, which it hid in its own bosom, O glorious one, being stirred by motherly affections; for it could not bear that strangers should enjoy thee.

*Troparion:*
Come to be a help unto me in the afflictions and adversities of life, and calm the storm of passions rising up against me, and lead me unto a calm harbor by the breeze of thy prayer, O father.

*Theotokion:*
Death held sway until Thee, O transcendent Son of God, Who wast well pleased to become like us from a husbandless Mother in order to save us, and to cleanse us by waters and by the divine fire of baptism.

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "Thou Hast Visited Us" (Посѣти́лъ ны̀):*
Let us all glorify with festal hymns the good shepherd Gregory, the all-wise bishop of Nyssa, the brother in the flesh and of one mind with the all-wise Basil.

*Glory... Both now... Of the Feast:*
The Savior, grace and truth, hath appeared in the streams of the Jordan, and hath enlightened those sleeping in darkness and shadow; for the unapproachable Light hath come and appeared.

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
Now strangely the Savior * bestows upon men a cleansing, * without the trial of fire, * and building up souls * without crushing.

*Verse:* The sea saw it and fled, * Jordan was driven back.[^1305]

The water of divine life * from the saving fountains, * O ye people, with gladness * draw ye zealously * for the redemption of souls.

*Verse:* What ailed thee, O sea, that thou fleddest? and thou, Jordan, that thou wast driven back?[^1306]

Enlightenment hath come, * grace hath appeared, redemption is at hand; * the world is enlightened: * O ye people, be filled with joy!

*Glory... Tone 4:*
O valiant ascetic of the true faith, who didst suffer together as a good soldier of Christ God, and didst please the Leader of the host: having fought now also the good fight for the Church, thou hast preserved her by thy dogmas upon an immovable foundation, O Gregory!

*Both now... Tone 8. By John the Monk:*
O Lord, desiring to fulfill what Thou didst establish from the ages, Thou didst receive ministers of Thy mystery from all creation: from the angels, Gabriel; from men, the Virgin; from the heavens, the star; and from the waters, the Jordan; wherein Thou didst destroy the lawlessness of the world: O our Savior, glory to Thee!

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes from the Canon of the Feast, Ode 5, with the heirmos on 4; and of the Saint, Ode 6, on 4. Prokeimenon:*
*Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones.*[^1307]

*Verse:* What shall I render unto the Lord for all that He hath rendered unto me?[^1308]

*Epistle to the Corinthians, Pericope 151 (1 Cor. 12:7–11).*

*Alleluia, Tone 2:*
*Thy priests shall be clothed with righteousness, and Thy venerable ones shall rejoice with joy.*[^1309]

*Gospel according to Matthew, Pericope 34 from the midpoint (Matt. 10:1, 5–8).*

*Communion Verse: The righteous man shall be in everlasting remembrance.*[^1310]

*In the same month, on the 11th day. Our Venerable Father Theodosius the Cenobiarch.*[^1311]

*At Vespers, "Blessed is the man," the first antiphon.*

*At "Lord, I have cried," we sing 6 Stichera, Tone 5, Podoben: "O Venerable Father" (Преподо́бне ѻ҆́тче):*
O venerable, God-bearing father Theodosius, thou didst strive exceedingly in this temporal life, in chantings, fastings, and vigils, having become an example unto thy disciples; and now thou dost dance with the bodiless hosts, unceasingly glorifying Christ, God the Word of God and our Redeemer, Who bowed His head unto the Forerunner and sanctified the nature of the waters: entreat Him, pray unto Him, O venerable one, to grant unto the Church oneness of mind, peace, and great mercy.

*Sticheron of the Saint:*
O venerable father: the grace of the All-Holy One made His abode in thee as a most pure light; by Whose operation being brightly adorned, thou dost unceasingly glorify Christ, the one Son in two essences, baptized by the hand of the Forerunner and witnessed by the Father's voice: entreat Him, pray unto Him, O venerable one, to grant unto the universe oneness of mind, peace, and great mercy.

*Sticheron of the Saint:*
O venerable, God-bearing father Theodosius, thou wast fittingly accounted worthy of the blessed life, having found it through purity and fasting; for while living thou didst pass over unto the life on high, bidding all to rejoice bidding all to rejoice, and with the bodiless hosts unceasingly glorifying Christ, Who ineffably received flesh from the Virgin and drowned our sins by baptism in the streams of the Jordan: entreat Him, pray unto Him, O holy one, to grant unto the universe oneness of mind, peace, and great mercy.

*Glory... Tone 2:*
O venerable father, like a city of the living God,[^1312] the river streams made glad thy sacred soul, the waters of remission of Christ our God, Who passed through the Jordan and poured forth the word of piety unto all the ends of the earth: entreat Him, O all-blessed Theodosius, that our souls may be saved.

*Both now... the same Tone:*
Thou didst bow Thy head unto the Forerunner, Thou didst crush the heads of the dragons;[^1313] having come into the streams, Thou didst enlighten all things to glorify Thee, O Savior, the Enlightener of our souls.

*Prokeimenon of the day, and the Readings:*

*Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon (Wisdom 5:15–6:3):*
The righteous live unto the ages, and their reward is in the Lord, and the care of them is with the Most High. Therefore shall they receive the kingdom of majesty, and the crown of comeliness from the hand of the Lord; for with His right hand shall He cover them, and with His arm shall He shield them. He shall take His jealousy for complete armor, and make the creation His weapon for the vengeance of His enemies. He shall put on righteousness as a breastplate, and take true judgment instead of a helmet. He shall take holiness for an invincible shield. His severe wrath shall He sharpen for a sword, and the world shall fight with Him against the unwise. Then shall the right-aiming thunderbolts go abroad; and from the clouds, as from a well-drawn bow, shall they fly to the mark. And hailstones full of wrath shall be cast as out of a stone bow, and the water of the sea shall rage against them, and the floods shall cruelly drown them. Yea, a mighty wind shall stand up against them, and like a storm shall it blow them away: thus iniquity shall lay waste the whole earth, and ill dealing shall overthrow the thrones of the mighty. Hear therefore, O ye kings, and understand; learn, ye that be judges of the ends of the earth. Give ear, ye that rule the people, and glory in the multitude of nations. For power is given you of the Lord, and sovereignty from the Most High.

*Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon (Wisdom 3:1–9):*
The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and there shall no torment touch them. In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die: and their departure was taken for misery, and their going from us to be utter destruction: but they are in peace. For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality. And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded: for God proved them, and found them worthy for Himself. As gold in the furnace hath He tried them, and received them as a whole burnt offering. And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble. They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and their Lord shall reign unto the ages. They that put their trust in Him shall understand the truth: and such as be faithful in love shall abide with Him: for grace and mercy is to His venerable ones, and visitation for His elect.

*Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon (Wisdom 4:7–15):*
Though the righteous be prevented with death, yet shall he be in rest. For honorable age is not that which stands in length of time, nor that is measured by number of years. But wisdom is the gray hair unto men, and an unspotted life is old age. He pleased God, and was beloved of Him: so that living among sinners he was translated. Yea, speedily was he taken away, lest that wickedness should alter his understanding, or deceit beguile his soul. For the bewitching of wickedness doth obscure things that are good; and the wandering of concupiscence doth undermine the simple mind. He, being made perfect in a short time, fulfilled a long time: for his soul pleased the Lord: therefore hasted He to take him away from among the wicked. This the people saw, and understood it not, neither laid they up this in their minds, that His grace and mercy is with His venerable ones, and that He hath respect unto His chosen.

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Hast Given a Sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе). By Joseph:*
How hast Thou clothed Thyself, * having put on mine image * which I created? * having humbled Himself beyond understanding, * the Lord said: Why then is it strange, O friend, * if I also bow down beneath thy right hand, * as one of thy fellow servants? * and I who am naked am clothed with waters; * for being compassionate, I desire to clothe those who are naked * in eternal incorruption.

*Verse:* The sea saw it and fled, * Jordan was driven back.[^1314]

Thou didst appear incarnate, * yet the womb that received Thee * remained unburnt; * for the furnace from afar foreshadowed her, * having not burnt the youths. * But I, who am grass, * how shall I place my hand upon the Fire, O Master, * Whom all things in heaven and on earth tremble before, * O Jesus all-powerful, * Savior of our souls?

*Verse:* What ailed thee, O sea, that thou fleddest? and thou, Jordan, that thou wast driven back?[^1315]

"Wash Me in the waters of the Jordan, Who have no defilement whatsoever," the Lord said; "and human nature, which was defiled * through Adam's transgression, * having washed itself, shall be made new. * For as I am baptized, renovation comes unto all men * through water and the Spirit."

*Glory... Tone 8. By the Studite:*
We honor thee, our father Theodosius, as the instructor of multitudes of monastics; for by thy path we have learned truly to walk uprightly. Blessed art thou who didst labor for Christ, and didst expose the power of the enemy. O companion of angels, partaker with the venerable and the righteous: with them pray unto the Lord that He have mercy upon our souls.

*Both now... the same Tone:*
The angelic hosts were awestruck at what was seen; for today, O Savior, as Thou stoodest naked in the waters in the Jordan, and didst bow Thy most pure head to be baptized by John. For when Thou didst willingly become poor, the world was enriched: O Lord, glory to Thee!

*Troparion, Tone 8:*
With the streams of thy tears thou didst cultivate the barren desert, and by the sighings from the depths thou didst bear fruit for thy labors a hundredfold, and didst become a luminary unto the universe, shining with marvels, O our father Theodosius: pray unto Christ God that our souls may be saved.

*Glory... Both now... Of the Feast, Tone 1:*
When Thou, O Lord, wast baptized in the Jordan, the worship of the Trinity was made manifest; for the voice of the Parent bore witness unto Thee, calling Thee His beloved Son, and the Spirit in the form of a dove confirmed the certainty of the word: O Christ God, Who hast appeared and enlightened the world, glory to Thee!

*At Matins, at "God is the Lord," the Troparion of the Feast twice; Glory... of the Saint; Both now... of the Feast.*

*And the customary Kathismata.*

*After the 1st Stichologia, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph Marvelled" (Оу҆диви́ся і҆ѡ́сифъ):*
Joshua the son of Nun, leading the people across the river Jordan, and the Ark of God, prefigured the future beneficence;[^1316] for the mysterious passage prefigures by the Spirit for us an image of return and a true representation of rebirth in both: Christ hath appeared at the Jordan to sanctify the waters.

*Glory... Both now... The same.*

*After the 2nd Stichologia, Sessional Hymn Tone 5, Podoben: "Co-unoriginate Word" (Собезнача́лное сло́во):*
The angelic ranks, seeing the Word, Who is co-honored with the Father and the Spirit, incarnate out of tender mercy and being baptized, trembled; and the river Jordan, being ashamed and fearful, turned back, raising us up unto the height of salvation, who were corrupted by passions.

*Glory... Both now... The same.*

*After the Polyeleos, Sessional Hymn, Tone 3, Podoben: "Toward the Divine Faith" (Къ бж҃е́ственнѣй вѣ́рѣ):*
Having lifted up thine eyes unto the divine height, O venerable one, thou wast shown forth as a light-bearing pillar, shining with the rays of prayer; for having winged thy thought thither, and become a partaker of unutterable things, thou wast wholly radiant, entreating Christ God to grant us great mercy. *Twice.*

*Glory... Both now... Of the Feast, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дѣ́ва дне́сь):*
Today the Master came unto the Jordan, being baptized in the waters by the divine Forerunner; and from on high the Father bore witness: "This is My beloved Son, in Whom I am well pleased"; and the Spirit appeared over Him in the strange likeness of a dove.

*Gradual, the 1st Antiphon of Tone 4.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 4:*
*Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones.*[^1317]

*Verse:* What shall I render unto the Lord for all that He hath rendered unto me?[^1318]

*Let every breath.*

*Gospel according to Luke, Pericope 24 (Luke 6:17–23).*

*After Psalm 50, Sticheron, Tone 6:*
O venerable father, into all the earth went forth the sound of thine achievements;[^1319] therefore in the heavens thou hast found the reward of thy labors; thou didst destroy the ranks of demons, and didst attain unto the choirs of angels, whose blameless life thou didst zealously emulate; having boldness toward Christ God, ask peace for our souls.

*Canon of the Feast with the heirmos on 8, Tone 2. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Israel walks through the billowing tempest of the sea, which was shown forth as dry land; but the black deep, a grave spread over with water, covered all together the Egyptian captains, by the mighty power of the Master's right hand.[^1320]

*Troparion of the Feast:*
When a light-bearing dawn appeared unto men, coming now from the wilderness unto the waters of the Jordan, O King, Thou didst bow Thy neck unto the sun, to snatch the forefather from the dark choir, and to cleanse creation from all defilement.

*Troparion of the Feast:*
O Word without beginning, when Thou wast buried together with the streams, Thou didst lead over anew him who was corrupted by deceit; having ineffably received for him the sovereign voice from the Father: "This is My beloved Son; yet as a servant is the Child unto Me by nature."

*Canon of the Saint on 6, Tone 2. By Theophanes. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
In the deep of old, an overwhelmingly armed power laid low the whole host of Pharaoh; but the incarnate Word destroyed all-wicked sin, the most glorious Lord, for He hath been gloriously glorified.[^1321]

*Troparion:*
As our wise leader of the ranks, O father Theodosius, fittingly begin the singing unto Christ God, Who came for universal salvation, and Who glorifies together with thee thy most holy memory.

*Troparion:*
The Forerunner of Christ came forth from the wilderness, having sprouted from the maternal womb of Elizabeth; and Theodosius, being born of the font through the Spirit, became a citizen of the wilderness, following after him.

*Troparion:*
When Christ was baptized in the streams, the insolence of the Israelite assembly was destroyed; and in the Church an angel-like life was planted, which thou didst unwaveringly accomplish, O all-blessed Theodosius.

*Troparion:*
Having become through fasting a partaker of the passion of Him Who was nailed unto the cross for our sake, O father, thou wast worthily conformed unto His resurrection, and didst become the glory of those who are saved, O Theodosius.

*Theotokion:*
The divine choir of maidens most divinely names thee good among women, O Lady Mother of God, adorned with the beauties of the Godhead; for beyond word thou didst give birth unto the beneficent Word.

*Katavasia:*
He uncovered the bottom of the deep...[^1322]

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 3. Heirmos:*
As many of us as have been loosed from the ancient snares, being crushed in jaws as the food of lions, let us rejoice and open our mouth wide, weaving a word from words of sweet melody, wherein He delights in gifts bestowed upon us.[^1323]

*Troparion of the Feast:*
He who formerly planted mortification in creation, having fashioned himself into the nature of the evil beast, is darkened by the bodily coming; when dawn appeared, he dashed against the Master to crush his own hostile head.

*Troparion of the Feast:*
The belly of the tormentor draws unto itself the God-created nature, buried within its boundaries; the renovation of the earthborn is born again, as the Master sovereignly accomplishes the deed; for He came desiring to cleanse it.

*Another Canon of the Saint. Ode 3. Heirmos:*
The wilderness hath blossomed as a lily, O Lord, the barren Church of the Gentiles, by Thy coming, wherein my heart hath been established.[^1324]

*Troparion:*
The Lord Who covers His high places with waters,[^1325] is bodily clothed in the streams of the Jordan: wherein my heart hath been established.

*Troparion:*
The divine Light shining forth in the Jordan, a God-given sprouting unto those upon the earth, manifests thee, O Theodosius, as a son of blessing and good goodwill.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst forsake the world and the things in the world, O venerable one, emulating the Master's nakedness at the Jordan, O Theodosius.

*Troparion:*
Having taken the Savior's cross upon thy shoulders, thou didst run unto His tomb, as a hart unto the saving fountains of water,[^1326] O all-blessed Theodosius.

*Theotokion:*
The angelic ranks were awestruck, O all-immaculate one, and human hearts were struck with fear at thy childbearing; therefore with faith we honor thee as Mother of God.

*Katavasia:*
Thou Who givest strength unto our kings...[^1327]

*Kontakion of the Feast, Tone 4:*
Today Thou hast appeared unto the universe, and Thy light, O Lord, hath been signed upon us, who with understanding sing of Thee: Thou hast come and appeared, O Light unapproachable![^1328]

*Ikos:*
Unto Galilee of the Gentiles, unto the country of Zebulun, and the land of Naphtali, as the Prophet said, a great Light hath shone forth: Christ.[^1329] A bright dawn hath appeared unto those in darkness, shining forth from Bethlehem; yet more so from Mary, the Lord, the Sun of righteousness, shines His rays upon the whole universe.[^1330] Therefore, all ye who are naked from Adam, come, let us put Him on, that we may be warmed; for He covers those who are naked, and enlightens those who are in darkness: Thou hast come and appeared, O Light unapproachable!

*Sessional Hymn of the Saint, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Прему́дрости):*
Having adorned thy soul in a God-befitting manner with self-restraint, toils, and prayers, thou wast a fellow partaker with the monks, O blessed one; and in truth thou didst receive the gifts of marvels, to heal the infirmities of those who honor thee in faith; therefore, driving away multitudes of demons, thou dost grant healings unto men by grace: O God-bearing Theodosius, entreat Christ God to grant the remission of sins unto those who celebrate thy memory with faith. *Twice.*

*Glory... Both now... Of the Feast, the same Tone:*
The Jordan serves with streams, and John stretches forth a corruptible hand, when Thou, Who art invisible in the flesh, didst appear for baptism; yet the one indeed was turned back by fear, while the other straightway held Thee, the Incorruptible One, with trembling: truly the Lamb of God, the fountain of overflowing life, Who hast sanctified the fountains, the seas, and men. For the Trinity shone forth: from on high the Parent names Thee Son, and the Holy Spirit descends.

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Cleansed by the fire of a mystic vision, the Prophet, singing of the renovation of men, utters a voice clapping through the Spirit, revealing the incarnation of the ineffable Word, by Whom the dominions of the mighty have been shattered.[^1331]

*Troparion of the Feast:*
Sent forth from the Father, O all-radiant Word, Thou comest to drive away the ill-darkened onslaught of night, and to root out the sins of men; and by Thy baptism, O Good One, to draw forth radiant sons from the streams of the Jordan.

*Troparion of the Feast:*
Having foreseen the very Word designated, the herald clearly cries out unto creation: "Lo, He Who is before me, second in the flesh, hath shone forth conformed by divine power, to take away our hostile sin."

*Troparion of the Feast:*
Carrying in Himself life-giving pasture, God the Word catches the nests of serpents, rushing upon them with many snares, casting them down; and He trips up him who wounded the universal race: having destroyed him, He delivers creation.

*Another Canon of the Saint. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Thou hast come from the Virgin, not an intercessor nor an angel, but Thyself incarnate, O Lord, and hast saved me, the whole man; therefore I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^1332]

*Troparion:*
In the waters Thou didst crush the heads of the dragons,[^1333] and through the Spirit, O Word of God, Thou didst renew me, the whole man; therefore I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
By submission and surpassing humility, O father Theodosius, thou didst become like unto Christ Who bowed His head unto the Forerunner; and thou didst ascend the unshakable pillar of virtue.

*Troparion:*
Having served the Mother of Christ God of all, thou didst receive the invincible grace of the Spirit, O father Theodosius; and didst cast down the invisible enemies.

*Troparion:*
The glorious cave of Rhodos,[^1334] having received thee, showed thee forth as a bearer of gifts unto Christ Who was baptized for our sake, bringing faith, O Theodosius, and love with hope.

*Troparion:*
Strengthened by the passion of Christ before, thou didst endure martyrdom with a loving conscience, O father Theodosius, wrestling against the dark ruler of this world.

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst conceive the Lord in Thy womb without seed, and having given birth unto Him incarnate, Who saves the world by thy prayers; therefore we cry unto thee: Rejoice, Ever-Virgin Mother of God!

*Katavasia:*
*I have heard Thy voice, O Lord:*[^1335]

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Washed by the cleansing of the Spirit from the dark and defiled poison of the enemy, we have come unto a new and unerring path, leading unto inaccessible joy, accessible only unto those with whom God is reconciled.[^1336]

*Troparion of the Feast:*
The Creator, having seen in the gloom of transgressions him whom His crafty fingers had made, caught in inescapable snares, raises him up and places him upon both His shoulders; and now in the abundant waters He washes away the shame of Adam's ancient evil disposition.[^1337]

*Troparion of the Feast:*
With piety let us run diligently unto the most pure fountains of the saving stream, beholding the Word from incorruptible things, bringing ladles of divine thirst, sweetly healing the disease of the world.

*Another Canon of the Saint. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Thou hast been a mediator between God and men, O Christ God; for through Thee, O Master, we have access from the night of ignorance unto Thy Father, the Prince of Light.[^1338]

*Troparion:*
Having kindled the mind with Him Who renewed us in the waters, thou didst wisely strengthen those cast down, having conquered the body by fasting, O all-blessed Theodosius.

*Troparion:*
Having ever made thy life a meditation upon death, and striving to depart unto Him Who for our sake appeared in the flesh: thou didst make a tomb for thyself, O Theodosius.[^1339]

*Troparion:*
Emulating the voluntary death of Christ, O father Theodosius, thy glorious disciple Basil joyfully renews a new tomb.[^1340]

*Theotokion:*
Lo, in thy womb, O all-pure Mother of God, thou didst have Christ God beyond word, as Isaiah foretold; and beyond nature, O Parent of God, thou didst give birth unto Him.[^1341]

*Katavasia:*
*Jesus, the Prince of Life:*[^1342]

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 6. Heirmos:*
With an all-blessed voice, the Father declared Him the beloved Whom He brought forth from His belly: Yea, He says, this radiant Son, being of one essence, hath come forth from the human race: My living Word, and a man by providence.[^1343]

*Troparion of the Feast:*
Strangely bleating in the belly of the sea monster of the deep for three nights, the Prophet came forth straightway, showing forth beforehand unto all in the last times the salvation of regeneration from the man-slaying serpent.[^1344]

*Troparion of the Feast:*
When heaven was opened, as the all-radiant Scriptures say, the disciple sees the Spirit sent from the Father, abiding upon the most pure Word, having descended as a dove in an ineffable manner, and appearing unto the people who had come unto the Master.[^1345]

*Another Canon of the Saint. Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Wallowing in the abyss of sins, I call upon the unfathomable abyss of Thy compassion: bring me up from corruption, O God![^1346]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst grant incorruption unto us in Thy resurrection, O Christ; therefore Basil, Thy glorious servant, even having died, appears as living.[^1347]

*Troparion:*
He Who cleanses the world is baptized, God having become man for my sake like unto me; Whom in two natures, O blessed Theodosius, thou didst proclaim.[^1348]

*Troparion:*
Unto Christ God, Who turned the tears of the Myrrh-bearers into joy, the streams of thy tears dripped, O Theodosius, as the sweetness of gladness.

*Theotokion:*
Vouchsafe me thy compassion, O thou who didst give birth unto the most merciful Word, Who by His own blood delivered men from corruption.

*Katavasia:*
*The voice of the Word:*[^1349]

*Kontakion of the Saint, Tone 8, Podoben: "To Thee, the Champion Leader" (Взбра́нной):*
Planted in the courts of thy Lord,[^1350] thou didst blossom forth beautifully by thy venerable virtues, and didst multiply thy children in the wilderness, watered by the showers of thy tears, O shepherd of God's divine sheepfolds; therefore we cry: Rejoice, O father Theodosius!

*Ikos:*
A man indeed thou wast by nature, O father, yet thou didst appear as a fellow citizen of the angels; for having lived upon earth as though bodiless, O wise one, thou didst cast away all carnal forethought. Therefore thou hearest also from us: Rejoice, scion of a pious father! Rejoice, branch of a reverent mother! Rejoice, all-comely citizen of the wilderness! Rejoice, many-lighted luminary of the universe! Rejoice, for from youth thou didst follow Christ! Rejoice, for thou didst wither the pleasures of the flesh! Rejoice, mediator of salvation for monks! Rejoice, image of consolation for those in despondency! Rejoice, thou who didst deliver many from deceit! Rejoice, granting streams of marvels! Rejoice, thou who didst care for the poor! Rejoice, our protector and deliverer! Rejoice, O father Theodosius!

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The high flame of the furnace, which carried the pious youths, burned the heads of the dragons with a stream having stilled the unbearable gloom of sin, washes it all away with the dew of the Spirit.[^1351]

*Troparion of the Feast:*
Thou makest the Assyrian flame, which depicted Thee, terrible, turned into dew; therefore the water now, like a flame clothing harmful wickedness, O Christ, consumes what is concealed, calling us back from the slippery path.

*Troparion of the Feast:*
Having parted the Jordan of old, the people of Israel pass over on dry land;[^1352] now in the waters they drink Thee, the most sovereign Holder of creation, without delay, unto the incorruptible and profitable path.

*Troparion of the Feast:*
We know that the all-destructive flood first mercifully brought all unto corruption, O Thou Who hast wrought exceeding great and strange wonders! But now, O Christ, Thou hast drowned sin out of loving compassion and for the salvation of mankind.[^1353]

*Another Canon of the Saint. Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The God-opposing decree of the lawless tyrant lifted up the high flame, but Christ stretched forth the spiritual dew unto the pious youths: He Who is blessed and supremely glorified.[^1354]

*Troparion:*
Having combined in Thy baptism, O Word of God, a stream consuming sin and a flame bedewing the human race, O Lord, God supremely exalted: Blessed art Thou and supremely glorified!

*Troparion:*
Unto Him Who made the Jordan a furnace, thou didst offer thyself wholly as incense, O venerable one; and receiving the heavenly flame, the unfailing image of divine will, thou didst raise up a church saving for souls.[^1355]

*Troparion:*
By thy leadership the laws of Moses are fulfilled, now that grace hath appeared, O venerable one; for having cast down the invisible enemies, thy people inherit the heavenly city, O all-praised one.

*Troparion:*
Unto Him Who buried sin with streams, thou didst make thyself a God-pleasing dwelling, O Theodosius; having built a church to offer unceasing hymnody, thou didst decree rules in multilingual voices.[^1356]

*Troparion:*
Emulating the boldness of the youths, thou didst rebuke the fire-breathing threat of the tyrant, wisely defending the Church of Christ, O father Theodosius: for Whose sake He voluntarily appeared crucified in the flesh.[^1357]

*Theotokion:*
A pure conception and incorrupt childbearing thou alone didst show forth, remaining a Virgin; for thou didst conceive God Who is over all, O pure one, Who became man for the salvation and deliverance of the faithful.

*Katavasia:*
*The pious youths in the furnace:*[^1358]

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Free Creation is known to be free indeed, and those who were formerly darkened are become sons of light; the prince of darkness alone groans: now let the formerly wretched inheritance of the nations zealously bless the Cause.[^1359]

*Troparion of the Feast:*
Bedewed in the fire of the three-fold vision of God, illuminated by three all-radiant holinesses, they clearly showed forth the transcendent nature by human mixture, mercifully burning every destructive deceit with dew.

*Troparion of the Feast:*
Let every earthly nature be made white, being now raised from its fall unto heaven; for washed by the flowing streams through the Word by Whom all things are preserved, it hath escaped former sins, having been washed most brightly.

*Another Canon of the Saint. Ode 8. Heirmos:*
The fiery furnace of old in Babylon divided its operation by the divine command, burning the Chaldeans, but bedewing the faithful, who sang: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^1360]

*Troparion:*
The furnace of old in Babylon prefigured the streams of the Jordan, burning the adversaries by a supernatural baptism, but bedewing the faithful who sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*
Having surpassed bodily passions before thy departure, O Theodosius, drawing water from the depths of the earth, as a youth appeared unto thee crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^1361]

*Troparion:*
The blessing of thy hands was the most divine command of Christ Who is baptized in the streams, producing water for the unerring earth, and the sun warming it; for a grain was nourished without seed into a fruitful ear of wheat.[^1362]

*Troparion:*
Having entered into the spiritual gloom of the most divine light, O Theodosius, and written the tablets upon thy heart with the finger of God,[^1363] thou didst bring the teachings of piety unto thy disciples as a book of life, O all-blessed one.

*Troparion:*
Emulating the firm faith of the woman with the issue of blood, O father, a woman touched thy haircloth, and as darkness before light, the disease was driven away by the illumination in thee; for thou wast a vessel of election unto Christ Who appeared.[^1364]

*Triadikon:*
Having seen Thee, God of God, Christ Who didst ineffably appear in the flesh, we have known Thy invisible Father and Thy Holy Spirit, crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Theotokion:*
Him Who is inseparable from the Father, Who dwelt in thy womb in a God-manly manner, without seed thou didst con- ceive, and didst ineffably bear; therefore we know thee to be the salvation of us all.

*Katavasia:*
*A most glorious mystery:*[^1365]

*Canon of the Feast. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
O the marvels of thy childbearing beyond understanding! O all-pure bride, blessed Mother, through whom having obtained all-perfect salvation, we worthily praise Him as Benefactor, bringing as a gift a hymn of thanksgiving.[^1366]

*Troparion of the Feast:*
We have known the things revealed unto Moses by the bush; come with strange statutes wrought: for as the Virgin was preserved carrying fire, having given birth unto the light-bearing Benefactor, who is now revealed in the streams of the Jordan.[^1367]

*Troparion of the Feast:*
Perfecting human nature, O King without beginning, by communion with the Spirit, Thou anointest it, having washed it with pure streams from darkness; and having put to shame the haughty power, Thou hast now granted us an unending life.

*Another Canon of the Saint. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
The Son of the unoriginate Father, God and Lord, having become incarnate of the Virgin, hath appeared unto us, to enlighten those in darkness, to gather the scattered; therefore we magnify the all-hymned Mother of God.[^1368]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst preach the Councils, O God-wise Theodosius, equal in number unto the honorable Gospels of Christ,[^1369] receiving martyr's blood by zealous intention: and thou didst appear as a bloodless martyr of piety.

*Troparion:*
He justly judged the judgment of the unjust one, driving him away for thy banishment, and taking the ungodly soul from blasphemous lips, and depriving of life the enemy of life, O venerable one.[^1370]

*Troparion:*
Remembering thy teachings, O Theodosius, we preach Christ in two essences: knowing two wills, natural, operative, and self-determining, in God Who was baptized in the flesh.[^1371]

*Troparion:*
True to thy name, a good gift from the Father of lights,[^1372] thou wast a physician of souls and bodies, abundant food and drink unto those wasting away in hunger and thirst, clothing unto the naked, and setting-aright unto those who fall.

*Troparion:*
Cease not looking upon thy flock, O venerable father, and remembering thy promise, which we have bound unto the rock as an unbroken anchor of hope, having thee as a mediator unto Christ, O Theodosius.

*Triadikon:*
Let us the faithful piously praise and glorify the Trinity of one essence, the Monad in three counts: the indivisible, transcendent nature in three hypostases, the unwaning dawn, one and incorruptible, Who hath shone forth light upon us.

*Theotokion:*
As an early dawn in the night of life thou wast found, flashing with the rays of virginity: the Dayspring of the spiritual Sun of righteousness, who didst appear unto us, O all-pure Mother of God.[^1373]

*Katavasia:*
*Every tongue is at a loss:*[^1374]

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "Thou Hast Visited Us" (Посѣти́лъ ны̀):*
We have been brightly cleansed, O my Christ, by Thy cleansing; and now we are enriched with festal joy by the memory of honorable Theodosius: therefore the orders of monks rejoice. *Twice.*

*Glory... Both now... Of the Feast:*
The Savior, grace and truth, hath appeared in the streams of the Jordan, and hath enlightened those sleeping in darkness and shadow: for the unapproachable Light hath come and appeared.

*At the Praises, Stichera on 4, Tone 5, Podoben: "Rejoice" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ):*
Having prepared thyself beforehand, O Theodosius, as a house of lofty virtues, to dwell in the divine temple of the Mother of God and to consecrate it: for thou didst love to behold the brightness of God, and now thou beholdest the beauty and the ineffable splendor of the true tabernacle; which having founded, O venerable one, he who was gladdens those who zealously look unto Him: entreat Him to send down great mercy upon our souls.

*Sticheron of the Saint:*
Having cleansed thyself with ascetic sufferings, thou wast an imitator of thy Master, O all-blessed one; for touching the hem of thy garment, thou didst heal disease;[^1375] thou didst feed those wasting away from hunger in the wilderness, giving from an inexhaustible treasure, having been named after the gift of God; and thou didst proclaim the Orthodox faith, O venerable one, accounting the fury of the tyrant as nothing: entreat Christ Who grants great mercy unto the world.

*Sticheron of the Saint:*
Having kindled an unswerving and blazing flame of warm love towards God, thou didst receive radiance from heaven announcing divine goodwill unto thee: to build a most holy church, an instruction of virtue and a care of souls; which having begun, thou didst piously complete, where also thy much-suffering body lies, honored by honorable burials, O all-blessed one, held in veneration by those who call upon thee: entreat Christ to send down great mercy upon our souls.

*Sticheron of the Saint:*
Truly unto the marvelous tabernacle, even unto the house of God, O Theodosius, thou didst pass through with rejoicing and gladness of soul:[^1376] where the voice of those that keep festival is, O father, desiring to hear the comely and sweet singing, and of ineffable sweetness of soul and of consolation having become a participant of consolation, O blessed one; desiring this very thing, thou didst mortify the flesh, which also thou didst obtain, adorned with divine righteousness: entreat Christ to grant great mercy unto our souls.

*Glory... Tone 2:*
A ladder of virtues, an image appeared mystically upon earth; let us praise him as the adornment of ascetics. For having truly fasted, like great Anthony, showing forth measureless humility, and having shepherded his people piously, he settled them in the holy sheepfold, where the angelic choir abides. Diligently we cry unto thee: Forget not now thy flock, O all-blessed Theodosius, but by thy prayers unto the Lord, save us, we pray!

*Both now... The same Tone:*
Today Christ hath come to be baptized in the Jordan; today John touches the crown of the Master's head; the heavenly hosts were amazed, beholding the most glorious mystery:[^1377] the sea saw it and fled, Jordan was driven back;[^1378] and we who are enlightened cry: Glory to God Who hath appeared, and was seen upon earth, and hath enlightened the world!

*Great Doxology.*
*After the Trisagion, the Troparion of the Saint:*
*Glory... Both now... of the Feast.*
*Litanies, and Dismissal. At the Liturgy:*
*The Beatitudes from the Canon of the Feast, Ode 6, on 4; and of the Saint, Ode 6, on 4.*
*Prokeimenon, Tone 7:*
*Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones.*[^1379]
*Verse: What shall I render unto the Lord for all that He hath rendered unto me?*[^1380]

*Epistle to the Corinthians, Pericope 163 (2 Cor. 4:6–15).*[^1381]

*Alleluia, Tone 2:*
*Blessed is the man that fears the Lord, in His commandments he will delight greatly.*[^1382]
*Verse: His seed shall be mighty upon the earth.*[^1383]

*Gospel according to Matthew, Pericope 43 (Matt. 11:27–30).*[^1384]

*Communion Verse: The righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance.*[^1385]

*It is fitting to know concerning this, how the Sunday of the Publican and the Pharisee falls.*[^1386]

*The Sunday of the Publican and the Pharisee begins on January 11, during the Afterfeast of Theophany, on the commemoration of our venerable father Theodosius; and it extends as far as February 15.*

*Be it known: That if the Sunday of the Publican and the Pharisee should happen to fall on January 11: the service of the venerable Theodosius is chanted whenever the Ecclesiarch decides, on another day.*

*On Saturday evening: At Little Vespers, the Resurrection Stichera, and of the Mother of God, ac-* cording to custom. At Great Vespers we sing: "Blessed is the man," the entire kathisma.[^1387]

*At "Lord, I have cried," we sing 3 Resurrection Stichera, and 1 Anatolian; and 3 of the Feast, of that day; and 2 Idiomela of the Triodion, repeating the first: Glory, of the Triodion; Both now, the first Theotokion of the tone. Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day.*

*At the Litiya: Stichera of the Feast, the Aposticha of that day from Vespers and Matins. Glory... Both now... of the Triodion, Tone 3.*

*At the Aposticha, the Resurrection Stichera according to the alphabet; Glory, of the Feast; Both now, of the Triodion. At the blessing of the loaves, the Troparion "O Virgin Mother of God," twice; and of the Feast, once; and a reading. But if there is no vigil: After "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart," the Resurrection Troparion; Glory... Both now... of the Feast. At Compline after "It is truly meet," and after "Our Father," the Kontakion of the Feast; Glory... Both now... of the Triodion.*

*At Matins, at "God is the Lord," the Resurrection Troparion, twice; Glory... Both now... of the Feast. After the kathismata, the Resurrection Sessional Hymns, with their Theotokia. And a reading in the Commentary Gospel, for the Sunday after the Enlightenment. After the Blameless, the Troparia "The Angelic Host"; and the Hypakoe of the tone. And a reading for the Sunday of the Publican and the Pharisee. The Anavathmoi, and the Prokeimenon of the tone. The Resurrection Gospel. "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ." Psalm 50. Glory, Tone 8: "Open unto me the doors of repentance." Both now, Theotokion: "Guide me upon the paths of salvation." Then, "Have mercy on me, O God," and "When I ponder the multitude of evil deeds I have done." And the customary prayer: "Save, O God, Thy people."*

*The Resurrection Canon with the heirmos on 4; and of the Feast on 4; and of the Triodion on 6. Katavasia of the Feast. After Ode 3, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Feast, and the Sessional Hymn; Glory... Both now... of the Triodion. After Ode 6, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Triodion. At Ode 9, we sing "More honorable than the Cherubim." The Resurrection Exapostilarion; Glory, of the Feast; Both now, of the Triodion. At the Praises, 3 Resurrection Stichera, and 3 of the Feast; and of the Triodion, Tone 3, with the verses: "Arise, O Lord my God"; for the Publican and the Pharisee: on 5, "I will confess unto Thee, O Lord": "The boastful voice of the Pharisee." Glory: "Through the deeds of boasting." Both now: "All-blessed art thou." And the Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, the Resurrection Troparion only. Litanies, and Dismissal. And the customary litiya in the narthex, in which we sing: Glory... Both now... the Gospel Sticheron. And the First Hour. At the Hours, the Resurrection Troparion; Glory, of the Feast; Both now, the Theotokion of the Hours. After "Our Father," the Kontakion of the Feast, and the complete dismissal. Likewise at the other Hours, we say the Resurrection Troparion and of the Feast; and we alternate the Kontakia.*

*At the Liturgy:*
*The Beatitudes of the tone on 4; and of the Feast the ordinary ode on 4; and of the Triodion Ode 6 on 4. After the Entrance, the Resurrection Troparion and of the Feast; Glory, the Kontakion of the Feast; Both now, of the Triodion. Prokeimenon of the Sunday after the Enlightenment; then of the Feast. Epistle and Gospel of the Sunday after the Enlightenment; then of the Publican and the Pharisee. Communion Verse: Praise the Lord from the heavens.*[^1388] *Another: Of the Feast.*

*In the same month, on the 12th day. Holy Martyr Tatiana.*[^1389]

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Feast, Tone 8, Podoben: "O Lord, Though at the Judgment Seat" (Гдⷭ҇и, а҆́ще и҆ на сꙋди́щи):*
O Lord, though Thou didst endure in the flesh to be baptized, O Sinless One, desiring to free the world from sin, yet knowing Thee as God we glorify Thee; for having been baptized, Thou didst deliver our souls from servitude.

*Sticheron of the Feast:*
O Lord, when incarnate Thou camest unto the streams of the Jordan, to sanctify the water by Thy glorious baptism, Thou wast pleased to bow Thy head unto John, and Thou art baptized by a servant, that Thou mightest save our souls.

*Sticheron of the Feast:*
O Lord, desiring to save the world from deceit, which Thou didst create, Thou wast pleased to become incarnate of a Virgin that knew not wedlock; and Thou didst deliver Adam from corruption as the Lover of mankind, and having been baptized Thou didst grant enlightenment unto our souls.

*Other Stichera of the Saint, Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*
When thou wast richly illuminated by the light of the Spirit, thou didst despise wealth, having loved only heavenly things; thou didst clearly clothe thyself with martyr's strength, and didst yield thyself unto measureless pains; therefore, having cast down the enemy, thou didst weave crowns of victory, O glorious martyr and passion-bearer!

*Sticheron of the Saint:*
When thou didst quench the stench of the flesh and the flame of sin, O honorable one, by the dew of the divine Spirit working with thee: then thou didst bridle the wild beasts in the midst of the tribunal,[^1390] having surrendered thy body unto wounds manfully; therefore, having cast down the enemy, thou didst weave crowns of victory, O God-blessed Tatiana!

*Sticheron of the Saint:*
Neither sword, nor fire, nor wounds, nor affliction, nor famine, nor any manner of torment blunted thy yearning towards the Lord; for seeking Him with an inflamed heart, thou didst spit upon all visible things once for all, O martyr, and didst make thy dwelling within the divine bridal chamber, having become the bride of the King of all.

*Glory... Both now... Tone 5:*
Beholding Thee naked in the waters asking baptism of the Creator, every nature of the earthborn changed with fear and was amazed; and the Forerunner was held with trembling, not daring to draw near unto Thee; the sea fled, Jordan turned back its streams; the mountains leaped, beholding; and the angelic hosts wondered, saying: O wonder! The Savior is stripped naked, desiring to clothe men with salvation and renewal!

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 6, Podoben: "The Angelic Hosts" (А҆́гг҃лскїа):*
Now let us cry prophetically unto the Lord: Thou hast appeared unto us, O our Savior and Creator! And Thou didst crush the mouths of the dragons in the Jordan, as Thou art compassionate, and didst enlighten the blinded by Thy light, O Christ: Blessed art Thou Who hast appeared, our God, glory to Thee!

*Verse: The sea saw it and fled, * Jordan was driven back.*[^1391]

*Sticheron of the Feast:*
By Thy baptism, O Word, Thou hast given us dominion over enemies, who love and honor Thy dispensation which Thou didst voluntarily accomplish, loosing men from the curse that fell in Eden; unto Whom we sing: Blessed art Thou Who hast appeared, our God, glory to Thee!

*Verse: What ailed thee, O sea, that thou fleddest? * and thou, Jordan, that thou wast driven back?*[^1392]

*Sticheron of the Feast:*
We who from Adam were of old voluntarily clothed with coats of skins through the fall,[^1393] having stripped ourselves today in the streams of the Jordan by the Lord's baptism, theologizing with the angels let us cry out unto Him: Blessed art Thou Who hast appeared, our God, glory to Thee!

*Glory... Both now... The same Tone, Idiomelon:*
Let us the faithful sing of the greatness of God's benefaction towards us; for having become man for the sake of our transgression, He is cleansed in the Jordan for our cleansing: the only pure and incorrupt One, sanctifying me and the waters, and crushing the heads of the dragons in the water.[^1394] Therefore let us draw water with gladness, O brethren; for the grace of the Spirit is invisibly given unto those who draw in faith, from Christ God and the Savior of our souls.

*Troparion of the Feast, Tone 1:*

When Thou wast baptized in the Jordan, O Lord, the worship of the Trinity was made manifest; for the voice of the Parent bare witness unto Thee, calling Thee His beloved Son; and the Spirit in the guise of a dove confirmed the certainty of the word. O Christ God Who hast appeared and enlightened the world, glory to Thee![^1395]

*At Matins, after the first Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph Marveled" (Оу҆диви́сѧ і҆ѡ́сифъ):*
O Jordan river, why wast thou amazed, beholding the Invisible One naked? I saw and trembled, it said; and how was I not to fear Him and turn back? His angels were afraid, beholding Him; heaven was struck with awe, and the earth trembled; and the sea was troubled, and all things visible and invisible. Christ appeared at the Jordan to sanctify the waters.[^1396]

*Glory... Both now... The same.*

*After the second Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "The Shepherds' Pipes" (Свирѣ́лей па́стырскихъ):*
Christ is baptized, Who enlightens the world; from on high the Father bare witness, saying: This is My beloved Son in Whom I am well pleased, hear ye Him. This is He Who enlightens the universe by His compassion, having been baptized and having saved the human race as God.[^1397]

*Glory... Both now... The same.*

*The Canon of the Feast with the Heirmos unto 8, and of the Saint unto 4.*

*Canon of the Feast, Tone 2.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
He laid bare the bottom of the deep, and leads His own dry-shod; having covered the adversaries therein, the Lord mighty in battle, for He hath been glorified.[^1398]

*Troparion:*
He renews fallen Adam with the streams of Jordan, and crushes the heads of dragons that nest therein, the King of ages, the Lord, for He hath been glorified.[^1399]

*Troparion:*
Having clothed Himself in material flesh with the immaterial fire of the Godhead, the Lord incarnate of the Virgin is encompassed by Jordan's water, for He hath been glorified.

*Troparion:*
Washing away the filth of men, cleansed with them in the Jordan, having willed to be made like unto them while remaining what He was, the Lord enlightens those that are in darkness, for He hath been glorified.[^1400]

*Canon of the Saint, the Work of Ignatius, Tone 2.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Come, O ye peoples, let us sing a song unto Christ God, Who divided the sea and guided the people whom He brought out of the bondage of Egypt, for He hath been glorified.[^1401]

*Troparion:*
Illumined with the splendors of martyrdom, thou standest before thy pure Bridegroom, O martyr, asking that they who praise thee be delivered from soul-corrupting transgressions.

*Troparion:*
Corruptible wealth thou didst utterly despise, O martyr, fervently seeking that which is incorruptible and abides in the heavens; and rejoicing thou didst pass through martyr's suffering.[^1402]

*Troparion:*
Fearlessly, O martyr, thou didst encounter wounds, ailments, and manifold beatings; for thou hadst the Savior's grace helping and strengthening thee.

*Theotokion:*
O Maiden, who gavest birth unto the Fountain of passionlessness, heal me that am wounded with passions, and snatch me from eternal fire, O only one full of God's grace.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
The Lord, Who gives strength unto our kings and exalts the horn of His anointed, is born of the Virgin, and comes unto baptism; let us the faithful cry aloud unto Him: There is none holy like our God.[^1403]

*Troparion:*
Rejoice today, O Church of Christ, which before wast barren and bitterly childless; for sons are born unto thee by water and the Spirit, crying out in faith: There is none holy like our God.[^1404]

*Troparion:*
With a great voice the Forerunner cries in the wilderness: Prepare the ways for Christ, and make straight the paths for our God, crying out in faith: There is none holy like our God.[^1405]

*Another [Canon of the Saint]. Heirmos:*
Having established me upon the rock of faith, Thou hast enlarged my mouth against mine enemies; for my spirit rejoiced when singing: There is none holy like our God, and there is none righteous beside Thee, O Lord.[^1406]

*Troparion:*
The surging storm of torments did not shake the pillar of thy heart, for it was established upon the rock of the love of Christ, O all-praised one, unto Whom thou didst cry aloud: For there is none holy beside Thee, O Lord.[^1407]

*Troparion:*
He Who bare human weakness winged thy weakness with power against the feeble serpent; therefore, O martyr, thou didst cast him down unto the ground, crying out in faith: For there is none holy beside Thee, O Lord.[^1408]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst dry up the torrents of iniquity by the streams of thy blood, O blessed one; and now thou dost delight in the torrent of sweetness, and dwellest in the unwaning light, crying out: For there is none holy beside Thee, O Lord.[^1409]

*Theotokion:*
Thy conceiving and thy childbearing are beyond word, for thou didst bear Him Who made the ages by a word, Who delivered the ends of the world from irrationality, O Maiden unwedded; pray Him always that He save our souls.[^1410]

*Kontakion of the Martyr, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Hast Appeared Today" (Ꙗ҆ви́лсѧ є҆сѝ дне́сь):*

Brightly didst thou shine forth in thy suffering, O passion-bearer, adorned with thy blood, and like a fair dove didst thou fly up unto heaven, O Tatiana; therefore pray ever for those that honor thee.[^1411]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily Anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*
Having accomplished a twofold struggle on earth, O martyr, thou wast accounted worthy to receive a twofold crown from the hand of thy Bridegroom; for thou didst fast, bridling the passions of the flesh, and having suffered lawfully thou didst cast down the enemy. Therefore by thy supplications save us from perils.[^1412]

*Glory... Both now... The same Tone and Podoben:*
He Who clothes Himself with light as with a garment, Christ our God, is clothed with Jordan's streams. When the Father of one throne bare witness from on high, and the Spirit of glory came below, He it is that enlightens and sanctifies us.[^1413]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I heard, O Lord, Thy voice which Thou didst utter, the voice of one crying in the wilderness, for Thou didst thunder over many waters, bearing witness unto Thy Son; being wholly filled with the Spirit that came down, he cried aloud: Thou art Christ, the Wisdom and Power of God.[^1414]

*Troparion:*
Who hath seen the sun, which is radiant by nature, being cleansed? the preacher cries aloud: Shall I wash Thee with waters, the Radiance of glory, the Image of the Ever-Existing Father? and being hay, shall I touch the fire of Thy Godhead? For Thou art Christ, the Wisdom and Power of God.[^1415]

*Troparion:*
Having the divine reverence that Moses had when he met with Thee; for as he understood that Thou didst speak out of the bush, he immediately turned away his face; so how shall I look upon Thee clearly? or how shall I lay my hand upon Thee? For Thou art Christ, the Wisdom and Power of God.[^1416]

*Troparion:*
Performing what is spiritual wisely, and being honored with reason, I am ashamed before soulless things; for if I baptize Thee, the smoking mountain accuses me, and the sea that fled divided in two, and this Jordan that turned back; for Thou art Christ, the Wisdom and Power of God.[^1417]

*Another [Canon of the Saint]. Heirmos:*
I sing unto Thee, for by hearing I have heard Thee, O Lord, and was afraid; for Thou comest unto me, seeking me that was lost; therefore I glorify Thy great condescension unto me, O most Merciful One.[^1418]

*Troparion:*
Bearing a fair spiritual disposition with the beauty of piety, Tatiana, shining gloriously moreover with the light of martyrdom, is lodged with the pure Bridegroom.

*Troparion:*
While the iniquitous scraped thy face with iron, unseen angels tortured the tormentors, having been sent from God unto thy aid, O martyr, who marveled at thy patience.[^1419]

*Troparion:*
Lawfully preaching Christ, thou didst conquer the lawless; and thou didst offer thyself unto Him as a blameless, acceptable, most perfect sacrifice, crying aloud: Loving Thee, O Savior, I am sacrificed.[^1420]

*Theotokion:*
Guide me unto a calm haven, O all-blameless Bride of God; for the storm tosses me, and the turbulence of sin bitterly; shaken by the winds of the evil spirits that afflict me.[^1421]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Jesus, the Prince of life, comes to loose the condemnation of Adam the first-formed; and though as God He needs no cleansing, He cleanses the fallen one in the Jordan; wherein having slain the enmity, He grants the peace that passes all understanding.[^1422]

*Troparion:*
When people without number came together to be baptized by John, He Himself stood in their midst, and he cried unto those present: Who hath warned you, ye disobedient, to flee from the wrath to come? Bring forth fruits worthy of Christ, for He that stands present now grants peace.[^1423]

*Troparion:*
The Husbandman and Creator standing in the midst, as the only One, searches the hearts of all; and taking the purifying fan in His hand, He most wisely separates the threshing-floor of the world, burning the barren, and granting eternal life unto the fruitful.[^1424]

*Another [Canon of the Saint]. Heirmos:*
The Enlightenment of those that lie in darkness, the Salvation of the despairing, O Christ my Savior: unto Thee I rise early, O King of peace; enlighten me with Thy radiance, for beside Thee I know no other God.[^1425]

*Troparion:*
Imitating Thy precious and blessed Passion, she that was united unto Thee in passionlessness suffers most fervently, being severed limb from limb, O Christ the Giver of life, crying out: Beside Thee I know no other God.[^1426]

*Troparion:*
Having conceived the fear of God in Thy womb by Thy mind, Thou didst gloriously bring forth the spirit of saving confession and martyrdom, O valiant-minded one, through steadfast suffering, and didst put to shame the opposing principalities.[^1427]

*Troparion:*
Thou shinest with radiant beams, being illuminated with the light-effusion of the Holy Spirit, and thou dost enlighten the hearts of the faithful, dispersing the darkness of sin, O martyr, passion-bearer of Christ, worthy of all marvel![^1428]

*Theotokion:*

O radiant cloud of the Sun, shine forth a beam upon me, drive away the darkness of my transgressions, stretch out a hand unto me who have fallen into the mire of sin; raise me that am prostrate, O only restoration of fallen Adam.[^1429]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
The voice of the Word, the candlestick of the Light, the morning star, the Forerunner, cries in the wilderness unto all peoples: Repent and be cleansed beforehand; for behold, Christ stands present, delivering the world from corruption.[^1430]

*Troparion:*
Born incorruptibly of God the Father, Christ is incarnate without defilement of the Virgin; Whose latchet of the union of the Word with us, the Forerunner teaches is hard to unloose, delivering the earthborn from deception.[^1431]

*Troparion:*
With final fire Christ baptizes the adversaries who think Him not to be God; but by the Spirit He renews with the water of grace those who acknowledge His Godhead, delivering them from transgressions.[^1432]

*Another [Canon of the Saint]. Heirmos:*
Wallowing in the abyss of sin, I call upon the unfathomable abyss of Thy lovingkindness; from corruption, O God, lead me up.[^1433]

*Troparion:*
When the honorable martyr recognized Thee stretched upon the Tree, she endured hanging and the lacerations of her flesh for the sake of Thy love, O Almighty One.[^1434]

*Troparion:*
The most savage wild beasts were ashamed, beholding thee suffering manfully in the midst of the arena, as of old with Thecla the first woman-martyr, whose zeal thou didst acquire, O ever-memorable one![^1435]

*Troparion:*
The heavenly angels, standing in the midst of the prison, illumined thee with light, taking away thy pains, and glorifying thee as God's lamb.[^1436]

*Theotokion:*
From all generations the Creator chose thee, the beauty of Jacob, which He loved, O all-blameless one; and having shone forth from thee, He appeared.[^1437]

*Kontakion [of the Feast], Tone 4:*
Thou hast appeared today unto the universe, and Thy light, O Lord, is signed upon us, who with understanding sing Thy praise: Thou hast come and hast appeared, the Light Unapproachable.[^1438]

*Ikos:*
Unto Galilee of the Gentiles, unto the country of Zabulon, and unto the land of Nephthalim, as the prophet said, Christ a great Light hath shone forth; unto them that were in darkness a radiant beam hath appeared, shining forth from Bethlehem, or rather from Mary the Lord, the Sun of righteousness, sheds His rays upon the whole universe. Therefore, all ye that are naked from Adam, come, let us clothe ourselves in Him, that we may be warmed; for He covers the naked, and enlightens the darkened; Thou hast come and hast appeared, the Light Unapproachable.[^1439]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The whistling wind of dew and the descent of the angel of God preserved unharmed the pious youths that had communion with the fiery furnace; therefore, bedewed in the flame, they sang with thanksgiving: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers, and praised above all![^1440]

*Troparion:*
As in heaven with trembling and wonder, the angelic hosts stood at the Jordan, beholding so great a condescension of God; how He that holds the expanse of the waters above, stood in the waters clothed in flesh, the God of our fathers.[^1441]

*Troparion:*
The cloud of old and the sea prefigured the marvel of divine baptism, wherein the ancient people of the law were baptized when going forth; and the sea was an image of water, and the cloud of the Spirit; by which being initiated, we cry: Blessed art Thou unto ages, O Lord God![^1442]

*Troparion:*
All we the faithful in Whom we received perfection, theologizing unceasingly with the angels, let us glorify the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit; for behold, the Trinity is consubstantial in hypostases, yet one God, unto Whom we sing: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto ages![^1443]

*Another [Canon of the Saint]. Heirmos:*
The contrary command of the lawless tyrant raised a high flame; but Christ spread spiritual dew upon the pious children, He Who is blessed and supremely glorified.[^1444]

*Troparion:*
Valiantly and invincibly, being cut, thou didst endure the shearing off of thy breasts most patiently; and by heavenly fire, O martyr, thou didst consume them that would not honor God, Whom all creation sings praising.[^1445]

*Troparion:*
Bearing the fire of divine love in thy heart, O blameless one, thou didst trample down the flame; thou wast not terrified of the material fire, imitating the courage and strength of the ancient children.[^1446]

*Troparion:*
The savagery of the wild beasts was subjected unto thee; thou didst pass unharmed through the gaping jaws of lions, when God glorified thee who hadst glorified Him; Whose sufferings thou didst fill up in thy flesh, O all-praised one![^1447]

*Theotokion:*
Having given birth unto Hypostatic Life for us, Who by death manifestly abolished death: put to death the passions of our flesh, for those that honor thee with faith, O pure one, as the Birthgiver of God and all-hymned![^1448]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
The furnace of Babylon showed forth a preeminent mystery, which gushed forth dew, as if with streams it would receive the immaterial fire, and encompass the Creator baptized in the flesh: Whom the peoples bless and supremely exalt unto all ages.[^1449]

*Troparion:*
Put away all fear, the Redeemer said unto the Forerunner: Obey Me as the Good One, approach Me, for this I became by nature; submit to My commands, and baptize Me Who have descended: Whom the peoples bless and supremely exalt unto all ages.[^1450]

*Troparion:*
When the Baptist heard the Master's words, he stretched forth his hand with trembling; yet touching with his hand the head of his Creator, he cried aloud unto Him that was baptized: Sanctify me! For Thou art my God, Whom the peoples bless and supremely exalt unto all ages.[^1451]

*Troparion:*
The manifestation of the Trinity took place in the Jordan; for the supreme divine Nature Itself, the Father, proclaimed: This One being baptized is My beloved Son; and the Spirit came unto His like: Whom the peoples bless and supremely exalt unto all ages.[^1452]

*Another [Canon of the Saint]. Heirmos:*
Him Who descended into the fiery furnace unto the Hebrew children, and changed the flame into dew, praise ye God as Lord, O all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^1453]

*Troparion:*
Adorned with virtues, thou wast embellished with the beauties of martyrdom, and wast betrothed unto the Bridegroom Who is fairer than all sons of men, shining with the beauty of immortality, O Tatiana wise in God![^1454]

*Troparion:*
With the bodiless ministers in prison thou didst sing praise unto the Creator, shining with the glory of divine radiance, and remaining unapproachable unto all who were held by the darkness of deception.[^1455]

*Troparion:*
The breaking of thy limbs crushed the craftiness of the enemies; the shedding of thy blood dried up the bitter torrents of ungodliness, O honorable one, when thou wast revealed unto us as an ocean of miracles![^1456]

*Theotokion:*
Save and have compassion upon us, O thou who beyond word didst bear for us God the compassionate Savior; taking away the burning heat of fiery thoughts and passions by thy prayers, O pure and supremely glorified one.[^1457]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Every tongue is at a loss to praise thee worthily, and even an angelical mind is dazed when singing of thee, O Theotokos; yet being good, accept our faith, for thou knowest our divine love; for thou art the protectress of Christians: thee we magnify.[^1458]

*Troparion:*
Come in the Spirit unto the enlightened: Draw near now, sing unto God in faith, saying: Be ye enlightened! This poor man, Adam in his fall, cried aloud, for the Lord heard him; and coming in the streams of Jordan, He renewed the corrupt.[^1459]

*Troparion:*
Isaiah says: Wash ye, be ye clean; put away wickednesses before the Lord; ye that thirst, go unto the living water; for Christ sprinkles water, renewing those who draw near unto Him in faith, and baptizes with the Spirit unto unaging life.[^1460]

*Troparion:*
We the faithful are preserved by grace and by the seal; for as the Hebrews escaped the destroyer of old because the lintel was sprinkled, so also this divine bath of regeneration shall be an exodus for us; and thence we shall behold the Trinity, the Unwaning Light.[^1461]

*Another [Canon of the Saint]. Heirmos:*
God the Word, of God, Who by ineffable wisdom came to renew Adam, who had bitterly fallen through eating into corruption; Who for our sake was ineffably incarnate of the Holy Virgin: let us the faithful magnify Him with one mind in hymns.[^1462]

*Troparion:*
After many torments, the cruel judge condemned thee unto sword-judgment; at whose departure the heavenly ranks applauded; and Christ with His all-powerful right hand crowned thee, O martyr, who hadst suffered lawfully.[^1463]

*Troparion:*
Pastured with the brightest flocks of martyrs, having most manifestly drawn near unto God, thou seest what the angels see, as a virgin dwelling in the bridal chamber, praying thy honorable Bridegroom that they who honor thee with love may be saved.[^1464]

*Troparion:*
We proclaim thee, O Tatiana, a sealed fountain and an enclosed garden, an honorable and sacred offering, an incorruptible bride of Christ, a slaughter and a sacrifice, a lamb and a noble dove, partaking of the blessed.[^1465]

*Theotokion:*
Thou who art bowed down by the voices of those who pray fervently unto thee, the only refuge of the faithful: save and have mercy, O Theotokos; preserve from harm and from every assault of the nations those who with faith and love ever magnify thee.[^1466]

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "He Hath Visited Us" (Посѣти́лъ ны̀):*
The Savior, Grace and Truth, hath appeared in the streams of the Jordan, and hath enlightened those who slept in darkness and shadow; for the Light Unapproachable hath come and appeared.[^1467]

*Glory... Both now... The same.*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "The Angelic Hosts" (А҆́гг҃лскїа):*

O my Jesus, Being Light, the Radiance from Light, Thou hast enlightened us by Thine ineffable shining; we who of old were blinded in Eden by the serpent, now beholding the Light in the Jordan by Thy light, sing in faith: Blessed art Thou Who hast appeared, our God, glory to Thee![^1468]

*Verse: The sea saw it and fled, * Jordan was driven back.*[^1469]

*Sticheron:*
O initiate and steward of awesome mysteries, forerunner of joy and eyewitness of the Spirit! Ask that the Word Who was baptized by thee, as He was well pleased, ever grant us the remission of transgressions; unto Whom we sing: Blessed art Thou Who hast appeared, our God, glory to Thee![^1470]

*Verse: What ailed thee, O sea, that thou fleddest? * and thou, Jordan, that thou wast driven back?*[^1471]

*Sticheron:*
Let us the faithful lift up our hearts in understanding; let us hasten with diligence unto the streams of Jordan, and behold the Creator baptized in the flesh by John the Forerunner, and theologizing with him let us sing: Blessed art Thou Who hast appeared, our God, glory to Thee![^1472]

*Glory... Both now... The same Tone and Podoben:*
O the divine dispensation beyond the mind! How does the Creator stand before the creature and bow His head unto him? For by an indication He introduces the pattern of humility unto us who are enlightened through Him, unto Whom we sing: Blessed art Thou Who hast appeared, our God, glory to Thee![^1473]

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Feast, Ode 7, on 6.*[^1474]

*In the same Month, on the 13th Day:*
*The Holy Martyrs Hermylus and Stratonicus; and on the same Day is chanted the Service of the Holy Fathers Slain in Sinai and Raithu.*[^1475]

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Martyrs, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Hast Given a Sign" (Дáлъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*
Glorious Hermylus and divine-minded Stratonicus, marvelous pair, confessing the uncreated Trinity, after many wounds and torments conquered polytheistic deception; and crowned with the crown of victory, they pray that peace and great mercy be granted unto the ends of the earth.[^1476]

*Sticheron:*
Having become a minister of the Word, O martyr Hermylus, chosen one of the Divine Spirit, having dyed the garment of the priesthood with the shedding of thy blood, truly thou didst make it most holy and bright; and now thou hast passed into the noetic realms, becoming an earnest intercessor for those that honor thee.[^1477]

*Sticheron:*
Having endured the adze by the command of the raging tyrant, ye were cast into a basket, and both receiving a blessed end and drowning in the waters, by these things ye wisely choked the many-wiled enemy; and now ye dwell most joyfully in the heavens, praying for all, O most valiant passion-bearers![^1478]

*Stichera of the Venerable Fathers, Tone 8, Podoben: "What Shall We Call You, O Saints?" (Что̀ ва́съ нарече́мъ ст҃і́и):*
Greatly did ye contend, O holy ones; ye endured the barbarian onslaught valiantly, fervently surrendering your souls unto the sword; ye were wreathed with martyr crowns, and ye dwell worthily with the angels; great was your patience, and greater are your gifts: pray that our souls may be saved![^1479]

*Sticheron:*
Ye contended, O venerable ones of Christ, having willingly despised the temporal things of life; ye valiantly subdued the wisdom of the flesh, and dying by the sword for Christ, ye dwell worthily with the angels; therefore celebrating your memory, we pray: pray that our souls may be saved![^1480]

*Sticheron:*
Ye lived well, O holy ones, having valiantly assimilated yourselves unto martyr struggles; ye received crowns from heaven; ye despised legitimate swords and the pit, as they trod down these torments, that ye might be clothed together with the crown of suffering: pray that our souls may be saved![^1481]

*Glory, Tone 8, the work of the Studite:*
O venerable fathers, meditating day and night in the law of the Lord, ye were accounted worthy to be partakers of the tree of life, and the fruit of your suffering blossomed into crowns. Having boldness before God the Bestower of the contest, ask for us cleansing and great mercy![^1482]

*Both now, the same Tone:*
O Lord, desiring to fulfill what Thou hadst ordained from of old, Thou didst receive ministers of Thy mystery from all creation: Gabriel from the angels, the Virgin from mankind, the star from the heavens, and the Jordan from the waters, wherein Thou didst abolish the iniquity of the world. O our Savior, glory to Thee![^1483]

*At the Aposticha At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
The radiance of the Father's glory has appeared in the streams of the Jordan, cleansing the defilement of our souls by baptism.

*Verse:* The sea saw it and fled; Jordan was driven back.[^1484]

Receive like a servant, O Prophet John, the Redeemer of the world, and baptize the Creator, unto the renewal of mankind.[^1485]

*Verse:* What ailed thee, O sea, that thou didst flee? And thou, Jordan, that thou wast driven back?[^1486]

Illumination has come, deliverance from delusion, in the streams of the Jordan: let us gather to be cleansed, and to hymn the Lover of mankind.[^1487]

*Glory, Tone 8:*
Having lived an equal-to-the-angels life through ascetic labors, O venerable fathers, having enslaved the body by abstinence, ye subjected it to the spirit, becoming doers of the commandments of the Lord. Ye preserved the archetypal beauty of the image, and accomplished martyr contests after ascetic sweats; and adorned with twofold crowns, earnestly pray to the Savior that we may be saved.[^1488]

*Both now, the same Tone:*
The angelic hosts were awestruck at what was seen this day in the Jordan: when Thou, O Savior, didst stand naked in the waters, and didst bow Thy most pure head to be baptized by John. For when Thou didst willingly become poor, the world was enriched: O Lord, glory to Thee![^1489]

*Troparion of the Martyrs, Tone 4:*
Thy martyrs, O Lord, in their sufferings received incorruptible crowns from Thee, our God. For having Thy might, they cast down the tormentors and crushed the powerless insolence of the demons. By their prayers save our souls.[^1490]

*Glory, of the Fathers, the same Tone:*
O God of our fathers, Who dealest ever with us according to Thy meekness, remove not Thy mercy from us, but by their prayers direct our life in peace.[^1491]

*Both now, of the Feast. Troparion, Tone 1:*
When Thou wast baptized in the Jordan, O Lord, the worship of the Trinity was made manifest; for the voice of the Parent bore witness unto Thee, calling Thee His beloved Son; and the Spirit in the form of a dove confirmed the certainty of the word. O Christ God, Who hast appeared and enlightened the world, glory to Thee![^1492]

*Glory and now, the same.*

*After the 1st Stichologia, Sessional Hymn, Tone 3, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дв҃а дне́сь):*
Having appeared this day, He came to the Jordan to be baptized in the waters by the divine Forerunner; and fulfilling all things, the Father bore witness: "This is My beloved Son, in Whom I am well pleased"; and the Spirit appeared in the marvelous form of a dove upon Him.[^1493]

*Glory and now, the same.*

*After the 2nd Stichologia, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
The Jordan ministers with its streams, and John stretches forth a corruptible hand unto Thee, Who invisibly didst appear in the flesh for baptism. But the one indeed turned back with fear, while the other held Thee, the incorruptible One, with trembling: truly the Lamb of God, the ever-living Fount, having sanctified the founts and seas and men; for the Trinity shone forth: from on high the Parent calls Thee Son, and the Holy Spirit descends.[^1494]

*Glory and now, the same.*

*Canon of the Feast, in 6, Tone 2. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
