Israel traversed the surging storm of the sea, which straightway appeared as dry land; but the black deep completely engulfed the Egyptian captains, a watery grave spread over them by the mighty power of the Beneficent Hand.[^1495]

*Troparion:*
When the light-bearing dawn appeared unto men, coming now from the wilderness unto the waters of the Jordan: O King of the sun, Thou didst bow Thy neck to snatch the ancestor from the dark realm, and to cleanse creation from every defilement.[^1496]

*Troparion:*
O unoriginate Word, when he was buried together with Thee in the streams, Thou dost bring forth renewed him that was corrupted by deception, receiving ineffably this sovereign voice from the Father: "This is My beloved Child, equal to Me by nature."[^1497]

*Another Canon of the Martyrs, whose acrostic is: "I honor the glory of Thy martyrs, O Savior. Joseph." Tone 8.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Let us sing unto the Lord, all ye people, Who submerged Pharaoh in the Red Sea, singing a song of victory, for He is glorified.[^1498]

*Troparion:*
As divinely radiant luminaries and stars, O wise ones, ye appeared on the firmament of the Church, illumining us with divine brightness, O martyrs.[^1499]

*Troparion:*
Ye appeared as noetic coals, kindled with the fire of the Spirit, O glorious ones; and ye quenched the idol hearth with the streams of your blood.[^1500]

*Troparion:*
Drowned in the waters for the sake of Christ, Who submerged our impiety in the waters, ye dried up the rivers of godlessness, O martyrs.[^1501]

*Theotokion:*
Stem the streams of my sins, O all-immaculate Birthgiver of God, having slain death by thy mystery, and grant me compunction.[^1502]

*Another Canon of the Venerable Fathers, whose acrostic is: "To sing the suffering, the great glory of the fathers. Joseph." Tone 4.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Israel of old traversed the deep of the Red Sea with dry feet, and by the cross-shaped hands of Moses conquered the power of Amalek in the wilderness.[^1503]

*Troparion:*
Having become luminous through abstinence, O most blessed ones, ye were visibly revealed as godlike by the shedding of your blood; therefore ye rejoice together with Christ's ascetics and martyrs.[^1504]

*Troparion:*
By a sea of tears ye first drowned the noetic Pharaoh, O wise ones, and afterwards by the streams of your blood ye destroyed him and consigned him unto oblivion.[^1505]

*Troparion:*
The Lord, the Giver of light, enlightened your fasting with endurance, O servants of Christ, making it radiant, and manifestly your suffering shines brighter than the beams of the sun.[^1506]

*Theotokion:*
He Who is the Lord by nature, Whom nothing can contain, is contained within thee, O Lady; having become man in His tender compassion, that in His ineffable love for mankind He might save men.[^1507]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
As many of us as have been loosed from the snares of old, and from the food of lions whose jaw-teeth are crushed, let us rejoice and open wide our mouth, weaving with words a melody of words unto Him Who delights in His gifts bestowed upon us.[^1508]

*Troparion:*
He who of old planted mortality in creation, taking the form of the baneful beast into nature, is darkened by the bodily coming of the Master; having assaulted the Master when the dawn appeared, that his hostile head might be crushed.[^1509]

*Troparion:*
The Master draws unto Himself nature formed by God, buried within the bounds of the tyrant's belly; the renewal of the earthborn is born again, as the Master sovereignly accomplishes the work; for He has come, desiring to cleanse it.[^1510]

*Another [Canon of the Martyrs]. Heirmos:*
Plant Thy fear, O Lord, in the hearts of Thy servants, and be Thou our confirmation, who call upon Thee in truth.[^1511]

*Troparion:*
Having hated the instability of fleeting things, ye longed for the incorruptible delight of things to come, O valiant passion-bearers of Christ the King of all.[^1512]

*Troparion:*
Ye valiantly resisted, O divinely wise ones, him who most lawlessly commanded you to submit to impiety, and ye received crowns of victory from heaven.[^1513]

*Troparion:*
Ye cast down the shrines of deceit, and as guileless martyrs of Christ ye raised yourselves up as venerable temples and pillars of the knowledge of God.[^1514]

*Theotokion:*
The flaming sword which turned every way of old gives way to me, being ashamed of the spear that pierced Him Who was born of thee, O Virgin Mother.[^1515]

*Another [Canon of the Venerable Fathers]. Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Not in wisdom, nor in power, nor in riches do we boast, but in Thee, the hypostatic Wisdom of the Father, O Christ; for there is none holy save Thee, O Lover of mankind.[^1516]

*Troparion:*
Having pleased God with a contrite mind, ye crushed the proud boasting of the enemy, O blessed ones, being crushed and slain with the sword.[^1517]

*Troparion:*
Beholding the everlasting nature of abiding things, O wise ones, ye cast away that which drags downward into instability and corruption; therefore are ye called blessed, O venerable martyrs.[^1518]

*Troparion:*
Having submitted with a well-obedient mind unto the divine law, ye destroyed carnal pleasures through abstinence; and having suffered now, ye attained glory.[^1519]

*Theotokion:*
O ever-virgin, who didst bear the most holy Word, sanctify our souls and bodies, who bless thee, O all-immaculate one.[^1520]

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the Highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*
Ye fled from worldly turmoil, and translated unto a calm haven, crowned with the blood of martyrdom and the labors of asceticism; therefore ye have been shown forth as fellow-dwellers of the martyrs and venerable ones.[^1521]

*Ikos:*
Having mortified your members on earth by life-bearing mortification, ye imaged the Passion of Christ and God: first in good fasting, and secondly again in suffering. Therefore He Himself sent down twofold crowns upon your heads, O fathers, having prepared a heavenly dwelling and an eternal place, where ye now appear rejoicing, fellow-dwellers of the martyrs and venerable ones.[^1522]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thy Tomb" (Гро́бъ тво́й):*
Together in the waters ye received your end, O blessed and wise martyrs, having submerged Belial in them by the grace of our God. Therefore receiving crowns as victors, ye rejoice with the angelic choirs; with them remember us.[^1523]

*Glory, of the Venerable Fathers, Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily Anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*
Appearing as sojourners and pilgrims upon earth, having pitched your tents in the wilderness, ye manifestly fasted, O venerable ones; adorned with the beauty of the garment of virtue, being conformed unto the passions of Christ; therefore ye also endured the barbarian slaughter.[^1524]

*Both now, the same Podoben:*
Thou didst sanctify the Jordan's streams, and didst shatter the dominion of sin, O Christ our God. Thou didst bow Thyself beneath the hands of the Forerunner, and didst save the human race from deception: therefore we pray Thee, save our souls.[^1525]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Purified by the fire of mystical contemplation, the prophet sang the renewal of mankind; he lifted up his voice, clapping by the Spirit, declaring the incarnation of the ineffable Word, by Whom the dominions of the mighty were broken.[^1526]

*Troparion:*
Sent from the Father, O all-radiant Word, to drive away the dark rush of night and to uproot the sins of men: Thou comest to draw forth sons radiant through Thy baptism, O Good One, from the Jordan streams.[^1527]

*Troparion:*
Having foreseen the very Word spoken of, clearly the herald cried unto creation: "This is He Who is before me, second in the flesh, conformed and shone forth by divine power to take away our hostile sin."[^1528]

*Troparion:*
Bearing in Himself life-creating pasture, God the Word snatches away, running against the nests of serpents with many snares; He casts them down, and ensnares him who wounded the whole race of the world; having destroyed him, He delivers creation.[^1529]

*Another [Canon of the Martyrs]. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation, I considered Thy works, and I glorified Thy divinity.[^1530]

*Troparion:*
As a minister of the Word, by thy words thou didst most earnestly expose the irrational folly of the lawless, O martyr Hermylus.[^1531]

*Troparion:*
Having proclaimed one nature of the Godhead, one dominion and lordship, O divinely wise ones, ye despised the polytheistic deception.[^1532]

*Troparion:*
Suspended and scraped, and afflicted with wounds, thou didst remain unyielding, O passion-bearer, divinely wise martyr Hermylus.[^1533]

*Theotokion:*
As the Mother of the Word, O all-pure one, call me to repentance, who am slumbering in despondency and covered over with sin.[^1534]

*Another [Canon of the Venerable Fathers]. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Beholding Thee, the Sun of righteousness, lifted up upon the Cross, the Church stood in her station, worthily crying out: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^1535]

*Troparion:*
Not conquered by bodily passions, ye conquered the enemy; and being put to death by the sword, O blessed ones, ye were translated together, rejoicing, unto life.[^1536]

*Troparion:*
Ye were fattened like lambs through abstinence, and like marked rams ye were slain by the hands of bloodthirsty wolves; and ye were brought unto Christ as perfect sacrifices, O venerable ones.[^1537]

*Troparion:*
Priests, and elders, and youths, who dwelt in Mount Raithu and Sinai, became martyrs, having lived venerably, and died by violence.[^1538]

*Theotokion:*
The pre-eternal Lord, appearing from the Virgin as a new infant and becoming man, remakes mankind. Unto Him let us sing: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^1539]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Washed clean by the purification of the Spirit from the dark and defiled venom of the enemy, we have entered upon a new unerrant path, leading unto inaccessible joy, accessible only to those with whom God is reconciled.[^1540]

*Troparion:*
Seeing him whom He formed from the dust bound in the darkness of transgressions by inescapable chains, the Creator lifted him high upon both shoulders: now in the abundant waters washing away the shame of the ancient wicked disposition of Adam.[^1541]

*Troparion:*
With piety let us earnestly run to the most pure streams of the saving flow, beholding the Word from the incorrupt One, bringing the ladles of divine thirst, sweetly healing the disease of the world.[^1542]

*Another [Canon of the Martyrs]. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Why hast Thou cast me off from Thy face, O unwaning Light, and an alien darkness has covered me, the wretched one? But convert me, and unto the light of Thy commandments direct my paths, I pray.[^1543]

*Troparion:*
The clouds of torments did not obscure your courage, O all-praised martyrs: for it shone brighter than the sun with the radiance of piety, enlightening the pious and encompassing the demonic gloom.[^1544]

*Troparion:*
Having surpassed the limits of humanity, O divinely blessed ones, and being united to the supernatural by perfect ranks, ye endured bitter torments, scrapings, and wounds with firmness of mind.[^1545]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst stoutly resist the judge, O glorious martyr Hermylus; and thou wast accounted worthy, O most blessed one, to hear a voice from heaven calling with love to approach as unto the Bestower of the contest, encouraging this martyr.[^1546]

*Theotokion:*
How good, how fair, how radiant with purity thou art: thou didst incarnate the Word Who is fair in beauty, and didst bear Him Who through the wealth of goodness divinely grants being unto all, O Virgin Mother.[^1547]

*Another [Canon of the Venerable Fathers]. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Thou, my Lord, hast come into the world as light, a holy Light turning from gloomy ignorance those that hymn Thee in faith.[^1548]

*Troparion:*
Paradise of sweetness, having the Lord in your midst as the tree of life, Who accepted your blood as a sacrifice.[^1549]

*Troparion:*
Having mingled the streams of your blood with streams of tears, O God-bearers, ye drowned the multiform serpent in them.[^1550]

*Troparion:*
Ye were accounted worthy to behold the beauty of God, receiving eternal rejoicing instead of labors and sicknesses, O blessed ones.[^1551]

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst give birth to God beyond word and thought; and after giving birth thou didst remain as before birth a virgin, O pure one, joyous in God.[^1552]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
With an all-blessed voice the Father declared Him Whom He brought forth from the womb, the Desired One: "This is He," He says, "this connatural Son, being radiant, sprang forth from the human race: My living Word, and a man through providence."[^1553]

*Troparion:*
The prophet who spent three evenings strangely in the belly of the sea monster of the deep came forth again, prefiguring unto all in the last times the salvation of regeneration from the maneater serpent.[^1554]

*Troparion:*
Above the all-luminous scriptures of the heavens, the disciple beholds the Spirit sent from the Father, abiding upon the most pure Word, having descended like a dove in an ineffable manner; and He is made manifest unto the people who have come unto the Master.[^1555]

*Another [Canon of the Martyrs]. Ode 6. Heirmos:*
I will pour out my prayer unto the Lord, and unto Him will I declare my sorrows; for my soul is full of evils, and my life has drawn nigh unto Hades; and I pray like Jonah: Lead me up from corruption, O God.[^1556]

*Troparion:*
Filled with life-giving waters, ye were cast into the river streams, and receiving your end in them, ye drowned the champion of malice, O all-praised ones; and now ye pour forth streams of healings unto us.[^1557]

*Troparion:*
Cast into a basket, ye fervently surrendered yourselves unto the deep, O passion-bearers, and were taken up unto divine life; having joyfully found that which was hoped for by you from the ages, O great-minded holy martyrs.[^1558]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst appear tormented in burning torment, and beaten with rods, O martyr Stratonicus, an invincible pillar of endurance, exalted by the steps of faith, consuming the resistance of the persecutors by both words and deeds.[^1559]

*Theotokion:*
O Virgin, as thou art merciful and all-holy, heal the passions of my feeble soul, and the sickness of my heart, and the multiform turns of my mind, and calm the fierce surging of my evils, I pray.[^1560]

*Another [Canon of the Venerable Fathers]. Ode 6. Heirmos:*
"I will sacrifice to Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord," the Church cries unto Thee, having been cleansed from the blood of demons by the blood which flowed for mercy's sake from Thy side.[^1561]

*Troparion:*
Having cast off the bonds of attachment through fasting, ye were loosed from the bodily bonds by a most violent death; and ye were bound unto the Creator by indissoluble love.[^1562]

*Troparion:*
Having appeared as high mountains by your way of life, ye brought under your feet by the power of Christ him that threatens those mountains and all creation.[^1563]

*Troparion:*
Watered with streams of tears, O blessed ones, like good and fertile earth, ye bring forth the grain of martyrdom in the eternal garners, preserved for Christ.[^1564]

*Theotokion:*
Calm the waves of the passions of my flesh by thy sleepless prayer, O Virgin, I pray; and grant me not to fall asleep in the heaviest slumber of sin.[^1565]

*Kontakion, Tone 4:*
Thou hast appeared this day unto the inhabited world, and Thy light, O Lord, has been signed upon us, who sing with understanding unto Thee: Thou hast come and appeared, the unapproachable Light.[^1566]

*Ikos:*
Upon Galilee of the Gentiles, upon the land of Zebulun and the territory of Naphtali, as the prophet said, a great light has shone forth, even Christ: a bright beam appeared unto those in darkness, shining out from Bethlehem, yet more from Mary the Lord, the Sun of righteousness, shines rays upon all the inhabited world. Therefore, all ye that are naked from Adam, come, let us clothe ourselves in Him, that we may be warmed; for He covers the naked and enlightens the dark. Thou hast come and appeared, the unapproachable Light.[^1567]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The lofty flame of the furnace, bearing the pious youths, scorched the dragon's heads with a stream; having stilled the unbearable gloom of sin, it washes away all things by the dew of the Spirit.[^1568]

*Troparion:*
Those who prefigured Thee made the Assyrian flame stilled and turned into dew; therefore the water now, like a flame clothing the clay, scorches hidden malice, O Christ, calling them back from the slippery path unto the divine way.[^1569]

*Troparion:*
When the Jordan was divided of old, the Israelite people passed through on dry land; portraying Thee now, the most sovereign One Who insupportably upholdest creation in the waters, unto the incorruptible and profitable path.[^1570]

*Troparion:*
We know that of old the all-ruinous flood mercifully brought all unto destruction through Thee; O Thou Who didst marvelous and strange deeds! And now in Thy tender compassion and for the salvation of man, O Christ, Thou hast drowned sin.[^1571]

*Another [Canon of the Martyrs]. Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The Hebrew youths boldly trod down the flame in the furnace, and changed the fire into dew, crying: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages.[^1572]

*Troparion:*
A honey-flowing word poured forth from thy lips, softening the bitterness of the despondency of thy fellow-sufferer Stratonicus, as he cried out, O Hermylus: O God, blessed art Thou unto the ages.[^1573]

*Troparion:*
Holding the saving Cross as a rod of power, O valiant martyr, thou didst eagerly endure the beating with rods, singing unto thy Creator, O Hermylus: O God, blessed art Thou.[^1574]

*Troparion:*
He Who wonderfully saved the prophet held fast from the belly of the whale saves your victorious relics from the river waters after your end, O passion-bearers.[^1575]

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst dwell in the all-immaculate Virgin, Who abolished the curse of Eve, pouring forth streams of purple dye unto those who cry: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages.[^1576]

*Another [Canon of the Venerable Fathers]. Ode 7. Heirmos:*
In the Persian furnace, Abraham's youths, burned rather by the love of piety than by the flame, cried out: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord.[^1577]

*Troparion:*
Enlightened with the brightness of abstinence and manifestly illuminated by sacred sufferings, O martyrs, ye passed unto the unwaning Light and became sons of the day.[^1578]

*Troparion:*
Voluntarily departing from the sweet things in the world, ye appeared as strangers to men in the flesh, having inherited everlasting, abiding, and incorruptible blessings, O venerable ones.[^1579]

*Troparion:*
Divine Paul, and John, and Diodorus, and Nilus, and together all who died and lived most gloriously: let the ascetics and glorious martyrs be blessed.[^1580]

*Theotokion:*
The jar that received the manna of old truly prefigured thee manifestly, who barest the Manna of life in thy womb: Blessed art thou among women, O all-immaculate Lady.[^1581]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Creation is known to be free, and those previously darkened are known as sons of light; the prince of darkness alone groans. Now let the formerly wretched inheritance of the nations fervently bless the Cause.[^1582]

*Troparion:*
The three godlike youths, bedewed in the fire and illuminated with three all-luminous sanctities, manifestly revealed the supreme Nature, united with humanity, burning away with dew every ruinous deception mercifully.[^1583]

*Troparion:*
Let all earthly nature be made white, being led up now from the fall unto heaven; for by the Word, by Whom all things are upheld, having washed in the flowing streams, it has escaped former transgressions, washed most brilliantly.[^1584]

*Another [Canon of the Martyrs]. Ode 8. Heirmos:*
The Chaldean tyrant furiously kindled the furnace sevenfold for the pious; but seeing them saved by a greater power, he cried unto the Creator and Redeemer: Ye children, bless; ye priests, sing praises; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^1585]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst endure being beaten, and cruelly scraped, afflicted with floods of sicknesses, O glorious Hermylus, and thou wast a guide unto Stratonicus for the contests of piety; with him thou didst cry: Ye priests, bless; ye people, supremely exalt the Lord unto the ages.[^1586]

*Troparion:*
Unbending in mind, valiant in suffering, and worthy of heavenly gifts: when commanded, they did not render honor unto stones, but cried unto God the Master of all: Ye people, supremely exalt Him unto the ages.[^1587]

*Troparion:*
When the tormentor scraped thy sides with claws and mercilessly cut thee with swords, he did not steal away thy mind strengthened by divine love and looking unto the beauty of the Redeemer; standing before Whom now with boldness thou criest: Ye people, supremely exalt the Lord unto the ages.[^1588]

*Theotokion:*
He Who is in every way perfect and unapproachable by nature appeared approachable unto me, clothed in flesh from thee who knewest not wedlock; earnestly pray Him to scatter the burden of my lawlessness and to save those who sing: Ye priests, bless; ye people, supremely exalt the Lord unto the ages.[^1589]

*Another [Canon of the Venerable Fathers]. Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Stretching forth his hands, Daniel shut the lions' mouths in the pit; and the youths, lovers of piety, girded with virtue, quenched the power of the fire, crying out: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord.[^1590]

*Troparion:*
Adorned with ascetic valor, the most majestic choir of the venerable ones this day reveals all the divine fellow-partakers, unto those who praise it, singing unto Christ: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord.[^1591]

*Troparion:*
Ye were slaughtered like lambs, cut down by barbarian swords; and ye were brought as perfect sacrifices unto the Word Who was slain, and ye took up your abode in the tabernacles of the firstborn, singing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord.[^1592]

*Troparion:*
By the craft of every pleasure, O venerable fathers, ye stripped the most wicked enemy who had stripped our forebears; and having received a holy garment as sufferers, ye wisely clothed him in shame.[^1593]

*Theotokion:*
For thy sake ancient Paradise is opened again, and the man formerly condemned is led into it; and he is most truly deified, O pure one full of God's grace, for the renewal of men, who cry: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord.[^1594]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
The wonders of thy childbirth surpass understanding, O all-pure Bride, blessed Mother, through whom having obtained all-perfect salvation, we worthily praise Him as Benefactor, bearing a gift, a hymn of thanksgiving.[^1595]

*Troparion:*
We have known the things revealed unto Moses by the bush; come, let us establish with strange statutes: for the Virgin was preserved, bearing the fire, having given birth to the light-bearing Benefactor, and He is manifested in the streams of the Jordan.[^1596]

*Troparion:*
Completing human nature, O King without beginning, by communion of the Spirit, having washed it with pure streams from darkness, Thou hast put to shame exalted strength, to reward it now in unending life.[^1597]

*Another [Canon of the Martyrs]. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Every hearing was terrified at the ineffable condescension of God: how the Most High willingly descended even unto flesh, from the virginal womb becoming man. Therefore, O faithful, we magnify the most pure Birthgiver of God.[^1598]

*Troparion:*
Having crossed the gulf of torments by the arrow of suffering, O martyrs of Christ, ye hastened unto the havens of rest, where are the ranks of martyrs and the assemblies of the righteous, where is the unwaning light, and the joy of those who feast in deed.[^1599]

*Troparion:*
Celebrating this day the sacred memory of your suffering, O all-blessed ones, the Church of Christ keeps a joyful and radiant feast, magnifying God, the Bestower of your crowns,[^1600] Who magnifies you as His pleasing servants.[^1601]

*Troparion:*
Ye were taken up unto the all-radiant height of witness, O truly holy ones, and ye received the fulfillment of desire, O truly blessed ones, having received the immovable Kingdom of God, O martyr Stratonicus, with wise and divinely minded Hermylus.[^1602]

*Theotokion:*
Spare me, O Savior Who wast born, and Who didst preserve incorrupt after childbirth her that bare Thee, when Thou shalt sit to judge my deeds; overlook my iniquities and my sins, as Thou art sinless, as God merciful and the Lover of mankind.[^1603]

*Another [Canon of the Venerable Fathers]. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
A cornerstone was cut out without hands from thee, the unhewn mountain, O Virgin, even Christ, Who joined together the parted natures. Therefore, rejoicing, we magnify thee, O Birthgiver of God.[^1604]

*Troparion:*
Come, let us praise with sacred hymns the venerable ones, let us with loud voice magnify the holy fathers who lived in holiness in Raithu and Sinai, and who suffered piously.[^1605]

*Troparion:*
Ye sanctified both body and soul unto the Lord, O venerable ones, having washed yourselves with the sweats of abstinence, and dried up the sea of barbarian malice with the streams of your blood.[^1606]

*Troparion:*
Your divinely radiant memory, illuminated by divine streams, for the sake of your sufferings for Christ, enlightens the thoughts of all, O blessed ones, by the grace of the Benefactor and of the Divine Spirit.[^1607]

*Theotokion:*
The Cherubim tremble beholding the Word, Who sits upon them by an ineffable word, held as an infant by thy maternal hands, O all-holy Lady, higher than all creation.[^1608]

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "In the spirit in the sanctuary" (Dukhom vo sviatilishchi):*
By the sufferings of fasting ye put to sleep utterly the evil-originating serpent, and at your end ye received the crown of martyrdom: O boast of fathers and glory of martyrs, the all-sacred multitude of marvelous fathers in Raithu and Sinai.[^1609]

*Glory, and now, of the Feast:*
The present day has become of the unwaning Light; for Christ the Truth has now come and appeared: let us worthily sing unto Him with psalms and hymns, as Creator and God. O new mystery! The Creator of Adam has willingly appeared as man.[^1610]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 6, Podoben: "On the third day" (Tridneven):*
Come, ye faithful, let us also run in feeling of heart unto the streams of the Jordan, and beholding Christ baptized in the flesh by John the Forerunner, now glorifying with him let us cry unto Him: Blessed art Thou Who hast appeared,[^1611] O our God, glory to Thee.[^1612]

*Verse: The sea saw it and fled; the Jordan was turned back.*[^1613]

The rod of Jesse has now budded, the divine ark, and the receptacle of the manna, from whom came forth the incorrupt Flower of life, Whom the Jordan feared, and John touching Christ with his hand cried out: Blessed art Thou in Thy manifestation, O our God, glory to Thee.[^1614]

*Verse: What ailed thee, O sea, that thou didst flee? And thou, Jordan, that thou wast turned back?*[^1615]

Sing hymns, ye heavenly hosts; sing, ye men, and rejoice in unison: for behold, the Master, the Father's radiance, comes unto the streams of the Jordan to be baptized by the servant; ye peoples, let us cry out: Blessed art Thou in Thy manifestation, O our God, glory to Thee.[^1616]

*Glory, Tone 8:*
Blessed are ye, O venerable ones and martyrs of Christ God: venerable indeed, because ye were driven out for righteousness' sake; and martyrs, because the sword did not separate you from the love of Christ; and therefore rejoice, for great is your reward in the heavens.[^1617]

*Both now, Tone 8:*
This day creation is enlightened; this day all things rejoice, heavenly and earthly together; angels and men mingle. For where the King's arrival is, there order also comes. Let us therefore hasten to the Jordan, and let us all behold John, how he baptizes the uncreated and sinless crown. Therefore, singing the apostolic voice, let us cry out in unison: The saving grace of God has appeared unto all men, enlightening and granting great mercy unto the faithful.[^1618]

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Feast, Ode 8, on 4; and of the Fathers, Ode 6, on 4.*
*Prokeimenon, Tone 7: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones.*[^1619]
*Verse: What shall I render unto the Lord for all that He has rendered unto me?*
*Epistle to the Romans, Pericope 94 [Rom. 8:28-39].*[^1620]
*Alleluia, Tone 4: The righteous cried, and the Lord heard them.*
*Gospel according to Luke, Pericope 24 [Luke 6:17-23].*
*Communion Hymn: Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous.*[^1621]

*In the same month, on the 14th day:*
*Of our venerable fathers slain in Sinai and Raithu.*[^1622]
*We sing the entire service of the venerable ones on the 13th day.*[^1623]
*For on this day is the Apodosis of the Feast of Illumination, and the service of the Feast is sung.*[^1624]
*At Vespers, the customary Kathisma. At "Lord, I have cried," the Stichera on 6, sung as on the Feast itself. Glory, and now: "Thou hast bowed Thy head to the Forerunner." Prokeimenon of the day. There is no Entrance. We do not read the Old Testament Readings. Then, "Vouchsafe, O Lord," and the litany: "Let us complete our evening prayer." At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Feast with their verses. Glory, and now, of the Feast. After "Now lettest Thou depart," and after the Trisagion, the Troparion of the Feast. Then the litany: "Have mercy on us, O God," and the Dismissal. And we commemorate the saint of the day at the Dismissal.*[^1625]
*In the morning, we sing the Midnight Office according to custom with the Kathisma, and we say the troparia of the day. And we say the prayer: "Remember, O Lord, in hope of resurrection." And the Dismissal.*[^1626]
*At Matins, at "God is the Lord," the Troparion of the Feast thrice. After the Kathismata, the Sessional Hymns of the Feast, and the reading of the Feast. The first Canon with the heirmos on 8; the other Canon with the heirmos on 6. We sing the heirmoi of both canons twice. Katavasia: the heirmos of the first canon, sung together. After Ode 3, the Hypakoe, Tone 5: "When by Thy manifestation." After Ode 6, the Kontakion of the Feast, and the Ikos. At Ode 9 we do not sing "More honorable," but we sing the Refrains of the Feast, as on the Feast itself. The Exapostilarion of the Feast once; Glory, and now, the same. At the Praises, Stichera of the Feast on 4. Glory, Tone 6: "With the waters of the Jordan;" Both now, Tone 2: "This day Christ comes to the Jordan." And the Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, the Troparion of the Feast. Litanies, and the Dismissal. And the customary procession into the narthex. And the First Hour. Troparion and Kontakion of the Feast.*[^1627]
*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes from both canons, Ode 4 on 8. We do not say the Antiphons of the Feast. After the Entrance, Troparion of the Feast; Glory, and now, Kontakion of the Feast. Then the Trisagion. Prokeimenon, Alleluia, and Communion Hymn of the Feast. Epistle and Gospel of the day.*[^1628]

*It should be known: If the Apodosis of the Theophany occurs on a Sunday before the Publican and the Pharisee.*[^1629]
*On Saturday at Small Vespers, at "Lord, I have cried," the Sunday Stichera; Glory, and now, of the Feast. At the Aposticha, one Sunday Sticheron; and the Aposticha of the Feast with its verses, from Great Vespers. Glory, and now, of the Feast: "This day Christ," written at the Praises.*[^1630]
*At Great Vespers, after the customary Stichology. At "Lord, I have cried," Sunday Stichera, 3, and of Anatolius, one; and of the Feast 6, sung as on the Feast itself. Glory of the Feast; both now, the first Theotokion of the Tone. At the Litiya, Stichera; Glory, and now, of the Feast. At the Aposticha, Sunday Stichera; Glory, and now, of the Feast. At the Blessing of Loaves, the Troparion "Birthgiver of God and Virgin" twice, and of the Feast once; and a reading from the Apostolic Epistles. But if there is no All-Night Vigil: After "Now lettest Thou depart," the Sunday Troparion; Glory, and now, of the Feast.*[^1631]
*At Compline, after "It is truly meet," after "Our Father," the Kontakion of the Feast.*[^1632]
*At Matins, at "God is the Lord," the Sunday Troparion twice; Glory, and now, of the Feast. After the Kathismata, the Sunday Sessional Hymns with their Theotokia; and a reading. Then the Blameless (Polyeleos) with the Troparia: "The angelic assembly." The Hypakoe of the Tone. The Hymns of Ascent. Prokeimenon. "Let every breath." The Sunday Gospel. And the rest of the Sunday service up to the Canon. The Sunday Canon with the heirmos on 4; and to the Birthgiver of God on 2; and both Canons of the Feast on 8. Katavasia of the Feast. After Ode 3, the Kontakion of the Feast, and the Ikos, and the Hypakoe of the Feast; and a reading of the Feast. After Ode 6, the Sunday Kontakion and Ikos; and we read the Prologue. At Ode 9 we sing "More honorable." The Sunday Exapostilarion; Glory, and now, of the Feast. At the Praises, Sunday Stichera, 4; and of the Feast 4, with the Doxasticon, with their refrains. Glory, the Gospel Sticheron; both now, "Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Birthgiver of God." The Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, the Sunday Troparion only. Litanies, and the Dismissal, and the Catechesis, and the customary procession into the narthex. And the First Hour. And the final Dismissal.*[^1633]
*At the Hours, the Sunday Troparion; Glory, of the Feast; both now, the Theotokion of the Hours. After "Our Father," the Kontakion of the Feast and of the Sunday, said alternating.*[^1634]
*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Tone on 6; and of the Feast, Ode 4 of both canons on 4. After the Entrance, the Sunday Troparion, and of the Feast. Glory, the Sunday Kontakion; both now, of the Feast. Prokeimenon, Epistle, and Gospel of the Sunday in course.*[^1635]

Alleluia and Communion Hymn of the Feast, and of the day.[^1636]
*We observe also this instruction: If the Sunday of the Publican and the Pharisee falls on the 14th or on the 15th, on the Apodosis of the Theophany. We sing the Sunday service, and of the Triodion, and of the Feast.*[^1637]
*On Saturday evening at Small Vespers, the Sunday Stichera on 4; Glory, and now, the first Theotokion of the Tone, of Small Vespers. At the Aposticha, one Sunday Sticheron; and the Aposticha of the Feast from Great Vespers with its verses. Glory, and now, of the Feast: "This day Christ," written at the Praises. After the Trisagion, the Sunday Troparion; Glory, and now, of the Feast. Little litany, and the Dismissal.*[^1638]
*At Great Vespers: "Blessed is the man," the entire Kathisma. At "Lord, I have cried," the Sunday Stichera of the Tone, 3; and of the Triodion 3, with the Doxasticon; and of the Feast 4, sung as on the Feast itself. Glory of the Feast; both now, the first Theotokion of the Tone. Entrance, Prokeimenon of the day. At the Litiya, Stichera of the Feast; and the Idiomela of the Triodion: "The all-wicked voice of the Pharisee." Glory: "Of the Publican and the Pharisee;" both now, of the Feast. At the Aposticha, Sunday Stichera; Glory, of the Triodion; both now, of the Feast. At the Blessing of Loaves: Troparion "Birthgiver of God and Virgin" twice; and of the Feast once; and a reading. But if there is no All-Night Vigil: After "Now lettest Thou depart," the Sunday Troparion; Glory, and now, of the Feast. At Compline, after "It is truly meet," after "Our Father," the Kontakion of the Feast; Glory, and now, of the Triodion.*[^1639]
*At Matins, at "God is the Lord," the Sunday Troparion twice; Glory, and now, of the Feast. After the Kathismata, the Sunday Sessional Hymns with their Theotokia; and a reading in the Commentary Gospel. And the Blameless (Polyeleos); the Hypakoe of the Tone, and a reading. The Hymns of Ascent, and the Prokeimenon of the Tone, and the Sunday Gospel. "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ;" Psalm 50; Glory: "The doors of repentance;" both now: "Guide me on the paths of salvation;" then "Have mercy on me, O God," and "When I ponder the multitude of my evil deeds." The Sunday Canon with the heirmos on 4; and of the Triodion on 4; and both Canons of the Feast on 6. Katavasia of the Feast. After Ode 3, the Kontakion, and Ikos, and Sessional Hymn of the Triodion; Glory, and now, of the Feast. After Ode 6, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Feast. At Ode 9 we sing "More honorable." The Sunday Exapostilarion; Glory, of the Triodion; both now, of the Feast. At the Praises, the Sunday Stichera, 4; and of the Feast with the Doxasticon, 4, with their refrains. Glory, the Idiomelon of the Triodion; both now: "Most blessed art thou, O Virgin Birthgiver of God." The Great Doxology. After the Trisagion, the Sunday Troparion only. Litanies, and the Dismissal, and the procession into the narthex. Glory, and now, the Gospel Sticheron.*[^1640]

the First Hour, and the complete Dismissal. At the First Hour, the Sunday Troparion; Glory, of the Feast; both now, the Theotokion of the Hours. After the Trisagion, the Kontakion of the Triodion. Likewise at the Third, Sixth, and Ninth Hours we say the troparia: but we say the Kontakia of the Feast and of the Triodion alternating. At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Tone on 4; and of the Triodion, Ode 3 on 4; and of the Feast, Ode 4 on 4. After the Entrance, the Sunday Troparion, and of the Feast; Glory, the Kontakion of the Triodion; both now, of the Feast. Prokeimenon of the Tone, and of the Feast. Epistle and Gospel of the day. Communion Hymn: "Praise the Lord from the heavens;" Another, of the Feast.[^1641]

*In the same month, on the 15th day:*
*Of our venerable fathers Paul of Thebes and John the Calybite.*[^1642]
*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 6, Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly hosts" (Nebesnykh chinov):*
Thou didst appear as the beginning of the virtuous, having established, O thrice-blessed Paul, the impassable paths of ascetic life: for thou didst well set spiritual ascents in thy soul, whereby thou didst attain the summit of virtues through abstinence and many afflictions.[^1643]

Having winged thy mind unto divine desire, O blessed one, thou didst ascend unto the heights of the desert, and didst draw nigh as unto the darkness; wherein thou wast illuminated brightly with the divine understanding, and on the tablets of thy soul thou wast anointed with the brightness of virtues.[^1644]

The desert blossomed fair with the flowers of thy virtues, for Thou didst destroy the thorns of passions therein: Thou didst plant the glorious labors of thy divine deeds. Therefore, like a lily from God, Thou dost now breathe forth unto us the fragrance of thy life.[^1645]

*Other Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Egda ot dreva):*
When by the divine nod thou didst rejoicing flee worldly beauties, O father, then didst thou prefer the narrow, painful, and exceedingly hard path rather than the broad way. Therefore thou didst take care for the soul,[^1646] having clothed thyself in the divine habit, by fleeing and by nakedness from all pleasures, O divinely blessed one.[^1647]

Thou didst understand the strange life and strange undertaking, wounded with the love of Christ, Whose ineffable poverty thou didst love: and before the gates of thy parents thou didst endure homeless, O father, straitened and afflicted. Therefore thou wast filled with gifts, and didst inherit the unshakeable wealth which is in the heavens.[^1648]

Bearing in thy hands the holy Gospel, O father, thou wast the fulfiller thereof. Having renounced the possessions of thy parents, O John, with tears and hardship thou didst accomplish all thy life, O venerable one. Therefore thou dost now enjoy divine consolation and unending rejoicing, O all-blessed one.[^1649]

*Glory, Tone 2:*
Having renounced the world and the things in the world, O venerable one, taking the Gospel, in evangelical manner thou didst follow Christ; and living in a hut secretly as in Paradise, by the ultimate harsh living of the flesh thou didst choke the manslaying serpent. Therefore thou hast taken up thy dwelling in the heavens, O blessed John; pray that peace be granted unto the world, and great mercy unto our souls.[^1650]

*Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Egda ot dreva):*
When the undefiled Ewe beheld her Lamb willingly dragged to slaughter as a man, weeping she said: Dost Thou now hasten to make me childless, O Christ, who bare Thee? What is this that Thou hast done, O Redeemer of all? Yet I hymn and glorify Thine extreme goodness, surpassing mind and word, O Lover of mankind.[^1651]

*At the Aposticha, from the Octoechos:*
*Glory, Tone 6:*
O venerable father, into all the earth has gone forth the sound of thy correct deeds; therefore in the heavens thou hast found the reward of thy labors. Thou didst destroy the hosts of demons and didst attain unto the ranks of angels, whose life thou didst blamelessly emulate. Having boldness before Christ God, entreat peace for our souls.[^1652]

*Both now, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "On the third day" (Tridneven):*
Beholding Thee crucified, O Christ, she that bare Thee cried out: What strange mystery is this which I behold, O my Son? How dost Thou die in the flesh, suspended upon the Tree, O Bestower of life?[^1653]

*Troparion, Tone 4:*

O God of our fathers, Who dealest ever with us according to Thy meekness, take not Thy mercy away from us, but through their intercessions guide our life in peace.[^1654]

*At Matins, one Canon from the Octoechos, and of the Saints two canons on 8.*
*Canon of Saint Paul.*
*A composition of John the Monk.*
*Tone 8.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Let us sing unto the Lord, Who led His people through the Red Sea, for He alone has been gloriously glorified.[^1655]

*Troparion:*
Having come together, ye faithful, let us worthily honor in hymns the God-bearing Paul, as the adornment of monastics.[^1656]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast the first inhabitant of the desert, O glorious Paul, and through fasting thou didst appear as an inheritor of the heavenly Kingdom.[^1657]

*Troparion:*
Having cleansed thyself wholly through abstinence, O all-blessed one, thou didst appear as a dwelling-place of God and fellow-citizen of angels.[^1658]

*Theotokion:*
O all-pure Birthgiver of God, who beyond nature gavest birth in the flesh to the pre-eternal and transcendent Word, we hymn thee.[^1659]

*Another Canon of John, the acrostic whereof is:*
*Show me poor in passions by thy prayers, O blessed one.*
*Joseph. Tone 2.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
In the deep of old, the all-armed power overwhelmed the whole host of Pharaoh; and the incarnate Word destroyed all-wicked sin, the most glorified Lord: for He has been gloriously glorified.[^1660]

*Troparion:*
Being enriched with divine virtues, thou didst despise earthly wealth and didst obtain heavenly wealth. Therefore enrich me, who have become impoverished, with the grace of divine understanding, that I may hymn thy life equal to the angels, O father.[^1661]

*Troparion:*
Having taken up the good yoke of the Lord from youth, O blessed one, by ascetic struggles thou didst bring low the enemy, arming thyself with the humility of Christ; whereby thou wast exalted to the height, O John, unto heaven.[^1662]

*Troparion:*
Having journeyed by the narrow way, with sorrows and tears, with groans and affliction, O venerable one, thou didst attain unto the most spacious breadth, having found a dwelling worthy of thy sufferings, O father John worthy of wonder.[^1663]

*Theotokion:*
Tossed by the tempest of fierce assaults of passions, O Maiden, and bowed down by the snares of sin, unto thine unashamed and invincible protection, O all-hymned one, with love I flee,[^1664] have compassion on me and save me, O Ever-Virgin.[^1665]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
O Lord Who didst establish the heavens by Thy Word, and didst found the earth upon many waters, strengthen me to sing the praise of Thy glory.[^1666]

*Troparion:*
Looking unto God with the eye of thy soul, O father, thou didst love Him, having hated earthly things and completed an angelic life.[^1667]

*Troparion:*
By the beams of thy virtues, O father, thou didst drive away the evil gloom of passions, having received the illumination of the Spirit in thy heart.[^1668]

*Troparion:*
Nourished with heavenly bread, as Elijah of old with food by a raven, thou didst flee the mental Jezebel, O father, unto the protection of Christ.[^1669]

*Theotokion:*
The King of glory and Creator, having dyed His purple robe from thy pure blood, O Mother of God, mystically colored it.[^1670]

*Another [Canon of Saint John]. Ode 3. Heirmos:*
The desert blossomed like a lily, O Lord, the barren church of the nations at Thy coming, wherein my heart has been established.[^1671]

*Troparion:*
As a sweet-smelling censer, O venerable one, thou didst bring thy struggles unto Christ: having smelled and received them, He numbered thee among the ascetic choirs.[^1672]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst appear as a most great wonder, O venerable one, striking awe into the hearts of the pious: how before the gates of thy parents thou didst endure, living in poverty and afflicted.[^1673]

*Troparion:*
Having lawfully endured in prayers and fastings, O venerable one, thou didst clothe thyself in dispassion, having humbled the carnal mind by the power of the Holy Spirit.[^1674]

*Theotokion:*
As a fragrant rose from the valleys, O all-pure one, He found thee pure, and dwelt in the midst of thee, filling humanity with fragrance.[^1675]

*Kontakion of Paul, Tone 8, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Deva dnes):*
As an unwaning luminary of the spiritual Sun, let us come together this day and praise thee in hymns: for thou didst shine forth upon those in the darkness of ignorance, leading all up unto the divine height, O adornment of Thebes, venerable Paul, steadfast foundation of fathers and ascetics.[^1676]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 1, Podoben: "Thy Tomb, O Savior" (Grob Tvoy Spase):*
Having hated the fair things of the world from the heart, and having loved the one God from the soul, thou didst attain the desert as an inhabited city, O Paul, exercising thyself in divine visions alone,[^1677] thou didst appear as an angel living with the flesh: therefore we honor thee.[^1678]

*Glory... Another Sessional Hymn of John, Tone 3, Podoben: "Beholding the Beauty of Thy Virginity" (Krasote devstva):*
Having forsaken corruptible wealth and fleeting glory, thou didst receive heavenly riches and truly everlasting glory, O blessed father. Therefore we bless thy holy falling asleep, and celebrating therein, we cry unto thee: Remember us before the Lord, O John, as having boldness.[^1679]

*Both now... Theotokion:*
As an uncultivated vine, O Virgin, thou didst bud forth the most fair cluster, gushing forth for us saving wine that gladdens the souls and bodies of all. Therefore, ever blessing thee as the cause of good things, with the angel we cry unto thee: Rejoice, full of grace![^1680]

*Stavrotheotokion:*
Thy pure Mother who knew not wedlock, O Christ, seeing Thee hanging dead upon the Cross, maternally weeping said: What has the lawless and ungrateful Jewish assembly repaid Thee, having enjoyed Thy many and great gifts, O my Son? I hymn Thy divine condescension.[^1681]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Mystically foreseeing Thee, O Word, incarnate of the Virgin, the Prophet cried in song: Glory to Thy power, O Lord.[^1682]

*Troparion:*
Planted in the house of God, thou didst sprout the good fruit of virtues, and didst wither the carnal uprisings by thine ascetic struggle.[^1683]

*Troparion:*
By the fire of God's love thou didst burn up the thorns of passions, and didst reveal thyself, O father, as a dwelling-place of the Spirit.[^1684]

*Troparion:*
By the rod of thy virtuous life, as wild beasts thou didst drive away the passions. Therefore, even after death, the wild beasts gathered for thy burial.[^1685]

*Theotokion:*
A mystical purple robe was woven from thy pure blood for the God of all, wherewith being clothed, O Birthgiver of God, He united us unto God and the Father.[^1686]

*Another [Canon of Saint John]. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Thou didst come from the Virgin, not an intercessor nor an angel, but Thyself, O Lord, having become incarnate, and hast saved me, the whole man. Therefore I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lord.[^1687]

*Troparion:*
In poor rags thou wast revealed as a hidden treasure, O God-inspired father; for thou didst love the divine garment, and being clothed, thou didst enter into the bridal chamber on high.[^1688]

*Troparion:*
Having received the heavenly seed with the furrows of thy heart, O God-inspired one,[^1689] thou didst cultivate a fair ear of corn, nourishing the minds of those who honor thy memory in a venerable manner.[^1690]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst endure in a most narrow cell, O marvelous one, becoming poor in sickness like another Lazarus. Therefore thou hast now found rest in the bosom of Abraham, O venerable father.[^1691]

*Theotokion:*
Direct the movements of my soul, O all-immaculate one, toward the divine commandments of Him Who shone forth from thy womb, delivering me from the tempest of worldly stumbling blocks by thine intercession.[^1692]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Rising early at dawn, we cry unto Thee: O Lord, save us, for Thou art our God, besides Thee we know none other.[^1693]

*Troparion:*
Having lived in hymnody and fastings, in prayers and vigils, O venerable one, thou didst make thy dwelling with God.[^1694]

*Troparion:*
Thy most venerable life was directed unto the Lord, O all-blessed Paul, and thy burial was most glorious.[^1695]

*Troparion:*
Having completed the course of fasting, O venerable one, thou wast a converser with the powers on high, O father.[^1696]

*Theotokion:*
We hymn thee as Virgin after childbirth, O Birthgiver of God, for thou didst bear God the Word in the flesh unto the world.[^1697]

*Another [Canon of Saint John]. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
O Enlightenment of those lying in darkness, Salvation of the despairing, O Christ my Savior: early at dawn I rise unto Thee, O King of peace; enlighten me with Thy radiance, for besides Thee I know no other God.[^1698]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast a stranger to earthly pleasures, a stranger to thine own, a stranger to thy parents by choice; and having cleansed thyself by abstinence, thou didst unite thyself unto the Almighty, O father John, having become poor in spirit.[^1699]

*Troparion:*
Having made thyself a temple of the Holy Trinity, thou didst endure in the narrowness of the cell, cleansing thy soul with divine meditations, and ever gazing upon the ineffable beauty of God, O father John.[^1700]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst appear as a fulfiller of the law of God, having preferred nothing above His love, O God-wise father. For neither the love of brethren nor of parents, nor wealth nor dignity, nor the pleasure of the flesh enfeebled thee.[^1701]

*Theotokion:*
Having incorruptibly given birth to Emmanuel, the Master of all, thou didst remain a virgin even after childbirth, O Virgin Mother. Him do thou unceasingly beseech to deliver from the temptations of the enemy those who flee under thy protection.[^1702]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Grant me a radiant robe, Thou Who deckest Thyself with light[^1703] as with a garment, O greatly merciful Christ our God.[^1704]

*Troparion:*
Having stretched out thy hands unto God, thou didst offer thy soul unto Him, O venerable one, well-pleasing Him day and night.[^1705]

*Troparion:*
The hosts of angels, the ranks of prophets, and the holy apostles glorified thy falling asleep, O venerable father.[^1706]

*Troparion:*
Having fled the tempest of passions by the sail of extreme fasting, O venerable one, thou didst hasten into the stormless haven of Christ.[^1707]

*Theotokion:*
O only one who by the word didst bear the Word in the flesh, deliver our souls from the snares of the enemy, we pray.[^1708]

*Another [Canon of Saint John]. Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Wallowing in the abyss of sins, I call upon the unfathomable abyss of Thy tender mercy: lead me up from corruption, O God.[^1709]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst cast down the proud serpent with the weapons of humility of mind, O all-blessed one, and being exalted in spirit, thou didst take up residence in the ever-living mansions.[^1710]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast filled with the gifts of the Spirit, and didst subdue the spirits of malice, as sensible and all-wise, and wholly dedicated unto God.[^1711]

*Troparion:*
Shining with the heights of dispassion, O father John, constrained in a hut and beset with temptations, thou didst endure, being divinely strengthened.[^1712]

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst incarnate from thy womb, O pure one, the Word Who is co-equal in power and co-enthroned with the One Who begat Him, Who through ineffable compassion bore all our nature.[^1713]

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the Highest" (Vyshnikh ishcha):*
Having loved unstealable poverty, O all-wise one, thou didst hate the wealth of thy parents; and holding the Gospel in thy hands, thou didst follow Christ God, O John, unceasingly praying for us all.[^1714]

*Ikos:*
Who is able to hymn thy labors and sicknesses, and manifold deeds, and glory and greatness? But by thy prayers well-pleasing unto God, grant me now the grace of the Spirit, that I may faithfully recount thy struggles beyond nature, and sing of thine endurance beyond words and the patience of thy conscience, O all-blessed one, whereby thou didst put to shame the deceitful enemy, unceasingly praying for us all.[^1715]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
Thou Who in the beginning didst establish the earth, and by the Word didst confirm the heavens: blessed art Thou unto the ages, O Lord God of our fathers.[^1716]

*Troparion:*
Having subjected the carnal mind to the Spirit, the venerable one cried: Blessed art Thou unto the ages, O Lord God of our fathers.[^1717]

*Troparion:*
Delivered from the snares of the enemy, the venerable one cried in joy: Blessed art Thou unto the ages, O Lord God of our fathers.[^1718]

*Troparion:*
Having burned away the entire flame of passions ascetically, the venerable one cried: Blessed art Thou unto the ages, O Lord God of our fathers.[^1719]

*Theotokion:*
He Who fashioned the Virgin, and shone forth from her like the sun: Blessed art Thou unto the ages, O Lord God of our fathers.[^1720]

*Another [Canon of Saint John]. Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The God-opposing command of the lawless tyrant raised a high flame; but Christ spread a spiritual dew upon the pious youths: He Who is blessed and supremely glorified.[^1721]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst prefer the narrow rather than the broad way, O highly renowned one, and rejoicing thou didst endure before the gates of thy parents, reviled and afflicted with many sicknesses, O divinely-blessed one.[^1722]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst adorn thyself with most fair ascents, O wise one, having put to death the carnal mind. Therefore thou didst dwell in the heavens, being ever numbered among the choir of venerable fathers, O worthy of wonder.[^1723]

*Troparion:*
The left-hand paths that lead away from divine rest thou didst avoid by the snare-settings of demons, O blessed one, being covered by divine grace, crying: Blessed and supremely glorified art Thou![^1724]

*Theotokion:*
We sing of thy childbirth, O blessed one, whereby we were delivered from the ancient condemnation; and we bless thee, O divinely-blessed one, the only one whom He loved Who is blessed and supremely glorified.[^1725]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
The beginningless King of glory, Whom the heavenly hosts tremble before: ye priests, sing; ye people, supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^1726]

*Troparion:*
Emulating the God-wise Forerunner John, struggling in fasting in the desert, with him thou wast counted worthy to attain the truly everlasting life.[^1727]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst quench the furnace of passions, O our father, with the dew of abstinence, crying out all-piously: Ye people, supremely exalt Christ unto the ages.[^1728]

*Troparion:*
A paradise in truth thou didst make the desert, excelling in it in every virtue; therefore thou wast also vouchsafed the sweetness of paradise.[^1729]

*Theotokion:*
As having boldness toward God, O all-hymned Mother of God, beseech Him to deliver from misfortunes[^1730] those who hymn thee in faith.[^1731]

*Another [Canon of Saint John]. Ode 8. Heirmos:*
God Who descended into the fiery furnace unto the Hebrew youths, and changed the flame into dew: sing unto Him as the Lord, all ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^1732]

*Troparion:*
Having woven for thyself an unaging tunic, O John, adorned with virtues, thou didst clothe thyself in the garment of poverty in the form of a beggar, enduring before the gates of thy parents.[^1733]

*Troparion:*
Blameless as another Job, thou didst suffer affliction before the gates, as if upon the dunghill, enduring the revilings of thy servants, O wise one, worn down by hunger and thirst. Therefore thou hast inherited the Kingdom on high.[^1734]

*Troparion:*
Manifestly thou didst follow the Gospel which thou didst receive in thy hands, and didst become poor, O blessed one, grieving throughout thy whole life; and thou wast meek and guileless, and an inheritor of the Kingdom on high.[^1735]

*Theotokion:*
Thou pourest forth an ever-flowing stream unto us who flee unto thee, O pure one; drawing abundant grace therefrom, we sing of thy childbirth, O most pure one, and supremely exalt it unto the ages.[^1736]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Receiving the Invisible One in divine form, O unwedded Virgin and Mother, in songs we magnify thy childbirth.[^1737]

*Troparion:*
As a spiritual hidden treasure, O venerable one, God revealed thee unto Anthony: and for us unto glory and rejoicing.[^1738]

*Troparion:*
Having nailed thyself to the fear of God, O venerable father, and having finished thy life in meditation on death, thou wast vouchsafed life.[^1739]

*Troparion:*
As having obtained boldness toward God, pray for those who on earth celebrate this thy memory in faith, O blessed Paul.[^1740]

*Theotokion:*
Having conceived Christ, co-beginningless with the Father and the Holy Spirit, and having given birth ineffably, O Virgin, pray that we may be saved.[^1741]

*Another [Canon of Saint John]. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
The Son of the unoriginate Father, God and Lord, incarnate of the Virgin appeared unto us, to enlighten those in darkness, to gather the dispersed: therefore we magnify the all-hymned Birthgiver of God.[^1742]

*Troparion:*
The Lord is my strength and song, thou didst cry, O father: herein I conquer the prince of darkness, in no wise fearing the phantom delusions from him, contemplating only the divine and unapproachable beauty.[^1743]

*Troparion:*
As rich soil, O venerable one, thy heart received the heavenly seed with the mental furrows, and yielded a hundredfold ear of corn,[^1744] nourishing the souls of all who faithfully honor thee, O divinely-blessed one.[^1745]

*Troparion:*
The Lord directed thy paths from the womb, O blessed one, and guided thy goings unto Himself; therefore thou wast joined unto the venerable who lived piously, with whom thou dost enjoy deification, O most glorious one.[^1746]

*Theotokion:*
Thy womb became a dwelling of Light, whereby those sitting in darkness saw the light; therefore with unceasing voices we ever hymn thee, O Mother of God, and honor thee with love as the hope of our souls.[^1747]

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "Give Ear, Ye Women" (Zheny uslyshite):*
Forsaking affection for thy parents and fleeting wealth, thou didst take up thy cross, O father, and didst follow Christ pre-eminently, O John; ascetically thou didst put the passions to death, and didst ascend unto dispassion, and dost pray for us, O God-bearer.[^1748]

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst give birth to Christ the King of glory, the Angel of Great Counsel of the Father, O all-hymned Maiden; Whose cross the venerable ones and ascetics took up and followed after Him: with whom unceasingly pray for us, O Birthgiver of God.[^1749]

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos: Glory, Tone 4:*
We honor thee as the instructor of a multitude of monks, O our father Paul: for by thy path we have learned truly to walk uprightly. Blessed art thou, having labored for Christ, and thou didst expose the power of the enemy, O converser with angels, fellow-partaker with the venerable and righteous: with whom pray unto the Lord that our souls may find mercy.[^1750]

*Both now, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "O Most Marvelous Wonder" (Preslavnago chudese):*
What is this visible sight which is seen by mine eyes, O Master? * Holding all creation, Thou art lifted up upon the Tree, and Thou diest, Who givest life unto all! * the Birthgiver of God weeping said, when she saw Him lifted up upon the Cross, * Who ineffably shone forth from her, God and Man.[^1751]

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of Paul, from the Canon Ode 3; and of John, Ode 6. Prokeimenon, Tone 7: The venerable shall boast in glory. Verse: Sing unto the Lord a new song. Epistle to the Galatians, Pericope 212 [Gal. 5:22–6:2]. Alleluia, Tone 6: Blessed is the man that fears the Lord. Verse: His seed shall be mighty upon earth. Gospel from Matthew, Pericope 43 [Matt. 11:27–30]. Communion Hymn: The righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance.*[^1752]

*Be it known that after the Apodosis of the Feast of the Theophany, from the 15th day of January, on Sundays and on days of celebrated saints, we sing the Katavasia: "The sun once shone upon dry land:" [Sushu gluboroditelnuyu zemlyu], until the Apodosis of the Meeting of the Lord.*[^1753]

*In the same month, on the 16th day:*
*The Veneration of the Precious Chains of the Holy and All-Praised Apostle Peter.*[^1754]
*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 6, Tone 4, Podoben: "As One Valiant among Martyrs" (Yako dobla):*
Thou didst bind delusion, * being bound for the Lord's sake, * and being shut up in prison, O apostle. * Therefore we honor thee with love, * and in faith we kiss thy chains, * drawing therefrom health of body * and salvation of soul; * as is meet we praise thee, O beholder of God, * converser with the bodiless. (Twice)[^1755]

Through thee they who were held in ignorance * receive understanding, * the many-seeded nations of the Gentiles formerly, * whose image from the height was shown * being carried in the vessel containing within * every living creature, O apostle. * Therefore every age glorifies thee, bowing down * unto the chains which thou didst bear * most earnestly for Christ. (Twice)[^1756]

Him Whom thou didst deny when He was judged, * when He was risen from the dead thou didst sing of, O apostle; * and thou didst preach * unto the ends of the world * both God and man, * Who in great goodness came unto those on earth. * Therefore with love we bless thee, O Peter, * bowing down unto the chains which thou didst bear * for Christ, O most glorious one. (Twice)[^1757]

*Glory, Tone 6: By Byzantios:*
Today the foundation of the Church, Peter the rock of faith, sets forth for us his precious chains for spiritual piety. Come, all ye, kissing them, let us crown him with hymns of praise: Rejoice, fervent champion of the faith, who with fervent understanding didst confess Christ and the Son of God with great boldness! Rejoice, rejoicing of the universe and keybearer of the heavenly Kingdom: grant grace unto those who honor thee with love, and who kiss thy precious[^1758] chains with desire: as standing before the throne of Christ the King of all, making prayer for us who celebrate thy memory.[^1759]

*Both now, Theotokion:*
*If it be Wednesday or Friday, Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "Having Risen on the Third Day" (Tridneven):*
Seeing our Life * hanging upon the Tree, * the all-immaculate Birthgiver of God, * maternally lamenting, cried: * O my Son and my God, * save those who hymn Thee with love.[^1760]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Octoechos: Glory, Tone 6:*
Again our fervent intercessor gathers us unto the spiritual banquet, Peter the rock of faith, setting forth for us his precious chains as costly food, the healing of diseases, consolation for the sorrowful, a haven for the storm-tossed. Come, all ye, kissing them, let us entreat Him Who glorified him: By his prayers, O Christ, save our souls.[^1761]

*Both now, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "Having Risen on the Third Day" (Tridneven):*
Seeing Thee crucified, O Christ, * she who bare Thee cried out: * What is this strange mystery which I see, O my Son? * How upon the Tree dost Thou die in the flesh, * suspended, O Bestower of life?[^1762]

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
Without leaving Rome thou didst come unto us, by the precious chains which thou didst bear, O primate of the apostles: bowing down unto which in faith we pray: By thy prayers unto God grant us great mercy.[^1763]

*At Matins, both Canons of the Octoechos, and of the Apostle on 6.*
*Canon of the Apostle.*
*The acrostic whereof is: I honor Peter, the foundation of dogmas. A composition of Joseph.*
*Tone 4.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
The choirs of Israel having traversed the Red Sea and the watery deep with unwetted feet, seeing the enemy captains submerged therein, with gladness sang: Let us sing unto our God, for He has been glorified.[^1764]

*Troparion:*
All the Church of Christ keeps festival, rejoicing in spirit, faithfully praising thee, and kissing in love the precious chains, O apostle and primate, which thou didst bear when bound, binding the tormentor.[^1765]

*Troparion:*
Catching men out of the deep of delusion, O Peter, like fishes thou didst bring them unto Him Who chose thee from fishermen, truly unto the primate of all the disciples: therefore we kiss the chains which thou didst bear.[^1766]

*Troparion:*
With the foundation of the faith thou didst build up the souls of all the faithful; and having cast down the temples of delusion, O Peter, thou didst build churches, which ever loudly honor thee,[^1767] and the chains which thou didst bear.[^1768]

*Theotokion:*
All the weapons of the deceitful enemy utterly failed, O most pure Virgin, when the Word Who dwelt in thy blameless womb was wounded by the spear: Whom I beseech thee, may my heart now be wounded with His sweetest desire.[^1769]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
The bow of the mighty has become weak, and the feeble have girded themselves with strength: therefore my heart has been established in the Lord.[^1770]

*Troparion:*
Being wholly united unto the purest Light by His divine communions, thou didst appear as a second light, O Peter, illuminating our souls.[^1771]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst establish the laws of Christ, and didst teach the most lawless righteousness, as the primate of the apostles, as the immovable foundation of dogmas.[^1772]

*Troparion:*
With a sacred tongue thou didst proclaim God Who suffered and was crucified upon the Cross: therefore, O Peter, we honor the chains that bound thee.[^1773]

*Theotokion:*
Death was checked from its unrestrainable rushing even unto thee: for thou didst bear the Fountain of immortality, O Birthgiver of God, Virgin Mother.[^1774]

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the Highest" (Vyshnikh ishcha):*
Christ the Rock brightly glorifies the rock of faith, the primate of the disciples; for He summons all to celebrate, O Peter, the precious chains of thy wonders, and grants forgiveness of transgressions.[^1775]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who Wast Lifted Up upon the Cross" (Voznesyisya):*
As the primate of the wise apostles, and as the keybearer of the heavenly Kingdom, in faith we praise thee, O apostle, and with pure conscience we kiss, O Peter, the chains which thou didst bear like a malefactor, destroying the malefactions of the enemy: from which pray that we may be delivered. (Twice)[^1776]

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
Higher than the Cherubim and Seraphim, more spacious than heaven and earth, and shown forth surpassing visible and invisible creation by incomprehensible judgment: for Him Whom the expanse of the heavens cannot contain, thou didst contain in thy womb, O pure one: Him do thou entreat that thy servants may be saved.[^1777]

*Stavrotheotokion:*
She who bare Thee in the flesh at the end of times, Who wast begotten of the beginningless Father, seeing Thee hanging upon the Cross, O Christ,[^1778] cried: Woe is me, most beloved Jesus! How art Thou, Who art glorified as God by the angels, now willingly crucified by lawless men, O my Son? I hymn Thee, O Long-suffering One.[^1779]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
For the sake of love of Thine image, O Compassionate One, Thou didst stand upon Thy Cross, and the nations melted away: for Thou, O Lover of mankind, art my strength and praise.[^1780]

*Troparion:*
Again witnessing the greatness, thou didst turn the hearts of disobedient Hebrews unto the divine faith, as the foundation of the faith.[^1781]

*Troparion:*
Thy goings were known upon the waters, through the superabundant love of Him Who walked upon them, O Peter, and revealed divine paths unto thee.[^1782]

*Troparion:*
Having a remedy for diverse diseases in thy divine chains, O blessed one: these we kiss in faith, honoring thee.[^1783]

*Theotokion:*
As into a spacious palace the King of all entered into thy holy womb, revealing thee incarnate, O all-immaculate Birthgiver of God.[^1784]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Send down Thy light upon us, O Lord, and loose us from the gloom of transgressions, O Good One, granting Thy peace.[^1785]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst preach the Son co-beginningless with the Father, by divine revelation, O all-praised one; and thou wast accounted worthy of the blessed proclamation from His mouth.[^1786]

*Troparion:*
When thou didst behold the light that shone forth upon Tabor, covering the rays of the sun, with the light that is from Light thou wast illumined, O Peter, and didst enlighten the faithful.[^1787]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst proclaim Christ Who was dead for three days, for Whose sake thou didst bear chains, O Peter: having been vouchsafed to venerate which, we piously honor thee.[^1788]

*Theotokion:*
Weighed down with the burden of many sins, O most pure one, lighten me now, strengthening me to bear the most light yoke of Christ.[^1789]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Prefiguring the three-day burial, the Prophet Jonah cried, praying in the sea-monster: Deliver me from corruption, O Jesus, King of powers.[^1790]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst most gloriously endure headlong crucifixion; thou didst prepare thy feet for the heavenly path: wherein teach us to walk,[^1791] disciple of Christ, strengthen [us].[^1792]

*Troparion:*
Thou hast taken up thy dwelling in the life of the living, and by the divine [power] for its sake, thou hast crushed the bonds of Belial who bound thee; therefore do we honor thy chains.[^1793]

*Troparion:*
Pray to the Master of creation, O all-blessed one, to send down cleansing, and peace, and mercy unto those who glorify thee, as His truest disciple.[^1794]

*Theotokion:*
The forefather was stripped of the coats of skins of mortality; for God the Creator clothed Himself therewith from thy blood, having become incarnate beyond word, O all-immaculate one.[^1795]

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "In supplications" (Въ мл҃твахъ):*
Let us praise the supreme and chief of the apostles, the divine disciple of truth, Peter the Great; and with faith let us kiss his chains, receiving remission of transgressions.[^1796]

*Ikos:*
What tongue of men can worthily praise the glorious and great disciple of the Lord? For whom the divine Word blessedly beatified, what mind shall praise? Yet what anyone possesses according to his strength, it is right to offer unto God, and this I also attempt to do. But O lovers of the feast, let us piously crown the first-enthroned with hymns, receiving remission of transgressions.[^1797]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
Of old in Babylon, the Abrahamic youths trampled upon the flame of the furnace, crying aloud with hymns: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.[^1798]

*Troparion:*
Thrice didst thou deny Christ, therefore by a threefold questioning He heals thy transgression, O all-glorious Peter, and shows [thee] the confirmation of many who waver.[^1799]

*Troparion:*
As a prisoner of Christ, with sweetest desire thou didst partake of various bonds; therefore unto thy chains also, which loose passions, O Peter, do we bow down in faith.[^1800]

*Troparion:*
Thou dost dispel the deep night of cruel polytheism, traversing the universe like a most great sun, O Peter, eyewitness of Christ, glory of the apostles.[^1801]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast the glory of Christ; Him thou didst glorify with thy members, O all-glorious Peter; therefore do we glorify thee, and bow down before the chains that bound thee.[^1802]

*Theotokion:*
He Who descended upon the earth like rain, O Virgin, watered all the earth with the knowledge of God, and showed thee, O honorable one, more honorable than all the angels.[^1803]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
O almighty Redeemer of all, having descended unto those who acted piously in the midst of the flame, Thou didst dew them and didst teach them to sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works, sing [unto the Lord].[^1804]

*Troparion:*
Cultivating hard hearts, O Peter, thou didst render them most fruitful unto the Husbandman of creation, Who delivered unto thee the divine keys to bind and to loose sins.[^1805]

*Troparion:*
We ever call thee blessed, O Peter, and kiss thy chains which thou didst wear as an evildoer, slaying the author of evil and binding [him] with thy fetters, O apostle.[^1806]

*Troparion:*
By thy unyielding rock of faith, O Peter, preserving the fullness of the Church, drive away scandals from the midst, O Peter, and ask peaceful ordering for her, O blessed one.[^1807]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst radiantly preach Him Who by bonds and His most pure Passion bound hades and death; therefore, O all-blessed one, kissing thy chains, we are sanctified.[^1808]

*Triadikon:*
Even as the celestial ranks, let us cry aloud with thrice-holy voices, glorifying now the all-causing Father, and the Son, and the Spirit: one essence, one power, and one operation.[^1809]

*Theotokion:*
The prophet prefigured thee as the noetic lampstand, O Mother of God, bearing the divine candle that enlightens those previously darkened by many obscurement of evils.[^1810]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Thy childbearing was revealed incorrupt: God came forth from thy loins, He appeared on earth bearing flesh, and lived among men; therefore, O Birthgiver of God, we all magnify thee.[^1811]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast accounted worthy to behold the things given, faithfully hoped for by thee, O Peter; and rejoicing, thou receivest the rewards of thy labors from God, the Lover of mankind, Whose divine Passion thou didst image forth in thy flesh.[^1812]

*Troparion:*
As the divine key-bearer of this Kingdom, open its entrances unto those who faithfully honor thee on earth and kiss thy venerable chains, O Peter, wherewith thou wast bound and didst bear them.[^1813]

*Troparion:*
Being with the Son on Tabor, thou wast accounted worthy to hear the Father's voice uttering this; for by the Divine Spirit, O Peter, thy heart was cleansed, being most gloriously illumined.[^1814]

*Troparion:*
Unto us who with love honor thee and kiss thy chains wherewith thou wast bound, O Peter, entreat cleansing and remission of debts, and the enjoyment of the Heavenly Kingdom.[^1815]

*Theotokion:*
Thou wast the dwelling-place of Light; therefore with light guide me O maiden, who am darkened by all temptations of the enemy, that in faith I may magnify thee, O all-pure one, Mother and Virgin.[^1816]

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "In spirit in the sanctuary" (Дꙋ́хомъ во ст҃или́щи):*
Loose me, the wretched one bound with the chains of passions, O blessed one, even as of old the angel of God loosed thy chains and most gloriously led thee forth from the prison when thou wast shut therein, O most blessed Peter, supreme among the apostles.[^1817]

*Theotokion:*
O all-immaculate Virgin, thou wast acknowledged as Mother, having borne both God and man beyond nature; and thy childbearing became salvation unto those who sing with love. Glory is due, and honor and worship unto the unapproachable and divine Trinity.[^1818]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera from the Octoechos:*

*Glory..., Tone 4. By John the Monk:*
By the threefold questioning, "Peter, dost thou love Me?", Christ corrected the threefold denial. Therefore Simon also said unto the Knower of hearts: "Lord, Thou knowest all things, Thou understandest all things; Thou knowest that I love Thee." Therefore the Savior said unto him: "Feed My sheep, feed My chosen ones, feed My lambs, which I have purchased with Mine own Blood for salvation." Pray unto Him, O God-blessed apostle, to grant us great mercy.[^1819]

*Both now..., Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "As noble" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*
When she who bore Thee, the Ewe-lamb, beheld Thee, the Lamb and Shepherd, upon the Tree, she wailed and maternally cried aloud unto Thee: "O most desired Son, how art Thou suspended upon the Tree of the Cross, O longsuffering One? How were Thy hands and feet nailed by the lawless, O Word, and Thou didst pour out Thy Blood, O Master?"[^1820]

*At the Liturgy, Beatitudes from the Canon of the apostle, Odes 3 and 6.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 8: Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world.[^1821] Verse: The heavens declare the glory of God.*

*Epistle from the Acts, Pericope 24.*

*Alleluia, Tone 1: The heavens shall confess Thy wonders, O Lord, and Thy truth in the congregation of the saints.[^1822] Gospel according to John, Pericope 67.*

*Communion Hymn: Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth On the same month, on the 17th day: The venerable and God-bearing Father our Anthony the Great.*

*If the superior will, we celebrate the Vigil.*

*At Small Vespers, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва тѧ̀):*

When in the tomb, for the sake of the salvation of the body, thou didst shut thyself up, O father, for the love of Christ, thou didst endure, growing stronger against the temptations of the demons, and by prayer and grace thou didst drive them away, with the most feeble counsels of the horde; then the angelic ranks assembled, crying aloud: Glory to Him Who strengthened thee, O Anthony! *(Twice)*[^1823]

Thou wast revealed as another Elijah, having thy glorious disciples like Elisha, O wise one, unto whom thou didst also leave thy twofold grace, being caught up as upon an aerial chariot, O father; therefore, living in the Spirit, now rejoicing together with them, remember all who celebrate with love thy venerable solemnity, O Anthony, all-blessed one.[^1824]

Even as the God-seer Moses, thou didst truly enter into the noetic darkness of visions, and straightway didst clearly see Him Whom thou didst desire. With glorified face, through that radiance, O father, to guide [the faithful] into the saving mansions; therefore coming together, O God-wise one, rejoicing we cry aloud: Glory to Christ God Who strengthened thee![^1825]

*Glory..., Tone 3. By Anatolius:*
Venerable Anthony, resting as in unwaning light, thou didst accomplish the burning and freezing life of hardest endurance; for having joined bodily solitude spiritually to the wilderness, thou didst trample underfoot the fiery darts of the demons; and having risen higher than every virtue, thou dwellest with the angels in the Heavenly Kingdom: with them pray unto Christ God that our souls may be saved.[^1826]

*Both now..., Theotokion:*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "O House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
