From thy mother's swaddling clothes, O God-bearer, thou wast revealed as a sanctified vessel, O Anthony, having become a house of the Holy Spirit.[^1827]

*Verse: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones.[^1828]*

Having put to shame the deceits of the wicked demons by the power of the Cross, thou didst make clear the glory of Christ, O father Anthony.[^1829]

*Verse: Blessed is the man* who fears the Lord, He shall delight exceedingly in His commandments.[^1830]

Thou wast taken up like Elijah upon a fiery chariot, and didst come, O blessed one, immediately unto the Trinity, O Anthony of worldwide renown.[^1831]

*Glory..., Both now..., Theotokion:*
The celestial choirs, O Virgin Birthgiver of God, sing of thee with those below, unceasingly glorifying thy most pure childbearing.[^1832]

*At Great Vespers, we sing "Blessed is the man," the first antiphon.*

*At "Lord, I have cried," we set 8 verses, and sing the Stichera, Tone 4, Podoben: "Called from on high" (Зва́нный свы́ше):*

Illumined with the rays of the Spirit, when divine desire inflamed thee and gave wings to thy soul to desire His love, truly the supreme good; then thou didst despise flesh and blood, and wast outside the world by much abstinence, and by hesychia wast united unto Him; therefore thou wast filled with the good things from thence as thou didst ask, and didst shine forth like a star, illumining our souls, O Anthony. *(Thrice)*[^1833]

Having shattered the bows and arrows of the demons by the grace of the Holy Spirit, thou didst make manifest unto all their malice and snaring, by divine teachings, being irradiated with divine splendors; thou wast the most God-radiant lamp of monastics, and the first adorner of the wilderness, and the most skillful and honorable physician of the sick, and the archetypal outline of the virtuous life, O father Anthony. *(Thrice)*[^1834]

Pure in soul and heart, earthly angel, heavenly man, teacher of virginity, sure measure of abstinence, O Anthony, living with thy Master, and offering unceasing doxology unto Him, O blessed one, with the angels and the venerable and all the righteous: deliver ever from cruel afflictions and transgressions those who celebrate thy sacred memory. *(Twice)*[^1835]

*Glory..., Tone 6:*
Having preserved that which is according to the image unharmed, having ascetically established the mind as master over ruinous passions, thou didst ascend, as far as possible, unto that which is according to the likeness; for having courageously compelled nature, thou didst hasten to subordinate the worse unto the better, and to enslave the flesh unto the spirit; therefore thou wast revealed as the summit of monastics, a citizen of the desert, an instructor of those who run well, a most sure rule of virtue; and now in the heavens, the mirrors being dissolved, O our father Anthony, thou purely beholdest the Holy Trinity, praying unceasingly for those who honor thee in faith and love.[^1836]

*Both now..., Theotokion: Who shall not call thee blessed...*

*Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day. Three Readings: They are written on the 31st day of this month.*[^1837]

*At the Litiya, the Sticheron of the temple, and of the saint, Tone 2, Automela. By the Studite:*

Having gathered ascetic instruction on earth, O venerable Anthony, thou didst drown all the assaults of passions in the stream of thy tears. A divine and venerable ladder leading up into heaven was thy God-accepted life known unto all; for having shown in thyself the fruits of piety, thereby thou healest the infirmities of the passions of those who faithfully cry unto thee: Rejoice, most gold-radiant star of the East, lamp and shepherd of monastics! Rejoice, ever-memorable one, most excellent nursling of the desert, and unshakable confirmation of the Church! Rejoice, great instructor of the wandering! Rejoice, our boast and the radiant joy of the universe![^1838]

An earthly angel and heavenly man of God, the adornment of the world, the sweetness of good things and of virtues, the boast of fasters, let us honor Anthony; for planted in the house of God, he blossomed righteously, and like a cedar in the wilderness, he multiplied Christ's flock of rational sheep in holiness and righteousness.[^1839]

Venerable father, having diligently trained in virtue from infancy, thou wast an instrument of the Holy Spirit; and having received from Him the operation of miracles, thou didst persuade men to despise pleasant things; and now being purely illumined with divine light, enlighten also our minds, O father Anthony.[^1840]

*Glory..., Tone 6:*
Venerable father, having heard the voice of the Gospel of the Lord, thou didst forsake the world, counting riches and glory as nothing; therefore thou didst cry aloud unto all: Love God, and ye shall find eternal grace; prefer nothing before His love, so that when He comes in His glory, ye may find rest with all the saints. By his prayers, O Christ, preserve and save our souls![^1841]

*Both now..., Theotokion:*
We call thee blessed, O Virgin Birthgiver of God, for from thee shone forth Christ the Sun of righteousness, Who hath great mercy.[^1842]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 6, Podoben: "Rejoice, O choir of ascetics" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ по́стникѡвъ):*
Rejoice, having been joined unto the angelic choirs on high, O Anthony; for their life upon earth, O father, was truly virtuous virtue, for having been trained in it, thou didst live. Thou wast revealed as a most venerable and undefiled mirror, receiving the radiant flashings of the All-Holy Spirit, O all-blessed one; therefore, being illumined, thou didst foresee future things, foretelling all, being taught by the divine epiphany of Christ: pray unto Him to grant our souls great mercy.[^1843]

*Verse: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones.[^1844]*

Rejoice, having become the chief leader and invincible champion of ascetics; for having cut out the roots of passions and the onrushes of demons, courageously resisting, thou didst expose their weakness and soul-destroying delusion; and thou didst manifest the operation and invincible power of the Savior's Cross, girded wherewith thou didst conquer all who reject the divine manifestation of Christ in the flesh: pray unto Him to grant our souls great mercy.[^1845]

*Verse: Blessed is the man who fears the Lord, he shall delight exceedingly in His commandments.[^1846]*

A luminous pillar of virtue firmly established, and a cloud overshadowing those who are in the wilderness wast thou revealed, guiding from earth unto heaven those who behold God. With the rod of the Cross having divided the sea of passions, and having conquered the noetic Amalek, thou didst find unhindered heavenly ascent, O God-blessed one, and an incorruptible heritage, joyfully standing before the throne of Christ with the bodiless hosts: pray unto Him to grant our souls great mercy.[^1847]

*Glory..., Tone 8:*
The multitudes of monastics honor thee as instructor, O our father Anthony; for by thy path we have truly learned to walk uprightly. Blessed art thou who didst labor for Christ and didst expose the enemy's power, companion of angels, fellow partaker with Paul of Thebes: with them pray unto the Lord that our souls may find mercy.[^1848]

*Both now..., Theotokion: O unwedded Virgin...*

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
Emulating the ways of the zealous Elijah, following the Baptist in upright paths, O father Anthony, thou wast a dweller in the wilderness and didst establish the universe by thy prayers; therefore pray unto Christ God that our souls may be saved.[^1849]

*At Matins, at "God is the Lord," the Troparion twice. Glory..., Both now..., Theotokion: "The mystery hidden from the ages..."*

*After the first stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*

Thou didst follow the calling of thy Lord, forsaking the world and all the fair things in the world, O all-blessed Anthony; with zeal thou didst endure the affliction of the wilderness, and didst courageously repel the hosts of demons; therefore do we ever faithfully praise thy memory with hymns. *(Twice)*[^1850]

*Glory..., Both now..., Theotokion:*
By thy divine childbearing, O pure one, thou hast renewed the mortal nature of earthborn men that was corrupted by passions, and hast raised all from death unto the life of incorruption; therefore as is due we all call thee blessed, O all-glorified Virgin, even as thou didst foretell.[^1851]

*After the second stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 5, Podoben: "Co-unoriginate Word" (Собезнача́лное сло́во):*
Let us honor the faster of the Lord with hymns, as one who truly put to death all assaults of passions by abstinence and steadfast endurance, and who utterly confounded the adversary enemy and all his pride; and who now prays unto the Lord that our souls may find mercy. *(Twice)*[^1852]

*Glory..., Both now..., Theotokion:*
The awesome miracle of conception and the ineffable manner of childbearing known in thee, O pure Ever-Virgin, astonishes my mind and confounds my thought; thy glory, O Birthgiver of God, is extended over all for the salvation of our souls.[^1853]

*After the Polyeleos, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
Enriched with pastoral skill, pillar and foundation of monastics, thou didst firmly shepherd thy rational flock; for having desired Christ's divine teachings, wherein thou didst sow the word, O venerable one; therefore thou didst also rouse all unto emulation of the angelic life, to glorify God with one mind, O God-bearer Anthony: pray unto Christ God to grant remission of transgressions unto those who honor with love thy holy memory. *(Twice)*[^1854]

*Glory..., Both now..., Theotokion:*
Let us hymn the heavenly gate and ark, the all-holy mountain, the bright cloud, the unburnt bush, the rational paradise, the recall of Eve, the great treasure of all the universe; for salvation was wrought in her for the world, and remission of ancient transgressions. Therefore do we cry unto her: Pray unto thy Son to grant remission of transgressions unto those who piously bow down before thy most holy childbearing.[^1855]

*Gradual Hymns, the 1st Antiphon of Tone 4.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 4: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones.[^1856] Verse: What shall I render unto the Lord for all that He hath rendered unto me?*

*Let every breath [praise the Lord]...*

*Gospel according to Matthew, Pericope 43 [Mt. 11:27-30].*

*After Psalm 50, Sticheron, Tone 6:*
Venerable father, into all the earth hath gone forth the sound of thy right deeds; therefore in the heavens thou hast found the reward of thy labors, thou didst conquer the demonic hosts, and didst attain unto the angelic ranks, whose blameless life thou didst emulate; having boldness before Christ God, ask peace for our souls.[^1857]

*The Canon of the Birthgiver of God on 6, and of the saint on 8.*

*The Canon of the Birthgiver of God, whose acrostic is: "I sing praise to the life-bearing Maiden." A creation of John Damascene, Tone 2.*[^1858]

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Walking untrodden, unaccustomed, unwetted along the path of the sea, chosen Israel cried aloud: Let us sing unto the Lord, for He is gloriously glorified![^1859]

*Troparion:*
The immaterial ladder of old and the wondrously congealed path of the sea revealed thy childbearing, O pure one, which we all hymn: For He is gloriously glorified![^1860]

*Troparion:*
The Power of the Most High, the perfect Hypostasis, the Wisdom of God, having become incarnate of thee, O all-pure one, conversed with men: For He is gloriously glorified![^1861]

*Troparion:*
The Sun of righteousness, O pure one, passed through the impassable door of the sealed gates of thy womb, and shone forth unto the world: For He is gloriously glorified![^1862]

*The Canon of the Venerable One, whose acrostic is: "Fittingly to praise the divine Anthony." A creation of Theophanes, Tone 8.*[^1863]

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
The wonderworking rod of Moses of old drowned the chariot-driver Pharaoh, having struck cruciformly and divided the sea, yet saved fugitive Israel going on foot, singing a hymn unto God.[^1864]

*Troparion:*
Having laid hold of the marks of immortality and eternal life, and being filled with the thrice-radiant light, O father: pray that by the illumination of grace my darkened soul may be enlightened, that I may worthily praise thee.[^1865]

*Troparion:*
Being young in bodily age, having received a new path of virtue, thou didst traverse it safely, obeying the new law of the Savior, O thrice-blessed one, and [following] the life-bearing commandments of the Gospel.[^1866]

*Troparion:*
Illumined with the thrice-sunned brilliance, O all-wise one, inflamed with divine desire, thou didst tear asunder like a spider's web the evil-minded fury of the demons, O blessed one, and the open jaws of wild beasts, and the pains of wounds.[^1867]

*Theotokion:*
As the Mother of God, having boldness toward the Only-Begotten Word born of thee, Who is co-unoriginate with the Father and consubstantial with the Spirit: cease not to pray, O all-immaculate one, that those who glorify thee as Birthgiver of God may be saved from afflictions.[^1868]

*Katavasia:*
The sun of old shone upon dry ground born of the deep, for the water became firm like a wall on both sides unto the people traversing the sea on foot and singing in a manner pleasing unto God: Let us sing unto the Lord, for He is gloriously glorified![^1869]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
The bow of the mighty was broken by Thy dominion, O Christ, and the weak girded themselves with strength.[^1870]

*Troparion:*
He Who is higher than all time, as Creator of the times, was voluntarily fashioned as an infant from thee, O Virgin.[^1871]

*Troparion:*
Thy womb became more spacious than the heavens, through which Adam lives rejoicing in the heavens.[^1872]

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*
O Thou Who in the beginning didst establish the heavens with understanding, and didst found the earth upon the waters: establish me, O Christ, upon the rock of Thy commandments, for there is none holy save Thee, O Thou only Lover of mankind.[^1873]

*Troparion:*
With established thought and firm endurance thou didst wither the flame of passions; in the radiant garment of dispassion wast thou clad, O father Anthony, and in the robe of salvation.[^1874]

*Troparion:*
The most violent assaults of the brazen demons, transforming themselves into forms of wild beasts, thou didst despise, as also their impotent power; for thou hadst a mighty Helper in battles.[^1875]

*Troparion:*
O God-bearer, having exposed the principalities and powers of darkness by steadfast abstinence, thou wast a valiant victor, O Anthony, glory of ascetics, boast of monastics.[^1876]

*Theotokion:*
My mortified mind do thou raise up by the life-giving operation manifested unto the world from thee, O pure one, and guide me unto life, who alone by thy childbearing hast destroyed the gates of death.[^1877]

*Katavasia:*
Establish, O Lord, the Church, the confirmation of those who put their trust in Thee[^1878] the Church, which Thou hast purchased with Thy precious Blood.[^1879]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "Of Wisdom" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
Having bound thy soul with the love of Christ, and wisely hated all earthly things, thou didst take up thine abode, O venerable father, in deserts and mountains; for having tasted of the tree of understanding, O glorious initiate of unsetting mysteries, thou didst live an angelic life. Therefore, having also passed through the gloom of thy flesh, thou didst drive away the darkness of the demons, O Anthony, chosen foremost of monastics: pray unto Christ God to grant remission of transgressions unto those who honor thy holy memory with love.[^1880] *(Twice)*

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
As the all-immaculate bride of the Creator, as the unwedded Mother of the Deliverer, as the receptacle of the Comforter, O all-hymned one: hasten to deliver me, who am a foul habitation of lawlessness and have knowingly become a plaything of demons, from their villainy, and make me a radiant dwelling of virtues, O light-bearing and incorrupt one; drive away the cloud of passions, and through thy prayers make me worthy of the supreme communion and of the unsetting light.[^1881]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I heard, O Lord, of Thy glorious dispensation, and I glorified Thine incomprehensible power, O Lover of mankind.[^1882]

*Troparion:*
Lo, the divine mountain of the house of the Lord is exalted, the Mother of God, situated higher than the heavenly hosts.[^1883]

*Troparion:*
Apart from the laws of nature, O Virgin, having alone given birth unto the Benefactor of creation, thou wast deemed worthy of a divine calling.[^1884]

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*
Thou art my strength, O Lord, Thou art also my power, Thou art my God, Thou art my rejoicing, Who didst not leave the bosom of the Father and yet didst visit our poverty. Therefore with the Prophet Habakkuk I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind.[^1885]

*Troparion:*
Having made use of the divine ladder of virtues, O father, thou didst ascend unto the heights, and didst behold God established thereon, imparting gifts exceedingly richly unto those who faithfully sing: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind.[^1886]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast wholly consecrated unto God, O Anthony, being united alone to the Alone in all wisdom by virtue and discourses, and deemed worthy of divine manifestations as one pure; for having departed from earth and earthly things, thou didst worthily find heavenly delight.[^1887]

*Troparion:*
Having purified thy mind and soul, O Anthony, thou didst expose the soul-destroying delusion, and the bitter craft and deceit, and the fantasies of the enemies. For having suffered, thou didst learn, and having been instructed, thou dost teach the multitudes of monastics, O all-blessed one.[^1888]

*Theotokion:*
Pray unto God Who was incarnate of thee, Who immutably remained what He was, naturally equal to the Father and become consubstantial with thee who didst bear Him, to grant remission of transgressions and salvation of souls unto those who sing of thee in faith.[^1889]

*Katavasia:*
Thy virtue hath covered the heavens, O Christ, for having come forth from the ark of Thy sanctification, Thine incorrupt Mother, Thou didst appear in the temple of Thy glory as an infant carried in arms, and all things were filled with Thy praise.[^1890]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
The coal revealed unto Isaiah, the Sun, hath shone forth from the virginal womb, granting the illumination of divine knowledge unto those that wandered in darkness.[^1891]

*Troparion:*
Ye clouds of rejoicing, drop down sweetness! For a child hath been given unto those upon earth, Who is before the ages, our God incarnate of the Virgin.[^1892]

*Troparion:*
Light hath shone forth upon my life and flesh, and destroyed the decay of sin: the Most High, Who in the end became incarnate of the Virgin without seed.[^1893]

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*
Why hast Thou cast me away from Thy presence, O unsetting Light, and an alien darkness hath enveloped me, the wretched one? But turn me back, and direct my ways unto the light of Thy commandments, I pray Thee.[^1894]

*Troparion:*
Having dwelling within thee God, Who sees God, O blessed one, instructing thee and illuminating and making thee wise: thou wast deemed worthy, O thrice-blessed one, to behold the ascents of pure and blessed souls.[^1895]

*Troparion:*
Christ granted thee the grace of healings over various infirmities, and authority over unclean spirits, O wise one; for having overcome nature, O father, thou didst partake of the supernatural gifts of the Spirit.[^1896]

*Theotokion:*
Having thee as a rampart, and preserved by thy protection, boasting in thy divine glory, we call thee blessed; for thou, O all-immaculate one, pourest forth joy and gladness unto our souls.[^1897]

*Katavasia:*
When Isaiah beheld in a figure God exalted upon a throne, upborne by angels of glory, he cried: O wretched me! For I have foreseen God becoming incarnate, the unsetting Light, and ruling over peace.[^1898]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Having heard the voice of suppliant words from an afflicted soul, O Master, deliver me from grievous things; for Thou alone art the Cause of our salvation.[^1899]

*Troparion:*
Human nature, being in bondage to sin, O pure Lady, hath attained freedom through thee; for thy Son is slain as a lamb for all.[^1900]

*Troparion:*
We all cry aloud unto thee, the true Mother of God: Deliver thy servants who have angered [Him]; for thou alone hast boldness toward thy Son.[^1901]

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*
The abyss of sins and the storm of transgressions confound me, and drag me into the deep of violent despair; but stretch forth Thy mighty hand unto me, as unto Peter, O Pilot, and save me.[^1902]

*Troparion:*
Having embraced a lawful athletic life from thine early youth, O God-wise one, thou didst keep it even unto the end; and as a divine champion, thou didst receive the crown of victory from the King of all.[^1903]

*Troparion:*
Having thee as a most mighty intercessor with God, O blessed one, and a sharer of concerns, a protector, defender, and pious mediator, we are saved from all tribulations, calamities, and adversities.[^1904]

*Theotokion:*
In all truth thou hast lifted up fallen human nature, having borne in thy womb without seed, O Mother of God, the unchangeable Son visible in divine form and equal to the Father.[^1905]

*Katavasia:*
The elder, having seen with his eyes the salvation that came from God unto the peoples, cried unto Thee: Christ, Thou art my God![^1906]

*Kontakion, Tone 2. Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*
Having cast aside the turmoil of this life, thou didst finish thy life in silence, imitating the Baptist in every way, O most venerable one; therefore with him we honor thee, O Anthony, father of fathers.[^1907]

*Ikos:*
Having heard the voice of Christ, thou didst walk after His commandments, having become stripped of worldly life; and thou didst cast away all anxieties of possessions, properties, and thy servants, and the love of thy sister, O God-bearing Anthony; and conversing most purely with God alone in the deserts, thou didst receive the grace of understanding: send this down unto me who praise thee in hymns, O Anthony, father of fathers.[^1908]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The most wise youths of old showed themselves as children, for from a God-received soul they sang, theologizing with their lips: O God of our fathers and our God, supremely divine God of our fathers and our God, blessed art Thou.[^1909]

*Troparion:*
Jacob indeed in the night beheld God as in an enigma, but incarnate of thee He hath appeared in brightness unto those who sing: O supremely divine and supremely glorious God of our fathers![^1910]

*Troparion:*
Manifesting signs of the ineffable intertwining with thee, He wrestled with Jacob, whereby of His own will He was united unto men, O pure one: O supremely divine and supremely glorious God of our fathers![^1911]

*Troparion:*
Abominable is he who proclaims Thee not as the Virgin's only Son, One of the all-hymned Trinity, crying with undoubted mind and tongue: O supremely divine and supremely glorious God of our fathers![^1912]

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*
The fire was ashamed before the condescension of God in Babylon of old; therefore the youths in the furnace, dancing with joyful step as in a flower garden, sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^1913]

*Troparion:*
Thy cheeks became cups of aromatic herbs, breathing forth the fragrance and salvation of virtues as from a flower garden unto those who cry in faith: Blessed is the God of our fathers![^1914]

*Troparion:*
The grace of the All-Holy Spirit having made its abode in thee, O father, made thee an expeller of the spirits of malice and an instructor of monastics, who cry: Blessed is the God of our fathers![^1915]

*Theotokion:*
Let us praise the all-pure and all-holy Mary, for through her the grace of gifts beyond understanding wells forth unto us as from a torrent of divine goodness; and let us now call her blessed with a pious mind.[^1916]

*Katavasia:*
Thee Who didst bedew the theologizing youths in the fire, and Who didst make Thine abode in the incorrupt Virgin, God the Word, we hymn, singing devoutly: Blessed is the God of our fathers![^1917]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Having despised the golden image, the thrice-blessed youths, beholding the immutable and living image of God, sang in the midst of the fire: Let all consecrated creation sing to the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages![^1918]

*Troparion:*
Through thee He was seen upon earth and lived among men, He Who is incomparable in goodness and power; unto Whom singing, all we faithful cry: Let all consecrated creation sing to the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages![^1919]

*Troparion:*
Proclaiming thee truly pure, we glorify thee, O maiden; for thou didst bear One of the Trinity incarnate, unto Whom with the Father and the Spirit we all sing: Let all creation sing to the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages![^1920]

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*
Sevenfold the Chaldean tyrant madly kindled the furnace for the godly, but beholding them saved by a greater power, he cried unto the Creator and Deliverer: Ye youths, bless; ye priests, sing; ye people, exalt Him above all unto all ages![^1921]

*Troparion:*
Having shown forth by purity of mind on earth as an angel vigilance in prayers, strength in fastings, and patient endurance in trials, O Anthony, thou didst cry unto God: Ye youths, bless; ye priests, sing; ye people, exalt Him above all unto all ages![^1922]

*Troparion:*
Continually drawing near unto God by prayers and supplications, O venerable one, Thou didst ascend unto the supreme height, having escaped the demonic snares; and being liberated from their tyranny, O God-wise one, Thou singest: Ye priests, sing; ye people, exalt Him above all unto all ages![^1923]

*Troparion:*
Having become a new Moses, thou didst set up in the wilderness a monument of victory over the enemy: leading the people, the assembly of ascetics, who in gladness and a new way of life cry unto the Benefactor: Ye priests, bless; ye people, exalt Him above all unto all ages![^1924]

*Theotokion:*
O all-pure Mother of God, cleanse the wounds and sinful sores of my soul, washing them with the fountains that flowed from the side of Him born of thee, and purifying them with the streams issuing therefrom; for unto thee do I cry, and unto thee do I flee, and thee do I invoke, who art full of divine grace.[^1925]

*Katavasia:*
Joined together in the unendurable fire, the youths standing for piety, unharmed by the flame, sang a divine hymn: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages![^1926]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Thou art all desire, Thou art all sweetness, O Word of God, Son of the Virgin, Lord God of gods, Holy of holies; therefore with her that bare Thee, we all magnify Thee.[^1927]

*Troparion:*
A rod of strength was given unto corruptible nature, the Word of God in thy womb, O pure one, and He raised it up when it had slipped down unto hades; therefore, O all-pure one, as Mother of God we magnify thee.[^1928]

*Troparion:*
Whom Thou didst choose, O Master, receive Thy Mother praying with maternal care for us, and all things shall be filled with Thy goodness, that we all may magnify Thee as our Benefactor.[^1929]

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*
Heaven was dismayed at this, and the ends of the earth were astonished, that God appeared unto men in the flesh, and thy womb became more spacious than the heavens; therefore the ranks of angels and men magnify thee as Mother of God.[^1930]

*Troparion:*
Thy light-bearing festival hath arrived, O all-blessed father Anthony, full of joy, full of spiritual gladness, full of the Holy Spirit, full of fragrance and illumination; and having thee now as the rule and lawgiver of fasting, we rejoice.[^1931]

*Troparion:*
Cease not praying unto the Deliverer, O all-honored father, to grant unto those who devoutly celebrate thy sacred memory remission of transgressions, distribution of gifts, divine protection, salvation of souls, and eternal rejoicing.[^1932]

*Troparion:*
Having lived an equal-to-the-angels life upon earth, thou didst find equal-to-the-angels radiance; for thou wast in communion with their most godlike brightness, with whom also thou rejoicest ever as a divine prophet, as a crowned martyr, as the leader of monastics.[^1933]

*Theotokion:*
Without seed thou didst conceive, O Virgin, the Word of God Who created all things, apart from carnal desires, and without corruption didst thou give birth, without maternal pangs; therefore, confessing thee with tongue and heart as Mother of God, we magnify thee.[^1934]

*Katavasia:*
In the shadow of the law and the scriptures, we faithful behold an image: every male that opens the womb is holy unto God; therefore the first-born Word of the unoriginate Father, the Son Who is the first-born of an unwedded Mother, do we magnify.[^1935]

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "O Changeless Light" (Свѣ́те неизмѣ́нный):*
Thou wast shown forth as a light of those of like mind, having taught the pious to walk in the paths of light, O Anthony, father of fathers: flashing forth anew the flame of lightning fire, and burning up the hosts of demons.[^1936] *(Twice)*

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
With unceasing hymns we call thee blessed, O Virgin, for thou didst bear One of the Trinity, O Mother of God, and didst carry in thy divine embrace the supersubstantial Word, immaterially and unchangeably.[^1937]

*At the Praises, Stichera on 4.*
*Tone 8, Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (Ѡ҆ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*
O venerable father Anthony, * taking the yoke of Christ upon thy shoulders, * thou didst manfully trample underfoot the assault of the enemy, * and didst show the deserts to be cities; * therefore we all honor thee in faith, * O all-blessed one, * boast of monastics, * incessantly pray unto Christ, that our souls may be saved.[^1938] *(Twice)*

*Sticheron:*
Having come together in faith, * we all honor thee, O Anthony, * as a faster of Christ; * for rejoicing, thou didst walk in the impassable desert, O wise one, * and wast an honorable guide therein. * Therefore in faith we cry unto thee: * O all-blessed one, * boast of monastics, * pray unto the Lord for us, * that our souls may be saved.[^1939]

*Sticheron:*
O venerable father Anthony, * for the sake of the true life * thou didst shut thyself up in a tomb, * fearing in no wise the invisible foes; * for once making blows they came unto thee, * yet by thy prayers thou didst reduce them to naught. * O patient of soul, * first leader of the desert: * therefore in faith we all honor and call thee blessed.[^1940]

*Glory... Tone 8:*
Having mounted the chariot of virtues coursing unto heaven, O marvelous one, thou didst reach the outer bounds through fasting, going round from the desert unto the beauteous things of the heavenly Jerusalem. And having worthily received the honors of thy painful ascetic labors, thou rejoicest with the heavenly ranks of angels, O all-blessed one, having become an heir of eternal blessings and a citizen of the Kingdom; but pray, O God-bearing Anthony, unto the Savior of all, to pacify the world and save our souls.[^1941]

*Both now... Theotokion:*
*O Lady, accept the prayers of thy servants...*

*The Great Doxology, and Dismissal.*

*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes from the Canon, Odes 3 and 6.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 7:* Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones.[^1942] *Verse: What shall I render unto the Lord for all that He hath rendered unto me?*

*Epistle to the Hebrews, Pericope 335 (Heb. 13:17-21).*

*Alleluia, Tone 6:* Blessed is the man that fears the Lord, in His commandments he will greatly delight.[^1943] *Verse: His seed shall be mighty upon the earth, the generation of the upright shall be blessed.*

*Gospel according to Luke, Pericope 24 (Lk. 6:17-23).*

*Communion Hymn:*
The righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance [Ps. 111:6].[^1944]

*In the same month, on the 18th day: Commemoration of our fathers among the saints, and Archbishops of Alexandria, Athanasius and Cyril.*[^1945]

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 6, Tone 4. Podoben: "As one valiant among martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*

*Sticheron:*
Thou didst endure persecutions * and undergo tribulations, * O God-proclaiming, venerable Athanasius, * until thou didst drive away * the godless deceit of Arius, * and didst save thy flock from impiety, * dogmatizing in orthodox manner * that the Son and the Spirit * are consubstantial with the Father, * O consecrated celebrant, * all-blessed one.[^1946]

*Sticheron:*
With the splendors of thy preaching * thou didst illuminate those in darkness, * and didst drive away all deceit, * contending boldly and firmly for the faith, O Athanasius, * as a true shepherd, * as an immovable foundation, * O glorious one, of the Church of Christ; * therefore having come together, * we honor thee, rejoicing in songs.[^1947]

*Sticheron:*
Thou wast disciplined in every virtue, * patiently, O God-inspired one, * and by the anointing of the Spirit, by the holy anointing, * thou wast clearly shown forth as a most sacred celebrant, * and a true shepherd, * and a champion of the faith; * therefore the whole Church glorifies thy memory, * sacredly celebrating it, * and glorifying the Savior.[^1948]

*Other Stichera of Saint Cyril, Tone and Podoben the same:*

*Sticheron:*
From the Church of Christ * thou didst drive away the noetic wolves, O Cyril, * with the staff of thy teachings, * and didst surround her about * with the fortifications of words; * and thou didst present her unto Christ immovable and unshakable. * Pray Him to deliver from corruption and perils * those who celebrate in faith * thy most honorable memory.[^1949]

*Sticheron:*
Having illumined thy mind with the splendors of the Spirit, * thou wast a light-beaming sun, * extending as rays of victory * unto all ends of the earth, * and illuminating * the fullness of the faithful, O all-blessed one, * and driving away the darkness of heresies, O God-bearer, * by the power of Him Who shone forth from the Virgin.[^1950]

*Sticheron:*
By the eloquence of thy words, O most sacred Cyril, * the whole Church is adorned, * and is devoutly embellished * with fair beauties; * and she sacredly honors * thy holy and renowned memory, O glorious one: * boast of the Orthodox, * foremost of the fathers assembled in council, * champion of the all-holy champion of the all-holy [Trinity].[^1951]

*Glory... Tone 6. By Germanus:*
Let us all hymn Christ's hierarch Athanasius, for he annulled all the opinions of Arius, and clearly proclaims the sovereignty of the Holy Trinity throughout the whole world, the one God in three undivided Persons: Whom also he entreats for us who celebrate his memory in faith.[^1952]

*Both now... Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "On the third day" (Трїдне́венъ):*
Beholding our Life hanging upon the Tree, * the all-immaculate Mother of God, * weeping maternally, cried aloud: * "O my Son and my God, * save those who praise Thee with love!"[^1953]

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos:*
*Glory... Tone 3. By Germanus:*
Again unto us the gold-flowing Nile, the namesake of immortality, coming in his yearly memory, with good ascents overflows with gold-streaming outpourings of immortality, and giving forth sweet nourishment by lofty divine proclamation, he teaches us to worship the undivided dominion of the Trinity; and welling forth divine teachings, he waters the thoughts of the faithful, and prays for our souls.[^1954]

*Both now... Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion:*
A sword pierced thy heart, O all-pure one, when thou didst behold thy Son upon the Cross, and didst cry aloud: "Make me not childless, O my Son and my God, Who didst preserve me a virgin after childbirth!"[^1955]

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
O God of our fathers, Who dealest ever with us according to Thy meekness: take not Thy mercy away from us, but by their prayers direct our life in peace.[^1956]

*Or this Troparion, Tone 3:*
Having shone forth by the works of Orthodoxy, and quenched all false glory, ye became victorious trophy-bearers, enriching all with piety, and greatly adorning the Church; worthily have ye found Christ God, Who grants unto us great mercy.[^1957]

*Both now... Theotokion.*

*At Matins: One Canon of the Octoechos, and two of the Saints.*
*One Canon of Saint Athanasius, its acrostic being: "Unto Athanasius praise of Orthodoxy is made." Composition of Theophanes.*
*Tone 8. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
The wonderworking rod of Moses, striking the sea in cruciform manner and dividing it of old, drowned Pharaoh, the driver of chariots, but saved Israel, the fugitive wayfarer, as he sang a hymn unto God.[^1958]

*Troparion:*
Offering praise unto Athanasius as praise unto virtue, I rather offer praise unto God, from Whom was given unto men the praiseworthy gift of virtue, of which he was the living image and seal.[^1959]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast full of divine wisdom, and having now shone forth more brightly than the sun through an angelic life, O blessed and venerable one, thou hast surpassed the bounds of praises from us; but accept them, O father, even though praised below thy worth.[^1960]

*Troparion:*
As is due, we weave a hymn in thy glorious memory, but falling short of greater things, O Athanasius, according to the worth of hymns due unto thee, we ask that forgiveness be given unto us, and through thee the abundant grace of the Spirit.[^1961]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst put to death the surge of carnal passions in youth, having acquired in thy youth elderly wisdom and steadfastness, O blessed Athanasius; for by the desire of the Wisdom of God thou didst direct thy senses.[^1962]

*Theotokion:*
Glorious things were spoken of thee from generation to generation, who didst contain God the Word in thy womb, yet remained pure, O Mother of God Mary; therefore we all honor thee, our protection after God.[^1963]

*Another Canon of Saint Cyril, its acrostic being: "Cyril is the flute of divine visions." Composition of John. Tone 4.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Having traversed the deep of the Red Sea with dryshod steps, ancient Israel of old conquered the power of Amalek in the wilderness by the cruciform hands of Moses.[^1964]

*Troparion:*
Having received light-giving grace from God, O Cyril, and been shown forth as a radiant luminary, thou didst shine upon us the spiritual rays of thy memory, that we may worthily sing of thee.[^1965]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast filled with the radiant manifestation of the Spirit, O wise Cyril, as a keeper of Christ's commandments; being cleansed of passions, thou wast truly a dwelling of the supremely divine Trinity.[^1966]

*Troparion:*
Being full of zeal and boldness, O glorious Cyril, thou didst truly refute all the God-fighters who babble with the tongues of wicked heresies, defending Orthodoxy.[^1967]

*Theotokion:*
One of the supremely divine Trinity didst thou bear, O all-immaculate Bride of God, Who appeared in flesh from thee like unto us, by the good will of the Father, and the cooperation of the All-Holy Spirit.[^1968]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
O Lord, Who in the beginning established the heavens with understanding, and founded the earth upon the waters: establish me, O Christ, upon the rock of Thy commandments; for there is none holy save Thee, O Thou Who alone lovest mankind.[^1969]

*Troparion:*
Having cleansed both soul and body from every defilement, O Athanasius, thou didst worthily show thyself a divine temple; therefore the fullness of the Trinity rested in thee, O all-blessed initiate of sacred mysteries.[^1970]

*Troparion:*
Finding thy soul cleansed of passions, as the grace of the Comforter desired, it clearly shows forth its workings in it, and sets thee forth, O father, as a most radiant luminary unto the world.[^1971]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast shown forth unto hierarchs as a rule of hierarchical ministry, and an exemplar of the active life; and thy word, O most wise one, clearly became an image of contemplation, and thy teaching the boundary of theology.[^1972]

*Theotokion:*
Higher than the Cherubim and Seraphim wast thou shown forth, O Mother of God; for thou alone, O undefiled one, didst receive the uncontainable God within thy womb; therefore with hymns, O pure one, all we faithful call thee blessed.[^1973]

*Another Canon. Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Thy Church rejoices in Thee, O Christ, crying: Thou art my strength, O Lord, and refuge and foundation![^1974]

*Troparion:*
Being strengthened in Christ, with steadfast mind, O Cyril, thou didst tear apart the snares of the subtle serpent like a spider's web.[^1975]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst shake off the mire of passions from thy soul, O Cyril, casting down every haughtiness of thoughts that exalts itself against Christ.[^1976]

*Troparion:*
As a victorious athlete, O father, thou didst steadfastly turn away from all carnal voluptuousness as corruptible and insidious.[^1977]

*Theotokion:*
Having been pre-purified in spirit, O pure one, thou didst give birth unto the Father's Word for the beneficence of rational nature.[^1978]

*Kontakion, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared today" (Ꙗ҆ви́лсѧ є҆сѝ):*
Supreme arch-hierarchs of piety and valiant champions of the Church of Christ, preserve all who sing: Save, O compassionate One, those who honor Thee in faith.[^1979]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 3, Podoben: "Awed by the beauty of thy virginity" (Красотѣ̀ дѣ́вства):*
Even as He Who pre-called thee pre-ordained, thou wast a pre-possession of immortality, having piously slain the Arian doctrines; for thou wast an unassailable champion of the truth, O father Athanasius, boast of the Orthodox. Therefore, singing of thee as is due, we celebrate we celebrate thy divine memory.[^1980]

*Glory... Of Saint Cyril, Tone and Podoben the same:*
Thou didst refute the deceit of heresies, and didst make clear the Orthodox faith, as one God-proclaiming and pious; thou didst preach in the world that one Godhead in Trinity is to be glorified, consubstantial in essence, and unconfused in Persons; therefore, having come together, O all-glorious Cyril, we honor thy memory.[^1981]

*Both now... Theotokion:*
Incomprehensible and past finding out, O Lady full of divine joy, is the awesome divine mystery wrought concerning thee; for having conceived the Uncircumscribed, thou didst give Him birth, clothed in flesh from thy most pure blood; Whom, O pure one, as thy Son, do thou ever entreat, that our souls may be saved.[^1982]

*Stavrotheotokion:*
The unwedded pure one and Thy Mother, O Christ, beholding Thee hanging dead upon the Cross, wept maternally and said: "What hath the lawless and ungrateful assembly of the Hebrews rendered unto Thee, which enjoyed Thy many and great gifts, O my Savior? I sing of Thy divine condescension."[^1983]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Thou art my strength, O Lord, Thou art also my power; Thou art my God, Thou art my rejoicing, Who left not the bosom of the Father, yet visited our poverty. Therefore with the Prophet Habbakuk I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind![^1984]

*Troparion:*
Lo, the life-bearing breath from on high breathed upon thee, which came in godlike manner from Christ's Spirit in the upper room and filled the disciples, showing thee forth, O father, as a thirteenth Apostle, preaching the Orthodox faith.[^1985]

*Troparion:*
Being greatly inflamed with divine zeal, thou didst assist in the Council, and before thou becamest the president, thou didst preach the Consubstantial in Nicaea; therefore Christ appointed thee chief shepherd and teacher of the Church.[^1986]

*Troparion:*
Having the helms of the Church committed unto thee by divine providence, O Athanasius, thou didst cut down all the soul-corrupting wordiness of heretics like an axe, and didst uproot it like thorns, and with wisdom didst cultivate the seed of the word unto fruitfulness.[^1987]

*Troparion:*
By thy fiery tongue the akin division of Arius was burned up, and the confusion of Sabellius, which are from boundless evil, equal in impiety, and with them every heretical blasphemy, O father Athanasius.[^1988]

*Theotokion:*

Thou art the boast of the faithful, O unwedded Bride; thou art the protectress, thou art the refuge of Christians, a rampart and a haven; for unto thy Son thou bearest supplications, O all-immaculate one, and dost save from perils those who with faith and love honor thee, knowing thee to be the Mother of God.[^1989]

*Another Canon. Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Beholding Thee lifted up upon the Cross, O Sun of Righteousness, the Church stood in her order, worthily crying aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^1990]

*Troparion:*
Seeing that thou hadst conquered soul-corrupting passions, and with the mind hadst mastered the flesh, O God-bearer Cyril, Christ appointed thee, O father, as president of His divine Church.[^1991]

*Troparion:*
As a beloved son thou didst inherit the paternal virtue of Mark, and becamest successor of his throne, following in the footsteps of the divine Evangelist.[^1992]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst shepherd thyself as a sheep of Christ, and as a shepherd thou didst tend the flock, O father, with thy soul-nourishing words as with grasses and flowers, abundantly feeding them with grace.[^1993]

*Theotokion:*
He Who brought all things out of nothingness by His divine power is born of thee, O Mother of God, illuminating the world with the bright rays of divinity and the splendor of the knowledge of God.[^1994]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Why hast Thou cast me away from Thy presence, O unsetting Light, and an alien darkness hath covered me, the wretched one? But turn me back, and unto the light of Thy commandments direct my ways, I pray.[^1995]

*Troparion:*
Having Christ speaking, O father, in the well-sounding instrument of thy tongue, thou didst put to shame the idol-like written heresy, instructing the straying and turning them unto the true God, O Athanasius.[^1996]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst refute all ruinous heresies, O father, by words and writings, casting out diverse deceit from the universe with wise demonstrations, and setting forth the Orthodox faith beyond contradiction, O blessed one.[^1997]

*Troparion:*
The Church of Christ truly proclaims thee a great teacher of wise teachers, O Athanasius, and counts thee with the Apostles, O father, as one who declares the blameless word of faith.[^1998]

*Theotokion:*
Having acquired maternal boldness toward thy Son, O all-pure one, despise not the kindred care of our race, we pray thee; for thee alone do we Christians mercifully offer unto the Master as a cleansing.[^1999]

*Another Canon. Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Thou, my Lord, art my light, and art come into the world, a holy light turning those who sing of Thee in faith from gloomy ignorance.[^2000]

*Troparion:*
Now beholding the face of Christ face to face, O Cyril, the mirrors being truly dissolved, thou art united unto Thy desire.[^2001]

*Troparion:*
Unto a violent torrent overflowing rivers, thy word, O Cyril, was likened, turning away the wiles of the ill-believing.[^2002]

*Troparion:*
Equally the abominable division of Arius, O Cyril, and the foul confusion of Sabellius, didst thou cast out from the deep.[^2003]

*Troparion:*
Wealth-producing words like gold hast thou left, O Cyril, and treasures like thy precious stones, unto the Church of Christ.[^2004]

*Theotokion:*
Thee do we set forth as an invincible weapon against foes; thee have we acquired, O Bride of God, as the confirmation and hope of our salvation.[^2005]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Cleanse me, O Savior, for my transgressions are many; and lead me up from the abyss of evils, I pray Thee; for unto Thee have I cried, and do Thou give ear unto me, O God of my salvation.[^2006]

*Troparion:*
Apollinarius having shown himself a sower of alien seed, depriving Christ of rational soul and human mind, was strongly refuted by thee, O all-blessed one, as foolish and corrupt of mind.[^2007]

*Troparion:*
Drawing waters of rational teachings poured forth from thy lips like from an ever-flowing fountain of grace, sweeter than honey, O venerable one, from a vessel let us faithful draw.[^2008]

*Troparion:*
Miriam marvels at the beauty of thy writings of divine teachings, lovingly receiving them, and prophetically foreseeing the heresies about to sprout forth being turned away by thee.[^2009]

*Theotokion:*
May we be delivered from grievous transgressions by thy supplications, O pure Mother of God, and may we obtain, O all-pure one, the divine illumination of the Son of God, ineffably incarnate of thee.[^2010]

*Another Canon. Ode 6. Heirmos:*
I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord, the Church cries unto Thee, having been cleansed from the blood of demons by the blood that flowed for mercy's sake from Thy side.[^2011]

*Troparion:*
As the Seraph with tongs gave the coal unto the Prophet, so unto the Church of Christ by thy hands, O initiate of sacred mysteries, dost thou impart the coal of cleansing from the divine fire.[^2012]

*Troparion:*
Not like Samson who destroyed neighboring Philistines, but thou didst cast down all alien heterodox teachings, and gavest dominion unto the Orthodox, O Cyril.[^2013]

*Troparion:*
Having clearly led the God-chosen Council, O father, thou didst cast down the impiety of Nestorius, that Christ-opposing audacity, breathing with zeal for the true Mother of God.[^2014]

*Theotokion:*
O wonder, the newest of all wonders! For a Virgin, having without husband conceived in the womb Him Who holds all things, did not restrain Him.[^2015]

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "The shedding of thy blood" (Крове́й твои́хъ):*
Having planted the teachings of Orthodoxy, thou didst cut down the thorns of false glory, multiplying the seed of faith by the rain of the Spirit, O venerable one; therefore we sing of thee, O Athanasius.[^2016]

*Ikos:*
Let us brethren today praise with hymns the all-festal memory of Athanasius and Cyril; for these men cast the deceitful Arius and Eunomius together with Sabellius into the abyss of their destruction, delivering them over unto the eternal fire to be burned, as having blasphemed unjustly against the Savior's Incarnation; therefore we sing of thee, O Athanasius.[^2017]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The fire of God's condescension was put to shame of old in Babylon; therefore the youths in the furnace with joyful step, as in a meadow of flowers, danced and sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^2018]

*Troparion:*
Having preached in orthodox manner the Word consubstantial and co-enthroned with the Father, the Only-begotten Son, O father namesake of immortality, thou straightway teachest that the Spirit is co-enthroned, consubstantial, and co-eternal.[^2019]

*Troparion:*
Beholding thee a consecrated teacher and proclaimer of the three-sun light, announcing the faith of Orthodoxy unto the ends of the earth, the father of impiety raised up exiles against thee.[^2020]

*Troparion:*
Boundless were the perils which thou didst endure, O blessed one, contending for piety, and equally radiant are thy crowns; for thou wast an adamant unto those striking thee, and unto thyself like a magnet thou didst draw all.[^2021]

*Troparion:*
Strange dogmas and things alien to the Church of Christ thou didst cast out, theologizing the Trinity in Hypostases and Monad in Godhead, unto Whom thou didst sing: Blessed is the God of our fathers![^2022]

*Theotokion:*
Now are all things filled with divine light through thee, O all-pure one; for thou wast shown forth as the door through which God conversed with the world, illuminating those who call out in faith: Blessed is the God of our fathers![^2023]

*Another Canon. Ode 7. Heirmos:*
In the Persian furnace, Abraham's children, burned by love of piety rather than by the flame, cried aloud: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord![^2024]

*Troparion:*
Entering into the darkness upon Mount Sinai of old, Moses received the law, O blessed Cyril, which kills by the letter; but thou didst unfold the hidden beauty of the Spirit.[^2025]

*Troparion:*
By the riddles of the giving of the Law, as unto infants of old, O father, given as a covering veil, thou didst unveil the shadows of understanding, explaining the types most clearly.[^2026]

*Troparion:*
Being inspired by grace, O Cyril, thou didst purely reveal unto us the difficult-to-understand books of the God-proclaiming and God-receiving Prophets, filled with the Spirit Who filled them.[^2027]

*Troparion:*
In unconfused divine union and clearly indivisible division, O father, theologizing three Hypostases, thou didst declare, O Cyril, that They are immutable in one essence and Godhead.[^2028]

*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, O sanctified divine dwelling of the Most High! For through thee was joy given unto those who cry aloud: Blessed art thou among women, O all-immaculate Lady![^2029]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
The Chaldean tyrant furiously heated the furnace sevenfold for the pious; but seeing them saved by a higher power, he cried unto the Creator and Deliverer: Ye youths, bless; ye priests, sing; ye people, exalt Him above all unto all ages![^2030]

*Troparion:*
Glorious adornment of hierarchs, O Athanasius, radiant pillar and confirmation of the Church, champion of the Trinity, golden trumpet of theology, certain lawgiver of monastic life: thou feastest with us, perfecting the priests, and leading the faithful people unto Christ unto all ages.[^2031]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast truly the namesake of immortality, for thou didst surpass those of active virtue in word, and didst surpass those skilled in word by the certainty of thy life, attaining the heights in both; therefore, having blossomed with ever-living virtue, thou hast acquired immortal memory unto all ages.[^2032]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst show forth a most radiant hierarchical ministry, O heavenly initiate acceptable unto God, by thy noble sufferings; and thou didst drive away deceit by thy frequent exiles for the sake of the Trinity, Whom preaching, thou didst cry aloud: Let us worship the Father worship the Father, bless the Son, and praise the Spirit unto all ages.[^2033]

*Theotokion:*
Unceasingly let us sing of her who gave birth in the flesh unto God, One of the Trinity, and after childbirth remained whole again, as higher than the Cherubim and more honorable than the Seraphim, crying aloud: Ye youths, bless; ye priests, sing; ye people, exalt Him above all unto all ages![^2034]

*Another Canon. Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Daniel, stretching out his hands, stopped the mouths of the lions in the pit; and the youths, lovers of piety, girded with virtue, quenched the power of the fire, crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^2035]

*Troparion:*
Truly like a wave of the sea the fountain of wisdom poured forth in thee; for ever-flowing rivers of pious teachings flowed from thy belly, O father, as Christ foretold; for thy God-proclaiming words surpass the sand.[^2036]

*Troparion:*
Having been shown forth as a wise shepherd and teacher of the Church, O venerable Cyril, thou didst clearly explain both Testaments; for having thy words as a jacinth stone and paternal heritage, she cries: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^2037]

*Troparion:*
Concerning the all-artful Word Who became incarnate for our sake, thou teachest His ineffable union, O Cyril: indivisible and unconfused, equally turning away from every inclination [to heresy], crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^2038]

*Theotokion:*
He Who was first the Word from the Father without a mother became second from thee without a father, O all-pure one; He Who was formerly bodiless, having become incarnate in His loving-kindness, desiring to save those who sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^2039]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Heaven was dismayed at this, and the ends of the earth were astonished, that God appeared unto men in the flesh, and thy womb became more spacious than the heavens; therefore the ranks of angels and men magnify thee as Mother of God.[^2040]

*Troparion:*
Thy life flashed forth like lightning, and thy proclamation was poured out unto all like thunder, O father, which the sun surveys; for thou hadst inspiration truly from heaven from on high; therefore the grave, the promoter of oblivion, hath not extinguished thy memory, O Athanasius.[^2041]

*Troparion:*
Now most clearly illuminated by the three-sun and tri-radiant Light, thou revealest ray-like illumination unto thy hymnographers, emitting it from on high like a mirror from the sun; and unto those who have left unto thee manifestations, O blessed one, even though that which is asked be great and exceeding our worth.[^2042]

*Troparion:*
Singing, we fervently entreat thee: pray for the Church, to grant victories by the Cross unto the King,[^2043] and strength unto the Orthodox faith against the heresies of foes, and salvation unto us, and peace unto the world, in thy memory, O Athanasius.[^2044]

*Theotokion:*
Without seed, O Virgin, didst thou conceive God the Word Who created all things, apart from carnal desires; and apart from corruption didst thou give Him birth, and without maternal pangs; therefore, confessing thee with tongue and heart as Mother of God, we magnify thee.[^2045]

*Another Canon. Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Eve indeed by the disease of disobedience brought in the curse; but thou, O Virgin Mother of God, by the blossoming of thy bearing in the womb, didst blossom forth blessing unto the world; therefore we all magnify thee.[^2046]

*Troparion:*
Every haughtiness exalting itself against the knowledge of Christ and of His Mother, O Cyril, thou didst strongly cast down: the godless duality of sons of Nestorius, as well as the confusion of headless natures.[^2047]

*Troparion:*
By the power of understanding and the illumination of grace, thou didst theologize the consubstantial Trinity, and the Son as God incarnate, O blessed one; and having been shown forth as a champion of the Mother of God, thou art now glorified in the highest.[^2048]

*Troparion:*
From on high thou dost mercifully survey us who sing thy praises, O father mindful of hymnody: granting victories unto the cross-bearing King,[^2049] and by thy prayers exalting the horn of the Orthodox, and enlightening those who magnify thy memory.[^2050]

*Theotokion:*
Show my heart, which is barren of divine virtues, O all-pure Mother of God, to be fruitful, O Virgin who wast born from a barren woman by the nod of Him Who transforms all things by His will, that I may sing of thee, the much-hymned one.[^2051]

*Exapostilarion of the Octoechos.*

*Glory... Of the Saints:*
Ye were shown forth as all-wise initiates and champions of the supremely divine Trinity, O blessed Athanasius and God-blessed Cyril, having cast down Arius, and with him Sabellius, and straightway the impious Nestorius, and with them every other deceit of impious heresies, O hierarchs of the Lord.[^2052]

*Both now... Theotokion:*
With boldness to proclaim the Mother of God, and that she is truly to be worshiped by the faithful, dost thou teach, O all-blessed Cyril, having destroyed the godless deceit of Nestorius.[^2053]

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos:*

*Then this refrain:*
*Verse: Thy priests shall be clothed with righteousness, and Thy venerable ones shall rejoice [Ps. 131:9 LXX].*

*Sticheron, Tone 2:*
Let us in sacred manner praise the great renown of the consecrated ones, Athanasius and Cyril, the unconquerable defenders; for cutting through the ranks of heresies by the power of the All-Holy Spirit, they raised up victories for Orthodoxy throughout all the universe: piously reckoning the mystery of the Trinity by the proper characteristics of Persons, and again joining Them into one unconfusedly by identity of essence, and theologizing in the manner of the Cherubim; they pray unceasingly for our souls.[^2054]

*Glory... Tone the same. By Germanus:*
The great trumpet of truth, the much-suffering Athanasius, summons the Church today unto a feast; let all we faithful brightly hasten to the solemnity of the good shepherd, honoring with hymns his sacred labors, that by his prayers we may receive great mercy from Christ God.[^2055]

*Both now... Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "Great is the power" (Ве́лїѧ):*
Beholding Him Who was born of thee hanging upon the Tree, O all-immaculate one, thou didst cry aloud, weeping: "O my most beloved Child, where hath Thy light-bearing beauty departed, Who hast adorned the human race?"[^2056]

*At the Liturgy:*
*The Beatitudes from the Canon of Saint Athanasius, Ode 3, and from the Canon of Saint Cyril, Ode 6.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 8:* The venerable ones shall boast in glory, and shall rejoice upon their beds [Ps. 149:5 LXX].[^2057] *Verse: Sing unto the Lord a new song, His praise is in the church of the venerable ones [Ps. 149:1 LXX].*

*Epistle to the Hebrews, Pericope 334 (Heb. 13:7-16).*

*Alleluia, Tone 2:* Thy priests shall be clothed with righteousness, and Thy venerable ones shall rejoice [Ps. 131:9 LXX].[^2058]

*Gospel according to Matthew, Pericope 11 (Mt. 5:14-19).*

*Communion Hymn:*
Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous: praise is seemly for the upright [Ps. 32:1 LXX].[^2059]

*In the same month, on the 19th day: Commemoration of our venerable father Macarius of Egypt.*[^2060]

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 6, Tone 4. Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*

*Sticheron:*
Desiring sacred blessedness beyond the mind, * O marvelous one, thou didst account * fasting as food, * poverty as riches, * non-possessiveness as true wealth, * and humility as glorious renown. * Therefore thou didst obtain the desire * which is according to understanding, * dwelling in the habitations of the saints, O Macarius.[^2061]

*Sticheron:*
Thou didst unswervingly finish the course of abstinence, * and didst keep the faith; * therefore also thou didst receive the crown of righteousness, O father, * which Christ prepared for thee, * according to worth granting recompense, * and honors of gifts, * and reward for thy toils. * Pray Him now to grant these unto us, O glorious one.[^2062]

*Sticheron:*
Subduing thy body, O God-wise one, * Thou didst cast away all voluptuousness, * mortifying the senses by rigorous abstinence and austerity of life, * by endurance of temptations, and patient waiting through tribulations; * for the sake of which Thou receivest unending delight, * and ceaseless nourishment, * and ineffable joy.[^2063]

*Glory... Tone 8. By Anatolius:*
Rejoice, O Egypt, who hast blossomed forth such a citizen among the blessed, Macarius; for he, being adorned with the wisdom of the Holy Spirit, brought forth every fruit of fasting in his virtuous life. Bringing him forward as our intercessor, we ask him to entreat Christ that our souls may be saved.[^2064]

*Both now... Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "Thy Martyrs, O Lord" (Мꙋ́ченицы твоѝ гдⷭ҇и):*
The undefiled Heifer, beholding the Bullock voluntarily nailed upon the Tree, weeping piteously, cried aloud: "Woe is me, O most beloved Child! What hath the ungrateful Hebrew gathering rendered unto Thee, desiring to make me childless of Thee, O dearly beloved?"[^2065]

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos:*

*Glory... Tone 6:*
O venerable father, into all the earth went out the sound of thy righteous deeds; therefore in the heavens thou hast found the reward of thy labors, thou didst destroy the hosts of demons, and didst attain the angelic ranks, whose life thou didst blamelessly[^2066] emulated blamelessly; having boldness before Christ God, entreat peace for our souls.[^2067]

*Both now... Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "On the third day" (Трїдне́венъ):*
Beholding our Life hanging upon the Tree, O all-immaculate Mother of God, weeping maternally thou didst cry aloud: "O my Son and my God, save those who sing of Thee with love."[^2068]

*Troparion, Tone 1:*
A dweller of the wilderness, and in the body an angel, and a wonderworker wast thou shown forth, O God-bearing father our Macarius: having received heavenly gifts through fasting, vigilance, and prayer, thou healest the sick, and the souls of those who run unto thee in faith. Glory to Him Who gave thee strength! Glory to Him Who crowned thee! Glory to Him Who through thee works healings for all![^2069]

*At Matins, both Canons of the Octoechos, and the Canon of the Saint on 6.*
*Its acrostic: "I praise Macarius, excellent among the fasters." By Theophanes, Tone 4.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
The choir of Israel, with unwetted steps passing through the Red Sea and the watery depth, and beholding the enemy captains and horsemen submerged therein, sang with joy: Let us sing unto our God, for He hath been glorified![^2070]

*Troparion:*
Shining with divine light, and now dwelling with the angels, O father, by thy prayers save those who celebrate thy most sacred memory, and in joy cry aloud: Let us sing unto our God, for He hath been glorified![^2071]

*Troparion:*
Walking unswervingly, O venerable one, thou didst complete the way leading unto life. Thou didst flee turmoil, and didst dispel demonic confusions, crying out joyfully: Let us sing unto our God, for He hath been glorified![^2072]

*Troparion:*
Having mortified carnal wisdom by thy fasting struggles, thou didst subject it unto the Divine Spirit, O father; and being guided by His divine power, in joy thou didst cry aloud: Let us sing unto our God, for He hath been glorified![^2073]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst forsake all beautiful things, having loved, O father, the unending beauty in the house of the Lord, where is the voice of those who purely keep festival, crying aloud in joy: Let us sing unto our God, for He hath been glorified![^2074]

*Theotokion:*
Having conceived in thy womb, O pure one, the timeless Son of the unoriginate Father Who for the sake of us men became flesh, in the fullness of time thou didst give Him birth, knowing not a man; unto Whom also rejoicing we sing: Let us sing unto our God, for gloriously hath He been glorified![^2075]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
The bow of the mighty hath grown weak, and the feeble have girded themselves with strength; therefore my heart is established in the Lord.[^2076]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst submit unto the law of the Spirit, girding thyself with His panoply, O venerable one, and didst not bow thy will unto the law of sin.[^2077]

*Troparion:*
Having thy mind on high toward God, O God-bearer, thou didst leave behind the things upon earth, being unceasingly unburdened by the labors of abstinence.[^2078]

*Troparion:*
Having sundered the bonds of nature by thy supernatural and pure life, O God-bearer, thou didst receive the operation of things that are beyond nature.[^2079]

*Troparion:*
That thou mightest converse with God in tranquility, O blessed one, thou didst choose to dwell in the wilderness, O father, withdrawing far from tumults.[^2080]

*Theotokion:*
Desiring to save man for that which is profitable, as the Benefactor and Lover of mankind, He dwelt uncircumscribably within thy womb, O Mother of God.[^2081]

*Kontakion, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared" (Ꙗ҆ви́лсѧ є҆сѝ):*
In the house of abstinence the Lord truly set thee as an unerring star, guiding with light the ends of the earth, O venerable father Macarius.[^2082]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thy tomb, O Savior" (Гро́бъ тво́й сп҃се):*
Having been tried by the fire of abstinence like gold in a furnace, O wise one, thou wast shown forth most radiant; therefore thou hast departed unto the heavenly Kingdom. Therefore, praising thee in faith, we cry aloud: Entreat grace, mercy, and cleansing of our transgressions, O father. *Twice.*[^2083]

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
Direct us onto the way of repentance, who have ever turned aside unto pathless evils and provoked the all-good Lord to anger, O unwedded, blessed Mary, refuge of desperate men, dwelling-place of God.[^2084]

*Stavrotheotokion:*
The undefiled Ewe-lamb, beholding the Lamb and Shepherd hanging dead upon the Tree, weeping said, crying aloud maternally: "How shall I endure Thy condescension which is beyond speech, O my Son, and Thy voluntary sufferings, O all-good God?"[^2085]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
He Who sits in glory upon the throne of the Godhead, Jesus the most divine, came upon a swift cloud, and by His incorrupt hand saved those who cry: Glory to Thy power, O Christ![^2086]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst straightway put off the corrupt old man, O father, with sinful passions by guiltless abstinence, and didst put on put on the new man in Christ, O all-honorable one.[^2087]

*Troparion:*
Thy most radiant life was shown forth as a most certain rule of every divine virtue, O father, in watchings and fastings, in vigils and supplications unto Christ the Lover of mankind.[^2088]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst not give slumber unto thine eyelids, O God-wise one, until, O father, thou didst make thyself a most beautiful house for the all-seeing Master, unto Whom thou didst cry: Glory to Thy power, O Christ![^2089]

*Troparion:*
From youth chastity, in old age understanding, and throughout all thy life patience and long-suffering, and love toward all didst thou show forth unto those who cry: Glory to Thy power, O Christ![^2090]

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst give life unto slain men, O all-immaculate one, and didst raise up those fallen into corruption, having given birth unto the Giver of life Who delivers those who cry: Glory to Thy power, O Christ![^2091]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Send down Thy light unto us, O Lord, and loose us from the gloom of transgressions, O Good One, granting Thy peace.[^2092]

*Troparion:*
Extending the noetic part of the soul, O glorious one, and wisely governing the senses, thou becamest a temple consecrated unto God, and all-honorable.[^2093]

*Troparion:*
Having exposed the crafty designs of the most tortuous serpent, thou didst blunt his bitter wiles, ever ordering thy soul in the divine law.[^2094]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst adorn the three-part nature of the soul, O venerable one, and setting the intellect as master, thou hadst Christ guiding thee unto heavenly life.[^2095]

*Theotokion:*
The good and all-pure one gave birth unto God, Who gives as law purity unto all, and proclaims the holiness of piety unto those upon earth.[^2096]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Prefiguring the three-day burial, the Prophet Jonah cried aloud, praying in the sea-monster: Deliver me from corruption, O Jesus, King of powers![^2097]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst fervently love to live in the wilderness, O God-bearer, receiving therein God Who delivers thee and preserves thy steps.[^2098]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst remain unbending in fasting, O God-wise one, keeping this strictness even unto the end, through which thou wast clearly accounted worthy of incorrupt delight.[^2099]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst live an angelic life upon earth, and didst worthily receive honor equal to the angels, standing before the God of all with the angels.[^2100]

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst conceive in thy womb, O Mother of God, the unoriginate God the Word, Who for the sake of us men became man, immutable according to our nature, known in two natures.[^2101]

*Kontakion, Tone 1, Podoben: "The choir of angels" (Ли́къ а҆́гглскїй):*
Having finished a blessed life in thy living, together with the choirs of martyrs thou dost worthily dwell in the land of the meek, O God-bearing Macarius; and having populated the wilderness as a city, thou didst receive from God the grace of wonders; therefore we honor thee.[^2102]

*Ikos:*
Having become truly a close disciple of the God-bearing Antony, O father, like wax thou didst portray his virtue and sufferings in truth. Therefore, as unto Elijah a double portion, so unto thee as another Elisha was given the grace of wonders, and having obtained the apprehension of the truth of foreknowledge, the record of thy life was set forth in all the world, raising up those who sleep in the abyss of perdition. Therefore we honor thee.[^2103]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
Thou Who didst save Thy Abrahamic youths in the fire, and didst slay the Chaldeans whom justice caught unexpectedly: O supremely praised Lord God of our fathers, blessed art Thou![^2104]

*Troparion:*
Having cast down the foes by a nod from on high and by the help of God, thou wast a victor, crying aloud: O supremely praised Lord God of our fathers, blessed art Thou![^2105]

*Troparion:*
Having cleansed the gloom caused by passions, thou wast illumined by the enlightenment of dispassion, crying, O blessed one: O supremely praised Lord God of our fathers, blessed art Thou![^2106]

*Troparion:*
Having made radiant thy soul with the splendors of virtues, becoming fair in beauty unto God, rejoicing thou didst sing: O supremely praised Lord God of our fathers, blessed art Thou![^2107]

*Theotokion:*
Calling us who were captive unto that which we were in the beginning, having dwelt within thy womb, He became incarnate, the Lord God of our fathers, the Lover of mankind, Who is blessed.[^2108]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
The Offspring of the Mother of God saved the pious youths in the furnace. What was then prefigured, now being fulfilled, raises up the whole universe to sing unto Thee: Bless the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him above all unto all ages![^2109]

*Troparion:*
Having received the words of eternal life in thy heart, O all-blessed one, thou didst wither the flesh; thou wast deadened unto the world, and clothed in life-bearing deadness, crying out: Bless the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him above all unto all ages![^2110]

*Troparion:*
Entreat the only Benefactor to be merciful, O God-bearer, unto those who celebrate thy most sacred memory, asking remission of sins for them: Bless the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him above all unto all ages![^2111]

*Troparion:*
Attending with unceasing contemplation unto God, and receiving the ray of the splendor from thence, like a mirror thou sendest back shining light unto those who look forward, crying: Bless the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him above all unto all ages![^2112]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst ascend, O father, upon the ladder extended unto heaven, upon which the Lord was revealed standing fast, ever advancing by divine ascents, O venerable one, until thou didst reach those who sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him above all unto all ages![^2113]

*Theotokion:*
We sing of thee, O full of grace, for thou didst give birth unto God incarnate for us; therefore we all name thee Mother of God, the God-receiving table, the beauty of Jacob, crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him above all unto all ages![^2114]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Eve indeed brought in the curse through the sickness of disobedience; but thou, O Virgin Mother of God, through the bud of thy bearing in the womb, didst blossom forth blessing unto the world; therefore we all magnify thee.[^2115]

*Troparion:*
With ascetic tears thou didst water the field of thy heart, and rejoicing now in joy, O God-bearing father, thou gatherest the sheaves of honors for thy struggles; therefore we all call thee blessed.[^2116]

*Troparion:*
The unwaning light shone forth unto thee, and everlasting joy received thee, where dancing with the angels around the King and Lord, be mindful of those who celebrate thy memory in faith, O all-blessed father.[^2117]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast able to escape the shooting of demons and their deceitful wiles; thy soul was saved, O blessed one, holy, pure, and undefiled, and was accounted worthy of incorrupt inheritance; be mindful therefore of those who sing of thee.[^2118]

*Troparion:*
According to the law of contestants, O father, thou didst struggle worthily, and didst conquer; therefore the only Benefactor honored thee with a crown of glory, and accounted thee worthy of divine illumination and of blessed delights.[^2119]

*Theotokion:*
As having given birth unto the Creator of all creation, O Mother of God, thou didst surpass all creation in divine glory, and holiness, and grace, and preeminence of every virtue; therefore we all magnify thee.[^2120]

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "O Thou Who hast adorned the heaven with stars" (Не́бо ѕвѣзда́ми):*
Desiring an angelic life, thou didst withdraw thyself into the wilderness and having subdued the carnal passions, thou wast shown forth equal to the angels, O our God-bearing father.[^2121]

*Theotokion:*
By thy mighty protection, O pure one, preserve all of us thy servants unhurt from the assault of enemies; for thee alone have we as a refuge in necessities.[^2122]

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos:*

*Glory... Tone 4:*
Thy good deeds shone forth like the sun, upon earth and in heaven, O Macarius, pleaser of Christ; for in orthodox manner thou didst preach unto us the true and blameless faith of Christ. Therefore pray, O venerable father, in thy memory, O God-bearer, to grant us great mercy.[^2123]

*Both now... Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "As noble among the martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*
When she who gave Thee birth, the Ewe-lamb, * beheld Thee, the Lamb and Shepherd, upon the Tree, * she wept and maternally said unto Thee: * "O my beloved Son, * how art Thou suspended upon the Wood of the Cross, O longsuffering One? * How were Thy hands and feet nailed by the lawless, O Word? * And how didst Thou pour out Thy blood, O Master?"[^2124]

*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the Octoechos on 4, and of the Saint, Ode 6, on 4; and the entire service of this month, on the 15th day.*[^2125]

*In the same month, on the 20th day: Commemoration of our venerable and God-bearing father Euthymius the Great.*[^2126]

*If the superior wills: We celebrate a Vigil.*[^2127]

*At Little Vespers, Stichera on 4, Tone 1. Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Нбⷭ҇ныхъ чинѡ́въ):*

*Sticheron:*
Soaring above lower circles * by divine virtue, O all-blessed father, * thou didst enter into the darkness, * whereby truly not in enigmas, O venerable one, * but in divine grace thou wast shown forth, * receiving splendors. *Twice.*[^2128]

*Sticheron:*
Having enlightened soul and intellect with virtues, * thou didst depart unto heaven into the Kingdom of Christ, * O thrice-blessed Euthymius, * bringing unto Him the sheaves of thy labors; * having shone forth among the ascetics like a beacon, * thou dost enjoy unaging enjoy unaging nourishment.[^2129]

*Sticheron:*
The consubstantial, truly unoriginate Trinity, * having placed in thee a dwelling of the Spirit, * showed thee forth as a most radiant beacon, * O God-bearing Euthymius; * having passed beyond all things that drag downward, * thou hast found a dwelling in the heavens.[^2130]

*Glory... Tone 2:*
O venerable father, having from infancy diligently trained in virtue, * thou wast an instrument of the Holy Spirit; and receiving from Him the operation of wonders, thou didst persuade men to despise sweet things. And now, being more purely illumined by divine light, enlighten also our thoughts, O father Euthymius.[^2131]

*Both now... Theotokion.*

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*

*Sticheron:*
Having exposed the deceit * of evil demons * by the power of the Cross, * thou didst make clear the glory of Christ, * O father Euthymius.[^2132]

*Verse: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones [Ps. 115:6 LXX].*

*Sticheron:*
Thou didst ascend like Elijah * upon a fiery chariot, * and thou standest, O blessed one, * immediately before the Trinity, * O most fair Euthymius.[^2133]

*Verse: Blessed is the man that fears the Lord, he shall delight exceedingly in His commandments [Ps. 111:1 LXX].*

*Sticheron:*
