Bearing in thy hands * the Cross of the Lord, O father, * thou didst utterly destroy demonic illusions, * O Euthymius.[^2134]

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion, Podoben: "House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
Rejoice, * thou who didst receive the Joy of the world, * Christ the Giver of life, * and didst put an end to the grief * of our first mother, O Virgin.[^2135]

*At Great Vespers, we sing "Blessed is the man," the 1st antiphon.*

*At "Lord, I have cried," we set 8 verses, and sing Stichera, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant among the martyrs" (Всехва́льнїи мч҃нцы):*

*Sticheron:*
O father Euthymius, * a sent heavenly angel foreannounced thy birth, * as that of John who sprouted from a barren womb; * for thou wast shown forth as his emulator * and fellow-citizen: * homeless, possessing nothing, * like the Baptist, * and nourished in the mountains, * shining with measureless wonders.[^2136]

*Sticheron:*
O father Euthymius, * thou didst sprout forth indeed as the fruit of barrenness, * yet wast shown forth truly fruitful with many children; * for by thy spiritual seed * the wilderness, formerly impassable, was filled with monks. * And now pray * to grant unto our souls * peace and great mercy.[^2137]

*Sticheron:*
O father Euthymius, * thy life is most excellent, * and thy faith truly orthodox; * for from action * thou didst attain unto the highest contemplation, * having become a dwelling of wisdom, * honoring Christ, One of the Trinity, in two natures; * entreat Him * for our souls our souls.[^2138]

*Sticheron:*
O father Euthymius, * having become a partaker of the sufferings * of Him Who was stretched upon the Cross, * thou by fasting * wast truly conformed unto His Resurrection and glory. * Pray Him now * to grant unto our souls * peace and great mercy.[^2139]

*Other Stichera, Tone 4, Podoben: "Called from on high" (Зва́нный свы́ше):*

*Sticheron:*
Sanctified from thy mother's womb, * when the all-seeing Eye * foresaw thy purpose and reverence * leading unswervingly unto the better things, * then, O all-blessed one, a God-given gift, * named after good cheer, thou wast announced, * loosing the grief of thy parents; * therefore, brought forth from infancy, * thou didst please God the Benefactor. * Entreat Him * to save and enlighten our souls. *Twice.*[^2140]

*Sticheron:*
Full of divine gifts, * Christ, having found thee, O father, as an undefiled mirror * of divine manifestations, * flashed forth unto thee with the bright splendor of His light; * whence thou wast shown forth an abundant fountain of healings, * and a nourisher of the hungry, * watering with showers the desire of those who thirst, * and beholding the pledges of the soul, * by thy word thou didst wisely make them better unto God; * entreat Him to save and enlighten our souls.[^2141]

*Sticheron:*
Having shone forth by contemplation and action, * thy angelic life was a rule of virtue * and a most certain model * for those who choose to serve God in perfection; * and thy God-wise word, O Euthymius, * taught men to honor the Trinity, * and Christ recognized as One in two natures, * and councils equal in number * to the quaternary of Christ's Gospels. * Entreat Him * to save and enlighten our souls.[^2142]

*Glory... Tone 6:*
Sanctified unto God from thy mother's womb, like another Samuel, O father Euthymius, according to thy name thou wast the good cheer of the faithful, and the staff and confirmation of monks, a pure dwelling of the Holy Spirit: entreat for us who honor thee great mercy.[^2143]

*Both now... Theotokion: "Who would not marvel" (Ка́кѡ не диви́мся):*[^2144]

*Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day, and 3 Readings: Written for this month on the 15th day.*[^2145]

*At the Litiya, Stichera, Tone 2, Idiomela: By Germanus:*

*Sticheron:*
Be of good cheer, said the angel of the Lord unto the parents, for a child shall be born unto you from your loins named after good cheer and thou wast conceived in the womb, dispelling their sorrow; and from swaddling clothes thou wast nurtured by thy mother, O father Euthymius.[^2146]

*By Studite:*
Having strengthened thy mind with divine understanding, O father Euthymius, thou didst pass through transient things, in nowise marveling at earthly things; in tribulations indeed thou wast shown forth magnanimous and most valiant, and in fasting and good cheer humble and meek. And having clearly sailed across the unstable deep of this present life, reaching the fair and calm haven, entreat Christ to have mercy on our souls.[^2147]

*Sticheron:*
Thou didst despise the things that exist in this life, O father Euthymius, as one who desired the life above; thou didst abhor riches, and didst clothe thyself in humility; thou didst hate luxury, and didst embrace abstinence; thou didst cast away unrighteousness, and didst pursue righteousness. Therefore, O venerable father, be mindful also of us in thy venerable prayers unto the Lord.[^2148]

*Glory... Tone 4:*
Thy good deeds shone forth like the sun, upon earth and in heaven, O Euthymius, pleaser of Christ; for in orthodox manner thou didst preach unto us the true and blameless faith of Christ. Therefore pray, O venerable father, in thy memory, O God-bearer, to grant us great mercy.[^2149]

*Both now... Theotokion: "Look upon the entreaties" (При́зри на моле́нїа):*[^2150]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 5, Podoben: "Rejoice, guide of ascetics" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ по́стникѡвъ):*

*Sticheron:*
Rejoice, for thou becamest the beginning of good cheer for the Church, O venerable father; for by thy birth all heretical assaults were repulsed by the providence of God. Therefore she names thee Euthymius, corresponding to thy name. Thou didst fill the ranks of heavenly beings with joy by the brightness of thy life; dwelling with them, and being filled with light, and enjoying all-blessed and divine illumination, entreat Christ now to give great mercy unto our souls.[^2151]

*Verse: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones [Ps. 115:6 LXX].*

*Sticheron:*
Being strengthened by the staff of the Cross, thou didst dry up the torrents of lawlessness; and being noetically watered, O all-blessed one, by the torrent of divine delight and the fountain of Paradise, thou didst show forth saving fountains in the wilderness. And being fattened by the streams of the Holy Spirit, O venerable one, like a palm tree thou didst ascend unto the heavenly height, and wast shown forth as a pillar of fire, O God-wise one, and full of light-bearing splendor. Entreat Christ therefore to give great mercy unto our souls.[^2152]

*Verse: Blessed is the man that fears the Lord, he shall delight exceedingly in His commandments [Ps. 111:1 LXX].*

*Sticheron:*
Truly unto the marvelous tabernacle, even unto the house of God, O all-blessed one, thou didst pass with rejoicing and gladness of soul, where hearing the fair sound of those who keep festival, O father, and partaking of sweet singing and ineffable delight and beauty, O Euthymius, desiring Him alone thou didst mortify the flesh, which also thou didst obtain, being adorned with divine righteousness; entreat Christ Who grants great mercy unto the world.[^2153]

*Glory... Tone the same:*
O venerable father, thou didst not give sleep unto thine eyes, nor slumber unto thine eyelids, until thou didst free soul and body from passions, and preparedst thyself a dwelling of the Spirit; for Christ coming with the Father made an abode in thee; and having become a servant of the consubstantial Trinity, O great proclaimer, our father Euthymius, pray for our souls.[^2154]

*Both now... Theotokion: "We bless thee, O Virgin Mother of God" (Бл҃жи́мъ тѧ̀ бцⷣе дв҃о):*[^2155]

*At the Blessing of Loaves, Troparion, Tone 4:*
Rejoice, O barren wilderness that barest not, be of good cheer, thou that travailest not; for the man of spiritual desires multiplied thy children, having planted them in piety and nurtured them in abstinence unto perfection of virtues. By his prayers, O Christ God, give peace unto our life. *Twice.*[^2156]

*Birthgiver of God, Virgin, rejoice... Once.*[^2157]

*At Matins, at "God is the Lord," Troparion of the Saint, twice.*

*Glory... Both now... The mystery hidden from all eternity:*[^2158]

*After the 1st Stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared today" (Ꙗ҆ви́лся є҆сѝ дне́сь):*
Shining with unapproachable light, like a star thou didst shine forth in the wilderness, enlightening with teachings, O Euthymius, those who draw near unto thee with an undoubting soul. *Twice.*[^2159]

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*
Receiving from us the supplication of those who flee unto thy protection, O all-immaculate Virgin, cease not to pray unto the Lover of mankind to save thy servants.[^2160]

*After the 2nd Stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 5, Podoben: "Co-unoriginate Word" (Собезна́чальное сло́во):*
Having cast away the cares of life and received the angelic life, by abstinence thou didst adorn thy soul[^2161] thou didst, and didst richly receive from God the grace of miracles, O God-bearing Euthymius, praying for us who piously praise thee.
*Twice.*

*Glory, and now, Theotokion:*
Ever have mercy on us, who flee with faith unto thee, the compassionate, and ask for Thy fervent protection; for thou canst save all things, as good, being the Mother of the Most High God, ever offering Thy maternal prayers, O full of God's grace.

*After the Polyeleos, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom and the Word" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
Having received the poverty of Him Who was truly born for our sake, thou didst count temporal things as grass, O blessed one; for having tasted of the intelligible tree, O venerable one, thou didst show thyself to be a divine teacher of monastics. Therefore thou didst rouse all men to the zeal of the angelic way of life and to the knowledge of the faith, O sign-bearing Euthymius, our father; pray unto Christ God to grant remission of transgressions unto those who celebrate thy holy memory with love.
*Twice.*

*Glory, and now, Theotokion:*
As the Virgin and only one among women, who without seed gavest birth to God in the flesh, all we generations of men call thee blessed; for the fire of the Godhead made its abode in thee, and as an Infant thou dost nourish with milk the Creator and Lord. Therefore, we the angelic and human race worthily glorify thy most holy birthgiving, and with one accord cry out to thee: Pray unto Christ God to grant remission of transgressions unto those who venerate thy most holy birthgiving with faith.

*Songs of Ascents, the 1st Antiphon of Tone 4. Prokeimenon:*
*Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones.*[^2162]
*Verse:*
*What shall I render unto the Lord for all that He hath rendered unto me?*[^2163]
*The Gospel according to Matthew, pericope 43 [Mt. 11:27–30].*
*After Psalm 50, Sticheron, Tone 2:*
O venerable father, into all the earth went forth the proclamation of thy righteous deeds; therefore in the heavens thou hast found the reward of thy labors, thou hast destroyed the legions of demons, and hast attained unto the angelic ranks, whose life thou didst blamelessly emulate. Having boldness before Christ God, entreat peace for our souls.

*The Canon of the Birthgiver of God with the heirmos to 6, and two canons of the saint to 8.*
*The Canon of the Venerable One, whose acrostic with the heirmoi is: "A wealth of the earthborn thou hast appeared, Euthymius." By John of Damascus. Tone 4.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
There is none like unto Thee, O most glorified Lord; for with a strong hand Thou hast delivered the people whom Thou hast acquired, O Lover of mankind.

*Troparion:*
Thou dost loose the sorrow of those who brought thee forth in glorious manner, being promised by God, and before thy birth a gift eponymous of good cheer.

*Troparion:*
The Church cries aloud a thanksgiving, O venerable one, having received thee as an offshoot from God, foretelling peaceful good cheer.

*Another Canon of the Venerable One, whose acrostic is: "By thy prayers, O all-blessed one, grant light unto me." By Theophanes. Tone 8.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
The charioteer Pharaoh did the wonderworking rod of Moses once drown, striking crosswise and dividing the sea; but it saved Israel, a fleeing pedestrian, as he chanted a song unto God.

*Troparion:*
By thy prayers and supplications entreat God, O all-blessed one, and disperse the dark cloud of my despondency; for standing before the King of all, thou art full of good cheer and consolation.

*Troparion:*
Another new Samuel, given by God, and promised before thy conception, O father, thou hast appeared unto all the churches, O venerable one, eponymous in name, being led in both respects by the brightness of good cheer.

*Troparion:*
Making prayers and supplications unto God, thy parents receive thee as a divine gift and a light-bearing offshoot, by thy birth proclaiming the radiance of piety and the reproof of heresy.

*Troparion:*
From childhood thou didst dedicate thyself, O venerable one, unto God Who gave thee, and looking unto Him and guided by His life-creating commandments, O God-bearer, through faith in virtues thou didst ascend unto the highest height.

*Theotokion:*
Having thee as our intercession, O Mother of God, we who piously glorify God of all and the Lord Who was born of thee shall not fear the array of adversaries who rise against us; Him do thou entreat for us.

*Katavasia: The sun did once traverse the dry, deep-generating earth...*[^2164]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
We boast not in wisdom, nor in power, nor in riches, but in Thee, the hypostatic Wisdom of the Father, O Christ; for there is none holy save Thee, O Lover of mankind.

*Troparion:*
She who gave birth to thee, emulating Anna, brought the venerable one as a living sacrifice unto God Who had glorified him even before his conception, like Samuel of old.

*Troparion:*
Enkindled with rich love toward God, with all-pious mind Thou didst restrain the passions, O venerable one; therefore divine grace rested upon thee.

*Another. Heirmos:*
Thou Who in the beginning didst establish the heavens by understanding, and didst found the earth upon the waters, establish me, O Christ, upon the rock of Thy commandments; for there is none holy save Thee, O only Lover of mankind.

*Troparion:*
As the child of a barren woman, thou didst appear as a most fruitful husbandman of spiritual fruitfulness, O venerable one, cutting down the thorns of impiety and divinely casting in the seed of piety.

*Troparion:*
Having become a celebrant of supernatural and mystical visions, O God-bearer, leading the unbelieving unto Christ, those who believe in godly manner are instructed by thy teachings, O father, which breathe upon them.

*Troparion:*
Held by a most chaste and pious mind, thou didst straightway prefer eternal life and sweetness to fleeting and corruptible things, having mortified the flesh by extreme abstinence, O Euthymius.

*Troparion:*
With a soul on fire and wounded with the love of Christ, having escaped the burning snares of the demons, thou wast enlightened by the dewy grace, O father, having become a sign-bearer.

*Theotokion:*
Thou hast sealed the sayings of the divine prophets and their prophecies, having given birth to the Word Who spoke through them and Who fulfilled all their divine utterances, O blessed and all-immaculate one.

*Katavasia: The firm foundation of those who hope in Thee...*[^2165]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom and the Word" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
With the oil of abstinence thou didst spiritually fill the lamp of thy soul, desiring the ever-radiant coming of thy Bridegroom; with watchful prayers thou didst preserve it, O venerable one, and didst dwell in His bridal chamber, O blessed one. Therefore thou didst worthily receive sweetness, truly the ever-living operation of miracles, O God-bearing Euthymius; pray unto Christ God to grant remission of transgressions unto those who celebrate thy holy memory with love.
*Twice.*

*Glory, and now, Theotokion:*
As is due, like that widow with the two mites, I offer thanksgiving praise unto thee, O Lady, for all thy gifts; for thou hast appeared as both protection and help, ever delivering me from perils and afflictions. Therefore, as one delivered from the midst of the burning furnace from those who afflict me, from the heart I cry out to thee: O Birthgiver of God, help me, praying unto Christ God to grant me remission of transgressions; for thy servant hath thee as hope.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
In Thy wisdom Thou didst bow down the heavens by Thy condescension, O Christ, and didst appear incarnate upon earth. Therefore we all cry aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
Having preserved thy mind immutable, from swaddling clothes by thy life thou didst show an ascent unto God, drawing near to Whom thou didst ascend from strength to strength, O father.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst desire the humility of Christ, having migrated hence unto the God-receiving city, to be crucified in mind with Him Who suffered for thy sake upon the Cross.

*Troparion:*
Choosing to suffer lawfully, thou didst strip thyself of the affairs of life; and naked, wrestling against the adversary in the likeness of Christ, thou didst erect a trophy of victory in the wilderness.

*Another. Heirmos:*
Thou art my strength, O Lord, Thou art also my power, Thou art my God, Thou art my rejoicing, Who didst not leave the bosom of the Father, yet didst visit our poverty. Therefore with the Prophet Habakkuk I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind![^2166]

*Troparion:*
Having dedicated thyself wholly unto God, O father, desiring immortal glory, thou didst run fervently unto Him by blameless living and abstinence and the radiance of life, unceasingly crying aloud: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
Having loved the Source of goodness with all thy might, O venerable one, thou wast a source of divine gifts unto fasters, healing those who thirsted for them; for like Moses of old in the wilderness, O all-blessed one, thou didst gush forth springs in marvelous manner.

*Troparion:*
Appearing from the unsetting rays of the Spirit, thou didst set free the children of the bondwoman, renewing them as worthy sons of God through the baptism of adoption; for having emulated the life of the divine Forerunner, thou didst show thyself to be a baptizer, O Euthymius.

*Troparion:*
Enlightened by the grace of God, thou didst become known unto those who knew thee not, O Euthymius; for it was truly not fitting for thy virtue to remain hidden and concealed in the wildernesses. Therefore the Master of all showed thee forth unto all as a light-bearing luminary.

*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, O honored one; rejoice, O all-pure Virgin; rejoice, O mountain overshadowed by grace; rejoice O tabernacle; rejoice, O ark; rejoice, O lampstand bearing the divine Light; for thou hast been the mediatress of ineffable joy and gladness of souls unto the faithful.

*Katavasia: The heavens were covered...*[^2167]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
The ungodly shall not see Thy glory, O Christ; but rising early at dawn from the night, we hymn Thee, O Only-begotten One, the radiance of the Father's glory of the Godhead, O Lover of mankind.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst subject thyself unto the law of God; for thou didst enslave thy body as an instrument of the soul, O God-bearer, subduing the carnal mind unto the Spirit.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst run the whole path of life, and conceiving the fear of God within thyself thou didst give birth to salvation, having shone forth like the sun unto those who had gone astray, though concealed by the wilderness.

*Another. Heirmos:*
Why hast Thou cast me off from Thy presence, O unwaning Light, and an alien darkness hath covered me, the wretched one? But turn me back, and direct my paths toward the light of Thy commandments, I pray.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst lead fasters of piety onto another path, O father Euthymius, and leading them up to the imperishable inheritance on high, thou wast revealed as a pillar of fire and a cloud by the radiance of the Spirit.

*Troparion:*
Christ granted thee unto the world, O father, as a most merciful physician to the sick, and a marvelous nourisher to the hungry, an instructor to the foolish, a chastener to the undiscerning, a protector to orphans and the poor.

*Troparion:*
Thou wast compassionate, merciful, bearing a humble-minded disposition, cutting off the causes of passions by divine teachings, and making wise and instructing thy disciples, O father, and healing the diseases of souls.

*Troparion:*
Shining and emitting rays of thy miracles, thou didst enlighten all men; and like a magnet thou didst draw them unto thy teachings, edifying their manners and the pledges of their souls, passing through in purity of soul.

*Theotokion:*
All we proclaim thee to be the true Birthgiver of God, O divinely-blessed one, having been delivered from corrupt birth through thy birthgiving, and called back unto a better life, through the tender mercy of our God.

*Katavasia: As Isaiah saw...*[^2168]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
I am come into the depths of the sea, and the tempest of many sins hath overwhelmed me; but as God lead up my life from the depths, O most Merciful One!

*Troparion:*
As of old the offspring of the bondwoman, so now having adopted us through the laver of regeneration, by thy prayers, O God-bearer, crush the yoke of our bondage.

*Troparion:*
The grace of God which actively made its abode in thee, O God-bearer, established thee as a most wise administrator and instructor to the foolish, and a dispeller of evil spirits.

*Another. Heirmos:*
Cleanse me, O Savior, for many are mine iniquities; and lead me up from the depth of evils, I pray, for unto Thee have I cried, and do Thou give ear unto me, O God of my salvation!

*Troparion:*
Having received the greatest grace from God, thou didst drive away multitudes of hostile demons, healing all the perversities of those who in faith draw near unto thee.

*Troparion:*
Truly blessed wast thou, O father Euthymius, having acquired wealth-producing poverty and joyful mourning, O venerable one, through which thou didst inherit the Kingdom of heaven.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst cast away the readily fading honor and glory that is upon earth, and didst receive the ever-existing life and imperishable inheritance, O all-blessed one, having most surely settled in the heavenly mansions.

*Theotokion:*
We name thee the Sovereign Lady of all things and of the eternal ones of God; for in truth thou gavest birth ineffably unto the existing God, Who created all things, and Who upholds and embraces all, O all-immaculate one.

*Katavasia: The Elder cried aloud unto Thee...*[^2169]

*Kontakion, Tone 8, Podoben: "As the first-fruits" (Я́кѡ нача́тки):*
In thy venerable birthgiving creation found joy, and in thy divine memory, O venerable one, it received the good cheer of thy many miracles; richly grant of these unto our souls, and cleanse the defilements of sins, that we may chant: Alleluia!

*Ikos:*
How shall I, the wretched one, bring praise from a sluggish heart? I am terrified and in fear of the great Euthymius; yet relying upon his supplications, with good cheer and much diligence I shall begin the song, and declare unto all his life and birth, and how his parents chant unto God: Alleluia!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The three youths in Babylon, turning the tyrant's command into foolishness, cried aloud in the midst of the flame: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst enter inside the cloud, O father, covered with supernatural fire covered, as a divine initiate of ineffable things: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
The Creator imparts unto thee, O father, supernatural things above nature without envy; and revealing the pledges of the souls of those who partake, O venerable one, of the Body of thy Lord.

*Troparion:*
Honoring the Only-begotten One even after His divine Incarnation in two natures, O Euthymius, thou didst cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, God of our fathers!

*Another. Heirmos:*
The fire was ashamed before the condescension of God in Babylon of old; therefore the youths in the furnace, rejoicing with nimble step as in a meadow of flowers, chanted: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Having acquired the discipline of fasting as an arena of contest, O father, thou didst show forth thy life, uniting thyself with the bodiless hosts by extreme abstinence, crying aloud, O Euthymius: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Christ showed thee forth as a two-edged sword, piercing the hearts of the enemy and slaying the legions of demons, and gladdening the souls of those who chant: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Feasting upon the tri-hypostatic Light, O father, having become a second light by participation in the First, conformable to Him, O Euthymius, thou didst emit rays unto those who chant: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
Thou didst dawn as the morning, having the Sun of Righteousness, Who cleanses the world from the darkness of ignorance by the dawn of divine knowledge, unto Whom we chant: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Katavasia: In the fire Thou didst bedew...*[^2170]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
The birthgiving of the Birthgiver of God saved the pious youths in the furnace; then prefigured, but now in reality, it rouses the whole universe to chant unto Thee: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Having sanctified thyself unto God, and having kindled the furnace of conscience, O Euthymius, rejoicing thou didst offer up thy whole life as an immaculate whole-burnt offering, chanting unto Christ: Bless the Lord, all ye works, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Having been adopted through divine grace, as an inheritance thou didst receive knowledge of things to come; for having mastered nature, thou didst knowingly surpass nature, hastening unto fulfillment, O Euthymius: Bless the Lord, all ye works all ye works, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Another. Heirmos:*
Sevenfold did the Chaldean tyrant fiercely kindle the furnace for the godly; but having seen them saved by a greater power, he cried aloud unto the Creator and Deliverer: Ye youths, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Having acquired the most steadfast life, O all-blessed one, thou didst attain unto the highest vision, having become a capacious receptacle of the life-creating Spirit, and of the gifts richly flowing thence, chanting unceasingly: Ye people, exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
By migration thou hast reached the Citadel of Zion, and hast entered into the eternal mansions, and having found a heavenly inheritance through thy painful labors, with the angelic choirs thou dost chant: Ye youths, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst shine like the sun, and didst enlighten the wildernesses; thou didst drive away the dark-visaged demons, and wast an all-radiant, unapproachable pillar, shining with wonderworking splendors, unceasingly crying unto the Master: Ye priests, hymn; ye people, exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Adorned with the most sacred deeds of life, thou didst accomplish the foremost virtue; having become bright with rectitude of teachings, and an expounder of certain theology, crying unceasingly: Ye priests, hymn; ye people, exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
O all-immaculate Bride of God, snatch away from the captivity of passions those who flee unto thee, and grant sovereign freedom unto the churches of the Orthodox, who chant with faith: Ye priests, hymn; ye people, exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Katavasia: In the unendurable fire...*[^2171]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Knowing thee, O pure and most immaculate one, to be such after birthgiving, and before birthgiving, and in birthgiving, all creation magnifies thee as the true Birthgiver of God.

*Troparion:*
Having found thee as a fountain of healings both before thy death and asleep whole in thy shrine, O venerable one, we bless thee as a victorious champion.

*Troparion:*
He Who is in the highest made thee a helper to the earthly emperor against the barbarians, and to thy flock against diverse sowing of heresies, O venerable father.

*Another. Heirmos:*
Heaven was dismayed at this, and the ends of the earth were astonished, that God appeared unto men in the flesh, and thy womb became more spacious than the heavens. Therefore the ranks of angels and men magnify thee as the Birthgiver of God.

*Troparion:*
Christ made known unto thee, O father, thy much-longed-for departure unto Him, as unto Moses the God-seer of old; emulating whom in virtue, thou didst part the sea of passions and didst pass unhindered unto the land of promise, having triumphed over adversaries.

*Troparion:*
Like Elijah the zealot thou wast translated, mounting unto heaven by the chariot of virtues, where thy citizenship was visibly enrolled, O venerable one; and now standing before the Master, remember those who celebrate thy light-bearing and all-sacred memory with faith.

*Troparion:*
Thy way of life was angelic, O all-blessed one, and thy life was most bright, O divinely-wise one; thy soul was most light-resembling and godlike, and thy faith was pious; for thou wast an expounder of divine dogmas, O God-bearer, and didst show thyself to be a preacher of Orthodox teaching.

*Troparion:*
I zealously present thee as an intercessor and supplicant praying unto God, O father, asking for remission of sins and the cutting off of my debts, constraining divine compassions, being confirmed in hope by thy prayer, O divinely-wise one.

*Theotokion:*
Be unto me a saving pillar, O pure one, checking the legions of demons, driving away the tumult of perils and afflictions, chasing far off the assault of passions, granting pure freedom, and bestowing an abundance of divine gifts.

*Katavasia: In the law of the shadow and the scriptures...*[^2172]

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "Hear, ye women" (Жены̀ оу҆слы́шите):*
From the womb God sanctified thee, O venerable father, like Jeremiah of old, and Samuel, O God-bearer, showing thee forth as a divine prophet, O wonderworking Euthymius, companion of the angels; with them do thou remember all who faithfully hymn thee.
*Twice.*

*Glory, and now, Theotokion:*
In truth we confess thee to be the Birthgiver of God, O Sovereign Lady, who have been saved through thee; for ineffably thou didst give birth unto God, Who destroyed death by the Cross and drew the assemblies of the venerable ones unto Himself; with them we praise thee, O Virgin.

*At the Praises, Stichera on 4, Tone 8, Podoben: "O marvelous wonder" (Ѡ҆ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*
O venerable father Euthymius, having forsaken the things upon earth thou didst follow Christ, not preferring perishable things before those to come, O glorious one; dwelling in the wilderness as in a city, thou didst destroy the legions of demons. O who could recount, O ever-glorious one, the true fervor of thy soul toward the Lord?
*Twice.*

*Sticheron:*
O venerable father Euthymius, thou didst appear as the rule of monastics and their praise, the sweetness of the Orthodox, and the bright luminary of the universe; for dwelling in the cave, thou wast not terrified by the frightful visions of the deceitful enemy. O sacred gift within thee, O blessed one, whereby thou didst visibly trample all the shelter of demons!

*Sticheron:*
O venerable father Euthymius, truly thou didst wing thy soul toward God, and having cleansed thy senses by fasting, and through unceasing prayers, O all-blessed one, thou wast counted worthy of immortal life. O glorious adornment of fasters: for Christ rejoicing received thee into the immaterial mansions.

*Glory, the same Tone:*
We honor thee, our father Euthymius, as the instructor of multitudes of monks; for by thy path we have learned truly to walk uprightly. Blessed art thou who didst labor for Christ and didst reprove the power of the enemy, O conversationalist with the angels, companion of the venerable and righteous; with them pray unto the Lord that our souls may find mercy.

*Both now: Receive, O Sovereign Lady...*

*The Great Doxology, and Dismissal. The First Hour. And the final Dismissal.*

*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes from the canon, Ode 3 and Ode 6.*
*Prokeimenon, Tone 7: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones.*[^2173]
*Verse: What shall I render unto the Lord for all that He hath rendered unto me?*[^2174]
*The Epistle to the Hebrews, pericope 335 [Heb. 13:17–21].*
*Alleluia, Tone 6: Blessed is the man that fears the Lord, in His commandments he will take great delight.*[^2175]
*Verse: His seed shall be mighty upon earth.*[^2176]
*The Gospel according to Luke, pericope 24 [Lk. 6:17–23].*
*Communion Verse: In everlasting memory shall the righteous be.*[^2177]

*In the same month, on the 21st day:*  
*The Venerable Father our Maximus the Confessor;*  
*And the Holy Martyr Neophytus;*  
*And the Holy Martyrs Eugene, Candidus, Valerian, and Aquila.*  
*Their service is chanted at Compline.*  
*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of Maximus, to 6; Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant among martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*  
Him Who through tender mercy became Man, as He was well pleased, understood in two wills and operations, O venerable one, thou didst proclaim, O Maximus, stopping the unclosed mouths of the vile who glorify Him as of one will and one operation, who wrought evil through the temptation of the devil; and the Incarnation in two essences unto men of Him Who willed to appear in one hypostasis.

With the sinews of thy teachings, O father, Thou didst throttle Pyrrhus, who babbled evilly, O Maximus; and Thou didst endure persecutions and afflictions most manfully, cruelly mutilated, and having thy tongue cut out, and that divine hand which was ever outstretched unto God, wherewith writing, Thou didst accomplish lofty words.

Like the reed-pen of a swift-writing scribe, sharpened by the Spirit,[^2178] holy was thy tongue, O blessed one, beautifully writing by grace upon the tablets of our hearts the law of divine virtues and the certainty of teachings: and the Incarnation in two essences unto men of Him Who willed to appear in one hypostasis.

*Other Stichera of the Martyr Neophytus, Tone 8, Podoben: "O marvelous wonder" (Ѡ҆ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*  
O marvelous wonder! A dove came from on high, making bright for the Martyr Neophytus with human utterance, on whose account his equal-to-the-angels life shone forth, wherewith in his youth he suffered manfully. O divine deeds of the sorely-suffering martyr! By his prayers save our souls, O Christ, for Thou art compassionate.

O marvelous wonder! From his very swaddling clothes, the perfectly-wise Neophytus accomplishes miracles by the operation of the Spirit: he gushes forth water from a rock by prayers,[^2179] he raises the dead woman of whom he was the offspring. O divine deeds of the sorely-suffering martyr! By his prayers save our souls O Christ, for Thou art compassionate.

O marvelous wonder! Suffering for Christ, the thrice-blessed Neophytus struck fear into the enemies by surpassing visions: the fire was extinguished when he was cast into it; he showed forth the beasts terrified before him. O invincible power, in which the sufferer is made marvelous! But by his prayers save us, O God.

*Glory, of the Venerable One, Tone 6:*  
O venerable father, into all the earth went forth the proclamation of thy righteous deeds;[^2180] therefore in the heavens thou hast found the reward of thy labors; thou hast destroyed the legions of demons and attained unto the angelic ranks, whose blameless life thou didst emulate. Having boldness before Christ God, entreat peace for our souls.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*  
*If Wednesday or Friday, Stavrotheotokion, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having laid aside all earthly hope" (Всѐ ѿло́жше):*  
When of old the ewe-lamb, the immaculate and blameless Sovereign Lady, beheld her own Lamb upon the Tree of the Cross, she cried aloud as a Mother, and marveling, cried out: O sweetest Child, what is this new and glorious spectacle? How hath the ungrateful gathering delivered Thee to Pilate's judgment seat and condemned Thee to death, the Life of all? Yet I hymn Thine ineffable condescension, O Word!

*At the Aposticha, from the Octoechos.*  
*Glory, Tone 8:*  
We honor thee, our father Maximus, as the instructor of multitudes of monks; for by thy path we have learned truly to walk uprightly. Blessed art thou who didst labor for Christ and didst reprove the power of the enemy, O conversationalist with the angels, companion of the venerable and righteous; with them pray unto the Lord that our souls may find mercy.

*Now and ever, Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 8, Podoben: "O marvelous wonder" (Ѡ҆ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*  
What is this visible sight which is seen by mine eyes, O Master? Thou Who upholdest all creation art lifted up upon the Tree, and dost die, Who givest life unto all? the Birthgiver of God said weeping, when she beheld Him Who ineffably shone forth from her, God and Man, lifted up upon the Cross.

*Troparion, Tone 8:*  
O guide of Orthodoxy, teacher of piety and purity, luminary of the universe, divinely-inspired adornment of monastics, O all-wise Maximus: by thy teachings thou hast enlightened all men, O spiritual flute; pray unto Christ God that our souls may be saved.

*Another Troparion of the Martyr, Tone 4:*  
Thy martyr Neophytus, O Lord, in his suffering received an imperishable crown from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength, he cast down the torturers and crushed the powerless audacities of the demons; by his prayers save our souls.

*The Office of the Martyrs is chanted at Compline.*  
*The Canon, whose acrostic is: "I sing of the four victorious martyrs." Tone 2.*  
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*  
Traversing without a path, unusually, and without wetting the feet the path of the sea, chosen Israel cried aloud: Let us sing unto the Lord, for He is gloriously glorified![^2181]

*Troparion:*  
Enlightened by the radiance of the thrice-sunlit grace, O glorious martyrs, enlighten those who piously hymn your memory, delivering them from the darkness of passions and adversities.

*Troparion:*  
Illumined by the All-holy Spirit, having forsaken the storm of the world, ye withdrew into the mountains, O wise and glorious martyrs, being trained for divine suffering, which also ye splendidly accomplished.

*Troparion:*  
Confirmed by the sovereign and all-strong power of the Creator, O divine martyrs, through many adornments ye appeared steadfast in torments, having trampled underfoot all the power of the enemies.

*Theotokion:*  
Vouchsafe me to obtain the divine mercies by thy mediation, O blessed Sovereign Lady, who gavest birth in the flesh to the most merciful and propitious Word, Who receives those who flee unto Him.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*  
Having established me upon the rock of the faith, Thou hast enlarged my mouth against mine enemies; for my spirit rejoiced in chanting: There is none holy like our God, and none righteous besides Thee, O Lord![^2182]

*Troparion:*  
Wounded with the Master's love, ye endured manifold torments; for beaten with raw ox-sinews, O sufferers, and cruelly scorched on every side by fire, ye remained steadfast.

*Troparion:*  
Strengthened by the power of the Lord, ye went forth to wrestle against the enemy, and cast him down, O passion-bearers, crying unto Christ: Thou art our God, and there is none righteous besides Thee, O Lord!

*Troparion:*  
Rejoicing with the angels on high, and joined to the assemblies of the martyrs, with them pray to deliver from every affliction and adversity those who honor you, O divine martyrs.

*Theotokion:*  
With one accord we bless thee who art hymned, from whom shone forth upon us the ineffable heavenly radiance, and we cry: Save thy servants from every affliction, for thou art the helper of the faithful.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*  
I sing to Thee, for by hearing have I heard Thee, O Lord, and was afraid;[^2183] for Thou comest unto me, seeking me who had gone astray. Therefore I glorify Thy great condescension toward me, O most Merciful One.

*Troparion:*  
Chanting piously, let us honor the boldness of Eugene, the resistance of Aquila, and the endurance of Candidus, together with them honoring also the fortitude of Valerian.

*Troparion:*  
Possessed by fury, the torturer commands thee to be stretched out with cords and unmercifully beaten, and to be sorely scraped with iron, O Eugene, and thy body scorched with candles.

*Troparion:*  
Thinking to destroy your firmness by torments, O wise martyrs, the all-senseless torturer subjected you to bitterer torments; but by the grace of Christ the Creator of all, ye put Him to shame.

*Theotokion:*  
As the only help of the faithful, O all-blessed Birthgiver of God, deliver from all afflictions thy servants who fervently bless thee, and who flee under thy divine protection.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*  
O Enlightenment of those lying in darkness, Salvation of the despairing, O Christ my Savior, unto Thee do I rise early at dawn, O King of peace; enlighten me with Thy radiance, for besides Thee I know no other God.[^2184]

*Troparion:*  
Showing forth truly the martyrs' endurance, thou didst stand like an adamant, undergoing bitter torments and crying out thankfully unto the Creator, O Martyr Eugene: For besides Thee we know no other God!

*Troparion:*  
With lime thou didst cast down the idol gods beforehand through thy most sacred prayers unto the Creator; thou didst endure manifold wounds over all thy body, O Martyr Eugene, being unsparingly wounded with clubs.

*Theotokion:*  
Deliver us from every harm, O all-holy Virgin, for thou art the protectress of us who hope in thee, O Birthgiver of God, and cry aloud unto thy divine Offspring: For besides Thee we know no other God!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*  
From the whale Jonah cried unto the Lord: Do Thou lead me up from the depths of hades, I pray, that unto Thee as Deliverer in the voice of praise, and in the spirit of truth, I may sacrifice unto Thee![^2185]

*Troparion:*  
Stretched out upon the tree, and scraped with iron by the fury of the judge, and lashed with ox-sinews unsparingly across the shoulders, and scorched with fire, the noble-victorious martyrs rejoiced.

*Troparion:*  
Thou didst endure in thy body, being scorched with candles, and stretched out upon the tree, O glorious Eugene, and having thy wounds unsparingly sprinkled with salt, through the brutality of the lawless torturer.

*Theotokion:*  
May we be delivered from every assault and affliction, O full of God's grace, who flee unto thy protection, ever piously glorifying thee with love as the all-immaculate Mother of God.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared today" (Ꙗ҆ви́лся є҆сѝ дне́сь):*  
The fourfold company of steadfast martyrs, shining forth in beauty, hath illumined the four corners of the world with rays, by the sufferings and powers of the martyrs, among whom shines the great Eugene.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*  
When the golden image was worshiped on the plain of Dura, Thy three youths disregarded the godless command; cast into the midst of the fire, bedewed they sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^2186]

*Troparion:*  
With bright ascetic deeds thou didst manfully arm thyself against delusion, and having become victorious by divine decree, O Eugene, thou hast found the recompense of thy labors, and with the angels thou dost chant: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*  
Having the Cross of Christ as a divine weapon, O sufferers, ye together cast down the array of the devil and the opposition of the torturers, receiving the crowns of victory from the life-bearing right hand of God, the Arbiter of contests.

*Troparion:*  
With a pure mind thou wast not shaken by the assaults of torments, but being incessantly beaten with clubs, O Eugene, most excellently didst thou cut down, O martyr, by the resistance of thy sufferings, the heads of the enemies and invisible adversaries.

*Theotokion:*  
Behold, truly as thou didst foretell, all generations worthily call thee blessed, O all-immaculate one,[^2187] and as is due we glorify thee; for thou gavest birth to the Father's co-unoriginate Word, incarnate of thee, in order to save mankind.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*  
God Who descended into the fiery furnace unto the Hebrew youths, and changed the flame into dew, hymn Him, ye works, as the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages![^2188]

*Troparion:*  
Unto every crafty deceit of the persecutors did Valerian resist, and with him the glorious Aquila and the divine Eugene, together with the valiant sufferer Candidus.

*Troparion:*  
The divinely-radiant memory of the marvelous passion-bearers of Christ hath arrived: of Valerian and Eugene together, of the divine Aquila and Candidus, which we joyfully celebrate with love.

*Troparion:*  
Shining brightly upon us with light-resembling rays, the yearly memory of the passion-bearers of Christ hath arrived: of the divine Aquila and Candidus together, and of Eugene and Valerian.

*Theotokion:*  
The Son, co-ever-existing and co-unoriginate with the Father, came forth from thee in the last times, in order to save us, O pure Virgin who knewest not wedlock; cease not to make Him merciful unto us.

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*  
Him Who from God is God the Word, Who by ineffable wisdom came to renew Adam who had cruelly fallen into corruption through food, Who was ineffably incarnate of the Holy Virgin for our sake, with one mind we the faithful magnify in songs.

*Troparion:*  
Thou didst overcome the assault of the torturers, after manifold torments having passed over unto God with exceeding joy, receiving the rewards of victory as a valiant warrior, as a great champion, as a chosen soldier of Christ, O most excellent Eugene.

*Troparion:*  
They were joined with the angelic choirs, the assemblies of the martyrs, and the ranks of the righteous; now with them pray, O martyrs, that cleansing of sins and deliverance from all perils may be granted unto those who hymn you.

*Troparion:*  
On behalf of us who celebrate your radiant memory, O divinely-wise Eugene, O piously all-glorious Martyr Aquila, and Valerian with Candidus thy fellow-sufferer, earnestly entreat Christ the All-good.

*Theotokion:*  
Thee, O all-holy Virgin, the multitudes of angels and all generations of men call blessed with exceeding joy; for thou gavest birth unto the Savior, Creator, Master, and God of all, Whom do thou entreat for us.

*Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*  
With what [praises] shall we the faithful laud the truly divine warriors and sufferers of Christ: the wise Eugene and Valerian, the glorious Candidus, and fellow-sufferer together with Aquila, faithfully calling them blessed, as having suffered strangely, so that at the hour of condemnation they may deliver us from torment.

*Sticheron:*  
O passion-bearing martyr of Christ, thy burdened body was burnt, by the fury of the torturer was sorely scraped, and unsparingly scorched, beaten, O martyr, scorched with candles, and rubbed with salt and most bitter vinegar; yet thou didst endure all things, O blessed Eugene, for the sake of the Lord.

*Sticheron:*  
Having manifestly the saving law in thy heart, O martyr, thou didst forsake the world and drew near unto the mountains, being trained for truly perfect divine suffering, O blessed one; receiving which with joy, thou didst endure the entire scraping of thy body, and the most cruel scorching of fire, O Martyr Valerian.

*Glory, both now, Theotokion:*  
Rejoice, all creation cries unto thee: Rejoice, O all-holy Virgin; rejoice, sceptre of David; rejoice, thou that didst bud forth the mystical cluster of grapes; rejoice, heavenly gate and unburnt bush;[^2189] rejoice, light of all the world; rejoice, joy of all; rejoice, protection; rejoice, all-immaculate one of those who purely flee unto thy help.

*Stavrotheotokion:*  
When the undefiled ewe-lamb beheld her own Lamb led willingly to the slaughter as a man,[^2190] weeping she said: Dost Thou now hasten to leave me childless, O Christ Who gavest me birth? What is this that Thou hast done, O Deliverer of all? Yet I hymn and glorify Thine extreme goodness, which passes mind and word, O Lover of mankind.

*At Matins, one canon from the Octoechos, and two of the saints.*  
*The Canon of the Venerable One, whose acrostic apart from the Theotokia is: "Let the most great Maximus be glorified." A composition of John the Monk. Tone 8.*  
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*  
Let us sing unto the Lord, Who led His people through the Red Sea, for He alone is gloriously glorified![^2191]

*Troparion:*  
Gush forth unto me, drop down from thy sweet and honey-flowing tongue, O divine Maximus, the divinely-inspired grace of the Spirit.

*Troparion:*  
A burning fire didst thou appear against heresies, O blessed one; for like reeds thou didst consume them by the zeal of the Spirit.

*Troparion:*  
The irrational teaching of one will was put forward from a most impious disposition; but by thy words, O father, it was refuted.

*Theotokion:*  
He Who was well-pleased to be born from thy womb, O Bride of God, is all desire, and sweetness, and unwaning light.[^2192]

*The Canon of the Martyr, the same Tone, whose* acrostic is: "A new garden of Christ I praise thee well, O martyr." A composition of Joseph.*
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*  
Traversing the water as dry land, and having escaped the evil of Egypt, the Israelite cried aloud: Let us sing unto our Deliverer and God![^2193]

*Troparion:*  
Knowing thee, O all-blessed one, to be a new garden of Christ, which blossomed in the garden of martyrs and brought forth sacred fruits of piety, we sing unto thee, O Neophytus.

*Troparion:*  
Thou wast shown to be a fulfiller of the divine words, O blessed one; from infancy thou didst wisely choose the good part,[^2194] and becamest a guide unto those who strayed.

*Troparion:*  
Desiring to see Christ, Who in the flesh was an Infant from the Virgin for our sake: being thyself an infant, thou didst lead the mind of infants unto perfection.

*Troparion:*  
Dropping from thy sacred lips the sweetness of divine knowledge, O divinely-wise one, thou didst honorably sweeten souls that were bewitched by the malice of the alien.

*Theotokion:*  
Having given birth by nature unto the Creator, thou hast deified the whole nature of the earthborn; therefore we confess thee in truth to be the Birthgiver of God, O Virgin Bride of God.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*  
Thou art the confirmation of those that flee unto Thee, O Lord; Thou art the light of the darkened, and my spirit sings of Thee.[^2195]

*Troparion:*  
The most great Maximus was shown by blood to be in all truth both preacher and martyr of the pious faith of Christ.

*Troparion:*  
O blessed Maximus, by fasting thou becamest a divinely-fitting and pure habitation of wisdom.

*Troparion:*  
Thy tongue poured forth a river of Christ's teachings piously, O all-blessed Maximus, nourisher of wisdom.

*Theotokion:*  
To show us the path leading unto holiness, O Master, Thou didst all-holily make Thine abode in the all-holy womb.

*Another [Canon]. The same Heirmos.*  
*Troparion:*  
The Pure Spirit preserved thee unharmed, O glorious one, who wast wholly dedicated unto the All-merciful Word.

*Troparion:*  
The multitudes of faithful people sang unto the Lord, having seen through thee, O martyr, the raising from the dead of her who bore thee.

*Troparion:*  
A dove shining with light summoned thee with a living voice and a saving path, O Neophytus.

*Theotokion:*  
Joyous song doth the human race ever offer unto thee, O Mother of God, having received immortality for thy sake.

*Kontakion, Tone 8, Podoben* "To Thee, the Champion Leader" (Взбра́нной):*
The lover of the Trinity and great Maximus, who clearly teaches the divine faith, to glorify Christ as existing in two natures, two wills, and two operations, let us the faithful honor with worthy songs, crying: Rejoice, preacher of the faith!

*Then the Sessional Hymn, Tone 5, Podoben: "The Word co-unoriginate" (Собезнача́льное сло́во):*  
Having endured persecutions for the faith, thou didst drive away every heresy, O father; and having thy tongue cut off together with thy hand, O Maximus, thou didst receive from the hand of the Creator the divinely-fitting crown of confession, O blessed one; Whom do thou now unceasingly entreat, that our souls may find mercy.

*Glory, of the Martyr, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up upon the Cross" (Вознесы́йся на крⷭ҇тъ):*  
As a new-flowering garden thou didst bud forth in the orchards of Christ's passion-bearers: thou didst bring forth the fruits of divine understanding, wherewith those who faithfully honor thee are nourished, O glorious Neophytus, valiantly-minded sufferer; but by thy prayers ever save us, as thou standest before God.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*  
After God having fled unto thy humble divine protection, O Birthgiver of God, falling down I pray: Have mercy, O all-pure one, for mine iniquities have passed over my head,[^2196] and I fear torments, O Sovereign Lady, and I tremble; make supplication, O pure one, unto thy Son, to deliver me from them.

*Stavrotheotokion:*  
Beholding Thee Who wast begotten of the beginningless Father, hanging upon the Cross, O Christ, she who at the last gave birth to Thee in the flesh cried out: Woe is me, O most beloved Jesus! How is it that Thou, Who art glorified as God by angels, dost now willingly submit to be crucified by lawless men? I sing to Thee, O Long-suffering One!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*  
I heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation; I considered Thy works, and glorified Thy Godhead.[^2197]

*Troparion:*  
The earthborn honor thee, and the ranks of the heavenly ones marvel; for through the love of wisdom thou wast shown, O father, to be as one incorporeal.

*Troparion:*  
Cruel indeed was the torturer, yet thine endurance was steadfast; therefore thou wast blessed, while the all-wicked one was cast out.

*Troparion:*  
Before thee, O Maximus, stands the all-blessed pair of disciples, who partook of thy sufferings; therefore also they received equal honors.

*Troparion:*  
Watered by the flow of thy blood, the Church of Christ causes the divine seed of patristic tradition to bud forth through thy teaching through thy teaching, O venerable one.

*Theotokion:*  
Having been delivered through thy birthgiving from the debt of sin, O all-immaculate one, we send up joyful song unto thee, O Bride of God.

*Another [Canon]. The same Heirmos.*  
*Troparion:*  
Beholding the blamelessness of thy life and the simplicity of thine understanding, exceeding many multitudes drew near unto God, O glorious martyr.

*Troparion:*  
Having reached the mountain, thou didst take up thy dwelling there, guided by the divine Spirit, O blessed one; and being nourished by an angel, thou didst show thyself equal in standing to the angels.

*Troparion:*  
Compassionately dispersing, thou didst give unto the poor,[^2198] as it was commanded, receiving recompense, O blessed one, unto unmeasured ages.

*Theotokion:*  
Thou gavest birth unto the Most-divine One, Who willingly became poor through the richness of goodness,[^2199] Who showed compassion upon our poverty.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*  
Rising early at dawn we cry unto Thee, O Lord, save us; for Thou art our God, besides Thee we know no other![^2200]

*Troparion:*  
Having gathered the understanding of the earthborn and of the heavenly ones, Maximus is rightly named a philosopher.

*Troparion:*  
Through an immeasurable desire for wisdom, thou wast shown to be a most excellent emulator of thy Christ, O glorious Maximus.

*Troparion:*  
By the wrath of the torturer thou wast exiled, yet thou didst find Jesus as thy consolation, O blessed one.

*Theotokion:*  
They that acknowledge thee not as Birthgiver of God, O Mother of God, shall not see the Light that was born of thee, O all-pure one.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*  
Why hast Thou cast me off from Thy presence, O unwaning Light, and an alien darkness hath covered me, the wretched one? But turn me back, and direct my paths toward the light of Thy commandments, I pray.[^2201]

*Troparion:*  
Filled with ineffable mysteries, O praiseworthy one, rejoicing thou didst manfully prepare thyself for the contests of the sufferings set before thee, not fearing torments nor death, O Martyr Neophytus.

*Troparion:*  
By the ineffable providence of Him Who directs thy paths, O glorious one, the divine angels stood by and drew thee forth unto the contest from the mountain, like another Moses, glorified in countenance with divine splendors.[^2202]

*Troparion:*  
Having a living word in thy heart, O all-glorious Martyr Neophytus, with a bold mind thou didst cry aloud unto the persecutors: Unsummoned, I was found of those that sought me not,[^2203] now to reprove the weakness of your faith.

*Theotokion:*

The divine mystery hidden before all ages, O all-immaculate Maiden, through thee was made known unto the ends [of the earth]: the Son and Word of God, having become flesh and deified man, O Virgin.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*  
Grant me a radiant robe, Thou that clothest Thyself with light as with a garment, O most merciful Christ our God.[^2204]

*Troparion:*  
Unceasingly dost thou offer prayer unto God, O divinely-wise one, that I may be delivered from passions of soul and body, and from corruption.

*Troparion:*  
The entire turbid fountain of heresies was dried up, O glorious Maximus, being stopped by the rushing sound of thy tongue.

*Troparion:*  
Cleanse me, O only Good One, and pour forth the fountain of grace into my heart, O Christ, through the prayers of Thy venerable one.

*Theotokion:*  
Fairer in beauty than all the sons of men is Thy Son, O all-immaculate one, in the beauty of Godhead, even though for our sake He became flesh.[^2205]

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*  
I will pour out my prayer unto the Lord, and unto Him will I declare my sorrows; for my soul is filled with evils, and my life hath drawn near unto Hades, and like Jonah I pray: Lead me up from corruption, O God![^2206]

*Troparion:*  
Lifted up upon the wood, O all-blessed one, thou wast unmercifully scraped upon thy ribs with iron, and by thy reproaches thou didst tear asunder the hardened heart of the deceiver who commanded [thee] to sacrifice unto the gods, having found the immortal God.

*Troparion:*  
Torn and beaten, O martyr, thou didst grievously bind [him] unto the end, and by the power of the Spirit thou didst show the disorderly movements of the enemy to be of no effect, and didst hasten unto heaven as a crown-bearer to stand before the Lord.

*Troparion:*  
Delighting in the beauties of the Master, thou didst cleave unto Him, crying: O Word of God, for Thy sake Who willingly didst offer Thyself in sacrifice, I am slaughtered, being made conformable in a most divine manner to Thy precious and divine sufferings.

*Theotokion:*  
A most radiant throne of the heavenly King wast thou shown to be, O Virgin, whereon He willingly rested in the flesh, and took away our great debt; and He seated man upon the Father's throne, even as He was well pleased.

*Kontakion, Tone 6, Podoben: "Having fulfilled the dispensation for us" (Е҆́же ѡ҆ на́съ и҆спо́лнивъ):*  
The thrice-radiant Light having taken up His abode in thy soul showed thee to be a chosen vessel, O all-blessed one,[^2207] revealing divine things unto the ends [of the earth]; for thou didst explain hard-to-comprehend understandings, O blessed one, and didst clearly proclaim unto all, O Maximus, the Trinity, transcendent in essence and beginningless.

*Ikos:*  
Shown to be an imitator of the Savior's sufferings, and having Him in thy soul, O all-blessed one, thou didst set ascents in thy heart,[^2208] O exceedingly rich one. And He gave thee grace from heaven; for thou didst wisely and manfully oppose the torturers, proclaiming the beginningless, divine, and consubstantial Trinity, and reproving the ill-believing and God-fighting; thou didst endure countless tribulations, O all-lauded one: the cutting off of thy theological tongue, O venerable one, and together with it thy hand; yet thou didst not cease to speak with boldness and to confirm the faithful by thy divine teachings, clearly proclaiming unto all peoples the Trinity, transcendent in essence and beginningless.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*  
The youths having arrived from Judea in Babylon of old, by faith in the Trinity trampled down the flame of the furnace, singing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^2209]

*Troparion:*  
One nature of the Trinity, one will hast thou declared, and one operation; but of God incarnate in two natures, two wills and operations hast thou preached: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*  
Not two wills separated by opposition of mind, but rather differing by natural quality didst thou preach, O father: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*  
A pillar of Orthodoxy did thy divine words confirm: We honor the One of the Trinity in two essences and wills: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*  
Bearing as a young child God Who is before all ages, O all-immaculate one, Who became incarnate of thee, cease not to pray that He may save those who sing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*  
The Hebrew children in the furnace boldly trampled down the flame, and turned the fire into dew, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages![^2210]

*Troparion:*  
Making a furnace burning with living fire, the most lawless one shut thee up therein for three days, yet thou wast not burned by the fire, crying aloud, O Neophytus: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages!

*Troparion:*  
Delighting most gloriously in songs while thou didst stand in the midst of the flame, O blessed one, for the dew of God refreshed thee, O martyr, as thou didst cry: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages!

*Troparion:*  
So great a miracle wrought in thee amazed every mind, for the fire in no wise burned thee, O divinely-wise one, but spreading abroad burned the heirs of the fire.[^2211]

*Theotokion:*  
Thou wast shown to be higher than the angels, having given birth unto the Angel of Great Counsel, O pure Birthgiver of God,[^2212] unto Whom we all sing: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God, unto the ages!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*  
Having become victors over the torturer and the flame by Thy grace, cleaving earnestly unto Thy commandments, the children cried aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord![^2213]

*Troparion:*  
Greatly loving Him Who exceedingly loved the human race, thou didst take up thy cross and wast co-crucified with Him, O blessed one, singing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*  
Having shunned every death-bearing pleasure, O blessed one, thou didst make thyself entirely an undefiled, divine mirror, singing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Troparion:*  
Having received the life-bearing ray from the one tri-hypostatic Godhead, thou wast shown to be a sun unto those in darkness that had gone astray, singing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!

*Theotokion:*  
Knowing thee to be the Mother of Life and the Parent of God, with Orthodox faith we all call thee blessed, O Birthgiver of God, blessing together thy birthgiving, O pure one, and supreme-exalting it unto the ages.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*  
Sevenfold did the Chaldean torturer furiously heat the furnace for the godly ones; but seeing them saved by a higher power, he cried aloud unto the Creator and Deliverer: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supreme-exalt Him unto all ages![^2214]

*Troparion:*  
Being young in body, O all-blessed one, and perfect in wise mature age, thou didst destroy the malice of the origin of evil: a most fair plant that sprouted in the courts from the Root of Jesse that grew forth,[^2215] unto Whom thou didst unceasingly cry: Ye priests, hymn; ye people, supreme-exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*  
At the judgment seat the beasts were put to shame before thee, O passion-bearer, even as before holy Daniel of old;[^2216] for they recognized thee as a witness of Christ's sufferings, Whom confessing, thou didst endure intolerable torments, crying aloud: Ye priests, hymn; ye people, supreme-exalt Him unto all ages!

*Troparion:*  
Having recognized thee first on the mountain, O Neophytus, a most great lion was brought bound to the judgment seat and loosed against thee in thy martyrdom, O sufferer; yet recognizing thee, he bowed down before thee with fear, seized with shame, and [poured forth] fountains of tears in compunction perceptibly shedding them, O divinely-blessed one.

*Theotokion:*  
Thou didst give birth unto a new Child, Who before all creation was ineffably begotten of the Father, O all-pure one;[^2217] Him therefore do thou entreat, to renew me who am now waxed old through transgressions, and to save me who cry: Ye children, bless; ye priests, hymn; ye people, supreme-exalt Him unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*  
The birthgiving of the Ever-Virgin, prefigured on the mountain unto the lawgiver in the fire and the bush for the salvation of us the faithful,[^2218] with unceasing hymns we magnify.

*Troparion:*  
Thy blood, even as Abel's,[^2219] unto all ages proclaims divinely-inspired dogmas with a clear voice unto the Church of Christ, O all-blessed and most great Maximus.

*Troparion:*  
Thy hand was cut off, yet by the divine finger, as with a reed and ink, by thy cut-off tongue and by thy precious blood, it writes the Orthodox faith in our hearts.[^2220]

*Troparion:*  
Thou hast stood before the divine throne together with the martyrs, whose zeal and faith thou didst share, O father; make us also familiar unto the Master, and make [us] imitators of thee.

*Theotokion:*  
Thou art our weapon and wall, O Birthgiver of God; thou art the protection of those who flee unto thee; thee do we now offer in prayer, that we may be delivered from our enemies.

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*  
Every ear was terrified at the ineffable condescension of God, how the Most High willingly came down even unto the flesh, from the virginal womb, having become man; therefore the all-pure Birthgiver of God we the faithful magnify.

*Troparion:*  
Thou didst stand as a lamb, willingly set forth for slaughter unto the bitter torturers who slew thee, O Martyr Neophytus;[^2221] for being pierced in thy ribs with a spear, thou didst receive a blessed end, O passion-bearer of Christ, most valiantly.

*Troparion:*  
As a sacrifice, as a good lamb, as a precious slaughter, as an offering of the holy temple, as a pure oblation, as a chosen bird, as a costly crown, as Noah's garden of paradise, O blessed one,[^2222] thou didst offer thyself unto God.

*Troparion:*  
Conformed wast thou to the sufferings of Him Who suffered for our sake through goodness,[^2223] and by the likeness of the spear, O martyr, thou wast truly glorified; and now thou dwellest in the heavens, adorned with the diadem of victory, and filled with unceasing joy.

*Theotokion:*

Bearing as heavenly tongs the Coal, O Birthgiver of God, which consumes all the brushwood passions of my heart,[^2224] pray that I may be delivered from the fire of Gehenna, that I may glorify thee, the hope of the faithful, O all-immaculate one.

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "O Light immutable" (Свѣ́те неизмѣ́нный):*  
A trumpet of wisdom wast thou shown to be by thy fair-speaking tongue, terrifying the ranks of adversaries, O Maximus, light of monastics; therefore fed by thy words, we know the true nature of things.

*Theotokion:*  
The Light of spiritual gladness hast thou made to dawn in the world, O Virgin Parent of God: the Deliverer and Master; therefore pray that the pupils of my soul may be enlightened with the light of divine brightness.

*At the Liturgy, the Prokeimenon, Tone 4:*  
*To the saints that are in His earth, the Lord hath been marvelous in all His desires in them.*[^2225]  
*Verse: I beheld the Lord ever before me, for He is at my right hand, that I might not be shaken.*[^2226]  
*The Epistle to the Hebrews, section 330.*[^2227]  
*Alleluia, Tone 4: The righteous cried, and the Lord gave ear unto them.*[^2228]  
*The Gospel of Luke, section 64.*[^2229]  
*Communion Verse: Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous!*[^2230]

*Month of the same, the 22nd Day.*  
*The Holy Apostle Timothy; and the Holy Venerable Martyr Anastasius the Persian.*

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Apostle, Tone 4, Podoben: "O all-praised martyrs" (Всехва́льнїи мч҃ницы):*  
Manifestly enlightened by the rays of the Spirit, O divinely-manifested Timothy, thou wast shown to be a most radiant beacon, traversing the whole earth and enlightening [it] by grace; and now pray that peace and great mercy may be granted unto our souls.

O divinely-wise Timothy, thou didst drink the torrent of pleasure,[^2231] and in a divinely-wise manner didst give drink from the divine understanding unto those who fervently desired it, emulating Christ; unto Whom now thou hast departed with joy, contemplating most radiant glory, and sending down God-bearing peace sending [it] down.

*Sticheron:*  
Obeying Paul, conversing through the Scriptures of the Spirit, thou wast wholly light-radiant, a workman unashamed,[^2232] and a fervent servant of the Lord, O all-wise one, having lived chastely and piously, O Timothy; and thou wast accounted worthy of crowns of victory, as a lawful athlete.[^2233]

*Stichera of the Venerable Martyr, Tone and Podoben the same:*  
O boast of martyrs, having set up radiant victories over deception, thou bearest in thy name the well-blessed appellation of the Resurrection,[^2234] O all-blessed one, borne abroad everywhere as a steadfast conqueror, O Anastasius; and now raise up from falls of sin those who honor thy memory with faith.

*Sticheron:*  
O Martyr Anastasius, having set up a radiant victory over deceit, thou didst receive a twofold crown for thy fasting and thy steadfast suffering, even resisting unto death;[^2235] and the Master Christ granted unto thee a worthy working of miracles.

*Sticheron:*  
The ends of the world now sing of thy miracles, O wonder-working Anastasius; for Christ adorned thee, rewarding thee with wonder-workings because thou didst endure torments for His sake, and after death thou wast accounted worthy of immortal blessedness and beatitude.

*Glory, Tone 8:*  
Foreordained of God, and having become a disciple of the wise Paul, thou wast instructed in divine things, having lived right well, and having kept the faith without doubting even unto blood,[^2236] thou wast shown to be a faithful hierarch, O Apostle Timothy; therefore reproving those who raged for idols, surrounded with clubs and stones, thou didst receive the crown of martyrdom; therefore, O all-blessed one, pray for us who with faith celebrate thy most honorable memory.

*Both now, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 8, Podoben: "O martyrs of the Lord" (Мꙋ́ченицы гдⷭ҇ни):*  
The undefiled heifer, beholding the Young Bull willingly nailed to the wood, weeping piteously, cried: Woe is me, O most beloved Child! What hath the ungrateful congregation of the Hebrews rendered unto Thee, desiring to bereave me of Thee, O All-beloved?

*At the Aposticha, from the Octoechos. Then we say the refrain:*  
*His proclamation went forth into all the earth, and His words unto the ends of the universe.*[^2237]  
*And we sing the automelon Sticheron of the Apostle, Tone 4:*  
The light of the faithful and the apostle who shone forth in the Gospel, Timothy, come, ye people, let us hymn, saying: Rejoice, fair shoot of the faith, of divine Paul's adoption as a son; rejoice, pure observer of virtues, most wise mouth of the Word; rejoice, God-proclaimed lyre of the ends [of the earth]; rejoice, pillar of the faith, and confirmation of the Church.

*Glory, Tone 6:*  
Thou hast magnified, O Christ, as in Judea so also in Babylon, the power of the precious Cross; for through it they came to know the festival of the life-bearing Resurrection. And unto them the captive became a deliverer from the madness of idolatry, and a martyr of undescribed miracles: now the lauded Anastasius, the glorious sufferer, rejoicing with the angels, and praying for our souls.

*Both now, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*  
Having endured many sorrows at the crucifixion of thy Son and God, O all-pure one, she groaned with tears, crying aloud: Woe is me, sweet Child! How is it that Thou sufferest unjustly, desiring to deliver the earthborn of Adam's line? Therefore, O all-pure Virgin, we pray thee in faith: Make Him merciful unto us!

*Troparion of the Apostle, Tone 4:*  
Having learned goodness and being sober in all things,[^2238] vested with a good conscience as befits a sacred minister,[^2239] thou didst draw ineffable things from the chosen vessel,[^2240] and having kept the faith, thou didst finish a course like unto his,[^2241] O Apostle Timothy: entreat Christ God, that our souls may be saved.

*Troparion of the Martyr, the same Tone:*  
Thy martyr, O Lord, Anastasius, in his suffering received an incorruptible crown from Thee, our God; for having Thy strength, he cast down the torturers, and crushed the powerless boldness of demons: by his prayers save our souls.

*At Matins, one canon from the Octoechos, and two of the saints, unto 8.*  
*The Canon of the Apostle, whose acrostic is: "Timothy the Apostle I honor with songs." A composition of Theophanes. Tone 4.*  
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*  
Thy victorious right hand hath been glorified in power in a manner befitting God; for it, O Immortal One, being all-powerful, shattered the adversaries, making anew for the Israelites a path through the deep.[^2242]

*Troparion:*  
Dispel the uprisings of passions and the darkness of ignorance by thy prayers, O blessed one, through the radiant grace of dispassion, that I may now worthily hymn thee, the divinely-manifested.

*Troparion:*  
Beholding the beauty of thy mind, O Timothy, the Foreknower and God [showed thee] unto the divine apostles accounting thee worthy as a fellow-minister, through His wise providence caring for us.

*Troparion:*  
We know the one transcendent Beginning that foreknows all things; for from the Greeks the apostle was enlightened by the grace of Christ, and now Timothy is numbered with the divine Paul.

*Canon of the Martyr:*  
*Troparion:*  
Illuminated by the most radiant dawn of Thy Resurrection, O Christ, he who shares its name[^2243] hath darted forth from the East like the sun, and now illuminates the Church with miracles.

*Troparion:*  
Filled with divine love, thou didst patiently endure torments, O Martyr Anastasius; and adorned with ascetic virtues, thou didst joyfully offer thyself unto Christ as a sweet-smelling sacrifice, O blessed one.[^2244]

*Theotokion:*  
Rejoice, fountain of grace; rejoice, ladder and heavenly gate;[^2245] rejoice, candlestick and golden urn,[^2246] and unhewn mountain,[^2247] who gavest birth to Christ the Giver of Life unto the world.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*  
Thou Who alone knowest the weakness of human nature, and didst mercifully take form therein: gird me with power from on high,[^2248] that I may cry unto Thee: Holy is the animate temple of Thine ineffable glory, O Lover of mankind![^2249]

*Troparion:*  
Grace was poured forth richly upon thy lips, O all-blessed one,[^2250] and poured out rivers of dogmas which water the Church of Christ and bring forth abundant fruit, O preacher of Christ Timothy, divinely-wise apostle.

*Troparion:*  
Thy feet prophetically, O all-blessed one, were made beautiful; for thou didst preach the peace that surpasses all understanding, O all-wise one,[^2251] of the Savior of all and Lord Who dissolved the ancient enmity of men.[^2252]

*Troparion:*  
Having mortified thy earthly members,[^2253] thou didst subject that which is baser unto the Word, O blessed Timothy, granting dominion unto that which is better; and having restrained the passions, thou didst enlighten thy soul, guided by Paul's teachings.

*Canon of the Martyr:*  
*Troparion:*  
Shielded by holy ascetic life, first indeed through fasting, thou didst advance unto the glory of martyrdom; for through pains thou didst find delight for the sake of suffering, O glorious Martyr Anastasius, receiving heavenly beauty.

*Troparion:*  
The report of the pain of thy suffering went forth into all the universe, O invincible martyr; for resisting against sin even unto blood,[^2254] thou wast a victor and wast adorned with the crown of victory.

*Theotokion:*

From thee sprouted forth the unfading flower, O pure one,[^2255] which fills all mankind with fragrance through the divine myrrh of His own nature; He Who is co-beginningless with the Father, and of thee became subject to time, O all-immaculate Virgin.[^2256]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Go Thou before" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*  
Adorned with divine gifts, thou didst beautify the radiant metropolis of Ephesus, O glorious apostle; for shown to be a preacher, together with divine Paul thou didst proclaim the saving word unto all. Therefore with faith we celebrate thy memory.

*Glory, of the Martyr, the same Tone:*  
Most honorable wast thou shown to be by the glory of perfection, for having enlightened thy mind with divine light-radiance, and having known the strength of the Cross: through fasting thou becamest venerable, and through blood a martyr in a divinely-wise manner, O blessed Anastasius. Therefore Christ also pours forth through thee the gift of miracles.

*Now and ever, Theotokion:*  
O all-immaculate Virgin, who gavest birth unto God Who is transcendent in essence: together with the bodiless hosts unceasingly pray Him, to grant us remission of transgressions and correction of life before the end, unto us who with faith and love hymn thee as is meet, O only all-praised one.

*Stavrotheotokion:*  
When Thine all-pure Mother beheld Thee lifted up upon the Cross, O Word of God, weeping maternally she spoke: What is this new and strange wonder, O my Son?[^2257] How dost Thou, the Life of all, taste death,[^2258] desiring to give life unto the dead, as Thou art compassionate?

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*  
Perceiving thee with farsighted eyes as the mountain overshadowed by the grace of God, Habakkuk proclaimed that out of thee should go forth the Holy One of Israel,[^2259] for our salvation and renewal.

*Troparion:*  
Having chosen to suffer lawfully, O all-blessed one, through total abstinence thou didst subject the surging billows of the passions unto the mind, receiving the perfection of virtue, O great-preaching, divinely-wise Timothy.

*Troparion:*  
Paul, having shone forth like the sun, sent thee forth like a radiant ray, enlightening the universe with abundant light, light-manifestly, O divinely-manifested Timothy, for our guidance and confirmation.

*Troparion:*  
Having fervently desired the summit of desires, and being mingled with love, through affection thou didst pass over unto another life, O God-received one: ever contemplating Thy Beloved, and being filled with His vision.

*Canon of the Martyr, the same [Ode]:*

Nothing separated thee from the love that is toward Christ: not the cutting off of limbs, nor the threatening of wounds, nor the sword, nor death, nor fire, nor famine, O Anastasius,[^2260] fellow-sharer of heavenly rejoicing.

*Troparion:*
