Having zealously taken thy cross upon thy shoulder, thou didst follow Christ's saving commandments;[^2261] and having become His imitator even unto death, most excellently, now thou delightest in His brightness.

*Theotokion:*  
Coming manifestly from heaven, O pure one, the Archistrategos announced joy unto thee, saying: God shall come forth in the flesh from thee, O all-pure Virgin, for the salvation of those who hymn thee with love.[^2262]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*  
Being God of peace and Father of mercies, Thou hast sent unto us the Angel of Thy Great Counsel, Who grants peace;[^2263] therefore guided unto the light of divine knowledge, waking early from the night, we glorify Thee, O Lover of mankind![^2264]

*Troparion:*  
Enlightened by the immaterial radiances of the primal Light Who is the Cause of all, thou didst illumine the world by thy honorable preaching: holding forth the word of life,[^2265] thou wast clearly shown to be a light of piety, O all-blessed initiate of sacred mysteries.

*Troparion:*  
The true disciple of divine Paul follows the steps of his teacher, sowing his teachings unto the faithful; guided by which unto the light of piety, waking early from the night, we glorify Thee, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*  
In illumination thou wast shown to be a second Paul, O blessed one, ministering unto the primal Brightness; illuminate us through this knowledge, for Timothy was shown to be his partner, victoriously shielded by his armour.[^2266]

*Canon of the Martyr:*  
*Troparion:*  
He who before boasted immeasurably, threatening to encompass the earth and priding himself to swallow all the sea, through thy divine courage, O Martyr Anastasius, is trampled underfoot, the God-opposer.[^2267]

*Troparion:*  
Having suffered lawfully, the martyr of Christ openly receives the rewards of victory for his sufferings, the working of miracles; for he heals sicknesses and casts out demons, working wonders by the power of Christ, Anastasius.

*Theotokion:*  
The curse of Eve, the mother of all, thou didst annul by thy birthgiving, O Virgin,[^2268] having budded forth Christ, the Blessing unto the world; therefore rejoicing, with lips and tongue confessing thee truly to be the Birthgiver of God, we magnify thee.

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

The sea beast vomited forth Jonah from its entrails as an infant, just as it had received him; and the Word, having dwelt in the Virgin and taken flesh, came forth, having preserved her incorrupt; for He, having suffered no corruption, kept her who bore Him unharmed.[^2269]

*Troparion:*  
Thou wast shown to be a chariot of God, O Timothy, bearing His divine Name before the face of godless torturers, O God-received one,[^2270] not being terrified at their savagery; for thou wast clothed in the invincible strength of the Savior.

*Troparion:*  
Thou hast received a comely crown, O most wealthy Timothy, O divinely-wise apostle; and worthily wast thou arrayed for the ministry of the Kingdom, and hast stood before the throne of thy Master, rejoicing with Paul among the heavenly powers, O blessed one.[^2271]

*Troparion:*  
Inhaling the noetic myrrh of Christ, Who for our sake emptied Himself in the flesh, O all-honorable Timothy, thou didst receive His fragrance;[^2272] and thou didst impart it by faith unto those who flee unto thee, O initiate of ineffable things, through the intellectual affection of His love.

*Canon of the Martyr:*  
*Troparion:*  
Manifestly enlightened by the radiance of the Cross, thou didst dispel the gloom of deceit, and joining combat with the torturer, thou didst conquer, O all-glorious one; and rejoicing, thou didst receive thy tokens of victory, O martyr of Christ Anastasius, together with the choirs of the martyric armies.[^2273]

*Theotokion:*  
The whole choir of the prophets, instructed by God, foretold the mystery of the ineffable and divine conception of the divine Word from thee, O Virgin Mother; for thou hast revealed the most true and ancient counsel.[^2274]

*Kontakion, Tone 1, Podoben: "The Angelic Choir" (Ли́къ а҆́гг҃льскїй):*  
Let all us faithful hymn the divine disciple and traveling companion of Paul, Timothy,[^2275] with him honoring the wise Anastasius, who shone forth from Persia as a star,[^2276] and drives away our spiritual passions and bodily infirmities.

*Ikos:*  
More than the sun hath the yearly festival of the saints shone forth, and enlightened the faithful, and driven back the dark power of demons; and it cleanses infirmities, and fulfills the petitions of those who ask. Therefore do I, wretched, flee unto them, and pray from the pain of my passion-fraught heart, that I may receive what I desire, and find what I need: the changing of sorrow, and a life free of cares, and forgiveness of transgressions, and divine healing both spiritual and bodily.[^2277]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*  
Thee, O Mother of God, we the faithful perceive as a noetic furnace; as for just as the Exalted One saved the three children, so the praised and all-glorious God of our fathers hath wholly renewed the world in thy womb.[^2278]

*Troparion:*  
Having worthily become a fellow-chorister of the heavenly rank, thou makest merry joyfully, satisfied with the light-bestowing radiance, O blessed one, O sacred initiate of mysteries, Timothy: proclaiming the praised and all-glorious God.[^2279]

*Troparion:*  
Sacredly ministering the Gospel of Christ from the heights of virtue, the most divine Paul rejoicing sent divinely-inscribed epistles unto thee, his disciple, O Timothy:[^2280] proclaiming the praised and all-glorious God.

*Troparion:*  
Strengthening the weakness of the flesh by the good vigor of the soul,[^2281] for as one bodiless thou didst live upon earth, thou becamest a martyr, being crushed upon the head, O sacred minister of the mysteries of God, O divinely-blessed one.[^2282]

*Canon of the Martyr:*  
*Troparion:*  
The sufferer instructs the faithful, having clearly shown his courage as an example, now to emulate the most divine, painful Passion which He endured for our sake: the praised and all-glorious God of our fathers.[^2283]

*Troparion:*  
The equally potent Trinity is believed on by the lovers of piety; for the valiant sufferers suffered for Her sake, shedding their blood, valiantly contending, and openly surrendering their souls, and being slain.[^2284]

*Theotokion:*  
Rejoice, O pure one, from thee came forth the Shepherd, Who truly clothed Himself in Adam's skin,[^2285] for He, exalted eternally, [renewed] me, man, for the sake of His incomprehensible compassion: the praised and all-glorious God of our fathers.

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*  
The dew-bearing furnace depicted an image of a supernatural wonder; for it burned not the youths whom it received, just as the fire of the Godhead [burned not] the womb of the Virgin wherein He entered. Therefore singing let us sing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages![^2286]

*Troparion:*  
Being accounted worthy of the angelic station of the heavenly ranks, thou wast shown forth, O blessed Timothy; for having learned in a fitting manner, thou didst emulate their brightness, O wise one; with whom thou singest, making merry: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

*Troparion:*  
Being clothed with power from heaven, which came down in marvelous wise upon the disciples and eyewitnesses of the Word,[^2287] thou wast shown to be an apostle, O divinely-wise Timothy, with whom thou singest, rejoicing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

*Troparion:*  
Thou hast clearly reached the summit of desire, O all-blessed one, having attained good things, O Timothy, preacher of God, ever illumined by the light of the Trinity; and now thou singest, making merry: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

*Canon of the Martyr:*  
*Troparion:*  
From earth unto the heavens, crown-bearer, O martyr Anastasius, thou didst take flight, having escaped all demonic deceit, and having trampled underfoot the shrines of idols; therefore also now thou criest, rejoicing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

*Troparion:*  
Thou didst dye thy garment with thy martyric blood, O most wealthy martyr; and bearing the Cross as a scepter, thou reignest with Christ unto the ages, O Anastasius; unto Whom now thou singest, rejoicing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages![^2288]

*Theotokion:*  
The wealthy Word, Who is glorified with angelic hymns of praise, for our sake became poor, having chosen thee, the blessed one, as Mother, the excellency of Jacob;[^2289] therefore singing we chant: Let all creation bless the Lord, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*  
The bush burning with fire yet unconsumed showed forth an image of thy pure childbearing; and now we pray thee to quench the furnace of temptations that rages against us, that we may unceasingly magnify thee, O Mother of God.[^2290]

*Troparion:*  
The saying of David hath been fulfilled; for as lightning unto the universe thou didst appear, enlightening the ends [of the earth] by thy preaching, O ever-memorable, blessed Timothy;[^2291] therefore, O divinely-blessed one, we unceasingly magnify thee.

*Troparion:*  
Being filled with the light-originating radiance, O all-wise one, and purely delighting in the divine, tri-solar illumination, save from the gloom of transgressions those who praise thee, O blessed one, O all-honorable initiate of sacred mysteries.

*Troparion:*  
Rightly believing, we glorify Thee as equal to the Father and the Spirit, O Only-begotten One, being established by the teachings of Thine apostles, O Master: of Paul, the preacher of Thy dispensation, and of Timothy the divinely-wise.

*Canon of the Martyr:*  
*Troparion:*  
By the streams of thy blood, O glorious one, thou didst extinguish all idol deceit, and didst make bright the fullness of the Church; pray for her most excellently, cease not, O blessed one: that we all may call thee blessed.[^2292]

Above words is thy glory, and of the ineffable, truly divine radiance! Whereof Thou art a partaker as a conqueror, O Anastasius, standing before the Master Christ; Whom do Thou now also entreat for us who hymn thee.[^2293]

*Theotokion:*  
O thy awesome wonder! For thou, O Virgin Mother of God, having ineffably given birth unto God the Word, hast revealed the mystery hidden before generations and before ages in God Who created all things.[^2294]

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "O Light immutable" (Свѣ́те неизмѣ́нный):*  
Two luminaries shine luminously in the world: the great Timothy among Christ's apostles, and Anastasius, martyr of the like-minded; whom let us praise together.[^2295]

*Theotokion:*  
All we the faithful offer thee as mediatress unto Him Who was now born of thee, O all-immaculate one; and we are co-crucified with Him for the sake of that which is little better;[^2296] therefore cease not praying for us.

*At the Aposticha, from the Octoechos.*  
*Glory, Tone 5:*  
O venerable father, having become conqueror of the spiritual Medes and Chaldeans, thou didst cast down all the deceit of Babylon by the power of the Cross:[^2297] neither wast thou softened by the smoothness of pleasures, nor didst thou fear the fire of temptations. Therefore Christ our God crowned thee with tokens of victory. Therefore standing with the angels, pray unto the Lord, asking peace and great mercy for our souls.

*Both now, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 5, Podoben: "Rejoice, O container of ascetics" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ):*  
When thou, as a vine, didst put forth the unplanted, consecrated Cluster,[^2298] beholding Him suspended upon the Tree, and pierced in His divine ribs with a spear, what is this, didst thou say, O my Son and God? How dost Thou, Who healest all infirmities and passions, suffer passions, being impassible according to Thy divine nature? What have the ungrateful people rendered unto Thee, the Benefactor, in return for benefits? cried the all-immaculate one: but by His passions, unceasingly pray Him to deliver me from passions, that I may glorify thee.

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Octoechos on 4; and of the Apostle, Ode 3, on 4.*  
*Prokeimenon, Tone 8:*  
*Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the universe.*[^2299]  
*Verse: The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of His hands.*[^2300]  
*The Epistle of the Apostle to Timothy, section 280 from the midpoint [1 Tim. 1:12ff.]: "Child Timothy: I thank God..."*[^2301]  
*Alleluia Tone 1: The heavens shall confess Thy wonders, O Lord, and Thy truth in the church of the saints.*[^2302]
*The Gospel of Luke, section 50 [Luke 10:1–15].*[^2303]  
*Communion Verse: Their sound hath gone forth into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the universe.*[^2304]

*Month of the same, the 23rd Day.*  
*The Holy Hieromartyr Clement, Bishop of Ancyra; and the Holy Martyr Agathangelus.*

*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 6, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant among martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*  
Abiding in the faith as in Christ's vineyard, in due season thou didst receive the working of pains, O martyr, in manifold ways; therefore thou didst bring forth the fruit of salvation, eponymously named for the King and Husbandman,[^2305] O glorious hieromartyr Clement.

*Sticheron:*  
The fourfold seven of thy suffering, O wise one,[^2306] was shown to be truly honorable unto God, and unto angels, and unto all men; for having undergone the trial of bitter fire and cutting, and many wounds, traversing cities and countries, thou didst not depart from the love of Christ.

*Sticheron:*  
Having shone pastorally, O hieromartyr of Christ, thou didst valiantly exhibit martyric struggles: receiving as one a crown through both, adorned in both, in the priesthood and in the pains of martyrdom; therefore pray that we may be saved.[^2307]

*Other Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*  
A branch of the living vineyard wast thou shown to be, cultivated by mystical husbanding: trimmed indeed by the pains of fasting, O father, and pruned by the sword of martyrdom, thou didst mingle for us the wine of compunction;[^2308] wherewith now being satisfied, in faith we celebrate thine ever-memorable memory, O blessed one.

*Sticheron:*  
When thou didst sacredly celebrate the awesome, most perfect, and otherworldly Sacrifice, then wast thou thyself offered, O all-blessed one, through sacred ministry; and with a most zealous heart, O all-wise one, thou didst mingle thy blood with the blood of thy Master;[^2309] sprinkled wherewith, O blessed one, thou wast shown to be wholly pure, wholly most sacred, O speaker of God.

*Sticheron:*  
Sacrificing to the Lamb of God Who takes away the sins of the world,[^2310] and Who abolished corruption and death: as a blameless lamb thou wast sacrificed, O divinely-wise one, having become united in the likeness of His life-bearing death;[^2311] and now thou hast attained His Kingdom, O worthy of all beatitude.

*Glory, Tone 8:*  
The course of the four seasons thou didst multiply sevenfold, O divinely-called one:[^2312] being beaten, scraped, changing cities and countries, being crucified for Christ's sake; yet neither fire, nor sword, nor wounds dissolved the steadfastness of thy soul, and thou didst destroy the strength of demons, O hieromartyr Clement; therefore pray unto Christ that our souls may be saved.

*Both now, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 8, Podoben: "O martyrs of the Lord" (Мꙋ́ченицы гдⷭ҇ни):*  
I cannot endure, O Child, to see Thee fallen asleep upon the Tree, Who givest vigilance unto all: that unto those who slept of old with the sleep of perdition through the fruit of transgression, Thou mightest grant divine and saving vigilance,[^2313] said the Virgin, weeping, whom we magnify.

*At the Aposticha, Stichera of the Octoechos.*  
*Glory, Tone 4. By Anatolius:*  
The marvelous martyr among the priests, Clement, by the trial of torments over a long time, was accounted worthy to obtain the sweetness of eternal good things and of divine riches, having anointed many unto struggles by his own example, and having subdued the flesh, to think higher than death; unto whom let us the faithful cry aloud: O glorious great martyr, by thy prayers unto Christ, dissolve the year-long assaults of our passions, and deliver us from cruel things by thy prayers!

*Both now, Theotokion, or Stavrotheotokion, Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Небе́сныхъ чинѡ́въ):*  
Standing by the Cross of thy Son and God, and beholding His longsuffering, weeping the pure Mother said: Woe is me, sweetest Child! Why dost Thou suffer these things unjustly, O Word of God? That Thou mayest save mankind.[^2314]

*Troparion, Tone 4:*  
A shoot of holiness, and a stem of suffering, a most sacred blossom, and a God-given fruit, O all-sacred one, thou wast granted unto the faithful, ever flourishing;[^2315] but as fellow-sufferer of the martyrs, and fellow-enthroned with the hierarchs, pray unto Christ God that our souls may be saved.

*At Matins, both canons of the Octoechos; and of the Saint on 4. Whose acrostic is: "I sing"*[^2316] *the shoot of the noetic vine." A composition of Theophanes. Tone 6.*[^2317]

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*  
Having traversed the deep on foot as on dry land, Israel, seeing Pharaoh their pursuer drowning, cried aloud: Let us sing unto God a song of victory![^2318]

*Troparion:*  
Standing before Christ with the heavenly choirs as a priest and as a glorious martyr, fervently pray that those who praise thee may obtain thine illumination.

*Troparion:*  
Having completed extended struggles upon earth, O venerable one, thou wast accounted worthy to receive the crown of the heavenly Kingdom, and eternal, indestructible life.

*Troparion:*  
Delivered by the Passion of the Impassible One, by suffering thou didst hasten to attain unto Him, having clearly become an imitator of His sufferings, O fellow-companion of angels.[^2319]

*Theotokion:*  
Exceedingly adorned with the beauty of virtues, O all-pure Mother of God, thou didst conceive for us the Virtue of the true God, Who pours forth the wellspring of good things.[^2320]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*  
There is none holy as Thou, O Lord my God, Who hast exalted the horn of Thy faithful, O Good One, and established us upon the rock of Thy confession.[^2321]

*Troparion:*  
Fair fruits didst thou bring forth, having become a branch of the life-bearing Vine; and having adorned them with martyric splendors, thou didst consecrate them unto the Savior of all.[^2322]

*Troparion:*  
Thou wast shown to be an imitator of Paul, having traversed the whole universe, O all-blessed one, sanctifying [it] by God-working baptism and by the blood of the sprinkling of thy confession.[^2323]

*Theotokion:*  
None is undefiled as thou, O all-undefiled Mother of God; for thou alone from of old didst give birth above words unto the true God and Creator of all, God the Word.

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom and the Word" (Премꙋ́дрости):*  
The divinely-radiant star of Ancyra, the praise of Cappadocia,[^2324] let us piously honor: Clement, the much-suffering martyr, the glory of priests, the boast of the venerable, the defender of orphans, the champion of the poor, who having suffered into his twenty-eighth year, enlightened many, and the much-suffering martyr sanctified his homeland; and he prays unto Christ God to grant remission of transgressions unto those who honor his holy memory with love.[^2325]

*Glory, Both now, Theotokion:*  
As Virgin and the only one among women who without seed gavest birth in the flesh unto God, all we generations of men call thee blessed; for the fire of the Godhead dwelt in thee, and as an infant with milk dost thou nourish the Creator and Lord; therefore both the angelic and the human race worthily glorify thy most holy childbearing, and with one accord cry unto thee: Pray unto Christ God to grant remission of transgressions unto those who bow down in faith before thy most holy childbearing.[^2326]

*Stavrotheotokion:*  
Beholding the Lamb, the Shepherd, and the Deliverer upon the Cross, the Ewe-lamb cried aloud, weeping, and bitterly lamenting exclaimed: The world indeed rejoices, receiving deliverance through Thee, but my womb burns, seeing Thy crucifixion which Thou endurest through the tender compassion of mercy, O longsuffering Lord, abyss of mercy and inexhaustible wellspring; have compassion and grant remission of transgressions unto those who hymn Thy divine passions with faith.[^2327]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*  
Christ is my power, God and Lord, the honorable Church divinely sings, crying aloud from a pure mind, keeping feast in the Lord.[^2328]

*Troparion:*  
Having traversed the whole earth, thou didst stretch forth the branch of thy struggles, dropping down the joy of suffering and the sweetness of fragrance, O all-blessed passion-bearer.[^2329]

*Troparion:*  
Beholding the death of thy suffering, rejoicing we reap the blossoms of thy wounds, O blessed one, and by diverse miracles we gladden our senses.

*Troparion:*  
Thou wast a son of the day and of the never-setting Light, O marvelous one, unceasingly illuminated by the tri-solar light and by the radiance of preaching.[^2330]

*Theotokion:*  
O Mary all-pure, having become the spacious receptacle of purity for the divine indwelling: destroy my spiritual defilement and wretchedness.

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*  
With Thy divine light, O Good One, illumine, I pray Thee, the souls of those who rise early unto Thee with love, to know Thee, O Word of God, the true God, Who callest us back from the gloom of sins.[^2331]

*Troparion:*  
Enduring wounds of many years and prolonged duration, O all-wise one, thou wast much-suffering; and now thou hast inherited the everlasting sweetness of incorruptible blessedness.

*Troparion:*  
Having laid faith, hope, and love as a firm anchor and foundation,[^2332] thou didst offer thyself unto the honorable Trinity as an endowed temple, O father most wealthy.

*Troparion:*  
The divinely-adorned, most radiant pair [Clement and Agathangelus], having contended in the arena of suffering, having received eternal life, keeps festival and rejoices together with the angels.[^2333]

*Theotokion:*  
Desiring to save from corruption human nature that had corrupted, the Creator[^2334] and Lord, having dwelt in a womb purified by the Holy Spirit, was ineffably formed in fashion.[^2335]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*  
Beholding the sea of life surging with the storm of temptations, having fled unto Thy calm haven, I cry unto Thee: Lead up my life from corruption, O Plenteous in mercy![^2336]

*Troparion:*  
Having suffered lawfully, ye received crowns from the Master's hand, distributions of diverse gifts, and the grace of healings, and to cure the infirmities of the faithful.[^2337]

*Troparion:*  
A divine life, the manifestation of struggles, the extension of wounds: these became for thee a secret crowning of comeliness, and a diadem of beauty, and a garment of incorruption.[^2338]

*Theotokion:*  
Purify, O Lady, who didst give birth unto the Helmsman and Lord for earthborn men, the instability of my passions, and calm the cruel turmoil, and grant tranquility unto my heart.

*Kontakion, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared today" (Ꙗ҆ви́лсѧ є҆сѝ дне́сь):*  
Thou wast an honorable branch of the Vine of Christ, O much-suffering, all-praised Clement, shown forth; and with those who suffered thou didst cry aloud: Thou, O Christ, art the radiant rejoicing of martyrs.[^2339]

*Ikos:*  
Him who from infancy was sacredly suckled, the branch of the vine of Christ the King, let us the faithful honor with songs:[^2340] for he was shown to be truly honorable in gladness and beauty, unyielding in torments and sufferings, portrayed as a hierarch in the priesthood, and a partaker of the Kingdom of God; for having accounted as nothing the shrines of idols and the fury of torturers, in the arena he joyfully confessed the only Savior: Thou, O Christ, art the radiant rejoicing of martyrs.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*  
The youths in Babylon feared not the flame of the furnace, but cast into the midst of the flame, being bedewed they sang: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, God of our fathers![^2341]

*Troparion:*  
By the radiance of martyrdom thou didst illumine the universe, singing unto Christ with purity of mind and soul: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*  
The most sacred celebration of thy righteous deeds, shining with heavenly light, illumines those who cry: Blessed art Thou, O Lord, God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*  
Thou wast the Mother of all-wise Wisdom, O Virgin, Who wisely directs all things by natural grace; blessed, O all-pure one, is the fruit of thy womb.[^2342]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*  
Endangering themselves for their fathers' laws, the blessed youths in Babylon spat upon the foolish decree of the haughty king; and united, not being consumed by the fire, they sang a worthy hymn unto the Sovereign: Sing unto the Lord, ye works, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages![^2343]

*Troparion:*  
Having appeared upon earth as most radiant luminaries, ye illumine the firmament of the honorable Church, O most wealthy ones; and in the heavens with the radiance of your suffering, in the assembly of the firstborn, ye make merry, crying aloud:[^2344] Sing unto the Lord, ye works, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

*Troparion:*  
With gladness we now celebrate the joyful memory of thy struggles: for as one incorporeal thou didst endure the surging billows of wounds; but instead of these thou hast worthily received as a rich recompense everlasting food, crying aloud: Sing unto the Lord, ye works, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

*Troparion:*  
Thou hast clothed thyself with an adorned and most radiant garment of glory, instead of the spirit of cruel despondency, O most wealthy one;[^2345] instead of torments, thou didst exchange them and receive the angelic dwelling of everlasting life, crying: Sing unto the Lord, ye works, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*  
From the ever-existing Begetter, the co-eternal and co-comprehended Word, at the end of the ages having become incarnate of the Virgin,[^2346] made the whole human form divine, having inconfusedly united [it] unto Himself according to hypostasis:[^2347] Sing unto the Lord, ye works, and exalt Him supremely unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*  
It is not possible for men to see God, upon Whom the ranks of angels dare not gaze;[^2348] but through thee, O all-pure one, the incarnate Word hath appeared unto men; Whom magnifying, with the heavenly hosts we call thee blessed.[^2349]

*Troparion:*  
Sanctified by the font of luminous baptism, and with the chrism of the priesthood, and washed with martyric blood, O blessed one:[^2350] adorned, rejoicing thou didst ascend unto the heavenly armies, O divinely-blessed one.

*Troparion:*  
The Word of God, the crown of the holy martyrs, the never-setting Sun of righteousness,[^2351] adorned thy holy head with a crown of gifts, O marvelous one; for Whose sake rejoicing thou didst endure prolonged struggles.

*Theotokion:*  
The unoriginate Son and Word of God, having become incarnate, becomes the Son of the Virgin by the good pleasure of the Father and the cooperation of the Divine Spirit,[^2352] and wholly renewed my corrupted form, as He is almighty.

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Жены̀ оу҆слы́шите):*  
Even as Paul the apostle, thou didst traverse all the earth, and with prolonged[^2353] struggles, O Clement, thou didst stretch forth a branch, and with the net of faith thou dost catch Agathangelus, fellow-communicant and co-martyr, the sufferer named after good tidings.[^2354]

*Theotokion:*  
Thou art my protection, O all-pure one, and a firm refuge; thou art also my intercessor and shelter, and unto thee I fall down, crying aloud: Deliver me from my tribulations, as thou hast given birth unto Joy, and snatch me who hope in thee from the eternal fire, O Virgin.[^2355]

*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes of the Octoechos; and Ode 3 of the Saint, on 4. Prokeimenon, Tone 7:* Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His venerable ones.[^2356] *Verse:* What shall I render unto the Lord for all that He has rendered unto me?[^2357] *Epistle to the Hebrews, section 334.*[^2358] *Alleluia, Tone 2:* Thy priests shall be clothed with righteousness, and Thy venerable ones shall rejoice.[^2359] *Gospel of John, section 36.*[^2360] *Communion Verse:* In everlasting memory shall the righteous be.[^2361]

*Month of the same, the 24th Day.*  
*Our Venerable Mother Xenia.*[^2362]  
*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Octoechos, 3; and of the Saint, 3.*  
*Tone 1, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Небныхъ чино́въ):*  
Having first transformed thyself from worldly love, O venerable one, and confirmed thyself by deed with better thought, thou didst go forth from the vanity of pleasure's crookedness, O blessed one; and walking rightly in the arduous ascent of virtues, thou didst live as a stranger.[^2363]

Hastening unto the divine haven, thou didst peacefully pass through the tempests of worldly turmoil, steering the ship of thy soul unswamped, O divinely-wise one, away from the bitterness of pleasures, full of mystical treasures.[^2364]

In a manner befitting God, emulating Him Who for our sake descended from above to raise up the fallen, thou didst live as a stranger, O wise one, remaining unknown to thy kinsfolk, but known rather to the pious, ever praying unto God, O Xenia.[^2365]

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

Exceedingly glorified art thou in generations of generations, O Virgin Maiden Mother, Birthgiver of God Mary, protection of the world, having in the flesh given birth unto the Son of the unoriginate Father, Who is truly co-eternal with the Spirit: entreat Him that we may be saved.[^2366]

*Stavrotheotokion:*  
When the blameless Virgin beheld the Lamb lifted up upon the Cross, weeping she cried aloud: "O my sweetest Child, what is this new and glorious sight? How dost Thou Who holdest all creation in Thy palm hang upon the Tree, nailed in the flesh?"[^2367]

*Troparion, Tone 8:*  
In thee, O mother, was preserved that which was according to the image; for having taken up the Cross, thou didst follow Christ, and by thy deeds thou didst teach to despise the flesh, for it passes away, but to care for the soul, a thing immortal: therefore, O venerable Xenia, thy spirit rejoices together with the angels.[^2368]

*At Matins, both Canons of the Octoechos; and of the Saint on 4, Tone 8.*  
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*  
Let us send up a hymn, ye people, unto our marvelous God, Who freed Israel from bondage, singing a song of victory and crying aloud: We sing unto Thee, the only Master.[^2369]

*Troparion:*  
Me who am a stranger to every virtue and estranged from God by unseemly deeds, reconcile unto Him through thy well-pleasing prayers, O honorable and all-praised Xenia,[^2370] as I bless thy strange and marvelous life.[^2371]

*Troparion:*  
A noetic fire kindled thee, as combustible material, to despise worldly deceit, and persuaded thee with most courageous resolve to renounce a carnal betrothed, and to betroth thyself purely unto the Lord.[^2372]

*Troparion:*  
Having strangely perceived the life that abides in the heavens and never passes away, thou didst exchange thy name as well as thy deeds, and didst run like a thirsting hart after the immortal Bridegroom.[^2373]

*Theotokion:*  
With hymns let us, the faithful, praise the all-honorable Mary, the joyous Mother of God, the divine protection, the calm haven, the salvation of all the faithful.[^2374]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*  
O Lord, Who didst establish the heavens by Thy word, and didst found the earth upon many waters: establish me unto the singing of Thy glorification.[^2375]

*Troparion:*  
Having held fast the divine desire of thy soul, O honorable one, it persuaded thee to receive forgetfulness of the pains of fasting and of nature.[^2376]

Delighting in the beauties of the immortal Bridegroom, thou didst wither the comeliness of the flesh, and wast revealed most beautiful, having dwelt within the divine bridal chamber.[^2377]

*Troparion:*  
Having acquired the gilded wings of virtues, thou didst soar unto the heavenly height, O blessed one, like an incorruptible dove.[^2378]

*Theotokion:*  
O luminous cloud of the intelligible and all-radiant Sun Who shone forth from thy womb, O Virgin: enlighten the souls of those who hymn thee.[^2379]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom and the Word" (Премꙋ́дрости):*  
Having for the sake of the tender mercy that appeared on earth loved the Word of God the Father, thou didst follow Him as thy Bridegroom, O all-blessed one, and didst eagerly forsake a corruptible bridegroom, forsaking also corruptible wealth: therefore, eponymously living in estrangement, thou didst mortify the passions and didst inherit the heritage of the living, O divinely-inspired one: entreat Christ God to grant remission of transgressions unto those who celebrate thy holy memory with love.[^2380]

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*  
Having fallen into manifold temptations from visible and invisible enemies, held fast by the tempest of my countless transgressions: as unto my fervent protection and shelter, O pure one, I flee unto the haven of thy goodness. Therefore, O all-honorable one, pray earnestly unto Him Who was incarnate from thee without seed on behalf of all thy servants who unceasingly pray unto thee, O all-pure Birthgiver of God, ever entreating Him to grant remission of transgressions unto those who worthily hymn thy glory.[^2381]

*Stavrotheotokion:*  
The Ewe-lamb, beholding the Lamb and Shepherd and Deliverer upon the Cross, cried out weeping and bitterly lamenting, exclaiming: "The world indeed rejoices, receiving redemption through Thee, but my womb burns beholding Thy Crucifixion, which Thou dost endure through tender compassion of mercy, O long-suffering Lord, Abyss of mercy and inexhaustible Fountain: have mercy and grant remission of transgressions unto those who with faith hymn Thy divine sufferings!"[^2382]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*  
From the overshadowing mountain, O Word—from the only Birthgiver of God—the prophet divinely foresaw Thee about to become incarnate, and with fear glorified Thy power.[^2383]

*Troparion:*  
As a dowry unto Christ thou didst offer purity, the mortification of limbs, and the afflictions of abstinence: and thou didst receive the heavenly Kingdom and everlasting delight.[^2384]

*Troparion:*  
Setting forth thyself as an example unto virgins, thou didst draw many souls unto salvation, tearing thyself away from worldly attachment, O divinely-wise and all-laudable Xenia.[^2385]

*Troparion:*  
Wetting thy bed with tears, O venerable one, and eating bread with ashes, thou didst receive an unfading consolation and the delight of paradise.[^2386]

*Theotokion:*  
Rejoice from us, O holy Birthgiver of God; rejoice, thou who didst bring forth joy unto the world; rejoice, thou only defense of mankind: blessed and pure Birthgiver of God.[^2387]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*  
Dispel the gloom of my soul, O Giver of light, Christ God, having driven away the primal darkness of the abyss, and grant unto me the light of Thy commandments, O Word, that rising early I may glorify Thee.[^2388]

*Troparion:*  
As a heifer desiring the divine beauty of the Shepherd, thou didst cry aloud: "Where pasturest Thou now, O Bridegroom? Where restest Thou, tell me: I long to see Thy most excellent appearance, and I am wholly inflamed!"[^2389]

*Troparion:*  
Unto those who love My beauty, the Bridegroom exclaims: "Seeking, O honorable one, shining with virtues, look upon Me in the heavens: there do I pasture, and thither do I ever summon My sheep."[^2390]

*Troparion:*  
A most beautiful turtledove, a most radiant swallow, and a spiritual nightingale, flying above the sufficiency of noetic snares, wast thou revealed, O honorable Xenia, and all-laudable in thy desire for Christ's beauty.[^2391]

*Theotokion:*  
Motherless on high, unto those below in the latter times thou dost give birth without a father unto Him Who shared our nature, O Virgin, through His great tender mercy: entreat Him to save from corruption those who hymn thee.[^2392]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*  
Cleanse me, O Savior, for many are mine iniquities, and bring me up from the depth of evils, I pray Thee: for unto Thee have I cried, and give ear unto me, O God of my salvation.[^2393]

*Troparion:*  
Glorifying thy strange life and thy fasting surpassing human nature, He Who for thy sake lived as a stranger, O glorious one, truly adorned thee, O venerable one, with signs and most glorious wonders.[^2394]

*Troparion:*  
Crowned with the circle of virtues, thou didst ascend unto Christ Whom thou didst desire, while a crown of stars marvelously proclaimed thee beyond mind unto those near and far, O glorious Xenia.[^2395]

*Troparion:*  
Estranged far from the commandments of our God, make me His own through Thy venerable supplications, and make me a stranger unto the bitter Gehenna and unto the passions that hold me fast.[^2396]

*Theotokion:*  
He Who sits uncircumscribably upon the shoulders of the Cherubim, dwelt circumscribed within thy womb in the flesh, but not in His Godhead, and came forth from thee, saving mankind.[^2397]

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "The shedding of thy blood" (Крове́й твои́хъ):*  
Celebrating thy marvelously strange memory, O Xenia, we who honor thee with love hymn Christ, Who in all things grants thee power of healings: pray thou unto Him unceasingly on behalf of us all.[^2398]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*  
O Thou Who didst bedew the youths in the furnace, and didst preserve the Virgin who bore Thee after childbirth: blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.[^2399]

*Troparion:*  
Rome boasts in thy swaddling clothes, but Mylasa rejoices having acquired thy relics, from which wonders pour forth unto the faithful, O bride of God.[^2400]

*Troparion:*  
Thou wast revealed as a river of healings, drowning the sea of passions of those who sing: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers.[^2401]

*Troparion:*  
Thou didst lull to sleep soul-destroying passions in many vigils, O blessed one, and didst fall asleep in a sleep like unto the righteous, praying for the world.[^2402]

*Theotokion:*  
Praying unceasingly unto Him Who was incarnate from thee beyond understanding, O all-hymned Birthgiver of God, cease not to deliver our souls from the snares of the enemy.[^2403]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*  
O Thou Who coverest Thy chambers with waters, Who settest the sand as a boundary for the sea, and holdest all things: the sun sings of Thee, the moon glorifies Thee, all creation offers a hymn unto Thee, as the Creator of all, unto the ages.[^2404]

*Troparion:*  
Having been betrothed, as it is written, unto one Husband, Christ, Who is fair in comeliness, thou didst piously learn every form of virtue, O glorious one, and didst dwell in the divine bridal chamber, receiving as a dowry the grace of healings unto all ages.[^2405]

*Troparion:*  
"My soul has cleaved after Thee, O Christ," thou didst cry aloud with love; "as a thirsty land I seek Thee, the Living Water, O Lord; unto Thee I offer clouds of tears; with the stream of Thy love water me, O Savior, unto all ages."[^2406]

*Troparion:*  
Thou wast adorned having loved that which is truly desirable; thou didst glorify [thyself], O maiden, having cleaved unto the exceedingly glorified God: thou didst lead a holy choir of virgins unto the Savior who emulated thee, with whom thou dost exult in the heavenly mansions.[^2407]

*Theotokion:*  
The Father's Word chose thee alone as the beauty of Jacob, and dwelt within thee, and as He was well pleased passed through, He Who is fairer than all sons of men, O all-honorable one, cleansing our darkened nature.[^2408]

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*  
Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, Who has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of His servant David, whereby the Dayspring from on high has visited us, and has guided us into the way of peace.[^2409]

*Troparion:*  
Through weakness, O glorious one, thou didst conquer the powerless enemy, living a stranger's life and having mortified the carnal passions: and now thou dwellest in the heavens, where thou hast thy true citizenship, as a pure virgin.[^2410]

*Troparion:*  
Blessed is the Lord, Who has revealed thy precious shrine as a calm haven of healings unto us who are ever imperiled in the deep and by the tempest of passions: O glory of monastics and praise of virgins, God-bearing Xenia.[^2411]

*Troparion:*  
As a temple of virginity, as a pure dove, as a blameless turtledove, as a bride of Christ fair in comeliness and immaculate, as an image of divine virtues, as an enclosed garden,[^2412] do we, the faithful, honor thee, O God-bearing Xenia.[^2413]

*Theotokion:*  
Following thy words, generations of generations ever call thee blessed, O blessed one: for thou, O pure Virgin, didst truly give birth unto the blessed God, Who unfailingly makes blessed all those who serve Him.[^2414]

*Month of the same, the 25th Day.*  
*Our Father among the Saints Gregory the Theologian, Archbishop of Constantinople.*[^2415]  
*If the Superior wills, we celebrate a Vigil.*  
*At Small Vespers, Stichera, Tone 1, Podoben: "As one valiant among martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*  
With thy theological lips, * O theologian Gregory, * and with thy theological tongue, * thou didst preach the consubstantial God * sung in Trinity: * the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit. * Thou didst refute the folly of the Hellenes, * and didst clearly proclaim the truth * in divinely-uttered words.[^2416]

Both thy countenance was venerable * and thy look reverent, * O holy Gregory: * therefore with joyful singing we honor thee and say: * Rejoice, O spiritual star, * illuminating the ends of the earth with the brightness * of thy most wise sayings! * Rejoice, trumpet proclaiming unto the world * the commandments of Jesus![^2417]

The many-voiced instrument, * the musically attuned harp, * the sweet-breathing pipe and lute, * the highest of hierarchs, the great teacher of the Church of Christ, * let us praise, singing: * Rejoice, depth of divine grace! * Rejoice, height of heavenly understandings, * father of fathers, Gregory![^2418]

With the sling of thy divine, * God-inspired words, * powerfully and most gloriously thou didst smite Arius like a wolf, * and didst drive him far from the flock of Christ, * O most excellent shepherd: * warming and refreshing thy sheep * with the pasture of the consubstantial Trinity: * therefore we honor thee, * O shepherd of shepherds, Gregory![^2419]

*Glory, Tone 6:*  
Having assembled, O ye who are wise in God, let us praise with spiritual praises the leader of hierarchs, the honor of patriarchs, the initiate of the seers of God, and the supreme intellect in understanding Christ, saying: Rejoice, fount of theology, river of wisdom, and stream of divine understanding! Rejoice, most radiant star, for with thy dogmas thou dost enlighten the whole world! Rejoice, great champion of piety and valiant dispeller of impiety! But, O all-wise theologian Gregory, cease not to pray unto Christ God on behalf of those who ever celebrate with faith and love thy God-pleasing and honorable memory![^2420]

*Both now:*  
*O Birthgiver of God, thou art the vine...*[^2421]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "House of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*  
A second son of thunder * wast thou shown to be * by the providence of God, * and a theologian unto the world, O Gregory, * both disciple and bosom friend.[^2422]

*Verse:* My mouth shall speak of wisdom, and the meditation of my heart shall be of understanding.[^2423]  
Like the shining of lightning * went forth thy utterance, * truly enlightening the faithful * but casting down the heretics * with thunderous arrows.[^2424]

*Verse:* The mouth of the righteous shall meditate on wisdom, and his tongue shall speak of judgment.[^2425]  
Thy mind was ignited with fire * and flame-bearing were thy lips, * wherewith the rages of those who hold heresy * are consumed, O Gregory together with their godless teachings.[^2426]

*Glory, Tone and Podoben the same:*  
Unto the venerable Trinity: * the Father, the Word, * and the Spirit: * the divine theologian * taught us to believe, * as one indivisible God.[^2427]

*Both now:*  
Preaching the One of the all-creating * Trinity, * Who sprouted forth from the Virgin, * thou stoppest, O Gregory, * the mouths of heretics.[^2428]

*At Great Vespers, we sing: "Blessed is the man," the first antiphon.*  
*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 8. Tone 4, Podoben: "O all-praised martyrs" (Бѡ́зꙋхва́льні́и мꙋ́ченицы):*  
O father Gregory, * neither did the grave, mediator of forgetfulness, * close thy lips: * for thou wast revealed as the mouth of theology, * proclaiming even now * the dogmas of piety unto the universe. * Therefore pray * that unto our souls may be granted * peace and great mercy.[^2429]

O father Gregory, * wisely didst thou turn away from the well-settled * and insidious flesh: * and mounting the heavenly four-horse chariot of virtues, * thou didst soar * unto the ineffable Beauty, * wherewith being filled, thou now bestowest upon our souls * peace and great mercy.[^2430]

O father Gregory, * unto God and men * thou wast a faithful mediator by grace: * and having now made Christ * favorable unto us by thy bold prayers: * cease not, O venerable one, entreating the Lord * to grant peace and great mercy unto our souls.[^2431]

*Other Stichera, Tone 2, Podoben: "With what praises" (Кі́ими похва́лными):*  
With what sacred songs shall we praise the divinely-speaking Gregory? The eye of grace and the all-wise mouth of the Holy Spirit, the radiant luminary of the universe, the great instruction of the Church, the glory of Orthodoxy, the divinely-marvelous stream of theology, the ever-flowing river of divine dogmas, the ever-gushing fountain of the divine water of incorruption! *Twice.*[^2432]

With spiritual love today let us hymn the hierarch, equal in character unto the apostles and champion of piety, the deluge of eloquence, the most sweet torrent of teaching, the firmness of elevated words, the unbridled mouth, the fire-breathing tongue, the treasury of wisdom, the preacher of the Word, the adornment of the faithful.[^2433]

With what due [hymns] shall we all praise the Theologian? The guardian of Christ's flock, the hunter of wolves and all-wise captor who rooted out adulterous offspring, the sower of upright dogmas, the all-marvelous; the most powerful driver-away of heretics, who truly by divine vigilance multiplied the talents of Christ, as was fitting, and enlightened the world with the divine brightness of his teachings![^2434]

*Glory, Tone 8:*  
Thy tongue, vigilant unto teaching, sounding aloud in the ears of hearts, raises up the souls of the slothful; and by thy divinely-uttered words a ladder is found leading upward from earth unto God. Therefore, O theologian Gregory, cease not to pray unto Christ that our souls may be saved from tribulations.[^2435]

*Both now, Theotokion:*  
*The King of heaven...*[^2436]

*Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day.*  
*And the Readings:*  
*The Reading from Proverbs (Chapter 10):*[^2437]  
The memory of the righteous is with praises, and the blessing of the Lord is upon his head.[^2438] Blessed is the man that has found wisdom, and the mortal that knows understanding.[^2439] For it is better to traffic for her than for treasures of gold and silver. And she is more precious than costly stones; and everything that is honored is not worthy of her. For length of days and years of life are in her right hand, and in her left hand are riches and glory. Out of her mouth proceeds righteousness, and law and mercy she bears upon her tongue.[^2440] give ear then unto me, O children, for I will speak honorable things; and blessed is the man that shall keep my ways; for my goings out are the goings out of life, and preparation of will from the Lord.[^2441] Therefore I beseech you, and put forth my voice unto the sons of men; for I, wisdom, have set up counsel, and understanding and knowledge have I called upon. Mine is counsel and safety, mine is understanding, and mine is strength. I love them that love me, and they that seek me shall find grace.[^2442] Understand, therefore, ye simple ones, subtlety; and ye untaught, lay it to heart. Give ear unto me yet again, for I will speak honorable things, and I will open upright things from my lips; for my throat shall meditate truth, and false lips are an abomination before me. All the words of my mouth are with righteousness; there is nothing crooked or perverse in them. They are all upright to them that understand, and plain to them that find knowledge. For I instruct you in truth, that your hope may be in the Lord, and that ye may be filled with the Spirit.[^2443]

*The Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon (Chapter 4):*[^2444]  
The mouth of the righteous drops wisdom, and the lips of wise men know grace.[^2445] The mouth of the wise meditates on wisdom and righteousness delivers them from death.[^2446] When a righteous man dies, his hope perishes not.[^2447] For a righteous son is born unto life, and in his good things he shall reap the fruit of righteousness.[^2448] There is light for the righteous evermore, and from the Lord they shall find grace and glory.[^2449] The tongue of the wise knows good things, and in their heart wisdom rests.[^2450] The Lord loves venerable hearts, and acceptable unto Him are all they that are undefiled in the way.[^2451] The wisdom of the Lord illuminates the countenance of the prudent.[^2452] For she anticipates them that desire her, before that they know her, and she is easily seen of them that love her. He that rises early unto her shall have no great travail, and he that watches for her shall quickly be without care.[^2453] For she goes about herself seeking such as are worthy of her, and shows herself favorably unto them in the ways.[^2454] Wickedness shall never prevail against wisdom.[^2455] For these things' sake I became a lover of her beauty, and I loved her and sought her out from my youth; and I desired to make her my spouse, for the Master of all loved her.[^2456] For she is an initiate of the knowledge of God, and a chooser of His works.[^2457] Her labors are virtues: for she teaches temperance and prudence, justice and fortitude, than which nothing is more profitable in life for men.[^2458] And if a man desire much experience, she knows the things of old, and considers things to come; she knows the subtilties of speeches and the solutions of riddles; she foresees signs and wonders, and the issues of seasons and years: and unto all she is a good counselor, for immortality is in her, and good report in communion with her words.[^2459] For this cause I spake unto the Lord, and made supplication unto Him, and said from my whole heart: O God of the fathers and Lord of mercy, Who hast made all things by Thy word, and by Thy wisdom hast fashioned man, that he should have dominion over the creatures made by Thee, and rule the world in holiness and righteousness: Give me wisdom, that sits by Thy thrones; and reject me not from among Thy children: for I am Thy servant and son of Thine handmaid.[^2460] Send her out of Thy holy heavens, and from the throne of Thy glory, that being present she may labor with me, that I may know what is pleasing before Thee: and she shall lead me soberly in understanding, and preserve me in her glory.[^2461] For the thoughts of mortal men are fearful, and their devices are fallible.[^2462]

*The Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon (Chapter 4):*[^2463]

Though the righteous man happen to die, he shall be in rest.[^2464] For venerable age is not that of many years, neither is it measured by number of years.[^2465] But wisdom is the gray hair unto men, and an unspotted life is the ripeness of old age.[^2466] Pleasing God, he became beloved, and living among sinners, he was translated.[^2467] He was snatched away, lest wickedness should alter his understanding, or deceit beguile his soul.[^2468] For the fascination of wickedness darkens good things, and the roving of desire transforms the innocent mind.[^2469] Being made perfect in a short time, he fulfilled long years; for his soul was pleasing unto the Lord: therefore He hastened to take him away from the midst of iniquity.[^2470] But the peoples saw it, and understood it not, neither laid they such a thing to their mind: that grace and mercy are in His holy ones, and visitation among His elect.[^2471]

*At the Litiya, the Sticheron of the Temple.*  
*Then the Stichera of the Saint, Tone 4: Automela.*  
*By Anatolios.*  
Having opened thy mouth by the Word of God, * thou didst draw down the Spirit of wisdom; * and being full of grace, * thou didst thunder forth divine teachings, * O thrice-blessed Gregory: * and having joined the angelic powers, * thou didst preach the light of the Trinity and indivisible. * Therefore, illuminated by thy divinely-spoken utterances, * we worship the Trinity known in one Godhead, * unto the salvation of our souls.[^2472]  

With thy fiery, divinely-speaking tongue, O Gregory, * thou didst burn up the god-fighting babblings of heretics: * for thou wast truly revealed as the divine mouth * proclaiming by the Spirit the great things of God, * and depicting in writings the equally potent essence of the hiddenly-mystic Trinity; * and having enlightened the earthly world with the three-sun light, * thou prayest unceasingly for our souls.[^2473]  

*Glory, Tone the same:*  
Lawfully purifying body and soul through divine actions, * thou didst pass beyond the boundaries of theology, * initiating the divine mysteries, O divinely-manifest Gregory: * and having entered into the unwaning darkness, * thou didst receive the God-inscribed lawgiving, * having written of the consubstantial Trinity; * worshipping Whom through thee, * singing we say: * O Unity understood in Trinity, have mercy on us![^2474]  

*Both now, Theotokion:*  
*Look down upon the entreaties...*[^2475]  

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 5, Podoben: "Rejoice" (Ра́дуйся):*[^2476]  

Rejoice, fount of theology and dwelling of exalted contemplation of God: * for having investigated the supreme depth with pious mind, O father, * thou didst elucidate unto all: * that in three suns there is one blending of light, * united by the identity of Godhead, * yet existing in Trinity by venerable hypostases. * Therefore, teaching by the purity of thy life and the radiance of thy words * to honor the all-holy Trinity, O divinely-inspired one, * pray that great mercy be sent down upon our souls.[^2477]  

*Verse:* My mouth shall speak of wisdom, and the meditation of my heart shall be of understanding.[^2478]  

By the dawn of thy theology * thou didst destroy the dark fury of heresies: * for having anticipated the Fount of illuminations with pious mind, O theologian, * thou didst partake of the divinely-wise splendors granted therefrom. * For having made thy mind luminous as a mirror, * thou didst receive the light of the Trinity of the Godhead, O father, indivisible and most brilliant, * and richly didst contain the unified beam: * Whom entreat now to grant great mercy unto our souls.[^2479]  

*Verse:* The mouth of the righteous shall meditate on wisdom, and his tongue shall speak of judgment.[^2480]  

Rejoice, river of God, * which art ever full of the waters of grace, * making glad every city of Christ the King * with divine words and teachings: * sweet-flowing torrent, inexhaustible abyss, * certain and lawful guardian of dogmas, * most fervent champion of the Trinity, * instrument of the Holy Spirit, * vigilant mind, clear-sounding tongue expounding the depth of the Scriptures: * pray Christ now to grant great mercy unto our souls.[^2481]  

*Glory, Tone 8:*  
Farming the hearts of the faithful with thy tongue, O Gregory, * thou didst cause to grow therein unto God the ever-blooming fruits of piety: * cutting down thorny heresies from the root, * and adorning them with the purity of understanding. * Therefore, receiving our praises, O divine lute, * vigilant eye, shepherd of shepherds, hunter of wolves: * pray fervently, O theologian, unto the Word on behalf of our souls.[^2482]  

*Both now, Theotokion:*  
*O unwedded Virgin...*[^2483]  

*Troparion, Tone 1:*  
The pastoral pipe of thy theology * conquered the trumpets of the rhetors; * for having searched out the depths of the Spirit, * the beauties of utterance were also added unto thee; * but pray Christ God, O father Gregory, * that our souls may be saved.[^2484]

*At Matins, at "God is the Lord", the Troparion twice. Glory... Both now:*  
*When Gabriel proclaimed...*[^2485]  

*After the first Stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 3, Podoben: "Of divine faith" (Бж҃е́ственныя вѣ́ры):*[^2486]  
Having inherited divine radiance, * thou didst abound in an immaterial life, * excelling by the priesthood of identical name; * for having supernaturally elucidated the dogmas, * thou didst confirm the faith with Orthodoxy, O venerable father: * entreat Christ God to grant great mercy unto us.[^2487]  

*Glory:*  
Thou wast a pillar of the Church, * an unstolen wealth of piety, * thou didst appear, O theologian Gregory: * having made thy life radiant by dispassion, * and having elucidated the dogmas of the Trinity. * O venerable father, pray Christ God * to grant great mercy unto us.[^2488]  

*Both now, Theotokion:*  
Thou wast the divine tabernacle of the Word, * O only all-pure Virgin Mother, * who by purity didst surpass the angels: * cleanse me who beyond all others am dust, * defiled by carnal transgressions, * with the divine waters of thy prayers, * granting, O pure one, great mercy.[^2489]  

*After the second Stichology, Sessional Hymn, Tone 5, Podoben: "Co-beginningless Word" (Собезна́чалное сло́во):*[^2490]  
Having been vigilant by the word of truth, * having theologically praised the dominion of the Trinity, * having cast down the impiety of Arius * and his most lawless blasphemy, * as a champion and defender of piety, O hierarch, * thou didst enlighten those sitting in the darkness of ignorance. *Twice.*[^2491]  

*Glory... Both now, Theotokion:*  
Swiftly heal the many-painful passions of my soul * and the infirmities of my flesh, * and still the wanderings of my mind, O all-immaculate one: * and vouchsafe me in tranquility of thoughts to offer pure prayers * unto the King of all, O Birthgiver of God, * and to ask for the remission of transgressions.[^2492]  

*After the Polyeleos, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom [and Word]" (Премꙋ́дрости):*[^2493]  
Having refuted the deception of the impious, * having opened the Scriptures in a God-befitting manner, * Thou didst send forth dogmas sweetening the hearts of the faithful more than honey, * clearly, O praiseworthy one, * to serve the Trinity in the unity of the Godhead; * therefore Thou didst set forth the image of the Savior upon the icon to be kissed, * having substantially [assumed] humanity, O theologian Gregory: * pray Christ God to grant remission of sins * unto those who celebrate with love thy holy memory. *Twice.*[^2494]

*Glory... Both now, Theotokion:*  
When the Master and Creator of all shall come to judge the whole earth, * count me who am condemned among the sheep on the right hand: * and from the outer darkness and from all torment * snatch me away, Thine unprofitable servant, I pray. * That thankfully I may magnify the wealth of thy goodness, O all-immaculate Birthgiver of God, * and cry unto thee rejoicing: * Pray Christ God to grant me remission of transgressions; * for I, thy servant, have thee as my hope.[^2495]  

*And we read from the Life of the Saint.*  
*The Songs of Ascents [Anabathmoi], the first Antiphon of Tone 4.*  
*Prokeimenon, Tone 4:*  
*My mouth shall speak of wisdom, and the meditation of my heart shall be of understanding.*[^2496]  
*Verse:* Hear this, all ye nations, give ear, all ye that inhabit the world.[^2497]  
*Let every breath...*  
*The Gospel according to John, Section 35 [Jn 10:9-16].*[^2498]  
*After Psalm 50, Sticheron, Tone 6:*  
O venerable, thrice-blessed, most holy father, * good shepherd and disciple of Christ the Chief Shepherd, * who didst lay down thy life for the sheep: * do thou also now, O all-praised theologian Gregory, * ask by thy prayers that great mercy be granted unto us.[^2499]  

*Canon of the most holy Birthgiver of God with the Heirmos on 6, and two of the Saint on 8.*  
*Canon of the Birthgiver of God, Tone 8.*  
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*  
Let us sing unto the Lord, Who led His people through the Red Sea, for He alone is gloriously glorified.[^2500]  

*Troparion:*  
O all-pure Birthgiver of God, who beyond nature didst give birth unto the incarnate, ever-existing, and supremely divine Word: we hymn thee.[^2501]  

*Troparion:*  
The Virgin gave birth unto Christ, the life-bearing cluster of grapes that drips forth the sweetness of universal salvation.[^2502]  

*Troparion:*  
The race of Adam, led up through thee, O Birthgiver of God, unto the beatitude that is beyond understanding, worthily glorifies thee.[^2503]  

*Then the Canon of the Saint, whose acrostic is: "I sing the divinely-speaking, ever-memorable Gregory."*  
*A composition of Theophanes. Tone 1.*  
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*  
Christ is born, give ye glory! Christ comes from heaven, meet ye Him! Christ is on earth, be ye exalted! Sing unto the Lord, all the earth, and with gladness hymn Him, O ye peoples, for He is glorified![^2504]  

*Troparion:*  
Come, ye lovers of his words, having assembled with love let us praise the second Theologian, the bright heavenly pillar, the trumpet of the wisdom of God, as a preacher of God.[^2505]  

*Troparion:*  
The co-beginningless Word of the Father, the Provider of all as God, by providential power gives thee, O blessed one, as a gift unto the Church as unto a mother, having enriched thy mind with word and wisdom.[^2506]  

*Troparion:*  
Making the mind master, thou didst restrain carnal passions; and having become capable of containing divine illuminations, thou didst enlighten us to honor the one God in three Persons, O Gregory.[^2507]  

*Theotokion:*  
The Wisdom of God built Himself a temple, having dwelt within thy most immaculate womb, O full of grace: and having united Himself hypostatically beyond understanding unto this [flesh], O pure one, He appeared as man.[^2508]  

*Another Canon, a composition of Cosmas the Monk, Tone the same.*  
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*  
Moses the beholder of God proclaims the praise beforehand unto Israel, and Mariam leads the wise women in the song of victory: Let us all sing unto God our Redeemer![^2509]  

*Troparion:*  
Having escaped the ancestral [error], and having stood offering the God-flowing blood over those passions that were cast aside as a sacrifice: do thou also now, O all-wise Gregory, render God easily reconciled unto us faithful.[^2510]  

*Troparion:*  
Having once entered into the darkness, Moses received the God-inscribed tablets: but thou, having set up a God-acceptable table in thy mind, didst fervently entreat God.[^2511]  

*Theotokion:*  
Wishing in His tender mercy to recall human nature once more from death and corruption, the supremely divine One dwelt within thy pure womb, O all-immaculate Virgin.[^2512]  

*Katavasia:*  
*The sun once looked down upon the dry land born of the deep...*[^2513]  

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*  
Thou art the confirmation of those that flee unto Thee, O Lord; Thou art the light of the darkened, and my spirit hymns Thee.[^2514]  

*Troparion:*  
Grant us help by thy prayers, O all-pure one, repelling the assaults of cruel circumstances.[^2515]  

*Troparion:*  
Thou wast the setting-aright of our foremother Eve, having given birth unto Christ, the Author of life, for the world, O Birthgiver of God.[^2516]  

*Troparion:*  
Gird me with power, O all-pure one, who in truth didst give birth in the flesh unto God, the hypostatic Power of the Father.[^2517]  

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*  
Unto the Son begotten incorruptibly of the Father before the ages, and in these latter times incarnate seedlessly of the Virgin, unto Christ God let us cry: Thou Who hast exalted our horn, holy art Thou, O Lord![^2518]  

*Troparion:*  
Possessing the fount of wisdom, unceasingly pouring forth of thy most wise teachings, O all-blessed one, thou didst fill the Church of Christ, crying aloud unto God Who is over all: Holy art Thou, O Lord![^2519]

*Troparion:*  
A loud-voiced preacher of piety, and an illustrious theologian of theology: the treasury of the vision of God is bountifully set forth, and richly distributes unto us an inexhaustible wealth.[^2520]  

*Troparion:*  
A fiery-inspired rhetor, a divinely-speaking lute of grace, having sounded forth illustriously by theological inspiration and divinely-breathed utterance, sang unto us the hymn of the three-hypostatic Essence.[^2521]  

*Theotokion:*  
O Birthgiver of God, Queen of all creation, cease not praying unto Christ the King of all, Whom thou didst bear for us unto the salvation of those upon earth, to save those who hymn thee.[^2522]  

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*  
Having undoubtingly promised the venerable Samuel unto God before conception, the holy mother Anna now rejoicing sings with us: My heart is established in the Lord![^2523]  

*Troparion:*  
Before coming forth from the womb of her who bore thee, thou wast foretold, O venerable father; bearing a worthy title, O most wise hierarchical leader, with all our soul we cry unto thee: Rejoice, O father![^2524]  

*Troparion:*  
Before even choosing evil things, thou didst choose God-beholding purity and chastity as a spouse and helper through manifest divine things, O champion of the faithful; rejoicing, we cry unto thee: Rejoice, O father![^2525]  

*Theotokion:*  
Thou didst set right the former stumbling of our foremother Eve, having received into thyself, by unconquerable power, the Word of the Father Who raises up those cast down, O Virgin Mother.[^2526]  

*Katavasia:*  
*O Lord, the confirmation of those that hope in Thee...*[^2527]  

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom [and Word]" (Премꙋ́дрости):*[^2528]  
Having opened thy mouth by the Word of God, * thou didst pour forth wisdom, O preacher of light: * and having sown divine understanding in the universe, * thou didst truly confirm the dogmas of the fathers, * and according to Paul wast revealed as a champion of the faith. * Therefore thou art also a fellow citizen of the angels, * and didst appear as their conversational partner, O blessed one: * O theologian Gregory, pray Christ God to grant remission of transgressions * unto those who celebrate with love thy holy memory. *Twice.*[^2529]  

*Glory... Both now, Theotokion:*  
Having slipped through evil thoughts, I have fallen into the depths of sin, and groaning I cry unto thee from the heart, O all-pure one: * make marvelous upon me thy rich mercy * and the boundless abyss of thy compassion * and the unnumbered wealth of thy bounties, * and grant me repentance and forgiveness of transgressions, * that with love I may cry unto thee: * Pray Christ God to grant me remission of transgressions; * for I, thy servant, have thee as my hope.[^2530]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*  
I heard, O Lord, the mystery of Thy dispensation; I understood Thy works, and I glorified Thy divinity.[^2531]  

*Troparion:*  
O unplowed field that didst grow the life-bearing Wheat that gives life unto the world: O Birthgiver of God, save those who hymn thee.[^2532]  

*Troparion:*  
Enlightened, we all know thee as the Birthgiver of God, O all-pure one; for thou didst bear the Sun of righteousness, O Ever-Virgin.[^2533]  

*Troparion:*  
Grant us cleansing of our ignorances, for Thou art without sin, and give peace unto Thy world, O God, through the prayers of her that bore Thee.[^2534]  

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*  
A rod from the root of Jesse and a flower from him, O Christ, Thou hast budded forth from the Virgin; from the mountain overshadowed and dense, O praised One, Thou hast come, incarnate from the unwedded [Maiden], O immaterial One and God: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^2535]  

*Troparion:*  
Having become an initiate of the Trinity, thou didst illuminate the universe with understanding, O wise one, flashing forth the beams of dogmas, O venerable one, of thy certain teaching; meditating ever upon which, we all piously praise thee.[^2536]  

*Troparion:*  
A radiant morning of piety, having received the three-sun beam within thyself thou didst shine forth, and the dark night of impious heresies thou didst drive away by the dawn of thy wise dogmas, and didst make clear the souls of the faithful, O father.[^2537]  

*Troparion:*  
Having pre-purified thy mind, O father, from visible perceptions, and having been taught by the transcendent Mind, the Fount of Word and Spirit, the ever-existing One: with theological thunder, O all-blessed one, theologically speaking thou didst piously teach of Him.[^2538]  

*Troparion:*  
Thou didst ascend the mountain of virtues, departing from the earthly and retreating from dead works; and as tablets inscribed by the hand of God, thou didst receive the dogmas of thy pure theology, O mystagogue of divine mysteries, Gregory.[^2539]  

*Theotokion:*  
Thou didst raise up Adam who had fallen in understanding, O all-immaculate one, having given birth unto the hypostatic Life from virginal loins sanctified by the Spirit; and unto the dispassionate, most divine, and incorruptible food, thou didst lead him up, O Birthgiver of God.[^2540]

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*  
Standing with the marvelous Habbakuk upon thy divine watch, O Gregory, and having known Him Who sits upon the cherubic shoulders, thou wast a proclaimer of universal salvation, ever crying: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^2541]  

*Troparion:*  
Likening thyself unto the chief ranks that appear near and stand before God, O all-wise one, flying with thy mind above them, yet not attaining to the depth of that supreme standing, thou didst bring forth thence unto men an inalienable wealth.[^2542]  

*Troparion:*  
Having entered into the incomprehensible darkness, and as from the cleft of the rock having beheld His back parts: thou wast the proclaimer of the material mingled with the immaterial nature, and of the unconfused mixture, O pleaser of Christ, entreating Him to be merciful unto His servants.[^2543]  

*Theotokion:*  
Thou wast revealed as a spiritual mountain, from which the precious Stone was cut without hands, crushing the image of dark deceit, and illuminating with the radiance of grace those who ever cry with faith: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^2544]  

*Katavasia:*  
*Thy virtue has covered the heavens, O Christ...*[^2545]  

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*  
Rising early from the night we cry unto Thee: O Lord, save us; for Thou art our God, besides Thee we know none other.[^2546]  

*Troparion:*  
Still the intolerable storm of my passions, O thou who didst give birth unto God, the Helmsman and Lord.[^2547]  

*Troparion:*  
The angelic ranks and the assemblies of men minister unto thy childbearing, O all-pure Birthgiver of God.[^2548]  

*Troparion:*  
O Mary, unwedded Birthgiver of God, make vain the hopes of the enemies, and gladden those who hymn thee.[^2549]  

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*  
Being the God of peace and Father of bounties, Thou hast sent unto us the Angel of Thy great counsel, granting peace; therefore, guided unto the light of divine knowledge, rising early from the night we glorify Thee, O Lover of mankind.[^2550]  

*Troparion:*  
The divine utterance of thy words and the divine grace of thy dogmas traversed the whole earth like the swiftness of lightning, theologically teaching and instructing us to worship the Trinity in Unity, and the Unity in Trinity, O theologian.[^2551]  

*Troparion:*  
Truly thou didst desire the wisdom of God, and didst love the beauty of words, preferring them above all fair things on earth: therefore He adorned thee in a God-befitting manner with a crown of gifts, O all-blessed one, and made thee a theologian.[^2552]  

*Troparion:*  
Wisely didst thou desire to behold Him Who is, O divinely-speaking one, as once did Moses; and covered by the rock, thou wast vouchsafed to see His back parts: and thou didst learn the abysses of divine wisdom that are incomprehensibly manifested.[^2553]  

*Theotokion:*  
He Who of old fashioned Eve thy foremother is fashioned from thee, manifestly healing and loosing her condemnation and disobedience, as the compassionate One and Master of all, O Birthgiver of God, Virgin Mother.[^2554]  

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*  
The burning coal that was once applied unto the lips of Isaiah, taken by the seraph with tongs, having been applied: and he, cleansed, proclaimed unto all to learn righteousness.[^2555]  

*Troparion:*  
Having approached this fire of the vision of God, O all-blessed Gregory, with purity of mind and soul, unobstructedly and spontaneously thou didst draw forth the three-shining light of equal dignity.[^2556]  

*Troparion:*  
Having shone with the rays of the three-sun illumination, inflamed by the radiance, and illuminating the mind with divine beams, thou didst flash forth counter-shining rays unto all.[^2557]  

*Theotokion:*  
Having received Light of Light, the co-beginningless only-begotten Word of the Father, O Virgin Mother: thou wast manifestly the Gate of light, having caused the Sun of righteousness to shine upon all.[^2558]  

*Katavasia:*  
*As Isaiah saw the coal in a figure...*[^2559]  

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*  
Grant me a robe of light, Thou that clothest Thyself with light as with a garment, O most merciful Christ our God.[^2560]  

*Troparion:*  
As the temple and ark of God, the animate bridal chamber, and the heavenly gate, do we faithful proclaim thee, O Birthgiver of God.[^2561]  

*Troparion:*  
As God the Deliverer of souls, Thy childbearing, O Mother and Bride of God, is worshipped together with the Father and the Spirit.[^2562]  

*Troparion:*  
The Word of God revealed thee unto earthborn men as the heavenly ladder, O Birthgiver of God; for through thee He came down unto us.[^2563]  

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*  
From the belly the sea monster cast forth Jonah like a babe, just as it had received him; and the Word, having dwelt within the Virgin and taken flesh, came forth, having preserved her incorrupt: for He kept unharmed her that bore Him, suffering no corruption.[^2564]  

*Troparion:*  
By the streams of thy wise teachings, O all-wise one, thou didst dry up the turbid mind of Arius, preserving thy flock unsubmerged in tranquility, like a spiritual ark, wherein thou didst place the seeds of piety through the beauty of thy words.[^2565]  

*Troparion:*  
That thou mightest enrich thy mind with the radiance of the honorable Trinity, O father: thou didst make it bright as an unblemished and newly-instructed mirror, having fashioned it through extraordinary abstinence. Therefore thou wast also shown to be most God-beholding through divine manifestations.[^2566]

*Troparion:*  
Wholly mingled with the dawn of the Spirit, thou wast an all-radiant lamp, O father: illuminating the ends of the earth with the brightness of thy words, and adorning with the purity of theology the fair triumph of the faithful, O theologian Gregory.[^2567]  

*Troparion:*  
Thou wast revealed as a new God-given Samuel, given unto God even before conception, O all-blessed one: adorned with chastity and purity, and embellished with the all-holy vesture of the priesthood, O father, mediating between the Creator and the creation.[^2568]  

*Theotokion:*  
As a clean scroll receiving the written Word, formerly uncircumscribed in Godhead, thou wast foreknown by the prophets and of old, O Virgin Mother Mary, Bride of God: for thou didst ineffably contain in thy womb the Incontainable One.[^2569]  

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*  
Having suffered confinement in the deep to escape the tempest, and by the casting of lots, and caught in the mouth of the sea monster, Jonah remained unharmed, but cried: Unto Thee let my life ascend, O Christ![^2570]  

*Troparion:*  
Not having been drowned in understanding, and having searched out the divine depths to the very bottom, thou didst thence draw forth the pearl for the Master, O Gregory; and thou didst most excellently establish silence as a word.[^2571]  

*Troparion:*  
By pure prayer thou didst calm the raging sea, and having braided the brine of strange words, for the Master thou didst set right the faithful people like a certain drop, O Gregory.[^2572]  

*Theotokion:*  
Incomprehensible to human thoughts is the mystery of thy ineffable and awesome childbearing, O Mother of God: for having given birth unto the Creator of all, O Virgin, a Virgin thou didst remain.[^2573]  

*Katavasia:*  
*The Elder cried unto Thee, having seen with his eyes...*[^2574]  

*Kontakion, Tone 3, Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дв҃а дне́сь):*[^2575]  
Having dissolved the entanglements of the rhetors with thy theological tongue, O glorious one, * thou didst adorn the Church with the garment of Orthodoxy woven from above: * which she, wearing, cries with us thy children: * Rejoice, O father, supreme intellect of theology![^2576]  

*Ikos:*[^2577]  
Fill my poor and passionate mind with thy theological and exalted wisdom, that I may hymn thy life, O father: for I cannot offer a word unto thee unless thou grant me strength of word, understanding, and wisdom and wisdom: that I may offer unto thee thine own from thine own, and from the riches of thy virtues may find cause therefor, and may crown thy precious and holy head, crying out with the faithful: Rejoice, O father, most supreme mind of theology![^2578]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*  
The youths having come from Judea in Babylon of old, by faith in the Trinity trampled down the flame of the furnace, singing: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.[^2579]  

*Troparion:*  
Having become incarnate from virginal loins, Thou didst appear for our salvation; therefore, knowing Thy Mother to be the Birthgiver of God, we cry out in orthodox manner: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.[^2580]  

*Troparion:*  
Thou hast budded forth as a rod from the root of Jesse, O Virgin most blessed, bearing a blossoming and saving fruit unto those who cry out with faith to thy Son: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.[^2581]  

*Troparion:*  
O hypostatic Wisdom of the Most High, fill with all divine wisdom and power those who with faith sing unto thee, O Birthgiver of God: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.[^2582]  

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*  
The youths nurtured together in piety, having disregarded the ungodly command, were not afraid of the threat of fire, but standing in the midst of the flame, sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.[^2583]  

*Troparion:*  
Thy word is manifestly all desire and sweetness, all full of joy and brightness, O Gregory, filling with sweet fragrance those who sing with faith: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.[^2584]  

*Troparion:*  
With an enlightened mind thou didst attain unto the Source of illuminations, and being enkindled by lightnings therefrom, thou didst burn up the idle babbling of Eunomius,[^2585] crying out unto the Trinity: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.[^2586]  

*Troparion:*
