Having opened the cataracts of the abyss of thy wise dogmas, and having made to gush forth the fountain of wisdom,[^2587] thou didst cover over the leaders of error, being irradiated with the eternal and thrice-sunlit Light.[^2588]  

*Theotokion:*  
Having descended like dew upon the fleece, the River of peace, the Fountain of goodness, He that numbers the raindrops, took up His dwelling in thy womb: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.[^2589]  

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*  
They passed through the unbearable flame of the furnace as through a bridal chamber, the holy youths who of old manifestly showed themselves forth for piety's sake, and harmoniously chanting a hymn, they sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.[^2590]  

*Troparion:*  
Standing before the tribunals of unjust governors, O Gregory, thou didst burn up with piety the onrushes of the heretics that breathed more fiercely than fire, crying out unto the Trinity: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.[^2591]  

*Troparion:*  
Having poured out upon the earth from thy lips an untroubled fountain of pious dogmas, O Gregory, thou hast shown the all-hymned Trinity to the inhabitants, watering them to blossom: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.[^2592]  

*Theotokion:*  
The forefather is put to death, having untimely tasted of sweetness; but thou, having brought forth the endless Life, the Word, hast raised him up to dwell in Paradise, O pure and blessed Birthgiver of God.[^2593]  

*Katavasia:*  
*Unto Thee Who didst bedew the youths in the fire...*[^2594]  

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*  
The King of heaven, Whom the angelic hosts hymn, praise ye and supremely exalt unto all ages.[^2595]  

*Troparion:*  
Extinguish the deceitful and flaming arrows of the adversaries directed against us, that we may hymn thee, O pure one, unto all ages.[^2596]  

*Troparion:*  
Supernaturally hast thou given birth unto the Creator and Savior, God the Word, O Virgin; therefore do we hymn thee, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^2597]  

*Troparion:*  
The unapproachable Light that took up His dwelling in thee, O Virgin, hath shown thee forth to be an illuminating and gold-gleaming candlestick unto all ages.[^2598]  

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*  
The furnace pouring forth dew prefigured the image of a supernatural wonder; for it burned not the youths whom it received, even as neither did the Fire of the Godhead burn the womb of the Virgin into which It entered. Therefore in praise let us sing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^2599]  

*Troparion:*  
Thou hast piously taught that the Word and the Spirit are equal unto the Father in goodness and kingdom, knowing Their essential and natural identity and unity. Therefore thou criest out rejoicing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^2600]  

*Troparion:*  
Thou wast accounted worthy of angelic glory, for as an angel thou didst blossom forth unto the world, having diligently purified soul, body, and mind for the Trinity, O all-wise one; unto Whom thou now singest with rejoicing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^2601]  

*Troparion:*  
Having rendered the Master merciful through thy prayers, ask remission of transgressions, O father, for those who celebrate with faith thy sacred and all-festive memory, in which with rejoicing we sing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^2602]  

*Troparion:*  
Having become an initiate of the tri-hypostatic monarchy and of the Godhead existing in Trinity through exercises in virtues, thou wast shown forth to be a theologian of the Trinity, O all-blessed one; and now thou singest rejoicing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^2603]  

*Theotokion:*  
The opulent Word Who is glorified by archangelic hymnody became poor for our sake, having chosen thee as His Mother, the blessed beauty of Jacob. Therefore in praise we sing: Let all creation bless the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^2604]  

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*  
The youths who defiled not themselves with the food of the king's table of old entered rejoicing into the fire, and bedewed in the flame, they zealously sang: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord.[^2605]  

*Troparion:*  
Having risen above the Babylonian flame, O father, and being enkindled with piety even more than that fire, thou wast shown forth as a heavenly initiate and preacher of the Trinity, crying out: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord.[^2606]  

*Troparion:*  
Having extinguished the fire of the varied tribulations and of the iron furnace, O father, and easily passing through tribulations, thou hast flown up to heaven, crying out: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord.[^2607]  

*Theotokion:*  
The gold-appearing candlestick prefigured thy divine childbearing, O undefiled and pure one; for thou didst cause the unapproachable Light to shine forth upon the world, unto Whom we cry: Hymn the Lord, all ye works of the Lord.[^2608]  

*Katavasia:*  
*Unto the unbearable fire...*[^2609]  

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*  
In truth do we confess thee to be the Birthgiver of God, who are saved through thee, O pure Virgin, magnifying thee with the bodiless choirs.[^2610]  

*Troparion:*  
Full of joy and gladness is thy memory, pouring forth healings unto those who approach and who piously proclaim thee to be the Birthgiver of God.[^2611]  

*Troparion:*  
With psalms do we hymn thee, O full of grace, and unceasingly cry out "Rejoice!": for thou hast poured forth joy unto all.[^2612]  

*Troparion:*  
Fair did thy fruit bud forth, O Birthgiver of God, mediating not corruption, but life unto those who partake thereof, who magnify thee with faith.[^2613]  

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*  
The burning bush unconsumed revealed the image of thy pure childbearing, and now we pray thee to extinguish the raging furnace of temptations that assaults us: that we may unceasingly magnify thee, O Birthgiver of God.[^2614]  

*Troparion:*  
The Sovereign Trinity, Whom thou didst confess as God, grants Thee incorruptible life, having accepted for Its sake thy struggles, teachings, and com- bats; before Whom thou now standest, O father, an exquisite intercessor for the world.[^2615]

*Troparion:*  
Illuminated by the beam of the tri-radiant brightness proceeding from the one Godhead, O Gregory, sacred initiate of mysteries, save those who sing unto thee with faith, and enrich them with the light of the theology of thy dogmas.[^2616]  

*Troparion:*  
Thou hast fought the good fight, contending for the Sovereign Trinity, and hast obtained deification as a theologian; and thou hast worthily received the fulfillment of thy divine desire, O fair embellishment of the Church.[^2617]  

*Theotokion:*  
O thy dreadful wonder! For thou, O Virgin Birthgiver of God, having given birth unto God the Word, hast ineffably revealed the mystery hidden before generations and before ages in God Who made all things.[^2618]  

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*  
Thou who didst piously open the supreme depth of divine incomprehensibility, and who by mind didst raise up the unhewn stone unto the God-originating Trinity, O all-blessed father, we magnify thee.[^2619]  

*Troparion:*  
Thou who didst rend the poor garment of the legal writing, and who didst expound unto us the divine and mystic beauty therein of the Scriptures of the divine Spirit, O thrice-blessed father, we magnify thee.[^2620]  

*Troparion:*  
Being numbered among the heavenly choirs, O venerable father, for with them thou dwellest unto the ages, offer prayers unto God for thy flock, O all-blessed father, we magnify thee.[^2621]  

*Troparion:*  
Instructed in divine things by the divine and transcendent inspiration, O venerable father, and through thy boundless desire having been mystically initiated into their untaught union, O all-blessed father, we magnify thee.[^2622]  

*Theotokion:*  
Thou, O pure one, wast the dwelling place of the divine nature that is above all praise, as lending flesh unto God, Who opened not the portals of thy virginity when giving birth without seed; we magnify thee.[^2623]  

*Katavasia:*  
*In the shadow and letter of the Law...*[^2624]  

*Exapostilarion, Tone 3, Podoben: "By the Spirit" (Дх҃омъ):*[^2625]  
The sword of thy words and the power thereof cut off the tongues of the unfaithful utterly; for like a scourge thou didst burn up their thorny and godless novelties; thou didst teach to worship the Trinity in a God-befitting manner, O Gregory the Theologian.[^2626]  

*Glory... Tone 2, Podoben: "With the disciples" (Со ᲂу҆чени́ки):*[^2627]  
Unto the tri-hypostatic Monad and the all-perfect Trinity in one Godhead, O all-wise theologian, thou didst teach to bow down: calling the Father Light, and the Son Light, and again Light the Holy Spirit; yet one Light, indivisible, unconfused; for God is one, and thou didst explain the consubstantiality, O blessed Gregory.[^2628]

*Both now, Theotokion:*  
Together with the Mother of God and Virgin Mary, and with the great Basil, O all-wise one, standing before the unapproachable Trinity: ask peace for the world, victory for the pious King,[^2629] and salvation for us who now praise thee, O theologian, hierarch Gregory, orator of the Church.[^2630]  

*At the Praises, Stichera of the Saint, on 4, Tone 4, Podoben: "Called from on high" (Зва́нный свы́ше):*[^2631]  
Having cut through the darkness of the letter, * thou didst enter in the Spirit unto the highest Light; * and having received the illumination therefrom, * thou didst enrich all by theology, * O all-wise Gregory, * luminary of the Church; * and by the splendors of thy words * thou didst dispel the gloomy clouds of heresies. * Therefore thou dwellest where the voice of those who keep festival is heard, * a companion of the angels, * unceasingly praying * that our souls may be saved.[^2632]  

Second theologian and initiate * of the divine radiance, * luminous describer of the heart, * who concerning the ineffable and divine Nature * didst supernaturally teach, O Gregory: * and now more brightly delighting in God, * remember those who honor thee, * and fight for the Church * which thou didst assemble; * for thy sound went forth * unto all the ends of the universe,[^2633] * teaching to glorify * the consubstantial Trinity.[^2634]  

Having cultivated the earth with thy tongue, O divinely-speaking one, * [sowing] the divine seed into the furrows of the heart, * by the highest theology thou didst enrich * the whole fullness of the Church. * Therefore by the fire of the Spirit * thou didst burn up the heretical tares, * nourished by the love of divine philosophy: * O father of fathers, * and shepherd of shepherds, * and boast of the faithful, * luminary of priests, * glory of the universe, * O all-blessed Gregory.[^2635]  

Having brought thy precious lips near unto the cup of wisdom, * O father Gregory, * thou didst draw forth the divine water of theology, * and didst abundantly impart it unto the faithful; * thou didst dam up the soul-corrupting torrent of heresies * that was full of blasphemy; * for the Holy Spirit found thee to be a helmsman * who didst thrust away and drive off, like blasts of wind, * the assaults of the ungodly, * proclaiming the Trinity * in Unity of essence.[^2636]  

*Glory, Tone 4:*  
The lute of the Spirit, the conqueror of heresies, the delight of the Orthodox, the second beloved disciple, who became an eyewitness of the dogmas of the Word, the wise chief of shepherds, let us nurslings of the Church praise with theological hymns: Thou art the shepherd who didst give thyself, O Gregory, even as Christ the Master did for us; and thou dancest with Paul, and prayest for our souls.[^2637]  

*Both now, Theotokion.*  
*Great Doxology, and Dismissal.*  
*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes from the Canon of the Saint, Ode 3 and Ode 6.*  

*Prokeimenon, Tone 1:* My mouth shall speak of wisdom, and the meditation of my heart shall be of understanding.[^2638] *Verse:* Hear this, all ye nations; give ear, all ye that inhabit the universe.[^2639] *Epistle to the Corinthians, section 154.*[^2640] *Alleluia, Tone 2:* Attend, O My people, to My law; incline your ear to the words of My mouth.[^2641] *Gospel of John, section 36.*[^2642] *Communion Verse:* In everlasting memory shall the righteous be.[^2643]  
*At the table, consolation for the brethren, and we read the Life of the Saint.*[^2644]  

*Month of the same, the 26th Day.*  
*Our Venerable Father Xenophon and his Companions:*[^2645]  
*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera of the Octoechos, 3; and of the Saint, 3, Tone 2, Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Є҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*[^2646]  
Shining with the dignity of the soul, * by almsgiving and faith thou didst illuminate the physical man: * Rejoice, thou hast dispersed, thou hast given to the poor, * and thy righteousness abides unto the age; * the never-setting Light hath shone forth upon thee, O father, * where thou beholdest thy venerable children * and their holy mother, * living in the heavenly city.[^2647]  

Having despised corruptible glory, * ye were accounted worthy of incorruptible and divine glory; * for having trampled down all the beauty of life, * ye exceedingly desired Christ, the truly Beautiful One, O God-bearers, * Who saved you from the worldly tempest and storm, * and directed you unto a calm and light-bearing life, * O most wealthy ones.[^2648]  

Having mortified the carnal passions, ye clothed yourselves in the garments of dispassion, having woven them by the purity of your life; and having manifestly displayed an angel-like life while yet in the body, O stout-hearted ones, ye all were accounted worthy of angelic glory in the highest, delighting in divine brightness.[^2649]  

*Glory... Both now, Theotokion:*  
Thou alone, O all-immaculate Bride of God, didst bear within thy womb the uncontainable God in an uncontainable manner, Who for our goodness' sake became man; therefore I pray thee: Deliver me from the passions that oppress me, that having walked along the narrow and straight path, I may attain unto that which leads unto life, O Virgin.[^2650]  

*Stavrotheotokion:*  
When the pure one beheld Him hanging upon the Tree, the all-ripe Cluster Whom she had borne in her womb without cultivation, weeping she cried out and exclaimed: O Child, drop down sweetness, whereby all the drunkenness of passions may be taken away, O Benefactor, being entreated by Thy tender mercy for the sake of me who bore Thee.[^2651]  

*Troparion, Tone 4:*  
O God of our fathers, Who dealest ever with us according to Thy gentleness, turn not Thy mercy away from us; but through their intercessions direct our life in peace.[^2652]  

*At Matins, both Canons of the Octoechos; and the Canon of the Saints, on 4. Whose acrostic is: "I sing Xenophon with his spouse and children. A work of Theophanes." Tone 2.*[^2653]  

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*  
Come, ye peoples, let us sing a hymn unto Christ God, Who divided the sea and guided the people whom He brought out of the bondage of Egypt, for He hath been glorified.[^2654]  

*Troparion:*  
Now together with your whole household receiving the Tree of life and true delight of Paradise, O all-wise ones: pray unto the Lover of mankind to save those who praise you.[^2655]  

*Troparion:*  
Walking fervently in the path of Thy commandments, O Master, Thy servant reached the mansions, delighting with double desire in eternal life.[^2656]  

*Troparion:*  
Thou didst show thy house unto all as a new tabernacle of Abraham; therefore, O marvelous one, thou didst worthily and righteously find rest in the bosom of Abraham.[^2657]  

*Theotokion:*  
Wholly taking up His dwelling in thee, O all-immaculate one, renewing all of me, man, He that shone forth from the Father before all ages, the unoriginate Word.[^2658]  

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*  
Having established me upon the rock of faith, Thou hast enlarged my mouth against mine enemies; for my spirit hath rejoiced to sing: There is none holy like our God, and none righteous more than Thee, O Lord.[^2659]

*Troparion:*  
Honored with the brightest dignities, adorned with a light-bearing life, thou didst show forth action to be the ascent unto contemplation, crying out: Thou art our God, and there is none holy more than Thee, O Lord.[^2660]  

*Troparion:*  
Having become the steward of all, thou didst take up care for all, distributing thy wealth unto those in need, and receiving with wisdom the monastic ranks, O venerable father.[^2661]  

*Troparion:*  
Nourished by the laws of the Master, in the law and by instruction and admonition of the Lord thou didst instruct thy children, crying out, O marvelous one: Thou art our God, and there is none holy more than Thee, O Lord.[^2662]  

*Theotokion:*  
Come, ye faithful, let us hymn Mary, who alone remained a Virgin after childbearing, the holiest of the holy, the unwedded Birthgiver of God, crying out: Rejoice, O pure Mother; rejoice, O Sovereign Lady.[^2663]  

*Kontakion, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared" (Ꙗ҆ви́лсѧ є҆сѝ):*[^2664]  
Thou didst keep vigil in the commandments of the Master, quietly distributing thy wealth unto the poor, O blessed one, together with thy spouse and thy children; therefore ye inherit divine delight.[^2665]  

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom [and Word]" (Премꙋ́дрости):*[^2666]  
Keeping watch in the commandments of the Master, instructing thy children and thy spouse in like manner, O blessed Xenophon, with whom thou didst inherit the kingdom on high, being delivered from every affliction: therefore we all piously praise you, and honor you with love, and with faith cry aloud: O all-blessed God-bearers, pray Christ God to grant remission of sins unto those who celebrate with love your holy memory.[^2667]  

*Glory... Both now, Theotokion:*  
As a Virgin and the only one among women who without seed gavest birth unto God in the flesh, all we generations of men call thee blessed; for the fire of the Godhead dwelt in thee, and as an infant with milk dost thou nourish the Creator and Lord. Therefore, both the angelic and human race, we worthily glorify thy most holy childbearing, and with one accord cry unto thee: Pray Christ God to grant remission of transgressions unto those who bow down in faith before thy most holy childbearing.[^2668]  

*Stavrotheotokion:*  
Beholding the Lamb, the Shepherd, and the Deliverer upon the Cross, the Ewe-lamb cried out, weeping, and bitterly lamenting, exclaimed: The world indeed rejoices, receiving deliverance through Thee; but my womb burns, seeing Thy crucifixion, which Thou endurest out of tender compassion of mercy, O longsuffering Lord, abyss of mercy and inexhaustible wellspring; have compassion and grant remission of transgressions unto those who hymn Thy divine passions with faith.[^2669]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*  
I heard, O Lord, the report of Thy dispensation, and I glorified Thee, Who alone art the Lover of mankind.[^2670]  

*Troparion:*  
Having been saved from the worldly tempest, ye hastened unto the haven of piety, O most blessed children.[^2671]  

*Troparion:*  
Having been instructed in the knowledge of things divine and human, ye chose to serve God.[^2672]  

*Troparion:*  
Having been gloriously delivered from the worldly abyss, O venerable ones, ye came unto the abyss of good things.[^2673]  

*Theotokion:*  
Delivered by the Blood poured forth from the rib of thy Son, O Mother of God, we all call thee blessed.[^2674]  

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*  
O Giver of light and Creator of the ages, O Lord, guide us in the light of Thy commandments; for besides Thee we know no other God.[^2675]  

*Troparion:*  
Passing over unto the imperishable life, thou didst hasten to reach the holy city, O sacred Arcadius, and didst bow down before the sepulchre of Life Himself.[^2676]  

*Troparion:*  
As truly comely was the providence that was over thee, and marvelous and most glorious was the divine guidance in all good things, O all-blessed Arcadius.[^2677]  

*Troparion:*  
He that provids for thee, Who of old reclined in the embrace of Simeon the divine elder: Christ guided thee, Arcadius, and brought thee unto a divine elder.[^2678]  

*Theotokion:*  
Thou didst supernaturally give birth unto the unoriginate Son, Who is co-eternal with the Father, incarnate from thee, O all-immaculate Maiden; therefore do we proclaim thee to be the pure Birthgiver of God.[^2679]  

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*  
Wallowing in the abyss of sin, I call upon the fathomless abyss of Thy tender mercy: Bring me up from corruption, O God.[^2680]  

*Troparion:*  
Desiring the blessed life, thou didst run unto the assembly of the monastics, O John, making life-giving inspiration thy helper.[^2681]  

*Troparion:*  
Having fled from the abomination of the manslayer's malice and his deadly poison, thou didst run, O John, unto the life-bearing Sepulchre of Christ.[^2682]  

*Troparion:*  
Thou didst emulate the life of John [the Forerunner], for like him thou didst dwell in the wilderness, and didst live purely, O John, being made wise in Christ.[^2683]  

...He Who stretched out the heaven by His will made thee, O pure Mother of God, an animate other heaven; and from thee He shone forth upon those who were in darkness.[^2684]  

*Kontakion, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast appeared today" (Ꙗ҆ви́лсѧ є҆сѝ дне́сь):*[^2685]  
Having fled the sea of this life, righteous Xenophon, with his honorable spouse, rejoicing in the heavens with their children, magnify Christ.[^2686]  

*Ikos:*[^2687]  
In a God-befitting manner didst thou walk the early path, O Xenophon, together with thy spouse; ye forgot nature, even as the bodiless ones manifestly appeared upon earth; therefore the gates of heaven were opened unto you, and with the angels ye dance, having become divine laborers of the vineyard of the Lord, together with your children: pray therefore unto Christ to grant the dawn of illumination unto our darkened hearts, as we celebrate your light-bearing memory, magnifying Christ the Crown-giver.[^2688]  

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*  
The god-opposing command of the lawless tyrant raised up a high flame; but Christ spread a spiritual dew upon the pious children, He Who is blessed and supremely glorified.[^2689]  

*Troparion:*  
Beholding by purity of mind your coming together, the God-bearer foretold it; for God the righteous One, having divinely rewarded your piety, assembled you into one, as He is merciful.[^2690]  

*Troparion:*  
Beholding the zeal of piety, having accepted your desire, and having looked upon your faith, the Lover of mankind assembled you all at one table, as the Benefactor and supremely glorified One.[^2691]  

*Theotokion:*  
Hope that puts not to shame, certain hope, and unshakable wall, protection and helper be thou unto me who hope in thee, O all-immaculate one; for upon thee, O pure one, do I place all the hope of my salvation.[^2692]  

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*  
The fiery furnace in Babylon of old divided its action by divine command, burning the Chaldeans, but bedewing the faithful who sang: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord.[^2693]  

*Troparion:*  
As a furnace exceedingly inflamed with fire, ye steadfastly endured separation from one another; for torn in your bowels and inflamed in your souls by the sting of kinship, ye underwent the sufferings of the martyrs.[^2694]  

*Troparion:*  
From on high a dew-bearing cloud of divine love overshadowed you on the mountains of Zion, where the dew of the Spirit enlightened the disciples who cry: Bless [the Lord, all ye works of the Lord].[^2695]

...all ye works of the Lord, the Lord.  

*Troparion:*  
Entreat the Benefactor to be merciful and compassionate unto us, O all-wealthy fathers, who celebrate your sacred memory, you who were united by nature, and joined together by grace.[^2696]  

*Theotokion:*  
Thou didst give birth unto the only-begotten Son and God the Word, Who ineffably shone forth before the ages from the unoriginate Father, and became the Firstborn of creation; therefore, O Mother of God, all we nations glorify thee.[^2697]  

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*  
The Son of the unoriginate Begetter, God and Lord, incarnate of the Virgin, hath appeared unto us, to enlighten those in darkness and to gather together the dispersed; therefore the all-hymned Birthgiver of God do we magnify.[^2698]  

*Troparion:*  
Taking the Cross of Christ upon your shoulders, ye truly walked along the path of abstinence, accomplishing every virtue, until ye received truly incorruptible life itself, crowned as an entire household.[^2699]  

*Troparion:*  
Having overcome carnal mindedness, ye laid up the wealth of the Spirit as treasure, having received the grace of healing from the Fountain of gifts, unto Whom having now passed over, ye rest eternally.[^2700]  

*Troparion:*  
Having conquered the wiles of the serpent, at the end of honors ye were named venerable ones, worthily receiving crowns of righteousness from Christ; Whom now entreat, that our souls may be saved.[^2701]  

*Theotokion:*  
Motherless before according to His first begetting, for our sake incarnate dost thou bring Him forth without a father, known in two natures, divine and human, and believed in these operations, O Bride of God.[^2702]  

*Exapostilarion, Tone 3, Podoben: "The sky with stars" (Не́бо ѕвѣзда́ми):*[^2703]  
Thou didst disperse thy wealth unto the poor in a God-pleasing manner, and as an entire household thou didst unite thyself unto the Lord, O father Xenophon; entreat Him, O all-blessed one, to deliver us from passions.[^2704]  

*Theotokion:*  
The hosts of angels and the choirs of the saints have truly been surpassed by thy majesties, O pure one; therefore entreat Christ for the people who have sinned.[^2705]  

*Month of the same, the 27th Day.*  
*The Translation of the Relics of our Father among the Saints, John Chrysostom:*[^2706]  
*At Vespers, "Blessed is the man," the first antiphon.*[^2707]  
*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 8, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*[^2708]  
The gold-forged trumpet, * the God-inspired instrument, * the inexhaustible deep of dogmas, * the firm support of the Church, * the heavenly mind, * the depth of wisdom, * the all-golden cup * pouring forth rivers of honey-flowing teachings * and watering creation, * let us hymn with songs. *(Twice)*[^2709]  

The unsetting star, * enlightening the whole universe * with the rays of teachings, * the preacher of repentance, * the all-golden sponge taking away the moisture of grievous despair, * and bedewing hearts melted by sins, * let us worthily honor John, the golden-worded.[^2710]  

An earthly angel and heavenly man, * a swallow eloquent * and manifold in voice, * treasury of virtues, * an unbroken stone, * the model of the faithful, * peer of the martyrs, * fellow-stander with the holy angels, * of one mind with the apostles: * let Chrysostom be magnified in hymns![^2711]  

*Other Stichera, the same Tone, Podoben: "Called from on high" (Зва́нный свы́ше):*[^2712]  
Let us form a most harmonious dance; * for the golden-radiant crown of the Church of Christ, * unto the glory of the Church today, * comes from Comana unto the ruling city. * Shining from on high, he radiates * in his return, * bringing the faithful unto the immaterial kingdom, * and continually leading all. * Therefore we cry aloud: O father named of gold, * divine, all-golden Chrysostom, * entreat [Him] to save and enlighten our souls.[^2713]  

As a bright heaven of the Church, * having undergone exile as a sunset, O Chrysostom, * from the most harsh [regions] * thou shinest forth now, rejoicing, an unsetting [light] unto creation, * adorned with virtues, * with the stars of miracles, O wise one, * bearing Christ the exceedingly bright One * after the manner of the sun, Who now enlightens thy return. * Therefore we cry aloud: O most radiant, light-speaking Chrysostom, all-wise one, entreat [Him] to save and enlighten our souls.[^2714]  

Another heaven dances with the angels; * the assemblies of men rejoice together with creation; * for he who showed forth all upon earth to be heavenly minded * by the divine ladder of his precious words, * this one, by ascent to the heights * on steps trodden by God, * shows forth as a new Jacob * the divine angels * rejoicing at his translation. * Therefore we cry aloud: O all-blessed one, * companion of the immaterial angels, golden-worded one, * pray that our souls may be saved.[^2715]  

*Glory, the same Tone [Tone 4]:*  
*Idiomelon:*  
It was not fitting for thee, O Chrysostom, having left the royal city, to dwell in Comana; therefore the royal and all-firm decree, guided by God, returned thee again unto the royal city. And the Church was glad when she beheld thee, confessing and saying: My glory magnifies the Lord, Who hath given back to me my brideman, and the confirmation of the faith, the upholding of my dignities, and the resting of my temples, the height of humility of mind, and the depth of almsgiving, and the breadth of my poverty, and the length of repentance. Therefore we pray thee, O venerable father: ask peace and great mercy for our souls.[^2716]  

*Both now, Theotokion:*  
*He Who for thy sake:*[^2717]  
*Prokeimenon of the day, and the Readings.*[^2718]  
*Reading from Proverbs:* [Composite: Prov. 10:7, 6; 3:13–16; 8:6, 32, 34, 4, 12, 14, 17; 9:4–5][^2719]  
The memory of the righteous is with praises, and the blessing of the Lord is upon his head. Blessed is the man that finds wisdom, and the mortal that knows understanding. For it is better to buy her than treasures of gold and silver. And she is more precious than costly stones; and no honorable thing is worthy of her. For length of days and years of life are in her right hand, and in her left hand are riches and glory. From her mouth proceeds righteousness, and law and mercy she bears upon her tongue. Hear me, therefore, O children, for I will speak honorable things; and blessed is the man that shall keep my ways. For my goings forth are the goings forth of life, and favor is prepared from the Lord. Therefore I pray you, and utter my voice unto the sons of men: for I, wisdom, have established counsel, and understanding and knowledge have I called upon. Mine is counsel and firm support; mine is understanding, and mine is strength. I love them that love me, and they that seek me shall find grace. Understand craftiness, therefore, ye simple ones, and ye uninstructed, lay it to heart;  

...and again: For I will speak honorable things; and from my lips I will bring forth right things, for my mouth shall meditate truth, and false lips are an abomination before me. All the words of my mouth are with righteousness; there is nothing crooked or perverse in them. All things are right to them that understand, and straight to them that find knowledge. For I teach you the truth, that your hope may be in the Lord, and that ye may be filled with the Spirit.[^2720]  

*Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon:* [Composite: Prov. 10:31–32; 10:2; 11:7; 13:9; 15:2; 16:13; Wis. 6:12–16; 7:7–8, 12, 14, 22, 25; 8:2, 4, 7–8; 9:1–3, 4, 10–11, 14][^2721]  
The mouth of the righteous drops wisdom, and the lips of wise men know grace. The mouth of the wise meditates wisdom, and righteousness delivers them from death. When a righteous man dies, hope does not perish. For a righteous son is born unto life, and in his good things he shall reap the fruit of righteousness. The light of the righteous is at all times, and from the Lord they shall find grace and glory. The tongue of the wise knows good things, and in their heart wisdom rests. The Lord loves venerable hearts, and all the blameless in the way are acceptable unto Him. The wisdom of the Lord enlightens the face of the prudent. For she anticipates them that desire her, before they know her, and she is easily seen by them that love her. He that watches early for her shall have no travail, and he that watches for her sake shall soon be without care. For she goes about seeking such as are worthy of her, and graciously appears unto them in the ways. Malice can never prevail against wisdom. For these things I was a lover of her beauty, and I loved her and sought her out from my youth; and I sought to take her to myself for a bride, for the Master of all loved her. For she is an initiate of the knowledge of God, and a chooser of His works. Her labors are virtues, for she teaches temperance and understanding, righteousness and courage, than which nothing is more profitable in life unto men. And if anyone desires much experience, she knows things of old and considers things to come; she knows the subtleties of words and the solutions of dark sayings; signs and wonders she foreknows, and the events of seasons and times; and unto all she is a good counselor, for immortality is in her, and good fame in communion with her words. Therefore I conversed with the Lord, and prayed unto Him, and said from my whole heart: O God of our fathers and Lord of mercy, Who hast made all things by Thy word, and by Thy wisdom hast fashioned man, that he might have dominion over the creatures made by Thee, and order the world in holiness and righteousness: Give me Wis- -dom, that sits by Thy thrones, and reject me not from among Thy servants, for I am Thy servant and the son of Thine handmaid. Send her out of Thy holy heavens and from the throne of Thy glory, that being present with me she may teach me what is well-pleasing before Thee; and she shall guide me in understanding, and preserve me in her glory. For the thoughts of mortals are all fearful, and their devices are fallible.[^2722]

*Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon:* [Composite: Wis. 4:7–14; 6:18, 20–22; 7:15–16, 21–22, 26, 29; 10:9–10, 12; 2:1, 10–18, 21; 3:1–3, 8; 11:23–26; 12:16, 19][^2723]  
When the righteous is praised, the peoples shall rejoice; for the memory of him is immortality, because it is known by the Lord and by men, and his soul was pleasing unto the Lord. Love wisdom, therefore, O ye men, and ye shall live; desire her, and ye shall be instructed; for the beginning of her is love, and the keeping of the law. Honor wisdom, that ye may reign unto the ages. I will declare unto you, and will not hide from you the mysteries of God: for He is the guide of wisdom and the director of the wise, and the craftsman of every understanding and work. And with all understanding wisdom shall teach; for in her is a spirit of understanding and holy, and the brightness of the everlasting light, and the image of the goodness of God. She makes friends of God and prophets. She is more comely than the sun, and above every order of stars; being compared with light, she is found prior. She delivered them that pleased her from tribulations, and guided them along right paths. She gave them to have holy understanding, and kept them safe from them that lay in wait, and gave them a mighty conflict, that all might know that godliness is stronger than all. And malice can never prevail against wisdom, neither shall judgment pass by the evil, convicting them. For they said within themselves, reasoning unrighteously: Let us oppress the righteous man, and let us not spare his holiness, neither let us revere the gray hairs of the aged of many years. For our strength shall be our law; and let us lie in wait for the righteous, because he is displeasing unto us, and contrary to our works, and reproaches us with the transgressions of the law, and objects to our sins the transgressions of our training. He professes to have knowledge of God, and calls himself the child of the Lord. He became unto us a reproof of our thoughts, and he is grievous unto us even to behold; for his life is not like that of others, and his paths are changed. We are esteemed by him as a mockery, and he avoids our ways as filthiness, and pronounces the end of the righteous to be blessed. Let us see, therefore, if his words be true- -and let us test what shall happen unto him. Let us examine him with insult and torture, that we may know his meekness and test his forbearance. Let us condemn him with a shameful death, for visitation shall be made according to his words. Such things did they imagine, and were deceived; for their malice blinded them, and they knew not the mysteries of God, neither did they judge that Thou art God alone, Who hast the power of life and death, and savest in the time of affliction, and deliverest from every evil, compassionate and merciful, giving grace unto Thy venerable ones, and with Thine arm resisting the proud.[^2724]

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 6, Podoben: "Rejoice" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ):*[^2725]  
The Church of Christ rejoices, having received upon the candlestick, O sacred one, thee, the radiant luminary, whom the enemies having cast down, hid under the bushel of silence; on the mountain of virtues she honors thee, O venerable father, as a divine radiance shining with miracles upon the ends of the universe brighter than the sun; today the unimpeded judgment of God shows forth thy righteousness from on high like the most bright midday, and grants peace and great mercy unto those in the world.[^2726]  

*Verse:* My mouth shall speak of wisdom, and the meditation of my heart shall be of understanding.[^2727]  

The faithful dispenser of the wheat of spiritual myrrh, who with heavenly sweetness nourished the hearts of all, comes not from Egypt; but appearing as a new Joseph, he comes from Comana with his precious relics, cutting off today the storm and abyss of grievous sorrows by his prayers. Him therefore let us bless, and in faith cry aloud: Come, O blessed one, into the midst of those who celebrate thy memory, granting unto them salvation richly, and great mercy.[^2728]  

*Verse:* The mouth of the righteous shall meditate wisdom, and his tongue shall speak of judgment.[^2729]  

Thy shrine, O Chrysostom, pours forth unto the world the miracles of divine myrrh like a beautiful vessel of myrrh, and with streams of healing perfumes the souls of those who honor thee. For with the graces of Christ, as with immaterial spices, thou hast enriched it, and thou bestowest fragrance ever-living upon those who have recourse unto thee with faith; therefore, enjoying thy grace, O all-wise one, and having been satisfied with thy most pure and divine relics, we faithfully pray: Grant great mercy unto our souls.[^2730]  

*Glory, Tone 6:*  

O venerable, thrice-blessed, most holy father, good shepherd and disciple of Christ the Chief Shepherd, who didst lay down thy life for the sheep: do thou now also, O all-praised John Chrysostom, ask by thy prayers that great mercy be granted unto us.[^2731]  

*Both now, Theotokion:*  
*Theotokos, thou art the true vine:*[^2732]  

*Troparion, Tone 8:*  
The grace of thy lips, shining forth like a brilliance of fire, enlightened the universe; it stored up not the treasures of love of silver for the world, but showed forth unto us the height of humility of mind. But instructing us by thy words, O father John Chrysostom, entreat Christ God the Word, that our souls may be saved.[^2733]  

*At Matins, after the 1st Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4:*  
As a golden-radiant and beautiful golden-speaking instrument, divinely under the Church, thou wast granted by God, O Chrysostom, a swallow sweet-speaking, of golden appearance, a mind clad in gold, O blessed one: lute of repentance, save from temptations those who honor thee, by thy prayers, O shepherd worthy of marvel. *(Twice)*[^2734]  

*Glory... Both now, Theotokion:*  
For having fled, after God, unto thy humble divine protection, O Mother of God, falling down I pray thee: Have mercy, O all-immaculate one, for my sins have exceeded my head, and I fear the torments and tremble, O Sovereign Lady: make supplication, O pure one, unto thy Son, to deliver me from them.[^2735]  

*After the 2nd Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4, Podoben: "Joseph was amazed" (Оу҆ди́висѧ і҆ѡ́сифъ):*[^2736]  
Having been accounted worthy of the flock of Christ by divine judgment, O shepherd worthy of marvel, as wolves from it thou didst drive them away by the sling of thy words, unsparingly reproving the lawless ones, O wise one. Therefore also thou wast driven away by envy, O Chrysostom, and didst journey a distant path, being steadfast upon it, in which also thou didst die; yet thou didst return with great glory, bestowing divine gifts. *(Twice)*[^2737]  

*Glory... Both now, Theotokion:*  
Joseph was amazed, beholding that which was above nature, and he pondered in his mind the rain upon the fleece in thy seedless conception, O Mother of God, the bush unburned by fire, the rod of Aaron that budded; and bearing witness, thy betrothed and guardian cried aloud unto the priests: A Virgin gives birth, and after childbearing remains again a Virgin.[^2738]  

*After the Polyeleos, Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "That which was ordered mystically" (Повелѣ́нное та́иннѡ):*[^2739]  
By true hierarchic rule thou didst make thy life radiant, thou didst piously sow the word of the Lord unto men, O Chrysostom, pouring out showers of teachings upon the earth most wisely by the ray of the Spirit, planting good manners. Therefore, having received the fruits of understanding by faith, having tasted them we have known the enjoyment of divine glory. *(Twice)*[^2740]

*Glory... Both now, Theotokion:*  
We give thanks unto thee at all times, O Mother of God, and we magnify thee, O all-immaculate one, and bow down, hymning thy childbearing, O full of grace, crying unceasingly: Save us, O all-merciful Virgin, as thou art good, and snatch us away from the dread judgment of the demons in the hour of trial, that we thy servants may not be put to shame.[^2741]  

*The Gradual, the 1st Antiphon of Tone 4.*[^2742]  
*Prokeimenon, Tone 4:* My mouth shall speak of wisdom, and the meditation of my heart shall be of understanding.[^2743]  
*Verse:* Hear this, all ye nations; give ear, all ye that inhabit the universe.[^2744]  
*Gospel of John, section 35 from the half [John 10:1–9].*[^2745]  

*After Psalm 50, Sticheron, Tone 6:*  
Thou hast appeared as a golden-voiced trumpet, O golden-speaking Chrysostom, making the hearts of the faithful golden by thy gold-wrought teachings; for prophetically the utterance of thy righteous deeds went forth, O venerable father, and enlightened all the ends of the world.[^2746]  

*Canon of the Most Holy Theotokos, with the Heirmos on 6; and of the Saint on 8.*[^2747]  
*Canon of the Theotokos, whose acrostic is: "Rejoice, dwelling-place of joy, resolution of sorrow. A work of John." Tone 8.*[^2748]  
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*  
He that pursued with chariots, Pharaoh, was drowned of old by the wonderworking rod of Moses, when striking in the form of a cross and dividing the sea, but it saved fleeing Israel, the pedestrian, as he sang a song unto God.[^2749]  

*Troparion:*  
Rejoice, deliverance from the ancient curse, and wellspring of blessing; rejoice, Mother of Life, overthrow of hades, slaying of death; rejoice, release of sorrow, spacious receptacle of joy; rejoice, O all-hymned Birthgiver of God.[^2750]  

*Troparion:*  
Noetic and living chariot of the Word, rejoice, O all-immaculate one; rejoice, David's chariot of many names, chariot marked out by myriads; rejoice, thou that without comparison art higher than the Cherubim and surpassest the Seraphim.[^2751]  

*Troparion:*  
Most acceptable unto the spiritual hosts, rejoice, O Bride of God; rejoice, thou that art higher than all created nature, higher than all created nature; rejoice, palace of God; rejoice, fiery throne; rejoice, luminary shining with much light; rejoice, Sovereign Lady named by myriads of the pious.[^2752]

Rejoice, O undefiled one, who didst bud forth the Rod from the root of Jesse; rejoice, thou who mystically and profoundly didst foreshadow of old the budding of the rod of Aaron; for even as that rod brought forth almonds, so didst thou blossom forth Christ.[^2753]  

*Canon of the Saint, whose acrostic is: "I sing thee, golden divine lute. A work of Joseph." Tone 6.*[^2754]  
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*  
The Red Sea was cut asunder by the rod, and the wave-nourished deep was dried up, becoming passable at once unto the unarmed, and a grave unto the fully-armed; and a God-adorned hymn was sung: Christ our God hath been gloriously glorified.[^2755]  

*Troparion:*  
Filled with the unsetting rays, O venerable one, and standing ever before the divine throne together with all the elect: pray that peace and great mercy be granted unto us who faithfully honor thee and celebrate thy divine return.[^2756]  

*Troparion:*  
The earth dances, and heaven rejoices with men together with us in a God-befitting manner, on thy holy feast, O wise one, wherein thy sacred body was returned unto thy flock, O glorious Chrysostom, honorable dwelling-place of the Spirit.[^2757]  

*Troparion:*  
The manifold crafty one, unable to endure the divine brilliancies of thy mind, O blessed one, raised up temptations against thee, even as of old against Job; but he was darkened the more; for behold, after exile thou hast entered into thy flock more radiant.[^2758]  

*Troparion:*  
With thine all-golden words thou didst gild the thoughts of the faithful, O golden-worded one; and having been exiled from the flock through envy, by divine nod thou didst return unto it again after thy burial, brightly praised, O all-blessed Chrysostom.[^2759]  

*Theotokion:*  
Thou hast appeared holier than the Cherubim, having given birth unto the most holy God; Whom entreat as the Creator of all, O pure one, to sanctify all who bless thee with holy voices, O boast of the fathers and help of men.[^2760]  

*Another Canon of the Saint, whose acrostic is: "Unto the golden-tongued a third song I sing." Tone 4.*[^2761]  
*Ode 1. Heirmos:*  
He Who of old by divine nod gathered the waters into one gathering, and divided the sea for the people of Israel, this is our God, and He is supremely glorified; unto Him alone let us sing, for He hath been glorified.[^2762]

*Troparion:*  
O God-proclaimed mouth, golden-voiced instrument, by the brightness of thy words enlighten my mind through thy supplications, that I may hymn the memory of thy return, O John, named after divine grace.[^2763]  

*Troparion:*  
As a light-bearing star, as a sun enlightening men, as a luminary of piety, having gone beneath the earth, O venerable one, by the laws of nature: again hast thou shone forth unto us thy children, sending forth bright radiances of miracles.[^2764]  

*Troparion:*  
By thy golden-speaking tongue thou hast filled the whole universe with teachings; and with the golden rays of healings thou didst shine upon all, causing the darkness of afflictions to vanish, O venerable one, by thy return.[^2765]  

*Theotokion:*  
Being divine in essence, thou didst proclaim the Word to be of one hypostasis, even though double, God having come forth from the all-pure one having assumed flesh; whom we bless unceasingly, and faithfully glorify, O divine Chrysostom.[^2766]  

*Katavasia:*  
*The sun of old visited a land of the deep:*[^2767]  

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*  
O Lord, Creator of the vault of heaven and Builder of the Church, do Thou establish me in Thy love, O summit of desires, firm support of the faithful, Who alone art the Lover of mankind.[^2768]  

*Troparion:*  
Rejoice, mightiest weapon of the faithful, O Mother of God; rejoice, firm representation; rejoice, protection; rejoice, help of sinners; rejoice, wall of them that call upon thee; rejoice, joy of the world.[^2769]  

*Troparion:*  
Rejoice, firm support of human salvation; rejoice, recall of Adam and Eve, through whom they received their ancient good inheritance; rejoice, thou that hast opened Paradise again.[^2770]  

*Troparion:*  
Rejoice, bush unburned; rejoice, chariot of the light; rejoice, cloud of the sun; rejoice, throne of the King, most glorious and everywhere proclaimed; rejoice, living city of Christ the living God.[^2771]  

*Troparion:*  
O unwedded Mother, rejoice, pure Mother of God; rejoice, unplowed and uncultivated field, that didst cultivate the Cultivator of all; rejoice, earth that didst cause Truth to shine forth.[^2772]  

*Another [Heirmos]:*  
Being the Lord of all and God the Creator, the Passionless One, having impoverished Himself, united the created [nature] unto Himself, and being Himself the Passover for those for whom He was about to die, He sacrificed Himself beforehand[^2773] He sacrificed Himself beforehand, crying: Eat My Body, and be established in faith.

*Troparion:*  
Thou wast a pure receptacle of God, and didst search out the depths of dogmas, O blessed Chrysostom, drowning the minds of the ill-disposed, but watering the hearts of the faithful; therefore we celebrate today thy venerable return.[^2774]  

*Troparion:*  
A golden instrument, proclaiming unto us ineffable things, wast thou, O blessed Chrysostom; for this cause we faithfully hymn thee at the return of thy relics, O earthly angel of God and heavenly man.[^2775]  

*Troparion:*  
Words of life didst thou pour forth unto the faithful, and being unjustly envied, O all-blessed one, thou wast banished into distant exile and into many tribulations; but by the all-effective nod, after thy repose, O venerable one, thou art again granted unto thy flock.[^2776]  

*Theotokion:*  
The height and depth of thine ineffable childbearing, who can recount, O Maiden? For beyond all word and understanding thou didst give birth unto God, Who delivered men from corruption; therefore, as is due, all we the faithful call thee blessed.[^2777]  

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*  
O Most High Almighty, Who from non-being didst bring forth all things, created by the Word and perfected by the Spirit: establish me in Thy love.[^2778]  

*Troparion:*  
In caverns in exile the blinded empress hid Thee, the all-radiant luminary; but Christ, having returned Thee, sets Thee again upon the highest lampstand.[^2779]  

*Troparion:*  
Distilling streams of miracles, and pouring forth rivers of healings, thou hast returned, O Chrysostom, unto them that faithfully honor the memory of thy return, O John.[^2780]  

*Troparion:*  
The gold-flowing Nile, overflowing in words and miracles, hath returned; let us run together and faithfully draw abundantly, all of us, that we may be filled.[^2781]  

*Theotokion:*  
Earthly nature is not able to hymn thee, whom angels hymn as having given birth in the flesh; yet faithfully we, thy servants, take courage to hymn and glorify thee.[^2782]  

*Katavasia:*  
*Thou art the firm foundation of them that put their trust in Thee, [O Lord]:*[^2783]  

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8, Podoben: "The Wisdom and the Word" (Премꙋ́дрости):*[^2784]  
Having learned wisdom from on high, and the grace of words from God, Thou didst shine forth unto all as gold in a furnace, and didst preach the Holy Trinity in unity, piercing the deceit of the love of silver with thy words;

...therefore also, having rebuked the empress with zeal, thou didst put to shame the alien wisdom of Arius, O John Chrysostom: entreat Christ God to grant remission of transgressions unto those who celebrate with love thy holy memory. *(Twice)*  

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*  
Having conceived One of the Trinity supernaturally, O Virgin, thou didst marvelously bear Him beyond word and thought, and didst make human nature, which had been cast out of old, a partaker of the Divine Nature; therefore, having come together, all we who are saved by thy childbearing, O all-immaculate one, following thy words, as is due do call thee blessed, praying Christ God to grant remission of transgressions unto those who glorify thee with faith as His Mother.[^2785]  

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*  
Thou art my strength, O Lord, Thou art also my power, Thou art my God, Thou art my rejoicing, Who, without leaving the Father’s bosom, didst visit our poverty; therefore with the Prophet Habakkuk I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind![^2786]  

*Troparion:*  
Dawn of the Father’s radiance, and Sun that didst shine forth from the Father before the morning star: rejoice, O Birthgiver of God, light and living cloud, O Virgin; rejoice, Mother; rejoice, blessed one; rejoice, all-immaculate, most glorified one.[^2787]  

*Troparion:*  
Thou art the golden censer, O Sovereign Lady, of the unbearable and immaterial Coal, whereby the torn handwriting of Adam’s disobedience was burned; therefore I cry unto thee: Rejoice, through whom joy, and the sweetness and reception of Paradise, were given unto all.[^2788]  

*Troparion:*  
Thou art the glory of men, and honor and praise, and the crown and diadem of angels; therefore earth and heaven, having formed one church, cry out unto thee the all-harmonious: Rejoice; rejoice, good treasure of the world; rejoice, help of all men.[^2789]  

*Troparion:*  
Honorable couch which Solomon prefigured, surrounded by sixty mighty men: rejoice, O Virgin, gilded ark of the noetic sanctuary; rejoice, divine tongs; rejoice, fire-bearing bush; rejoice, door, and ladder, and bridge.[^2790]  

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*  
Foreseeing Thine ineffable mystery, O Christ, the Prophet proclaimed: Thou hast established a steadfast love of strength, O Compassionate One; for as good, Thou hast sent Thine Only-begotten Son into the world as a cleansing.[^2791]  

*Troparion:*  
Having acquired fire-breathing lips and a tongue, O venerable father, thou didst clearly unfold the clarity of the Scriptures, and didst die in unjust exile; today thy blessed body is granted unto us as a gift.[^2792]  

*Troparion:*  
Let the declarer of ineffable things, the Golden-mouthed, be magnified today; for behold, after temporal death, rightly by the divine nod he returns again to the imperial city, reverently praised with divine hymns.[^2793]  

*Troparion:*  
Having a mind illumined by the radiance of the All-Holy Spirit, thou dost enlighten that which is under the sun with divine teachings, and drivest away the darkness of impiety, O holy father Chrysostom, converser with the holy angels.[^2794]  

*Troparion:*  
Blessed wast thou shown to be for righteousness’ sake, O venerable one, driven away from the flock by evil envy; and now returning, thou art honored by all with sacred hymns, O wise one, hierarch of the Lord, Chrysostom.[^2795]  

*Theotokion:*  
From thee, O Virgin, salvation came and was revealed unto the world; from thee Christ our redemption shone forth; therefore, as is due, we hymn thee, O pure boast of all the sacred, and holy propitiatory of the faithful.[^2796]  

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*  
Thou hast established a steadfast love toward us, O Lord, for Thou didst give Thine Only-begotten Son unto death for us; therefore we cry unto Thee giving thanks: Glory to Thy power, O Lord![^2797]  

*Troparion:*  
Ye lovers of words, come, let us honor with sacred words the great adorner of words, who joyfully returns again, who by the wisdom of his words rebuked the babblings of vain-minded words.[^2798]  

*Troparion:*  
Thou hast enriched us with the wealth of teachings, O Chrysostom, most clearly rebuking the hand that was heavily weighed down with the wealth of extortion, but being rich in the wealth of divine grace alone.[^2799]  

*Troparion:*  
The bow of the mighty of tyrannical cruelty is broken; but thou, having lived like an angel in the infirmity of the flesh, didst prevail, O most sacred Chrysostom, having those who were formerly thy persecutors as supplicants.[^2800]  

*Theotokion:*  
The noetic ranks praise thee with songs, O Maiden; for Him Whom they cannot behold, thou didst bear from thy pure womb, having assumed flesh immutably, O all-pure Bride of God.[^2801]  

*Katavasia:*  
*Thy virtue hath covered the heavens:*[^2802]  

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*  
Why hast Thou cast me away from Thy presence, O Unwaning Light, and an alien darkness hath covered me, the wretched one? But turn me back, and unto the light of Thy commandments direct my ways, I pray.[^2803]  

*Troparion:*  
Count me worthy at the time of my departure to pass through without sorrow the mental rulers and the tyrannical aerial hosts, that joyfully I may cry unto thee the "Rejoice", O Sovereign Lady: Rejoice, unashamed hope of all.[^2804]  

*Troparion:*  
As thou didst conceive Joy, rejoice, O all-immaculate one; rejoice, receptacle; rejoice, sweet-smelling, purple-like flower of purity; rejoice, scarlet briar-rose of virginity dipped in crimson, and sweet-smelling fragrance of God.[^2805]  

*Troparion:*  
Rejoice, mystical myrrh-treasury, welling forth sweet-smelling myrrh; rejoice, divine fount that pours forth living water; rejoice, O Sovereign Lady, uncultivated vine that bears the life-bearing cluster of grapes.[^2806]  

*Troparion:*  
Rejoice, impassable gate, through which Christ alone passed; rejoice, thou that by thy childbearing didst open the gates of Paradise; rejoice, through whom the heavens rejoice and the earth exults, having joined the things on high with those below.[^2807]  

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*  
Bound by the bond of love, the Apostles, having committed themselves unto Christ Who rules over all, had their beautiful feet washed, proclaiming peace unto all.[^2808]  

*Troparion:*  
Thou wast shown to be a luminary shining unto all who are in the night of life, flashing forth the rays of divine words, O father Chrysostom, and illuminating our thoughts; therefore, as is due, we hymn thee.[^2809]  

*Troparion:*  
Thou didst distribute the wealth of words, enriching the hungry minds, O venerable golden-speaking one; and having been unjustly exiled, by a righteous judgment thou hast returned again unto thy flock, which rejoices in thy greatnesses.[^2810]  

*Troparion:*  
As from a fruitful horn, thou didst offer the wine of compunction; and rebuking the empress who had seized the widow’s vineyard, thou wast exiled, O father Chrysostom; therefore we honor thy return.[^2811]  

*Theotokion:*  
Him Whom the hosts of the bodiless cannot behold, O Sovereign Lady, thou didst carry in thine embrace as an infant, Who was contained in thee and became poor in flesh through tender mercy, that He might enrich the world that had become impoverished.[^2812]  

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*  
Unto Thee I rise early, O Creator of all, Who transcendest all understanding in peace; for Thy commandments are light, wherein guide Thou me.[^2813]  

*Troparion:*  
As spring thou didst appear, mystically breathing the fragrance of the flowers of graces upon the multitudes of the faithful; the winter of evils hath been dissolved, O father, at thy return.[^2814]  

*Troparion:*  
The divine wellspring, the fount of gifts hath returned; come, ye that thirst, draw the water of life with faith, rejoicing divinely.[^2815]  

*Troparion:*  
Having set, thou didst hide thyself, woe is me, my beauty! But thou hast returned unto me, O desired one, in thy due season, the Church of Christ cries unto thee upon thy return.[^2816]  

*Theotokion:*  
Make Him Who came forth from thy womb merciful unto me, O all-immaculate one, the flesh-bearing Word, Whom Simeon, holding in his arms in the temple, magnified as Creator.[^2817]  

*Katavasia:*  
*When Isaiah saw [symbolically]:*[^2818]  

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*  
I will pour out my prayer unto the Lord, and unto Him will I declare my sorrows, for my soul is filled with evils, and my life hath drawn near unto hades; and like Jonah I pray: From corruption, O God, lead me up.[^2819]  

*Troparion:*  
Rejoice, O Sovereign Lady, living vessel; rejoice, dye-vat that from thy most pure blood didst dye a crimson purple robe for the King of all, and didst cover the nakedness of Adam: rejoice, all-hymned one.[^2820]  

*Troparion:*  
Sensible bread indeed naturally strengthens the hearts of men, O Maiden; but thy holy name, when hymned, establishes the souls of Christians; whence also joyfully every tongue cries out unto thee: Rejoice.[^2821]  

*Troparion:*  
Rejoice, gold-gleaming candlestick; rejoice, ark capable of containing God; rejoice, tabernacle; rejoice, holy mountain; rejoice, living city of the living God; rejoice, palace of Christ; rejoice, all-radiant divine temple.[^2822]  

*Troparion:*  
Rejoice, all-pure, all-immaculate one, choice flower of nature; rejoice, common honor of the human race; and God-given grace, that didst honor dishonored human nature by thy childbearing: rejoice.[^2823]  

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*  
The uttermost abyss of sins hath encompassed me, and no longer enduring its surging, like Jonah I cry unto Thee, O Master: From corruption lead me up.[^2824]  

*Troparion:*  
Thy tongue poured forth all-golden streams for the Church, O all-blessed Chrysostom, and it enriches the hungry hearts of those who sacredly glorify thee.[^2825]  

*Troparion:*  
Precious before our God was shown to be thy death, O all-blessed one, wherein He is glorified again by thy coming unto thy throne, O father Chrysostom.[^2826]  

*Troparion:*  
Blessed is the tomb that contains thy venerable body, for it hath been enriched with wonder-workings for those who hasten unto it with faith, O all-blessed one, hierarch Chrysostom.[^2827]  

*Theotokion:*  
Having given birth unto the Most High, O all-pure Bride of God, thou dost raise up to the heavens our nature that lay below; therefore, as is due, we glorify thee.[^2828]  

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*  
The uttermost abyss of sins hath encompassed me, and my spirit fails; but stretch out Thy high arm, O Master, and save me, O Helmsman, even as Peter.[^2829]  

*Troparion:*  
The foolish empress slandered thee [and cast thee out] from the Church of Christ, as thou didst fiercely rebuke her; but straightway she defiled herself, while thou dost rebuke her even after death, having wrought a marvelous brilliance.[^2830]  

*Troparion:*  
Thou wast shown to be an instrument of the all-working Spirit, O Chrysostom, sounding forth most melodiously; but the tormentress became deaf like the asp... and through a most wretched death she was visited with retribution.[^2831]  

*Troparion:*  
Even though he died the death, yet to suffer he is not subject: so the Golden-mouthed taught the rulers; for he who did not formerly submit unto their commands, afterward returned unto their supplications.[^2832]  

*Theotokion:*  
Contemplating Thee as being One from the Virgin, though Thou didst take flesh and became twofold, John Chrysostom drove far away both division and confusion, O God-man Jesus.[^2833]  

*Katavasia:*  
*The Elder cried aloud unto Thee:*[^2834]  

*Kontakion, Tone 6, Podoben: "The angelic choir" (Ли́къ а҆́гглскїй):*[^2835]  
The venerable Church was mystically gladdened by the return of thy precious relics; and having hidden them as costly gold, she unstintingly grants unto those who sing of thee the grace of healings through thy prayers, O John Chrysostom.  

*Ikos:*  
The lamp of my deeds was dark, O John Chrysostom, and I am terrified at the meeting of thy sacred relics; but do thou thyself guide me, and direct my paths, granting me a time of repentance, for thou art its divine preacher; and quiet the storm of my manifold passions, and snatching me from the net of the devils, save me unto the end; that I may worthily hymn thy glorious return, even as formerly, taking courage, I glorified thy falling asleep, O John Chrysostom.[^2836]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*  
The fire was ashamed before the condescension of God in Babylon of old; therefore the Children in the furnace, dancing with rejoicing foot as in a meadow, sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^2837]  

*Troparion:*  
Only unwedded one, and only incorrupt one: rejoice, O Birthgiver of God, Virgin and Mother who gavest birth to the Son, and unwedded one; rejoice, strange and awesome mystery; rejoice, sweetness of angels; rejoice, joy of men.[^2838]  

*Troparion:*  
O Zion, living city of Christ the King of kings, concerning which glorious things were spoken: rejoice, Bride of God; rejoice, ladder whereby we ascend from earth to heaven, and from corruption unto life.[^2839]  

*Troparion:*  
A God-planted flower garden, a sweet-smelling garden tilled by God hast thou appeared, O Virgin, who didst bud forth the flower of immortality; therefore with one accord we cry unto thee: Rejoice; rejoice, giver of joy; rejoice, fount of sweetness.[^2840]  

*Troparion:*  
O all-pure Sovereign Lady, deliver me from the dishonor of passions, that joyfully I may cry unto thee: Rejoice; rejoice, fount of holiness; rejoice, treasury of all purity; rejoice, receptacle of God; rejoice, dwelling place of Christ.[^2841]  

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*  
The Children in Babylon feared not the flame of the furnace, but cast into the midst of the flame, being bedewed they sang: Blessed art Thou, O Lord God of our fathers![^2842]  

*Troparion:*  
Shining with wonder-workings, adorned with gold-beaming theology, O wise one, thou wast surrendered unto cruel exiles, from which returning, thou hast been glorified by all.[^2843]  

*Troparion:*  
Thou cuttest down the roots of malice with the axe of thy divine teachings, and plantest divine knowledge in souls, O hierarch Chrysostom; therefore we glorify the return of thy relics.[^2844]  

*Troparion:*  
Having returned, O venerable one, thou didst reconcile those who were at variance, and wast laid in the church of the all-wise Apostles, O Chrysostom, with whose honorable authority thou wast enriched, O all-praised one.[^2845]  

*Theotokion:*  
Thou didst bear One of the supersubstantial Trinity, O all-pure one, Jesus Christ; Whom entreat, in His ineffable tender mercy, O all-immaculate one, to forgive my manifold transgressions.[^2846]  

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*  
As of old Thou didst bedew the three pious Children in the Chaldean flame, with the radiant fire of the Godhead enlighten us also, who cry aloud: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers![^2847]  

*Troparion:*  
When an injustice was done to the widow, O all-wise one, and she was unforgivably overcome by her own: a reckless woman alienated thee from the reigning city, and she herself became alienated from divine grace, alienating herself from thy most wise teachings.[^2848]  

*Troparion:*  
Yet thou hast returned sweet, like the sun that was covered by clouds, O exceedingly great luminary, through the mystical radiance of the light-bearing golden teachings, all being enlightened, O John Chrysostom.[^2849]  

*Troparion:*  
I stretch forth my hands unto thee, O Chrysostom, to receive thee within my walls, the bridal escort returning brightly and most lovely, who was delayed for years: so the Church cries out unto thee, celebrating today.[^2850]  

*Theotokion:*  
As a certain mystical tongs, carrying the noetic Coal, thou comest to the temple, Whom Simeon, receiving into his arms, O all-pure one, was enlightened, and shall prophesy concerning the signs of His Passion most clearly.[^2851]  

*Katavasia:*  
*Thee Who in the fire didst bedew:*[^2852]  

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*  
Bless, ye Children equal in number to the Trinity, God the Father, the Creator; hymn the Word Who descended and changed the fire into dew; and supremely exalt the All-Holy Spirit, Who gives life unto all, unto the ages.[^2853]  

*Troparion:*  
Rejoice, rod that didst bud forth from the root of Jesse; rejoice, thou that without being watered didst bear the flower, Christ the beautiful Flower; rejoice, fertile mountain; rejoice, overshadowing mountain; rejoice, mountain of God, wherein the Word was well-pleased to dwell before all ages.[^2854]  

*Troparion:*  
With the iron rod of thy mighty protection, like barking dogs, like roaring beasts, drive away the passions that fiercely beset me and defile my humble soul, that I may cry unto thee the "Rejoice", O Virgin.[^2855]  

*Troparion:*  
Thou wast adorned, having given birth unto God, Christ Who is fair in beauties beyond the sons of men, O thou who art fair among women; therefore rejoicing we cry unto thee: Rejoice; rejoice, O pure Birthgiver of God, full of grace; rejoice, most glorious of all creation.[^2856]  

*Troparion:*  
Rejoice, O Birthgiver of God, the mountain which Daniel foresaw unhewn, from which the cornerstone was cut off; rejoice, tongs that received God, carrying the Coal; rejoice, thou that art holier than the immaterial angels; rejoice, most honorable of creation.[^2857]  

*Another [Canon]. Heirmos:*  
For the sake of ancestral laws, the blessed youths in Babylon, braving danger, spat upon the foolish command of the ruler; and united with the fire wherein they were not burned, they sang a worthy hymn unto the Almighty: Hymn the Lord, ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^2858]  

*Troparion:*  
Having authority to loose and to bind, O venerable one, loose all transgressions of those who brightly celebrate thy divine return, and entreat that the heavenly kingdom may be vouchsafed unto those who sing with compunction of heart: Hymn the Lord, ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^2859]  

*Troparion:*  
In exile thou didst endure illnesses, O God-wise father, wherein having received a blessed and glorious end, O Chrysostom, by the divine will thou returnest again unto thy divine throne, being honored by those who sing: Hymn the Lord, ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^2860]  

*Troparion:*  
Unable to endure the arrows of thy words, O venerable one, the deceitful serpent begged to test thee even as the good Job; but he was vanquished by thy patience for Christ’s sake, and became a great laughing-stock, while thou dost hymn with faith: Hymn the Lord, ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^2861]  

*Trinity Hymn:*  
Unoriginate Father, and co-unoriginate Son, and Divine Spirit, indivisible Trinity, one essence, one power, and one authority: fill with all good things them that sing of Thee, and deliver from torment those who unceasingly sing: Hymn the Lord, ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^2862]  

*Theotokion:*  
The human mind cannot comprehend the mystery of thine ineffable childbearing, O Maiden, which is beyond mind and word; for God was revealed in the flesh from thee, saving those who had fallen into corruption, and raising up to the first dignity those who sing: Hymn the Lord, ye works, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^2863]  

*Another Canon. Heirmos:*  
Joined to the unbearable fire, the youths standing for piety, unharmed by the flame, sang the divine song: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord, and supremely exalt Him unto all ages.[^2864]  

*Troparion:*  
With the sheep of piety, O venerable father, thou dost nourish the Church which nurtured thee, repaying her with the sevenfold bread of divine grace, pouring forth thy sweetness unto her nourisher as a drink of healings, O all-blessed Chrysostom.[^2865]  

*Troparion:*  
Into all the earth went forth the proclamation of thy dogmas, O father, but the foolish empress commanded thee to be banished locally; yet she was deceived, for like a high-running giant, thou dost shine everywhere with the rays of thy words.[^2866]  

*Troparion:*  
Let the assembly of the faithful be enlightened today, meeting with rejoicing the most excellent teacher; for he hath come and is bodily present, distributing abundant grace unto all, of which may we partake, richly rejoicing.[^2867]  

*Theotokion:*  
I behold Thee in maternal arms, yet I know Thee to be unapproachable in the essence of the Godhead; how then, O Word, art Thou held by hands, Who holdest all creation in Thine hand? said Simeon, O God-man, glorifying Thine ineffable power.[^2868]  

*Katavasia:*  
*In the unbearable fire:*[^2869]  

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*  
Every ear was dismayed at the ineffable condescension of God, that the Most High willingly came down even unto the flesh, being made man from a virginal womb; therefore, the all-pure Birthgiver of God, we the faithful do magnify.[^2870]  

*Troparion:*  
Behold, all generations call thee ever-blessed, even as thou didst foretell from the Holy Spirit, O Birthgiver of God; and as unto her that bare Joy, they cry unto thee: Rejoice; rejoice, treasury of life; rejoice, fount pouring forth the honey of the soul.[^2871]  

*Troparion:*  
Thou didst correct, O pure Sovereign Lady, the slip of forefather Adam, and the sorrow of foremother Eve thou didst turn into joy; therefore as unto the cause of joy, we cry unto thee: Rejoice; rejoice, joy of the faithful; rejoice, gladness of Christians.[^2872]  

*Troparion:*  
It is truly meet to cry unto thee: Rejoice; for essentially the ever-existing Joy took up His abode in thee, O Virgin Maiden, Birthgiver of God; rejoice, paradise of sweetness; rejoice, gold-flowing fount of immortality; rejoice, thou that pourest forth true drink.[^2873]  

*Troparion:*  
Desire for thee, O all-hymned one, pierced my heart with a sweet arrow, and impels me ever to call unto thee: Rejoice, and to cry: Rejoice, quiet harbor; rejoice, sweetest impassable sea that didst drown the spiritual Pharaoh.[^2874]

*Another. Heirmos:*
Every tongue is at a loss to praise thee worthily, and even an intellect beyond this world is dazed to hymn thee, O Birthgiver of God; nevertheless, being good, accept our faith, for thou knowest our divine love; for thou art the protectress of Christians: thee do we magnify.[^2875]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast a rule of the priesthood, O God-proclaimer, clothed with righteousness as with a divine garment, having enriched the Church with thy words, and spiritually laid bare the mind of the Scriptures; therefore do we celebrate thy return, O father.[^2876]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst appear fair as a nightingale, O father, declaring the divine springtime of repentance unto those enslaved to the winter of sin; but having been exiled through the plot of the deceitful one, O wise one, thou comest running again with joy unto the flock that longs for thee, O blessed Chrysostom.[^2877]

*Troparion:*
Today the hearts of all leap for joy, beholding thee, O pure bridegroom, venerable one, given by grace unto thy bride the Church; and with unceasing voices they hymn the Giver of good things, and worthily praise and bless thee.[^2878]

*Troparion:*
The lamp hath arrived from Comana to be placed upon the lampstand; the adornment of the Church of God hath drawn near; sing unto the Lord, sing with gladness, and offering a spiritual welcome unto him, let us all cry aloud: O father, by thy prayers save us.[^2879]

*Theotokion:*
With the most radiant lightnings of Him Who was ineffably born of thee, O Maiden, holy Birthgiver of God, enlighten my soul, darkened by material transgressions, O all-pure one, and unwilling to do good; that I may unceasingly proclaim thy greatness.[^2880]

*Another. Heirmos:*
A new and God-befitting wonder: for the Lord openly passes through the shut virginal portal; bare at His entrance, God hath appeared flesh-bearing at His going forth, and the door remains shut; her do we ineffably magnify as the Mother of God.[^2881]

*Troparion:*
The host of angels, the assembly of prophets, and the divine choir of apostles and martyrs rejoice radiantly with us, sharing in the feast, O all-blessed one, and imparting the unfailing grace of thy hymns; for thou didst hold within thyself the life of all, imaging it forth.[^2882]

*Troparion:*
Behold the light of God for the world! In him the sublime divine lamp hath appeared, the sweet deep of divine gifts; come, brethren, let us be nourished by the light, let us be warmed, let us persevere, from the heart magnifying the golden-spoken one with hymns.[^2883]

*Troparion:*
As two mites, receive this hymn unto thee from my unworthy and wretched soul, wretchedly widowed of all good things, yet from zeal for divine wealth offering this, imitating divine goodness, granting me richly endowed grace in return.[^2884]

*Theotokion:*
Approaching, Simeon said trembling: Holding in my arms Him Who makes the whole earth to tremble from on high merely by looking upon it, I am strengthened, even Thy Offspring, O Virgin; being now released from my trembling flesh, as the assurance of what was to happen unto me is already fulfilled, I carry Him rejoicing, and announce deliverance unto those in Hades.[^2885]

*Katavasia of the Meeting of the Lord (Ode 9):*
*In the law of the shadow and the Scriptures...*[^2886]

*Exapostilarion, Podoben: "Give ear, ye women" (Же́ны ᲂу҆слы́шите):*
Rejoice, O city reigning over all cities, receiving today the body of thy good shepherd and arch-pastor, which directs and saves thee and the whole world with the honey-flowing words of Chrysostom, and clap thy hands with hymns. *Twice.*[^2887]

*Glory... Both now..., Theotokion:*
Rejoice, palace of God; rejoice, overshadowed mountain; rejoice, unburnt bush; rejoice, throne of glory; rejoice, divine table; rejoice, all-golden urn; rejoice, all-radiant lampstand; rejoice, light cloud: O Virgin Mother Mary.[^2888]

*At the Praises, Stichera on 4, Tone 4, Podoben: "Thou hast given a sign" (Да́лъ є҆сѝ зна́менїе):*
Brighter than gold, thy sacred teachings poured forth, O all-wise one, enrich minds in golden fashion with what is best, and drive away the mist of passions and the bitter winter of love of money; therefore do we bless thee as is meet, and honor the return of thy relics as a source of sanctification.[^2889]

*Sticheron:*
Unjustly driven from thy flock, O venerable father, thou didst endure in afflictions and bitter banishments, in which thou wast deemed worthy of a blessed end, as a good combatant who trampled down the wily one; therefore the Church rejoices in thy return, which thou didst adorn as with gold by thy most wise teachings.[^2890]

*Sticheron:*
The pillar of fire, the river flowing with the waters of teachings, the heavenly mind, the all-golden mouth of theology, the surety of sinners, the herald of repentance, the most radiant divine lamp, the heavenly man: let the blessed Chrysostom be hymned today.[^2891]

*Sticheron:*
Receiving thy relics as an imperial adornment, O Chrysostom, the imperial city is adorned with them, and boasting in thy words, it summons the universe unto gladness and the divine communion of thine abundant gifts, crying with a loud voice: O most good Jesus, Thou art the glory of Thy servants.[^2892]

*Glory..., in the same Tone [Tone 4], Automelon. By Germanus:*
O father Chrysostom, as a God-flowing river mystically going forth from Eden into four heads, thou didst traverse the ends of the earth with thy words, and didst water every believer with thine all-golden teaching; therefore, having clearly depicted for us the city-dwelling return of thy divine relics, pray now that our souls may be saved, O John, who hymn thee.[^2893]

*Both now..., Theotokion:*
*From all dangers [preserve] thy servants...*[^2894]

*Great Doxology and Dismissal.*
*At the Liturgy, the Beatitudes from the canon of the Saint, Ode 3 and Ode 6. Prokeimenon, Tone 1: My mouth shall speak of wisdom, and the meditation of my heart shall be of understanding [LXX Ps. 48:4]. Verse: Hear this, all ye nations; give ear, all ye that dwell in the universe [LXX Ps. 48:2]. Epistle to the Hebrews, Pericope 318 [Heb. 7:26-8:2]. Alleluia, Tone 2: The mouth of the righteous shall meditate wisdom, and his tongue shall speak of judgment [LXX Ps. 36:30]. Verse: The law of his God is in his heart, and his steps shall not be tripped [LXX Ps. 36:31]. Gospel according to John, Pericope 36 [Jn. 10:9-16]. Communion Hymn: In everlasting remembrance... [LXX Ps. 111:6b].*[^2895]

*In the same month, on the 28th day: Commemoration of our venerable father Ephrem the Syrian.*[^2896]
*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 6, Tone 2, Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly hosts" (Небе́сныхъ чинѡ́въ):*
