Gazing upon the beauties of paradise, and richly delighting in the incorruptible flower-beds, thou didst blossom forth the divine understanding unto the world; partaking whereof, O venerable one, with spiritual love we grow spiritually in our souls.[^2897]

*Sticheron:*
Having depicted the coming of the Judge with streams of tears, thou teachest us to kindle the lamps of our souls, crying unto all with a pure voice the coming of the Bridegroom: Let us all clothe ourselves in radiant raiment to meet Christ the Bridegroom.[^2898]

*Sticheron:*
Having hedged thy body round with abstinence, thou didst mortify the motions of the passions, O father, through prayers and vigils; therefore the power of the Spirit, having taken up abode in thee, showed thee forth as a noetic and universal luminary.[^2899]

*Glory..., Tone 6:*
Wisely having withdrawn from the turbulence of life, O ever-memorable Ephrem, through love of silence thou didst reach the wilderness; and being led thereby actively unto God, thou didst shine forth as a beacon unto the world, and didst pour forth words of life unto men; therefore, unceasingly strengthening us by thy prayers, [pray] to deliver our souls from the harm of the alien one, O venerable father.[^2900]

*Both now..., Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion:*
Beholding our Life hanging upon the Tree, the all-immaculate Birthgiver of God, maternally lamenting, cried aloud: O my Son and my God, save those who hymn Thee with love.[^2901]

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos: Glory..., Tone 4. By Anatolius:*
Prophetically soaking thy couch with tears, and [manifesting] the repentance of thy life in subjection; by deeds thou hast shown unto us the judgment of standing [before God] through words; and assembled together, O all-blessed one, we all honor thy memory, self-worker of glorious deeds, O ever-memorable Ephrem of the Lord; therefore even now we pray thee: Pray unto Christ God for our souls.[^2902]

*Both now..., of the same, or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "As one valiant among martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*
When she who bare Thee, the ewe-lamb, beheld Thee, the Lamb and Shepherd, upon the Tree, she lamented and maternally spake unto Thee: O most longed-for Son, how art Thou suspended upon the wood of the Cross, O longsuffering One? How have Thy hands and feet been nailed by the lawless, O Word, and Thou hast poured forth Thy blood, O Master?[^2903]

*Troparion, Tone 8:*
With the streams of thy tears thou didst cultivate the barren desert, and by sighings from the depths thou didst make thy labors fruitful a hundredfold; and thou becamest a luminary to the universe, shining with marvels, O Ephrem our father: pray unto Christ God that our souls may be saved.[^2904]

*At Matins, both canons of the Octoechos, and of the Saint on 6.*
*Whose acrostic is: "I honor Ephrem, the noetic Euphrates." A composition of Theophanes.*
*Tone 6. Ode 1. Heirmos:*
*Traversing the deep on foot as on dry land*[^2905] *Troparion:*
With the Euphrates-like rain of thy prayers, water my soul dried up by the heat of passions, and inspire in me a word as I praise thy feast, O all-blessed one.[^2906]

*Troparion:*
Having flashed forth with noetic light, thou didst appear as a bright sun, shining with light-beaming virtues and with the beauties of teachings, O Ephrem, illuminating the whole fullness of the faithful.[^2907]

*Troparion:*
Having quenched the flame of passions with torrents of tears, thou wast an honorable vessel of the Holy Spirit, O Ephrem, pouring forth fountains of teachings, O divinely blessed one.[^2908]

*Theotokion:*
Having incorruptibly received the Word in thy womb, thou didst give birth unto Him Who delivers from corruption those who ever serve Him, O pure Virgin Mother, truly the gate of life.[^2909]

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
There is none holy as Thou, O Lord my God, Who hast exalted the horn of Thy faithful, O Good One, and established us upon the rock of Thy confession.[^2910]

*Troparion:*
Having cleansed thyself of all mire of the passions, thou didst truly appear as a receptacle of virtues and a capacious vessel of the gifts of the Holy Spirit.[^2911]

*Troparion:*
In no wise giving sleep unto thine eyes, thou didst appear as a temple of the Holy Trinity and a treasury of wisdom, enriching the world with golden-beaming teachings, O blessed one.[^2912]

*Troparion:*
The honorable Church of Christ knows thee as another gold-flowing Euphrates, overflowing with streams of wise teachings and filling all creation.[^2913]

*Theotokion:*
One of the Holy Trinity, in two natures, having become incarnate from thy pure blood, came forth in a God-befitting manner, saving by grace those descended from Adam, O all-pure one.[^2914]

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 5, Podoben: "The Word co-unoriginate" (Собезнача́льное сло́во):*
As a treasury of wisdom of the mysteries of Christ and a cup of divine contrition, let us, the faithful, hymn Ephrem in his memory; for in accordance with his name he ever gladdens the hearts of the faithful with divine words, as a laborer and initiate of the revelations of the Lord. *Twice.*[^2915]

*Glory... Both now..., Theotokion:*
Fervent and unconquerable protectress, certain and unashamed hope, rampart, shelter, and haven of those who flee unto thee, O ever-virgin pure one: pray with the angels unto thy Son and God to give peace unto the world, and salvation, and great mercy.[^2916]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*

*Stavrotheotokion:*
By the Cross of thy Son, O woman full of the grace of God, all idolatrous delusion hath been abolished, and the power of demons hath been trampled down; therefore do we, the faithful, ever hymn and bless thee as is meet, and confessing thee to be truly the Birthgiver of God, we magnify thee.[^2917]

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Christ is my power, my God and Lord, the honorable Church sings in a God-befitting manner, crying out from a pure mind, keeping festival in the Lord.[^2918]

*Troparion:*
The power of thy words traversed the whole world, driving away the blindness of souls with the sublime radiance of humility, O blessed one.[^2919]

*Troparion:*
Blamelessly didst thou complete thy life, washing thyself with tears; and having depicted the coming of the Judge unto all with wise words, O divinely blessed, right marvelous one.[^2920]

*Troparion:*
The Lord, beholding the glorious height of Thy humility, grants thee a lofty word, whereby the fierce haughtiness of heresies was brought low.[^2921]

*Troparion:*
Having been strengthened by the grace of the Almighty, thou didst take the field against the principalities of demons, O father, and didst vanquish them, praying fervently for us who praise thee.[^2922]

*Theotokion:*
As a divine temple, as a holy mountain, as a fountain of incorruption, as the only chosen one for God our Creator, let us bless the Virgin.[^2923]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
With Thy divine light, O Good One, enlighten with love the souls of those who rise early unto Thee, I pray, that they may know Thee, O Word of God, the true God, Who callest them from the gloom of sin.[^2924]

*Troparion:*
With torrents of tears, O father, thou didst dry up the deep of the passions unto the end; and by the flowings of thy teachings, O blessed one, thou didst drown the floods of heresies.[^2925]

*Troparion:*
Enlightened by thy nod toward God, O father Ephrem, thy mind became wholly God-like, receiving immaterially the manifestations of the Divine Spirit, as a mirror.[^2926]

*Troparion:*
Truly wast thou a capacious temple of the Trinity, O father, variegated with grace, with the illumination of pure virtues, and with the soundness of teachings.[^2927]

*Theotokion:*
The tasting of the tree in Eden showed me dead through the wicked assault of the serpent; but thou, having given birth unto Christ the Giver of life, hast quickened me, O only woman full of the grace of God.[^2928]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Beholding the sea of life surging with the tempest of temptations, and fleeing unto Thy calm haven, I cry unto Thee: Lead up my life from corruption, O Greatly Merciful One.[^2929]

*Troparion:*
Having laid down not sand as a foundation, but unbroken faith, O God-bearer, thou didst remain unbent by all the assaults of the enemy, steered by an invincible hand.[^2930]

*Troparion:*
Thy tongue truly became as the pen of a swiftly writing scribe, recounting all-pious understanding, inscribing upon the tablets of the heart the law of the Spirit, O father.[^2931]

*Troparion:*
Sailing in the calm of thy dogmas, O divinely wise Ephrem, men are delivered from the deeps of soul-corrupting billows, and are saved by faith from the warring tempest of heresies.[^2932]

*Theotokion:*
He Who is higher than all understood and visible creation, as God, came forth incarnate from thy womb, having preserved thee incorrupt even as thou wast before childbirth, O Virgin Mother.[^2933]

*Kontakion, Tone 2, Podoben: "Seeking the highest" (Вы́шнихъ и҆щѧ̀):*
Ever foreseeing the hour of judgment, thou didst weep bitterly, O Ephrem, as a lover of silence; and thou wast an active teacher in deeds, O venerable one; therefore, O universal father, thou dost rouse the slothful unto repentance.[^2934]

*Ikos:*
Distill the waters of thy grace into my soul, washing it from every defilement of impurity; that having been cleansed from these, and having completed the remaining time of life zealously and spiritually in all things, it may delight in the divine sweetness whereof thou hast partaken, and wherewith thou hast watered all who are burned by the passions; for behold, by thy words thou dost rouse the slothful unto repentance.[^2935]

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
The angel made the furnace dew-yielding for the venerable youths, but the command of God, consuming the Chaldeans, persuaded the tyrant to cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.[^2936]

*Troparion:*
Thou didst appear as the most sure lawgiver of monastics, O all-honored one, and deliverer from all entanglements of the enemy; therefore men honor thy precious and sacred memory upon earth, O blessed one.[^2937]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast a choice instrument of the Spirit, O ever-memorable one, ever resounding through thine inspirations, and singing unto us a saving hymn of repentance, as we praise thee.[^2938]

*Theotokion:*
Beyond word is thy conception, O Bride of God, for thou didst bear God the Word, Who delivered all men from irrationality, and grants a word to cry: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers.[^2939]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
From the flame Thou didst pour forth dew for the venerable ones, and the sacrifice of the righteous one Thou didst consume with water; for Thou, O Christ, doest all things solely by willing: Thee do we exalt above all unto all ages.[^2940]

*Troparion:*
Light-bearing as another sun didst thou appear, emitting the rays of teachings unto the ends of the earth; thou didst drive away the gloom of ignorance and of every sin, O blessed one, by the light of repentance.[^2941]

*Troparion:*
Besprinkled with the streams of divine dogmas, flowing as another river from Eden, thou didst water the face of the earth, O marvelous one, and didst choke the tares of impiety.[^2942]

*Theotokion:*

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
It is impossible for men to see God, upon Whom the ranks of angels dare not gaze; but through thee, O all-pure one, the Word incarnate hath appeared unto men; Whom magnifying, with the heavenly hosts we bless thee.[^2944]

*Troparion:*
Wounded by love for the Almighty, weeping didst thou finish all thy life, crying aloud with dread, O venerable one: Subside the waves of Thy grace, O Savior, preserving it richly for me in the life to come.[^2945]

*Troparion:*
Sweet is thy word and bestower of contrition, filled with enlightenment for those who run unto thee, O God-bearing Ephrem, right marvelous one; and blameless is thy life, adorned and illuminated in all things by God-woven virtues.[^2946]

*Troparion:*
Thou wast a temple of the Spirit and a river filled with life-giving waters, an unshakable foundation of the Church, the confirmation of monastics, an ever-flowing stream of divine contrition, O Ephrem, right marvelous one.[^2947]

*Theotokion:*
The human intellect cannot grasp the mystery of thy childbirth beyond mind, O Virgin; for God, having taken up abode in thy womb, did not disrupt the lock of virginity, as He alone knows, the Incomprehensible.[^2948]

By thy contrition, O venerable father Ephrem, thou didst appear as a chalice of the hidden treasures of the wisdom of Christ, and by thy divine teachings thou dost gladden the souls of the faithful.[^2949]

*Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:*

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos. Glory..., Tone 2. By Cyprian:*
Like a palm tree according to David, thou didst blossom forth, O venerable father; with the sword thou didst cut off the tongues of blasphemers, O Ephrem; by abstinence thou didst dry up the deeps of the passions; thou didst appear as an instrument of the Holy Spirit, having taken up the weapon of the Cross: unceasingly pray unto Christ for us, who ever celebrate Thy precious memory with faith.[^2951]

*Both now..., Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "When from the tree" (Е҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*
Beholding the Creator of all, Who had endured many insults and was lifted up upon the Cross, the all-pure one groaned, saying: O all-hymned Lord, my Son and my God, how, wishing to honor Thy creation, O Master, dost Thou endure dishonor in the flesh? Glory unto Thy great compassion and unto Thy condescension, O Lover of mankind.[^2952]

*In the same month, on the 29th day: The translation of the relics of the holy hieromartyr Ignatius the God-bearer.*[^2954]
*At "Lord, I have cried," Stichera on 6, Tone 4, Podoben: "As one valiant among martyrs" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*
Having been the foremost successor of the Theologians, thou didst follow in their footsteps; hastening from the East, thou didst appear in the West, illuminating with prayers of divine preaching, where, O all-wise one, having set from the world, thou didst shine forth unto God, crowned with the radiance of grace.[^2955]

*Sticheron:*
Holily were thy relics restored unto thy city, O all-wise God-bearer, more radiantly sanctified on account of suffering, and shining with grace, having through their return become the mediator of festival unto us, filling us with divinely inspired gladness, and satisfying with fragrance those who piously honor thee.[^2956]

*Sticheron:*
From the East first as the day-star, O Ignatius, thou didst shine forth most radiantly in the West; and now by the return of thy divine relics thou hast stretched forth rays upon earth from the evening; and thou prayest unto Christ to deliver from corruption and perils those who celebrate thy most precious memory with faith.[^2957]

*Glory..., Tone 8. By Anatolius:*
O God-bearer Ignatius, having winged thyself with thy desired Christ, thou didst receive the reward of the sacred ministry of the Gospel of Christ, which was to be finished by blood; therefore, having become the wheat of the immortal Husbandman, thou wast ground by the teeth of wild beasts, and didst show thyself as sweet bread unto Him: pray for us, O blessed sufferer.[^2958]

*Both now..., Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (Ѡ҆ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ!):*
What is this visible sight which is seen by mine eyes, O Master? Thou Who upholdest all creation, being lifted up upon the Tree, dost die, Who givest life unto all!—cried the Birthgiver of God weeping, when she beheld lifted up upon the Cross Him Who had ineffably shone forth from her as God and man.[^2959]

*At the Aposticha of the Octoechos. Glory..., Tone 4. By the Studite:*
O firm and adamantine soul of thine, right blessed Ignatius! For having an unslackening longing toward Him Who is thy true Lover, thou didst say: There is not in me a material-loving fire, but rather living water speaking within me, saying inwardly unto me: Come unto the Father. Therefore, inflamed by the Divine Spirit, thou didst choose that the wild beasts should more quickly sever thee from the world and dispatch thee unto the desired Christ; Whom pray thou to save our souls.[^2960]

*Both now..., Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion, Podoben: "All-praised martyrs" (Всехва́льнїи мꙋ́ченицы):*
Standing by the Cross of thy Son and God, and beholding His longsuffering, the pure Mother said weeping: Woe is me, O sweetest Child! Why dost Thou suffer these things unjustly, O Word of God, that Thou mayest save mankind?[^2961]

*January 29 (Fol. 205r).*

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
And being a sharer in ways, and successor to the thrones of the Apostles, thou didst find practice, O God-inspired one, an ascent unto contemplation; therefore, rightly dividing the word of truth, thou didst also suffer for the faith even unto blood, O holy hieromartyr Ignatius: pray to Christ God that our souls may be saved.

*Ikos:*
God, having sanctified Jeremiah from the womb, and knowing him before he was born as a foreseer that he would be a vessel of that Holy Spirit, fills him forthwith from his youthful life, and sends him as a prophet and preacher unto all to foretell in the streets His coming upon earth; so also God Himself, born of the Virgin, having come unto preaching, found from infancy a disciple worthy of His grace, the God-bearing and divine Ignatius.

*At Small Vespers, Stichera on 4, Tone 4. Podoben: "As noble" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ):*
Having ascended unto the height of the elevation of Christ's love, thou didst behold His unutterable and divine mysteries; which having revealed, thou didst explain unto the people as a wise preacher of piety; therefore pray that they may be delivered from corruption and afflictions, who faithfully follow thy teachings, O venerable one.[^2972]

Having loosed the bonds of heresies, O venerable one, by the wisdom of thy words and teachings, thou didst gather into oneness of mind those who praise Christ in right understanding of the Orthodox faith, O Gregory; Whom do thou beseech, that they may be delivered from corruption and afflictions, who faithfully receive thy God-proclaimed teachings.

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 2. Podoben: "O house of Ephratha" (До́ме є҆ѵфра́ѳовъ):*
The grace of Christ's Church hath prevailed and is exceedingly adorned; she is filled with all understanding by the life and teachings of the Apostles and by the sacred ministry of the great hierarchs.[^2973]

*Verse:* Their sound is gone forth into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world.[^2974]

Heavenly wisdom and human wisdom with them, of eminent holy graces, with accomplishments overcoming all human speech, hast thou made marvelous in these three holy ones.

*Verse:* Thy priests shall be clothed with righteousness, and Thy righteous ones shall rejoice.[^2975]

Basil the divine mind, Gregory the divine voice, John the all-fair luminary: let the three highest servants and ministers of the Trinity be glorified together.

*Glory..., Tone 6:*
O good, kind, and faithful servants, good laborers of Christ's vineyard, who also bore the burden of the day, and increased the talent given unto you, and envied not those who came after you; therefore the gates of heaven were opened unto you: enter therefore into the joy of the Master, Christ, and pray for us, O holy teachers.[^2976]

*Both now..., Theotokion:*
No one that hastens unto thee departs ashamed from thee, O most pure Virgin Mother of God; but asks for grace, and receives the gift according to his profitable petition.

*Troparion, Tone 4:*
As being of one mind with the Apostles, and teachers of the universe, entreat the Master of all to grant peace unto the universe, and great mercy unto our souls.

*Glory..., Both now..., Theotokion:*

*At Great Vespers, "Blessed is the man", the first antiphon.*

*On "Lord, I have cried", Stichera on 8: Tone 4, Podoben: "As noble" (Ꙗ҆́кѡ до́блѧ): Trum- Month of January (Fol. 208v).*

*Stichera on "Lord, I have cried" (continued):*
*...pets of preaching, with fearful and well-heard thunders roaring from on high, and declaring the glory of God unto the ends of the earth: those preachers of the great Trinity, John and Basil, let us worthily glorify together with Gregory.*

*The champions of the Trinity, the ramparts of piety, who are three Apostles after the Twelve, rivers pouring forth living water from Eden, watering the face of the earth with life-giving, divine streams, great elements who established the faith like creation: let them be honored worthily.*

*Verse:* There are no speeches nor languages where their voices are not heard.[^2977]

*Not drowning in the abyss of the sea with those who suffer shipwreck, but snatching men from the counter-wave of divine and wise teachings, and leading them up to the light of salvation ordained by divine baptism: the consecrated judges of orthodoxy, confirming all the ends of the earth, the three great preachers: let us ever praise them with words in singing voices, following their dogmas, praying ever: who having boldness before God, to grant peace and steadfast orthodoxy unto the universe.*

*Podoben: "With what laudatory crowns" (Кі́ими похва́льными вѣнцы̑):*
*With what laudatory crowns shall we crown the teachers? Divided in bodies and united in the Spirit, God-bearing intercessors of the single-numbered Trinity and ministers, luminaries enlightening the universe, pillars of the Church, whom with crowns of glory, as victors, Christ our God, Who hath great mercy, crowns.*

*With what songful beauties shall we crown the God-bearers? Heavenly initiates of mysteries and preachers, theologians exceedingly eminent in orthodoxy: great Basil, the sacredly revealed, divine and God-speaking Gregory, and John, exceedingly golden in tongue; whom the Trinity, the Lord Who hath great mercy, worthily glorified.*

*With what laudatory words shall we bless the hierarchs? Equal to the Apostles by grace, and with honorable gifts, and supernatural endowments; true and genuine saviors, and our blessed ones in word and deed; who establish all the Christ-illumined ones in faith; heavenly men, whom Christ our God, Who hath great mercy, honored.*

*With what [laudatory crowns shall we wreathe John, and exceedingly] January 30 (Fol. 209r).*

*Stichera on "Lord, I have cried" (continued):*
*...with Basil, Gregory, and John exceedingly: honorable receptacles of the Spirit, steadfast champions of the faith, pillars of the Church, confirmation of the faithful, consolation of all that sin; fountains welling forth water, drawing from which we are sweetened in soul, asking remission of transgressions and great mercy.*

*Glory..., Tone 6:*
Today let us praise the mystical trumpets of the Spirit, the God-bearing fathers, who sang in the midst of the Church a harmonious song of theology: one unchangeable Trinity, essence and Godhead; the overthrowers of Arius and champions of the Orthodox, who ever pray unto the Lord that our souls may find mercy.

*Both now..., Theotokion:*
Who shall not bless thee...

*Entrance. Prokeimenon of the day. And the Readings.*

*The Reading from Deuteronomy (Deut. 1:8–17):*[^2978]
In those days, Moses said unto the sons of Israel: Behold, I have delivered the land before your face; go in and inherit it, which the Lord sware unto your fathers, Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, to give it unto them, and to their seed after them. And I spake unto you at that time, saying: I am not able to bear you myself alone. The Lord your God hath multiplied you, and behold, ye are this day as the stars of heaven for multitude. May the Lord God of our fathers add unto you, that ye may be a thousand times more, and bless you as He hath said unto you. And I took of you wise men, and skillful, and understanding, and I set them to rule over you, rulers over thousands, and rulers over hundreds, and rulers over fifties, and rulers over tens, and officers to your judges. And I charged your judges at that time, saying: Hear the causes between your brethren, and judge righteously between a man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him. Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; thou shalt judge the small and the great alike; thou shalt not be afraid of the face of man, for the judgment is God's.

*The Reading from Deuteronomy (Deut. 10:14–16):*[^2979]
In those days, Moses said unto the sons of Israel: Behold, the heaven and the heaven of heavens belong to the Lord thy God, the earth also, and all things that are therein. Yet the Lord preferred your fathers, to love them; and He chose their seed after them, even you, above all nations, as at this day. Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart, and stiffen your neck no more *Month of January (Fol. 209v).*

*The Reading from Deuteronomy (continued, Deut. 10:17–21):*
...any more. For the Lord your God, He is God of gods, and Lord of lords, a God great, mighty, and terrible, Who regards not persons, nor takes reward. He executes judgment for the fatherless and widow, and loves the stranger, in giving him food and raiment. Love ye therefore the stranger; for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt. Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God; Him only shalt thou serve, and to Him shalt thou cleave, and swear by His name. He is thy boast, and He is thy God, Who hath done for thee these great and glorious things, which thine eyes have seen.

*The Reading from the Wisdom of Solomon (Wis. 3:1–9):*[^2980]
The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and there shall no torment touch them. In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die, and their departure was taken for misery, and their going from us to be utter destruction; but they are in peace. For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality. And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded; for God proved them, and found them worthy for Himself. As gold in the furnace hath He tried them, and received them as a burnt offering sacrifice. And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble. They shall judge nations, and have dominion over peoples, and the Lord shall reign over them unto the ages. They that put their trust in Him shall understand the truth, and such as be faithful in love shall abide with Him; for grace and mercy is in His saints, and He hath visitation in His elect.

*At the Litiya, Sticheron, Tone 2. By Nilus Xanthopoulos:[^2981]*
Come, ye servants of the heavenly Trinity, let us praise the earthly trinity of holy hierarchs: Basil, namesake of the kingdom; Gregory, surnamed from theology; and John, truly named of grace; who searched out the depths of the Spirit's wisdom; streams of the ocean, ever-flowing fountains welling with living water, pellucid pearls, earthly luminaries, rudders of the Church, bright fruit-bearing trees, stewards of grace, the mouth of my Christ, and champions of the Trinity, immediately illumined by Her, and praying unceasingly for our souls.

*Sticheron:*
The burning coals of the intolerable fire, who were enlightened thereby, let us faithfully praise; for they, having been kindled by union with Him became luminaries of the world, having shown forth as a life-bearing power for the poor; they piously proclaimed openly the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit. Therefore let us also say: Rejoice, O divinely wise trinity of the Trinity!

*Tone 6:*

*Sticheron:*
O Holy and Adorable Trinity, glory to Thy wise providence, for Thou hast granted unto men three great luminaries taken from among men, enlightening them with the light of Thy knowledge, and illuminating them with the radiance of Thy saving and honorable desires, whereby the universe, being enriched by the light of understanding, is illumined with Thy glory and hastens toward Thy blessed Kingdom. Admonishing us to hear their divine teachings, do Thou Thyself, O Holy Trinity, listen to their prayers offered on our behalf, as God all-bountiful, and save our souls, O Lover of mankind!

*Glory... Tone 6:*

*Sticheron:*
Hierarchs of Christ, and glory of the fathers, pillars of the faith, and teachers and guardians of the faithful: having come together, O ye lovers of the feast, let us sing with praises in hymns, saying: Rejoice, O light of the Church, Basil all-wise, and immovable pillar! Rejoice, O heavenly mind, supreme hierarch, Gregory the Theologian! Rejoice, O golden-worded, all-golden John, radiant preacher of repentance! But O thrice-rich fathers, cease not ever to pray unto Christ on behalf of those who celebrate with faith and love your all-sacred and divine solemnity!

*Both now... Theotokion, in the same tone:*

*Theotokion:*
The divine beauty and spiritual joy, the only Birthgiver of God[^2982] and steadfast rampart of the faithful: having come together, O ye lovers of the feast, let us sing with praises in hymns, saying: Rejoice, O pure Virgin Mother, radiant lamp, and heavenly gate! Rejoice, O tabernacle of consecration, who didst contain God within thy womb, O all-spotless one! Rejoice, who art higher beyond comprehension than all the heavenly ranks! Therefore, O unwedded Mother, Birthgiver of God, cease not to preserve thy servants, who ever hymn thee with faith and love, and bow down before thy seedless childbearing!

*At the Aposticha, Stichera, Tone 1. Podoben: "O all-lauded martyrs" (Всехва́льніи мꙋ́ченицы):*

*Sticheron:*
The mystical initiates of the Spirit together, the articulate trumpets of God, the divine mirrors: let us worthily praise today Basil the Great, Gregory the divine and fire-inspired, and John Chrysostom,[^2983] who pours forth golden-flowing teachings unto us Chrysostom.

*Verse: The saints shall boast in glory, and they shall rejoice upon their beds [LXX Ps. 149:5].*

*Sticheron:*
The foundation of faith, the divine and vigilant mind, the golden-flowing river, the most radiant and honorable luminaries, champions of the Trinity, receptacles of the graces of the Spirit, immovable pillars, confirmations of the Church: let us worthily praise them with hymns!

*Verse: Thy priests shall be clothed with righteousness, and Thy righteous ones shall rejoice [LXX Ps. 131:9].*

*Sticheron:*
Instruments of the Spirit, trumpets of the divine thunder, lightnings of the preaching, all-radiant lamps, golden and light-bearing from God: O thrice-blessed Basil, Gregory divinely wise, all-golden and all-honorable John: pray unto Christ that He save those who honor you!

*Glory... Tone 6:*

*Sticheron:*
Today the souls of earthborn mortals are lifted up from earthly things; today they become heavenly in the memory of the saints: for the heavenly gates are lifted up, and the Master's mysteries are declared unto us; the words of the Word are proclaimed, and tongues sing wonders. Let us also cry aloud unto the Savior: Glory to Thee, O Christ God, for peace was granted unto the faithful through them!

*Both now... Of the Feast:*

*Sticheron:*
Today Christ is brought into the sanctuary as an infant; today He Who gave the Law unto Moses is brought under the Law. The angelic hosts marveled, beholding Him Who holds all things held in the hands of the elder. Simeon, having been filled with reverent awe, cried aloud with joy: Now lettest Thou me depart, O Savior, from temporal life unto unaging rest; for I have seen Thee, and I have rejoiced!

*At the blessing of the loaves, Troparion, Tone 4:*
*Being of one mind with the Apostles... (Written at Small Vespers). And Rejoice, O Virgin Birthgiver of God: twice.*

*The Office of the Hieromartyr Hippolytus,[^2984] sung at Compline.*

*Canon, Tone 4. By John the Monk.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
The One mighty in battle cast the chariots of Pharaoh and his power into the sea; let us sing a new song, for He is glorified!

*Troparion:*
Come, let us praise the hieromartyr with songs of martyrdom, beholding him radiant with God-illumined grace, ever glorifying Christ.

*Troparion:*
Contending for the spiritual flock entrusted unto thee by Christ for the suffering flock in distress, thou didst abundantly lay down thy life, O father, and wast adorned with a twofold crown.

*Troparion:*
Having been consecrated by divine command, O Hippolytus, and anointed with the oil of rejoicing, thou hast marked thyself with the blood of martyrdom.

*Theotokion:*
Beholding on Mount Sinai the unconsumed bush which prefigured thee, O Virgin, Moses saw that it was unconsumed by the radiance of the divine fire, for thou hast given birth unto God.

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
The bow of the mighty hath grown weak, and the feeble have girded themselves with strength; therefore my heart is established in the Lord [LXX 1 Kings 2:4].

*Troparion:*
Thou didst shepherd the rational sheep, and like a lamb among sheep thou wast sacrificed beforehand, imitating the Chief Shepherd of all and the Lamb of God.

*Troparion:*
With spiritual milk, O Hippolytus, thou didst divinely inspire and nourish thy flock; and rejoicing, thou didst drink the cup of the testimony of Christ.

*Troparion:*
Leading assemblies of passion-bearers, thou didst receive suffering for piety, glorifying the one God the Father, with the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

*Theotokion:*
Rejoice, O Mother unwedded, who didst contain God the Word in thy womb, and didst give birth unto Him incarnate as both God and man!

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
Proclaiming the advent of Thine appearance upon earth, O Christ God, the prophet cried aloud with joy: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Like an intricately woven divine chain of thy virtues, O Hippolytus, as shepherd and witness thou wast honored greatly by God, rejoicing in Him.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst surpass the offering of Abel, for thou didst bring rational lambs unto God, and rejoicing with thy blood thou didst stand openly before His presence.

*Troparion:*
Having conquered by the Spirit the blasphemous malice of the heretics, O blessed one, thou wast an eminent hieromartyr through love of the Master.

*Theotokion:*
When the angels beheld the Son of God coming forth from thy womb, O pure Virgin, they cried aloud with joy: Glory to thy childbearing, O blessed one!

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
Thou, O my Lord, hast come as a light into the world, a holy light turning from gloomy ignorance those who hymn Thee in faith.

*Troparion:*
Thou wast a true martyr among priests, and hierarch among martyrs, and thou shinest with twofold gifts, O Hippolytus.

*Troparion:*
Thou art indeed a golden-radiant and beautiful stone, O Hippolytus, and thy suffering was adorned with the radiance of thy sacred hierarchical office.

*Troparion:*
Piously didst thou refute Hellenic myths, O most distinguished among martyrs, and the lawless deceit of the Hebrews by divine grace.

*Theotokion:*
Thee do we set forth as an unconquerable weapon against enemies; thee have we acquired as the hope and anchor of our salvation, O Bride of God!

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord, the Church cries aloud unto Thee, having been cleansed from the blood of demons by the blood which flowed for mercy's sake from Thy side [LXX Jonah 2:10].

*Troparion:*
Thou didst offer unto the Savior a sacrifice of praise in the assembly of the venerable, as mediator between God and men; and fervently didst thou offer thy soul through blood.

*Troparion:*
Thou didst receive an abundance of gifts through the Spirit from God, O hieromartyr, in the opening of thy divine lips, and thou dost offer thyself thankfully in mortification.

*Troparion:*
O Christ, as the divine assembly of Thy passion-bearers gave hope to those lying in affliction, seeing they were already nourished with future goods and considered death as sweet life...

*Theotokion:*
O wonder, newest of all wonders! For having conceived without knowing man, a Virgin contained without constraint in her womb Him Who holds all things!

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 1. Podoben: "While the soldiers were guarding Thy tomb" (Гро́бъ тво́й Сп҃се):*
An ever-radiant luminary hast thou appeared unto the world, illuminating the minds of the faithful with the lightnings of thy divine words, O Hierarch Hippolytus. Therefore do we all joyfully celebrate today thy sacred and divine memory, and honor it with faith.

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
Thou Who didst save Thy children of Abraham in the fire, and didst slay the Chaldeans whom justice righteously snared: all-praised Lord God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Troparion:*
With the splendors of martyrdom and of the priesthood, O hieromartyr, thou dost clearly enlighten those who cry aloud unto Christ in thy memory: All-praised Lord God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Troparion:*
Beholding the most sacred suffering of martyrdom standing before thee, from the One Who foreknows from afar, O father, rejoicing thou didst cry aloud: All-praised Lord God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

Having endured wounds of torment from ardent love, patiently with boldness Hippolytus cried aloud: All-praised Lord God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Theotokion:*
Praise the unchanging God, Who for His compassion toward men came and was conceived in thy womb seedlessly and supernaturally: All-praised Lord God of our fathers, blessed art Thou!

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Hymn Christ God, Who in the form of an angel appeared in the fiery furnace unto the singers, O ye children; bless Him, ye priests; and exalt Him above all, ye people, unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
As a tender and fat sacrifice, the good shepherd is led like a sheep unto Christ, crying aloud: Bless Him, ye priests; and exalt Him above all, ye people, unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Shining with the crown of martyrdom, O Christ, the hierarch shone forth upon Thy Church, crying aloud with joy: Praise Him, ye children; and exalt Him above all, ye people, unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Under the menacing sentence of death, Christ's passion-bearer Hippolytus cried aloud with joy: Ye children, bless Christ; and exalt Him above all, ye people, unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
Hymn Christ God, Who was ineffably and seedlessly conceived, and brought forth joy unto the universe, O ye children; bless Him, ye priests; and exalt Him above all, ye people, unto all ages!

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
Thy childbearing was shown to be incorrupt: God came forth from thy womb, as a flesh-bearer He appeared upon earth and dwelt among men. Therefore, O Birthgiver of God, we all magnify thee!

*Troparion:*
As an all-blessed hieromartyr, thou didst illuminate the Church of Christ with a twofold radiance, and thou makest glad the hearts of those who hymn thee. Therefore do we all worthily bless thee.

*Troparion:*
Having poured forth a fountain of teachings for the Church of Christ, O all-blessed one, thou offerest like a river unto God streams from the blood of thy martyrdom: therefore do we all bless thee, O Hippolytus.

*Troparion:*
Divinely speaking, thou didst teach us to worship the one God in Trinity, the Creator of all creatures visible and invisible; and thou hast been adorned with the crown of martyrdom.

*Theotokion:*
The shining angel stood before thee and was greatly illumined by the rays of thy virginity;[^2985] forgetting his own proper glory, with fear he cried unto thee: Rejoice!

*Stichera, Tone 1. Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Небе́сныхъ чинѡ́въ):*

*Sticheron:*
Having received the grace of the priesthood having received the grace of the priesthood, O father, thou didst enlighten all with divine teachings, O divinely wise Hippolytus; and with sacred writings thou didst interpret the divine sayings of the prophets, clarifying for us what was to come from thence.

*Sticheron:*
Adorned with the divine crown of confession, by the drops of thy blood thou didst adorn the garment of the priesthood; all-radiant and beautiful didst thou stand before the King, Master, and Creator, O all-blessed Hippolytus!

*Sticheron:*
Having now acquired boldness toward Christ the Savior, O all-blessed one: save from tribulations, misfortunes, cruel circumstances, passions, falls, and necessities all those who honor thee in faith, through thy well-pleasing prayers!

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:*
By the rod of thy protection, O pure Birthgiver of God, drive away the beast-like passions of my wretched soul, leading me thence peacefully unto life, and number me among the holy flock of thine elect sheep!

*At Matins, at God is the Lord, Troparion of the Saints, twice:*

*Glory... Both now... Theotokion:*

*After the first Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 5. Podoben: "The Word co-unoriginate" (Собезнача́льное Сло́во):*[^2986]
Let us all praise Basil as the royal ornament of the Church, the inexhaustible treasury of dogmas: for by these he himself instructed us to honor the Holy Trinity, united indeed in essence, yet divided in hypostases.

*Glory... Tone 4. Podoben: "Speedily anticipate" (Ско́рѡ предварѝ):*
Most radiant luminaries of the Church of Christ, ye have enlightened the world by your teachings, O divinely wise fathers! Having dried up the heresies of all the blasphemous, and extinguished the flame-like confusion of their blasphemies: therefore, as hierarchs of Christ, pray that we may be saved!

*Both now... Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:*
O all-hymned Virgin, Mother of Christ God, Mary Bride of God unwedded, protectress of the faithful: deliver from every tribulation and every necessity, O beneficent Birthgiver of God, those who with faith and love flee under thy protection, O only unwedded Bride!

*After the second Kathisma, Sessional Hymn, Tone 3. Podoben: "Of the divine faith" (Бж҃е́ственныя вѣ́ры):*
Thou wast a pillar of the Church, and didst show thyself to be an unstealable treasury of piety, O Gregory the Theologian! In passionlessness didst thou live thy life, and didst explain the dogmas of the Trinity, O venerable father: pray unto Christ God for the salvation of our souls!

*Glory* Tone 4. Podoben: "Joseph marveled" (Оу҆диви́ся і҆ѡ́сифъ):*
Flying like wise bees through the flower-meadow of the Scriptures, ye did gather well from the most excellent flowers; and the honey of your teachings ye present together unto all the faithful for their sweet delight. Therefore everyone who partakes thereof cries aloud with joy: Stand by us again even after death, O blessed ones, who praise you!

*Both now... Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:*
Storm-tossed by the surging waves of passions, I, lacking conscience, warmly call upon thee, O all-pure one: despise me not, a wretched one, to perish, O thou who hast given birth unto the abyss of mercy; for besides thee I have no other hope. Let me not, having put my hope in thee, appear as a rejoicing and laughing-stock unto enemies: for thou canst do whatsoever thou desirest, as Mother of the God of all!

*After the Polyeleos, Sessional Hymn, Tone 4. Podoben: "Thou hast appeared today" (Ꙗ҆ви́лся є҆сѝ):*
Let the all-wise teachers of the universe, who glorified God on earth by word and deed, be magnified today, as our intercessors for salvation.

*Glory...*
Today the Church celebrates the honorable festival of the three teachers: for they established the Church by their divine dogmas.

*Both now... Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:*
Unassailable protectress of the afflicted, and fervent intercessor of them that trust in thee: deliver me from tribulations, for thou art the helper of all!

*Then: Songs of Ascents [Anabathmoi], first Antiphon of Tone 4.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 4: Thy priests shall be clothed with righteousness, and Thy righteous ones shall rejoice [LXX Ps. 131:9].*

*Verse: My mouth shall speak wisdom, and the meditation of my heart shall be understanding [LXX Ps. 48:4].*

*Let every breath [praise the Lord].*

*Gospel according to John, pericope 36 [Jn. 10:9–16].[^2987]*

*After Psalm 50, Sticheron, Tone 6:*
Grace was poured forth upon your lips, O venerable fathers, and ye became shepherds of the Church of Christ, teaching the rational sheep to believe in the consubstantial Trinity in one Godhead!

*Canon of the Birthgiver of God with the heirmos on 6, Tone 6; and of the Saints, two canons on 8. By John of Euchaita.[^2988]*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
Come, ye people, let us sing a song unto Christ God, Who divided the sea and guided the people whom He brought out of Egyptian bondage, for He is glorified!

*Troparion:*
Piously confessing thee with soul and body as the pure and true Birthgiver of God, O all-pure one: save me from cruel tribulations, diseases, and sins, do thou save me!

*Troparion:*
We have known the abyss of gifts lying in thee as an ocean. Therefore, fleeing fervently unto thy divine protection, O Birthgiver of God, we are saved.

*Troparion:*
Pray for us who hymn thee, O all-pure one, unto Him Who was incarnate from thy most pure and precious blood, that we may be delivered from transgressions and bitter illnesses.

*Another Canon of the Saints, whose Acrostic is: I praise the three rays of the Tri-sunned light.[^2989] The composition of the same John.*

*Ode 1, Tone and Heirmos the same:*

*Troparion:*
What thanksgiving, what recompense worthy of our benefactors, O men, shall be offered by us, through whom we are guided unto well-being?

*Troparion:*
Let all eloquent tongues, skills, and arts, and all the power of words, now be moved unto one cause, and honoring them mutually, let them pay due honor!

*Troparion:*
The heavenly-minded ones did not seek to possess anything of their own upon the earth; having shown themselves to be guardians and protectors of the commonwealth, let them be counted worthy of common praises!

*Theotokion:*
As the common honor of our nature, O all-spotless one, we all glorify thee, having become one mouth and forming a single harmony.

*Second Canon of the Saints. By the same author. Tone 8. Heirmos:*
The rod of Moses, performing wonders in ancient times, smote and divided the sea in the form of a cross, and submerged Pharaoh who drove the chariots; and it saved Israel as a fugitive, who journeyed on foot, singing a hymn unto God!

*Troparion:*
This undertaking is not the achievement of human effort; but let the Wisdom that sits beside Thy throne, O Lover of mankind, assist me, granting the grace of speech whereby I may be able to glorify those whom she herself hath excellently pre-glorified!

*Troparion:*
As a cup is filled to overflowing, O Master, Thy grace and the abundant richness of Thy love for mankind are poured out and flowed, so as to show forth in bodily composition other angels, who are now set forth for our praise.

*Troparion:*
It is indeed fitting that these praises should be heavenly, an angelic hymn suited to these divine men: for they are gods by participation, having by nature in themselves the one true God living and speaking in them.

*Theotokion:*
The divinely wise choir celebrates the memory of the righteous with praises; and with them the Mother of God, as their head, is glorified together in beauty, holding the final, first, and middle place, and partaking in the good praises.

*Katavasia: The sun once traversed the dry depth-bearing land...[^2990]*

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
Establish us in Thee, O Lord, Who by the Tree didst put sin to death, and plant Thy fear in the hearts of us who hymn Thee!

*Troparion:*
Through thy prayers, O pure one, grant that God Whom thou didst bear be well-disposed toward thy servants who flee unto thy protection, and who faithfully bow down before thy childbearing.

*Troparion:*
Direct this my life, O Virgin, my hope and protectress, delivering me from cruel temptations and circumstances, O Ever-virgin!

*Troparion:*
As thou didst bear the hypostatic Wisdom of God in thine embrace, O Birthgiver of God: pray that those who hymn thee may be delivered from ignorance and delusion!

*Another Heirmos:*
Establishing me upon the rock of faith, Thou hast enlarged my mouth against mine enemies, for my spirit rejoiced in singing: There is none holy like our God, and none righteous besides Thee, O Lord! [LXX 1 Kings 2:1–2].

*Troparion:*
The great trumpet of the Church, the luminary enlightening the universe, the preacher embracing all the ends of the earth with his utterance: the renowned Basil rallies this gathering!

*Troparion:*
Radiant in life and deeds, radiant in words and teachings, surpassing all in all things—even as a second sun surpasses the stars—the much-hymned Theologian is blessed today!

*Troparion:*
Behold, the light of the world shines upon the world! Behold, the salt of the earth sweetens the earth! Behold, the tree of life offers fruits of immortality: the golden-mouthed saint! Come, ye who desire not to die, take your delight!

*Theotokion:*
He Who brought all things from non-being into being, and gave nature to each of existing things: He also knows how to alter the given laws of nature as He wills. Whence it is heard that a Virgin gave birth: who will not marvel!

*Another Heirmos:*
Thou Who in the beginning didst establish the heavens with understanding, and didst found the earth upon the waters: establish me, O Christ, upon the rock of Thy commandments, for there is none holy besides Thee, O only Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
Those who corrected morals and guided souls, the common saviors of all: who showed forth unto us examples of deeds and words, the radiant instructors of life, let them be radiantly praised!

*Troparion:*
The Spirit of God filled Basil with skill; Gregory had one of the tongues of fire, and breathed with the fire of sublime eloquence; and the mouth of Christ spoke in John.

*Troparion:*
The wisdom of this present age has the power of the preaching visibly rendering it idle, submitting to it, and serving it as a slave; for grace presents wise rhetors as preachers.

*Theotokion:*
He Who dwelt in the womb of the pure Virgin makes the souls of the God-bearing saints His dwelling; and through their lips He declares the mystery concerning His Mother.

*Katavasia: O Lord, the confirmation of them that put their trust in Thee...[^2991]*

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 8. Podoben: "The Wisdom and the Word" (Премꙋ́дрости):*
The great and radiant luminaries, the indestructible pillars of the Church, let us harmoniously praise, delighting in their virtues and words, and together in grace: the all-wise Chrysostom and Basil the Great, with Gregory the radiant Theologian; unto whom let us cry from the heart, calling aloud: O supreme hierarchs, pray unto Christ God to grant remission of transgressions unto those who lovingly celebrate your holy memory!

*Glory...*
Having received wisdom from God, like another three apostles of Christ, by the word of understanding ye compose dogmas which the fishermen previously set forth in simple words through understanding by the power of the Spirit; for thus was it fitting that our simple faith should acquire composition. Therefore we all cry aloud unto you: Pray unto Christ God to grant remission of transgressions unto those who lovingly celebrate your holy memory!

*Both now... Theotokion:*

*Theotokion:*
My humble soul, tossed by the storm of life's temptations, now being as it were without governance, sinking beneath the waves, appearing filled with the burden of sins and in peril of sinking to the bottom of Hades: anticipate with the mercy of thy prayers, O Birthgiver of God, granting calmness and delivering from perils; for thou art an unstormy harbor, praying unto thy Son and God to grant me remission of transgressions; for in thee do I have my hope, thine unworthy servant.

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
I have heard, O Lord, the report of Thy dispensation, and I glorified Thee, O only Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
O Birthgiver of God, who didst give birth unto God: grant me release from the wounds of my soul and the afflictions of my flesh!

*Troparion:*
Deliver me from adversity, and from tempest and perils, by thy prayers, O Mother of God, only all-hymned one!

*Troparion:*
Snatch me away, O Virgin, who am overwhelmed by the waves of this life, guiding me unto thy harbor!

*Another Heirmos:*
Thou didst come from the Virgin, neither an intercessor nor an angel, but Thou Thyself, O Lord, having become incarnate; and Thou didst save me, the whole man: therefore I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Having become discerning through earthly wisdom, O most glorious ones, ye acquired divine guidance; therefore, as a handmaid, ye did most wisely subject the former unto the latter.

*Troparion:*
O lovers of wisdom, if ye love the wise, become wise; and learn to speak, all ye who marvel at their words, being instructed thence in the exactness of action and contemplation.

*Theotokion:*
Like the late rain and the morning rain that came at the end,[^2992] the Creator of seasons and ages, bending down into thy womb, O all-spotless one, refreshes in due season them that languish.

*Another Heirmos:*
Thou art my strength, O Lord, Thou art also my power, Thou art my God, Thou art my rejoicing, Who, without leaving the bosom of the Father, hast visited our poverty. Therefore, with the Prophet Habakkuk, I cry unto Thee: Glory to Thy power, O Lover of mankind!

*Troparion:*
A pillar of fire preceding the faithful people and consuming the enemies of the faith, safely saving the tribes that follow him, the great Basil was shown forth. Let the Church of Christ take courage and conquer, having been enriched with so great a champion!

*Troparion:*
Sweetness of the tongue and delight of every hearing was thy word, O Gregory: manna of life, dew of sweetness, honey from the rock [LXX Ps. 80:17], angelic heavenly bread, exhorting men to be insatiably filled with its delight, and filling with sweetness them that partake thereof.

*Troparion:*
The river of spiritual gifts was filled even unto overflowing, and like a sweet stream from golden lips it waters the good face of the earth, gladdening and enriching every city of Christ with streams of divine waters.

*Theotokion:*
A nature simple enduring composition, and appearing higher than radiance in Thy Son, O Lady, the three God-bearing teachers confessed, proclaiming Him twofold according to nature, of two wills and twofold operation.[^2993]

*Katavasia: The heavens were covered...*[^2994]

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
O Giver of light and Creator of the ages, Lord: guide us in the light of Thy commandments, for besides Thee we know no other God!

*Troparion:*
Having an invincible weapon against the various temptations of the enemy, we who know thee to be the pure Birthgiver of God are continually delivered from every malice of the adversaries.

*Troparion:*
O thou who didst surpass the Cherubim: thou didst give birth unto the Fulfillment of the law, the only-begotten Son of God incarnate from thee; Him do thou implore for thy servants!

*Troparion:*
Having carried in thine arms the Creator of them that serve Him: grant Him unto us through thy prayers to be propitious, who now flee unto thee from the heart!

*Another Heirmos:*
Illumination of them that lie in darkness, salvation of the despairing, O Christ my Savior: early do I rise unto Thee, O King of peace; enlighten me with Thy radiance, for besides Thee I know no other God!

*Troparion:*
Thou didst give the fountain of Thy gifts unto the saints to drink of with all, O Lover of mankind, in no wise diminished by being poured forth; and Thou didst water the whole world with divine streams from their belly [Jn. 7:38].

*Troparion:*
What is gold to me? What to me are riches and glory and power? Smoke dispersing through the air: let all vanish, let the wind carry all away! To me, my one manifold wealth is the eloquence of the trinity of teachers.

*Troparion:*
The river pours forth incorruptible nourishment and divine drink; it pours forth immortal food unto the hungry and incorruptible drink unto the thirsty: living water unto the ages, keeping alive them that drink; be ye all filled with the abundant-flowing life!

*Theotokion:*
Malice had power over us, yet not unto the end; for it grew weak through the Virgin who gave birth in strength unto the Mighty One, Who assumed the weakness of the flesh and put to death him that was mighty in malice.

*Another Heirmos:*
Why hast Thou cast me away from Thy face, O unwaning Light, and an alien darkness has covered me, the wretched one? But turn me back, and direct my paths toward the light of Thy commandments, I pray!

*Troparion:*
Wise craftsmen in divine and human things craftsmen, wise in divine and human things, who with love of truth clearly made known unto us the natures of existing things, and fittingly declared unto all the Creator thereof: let us praise them with voices of thanksgiving!

*Troparion:*
The divine physicians of souls sweetened the bitter and tart remedies for salvation with the wise teachings of their words, both with skills and with graces; delight yourselves, all ye pious ones, and intertwine in beauty!

*Troparion:*
Every word is silent when the preachers of God speak divine things; and holding fast the honorable tablets, they set forth the New Covenant over the Old, legislating what is therein, unto whom the whole assembly of the faithful is numbered.

*Theotokion:*
A mortal nature outran the immortal unto holiness; and the virgin maiden surpassed the bodiless angels, having given birth unto God, the King of angels, upon Whom it is impossible for them to gaze.

*Katavasia: When Isaiah beheld...*[^2995]

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
Wallowing in the abyss of sin, I call upon the unsearchable abyss of Thy compassion: from corruption, O God, raise me up!

*Troparion:*
Knowing thee to be the harbor of salvation, as I sail the deep of this sorrowful life: I call upon thee, O Birthgiver of God: be the pilot of my soul!

*Troparion:*
I, the wretched one, have fallen away from a pure life through slothfulness; but raise me up, O blessed and all-spotless one, uniting me unto the commandments of thy Son!

*Troparion:*
Count me worthy of thy mercy, O Birthgiver of God, who didst bring forth the all-merciful Word, Who by His own blood delivered mankind from corruption!

*Another Heirmos:*
A great abyss of sins surrounds me, and imitating the prophet, I cry unto Thee: From corruption raise me up, O Lord!

*Troparion:*
Ye jointly theologize the three personal properties in the Trinity: the unbegottenness of the Father, the begetting of the Word, and the procession of the Spirit Himself.[^2996]

*Troparion:*
Heaven is the light-manifest salvation unto this house: for Christ, honoring two or three gathered in His name, greets them in their midst [Mt. 18:20].

*Troparion:*
Unfathomable is the earthly depth compared to the heavenly height; but heavenly desire lifted up the saints from the earth higher than the heavens.

*Theotokion:*
Having thee as a spring, O Virgin, and as the cause of all created things,[^2997] the three divinely speaking ones with new expressions fittingly apply a newly suited appellation.

*Another Heirmos:*
Cleanse me, O Savior, for many are mine iniquities; and lead me up from the abyss of evils, I pray, for unto Thee have I cried; and give ear unto me, O God of my salvation!

*Troparion:*
We have been taught to theologize the Trinity as one; we have received to hymn the Unity as three; we have learned from the fathers to worship the one three-hypostatic Nature.

*Troparion:*
The Word was God in the beginning with the Father, co-unoriginate; and the Spirit of God was God, pre-unoriginate; corresponding to Him, the Godhead is consubstantial and co-natural, as the divine preachers proclaim.

*Troparion:*
I unite and I divide that which is divided in unity; I conceive of one indivisibly, and I count three: receiving the three God-bearing teachers who thus persuade me to believe.

*Theotokion:*
Motherless before the flesh, fatherless after the incarnation: Son of the Father and of the Mother, calling both these above mind; for most glorious wonders belong unto God.

*Katavasia: I cried unto Thee...*[^2998]

*Kontakion, Tone 2. Podoben: "The firm" (Тве́рдыѧ):*
The sacred and God-speaking preachers, the summit of teachers, O Lord, Thou hast received into the enjoyment of Thy good things and into repose; for Thou didst accept their labors and death above all whole burnt offerings, O Thou Who alone dost glorify Thy saints!

*Ikos:*
Who is able to open his lips and move his tongue toward those who breathe with fire by the power of the Word and the Spirit? Yet so much do I dare to say: that these three surpassed all human nature by many and great gifts, having transcendently excelled in both action and contemplation by their brightness. Therefore hast Thou, O Holy One, counted them worthy of great gifts, as Thy faithful servants, O Thou Who alone dost glorify Thy saints!

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
When the golden image was worshiped on the plain of Dura [Dan. 3:1], Thy three children disregarded the godless command, and cast into the midst of the fire, being bedewed they sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Having been nailed to the Cross, He Who was incarnate from thee, O Birthgiver of God, tore up Adam's handwriting [Col. 2:14]; Him do thou now implore, O all-spotless one, that all who cry out in faith may be delivered from all perils: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Thou art a good hope and protectress of the faithful, O Lady; and now we pray thee to grant the abyss of compassion abyss of compassion unto all who put their trust in thee, and who cry unto thy Son: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Having been clothed through baptism with the fair garment of saving commandments, I, the wretched one, have defiled it through slothfulness; but now I flee unto thee, O Virgin, asking to be clothed again through thee with the garment of gladness.

*Another Heirmos:*
The contrary decree of the lawless tyrant raised a high flame; but Christ spread a spiritual dew upon the pious children, He Who is blessed and supremely glorified!

*Troparion:*
The unstable boldness of heresies that was aforetime is conquered and grows old, O blessed ones, melting like wax from the face of the fire; and every adulterous teaching is shown up when confronted by your fire-breathing utterances.

*Troparion:*
They turned away from the deceit of Hellenic prattle, and chose the persuasion that was the only rule among men; having established the truth under it, these three conquer and persuade the whole assembly of the faithful with words.

*Theotokion:*
In thee every prophecy found rest and received its fulfillment, causing those who speak to marvel; and from thee, O pure one, miracles pour forth more radiant than prophecies, manifesting wise expounders.

*Another Heirmos:*
The fire was ashamed before the condescension of God in Babylon of old; therefore the children in the furnace, dancing with joyful step as in a meadow of flowers, sang: Blessed art Thou, O God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Silent and crying out, visible and heard by virtue and wisdom, they were God-speaking pillars, bidding men to cry aloud by word and deed: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Wise in divine things, who thundered divine voices from above unto us, do ye pray for our souls; and receiving your utterances, O all-wise ones, we sing together with you: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Troparion:*
Hailstones of sling-stones from tongues shall fall upon the adversary, crushing rotten teachings if anyone dare among disputers to argue ignorantly: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Theotokion:*
He Who orders the elements and transforms natures as He wills dwelt in thee, O Virgin, and left thee a Virgin after childbirth, O Birthgiver of God Mary; unto Whom with thee, O all-spotless one, we cry aloud all-spotless one: Blessed is the God of our fathers!

*Katavasia: In the fire...*[^2999]

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
Him Who descended into the fiery furnace unto the Hebrew children, and changed the flame into dew, God: sing unto Him, all ye works, as the Lord, and exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Having acquired thee by faith as a firm pillar of strength, and a step, and a guardian, and an intercessor, we are ever saved, we sing of thy childbearing, O all-pure one, and we exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
We know thee to be the radiant fountain of immortality, O Birthgiver of God, as having given birth unto the Word of the immortal Father, Who delivers all from death who exalt Him above all unto the ages!

*Troparion:*
Thou dost ever pour forth a stream of healings unto us, the faithful; continually receiving His ungrudging grace, we hymn thy childbearing, O all-pure one, and we exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Another Heirmos, the same:*
We piously understand and honorably glorify one nature in boundless power, Unity and Trinity, directing all these things by the best words: for thus to glorify did the three God-bearing ones hand down, with whom we worship It unto the ages!

*Troparion:*
The three God-preachers were united, who united the three and preserved the indivisible in all by the divine nature; they received one undivided glory therefrom, summoning unto one praise them that exalt It above all unto the ages!

*Theotokion:*
Having assumed what is ours, and given His own in return, the Benefactor: He acted only, but suffered not, O Virgin; for He creates, yet orders not unto corruption; yea rather, suffering willingly, by passion He loosens passions, even as the three fathers mystically instruct us.

*Another Heirmos:*
Sevenfold did the Chaldean tyrant frantically kindle the furnace for the pious [Dan. 3:19]; but having seen them saved by a higher power, he cried unto the Creator and Deliverer: Ye children, bless; ye priests, sing; ye people, exalt Him above all unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
Those whom God hath united in honorable unity, let not man praising them separate; but esteeming them equal in those very gifts, let him count them equal also in hymnic praises: Ye children, bless; ye priests, sing; ye people, exalt Him above all unto all ages!

Mighty and invincible champions of the Godhead, and true, unerring fellow-workers, having searched well the depths of the Spirit, thence compose godly understandings concerning God, and teach men to sing: Ye people, exalt Christ above all unto all ages!

*Troparion:*
In the heavens two greatest luminaries by succession enlighten one after the other the land under the sun; but from the earth three other greatest luminaries shine more brightly upon the whole universe, shining upon one another, and singing together: Ye people, exalt Christ above all unto all ages!

*Theotokion:*
For our sake the incarnation and honorable passions, for our sake God was among the dead, without tasting death, as being free from passions; but by communion with mortal flesh, as is said, He partook of passions and death, with which we exalt Christ above all unto all ages!

*Katavasia: In the unendurable fire...*[^3000]

*At Ode 9 we do not sing "More honorable", but we sing the refrain:*
*Refrain: Magnify, O my soul, her who is more honorable than the heavenly hosts, the all-pure Virgin Birthgiver of God.*
*Then the Heirmos. Afterward we sing the same refrain also unto the other Theotokia.*

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
God the Word of God, Who by ineffable wisdom came to renew Adam who had fallen grievously into corruption through eating, and Who for our sake was ineffably incarnate of the Holy Virgin: with one mind, in hymns we faithful magnify Him!

*Refrain: Magnify, O my soul, her who is more honorable than the heavenly hosts, the all-pure Virgin Birthgiver of God.*
*Troparion:*
O all-blessed Maiden, I fervently place all my hope in thee: save me, O Mother of true life, and pray, O pure one, that I who magnify thee in hymns with faith and love may be filled with everlasting sweetness!

*Refrain: Magnify, O my soul, her who is more honorable than the heavenly hosts, the all-pure Virgin Birthgiver of God.*
*Troparion:*
Thou wast shown forth, O Virgin, as the gate of divine light: enlighten the darkness of my soul with the immaterial splendors of thy light, and implore, O pure one, that I who magnify thee in hymns with faith and love may be delivered from eternal fire!

*Refrain: Magnify, O my soul, her who is more honorable than the heavenly hosts, the all-pure Virgin Birthgiver of God.*
*Troparion:*
He Whom the Father begat from the womb before the ages as Son dwelt in thy womb: He became perfect man, and showed thee forth unto us, O Mother of God, as a fountain of gifts, who faithfully bow down before thine ineffable childbearing!

*Another Heirmos:*
The Son of the unoriginate Begetter, God and Lord, incarnate of the Virgin, hath appeared unto us, to enlighten what was darkened, to gather what was scattered therefore we magnify the all-hymned Birthgiver of God!

*Unto the canons of the Saints, at each troparion we sing these refrains:*

*Refrain: Magnify, O my soul, the three great luminaries among the hierarchs.*
*Troparion:*
O your labor and pastorship, both which greatest afflictions ye endured, having come together as one! And as three having jointly received, your most sweet union hath common praise.

*Refrain: Magnify, O my soul, the three holy hierarchs of the Church of Christ.*
*Troparion:*
Grace set forth not a two-edged sword against her adversaries, but a three-edged one: one unshielded sword sharpened with three powers, ever fighting on behalf of the one three-hypostatic Godhead.

*Refrain: Magnify, O my soul, those who enlighten the Church of Christ.*
*Troparion:*
Though your dwelling is in the heavens, O most glorious ones, and ye bore flesh undefiled unto the ages, in which ye now live in perfection: pray that we who abide upon the earth may both think and do heavenly things.

*Refrain: Magnify, O my soul, her who is more honorable than the heavenly hosts, the all-pure Virgin Birthgiver of God.*
*Theotokion:*
The multitude of thy majesties constrains me, O Lady, providing speech from their abundance; and most gloriously it falls to me to be at a loss concerning such powerful beneficence; therefore we glorify Him Who hath so magnified thee with godly greatness.

*Another Heirmos:*
Heaven was struck with awe at this, and the ends of the earth were amazed, that God appeared unto men in the flesh, and thy womb became more spacious than the heavens: therefore the hierarchies of angels and men magnify thee, the Birthgiver of God!

*Refrain: Magnify, O my soul, the three shepherds, the defenders.*[^3001]
*Troparion:*
Triune virtue was lifted up and filled with all glory, shining forth upon us another thrice-radiant ray, as its own brilliance, O heavenly mystagogues, by whom we are guided in piety unto the divine contemplation thereof!

*Refrain: Magnify, O my soul, the three great ones from the Tri-sunned Light.*
*Troparion:*
There is no second place among these three, for each of them bears the primacy, not being the first, and having supreme and equal honor; but rather they ever yield victory to one another with joy; for the boldness of envy, which corrupts concord, finds no room here.

*Refrain: Magnify, O my soul, the dominion of the three-hypostatic and undivided Godhead.*

The piety of the fathers having shown forth its firstborn sons, through them ever begets radiant and spotless children unto the light, perfected by the Spirit, for the Life that reigned in them; and it asks that peace, which it inherited concerning them, be preserved intact unto the end.

*Refrain: Magnify, O my soul, her who is more honorable than the heavenly hosts, the all-pure Virgin Birthgiver of God.*
*Theotokion:*
The summit of the wise teachers proclaimed Thy Son to be the Son of the living God by revelation of the Father [Mt. 16:16–17], having mystically learned this not from flesh and blood, O Mother of God; therefore, glorifying thee also as Virgin, he magnified thee as Mother and Birthgiver of God.

*Katavasia: In the law of the shadow and the letter...*[^3002]

*Exapostilarion. Podoben: "O unwaning Light" (Свѣ́те неизмѣ́нный):*[^3003]
Three radiant luminaries brighter than the sun's rays, from the Light-originating Trinity and Tri-sunned Unity, supernaturally commingled, let us praise the God-bearing fathers![^3004]

*Glory... Podoben: "He Who adorned the heaven with stars" (И҆́же не́бо ѕвѣзда́ми):*[^3005]
Receptacles of the light, lightning-gleaming bolts: Basil the Great, Gregory the Theologian, and John Chrysostom, let us all now praise!

*Both now... Theotokion:*
O unique Godhead, Father, Son, and Spirit: through the intercessions of Basil, Gregory, and John, and of the all-pure Birthgiver of God, let me not be separated from Thy glory!

*At the Praises, Stichera on 6, Tone 5. Podoben: "Rejoice" (Ра́дꙋйсѧ). By Neil the Chalcidican:*[^3006]

*Sticheron:*
Rejoice, trinity of hierarchs, great bulwarks of the Church: pillars of piety, confirmation of the faithful, overthrow of heretics; who pastured Christ's people with divine teachings and nourished them with manifold virtues, clear preachers of grace; who set forth laws for the fulfillment of Christ, guides unto the highest, entrances to paradise: pray unto Christ to send down great mercy upon our souls!

*Twice.*

*Sticheron:*
Rejoice, trinity of hierarchs, immaterial earthly angels, salvation of the world, joy of mankind, and teachers of the universe; champions of the Word, all-wise physicians of diseases of soul and body; ever-flowing spiritual rivers watering the whole face of the earth with words; theological degrees, divine golden-speakers: pray unto Christ to send down great mercy upon our souls!

*Sticheron:*
Rejoice, holy trinity, suns of the earthly firmament, rays and luminaries from the Tri-sunned radiance recovery of sight unto the darkened, fair-fragrant, most beautiful flowers of paradise; O Theologian, and wise Basil, and Chrysostom: tablets of the Spirit, God-inscribed tables; breasts pouring forth the milk of salvation, adornment of wisdom: pray unto Christ to grant great mercy upon our souls!

*Glory... Tone 6:*
Let us blow the trumpet of hymns, let us dance festively, and let us exult with joy in the all-honorable solemnity of our teachers! Let kings and princes run together, and let hierarchs applaud in songs: for having poured forth rivers of teachings, three very great ones, fertile and ever-living of the Spirit, pastors and teachers, three-fold sacred mystagogues of the most honorable Trinity, having come together let us praise: the wise philosophers; the priests, pastors; the sinners, intercessors; the poor, enrichers; those in tribulations, comforters; travelers, fellow-travelers; those at sea, pilots; and all of us praising the divine hierarchs who everywhere warmly anticipate, let us say thus: O all-holy teachers, make haste to deliver the faithful from the scandals of this life, and to save from eternal torments through your prayers!

*Both now... Theotokion. By Germanus the Patriarch:*[^3007]
Let us blow the trumpet of hymns: for leaning down from on high, the Queen of all, the Virgin Mother, crowns with blessings those who hymn her! Let kings and princes run together, and let them applaud the Queen in hymns who gave birth unto the King, Who lovingly was well pleased to release those formerly held fast by death. Pastors and teachers, coming together let us praise the all-pure Mother of the Good Shepherd: the golden-radiant lampstand, the light-bearing cloud, more spacious than the heavens, the living Ark, the fire-formed Throne of the Master, the manna-receiving golden urn, the closed door of the Word, the refuge of all Christians; praising her with God-speaking hymns, let us say thus: O Palace of the Word, make us, the humble, worthy of the heavenly Kingdom, for nothing is impossible unto thine intercession!

*Great Doxology and Dismissal.*

*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes from Canon 1, Ode 3; and from Canon 2, Ode 6.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 8: Their sound is gone out into all the earth, and their words unto the ends of the world [LXX Ps. 18:5].*

*Verse: The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of His hands [LXX Ps. 18:2].*

*Epistle to the Hebrews, pericope 334 [Heb. 13:7–16].[^3008]*

*Alleluia, Tone 4: The heavens shall confess*[^3009] *shall confess Thy wonders, O Lord, and Thy truth in the assembly of the saints [LXX Ps. 88:6].*

*Gospel according to Matthew, pericope 11 [Mt. 5:14–19]:*
*Ye are the light of the world.*

*Communion Verse: Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous [LXX Ps. 32:1].[^3010]*

*It is fitting to know: if the feast of the three holy hierarchs, Basil the Great, Gregory the Theologian, and John Chrysostom, should occur on the Sunday of the Publican and the Pharisee,[^3011] or of the Prodigal Son,[^3012] or on Meatfare Sunday:[^3013]*
*At Small Vespers, Resurrection Stichera: 4; Glory, of the Hierarchs; Both now, Theotokion of the tone, from Small Vespers. At the Aposticha, one Resurrection Sticheron, and the Aposticha of the Hierarchs from Great Vespers with their verses; Glory, of the Hierarchs; Both now, Theotokion in the same tone.*
*After "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart" and after "Our Father", the Resurrection Troparion; Glory, of the Saints; Both now, Theotokion. Little Ektenia, and the Dismissal.*
*At Great Vespers: After the Kathisma, at "Lord, I have cried", Resurrection Stichera: 3; and of the Triodion: 3; and of the Saints: 4.*
*If it be Meatfare Sunday: Resurrection Stichera: 3; and of the Triodion: 4; and of the Saints: 3; Glory, of the Triodion; Both now, the first Theotokion of the tone.*
*At the Litiya, Stichera of the temple; then the Stichera at the Praises of the Triodion; Glory, of the Saints; Both now, of the Triodion.*
*At the Aposticha, Resurrection Stichera; Glory, of the Saints; Both now, of the Triodion.*
*At the Blessing of the Loaves, the Troparion: "Rejoice, O Virgin Birthgiver of God" twice; and of the Saints, once; and a reading.*
*At Matins: At "God is the Lord", the Resurrection Troparion twice; Glory, of the Saints; Both now, the first Theotokion in the same tone. After the Kathismata, Resurrection Sessional Hymns with their Theotokia; and a reading in the Commentary Gospel; and the Polyeleos of the Saints.*
*If it be the Sunday of the Prodigal Son, or Meatfare Sunday:*
*We add also the third Psalm: "By the rivers of Babylon" [LXX Ps. 136].[^3014] Then, both Sessional Hymns of the Saints once each without Theotokia; Glory, the Polyeleos Sessional Hymn; Both now, Theotokion; and a reading of the Saints.*
*The Gradual Hymns and the Prokeimenon of the tone; "Let every breath praise the Lord"; the Resurrection Gospel; "Having beheld the Resurrection of Christ", and the rest. The Resurrection Canon with its Heirmos on 4; and of the Birthgiver of God on 2; and of the Triodion on 4; and of the Saints on 4. Katavasia: "The sun once shone upon the dry land that was deep" [Ode 1 of the Meeting].[^3015]*
*If it be Meatfare Sunday:*
*Resurrection Canon on 4; and of the Triodion on 6; and of the Saints on 4. Katavasia of the Triodion. After Ode 3, the Kontakion of the Saints and Ikos, and their Sessional Hymn; Both now, of the Triodion; and a reading. After Ode 6, the Kontakion of the Triodion and Ikos; and we read the Prologue. At Ode 9 we sing* "More honorable than the Cherubim". The Resurrection Exapostilarion; Glory, of the Saints; Both now, of the Triodion. At the Praises, Resurrection Stichera: 4; and of the Saints with the doxasticon: 4, with their verses.*
*If it be Meatfare Sunday:*
*Then after the Stichera of the Hierarchs we say the verse: "Arise, O Lord my God" [LXX Ps. 9:33]; and we sing the Idiomelon Sticheron of the Triodion; Glory, the same; Both now: "Thou art supremely blessed, O Virgin Birthgiver of God".*
*If it be not Meatfare Sunday:*
*Then we do not say a verse unto the Triodion, but after the Stichera of the Saints: Glory, of the Triodion; Both now: "Thou art supremely blessed, O Virgin Birthgiver of God". Great Doxology.
