After the Trisagion, the Resurrection Troparion only; and the Ektenias, and the Dismissal. The customary procession into the narthex; Glory, Both now, the Evangelical Sticheron; and the First Hour. At the Hours, the Resurrection Troparion; Glory, of the Saints; Both now, the Theotokion of the Hours. After "Our Father", the Kontakia of the Resurrection, of the Triodion, and of the Saints, saying them alternately.*
*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes of the tone on 4; and of the Triodion, Ode 3 on 4; and of the Saints, Ode 6 on 4. After the Little Entrance, the Resurrection Troparion, and of the Saints; then the Resurrection Kontakion; Glory, of the Saints; Both now, of the Triodion. Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, Gospel, and Communion Verse of the day and of the Saints.*
*If the feast of the three hierarchs should occur on Meatfare Saturday:[^3016]*
*We sing their entire service on the preceding Friday; we keep the vigil without fail.*
*If the feast of the three hierarchs should occur on Monday, Tuesday, or Thursday of Cheesefare Week,[^3017] or on Sunday evening:*
*We sing "Blessed is the man", the first antiphon [On the other days of Cheesefare Week, we say the Kathisma in course].*
*At "Lord, I have cried", Stichera of the Saints on 6; Glory, of the Saints; Both now, Theotokion: the first Dogmatikon of the tone of the Doxasticon of the Saints. Entrance, Prokeimenon of the day, and the readings of the Saints, and the Ektenias.*
*At the Aposticha, the Idiomelon of the Triodion of the day twice, and the Martyrikon; and we say the customary verses: "Unto Thee have I lifted up mine eyes" [LXX Ps. 122:1]; Glory, of the Saints; Both now, the Resurrection Theotokion. After "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart" and after the Trisagion, the Troparion of the Saints; Glory, Both now, Theotokion; and the Dismissal.*
*At Compline, after "It is truly meet" and after the Trisagion, the Kontakion of the Saints.*
*If the commemoration of these three hierarchs should occur on Thursday of Cheesefare Week:*
*Then on Wednesday at the Hours, after "Remit, forgive", and after the metanoias, the bells are rung for the all-night vigil, according to custom according to custom. And immediately we say: "Come, let us worship", the same customary Psalm [LXX Ps. 103]; and the Ektenia; and the Stichera according to what is prescribed. After the Entrance, the Prokeimenon of the reading of the day, and the Old Testament reading of the Triodion; and after it the Prokeimenon: "Let Israel hope in the Lord" [LXX Ps. 130:3]. Then the Old Testament readings of the Saints. Afterward: "Vouchsafe, O Lord". At the Aposticha, the Idiomelon of the Triodion of the day twice, and the Martyrikon; Glory, of the Saints; Both now, Theotokion. After "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart", after "Our Father", the Troparion of the Saints, and the Ektenia, and three great prostrations. Then: "All-holy Trinity"; and "Blessed be the name of the Lord" thrice; and Psalm 33; "It is truly meet"; and the Dismissal. And we enter the refectory, and partake of cheese and eggs.*
*At Matins: At "God is the Lord", the Troparion of the Saints twice; Glory, Both now, Theotokion. After the first Kathisma, the Sessional Hymn of the Triodion twice, written after the second Kathisma; Glory, Both now, its Theotokion; and the reading of the day. After the second Kathisma, both Sessional Hymns of the Saints once each; Glory, Both now, the Theotokion of the second Sessional Hymn; but the Theotokion of the first Sessional Hymn is omitted; and the reading of the day. Then the Polyeleos of the Saints, and their Sessional Hymns, and Theotokion, and a reading. After this, the Gradual Hymns, the first antiphon of Tone 4. Prokeimenon, Gospel, and Sticheron of the Saints.*
*Canon of the Birthgiver of God with the Heirmos on 6, the Heirmoi twice; and the two Canons of the Saints on 8. Katavasia: "The sun once shone upon the dry land that was deep" [Ode 1 of the Meeting], both choirs together. Where there is a triode,[^3018] we sing the Canons of the Saints with the Heirmos on 6, and the triode on 8. Katavasia of the Triodion. After Ode 3, the Sessional Hymns of the Saints, and their Theotokion; and the reading of the Saints. After Ode 6, the Kontakion and Ikos of the Saints; and we read the Prologue. After Ode 9, the Exapostilarion of the Saints twice; Glory, Both now, Theotokion. At the Praises, Stichera of the Saints on 4; and Glory, Both now. Then the reader says: "Glory to Thee Who hast shown us the light", and "Glory to God in the highest". After this, the Ektenia: "Let us complete our morning prayer". And at the Aposticha we sing the Idiomelon of the Triodion of the day twice, and the Martyrikon; and we say the customary verses: "We were filled in the morning with Thy mercy, O Lord" [LXX Ps. 89:14]; Glory, of the Saints, Tone 6: "O hierarchs of Christ"; Both now, Theotokion: "The virgin beauty", written at the Litiya. Then: "It is good to give praise", and the Trisagion; after "Our Father", the Troparion of the Saints; Glory, Both now, the Resurrection Theotokion. After this, the Ektenia: "Have mercy on us, O God", and the Exclamation. Then the Priest says: "Blessed is He Who is", and the chanters: "Amen. Establish, O God"; and the First Hour.*
*At the Hours at the Hours, the Troparion and Kontakion of the Saints.*

*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes from the Canons: of the first, Ode 3 with the Heirmos on 4; and of the other, Ode 6 on 4. After the Little Entrance, Troparia: of the temple of Christ, or of the Birthgiver of God, and of the Saints; then the Kontakion of the temple of Christ; Glory, of the Saints; Both now, of the temple of the Birthgiver of God, or "O Protection of Christians". Prokeimenon, Epistle, Alleluia, Gospel, and Communion Verse of the day, and of the Saints.*
*If the feast of the three hierarchs should occur on Wednesday or Friday of Cheesefare Week:*
*We sing the whole service, evening and morning, on Tuesday or Thursday of the same Cheesefare Week.*

*The same month, on the 31st day.*
*The holy wonderworkers and unmercenaries, Cyrus and John.*[^3019]

*At "Lord, I have cried", Stichera of the Unmercenaries on 6, Tone 1. Podoben: "Joy of the heavenly ranks" (Небе́сныхъ чинѡ́въ):*[^3020]

*Sticheron:*
*Having shone upon the whole universe with the rays of miracles, O Cyrus and John, all-radiant luminaries: ye were made like unto heaven by grace, through the virtues of an exalted life, presented as stars!*

*Twice.*

*Sticheron:*
*O marvelously wise, rain-bringing clouds: with copious streams of marvelous gifts, O martyrs of the Lord, ye spiritually water the whole earth, urging all to offer hymns of health unto God!*

*Sticheron:*
*Having truly received skill from God to heal the passions of soul and body, O martyrs of the Lord: ye heal all things supernaturally, not with human remedies of physicians, but with divine inspirations!*

*Sticheron:*
*Walking among the heavenly powers, O light-radiant luminaries, Cyrus and John, noble sufferers: for Christ's sake ye heal the bodies and the wounds of soul of those on earth; beseech Him to save our souls!*

*Sticheron:*
*Following Christ like a stream of glory, ye appeared unto all as fountains of immortality: ye pour forth sweet streams of bodily and spiritual healing remedies, who poured out poured out streams of blood most zealously for Christ!*

*Glory..., Tone 8:*
*Today the pair of martyrs hath shone forth upon us, healing our spiritual diseases: Cyrus and John, the marvelous wonderworkers! The one, having embraced the angelic, solitary life, lived it unto the end, and through martyr's blood was joined unto Christ; while the other, having shone forth in the ranks of warriors, is enrolled in the heavenly armies. Therefore, in their commemoration, they bestow healings upon those who celebrate with faith, praying for our souls!*

*Both now..., Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion. Podoben: "O most marvelous wonder" (Ѽ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ):*[^3021]
*Beholding Thee, O Child, asleep upon the Tree, Who givest wakefulness unto all: that Thou mightest bestow divine and saving vigilance upon those who of old fell asleep in the sleep of perdition through the fruit of transgression: the Virgin, weeping, cried out; whom we magnify!*

*At the Aposticha, from the Octoechos.*

*Glory..., Tone 2:*
*Come, assembly of the faithful, today let us crown with hymns Cyrus and John, the laborers of grace, and most abundant givers unto them that ask! For in manifold ways they are most radiant physicians unto all; therefore they pray for our souls!*

*Both now..., Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion. Podoben: "When from the Tree" (Е҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва):*[^3022]
*O pure one, when thou didst behold hanging upon the Tree that all-ripe Cluster Whom thou didst bear untilled in thy womb, weeping thou didst cry aloud and exclaim: O Child, drop down sweetness whereby all drunkenness of passions may be removed, O Benefactor, for the sake of me who bore Thee, being enticed by Thy compassion!*

*Troparion, Tone 5:*
*O Christ God, Who hast granted us the wonders of Thy holy martyrs as an unassailable rampart: through their prayers destroy the counsels of the heathen, and strengthen the scepters of the kingdom, as Thou alone art good and the Lover of mankind!*

*At Matins, both Canons from the Octoechos; and of the Saints on 6, Tone 4.*

*Ode 1. Heirmos:*
*Traversing the watery deep of the Red Sea with unwetted feet, ancient Israel of old, by the cross-shaped hands of Moses, vanquished the power of Amalek in the wilderness.*

*Troparion:*
*Thou didst receive grace upon grace, O blessed Cyrus, having glorious John as a fellow-sufferer of afflictions; therefore ye enjoy better delights in the heavens.*

*Troparion (continued from p445):*
*...better delights in the heavens.*

*Troparion:*
*Having girded thyself with spiritual warfare, O all-honored Cyrus, and having forsaken earthly soldiership, O all-praised John: ye received from Christ the signs of victory over the demons.*

*Troparion:*
*Zealous for the virtue of the divine men, the holy women piously clothed themselves in the childlike, angel-like garment; and with martyric longing they stripped for the contests.*

*Theotokion:*
*Seedlessly, by the Father's will, from the divine Spirit of God thou didst conceive the Son; and in the flesh thou didst bear Him Who was motherless from the Father, and for our sake fatherless from thee.*

*Ode 3. Heirmos:*
*Thy Church rejoices in Thee, O Christ, crying aloud: Thou art my strength, O Lord, and my refuge and confirmation!*

*Troparion:*
*Strengthened through Christ's sufferings in the weakness of the flesh, the glorious martyrs cast down the manslayer.*

*Troparion:*
*Receiving in the spirit the pain of the flesh and the incorrupt sweetness of Christ, the martyrs rejoiced.*

*Troparion:*
*The weak nature of women was strengthened by the Cross; therefore they manfully vanquished[^3023] the serpent enemy.*

*Theotokion:*
*Thou alone, beyond nature, wast the Mediatress of good things unto mortals, having been the Mother of God; therefore unto thee we cry: Rejoice!*

*Sessional Hymn, Tone 4. Podoben: "Thou Who wast lifted up" (Вознесы́йся):*[^3024]
*Having trampled underfoot the pleasures that drag downward, O champions, ye were radiantly lifted up by grace unto the divine height of martyrdom, O Cyrus and John, luminaries of the universe! Therefore we pray: deliver us from the darkness of sin and sickness, praying unto God Who is over all!*

*Twice.*

*Glory..., Both now..., Theotokion:*
*Unto God, fleeing unto thy divine protection, O Birthgiver of God, I, the humble one, falling down pray: have mercy, O all-pure one, for my sins have exceeded my head, and I fear the good torments,[^3025] and I tremble; make supplication, O pure one, unto thy Son, to deliver me from them!*

*Stavrotheotokion:*
*Beholding Thee hanging upon the Cross, O Christ, she who bore Thee in the flesh in the latter times, Who wast begotten of the unoriginate Father, cried out: Woe is me, most beloved Jesus! How art Thou, Who art glorified as God by angels, now willing to be crucified by lawless men, O Son? I hymn Thee, O longsuffering One!*

*Ode 4. Heirmos:*
*Beholding Thee, the Sun of righteousness, lifted up upon the Cross, the Church stood Ode 4. Heirmos (continued from p446):*
*...stood in its rank, worthily crying out: Glory to Thy power, O Lord!*

*Troparion:*
*The radiance of the unwaning grace cast down the enemies of the gloomy deceit, having shown forth Cyrus and John as warriors thereof and shining luminaries.*

*Troparion:*
*Delighted by love for the Trinity, and having become beloved of God in It, O martyrs Cyrus and John: by a better union ye were revealed as instruments of God.*

*Troparion:*
*How honorable is your temple, driving away evil spirits! It drives away the sicknesses of all that are ill, O invincible martyrs, and grants the grace of healings.*

*Theotokion:*
*Without knowing wedlock thou didst give birth, O Virgin, and after childbirth thou wast revealed a virgin again; therefore with unceasing voices we cry unto thee with unwavering faith: Rejoice, O Birthgiver of God!*

*Ode 5. Heirmos:*
*Thou, my Lord, hast come into the world as a light, a holy light turning those who hymn Thee in faith from gloomy ignorance.*

*Troparion:*
*The pair of martyrs desired Thee, O Savior; and Thou, Who art holy in the saints, hast worthily honored Cyrus and John.*

*Troparion:*
*The destruction of the enemy is Thy work, O Good One: through the Cross Thou didst make them martyrs of piety, and didst crown them with glory.*

*Troparion:*
*Having been anointed by virginity to love Thee alone with heaven-instructed mind, John and Cyrus acted manfully.*

*Theotokion:*
*We set thee forth as an invincible weapon against enemies; we possess thee as the firmness and hope of our salvation, O Bride of God.*

*Ode 6. Heirmos:*
*I will sacrifice unto Thee with the voice of praise, O Lord, the Church cries unto Thee, having been cleansed from the blood of demons by the blood which flowed through mercy from Thy side.*

*Troparion:*
*The martyrs chose to be sacrificed for Christ rather than sacrifice unto idols, and to bring down the wicked tormentor for the sake of Him Who through compassion was sacrificed for us as a sheep.*

*Troparion:*
*They who unjustly scraped the martyrs with tortures grew weary, and unto those who were scraped, the wounds became as the arrows of babes [LXX Ps. 63:8];[^3026] for most gloriously they were strengthened by the divine Spirit.*

*Troparion:*
*Having confessed the Lord and King of all creation by faith, the like-minded and fellow-suffering pair resisted the lawless even unto blood.*

*Theotokion* (continued from p447):*
*O wonder newest of all wonders! For the Virgin, having conceived without husband Him Who holds all things in His womb, did not confine Him.*

*Kontakion, Tone 3. Podoben: "Today the Virgin" (Дѣ́ва дне́сь):*[^3027]
*Having received the gift of miracles from divine grace, O holy ones, ye perform wonders unceasingly, cutting away all our passions with invisible surgery, O divinely wise Cyrus together with glorious John; for ye are divine physicians!*

*Ikos:*
*Having yielded yourselves unto God, O holy ones, ye endured every trial of afflictions for His sake; and having died willingly, O noble martyrs, even after your end ye pour forth divine gifts unto all that are in diverse sicknesses, and heal them from many evils, whereof I, the wretched one, am one and the first; for I suffer in body and soul from cruel wounds, and in faith I cry unto you: heal me, for ye are divine physicians!*

*Ode 7. Heirmos:*
*In the Persian furnace, the children of Abraham, scorched by love of piety rather than by the flame, cried aloud: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!*

*Troparion:*
*Having weighed their understanding as upon the tipping of a balance, by the weight of immaculate glory the sufferers were lifted up, crying out: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!*

*Troparion:*
*Not ignorant of the adversary's devices [2 Cor. 2:11], the martyrs spat upon every kind of wounds and blandishments, crying aloud: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!*

*Troparion:*
*Crowned through the endurance of wounds, John and Cyrus, the defenders, cried unto the Trinity: Blessed art Thou in the temple of Thy glory, O Lord!*

*Theotokion:*
*Rejoice, consecrated divine dwelling of the Most High! For through thee joy was given, O Birthgiver of God, unto them that cry: Blessed art thou among women, O all-immaculate Lady!*

*Ode 8. Heirmos:*
*Stretching forth his hands, Daniel shut the lions' mouths in the pit [Dan. 6:22]; and the children, lovers of piety, girded with virtue, quenched the power of the fire [Dan. 3], crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!*

*Troparion:*
*Cruelly did the ungodly summon the martyrs unto the denial of Him Who is God by nature; but the invincible martyrs, confessing Him Who is the Creator of all creation, cried aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!*

*Troparion (continued from p448):*
*Raging in deceit with wrath, the tormentors who mind earthly things sent through death unto life those who possessed their citizenship indestructible in the heavens [Phil. 3:20], crying aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!*

*Troparion:*
*The relics of the martyrs shone forth upon the universe with the splendors of miracles, O Christ, putting to shame the delusional deceit of the evil demon, and fittingly bestowing healings upon those who cry aloud: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!*

*Theotokion:*
*He Who was formerly the Word from the Father without a mother, became from thee, O all-immaculate one, secondly without a father; He Who was formerly incorporeal, being incarnate through loving-kindness, was well-pleased to save those who sing: Bless the Lord, all ye works of the Lord!*

*Ode 9. Heirmos:*
*A cornerstone cut without hand from an uncut mountain [Dan. 2:34, 45], even from thee, O Virgin, was Christ, Who joined together the separated natures; therefore, rejoicing, we magnify thee, O Birthgiver of God!*

*Troparion:*
*The pair of invincible martyrs, John and Cyrus, showed themselves obedient unto death [Phil. 2:8] to the Master's divine commands; therefore into the hands of the Creator they commended their spirits.*

*Troparion:*
*Two luminaries shine forth the splendors of miracles from one light-bearing fountain, pouring forth incorruptible grace upon the weak; whom we worthily magnify.*

*Troparion:*
*The pair of invincible sufferers manfully theologized the Unity of the divine essence, yet Trinity in persons; and the incarnate Word, the one Christ in two natures.*

*Theotokion:*
*Spare me, O Christ, when Thou shalt come with glory to judge the world [Mt. 25:31]; dispel the mist of my passions through the prayers of her who bore Thee, and of Thy venerable martyrs, as Thou art good and abundant in mercy.*

*Exapostilarion. Podoben: "He Who adorned the heaven with stars" (И҆́же не́бо ѕвѣзда́ми):*[^3028]
*O wonderworking luminaries, Cyrus together with John, heal our spiritual and bodily sicknesses, having received the grace of healings from the Lord!*

*Theotokion:*
*Thou, O Birthgiver of God, wast the cause of the good things bestowed upon the world by God; even now pray unto the gracious God for the common salvation!*

*At the Aposticha, from the Octoechos.*

*Glory..., Tone 2:*
*With praiseworthy hymns, ye faithful, let us magnify Cyrus and John, kin in the spirit, and brothers unto one another in the flesh; together with whom praising noble Athanasia praising noble Athanasia and her offspring: Theodotia, Eudoxia, and Theoktiste,[^3029] passion-bearers and strangers,[^3030] who pray unto Christ for our souls!*

*Both now..., Theotokion or Stavrotheotokion. Podoben: "Called from on high" (Зва́нный свы́ше):*[^3031]
*Weep not for Me, O Mother, beholding hanging upon the Tree Thy Son and God, Who uncontainably suspended the earth upon the waters and created all creation [Job 26:7]; for I shall arise and be glorified, and I will shatter the kingdom of Hades by My might, and destroy his power, and deliver those who are bound from his malice, as I am compassionate, and bring them unto My Father, as I am the Lover of mankind!*

*At the Liturgy: The Beatitudes from the Octoechos on 4; and of the Saints from the Canon, Ode 3 on 4.*

*Prokeimenon, Tone 4: Unto the saints that are in His earth, the Lord hath made wonderful all His desires in them [LXX Ps. 15:3].*

*Verse: I foresaw the Lord always before me, for He is at my right hand, that I should not be moved [LXX Ps. 15:8].*

*Epistle to the Corinthians, pericope 153 [1 Cor. 12:27–13:8].[^3032]*

*Alleluia, Tone 2: Behold now, what is so good or what so pleasant as for brethren to dwell together in unity? [LXX Ps. 132:1].*

*Gospel according to Matthew, pericope 34 from the half [Mt. 10:1, 5–8].[^3033]*

*Communion Verse: Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous [LXX Ps. 32:1].[^3034]*

*(Typographic Tailpiece: Concluding rococo printer's mark of the Holy Dormition Pochaiv Lavra Press, displaying an ornate cartouche enclosing the Holy Name monogram IHS surmounted by the Cross and three Passion nails, encircled by floral sprays and scrolling foliage.)*[^3035]

*(Catchword at lower right: "Бгородичны" [Theotokia], indicating the traditional common appendix of Dismissal Theotokia in the complete printed edition.)*[^3036]

[^11]: Slavonic: *по все́ послѣ́дованїе я́коже изда́ся на ряду́* (the entire liturgical sequence as set forth in the daily order of the Menaion).
[^12]: Genesis 17:1–7 (LXX).

[^17]: Continued directly from the catchword (*брѣ́занъ*) at the foot of Folio 3v (leaf p4), concluding the Theotokion of the feast at Great Vespers: *therefore also circumcised was an eight-day-old man...*
[^18]: Saint Gregory of Nazianzus (the Theologian), *Oration 43: Funeral Oration on the Great Saint Basil, Bishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia* (PG 36:493–606). In the Byzantine and Ruthenian tradition, this lengthy homily was divided into four readings appointed across Matins.

[^23]: Prov. 1:7; 9:10: "The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom."
[^24]: 1 Kings (1 Sam.) 2:10; 2:2: "The Lord shall give strength unto our kings, and shall exalt the horn of His anointed."
[^25]: Isa. 40:3; Matt. 3:3; LXX Ps. 28:3; 1 Cor. 1:24.
[^26]: Refers to St. Basil the Great's *Hexaemeron* (Nine Homilies on the Six Days of Creation), commenting upon the cosmogony revealed by God unto Moses on Mount Sinai.
[^27]: Cf. Gen. 41:48–56, where Joseph measured out and distributed grain to the hungry in Egypt; St. Basil is hymned as dispensing not merely perishable grain, but the Divine Bread of the Holy Eucharist in the Liturgy.

[^30]: LXX Ps. 77:25; Wisdom 16:20: "bread of angels."

[^33]: Dan. 3:1–23.
[^34]: The theological and ascetic friendship of St. Basil the Great and St. Gregory the Theologian (Nazianzen), commemorated in Gregory's Funeral Oration (*Oratio 43.20*): "We seemed to have two bodies, but a single soul."
[^35]: Exod. 3:2: the burning bush on Horeb/Sinai prefiguring the virginal conception and the Incarnation of God the Word.
[^36]: Dan. 3:49–50 (LXX / Prayer of Azariah and the Song of the Three Holy Children).
[^37]: LXX Ps. 103:3: "Who covers His upper chambers with waters: Who makes the clouds His chariot: Who walks upon the wings of the winds."

[^660]: Psalm 5 (*Глаго́лы моѧ̑ внꙋшѝ гдⷭ҇и*), the opening psalm of the First Royal Hour, invoking morning prayer and divine guidance against deceitful adversaries (LXX Ps. 5).

[^709]: Prokeimenon of the Sixth Royal Hour, Tone 4 (LXX Ps. 76:20, 19: *Въ мо́ри пꙋтїѐ твоѝ*), witnessing the path of God through the depths of the sea and the voice of thunder.

[^712]: Gospel reading of the Sixth Royal Hour from Mark 1:9-15 (Pericope 2), detailing the Baptism of Jesus, the heavenly voice, the forty days' temptation in the wilderness, and the proclamation of the Kingdom.
[^713]: Verses appointed after the Gospel at the Sixth Hour from Psalm 78:8-9 (*Ско́рѡ да предварѧ́тъ ны̀ щедрѡ́ты твоѧ̑ гдⷭ҇и*), pleading for rapid divine deliverance.
[^714]: Concluding Prayer of the Sixth Hour by St. Basil the Great (*Бж҃е и҆ гдⷭ҇и си́лъ*), praising Christ's destruction of the handwriting of sins on the Cross and petitioning for spiritual illumination.
[^715]: Liturgical headpiece and opening for the Ninth Royal Hour (*ЧА́СЪ ДЕВЯ́ТЫЙ*), the final hour of the Theophany eve vigil services, commemorating Christ's death and baptismal consecration.
[^716]: Opening of Psalm 92:1-2 (LXX: *Гдⷭ҇ь воцр҃и́ся, въ лѣ́потꙋ ѡ҆блече́ся*), proclaiming the Lord's eternal kingdom and mastery over the cosmic floods.
[^717]: Conclusion of Psalm 92:2-5 (LXX), exalting the voice of many waters and the holiness of the house of God.
[^718]: Psalm 113:1-26 (LXX: *Во и҆схо́дѣ і҆и҃левѣ ѿ є҆гѵ́пта*), the great festal Theophany psalm witnessing Jordan turning back and the futility of pagan idols.
[^719]: Conclusion of Psalm 113 (LXX), confessing the living God of heaven Who blesses all who fear Him.

[^2992]: *morning rain that came at the end*: Scriptural allusion to Hosea 6:3, Joel 2:23, and James 5:7 concerning the early and latter rain.
[^2993]: *twofold according to nature, of two wills and twofold operation*: The dogmatic definition of the Sixth Ecumenical Council (Constantinople III, 680–681) against Monothelitism and Monoenergism, affirming two natural wills and two natural operations in Jesus Christ.
[^2994]: *Katavasia*: Ode 5 Katavasia of the Meeting of the Lord (Habakkuk 3:3; Church Slavonic *Покры́ла є҆́сть небеса̀ добродѣ́тель твоѧ̀, Хрїсте́*).

[^2996]: *the unbegottenness of the Father, the begetting of the Word, and the procession of the Spirit Himself*: The classical Cappadocian hypostatic properties (*ἰδιώματα*) formulated by St. Basil the Great and St. Gregory the Theologian distinguishing the persons of the Holy Trinity.

[^2999]: *Katavasia*: Ode 7 Katavasia of the Meeting of the Lord (Church Slavonic *Тебѐ во ѻ҆гнѝ ѡ҆роси́вшаго ѻ҆́троки бг҃осло́вившыѧ*).
[^3000]: *Katavasia*: Ode 8 Katavasia of the Meeting of the Lord (Church Slavonic *Нестерпи́момꙋ ѻ҆гню̀ соедини́вшеся, бг҃оче́стїѧ предстоѧ́ще ю҆́ношы*).
[^3001]: *the three shepherds, the defenders*: Church Slavonic *приты́лцы* (literally *those standing at the back/defenders*, or *fellow-protectors*).
[^3002]: *Katavasia*: Ode 9 Katavasia of the Meeting of the Lord (Hebrews 10:1; Church Slavonic *Въ зако́нѣ сѣ́ни и҆ писа́ній ѻ҆́бразъ ви́димъ вѣ́рнїи*).
[^3003]: *O unwaning Light*: Church Slavonic model melody *Свѣ́те неизмѣ́нный* (Tone 3).
[^3004]: *the God-bearing fathers*: The physical printed edition reads *є҆гоно́сныѧ*, an epigraphic misprint for *бг҃оно́сныѧ* (God-bearing).
[^3005]: *He Who adorned the heaven with stars*: Church Slavonic model melody *И҆́же не́бо ѕвѣзда́ми* (Tone 3).
[^3006]: *Neil the Chalcidican*: Church Slavonic *Ні́ла халкопꙋ́ла* (Nilus Chalcopolus or Neil the Metropolitan of Rhodes / John Neil Mauropous of Euchaita).
[^3007]: *Germanus the Patriarch*: St. Germanus I, Patriarch of Constantinople (715–730).
[^3008]: *Hebrews, pericope 334*: Hebrews 13:7–16 ("Remember your leaders, who have spoken unto you the word of God... Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and unto ages").
[^3009]: *The heavens shall confess...*: LXX Psalm 88:6 ("The heavens shall confess Thy wonders, O Lord, and Thy truth in the congregation of the saints").
[^3010]: *Communion Verse: Rejoice in the Lord*: LXX Psalm 32:1 ("Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous; praise becomes the upright", Slavonic *Ра́дꙋйтеся пра́веднїи ѡ҆ Го́сподѣ*).
[^3011]: *Sunday of the Publican and the Pharisee*: The opening pre-Lenten Sunday of the Lenten Triodion cycle.
[^3012]: *Sunday of the Prodigal Son*: The second pre-Lenten preparatory Sunday.
[^3013]: *Meatfare Sunday*: The third pre-Lenten preparatory Sunday, dedicated to the Commemoration of the Second Coming of Christ and the Universal Last Judgment.
[^3014]: *By the rivers of Babylon*: LXX Psalm 136, the third Polyeleos psalm prescribed alongside Psalms 134 and 135 on the pre-Lenten Sundays of the Prodigal Son, Meatfare, and Cheesefare.
[^3015]: *The sun once shone upon the dry land*: Heirmos of Ode 1 of the Canon of the Meeting of the Lord (Church Slavonic *Сꙋ́шꙋ глꙋбороди́тельнꙋю зе́млю*).
[^3016]: *Meatfare Saturday*: The Saturday before Meatfare Sunday, dedicated to the Universal Commemoration of all the Faithful Departed (Soul Saturday). Because of the solemn requiem character of this day, the festive vigil of the Three Hierarchs is transferred forward to the preceding Friday.
[^3017]: *Cheesefare Week*: The week immediately preceding Great Lent (Maslenitsa), during which meat is forbidden but dairy products and eggs are permitted throughout the week.
[^3018]: *Where there is a triode*: Church Slavonic *И҆ди́же трїпѣ́снѡ*, referring to the three-ode canons appointed in the Lenten Triodion for weekdays of Cheesefare Week.
[^3019]: *Cyrus and John*: The Holy Unmercenary Wonderworkers Cyrus (an Egyptian physician from Alexandria who became an anchorite in Arabia) and John (a former Roman soldier from Edessa), who together encouraged the Christian woman Athanasia and her three young daughters (Theodotia, Theoktiste, and Eudoxia) and were beheaded under Diocletian at Canopus in 311.
[^3020]: *Joy of the heavenly ranks*: Church Slavonic model melody *Небе́сныхъ чинѡ́въ* (Tone 1).
[^3021]: *O most marvelous wonder*: Church Slavonic model melody *Ѽ пресла́внагѡ чꙋдесѐ* (Tone 8).
[^3022]: *When from the Tree*: Church Slavonic model melody *Е҆гда̀ ѿ дре́ва* (Tone 2).
[^3023]: *manfully vanquished*: The physical print shows faint inking or a paper crease between *мꙋ́жески* and *ди́ша*, reading *[побѣ]ди́ша* ("manfully conquered/vanquished").
[^3024]: *Thou Who wast lifted up*: Church Slavonic model melody *Вознесы́йся* (Tone 4).
[^3025]: *good torments*: Church Slavonic *бл҃гое мꙋ́къ*, an epigraphic reading reflecting *[бо]я́знь мꙋ́къ* ("fear of torments") or Greek *δεινὰ τῶν κολάσεων* ("terrors of torments").
[^3026]: *arrows of babes*: Scriptural citation from LXX Psalm 63:8 ("The arrows of babes have become their wounds").
[^3027]: *Today the Virgin*: Church Slavonic model melody *Дѣ́ва дне́сь* (Tone 3).
[^3028]: *He Who adorned the heaven with stars*: Church Slavonic model melody *И҆́же не́бо ѕвѣзда́ми* (Tone 3).
[^3029]: *Theodotia, Eudoxia, and Theoktiste*: The three young daughters of St. Athanasia (aged fifteen, thirteen, and eleven respectively), martyred together with their mother and the holy unmercenaries Cyrus and John at Canopus near Alexandria in 311.
[^3030]: *strangers*: Church Slavonic *приходцы*, meaning pilgrims, sojourners, or newcomers (*προσήλυτοι* / *ἐπήλυδες*).
[^3031]: *Called from on high*: Church Slavonic model melody *Зва́нный свы́ше* (Tone 4).
[^3032]: *1 Corinthians, pericope 153*: 1 Corinthians 12:27–13:8 ("Now ye are the body of Christ, and members in particular...").
[^3033]: *Matthew, pericope 34 from the half*: Matthew 10:1, 5–8 ("And when He had called unto Him His twelve disciples, He gave them power against unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all manner of sickness and all manner of disease...").
[^3034]: *Communion Verse*: LXX Psalm 32:1 ("Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous").
[^3035]: *Typographic Tailpiece*: A characteristic Pochaiv monastic woodcut printer's mark bearing the radiate IHS monogram with cross and three nails, standardly employed by the Basilian Fathers of the Holy Dormition Pochaiv Lavra in their liturgical imprints.
[^3036]: *Catchword: Theotokia*: The catchword *Бг҃оро́дичны* at the lower margin indicates the sequence of Dismissal Theotokia for the eight tones found appended to the conclusion of the monthly volumes in the full liturgical set.
[^3037]: *Concluding Folio 224v*: This leaf concludes the text of the Month of January (leaves p1 through p450, folios 1r through 224v), completing the facsimiles and transcription of Volume 5 of the 1761 Pochaiv Menaion.
